CC.E1.RF.C.3.d: Use knowledge that every syllable must have a vowel sound to determine the number of syllables in a printed word.
CC.E1.RF.C.3.e: Decode two-syllable words following basic patterns by breaking the words into syllables.
CC.E1.RF.C.3.g: Recognize and read grade-appropriate irregularly spelled words.
CC.E1.RF.D.4: Read with sufficient accuracy and fluency to support comprehension.
CC.E1.RF.D.4.a: Read grade-level text with purpose and understanding.
CC.E1.RF.D.4.b: Read grade-level text orally with accuracy, appropriate rate, and expression on successive readings.
CC.E1.RF.D.4.c: Use context to confirm or self-correct word recognition and understanding, rereading as necessary.
CC.E1.W.A.1: Write opinion pieces in which they introduce the topic or name the book they are writing about, state an opinion, supply a reason for the opinion, and provide some sense of closure.
CC.E1.W.A.2: Write informative/explanatory texts in which they name a topic, supply some facts about the topic, and provide some sense of closure.
CC.E1.W.A.3: Write narratives in which they recount two or more appropriately sequenced events, include some details regarding what happened, use temporal words to signal event order, and provide some sense of closure.
CC.E1.W.B.5: With guidance and support from adults, focus on a topic, respond to questions and suggestions from peers, and add details to strengthen writing as needed.
CC.E1.W.B.6: With guidance and support from adults, use a variety of digital tools to produce and publish writing, including in collaboration with peers.
CC.E1.W.C.7: Participate in shared research and writing projects (e.g., explore a number of “how-to” books on a given topic and use them to write a sequence of instructions).
CC.E1.W.C.8: With guidance and support from adults, recall information from experiences or gather information from provided sources to answer a question.
CC.E1.SL.A.1: Participate in collaborative conversations with diverse partners about grade 1 topics and texts with peers and adults in small and larger groups.
CC.E1.SL.A.1.a: Follow agreed-upon rules for discussions (e.g., listening to others with care, speaking one at a time about the topics and texts under discussion).
CC.E1.SL.A.1.b: Build on others' talk in conversations by responding to the comments of others through multiple exchanges.
CC.E1.SL.A.1.c: Ask questions to clear up any confusion about the topics and texts under discussion.
CC.E1.SL.A.2: Ask and answer questions about key details in a text read aloud or information presented orally or through other media.
CC.E1.SL.A.3: Ask and answer questions about what a speaker says in order to gather additional information or clarify something that is not understood.
CC.E1.SL.B.4: Describe people, places, things, and events with relevant details, expressing ideas and feelings clearly.
CC.E1.SL.B.5: Add drawings or other visual displays to descriptions when appropriate to clarify ideas, thoughts, and feelings.
CC.E1.SL.B.6: Produce complete sentences when appropriate to task and situation. (See grade 1 Language standards 1 and 3 on page 26 for specific expectations.)
CC.E1.L.A.1: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.
CC.E1.L.A.1.a: Print all upper- and lowercase letters.
CC.E1.L.A.1.b: Use common, proper, and possessive nouns.
CC.E1.L.A.1.c: Use singular and plural nouns with matching verbs in basic sentences (e.g., He hops; We hop).
CC.E1.L.A.1.d: Use personal, possessive, and indefinite pronouns (e.g., I, me, my; they, them, their; anyone, everything).
CC.E1.L.A.1.e: Use verbs to convey a sense of past, present, and future (e.g., Yesterday I walked home; Today I walk home; Tomorrow I will walk home).
CC.E1.L.A.1.g: Use frequently occurring conjunctions (e.g., and, but, or, so, because).
CC.E1.L.A.1.i: Use frequently occurring prepositions (e.g., during, beyond, toward).
CC.E1.L.A.1.j: Produce and expand complete simple and compound declarative, interrogative, imperative, and exclamatory sentences in response to prompts.
CC.E1.L.A.2: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.
CC.E1.L.A.2.a: Capitalize dates and names of people.
CC.E1.L.A.2.c: Use commas in dates and to separate single words in a series.
CC.E1.L.A.2.d: Use conventional spelling for words with common spelling patterns and for frequently occurring irregular words.
CC.E1.L.A.2.e: Spell untaught words phonetically, drawing on phonemic awareness and spelling conventions.
CC.E1.L.C.4: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grade 1 reading and content, choosing flexibly from an array of strategies.
CC.E1.L.C.4.a: Use sentence-level context as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.
CC.E1.L.C.4.b: Use frequently occurring affixes as a clue to the meaning of a word.
CC.E1.L.C.4.c: Identify frequently occurring root words (e.g., look) and their inflectional forms (e.g., looks, looked, looking).
CC.E1.L.C.5: With guidance and support from adults, demonstrate understanding of word relationships and nuances in word meanings.
CC.E1.L.C.5.a: Sort words into categories (e.g., colors, clothing) to gain a sense of the concepts the categories represent.
CC.E1.L.C.5.b: Define words by category and by one or more key attributes (e.g., a duck is a bird that swims; a tiger is a large cat with stripes).
CC.E1.L.C.5.c: Identify real-life connections between words and their use (e.g., note places at home that are cozy).
CC.E1.L.C.5.d: Distinguish shades of meaning among verbs differing in manner (e.g., look, peek, glance, stare, glare, scowl) and adjectives differing in intensity (e.g., large, gigantic) by defining or choosing them or by acting out the meanings.
CC.E1.L.C.6: Use words and phrases acquired through conversations, reading and being read to, and responding to texts, including using frequently occurring conjunctions to signal simple relationships (e.g., because).
CC.M1.OA.A: Represent and solve problems involving addition and subtraction.
CC.M1.OA.A.1: Use addition and subtraction within 20 to solve word problems involving situations of adding to, taking from, putting together, taking apart, and comparing, with unknowns in all positions, e.g., by using objects, drawings, and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.
CC.M1.OA.A.2: Solve word problems that call for addition of three whole numbers whose sum is less than or equal to 20, e.g., by using objects, drawings, and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.
CC.M1.OA.B: Understand and apply properties of operations and the relationship between addition and subtraction.
CC.M1.OA.B.3: Apply properties of operations as strategies to add and subtract.
CC.M1.OA.B.4: Understand subtraction as an unknown-addend problem.
CC.M1.OA.C.5: Relate counting to addition and subtraction (e.g., by counting on 2 to add 2).
CC.M1.OA.C.6: Add and subtract within 20, demonstrating fluency for addition and subtraction within 10. Use strategies such as counting on; making ten (e.g., 8 + 6 = 8 + 2 + 4 = 10 + 4 = 14); decomposing a number leading to a ten (e.g., 13 - 4 = 13 - 3 - 1 = 10 - 1 = 9); using the relationship between addition and subtraction (e.g., knowing that 8 + 4 = 12, one knows 12 - 8 = 4); and creating equivalent but easier or known sums (e.g., adding 6 + 7 by creating the known equivalent 6 + 6 + 1 = 12 + 1 = 13).
CC.M1.OA.D: Work with addition and subtraction equations.
CC.M1.OA.D.7: Understand the meaning of the equal sign, and determine if equations involving addition and subtraction are true or false.
CC.M1.OA.D.8: Determine the unknown whole number in an addition or subtraction equation relating three whole numbers.
CC.M1.NBT.A.1: Count to 120, starting at any number less than 120. In this range, read and write numerals and represent a number of objects with a written numeral.
CC.M1.NBT.B.2: Understand that the two digits of a two-digit number represent amounts of tens and ones. Understand the following as special cases:
CC.M1.NBT.B.2.a: 10 can be thought of as a bundle of ten ones - called a “ten.”
CC.M1.NBT.B.2.b: The numbers from 11 to 19 are composed of a ten and one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine ones.
CC.M1.NBT.B.2.c: The numbers 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90 refer to one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine tens (and 0 ones).
CC.M1.NBT.B.3: Compare two two-digit numbers based on meanings of the tens and ones digits, recording the results of comparisons with the symbols `>,=,and<`.
CC.M1.NBT.C: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to add and subtract.
CC.M1.NBT.C.4: Add within `100`, including adding a two-digit number and a one-digit number, and adding a two-digit number and a multiple of 10, using concrete models or drawings and strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction; relate the strategy to a written method and explain the reasoning used. Understand that in adding two-digit numbers, one adds tens and tens, ones and ones; and sometimes it is necessary to compose a ten.
CC.M1.NBT.C.5: Given a two-digit number, mentally find 10 more or 10 less than the number, without having to count; explain the reasoning used.
CC.M1.NBT.C.6: Subtract multiples of `10` in the range `10-90` from multiples of `10` in the range `10-90` (positive or zero differences), using concrete models or drawings and strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction; relate the strategy to a written method and explain the reasoning used.
CC.M1.MD.A: Measure lengths indirectly and by iterating length units.
CC.M1.MD.A.1: Order three objects by length; compare the lengths of two objects indirectly by using a third object.
CC.M1.MD.A.2: Express the length of an object as a whole number of length units, by laying multiple copies of a shorter object (the length unit) end to end; understand that the length measurement of an object is the number of same-size length units that span it with no gaps or overlaps. Limit to contexts where the object being measured is spanned by a whole number of length units with no gaps or overlaps.
CC.M1.MD.B.3: Tell and write time in `text(hours)` and half-hours using analog and digital clocks.
CC.M1.MD.C.4: Organize, represent, and interpret data with up to three categories; ask and answer questions about the total number of data points, how many in each category, and how many more or less are in one category than in another.
CC.M1.G.A: Reason with shapes and their attributes.
CC.M1.G.A.1: Distinguish between defining attributes (e.g., triangles are closed and three-sided) versus non-defining attributes (e.g., color, orientation, overall size); build and draw shapes to possess defining attributes.
CC.M1.G.A.2: Compose two-dimensional shapes (rectangles, squares, trapezoids, triangles, half-circles, and quarter-circles) or three-dimensional shapes (cubes, right rectangular prisms, right circular cones, and right circular cylinders) to create a composite shape, and compose new shapes from the composite shape.
CC.M1.G.A.3: Partition circles and rectangles into two and four equal shares, describe the shares using the words halves, fourths, and quarters, and use the phrases half of, fourth of, and quarter of. Describe the whole as two of, or four of the shares. Understand for these examples that decomposing into more equal shares creates smaller shares.
CC.E2.RL.A.1: Ask and answer such questions as who, what, where, when, why, and how to demonstrate understanding of key details in a text.
CC.E2.RL.A.2: Recount stories, including fables and folktales from diverse cultures, and determine their central message, lesson, or moral.
CC.E2.RL.A.3: Describe how characters in a story respond to major events and challenges.
CC.E2.RL.B.4: Describe how words and phrases (e.g., regular beats, alliteration, rhymes, repeated lines) supply rhythm and meaning in a story, poem, or song.
CC.E2.RL.B.5: Describe the overall structure of a story, including describing how the beginning introduces the story and the ending concludes the action.
CC.E2.RL.B.6: Acknowledge differences in the points of view of characters, including by speaking in a different voice for each character when reading dialogue aloud.
CC.E2.RL.C.7: Use information gained from the illustrations and words in a print or digital text to demonstrate understanding of its characters, setting, or plot.
CC.E2.RL.C.9: Compare and contrast two or more versions of the same story (e.g., Cinderella stories) by different authors or from different cultures.
CC.E2.RL.D: Range Of Reading & Level Of Text Complexity
CC.E2.RL.D.10: By the end of the year, read and comprehend literature, including stories and poetry, in the grades 2-3 text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.
CC.E2.RI.A.1: Ask and answer such questions as who, what, where, when, why, and how to demonstrate understanding of key details in a text.
CC.E2.RI.A.2: Identify the main topic of a multiparagraph text as well as the focus of specific paragraphs within the text.
CC.E2.RI.A.3: Describe the connection between a series of historical events, scientific ideas or concepts, or steps in technical procedures in a text.
CC.E2.RI.B.4: Determine the meaning of words and phrases in a text relevant to a grade 2 topic or subject area.
CC.E2.RI.B.5: Know and use various text features (e.g., indexes, electronic menus, icons) to locate key facts or information in a text efficiently.
CC.E2.RI.B.6: Identify the main purpose of a text, including what the author wants to answer, explain, or describe.
CC.E2.RI.C.7: Explain how specific images (e.g., a diagram showing how a machine works) contribute to and clarify a text.
CC.E2.RI.C.8: Describe how reasons support specific points the author makes in a text.
CC.E2.RI.C.9: Compare and contrast the most important points presented by two texts on the same topic.
CC.E2.RI.D: Range Of Reading & Level Of Text Complexity
CC.E2.RI.D.10: By the end of year, read and comprehend informational texts, including history/social studies, science, and technical texts, in the grades 2-3 text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.
CC.E2.RF.C.3: Know and apply grade-level phonics and word analysis skills in decoding words.
CC.E2.RF.C.3.a: Distinguish long and short vowels when reading regularly spelled one-syllable words.
CC.E2.RF.C.3.b: Know spelling-sound correspondences for additional common vowel teams.
CC.E2.RF.C.3.c: Decode regularly spelled two-syllable words with long vowels.
CC.E2.RF.C.3.d: Decode words with common prefixes and suffixes.
CC.E2.RF.C.3.e: Identify words with inconsistent but common spelling-sound correspondences.
CC.E2.RF.C.3.f: Recognize and read grade-appropriate irregularly spelled words.
CC.E2.RF.D.4: Read with sufficient accuracy and fluency to support comprehension.
CC.E2.RF.D.4.a: Read grade-level text with purpose and understanding.
CC.E2.RF.D.4.b: Read grade-level text orally with accuracy, appropriate rate, and expression on successive readings.
CC.E2.RF.D.4.c: Use context to confirm or self-correct word recognition and understanding, rereading as necessary.
CC.E2.W.A.1: Write opinion pieces in which they introduce the topic or book they are writing about, state an opinion, supply reasons that support the opinion, use linking words (e.g., because, and, also) to connect opinion and reasons, and provide a concluding statement or section.
CC.E2.W.A.2: Write informative/explanatory texts in which they introduce a topic, use facts and definitions to develop points, and provide a concluding statement or section.
CC.E2.W.A.3: Write narratives in which they recount a well-elaborated event or short sequence of events, include details to describe actions, thoughts, and feelings, use temporal words to signal event order, and provide a sense of closure.
CC.E2.W.B.5: With guidance and support from adults and peers, focus on a topic and strengthen writing as needed by revising and editing.
CC.E2.W.B.6: With guidance and support from adults, use a variety of digital tools to produce and publish writing, including in collaboration with peers.
CC.E2.W.C.7: Participate in shared research and writing projects (e.g., read a number of books on a single topic to produce a report; record science observations).
CC.E2.W.C.8: Recall information from experiences or gather information from provided sources to answer a question.
CC.E2.SL.A.1: Participate in collaborative conversations with diverse partners about grade 2 topics and texts with peers and adults in small and larger groups.
CC.E2.SL.A.1.a: Follow agreed-upon rules for discussions (e.g., gaining the floor in respectful ways, listening to others with care, speaking one at a time about the topics and texts under discussion).
CC.E2.SL.A.1.b: Build on others' talk in conversations by linking their comments to the remarks of others.
CC.E2.SL.A.1.c: Ask for clarification and further explanation as needed about the topics and texts under discussion.
CC.E2.SL.A.2: Recount or describe key ideas or details from a text read aloud or information presented orally or through other media.
CC.E2.SL.A.3: Ask and answer questions about what a speaker says in order to clarify comprehension, gather additional information, or deepen understanding of a topic or issue.
CC.E2.SL.B.4: Tell a story or recount an experience with appropriate facts and relevant, descriptive details, speaking audibly in coherent sentences.
CC.E2.SL.B.5: Create audio recordings of stories or poems; add drawings or other visual displays to stories or recounts of experiences when appropriate to clarify ideas, thoughts, and feelings.
CC.E2.SL.B.6: Produce complete sentences when appropriate to task and situation in order to provide requested detail or clarification. (See grade 2 Language standards 1 and 3 on page 26 for specific expectations.)
CC.E2.L.A.1: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.
CC.E2.L.A.1.b: Form and use frequently occurring irregular plural nouns (e.g., feet, children, teeth, mice, fish).
CC.E2.L.A.1.d: Form and use the past tense of frequently occurring irregular verbs (e.g., sat, hid, told).
CC.E2.L.A.1.e: Use adjectives and adverbs, and choose between them depending on what is to be modified.
CC.E2.L.A.1.f: Produce, expand, and rearrange complete simple and compound sentences (e.g., The boy watched the movie; The little boy watched the movie; The action movie was watched by the little boy).
CC.E2.L.A.2: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.
CC.E2.L.A.2.a: Capitalize holidays, product names, and geographic names.
CC.E2.L.A.2.b: Capitalize holidays, product names, and geographic names.
CC.E2.L.A.2.c: Use an apostrophe to form contractions and frequently occurring possessives.
CC.E2.L.A.2.d: Generalize learned spelling patterns when writing words (e.g., cage → badge; boy → boil).
CC.E2.L.A.2.e: Consult reference materials, including beginning dictionaries, as needed to check and correct spellings.
CC.E2.L.B.3: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening. a. Compare formal and informal uses of English.
CC.E2.L.C.4: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grade 2 reading and content, choosing flexibly from an array of strategies.
CC.E2.L.C.4.a: Use sentence-level context as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.
CC.E2.L.C.4.b: Determine the meaning of the new word formed when a known prefix is added to a known word (e.g., happy/unhappy, tell/retell).
CC.E2.L.C.4.c: Use a known root word as a clue to the meaning of an unknown word with the same root (e.g., addition, additional).
CC.E2.L.C.4.d: Use knowledge of the meaning of individual words to predict the meaning of compound words (e.g., birdhouse, lighthouse, housefly; bookshelf, notebook, bookmark).
CC.E2.L.C.4.e: Use glossaries and beginning dictionaries, both print and digital, to determine or clarify the meaning of words and phrases.
CC.E2.L.C.5: Demonstrate understanding of word relationships and nuances in word meanings.
CC.E2.L.C.5.a: Identify real-life connections between words and their use (e.g., describe foods that are spicy or juicy).
CC.E2.L.C.5.b: Distinguish shades of meaning among closely related verbs (e.g., toss, throw, hurl) and closely related adjectives (e.g., thin, slender, skinny, scrawny).
CC.E2.L.C.6: Use words and phrases acquired through conversations, reading and being read to, and responding to texts, including using adjectives and adverbs to describe (e.g., When other kids are happy that makes me happy).
CC.M2.OA.A: Represent and solve problems involving addition and subtraction.
CC.M2.OA.A.1: Use addition and subtraction within `100` to solve one- and two-step word problems involving situations of adding to, taking from, putting together, taking apart, and comparing, with unknowns in all positions, e.g., by using drawings and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.
CC.M2.OA.B.2: Fluently add and subtract within 20 using mental strategies. By end of Grade 2, know from memory all sums of two one-digit numbers.
CC.M2.OA.C: Work with equal groups of objects to gain foundations for multiplication.
CC.M2.OA.C.3: Determine whether a group of objects (up to 20) has an odd or even number of members, e.g., by pairing objects or counting them by `2text(s)`; write an equation to express an even number as a sum of two equal addends.
CC.M2.OA.C.4: Use addition to find the total number of objects arranged in rectangular arrays with up to `5` rows and up to `5` columns; write an equation to express the total as a sum of equal addends.
CC.M2.NBT.A.1: Understand that the three digits of a three-digit number represent amounts of hundreds, tens, and ones; e.g., 706 equals 7 hundreds, 0 tens, and 6 ones. Understand the following as special cases:
CC.M2.NBT.A.1.a: 100 can be thought of as a bundle of ten tens - called a “hundred.”
CC.M2.NBT.A.1.b: The numbers 100, 200, 300, 400, 500, 600, 700, 800, 900 refer to one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine hundreds (and 0 tens and 0 ones).
CC.M2.NBT.A.3: Read and write numbers to `1000` using base-ten numerals, number names, and expanded form.
CC.M2.NBT.A.4: Compare two three-digit numbers based on meanings of the hundreds, tens, and ones digits, using `>,=,and<` symbols to record the results of comparisons.
CC.M2.NBT.B: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to add and subtract.
CC.M2.NBT.A.5: Fluently add and subtract within `100` using strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction.
CC.M2.NBT.B.6: Add up to four two-digit numbers using strategies based on place value and properties of operations.
CC.M2.NBT.B.7: Add and subtract within `1000`, using concrete models or drawings and strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction; relate the strategy to a written method. Understand that in adding or subtracting three-digit numbers, one adds or subtracts hundreds and hundreds, tens and tens, ones and ones; and sometimes it is necessary to compose or decompose tens or hundreds.
CC.M2.NBT.B.8: Mentally add `10or100` to a given number 100-900, and mentally subtract `10or100` from a given number 100-900.
CC.M2.NBT.B.9: Explain why addition and subtraction strategies work, using place value and the properties of operations.
CC.M2.MD.A: Measure and estimate lengths in standard units.
CC.M2.MD.A.1: Measure the length of an object by selecting and using appropriate tools such as rulers, yardsticks, meter sticks, and measuring tapes.
CC.M2.MD.A.2: Measure the length of an object twice, using length units of different lengths for the two measurements; describe how the two measurements relate to the size of the unit chosen.
CC.M2.MD.A.3: Estimate lengths using units of inches, feet, centimeters, and meters.
CC.M2.MD.A.4: Measure to determine how much longer one object is than another, expressing the length difference in terms of a standard length unit.
CC.M2.MD.B: Relate addition and subtraction to length.
CC.M2.MD.B.5: Use addition and subtraction within `100` to solve word problems involving lengths that are given in the same units, e.g., by using drawings (such as drawings of rulers) and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.
CC.M2.MD.B.6: Represent whole numbers as lengths from `0` on a number line diagram with equally spaced points corresponding to the numbers 0, 1, 2, ..., and represent whole-number sums and differences within `100` on a number line diagram.
CC.M2.MD.C.7: Tell and write time from analog and digital clocks to the nearest five minutes, using a.m. and p.m.
CC.M2.MD.C.8: Solve word problems involving dollar bills, quarters, dimes, nickels, and pennies, using $ and ¢ symbols appropriately. Example: If you have 2 dimes and 3 pennies, how many cents do you have?
CC.M2.MD.D.9: Generate measurement data by measuring lengths of several objects to the nearest whole unit, or by making repeated measurements of the same object. Show the measurements by making a line plot, where the horizontal scale is marked off in whole-number units.
CC.M2.MD.D.10: Draw a picture graph and a bar graph (with single-unit scale) to represent a data set with up to four categories. Solve simple put-together, take-apart, and compare problems using information presented in a bar graph.
CC.M2.G.A: Reason with shapes and their attributes.
CC.M2.G.A.1: Recognize and draw shapes having specified attributes, such as a given number of angles or a given number of equal faces. Identify triangles, quadrilaterals, pentagons, hexagons, and cubes.
CC.M2.G.A.2: Partition a rectangle into rows and columns of same-size squares and count to find the total number of them.
CC.M2.G.A.3: Partition circles and rectangles into two, three, or four equal shares, describe the shares using the words halves, thirds, half of, a third of, etc., and describe the whole as two halves, three thirds, four fourths. Recognize that equal shares of identical wholes need not have the same shape.
CC.E3.RL.A.1: Ask and answer questions to demonstrate understanding of a text, referring explicitly to the text as the basis for the answers.
CC.E3.RL.A.2: Recount stories, including fables, folktales, and myths from diverse cultures; determine the central message, lesson, or moral and explain how it is conveyed through key details in the text.
CC.E3.RL.A.3: Describe characters in a story (e.g., their traits, motivations, or feelings) and explain how their actions contribute to the sequence of events.
CC.E3.RL.B.4: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, distinguishing literal from nonliteral language.
CC.E3.RL.B.5: Refer to parts of stories, dramas, and poems when writing or speaking about a text, using terms such as chapter, scene, and stanza; describe how each successive part builds on earlier sections.
CC.E3.RL.B.6: Distinguish their own point of view from that of the narrator or those of the characters.
CC.E3.RL.C.7: Make connections between the text of a story or drama and a visual or oral presentation of the text, identifying where each version reflects specific descriptions and directions in the text.
CC.E3.RL.C.9: Compare and contrast the treatment of similar themes and topics (e.g., opposition of good and evil) and patterns of events (e.g., the quest) in stories, myths, and traditional literature from different cultures.
CC.E3.RL.D: Range Of Reading & Level Of Text Complexity
CC.E3.RL.D.10: By the end of the year, read and comprehend literature, including stories, dramas, and poetry, in the grades 4-5 text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.
CC.E3.RI.A.1: Ask and answer questions to demonstrate understanding of a text, referring explicitly to the text as the basis for the answers.
CC.E3.RI.A.2: Determine the main idea of a text; recount the key details and explain how they support the main idea.
CC.E3.RI.A.3: Describe the relationship between a series of historical events, scientific ideas or concepts, or steps in technical procedures in a text, using language that pertains to time, sequence, and cause/effect.
CC.E3.RI.B.4: Determine the meaning of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases in a text relevant to a grade 3 topic or subject area.
CC.E3.RI.B.5: Use text features and search tools (e.g., key words, sidebars, hyperlinks) to locate information relevant to a given topic efficiently.
CC.E3.RI.B.6: Distinguish their own point of view from that of the author of a text.
CC.E3.RI.C.7: Use information gained from illustrations (e.g., maps, photographs) and the words in a text to demonstrate understanding of the text (e.g., where, when, why, and how key events occur).
CC.E3.RI.C.8: Describe the logical connection between particular sentences and paragraphs in a text (e.g., comparison, cause/effect, first/second/third in a sequence).
CC.E3.RI.C.9: Compare and contrast the most important points and key details presented in two texts on the same topic.
CC.E3.RI.D: Range Of Reading & Level Of Text Complexity
CC.E3.RI.D.10: By the end of the year, read and comprehend informational texts, including history/social studies, science, and technical texts, at the high end of the grades 2-3 text complexity band independently and proficiently.
CC.E3.RF.C.3: Know and apply grade-level phonics and word analysis skills in decoding words.
CC.E3.RF.C.3.a: Identify and know the meaning of the most common prefixes and derivational suffixes.
CC.E3.RF.C.3.b: Decode words with common Latin suffixes.
CC.E3.RF.D.4: Read with sufficient accuracy and fluency to support comprehension.
CC.E3.RF.D.4.a: Read with sufficient accuracy and fluency to support comprehension.
CC.E3.RF.D.4.b: Read grade-level prose and poetry orally with accuracy, appropriate rate, and expression on successive readings
CC.E3.RF.D.4.c: Use context to confirm or self-correct word recognition and understanding, rereading as necessary.
CC.E3.W.A.1: Write opinion pieces on topics or texts, supporting a point of view with reasons.
CC.E3.W.A.1.a: Introduce the topic or text they are writing about, state an opinion, and create an organizational structure that lists reasons.
CC.E3.W.A.1.b: Provide reasons that support the opinion.
CC.E3.W.A.1.c: Use linking words and phrases (e.g., because, therefore, since, for example) to connect opinion and reasons.
CC.E3.W.A.1.d: Provide a concluding statement or section.
CC.E3.W.A.2: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine a topic and convey ideas and information clearly.
CC.E3.W.A.2.a: Introduce a topic and group related information together; include illustrations when useful to aiding comprehension.
CC.E3.W.A.2.b: Develop the topic with facts, definitions, and details.
CC.E3.W.A.2.c: Use linking words and phrases (e.g., also, another, and, more, but) to connect ideas within categories of information.
CC.E3.W.A.2.d: Provide a concluding statement or section.
CC.E3.W.A.3: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, descriptive details, and clear event sequences.
CC.E3.W.A.3.a: Establish a situation and introduce a narrator and/or characters; organize an event sequence that unfolds naturally.
CC.E3.W.A.3.b: Use dialogue and descriptions of actions, thoughts, and feelings to develop experiences and events or show the response of characters to situations.
CC.E3.W.A.3.c: Use temporal words and phrases to signal event order.
CC.E3.W.B.4: With guidance and support from adults, produce writing in which the development and organization are appropriate to task and purpose.
CC.E3.W.B.5: With guidance and support from peers and adults, develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, and editing.
CC.E3.W.B.6: With guidance and support from adults, use technology to produce and publish writing (using keyboarding skills) as well as to interact and collaborate with others.
CC.E3.W.C.7: Conduct short research projects that build knowledge about a topic.
CC.E3.W.C.8: Recall information from experiences or gather information from print and digital sources; take brief notes on sources and sort evidence into provided categories.
CC.E3.W.D.10: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of discipline-specific tasks, purposes, and audiences.
CC.E3.SL.A.1: Engage effectively in a range of collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in groups, and teacher-led) with diverse partners on grade 3 topics and texts, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly.
CC.E3.SL.A.1.a: Come to discussions prepared, having read or studied required material; explicitly draw on that preparation and other information known about the topic to explore ideas under discussion.
CC.E3.SL.A.1.b: Follow agreed-upon rules for discussions (e.g., gaining the floor in respectful ways, listening to others with care, speaking one at a time about the topics and texts under discussion).
CC.E3.SL.A.1.c: Ask questions to check understanding of information presented, stay on topic, and link their comments to the remarks of others.
CC.E3.SL.A.1.d: Explain their own ideas and understanding in light of the discussion.
CC.E3.SL.A.2: Determine the main ideas and supporting details of a text read aloud or information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.
CC.E3.SL.A.3: Ask and answer questions about information from a speaker, offering appropriate elaboration and detail.
CC.E3.SL.B.4: Report on a topic or text, tell a story, or recount an experience with appropriate facts and relevant, descriptive details, speaking clearly at an understandable pace.
CC.E3.SL.B.5: Create engaging audio recordings of stories or poems that demonstrate fluid reading at an understandable pace; add visual displays when appropriate to emphasize or enhance certain facts or details.
CC.E3.SL.B.6: Speak in complete sentences when appropriate to task and situation in order to provide requested detail or clarification. (See grade 3 Language standards 1 and 3 on page 28 for specific expectations.)
CC.E3.L.A.1: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.
CC.E3.L.A.1.a: Explain the function of nouns, pronouns, verbs, adjectives, and adverbs in general and their functions in particular sentences.
CC.E3.L.A.1.b: Form and use regular and irregular plural nouns.
CC.E3.L.A.1.d: Form and use regular and irregular verbs.
CC.E3.L.A.1.e: Form and use the simple (e.g., I walked; I walk; I will walk) verb tenses.
CC.E3.L.A.1.g: Form and use comparative and superlative adjectives and adverbs, and choose between them depending on what is to be modified.
CC.E3.L.A.1.i: Produce simple, compound, and complex sentences.
CC.E3.L.A.2: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.
CC.E3.L.A.2.c: Use commas and quotation marks in dialogue.
CC.E3.L.A.2.e: Use conventional spelling for high-frequency and other studied words and for adding suffixes to base words (e.g., sitting, smiled, cries, happiness).
CC.E3.L.A.2.f: Use spelling patterns and generalizations (e.g., word families, position-based spellings, syllable patterns, ending rules, meaningful word parts) in writing words.
CC.E3.L.A.2.g: Consult reference materials, including beginning dictionaries, as needed to check and correct spellings.
CC.E3.L.B.3: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening.
CC.E3.L.B.3.a: Choose words and phrases for effect.
CC.E3.L.B.3.b: Recognize and observe differences between the conventions of spoken and written standard English.
CC.E3.L.C.4: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning word and phrases based on grade 3 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.
CC.E3.L.C.4.a: Use sentence-level context as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.
CC.E3.L.C.4.b: Determine the meaning of the new word formed when a known affix is added to a known word (e.g., agreeable/disagreeable, comfortable/uncomfortable, care/careless, heat/preheat).
CC.E3.L.C.4.c: Use a known root word as a clue to the meaning of an unknown word with the same root (e.g., company, companion).
CC.E3.L.C.4.d: Use glossaries or beginning dictionaries, both print and digital, to determine or clarify the precise meaning of key words and phrases.
CC.E3.L.C.5: Demonstrate understanding of word relationships and nuances in word meanings.
CC.E3.L.C.5.a: Distinguish the literal and nonliteral meanings of words and phrases in context (e.g., take steps).
CC.E3.L.C.5.b: Identify real-life connections between words and their use (e.g., describe people who are friendly or helpful).
CC.E3.L.C.5.c: Distinguish shades of meaning among related words that describe states of mind or degrees of certainty (e.g., knew, believed, suspected, heard, wondered).
CC.E3.L.C.6: Acquire and use accurately grade-appropriate conversational, general academic, and domain-specific words and phrases, including those that signal spatial and temporal relationships (e.g., After dinner that night we went looking for them).
CC.M3.OA.A: Represent and solve problems involving multiplication and division.
CC.M3.OA.A.1: Interpret products of whole numbers, e.g., interpret `5xx7` as the total number of objects in `5` groups of `7` objects each.
CC.M3.OA.A.2: Interpret whole-number quotients of whole numbers, e.g., interpret `56-:8` as the number of objects in each share when `56` objects are partitioned equally into `8` shares, or as a number of shares when `56` objects are partitioned into equal shares of `8` objects each.
CC.M3.OA.A.3: Use multiplication and division within `100` to solve word problems in situations involving equal groups, arrays, and measurement quantities, e.g., by using drawings and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.
CC.M3.OA.A.4: Determine the unknown whole number in a multiplication or division equation relating three whole numbers.
CC.M3.OA.B: Understand properties of multiplication and the relationship between multiplication and division.
CC.M3.OA.B.5: Apply properties of operations as strategies to multiply and divide.
CC.M3.OA.B.6: Understand division as an unknown-factor problem.
CC.M3.OA.C.7: Fluently multiply and divide within `100`, using strategies such as the relationship between multiplication and division (e.g., knowing that `8xx5=40`, one knows `40-:5=8`) or properties of operations. By the end of Grade 3, know from memory all products of two one-digit numbers.
CC.M3.OA.D: Solve problems involving the four operations, and identify and explain patterns in arithmetic.
CC.M3.OA.D.8: Solve two-step word problems using the four operations. Represent these problems using equations with a letter standing for the unknown quantity. Assess the reasonableness of answers using mental computation and estimation strategies including rounding.
CC.M3.OA.D.9: Identify arithmetic patterns (including patterns in the addition table or multiplication table), and explain them using properties of operations.
CC.M3.NBT.A: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to perform multi-digit arithmetic.
CC.M3.NBT.A.1: Use place value understanding to round whole numbers to the nearest `10or100`.
CC.M3.NBT.A.2: Fluently add and subtract within `1000` using strategies and algorithms based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction.
CC.M3.NBT.A.3: Multiply one-digit whole numbers by multiples of `10` in the range `10-90` (e.g., `9xx80,5xx60`) using strategies based on place value and properties of operations.
CC.M3.NF.A: Develop understanding of fractions as numbers.
CC.M3.NF.A.1: Understand a fraction `1/b` as the quantity formed by `1` part when a whole is partitioned into `b` equal parts; understand a fraction `a/b` as the quantity formed by a parts of size `1/b`.
CC.M3.NF.A.2: Understand a fraction as a number on the number line; represent fractions on a number line diagram.
CC.M3.NF.A.2.a: Represent a fraction `1/b` on a number line diagram by defining the interval from `0` to `1` as the whole and partitioning it into `b` equal parts. Recognize that each part has size `1/b` and that the endpoint of the part based at `0` locates the number `1/b` on the number line.
CC.M3.NF.A.2.b: Represent a fraction `a/b` on a number line diagram by marking off a lengths `1/b` from `0`. Recognize that the resulting interval has size `a/b` and that its endpoint locates the number `a/b` on the number line.
CC.M3.NF.A.3: Explain equivalence of fractions in special cases, and compare fractions by reasoning about their size.
CC.M3.NF.A.3.a: Understand two fractions as equivalent (equal) if they are the same size, or the same point on a number line.
CC.M3.NF.A.3.b: Recognize and generate simple equivalent fractions, e.g., `1/2=2/4,4/6=2/3`. Explain why the fractions are equivalent, e.g., by using a visual fraction model.
CC.M3.NF.A.3.c: Express whole numbers as fractions, and recognize fractions that are equivalent to whole numbers.
CC.M3.NF.A.3.d: Compare two fractions with the same numerator or the same denominator by reasoning about their size. Recognize that comparisons are valid only when the two fractions refer to the same whole. Record the results of comparisons with the symbols `>,=,or<`, and justify the conclusions, e.g., by using a visual fraction model.
CC.M3.MD.A: Solve problems involving measurement and estimation of intervals of time, liquid volumes, and masses of objects.
CC.M3.MD.A.1: Tell and write time to the nearest minute and measure time intervals in `text(minutes)`. Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of time intervals in `text(minutes)`, e.g., by representing the problem on a number line diagram.
CC.M3.MD.A.2: Measure and estimate liquid volumes and masses of objects using standard units of grams (g), kilograms (kg), and liters (l). Add, subtract, multiply, or divide to solve one-step word problems involving masses or volumes that are given in the same units, e.g., by using drawings (such as a beaker with a measurement scale) to represent the problem.
CC.M3.MD.B.3: Draw a scaled picture graph and a scaled bar graph to represent a data set with several categories. Solve one- and two-step “how many more” and “how many less” problems using information presented in scaled bar graphs.
CC.M3.MD.B.4: Generate measurement data by measuring lengths using rulers marked with `text(halves)andtext(fourths of an inch)`. Show the data by making a line plot, where the horizontal scale is marked off in appropriate units - `text(whole numbers),text(halves),ortext(quarters)`.
CC.M3.MD.C: Geometric measurement: understand concepts of area and relate area to multiplication and to addition.
CC.M3.MD.C.5: Recognize area as an attribute of plane figures and understand concepts of area measurement.
CC.M3.MD.C.5.a: A square with side length`1` `text(unit)`, called “a unit square,” is said to have “one square unit” of area, and can be used to measure area.
CC.M3.MD.C.5.b: A plane figure which can be covered without gaps or overlaps by `n` `text(unit squares)` is said to have an area of `n` `text(square units)`.
CC.M3.MD.C.6: Measure areas by counting unit squares (`text(square cm),text(square m),text(square in),text(square ft)`, and improvised units).
CC.M3.MD.C.7: Relate area to the operations of multiplication and addition.
CC.M3.MD.C.7.a: Find the area of a rectangle with whole-number side lengths by tiling it, and show that the area is the same as would be found by multiplying the side lengths.
CC.M3.MD.C.7.b: Multiply side lengths to find areas of rectangles with whole-number side lengths in the context of solving real world and mathematical problems, and represent whole-number products as rectangular areas in mathematical reasoning.
CC.M3.MD.C.7.c: Use tiling to show in a concrete case that the area of a rectangle with whole-number side lengths `aandb+c` is the sum of `axxbandaxxc`. Use area models to represent the distributive property in mathematical reasoning.
CC.M3.MD.C.7.d: Recognize area as additive. Find areas of rectilinear figures by decomposing them into non-overlapping rectangles and adding the areas of the non-overlapping parts, applying this technique to solve real world problems.
CC.M3.MD.D: Geometric measurement: recognize perimeter as an attribute of plane figures and distinguish between linear and area measures.
CC.M3.MD.D.8: Solve real world and mathematical problems involving perimeters of polygons, including finding the perimeter given the side lengths, finding an unknown side length, and exhibiting rectangles with the same perimeter and different areas or with the same area and different perimeters.
CC.M3.G.A: Reason with shapes and their attributes.
CC.M3.G.A.1: Understand that shapes in different categories (e.g., rhombuses, rectangles, and others) may share attributes (e.g., having four sides), and that the shared attributes can define a larger category (e.g., quadrilaterals). Recognize rhombuses, rectangles, and squares as examples of quadrilaterals, and draw examples of quadrilaterals that do not belong to any of these subcategories.
CC.M3.G.A.2: Partition shapes into parts with equal areas. Express the area of each part as a unit fraction of the whole.
CC.E4.RL.A.1: Refer to details and examples in a text when explaining what the text says explicitly and when drawing inferences from the text.
CC.E4.RL.A.2: Determine a theme of a story, drama, or poem from details in the text; summarize the text.
CC.E4.RL.A.3: Describe in depth a character, setting, or event in a story or drama, drawing on specific details in the text (e.g., a character's thoughts, words, or actions).
CC.E4.RL.B.4: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including those that allude to significant characters found in mythology (e.g., Herculean).
CC.E4.RL.B.5: Explain major differences between poems, drama, and prose, and refer to the structural elements of poems (e.g., verse, rhythm, meter) and drama (e.g., casts of characters, settings, descriptions, dialogue, stage directions) when writing or speaking about a text.
CC.E4.RL.B.6: Compare and contrast the point of view from which different stories are narrate,d including the difference between first- and third-person narratives.
CC.E4.RL.C.7: Make connections between the text of a story or drama and a visual or oral presentation of the text, identifying where each version reflects specific descriptions and directions in the text.
CC.E4.RL.C.9: Compare and contrast the treatment of similar themes and topics (e.g., opposition of good and evil) and patterns of events (e.g., the quest) in stories, myths, and traditional literature from different cultures.
CC.E4.RL.D: Range Of Reading & Level Of Text Complexity
CC.E4.RL.D.10: By the end of the year, read and comprehend literature, including stories, dramas, and poetry, in the grades 4-5 text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.
CC.E4.RI.A.1: Refer to details and examples in a text when explaining what the text says explicitly and when drawing inferences from the text.
CC.E4.RI.A.2: Determine the main idea of a text and explain how it is supported by key details; summarize the text.
CC.E4.RI.A.3: Explain events, procedures, ideas, or concepts in a historical, scientific, or technical text, including what happened and why, based on specific information in the text.
CC.E4.RI.B.4: Determine the meaning of general academic and domain-specific words or phrases in a text relevant to a grade 4 topic or subject area.
CC.E4.RI.B.5: Describe the overall structure (e.g., chronology, comparison, cause/effect, problem/solution) of events, ideas, concepts, or information in a text or part of a text.
CC.E4.RI.B.6: Compare and contrast a firsthand and secondhand account of the same event or topic; describe the differences in focus and the information provided.
CC.E4.RI.C.7: Interpret information presented visually, orally, or quantitatively (e.g., in charts, graphs, diagrams, time lines, animations, or interactive elements on Web pages) and explain how the information contributes to an understanding of the text in which it appears.
CC.E4.RI.C.8: Explain how an author uses reasons and evidence to support particular points in a text.
CC.E4.RI.C.9: Integrate information from two texts on the same topic in order to write or speak about the subject knowledgeably.
CC.E4.RI.D: Range Of Reading & Level Of Text Complexity
CC.E4.RI.D.10: By the end of year, read and comprehend informational texts, including history/social studies, science, and technical texts, in the grades 4-5 text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.
CC.E4.RF.C.3: Know and apply grade-level phonics and word analysis skills in decoding words.
CC.E4.RF.C.3.a: Use combined knowledge of all letter-sound correspondences, syllabication patterns, and morphology (e.g., roots and affixes) to read accurately unfamiliar multisyllabic words in context and out of context.
CC.E4.RF.D.4: Read with sufficient accuracy and fluency to support comprehension.
CC.E4.RF.D.4.a: Read grade-level text with purpose and understanding.
CC.E4.RF.D.4.b: Read grade-level prose and poetry orally with accuracy, appropriate rate, and expression on successive readings.
CC.E4.RF.D.4.c: Use context to confirm or self-correct word recognition and understanding, rereading as necessary.
CC.E4.W.A.1: Write opinion pieces on topics or texts, supporting a point of view with reasons and information.
CC.E4.W.A.1.a: Introduce a topic or text clearly, state an opinion, and create an organizational structure in which related ideas are grouped to support the writer's purpose.
CC.E4.W.A.1.b: Provide reasons that are supported by facts and details.
CC.E4.W.A.1.c: Link opinion and reasons using words and phrases (e.g., for instance, in order to, in addition).
CC.E4.W.A.1.d: Provide a concluding statement or section related to the opinion presented.
CC.E4.W.A.2: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine a topic and convey ideas and information clearly.
CC.E4.W.A.2.a: Introduce a topic clearly and group related information in paragraphs and sections; include formatting (e.g., headings), illustrations, and multimedia when useful to aiding comprehension.
CC.E4.W.A.2.b: Develop the topic with facts, definitions, concrete details, quotations, or other information and examples related to the topic.
CC.E4.W.A.2.c: Link ideas within categories of information using words and phrases (e.g., another, for example, also, because).
CC.E4.W.A.2.d: Use precise language and domain-specific vocabulary to inform about or explain the topic.
CC.E4.W.A.2.e: Provide a concluding statement or section related to the information or explanation presented.
CC.E4.W.A.3: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, descriptive details, and clear event sequences.
CC.E4.W.A.3.a: Orient the reader by establishing a situation and introducing a narrator and/or characters; organize an event sequence that unfolds naturally.
CC.E4.W.A.3.b: Use dialogue and description to develop experiences and events or show the responses of characters to situations.
CC.E4.W.A.3.c: Use a variety of transitional words and phrases to manage the sequence of events.
CC.E4.W.A.3.d: Use concrete words and phrases and sensory details to convey experiences and events precisely.
CC.E4.W.A.3.e: Provide a conclusion that follows from the narrated experiences or events.
CC.E4.W.B.4: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development and organization are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.
CC.E4.W.B.5: With guidance and support from peers and adults, develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, and editing.
CC.E4.W.B.6: With some guidance and support from adults, use technology, including the Internet, to produce and publish writing as well as to interact and collaborate with others; demonstrate sufficient command of keyboarding skills to type a minimum of one page in a single sitting.
CC.E4.W.C.7: Conduct short research projects that build knowledge through investigation of different aspects of a topic.
CC.E4.W.C.8: Recall relevant information from experiences or gather relevant information from print and digital sources; take notes and categorize information, and provide a list of sources.
CC.E4.W.C.9: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.
CC.E4.W.C.9.a: Apply grade 4 Reading standards to literature (e.g., “Describe in depth a character, setting, or event in a story or drama, drawing on specific details in the text [e.g., a character's thoughts, words, or actions].”).
CC.E4.W.C.9.b: Apply grade 4 Reading standards to informational texts (e.g., “Explain how an author uses reasons and evidence to support particular points in a text”).
CC.E4.W.D.10: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of discipline-specific tasks, purposes, and audiences.
CC.E4.SL.A.1: Engage effectively in a range of collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in groups, and teacher-led) with diverse partners on grade 4 topics and texts, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly.
CC.E4.SL.A.1.a: Come to discussions prepared, having read or studied required material; explicitly draw on that preparation and other information known about the topic to explore ideas under discussion.
CC.E4.SL.A.1.b: Follow agreed-upon rules for discussions and carry out assigned roles.
CC.E4.SL.A.1.c: Pose and respond to specific questions to clarify or follow up on information, and make comments that contribute to the discussion and link to the remarks of others.
CC.E4.SL.A.1.d: Review the key ideas expressed and explain their own ideas and understanding in light of the discussion.
CC.E4.SL.A.2: Paraphrase portions of a text read aloud or information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.
CC.E4.SL.A.3: Identify the reasons and evidence a speaker provides to support particular points.
CC.E4.SL.B.4: Report on a topic or text, tell a story, or recount an experience in an organized manner, using appropriate facts and relevant, descriptive details to support main ideas or themes; speak clearly at an understandable pace.
CC.E4.SL.B.5: Add audio recordings and visual displays to presentations when appropriate to enhance the development of main ideas or themes.
CC.E4.SL.B.6: Differentiate between contexts that call for formal English (e.g., presenting ideas) and situations where informal discourse is appropriate (e.g., small-group discussion); use formal English when appropriate to task and situation. (See grade 4 Language standards 1 on page 28 for specific expectations.)
CC.E4.L.A.1: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.
CC.E4.L.A.1.a: Use relative pronouns (who, whose, whom, which, that) and relative adverbs (where, when, why).
CC.E4.L.A.1.b: Form and use the progressive (e.g., I was walking; I am walking; I will be walking) verb tenses.
CC.E4.L.A.1.c: Use modal auxiliaries (e.g., can, may, must) to convey various conditions.
CC.E4.L.A.1.d: Order adjectives within sentences according to conventional patterns (e.g., a small red bag rather than a red small bag).
CC.E4.L.A.1.f: Produce complete sentences, recognizing and correcting inappropriate fragments and run-ons.
CC.E4.L.A.1.g: Correctly use frequently confused words (e.g., to, too, two; there, their).
CC.E4.L.A.2: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.
CC.E4.L.A.2.b: Use commas and quotation marks to mark direct speech and quotations from a text.
CC.E4.L.A.2.c: Use a comma before a coordinating conjunction in a compound sentence.
CC.E4.L.A.2.d: Spell grade-appropriate words correctly, consulting references as needed.
CC.E4.L.B.3: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening.
CC.E4.L.B.3.a: Choose words and phrases to convey ideas precisely.
CC.E4.L.B.3.c: Differentiate between contexts that call for formal English (e.g., presenting ideas) and situations where informal discourse is appropriate (e.g., small-group discussion).
CC.E4.L.C.4: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grade 4 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.
CC.E4.L.C.4.a: Use context (e.g., definitions, examples, or restatements in text) as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.
CC.E4.L.C.4.b: Use common, grade-appropriate Greek and Latin affixes and roots as clues to the meaning of a word (e.g., telegraph, photograph, autograph).
CC.E4.L.C.4.c: Consult reference materials (e.g., dictionaries, glossaries, thesauruses), both print and digital, to find the pronunciation and determine or clarify the precise meaning of key words and phrases.
CC.E4.L.C.5: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.
CC.E4.L.C.5.a: Explain the meaning of simple similes and metaphors (e.g., as pretty as a picture) in context.
CC.E4.L.C.5.b: Recognize and explain the meaning of common idioms, adages, and proverbs.
CC.E4.L.C.5.c: Demonstrate understanding of words by relating them to their opposites (antonyms) and to words with similar but not identical meanings (synonyms).
CC.E4.L.C.6: Acquire and use accurately grade-appropriate general academic and domain-specific words and phrases, including those that signal precise actions, emotions, or states of being (e.g., quizzed, whined, stammered) and that are basic to a particular topic (e.g., wildlife, conservation, and endangered when discussing animal preservation).
CC.M4.OA.A: Use the four operations with whole numbers to solve problems.
CC.M4.OA.A.1: Interpret a multiplication equation as a comparison, e.g., interpret `35=5xx7` as a statement that `35` is `5` times as many as `7and7` times as many as `5`. Represent verbal statements of multiplicative comparisons as multiplication equations.
CC.M4.OA.A.2: Multiply or divide to solve word problems involving multiplicative comparison, e.g., by using drawings and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem, distinguishing multiplicative comparison from additive comparison.
CC.M4.OA.A.3: Solve multistep word problems posed with whole numbers and having whole-number answers using the four operations, including problems in which remainders must be interpreted. Represent these problems using equations with a letter standing for the unknown quantity. Assess the reasonableness of answers using mental computation and estimation strategies including rounding.
CC.M4.OA.B: Gain familiarity with factors and multiples.
CC.M4.OA.B.4: Find all factor pairs for a whole number in the range `1-100`. Recognize that a whole number is a multiple of each of its factors. Determine whether a given whole number in the range `1-100` is a multiple of a given one-digit number. Determine whether a given whole number in the range `1-100` is prime or composite.
CC.M4.OA.C.5: Generate a number or shape pattern that follows a given rule. Identify apparent features of the pattern that were not explicit in the rule itself.
CC.M4.NBT.A: Generalize place value understanding for multi-digit whole numbers.
CC.M4.NBT.A.1: Recognize that in a multi-digit whole number, a digit in one place represents ten times what it represents in the place to its right.
CC.M4.NBT.A.2: Read and write multi-digit whole numbers using base-ten numerals, number names, and expanded form. Compare two multi-digit numbers based on meanings of the digits in each place, using `>,=,and<` symbols to record the results of comparisons.
CC.M4.NBT.A.3: Use place value understanding to round multi-digit whole numbers to any place.
CC.M4.NBT.B: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to perform multi-digit arithmetic.
CC.M4.NBT.B.4: Fluently add and subtract multi-digit whole numbers using the standard algorithm.
CC.M4.NBT.B.5: Multiply a whole number of up to `text(four digits)` by a `text(one-digit whole number)`, and multiply `text(two two-digit)` numbers, using strategies based on place value and the properties of operations. Illustrate and explain the calculation by using equations, rectangular arrays, and/or area models.
CC.M4.NBT.B.6: Find whole-number quotients and remainders with up to four-digit dividends and one-digit divisors, using strategies based on place value, the properties of operations, and/or the relationship between multiplication and division. Illustrate and explain the calculation by using equations, rectangular arrays, and/or area models.
CC.M4.NF.A: Extend understanding of fraction equivalence and ordering.
CC.M4.NF.A.1: Explain why a fraction `a/b` is equivalent to a fraction `(nxxa)/(nxxb)` by using visual fraction models, with attention to how the number and size of the parts differ even though the two fractions themselves are the same size. Use this principle to recognize and generate equivalent fractions.
CC.M4.NF.A.2: Compare two fractions with different numerators and different denominators, e.g., by creating common denominators or numerators, or by comparing to a benchmark fraction such as `1/2`. Recognize that comparisons are valid only when the two fractions refer to the same whole. Record the results of comparisons with symbols `>,=,or<`, and justify the conclusions, e.g., by using a visual fraction model.
CC.M4.NF.B: Build fractions from unit fractions by applying and extending previous understandings of operations on whole numbers.
CC.M4.NF.B.3: Understand a fraction `a/b` with `a>1` as a sum of fractions `1/b`.
CC.M4.NF.B.3.a: Understand addition and subtraction of fractions as joining and separating parts referring to the same whole.
CC.M4.NF.B.3.b: Decompose a fraction into a sum of fractions with the same denominator in more than one way, recording each decomposition by an equation. Justify decompositions, e.g., by using a visual fraction model.
CC.M4.NF.B.3.c: Add and subtract mixed numbers with like denominators, e.g., by replacing each mixed number with an equivalent fraction, and/or by using properties of operations and the relationship between addition and subtraction.
CC.M4.NF.B.3.d: Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions referring to the same whole and having like denominators, e.g., by using visual fraction models and equations to represent the problem.
CC.M4.NF.B.4: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication to multiply a fraction by a whole number.
CC.M4.NF.B.4.a: Understand a fraction `a/b` as a multiple of `1/b`.
CC.M4.NF.B.4.b: Understand a multiple of `a/b` as a multiple of `1/b`, and use this understanding to multiply a fraction by a whole number.
CC.M4.NF.B.4.c: Solve word problems involving multiplication of a fraction by a whole number, e.g., by using visual fraction models and equations to represent the problem.
CC.M4.NF.C: Understand decimal notation for fractions, and compare decimal fractions.
CC.M4.NF.C.5: Express a fraction with denominator `10` as an equivalent fraction with denominator `100`, and use this technique to add two fractions with respective denominators `10and100`.
CC.M4.NF.C.6: Use decimal notation for fractions with denominators `10or100`.
CC.M4.NF.C.7: Compare two decimals to hundredths by reasoning about their size. Recognize that comparisons are valid only when the two decimals refer to the same whole. Record the results of comparisons with the symbols `>,=,or<`, and justify the conclusions, e.g., by using a visual model.
CC.M4.MD.A: Solve problems involving measurement and conversion of measurements from a larger unit to a smaller unit.
CC.M4.MD.A.1: Know relative sizes of measurement units within one system of units system of measurement, express measurements in a larger unit in terms of a smaller unit. Record measurement equivalents in a two-column table.
CC.M4.MD.A.2: Use the four operations to solve word problems involving distances, intervals of time, liquid volumes, masses of objects, and money, including problems involving simple fractions or decimals, and problems that require expressing measurements given in a larger unit in terms of a smaller unit. Represent measurement quantities using diagrams such as number line diagrams that feature a measurement scale.
CC.M4.MD.A.3: Apply the area and perimeter formulas for rectangles in real world and mathematical problems.
CC.M4.MD.B.4: Make a line plot to display a data set of measurements in fractions of a unit `(1/2,1/4,1/8)`. Solve problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions by using information presented in line plots.
CC.M4.MD.C: Geometric measurement: understand concepts of angle and measure angles.
CC.M4.MD.C.5: Recognize angles as geometric shapes that are formed wherever two rays share a common endpoint, and understand concepts of angle measurement.
CC.M4.MD.C.5.a: An angle is measured with reference to a circle with its center at the common endpoint of the rays, by considering the fraction of the circular arc between the points where the two rays intersect the circle. An angle that turns through `1/360` of a circle is called a “one-degree angle,” and can be used to measure angles.
CC.M4.MD.C.5.b: An angle that turns through `n` `text(one-degree)` angles is said to have an angle measure of `n` `text(degrees)`.
CC.M4.MD.C.6: Measure angles in whole-number degrees using a protractor. Sketch angles of specified measure.
CC.M4.MD.C.7: Recognize angle measure as additive. When an angle is decomposed into non-overlapping parts, the angle measure of the whole is the sum of the angle measures of the parts. Solve addition and subtraction problems to find unknown angles on a diagram in real world and mathematical problems, e.g., by using an equation with a symbol for the unknown angle measure.
CC.M4.G.A: Draw and identify lines and angles, and classify shapes by properties of their lines and angles.
CC.M4.G.A.1: Draw points, lines, line segments, rays, angles (right, acute, obtuse), and perpendicular and parallel lines. Identify these in two-dimensional figures.
CC.M4.G.A.2: Classify two-dimensional figures based on the presence or absence of parallel or perpendicular lines, or the presence or absence of angles of a specified size. Recognize right triangles as a category, and identify right triangles.
CC.M4.G.A.3: Recognize a line of symmetry for a two-dimensional figure as a line across the figure such that the figure can be folded along the line into matching parts. Identify line-symmetric figures and draw lines of symmetry.
CC.E5.RL.A.1: Quote accurately from a text when explaining what the text says explicitly and when drawing inferences from the text.
CC.E5.RL.A.2: Determine a theme of a story, drama, or poem from details in the text, including how characters in a story or drama respond to challenges or how the speaker in a poem reflects upon a topic; summarize the text.
CC.E5.RL.A.3: Compare and contrast two or more characters, settings, or events in a story or drama, drawing on specific details in the text (e.g., how characters interact).
CC.E5.RL.B.4: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including figurative language such as metaphors and similes.
CC.E5.RL.B.5: Explain how a series of chapters, scenes, or stanzas fits together to provide the overall structure of a particular story, drama, or poem.
CC.E5.RL.B.6: Describe how a narrator's or speaker's point of view influences how events are described.
CC.E5.RL.C.7: Analyze how visual and multimedia elements contribute to the meaning, tone, or beauty of a text (e.g., graphic novel, multimedia presentation of fiction, folktale, myth, poem).
CC.E5.RL.C.9: Compare and contrast stories in the same genre (e.g., mysteries and adventure stories) on their approaches to similar themes and topics.
CC.E5.RL.D: Range Of Reading & Level Of Text Complexity
