CO.E1.2.2.a.iv: Activate schema and background knowledge to construct meaning.
CO.E1.2.2.b.i: Ask and answer questions to help determine or clarify the meaning of words and phrases in a text.
CO.E1.2.2.b.ii: Know and use various text features (for example: headings, tables of contents, glossaries, electronic menus, icons) to locate key facts or information in a text.
CO.E1.2.2.b.iii: Distinguish between information provided by pictures or other illustrations and information provided by the words in a text.
CO.E1.2.2.c: Use Integration of Knowledge and Ideas to:
CO.E1.2.2.c.i: Use the illustrations and details in a text to describe its key ideas.
CO.E1.2.2.c.ii: Identify the reasons an author gives to support points in a text.
CO.E1.2.2.c.iii: Identify basic similarities in and differences between two texts on the same topic (for example: in illustrations, descriptions, or procedures).
CO.E1.2.2.d: Use Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity to:
CO.E1.2.2.d.i: With prompting and support, read informational texts appropriately complex for grade 1.
CO.E1.2.3: Refine foundational reading skills through understanding word structure, word relationships, and word families.
CO.E1.2.3.a: Demonstrate understanding of the organization and basic features of print.
CO.E1.2.3.a.i: Recognize the distinguishing features of a sentence (for example: first word, capitalization, ending punctuation).
CO.E1.2.3.b: Demonstrate understanding of spoken words, syllables, and sounds (phonemes).
CO.E1.2.3.b.i: Distinguish long from short vowel sounds in spoken single-syllable words.
CO.E1.2.3.b.ii: Orally produce single-syllable words by blending sounds (phonemes), including consonant blends.
CO.E1.2.3.b.iii: Isolate and pronounce initial, medial vowel, and final sounds (phonemes) in spoken single-syllable words.
CO.E1.2.3.b.iv: Segment spoken single-syllable words into their complete sequence of individual sounds (phonemes).
CO.E1.2.3.c: Know and apply grade-level phonics and word analysis skills in decoding words.
CO.E1.2.3.c.i: Know the spelling-sound correspondences for common consonant digraphs (two letters that represent one sound).
CO.E1.2.3.c.iii: Know final -e and common vowel team conventions for representing long vowel sounds.
CO.E1.2.3.c.iv: Use knowledge that every syllable must have a vowel sound to determine the number of syllables in a printed word.
CO.E1.2.3.c.v: Decode two-syllable words following basic patterns by breaking the words into syllables.
CO.E1.2.3.c.viii: Use onsets and rimes to create new words (for example: ip to make dip, lip, slip, ship).
CO.E1.2.3.c.ix: Accurately decode unknown words that follow a predictable letter/sound relationship.
CO.E1.2.3.d: Read with sufficient accuracy and fluency to support comprehension:
CO.E1.2.3.d.i: Read grade-level text with purpose and understanding.
CO.E1.2.3.d.ii: Read grade-level text orally with accuracy, appropriate rate, and expression.
CO.E1.2.3.d.iii: Use context to confirm or self-correct word recognition and understanding, rereading as necessary.
CO.E1.2.3.e: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grade 1 reading and content, choosing flexibly from an array of strategies.
CO.E1.2.3.e.i: Use sentence-level context as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.
CO.E1.2.3.e.ii: Use frequently occurring affixes as a clue to the meaning of a word.
CO.E1.2.3.e.iii: Identify frequently occurring root words (for example: look) and their inflectional forms (for example: looks, looked, looking).
CO.E1.2.3.f: With guidance and support from adults, demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships and nuances in word meanings.
CO.E1.2.3.f.i: Sort words into categories (for example: colors, clothing) to gain a sense of the concepts the categories represent.
CO.E1.2.3.f.ii: Define words by category and by one or more key attributes (for example: a duck is a bird that swims; a tiger is a large cat with stripes).
CO.E1.2.3.f.iii: Identify real-life connections between words and their use (for example: note places at home that are cozy).
CO.E1.2.3.f.iv: Distinguish shades of meaning among verbs differing in manner (for example: look, peek, glance, stare, glare, scowl) and adjectives differing in intensity (for example: large, gigantic) by defining or choosing them or by acting out the meanings.
CO.E1.2.3.g: Use words and phrases acquired through conversations, reading and being read to, and responding to texts, including using frequently occurring conjunctions to signal simple relationships (for example: because).
CO.E1.3.1: Write an opinion supported by reasons.
CO.E1.3.1.a: Introduce the topic or name the book they are writing about.
CO.E1.3.1.c: Supply a reason for the opinion.
CO.E1.3.2: Write informative/explanatory texts by naming a topic, providing related details, and giving the audience a sense of closure.
CO.E1.3.2.b: Supply some facts about the topic.
CO.E1.3.3: Recount real or imagined, sequenced events that include details and a sense of closure.
CO.E1.3.3.a: Recount two or more appropriately sequenced events.
CO.E1.3.3.b: Include some details regarding what happened.
CO.E1.3.4: Use appropriate grammar, spelling, capitalization, and punctuation.
CO.E1.3.4.a: Demonstrate command of the conventions of Standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.
CO.E1.3.4.a.i: Print all upper- and lowercase letters.
CO.E1.3.4.a.ii: Use common, proper, and possessive nouns.
CO.E1.3.4.a.iii: Use singular and plural nouns with matching verbs in basic sentences (for example: He hops; We hop).
CO.E1.3.4.a.iv: Use personal, possessive, and indefinite pronouns (for example: I, me, my; they, them, their, anyone, everything).
CO.E1.3.4.a.v: Use verbs to convey a sense of past, present, and future (for example: Yesterday I walked home; Today I walk home; Tomorrow I will walk home).
CO.E1.3.4.a.vii: Use frequently occurring conjunctions (for example: and, but, or, so, because).
CO.E1.3.4.a.ix: Use frequently occurring prepositions (for example: during, beyond, toward).
CO.E1.3.4.a.x: Produce and expand complete simple and compound declarative, interrogative, imperative, and exclamatory sentences in response to prompts.
CO.E1.3.4.b: Demonstrate command of the conventions of Standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.
CO.E1.3.4.b.ii: Capitalize dates and names of people.
CO.E1.3.4.b.iv: Use commas in dates and to separate single words in a series.
CO.E1.3.4.b.v: Use conventional spelling for words with common spelling patterns and for frequently occurring irregular words.
CO.E1.3.4.b.vi: Spell untaught words phonetically, drawing on phonemic awareness and spelling conventions.
CO.E1.3.4.c: With guidance and support from adults, focus on a topic, respond to questions and suggestions from peers, and add details to strengthen writing as needed.
CO.E1.3.4.d: With guidance and support from adults, use a variety of digital tools to produce and publish writing, including in collaboration with peers.
CO.E1.4.1: Participate in shared research and inquiry projects, writing, recalling, or gathering information to answer questions.
CO.E1.4.1.a: Participate in shared research and writing projects. For example: explore a number of “how-to” books on a given topic and use them to write a sequence of instructions.
CO.E1.4.1.b: Write or dictate questions for inquiry that arise during instruction.
CO.E1.4.1.c: With peers, use a variety of resources (for example: direct observation, trade books, texts read aloud or viewed) to answer questions of interest through guided inquiry.
CO.E1.4.1.d: Use text features (for example: titles, illustrations, headings, bold type) to locate, interpret, and use information.
CO.E1.4.1.e: Identify a clear and significant purpose for research.
CO.E1.4.1.f: With guidance and support from adults, recall information from `experiences or gather information from provided sources to answer a question.
CO.M1.NBT.A.1: Count to 120, starting at any number less than 120. In this range, read and write numerals and represent a number of objects with a written numeral.
CO.M1.NBT.B.2: Understand that the two digits of a two-digit number represent amounts of tens and ones. Understand the following as special cases:
CO.M1.NBT.B.2.a: 10 can be thought of as a bundle of ten ones - called a “ten.”
CO.M1.NBT.B.2.b: The numbers from 11 to 19 are composed of a ten and one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine ones.
CO.M1.NBT.B.2.c: The numbers 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90 refer to one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine tens (and 0 ones).
CO.M1.NBT.B.3: Compare two two-digit numbers based on meanings of the tens and ones digits, recording the results of comparisons with the symbols `>,=,and<`.
CO.M1.NBT.C: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to add and subtract.
CO.M1.NBT.C.4: Add within `100`, including adding a two-digit number and a one-digit number, and adding a two-digit number and a multiple of 10, using concrete models or drawings and strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction; relate the strategy to a written method and explain the reasoning used. Understand that in adding two-digit numbers, one adds tens and tens, ones and ones; and sometimes it is necessary to compose a ten.
CO.M1.NBT.C.5: Given a two-digit number, mentally find 10 more or 10 less than the number, without having to count; explain the reasoning used.
CO.M1.NBT.C.6: Subtract multiples of `10` in the range `10-90` from multiples of `10` in the range `10-90` (positive or zero differences), using concrete models or drawings and strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction; relate the strategy to a written method and explain the reasoning used.
CO.M1.OA.A: Represent and solve problems involving addition and subtraction.
CO.M1.OA.A.1: Use addition and subtraction within 20 to solve word problems involving situations of adding to, taking from, putting together, taking apart, and comparing, with unknowns in all positions, e.g., by using objects, drawings, and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.
CO.M1.OA.A.2: Solve word problems that call for addition of three whole numbers whose sum is less than or equal to 20, e.g., by using objects, drawings, and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.
CO.M1.OA.B: Understand and apply properties of operations and the relationship between addition and subtraction.
CO.M1.OA.B.3: Apply properties of operations as strategies to add and subtract.
CO.M1.OA.B.4: Understand subtraction as an unknown-addend problem.
CO.M1.OA.C.5: Relate counting to addition and subtraction (e.g., by counting on 2 to add 2).
CO.M1.OA.C.6: Add and subtract within 20, demonstrating fluency for addition and subtraction within 10. Use strategies such as counting on; making ten (e.g., 8 + 6 = 8 + 2 + 4 = 10 + 4 = 14); decomposing a number leading to a ten (e.g., 13- 4 = 13- 3- 1 = 10- 1 = 9); using the relationship between addition and subtraction (e.g., knowing that 8 + 4 = 12, one knows 12- 8 = 4); and creating equivalent but easier or known sums (e.g., adding 6 + 7 by creating the known equivalent 6 + 6 + 1 = 12 + 1 = 13).
CO.M1.OA.D: Work with addition and subtraction equations.
CO.M1.OA.D.7: Understand the meaning of the equal sign, and determine if equations involving addition and subtraction are true or false.
CO.M1.OA.D.8: Determine the unknown whole number in an addition or subtraction equation relating three whole numbers.
CO.M1.MD.A: Measure lengths indirectly and by iterating length units.
CO.M1.MD.A.1: Order three objects by length; compare the lengths of two objects indirectly by using a third object.
CO.M1.MD.A.2: Express the length of an object as a whole number of length units, by laying multiple copies of a shorter object (the length unit) end to end; understand that the length measurement of an object is the number of same-size length units that span it with no gaps or overlaps.
CO.M1.MD.B.3: Tell and write time in `text(hours)` and half-hours using analog and digital clocks.
CO.M1.MD.C.4: Organize, represent, and interpret data with up to three categories; ask and answer questions about the total number of data points, how many in each category, and how many more or less are in one category than in another.
CO.M1.G.A: Reason with shapes and their attributes.
CO.M1.G.A.1: Distinguish between defining attributes (e.g., triangles are closed and three-sided) versus non-defining attributes (e.g., color, orientation, overall size); build and draw shapes to possess defining attributes.
CO.M1.G.A.2: Compose two-dimensional shapes (rectangles, squares, trapezoids, triangles, half-circles, and quarter-circles) or three-dimensional shapes (cubes, right rectangular prisms, right circular cones, and right circular cylinders) to create a composite shape, and compose new shapes from the composite shape.
CO.M1.G.A.3: Partition circles and rectangles into two and four equal shares, describe the shares using the words halves, fourths, and quarters, and use the phrases half of, fourth of, and quarter of. Describe the whole as two of, or four of the shares. Understand for these examples that decomposing into more equal shares creates smaller shares.
CO.S1.1.1: Sound can make matter vibrate and vibrating matter can make sound.
CO.S1.1.1.a: Plan and conduct investigations to provide evidence that vibrating materials can make a sound and that sound can make materials vibrate.
CO.S1.1.1.b: Make observations to construct an evidence-based account that objects can be seen only when illuminated.
CO.S1.1.1.c: Plan and conduct an investigation to determine the effect of placing objects made with different materials in the path of a beam of light.
CO.S1.1.1.d: Use tools and materials to design and build a device that used light or sound to solve the problem of communicating over a distance.
CO.S1.2.1: All organisms have external parts that they use to perform daily functions.
CO.S1.2.1.a: Use materials to design a solution to a human problem by mimicking how plants and/or animals use their external parts to help them survive, grow and meet their needs.
CO.S1.2.1.b: Read texts and use media to determine patterns in behavior of parents and offspring that help offspring survive.
CO.S1.2.2: Young organisms are very much, but not exactly, like their parents, and also resemble other organisms of the same kind.
CO.S1.2.2.a: Make observations to construct an evidence-based account that young plants and animals are like, but not exactly like, their parents.
CO.S1.3.1: Patterns of movement of the sun, moon and stars as seen from Earth can be observed, described and predicted.
CO.S1.3.1.a: Use observations of the sun, moon, and stars to describe patterns that can be predicted.
CO.S1.3.1.b: Make observations at different times of year to relate the amount of daylight to the time of year.
CO.SS1.1.1: Ask questions and discuss ideas about patterns and chronological order of events from the past.
CO.SS1.1.1.a: Arrange life events in chronological order.
CO.SS1.1.1.b: Use words related to time, sequence, and change.
CO.SS1.1.1.c: Identify the organizational components of a calendar.
CO.SS1.1.1.d: Determine events from the past, present, and future, using the components of a calendar.
CO.SS1.1.1.e: Distinguish between primary and secondary sources.
CO.SS1.1.1.f: Identify information from primary and/or secondary sources that answer questions about patterns and chronological order of events from the past.
CO.SS1.1.2: Explain how the diverse perspectives and traditions of families from many cultures have shaped the United States.
CO.SS1.1.2.a: Identify the unique characteristics of oneself as well as the similarities and differences between themselves and others.
CO.SS1.1.2.b: Discuss common and unique characteristics of different cultures, including African American, Latino, Asian American, Hawaiian/Pacific Islanders, Indigenous Peoples, LGBTQ, and religious minorities, using multiple sources of information.
CO.SS1.1.2.c: Understand that the United States is made up of the diverse perspectives and traditions of many cultures.
CO.SS1.2.1: Use geographic terms and tools to describe places and spaces.
CO.SS1.2.1.a: Explain that maps and globes are different representations of Earth.
CO.SS1.2.1.b: Describe locations using terms related to direction and distance.
CO.SS1.2.1.c: Recite an address including city, state, and country, and explain how those labels help find places on a map.
CO.SS1.2.1.d: Distinguish between land and water on a map and globe.
CO.SS1.2.1.e: Create simple maps showing both human and natural features.
CO.SS1.2.2: Describe the characteristics of a community and how they are influenced by the environment.
CO.SS1.2.2.a: Provide examples of how individuals and families interact with their environment.
CO.SS1.2.2.b: Analyze how weather, climate and environmental characteristics influence individuals and the cultural characteristics of a family.
CO.SS1.2.2.c: Compare and contrast at least two different communities with respect to schools, neighborhoods, and culture.
CO.SS1.3.1: Understand that individuals work in different types of jobs to earn an income.
CO.SS1.3.1.a: Identify the goods and/or services that different types of businesses produce in the local community.
CO.SS1.3.1.b: Give examples of different types of jobs held by family members and/or individuals in the local community.
CO.SS1.3.1.c: Compare at least two different job choices that individuals have with respect to the benefits and costs of each job.
CO.SS1.4.1: Summarize how effective groups have responsible leaders and team members.
CO.SS1.4.1.a: Describe the characteristics of responsible leaders and how they communicate with others.
CO.SS1.4.1.b: Identify the attributes of a responsible team member and how they communicate with others.
CO.SS1.4.1.c: Demonstrate the ability to be both a leader and team member.
CO.SS1.4.1.d: Describe the qualities of an effective team.
CO.SS1.4.1.e: Listen and consider the ideas of others in order to make decisions as a group.
CO.SS1.4.2: Identify and explain how the significance of notable people, places, holidays, and civic symbols reflect the origins and values of the government and its citizens.
CO.SS1.4.2.a: Identify and explain the relevance of notable civic leaders from different community groups, including African American, Latino, Asian American, Hawaiian/Pacific Islander, Indigenous Peoples, LGBTQ, and religious minorities.
CO.SS1.4.2.b: Identify and explain the meaning of various civic symbols important to diverse community groups.
CO.SS1.4.2.c: Identify and explain the relevance of significant civic places.
CO.SS1.4.2.d: Explain the significance of major civic holidays.
CO.SS1.5.1: Plan how to spend, share, and save money.
CO.SS1.5.1.a: Discuss ways to earn or receive money.
CO.SS1.5.1.b: Identify types of currency and how currency is used.
CO.SS1.5.1.c: Define types of transactions such as deposit, purchase, borrow, donate, and barter.
CO.SS1.5.1.d: Find the value of a collection of a variety of coins.
CO.E2.1.1: Engage in dialogue and learn new information through active listening.
CO.E2.1.1.a: Participate in collaborative conversations with diverse partners about grade 2 topics and texts with peers and adults in small and larger groups.
CO.E2.1.1.a.i: Follow agreed-upon rules for discussions (for example: gaining the floor in respectful ways, listening to others with care, speaking one at a time about the topics and texts under discussion).
CO.E2.1.1.a.ii: Build on others' talk in conversations by linking their comments to the remarks of others.
CO.E2.1.1.a.iii: Ask for clarification and further explanation as needed about the topics and texts under discussion.
CO.E2.1.1.b: Recount or describe key ideas or details from a text read aloud or information presented orally or through other media.
CO.E2.1.1.c: Ask and answer questions about what a speaker says in order to clarify comprehension, gather additional information, or deepen understanding of a topic or issue.
CO.E2.1.2: Deliver presentations while maintaining focus on topic and be prepared to discuss.
CO.E2.1.2.a: Tell a story or recount an experience with appropriate facts and relevant, descriptive details, speaking audibly in coherent sentences.
CO.E2.1.2.b: Contribute knowledge to a small group or class discussion to develop a topic.
CO.E2.1.2.d: Create audio recordings of stories or poems; add drawings or other visual displays to stories or recounts of experiences when appropriate to clarify ideas, thoughts, and feelings.
CO.E2.1.2.e: Produce complete sentences when appropriate to task and situation in order to provide requested detail or clarification.
CO.E2.1.2.f: Use content-specific vocabulary to ask questions and provide information.
CO.E2.2.1: Apply specific skills to comprehend and fluently read literary texts.
CO.E2.2.1.a: Use Key Ideas and Details to:
CO.E2.2.1.a.i: Demonstrate use of self-monitoring comprehension strategies: rereading, checking context clues, predicting, questioning, clarifying, activating schema/background knowledge to construct meaning and draw inferences.
CO.E2.2.1.a.ii: Ask and answer such questions as who, what, where, when, why, and how to demonstrate understanding of key details in a text.
CO.E2.2.1.a.iii: Recount stories, including fables and folktales from diverse cultures, and determine their central message, lesson, or moral.
CO.E2.2.1.a.iv: Describe how characters in a story respond to major events and challenges.
CO.E2.2.1.b.i: Describe how words and phrases (for example: regular beats, alliteration, rhymes, repeated lines) supply rhythm and meaning in a story, poem, or song.
CO.E2.2.1.b.ii: Describe the overall structure of a story, including describing how the beginning introduces the story and the ending concludes the action.
CO.E2.2.1.b.iii: Acknowledge differences in the points of view of characters, including by speaking in a different voice for each character when reading dialogue aloud.
CO.E2.2.1.b.iv: Identify how word choice (for example: sensory details, figurative language) enhances meaning in poetry.
CO.E2.2.1.c: Use Integration of Knowledge and Ideas to:
CO.E2.2.1.c.i: Use information gained from the illustrations and words in a print or digital text to demonstrate understanding of its characters, setting, or plot.
CO.E2.2.1.c.ii: Compare and contrast two or more versions of the same story (for example: Cinderella stories) by different authors or from different cultures.
CO.E2.2.1.d: Use Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity to:
CO.E2.2.1.d.i: By the end of the year, read and comprehend literature, including stories and poetry, in the grades 2-3 text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.
CO.E2.2.2: Apply specific skills to comprehend and fluently read informational texts.
CO.E2.2.2.a: Use Key Ideas and Details to:
CO.E2.2.2.a.i: Ask and answer such questions as who, what, where, when, why, and how to demonstrate understanding of key details in a text.
CO.E2.2.2.a.ii: Identify the main topic of a multiparagraph text as well as the focus of specific paragraphs within the text.
CO.E2.2.2.a.iii: Summarize the main idea using relevant and significant details in a variety of texts.
CO.E2.2.2.a.iv: Describe the connection between a series of historical events, scientific ideas or concepts, or steps in technical procedures in a text.
CO.E2.2.2.b.i: Determine the meaning of words and phrases in a text relevant to a grade 2 topic or subject area.
CO.E2.2.2.b.ii: Know and use various text features (for example: captions, bold print, subheadings, glossaries, indexes, electronic menus, icons) to locate key facts or information in a text efficiently.
CO.E2.2.2.b.iii: Identify the main purpose of a text, including what the author wants to answer, explain, or describe.
CO.E2.2.2.b.iv: Read text to perform a specific task such as follow a recipe or play a game.
CO.E2.2.2.c: Use Integration of Knowledge and Ideas to:
CO.E2.2.2.c.i: Explain how specific images (for example: a diagram showing how a machine works) contribute to and clarify a text.
CO.E2.2.2.c.ii: Describe how reasons support specific points the author makes in a text.
CO.E2.2.2.c.iii: Compare and contrast the most important points presented by two texts on the same topic.
CO.E2.2.2.d: Use Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity to:
CO.E2.2.2.d.i: Adjust reading rate according to type of text and purpose for reading.
CO.E2.2.2.d.ii: By the end of year, read and comprehend informational texts, including history/social studies, science, and technical texts, in the grades 2-3 text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.
CO.E2.2.3: Apply knowledge of complex spelling patterns (orthography) and word meanings (morphology) to decode words with accuracy.
CO.E2.2.3.a: Know and apply grade-level phonics and word analysis skills in decoding words.
CO.E2.2.3.a.i: Distinguish long and short vowels when reading regularly spelled one- syllable words.
CO.E2.2.3.a.ii: Know spelling-sound correspondences for additional common vowel teams.
CO.E2.2.3.a.iii: Read multisyllabic words accurately and fluently.
CO.E2.2.3.a.iv: Decode regularly spelled two-syllable words with long vowels.
CO.E2.2.3.a.v: Decode words with common prefixes and suffixes.
CO.E2.2.3.a.vi: Identify words with inconsistent but common spelling-sound correspondences.
CO.E2.2.3.b: Read with sufficient accuracy and fluency to support comprehension.
CO.E2.2.3.b.i: Read grade-level text with purpose and understanding.
CO.E2.2.3.b.ii: Read grade-level text orally with accuracy, appropriate rate, and expression.
CO.E2.2.3.b.iii: Use context to confirm or self-correct word recognition and understanding, rereading as necessary.
CO.E2.2.3.b.iv: Read grade-level text accurately and fluently, attending to phrasing, intonation, and punctuation.
CO.E2.2.3.c: Compare formal and informal uses of English.
CO.E2.2.3.d: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grade 2 reading and content, choosing flexibly from an array of strategies.
CO.E2.2.3.d.i: Use sentence-level context as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.
CO.E2.2.3.d.ii: Determine the meaning of the new word formed when a known prefix is added to a known word (for example: happy/unhappy, tell/retell).
CO.E2.2.3.d.iii: Use a known root word as a clue to the meaning of an unknown word with the same root (for example: addition, additional).
CO.E2.2.3.d.iv: Use knowledge of the meaning of individual words to predict the meaning of compound words (for example: birdhouse, lighthouse, housefly; bookshelf, notebook, bookmark).
CO.E2.2.3.d.v: Create new words by combining base words with affixes to connect known words to new words.
CO.E2.2.3.d.vi: Use glossaries and beginning dictionaries, both print and digital, to determine or clarify the meaning of words and phrases.
CO.E2.2.3.e: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships and nuances in word meanings.
CO.E2.2.3.e.i: Identify real-life connections between words and their use (for example: describe foods that are spicy or juicy).
CO.E2.2.3.e.ii: Distinguish shades of meaning among closely related verbs (for example: toss, throw, hurl) and closely related adjectives (for example: thin, slender, skinny, scrawny).
CO.E2.2.3.f: Use words and phrases acquired through conversations, reading and being read to, and responding to texts, including using adjectives and adverbs to describe (for example: When other kids are happy that makes me happy).
CO.E2.2.3.g: Determine which strategies should be used to decode multisyllabic words.
CO.E2.3.1: Write pieces on a topic or book that state opinions and give supporting reasons.
CO.E2.3.1.a: Introduce the topic or book they are writing about.
CO.E2.3.1.c: Supply reasons that support the opinion.
CO.E2.3.1.d: Use linking words (for example: because, and, also) to connect opinion and reasons.
CO.E2.3.1.e: Provide a concluding statement or section.
CO.E2.3.2: Write informative/explanatory texts organized around main ideas which are supported by relevant details, facts, and definitions.
CO.E2.3.2.b: Use facts and definitions to develop points, including relevant details when writing to questions about texts.
CO.E2.3.2.c: Provide a concluding statement or section.
CO.E2.3.2.d: Write letters and “how-to's” (for example: procedures, directions, recipes) that follow a logical order and appropriate format.
CO.E2.3.2.e: Organize informational texts using main ideas and specific supporting details.
CO.E2.3.2.f: Apply appropriate transition words to writing.
CO.E2.3.2.g: Writers use technology to support the writing process.
CO.E2.3.3: Write real or imagined narratives that describe events in sequence and provide a sense of closure.
CO.E2.3.3.a: Include details to describe actions, thoughts, and feelings.
CO.E2.3.3.b: Use temporal words to signal event order.
CO.E2.3.3.e: Write with precise nouns, active verbs, and descriptive adjectives.
CO.E2.3.3.f: Apply knowledge about structure and craft gained from mentor text to narrative writing.
CO.E2.3.3.g: Develop characters both internally (thoughts and feelings) and externally (physical features, expressions, clothing).
CO.E2.3.4: Use a process to revise and edit so that thoughts and ideas are communicated clearly with appropriate spelling, capitalization, grammar, and punctuation.
CO.E2.3.4.a: Demonstrate command of the conventions of Standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.
CO.E2.3.4.a.ii: Use reflexive pronouns (for example: myself, ourselves).
CO.E2.3.4.a.iii: Form and use the past tense of frequently occurring irregular verbs (for example: sat, hid, told).
CO.E2.3.4.a.iv: Use adjectives and adverbs, and choose between them depending on what is to be modified.
CO.E2.3.4.a.v: Apply accurate subject-verb agreement while writing.
CO.E2.3.4.a.vi: Produce, expand, and rearrange complete simple and compound sentences (for example: The boy watched the movie; The little boy watched the movie; The action movie was watched by the little boy).
CO.E2.3.4.b: Demonstrate command of the conventions of Standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.
CO.E2.3.4.b.i: Capitalize holidays, product names, and geographic names.
CO.E2.3.4.b.ii: Use commas in greetings and closings of letters.
CO.E2.3.4.b.iii: Use an apostrophe to form contractions and frequently occurring possessives.
CO.E2.3.4.b.iv: Generalize learned spelling patterns when writing words (for example: cage → badge; boy → boil).
CO.E2.3.4.b.v: Consult reference materials, including beginning dictionaries, as needed to check and correct spellings.
CO.E2.3.4.c: With guidance and support from adults and peers, focus on a topic and strengthen writing as needed by revising and editing.
CO.E2.3.4.d: With guidance and support from adults, use a variety of digital tools to produce and publish writing, including in collaboration with peers.
CO.E2.4.1: Participate in shared research and inquiry, gathering information from a variety of resources to answer questions.
CO.E2.4.1.a: Participate in shared research and writing projects. For example: read a number of books on a single topic to produce a report; record science observations.
CO.E2.4.1.b: Identify a variety of resources and the information they might contain (for example: dictionary, trade book, library databases, internet web page).
CO.E2.4.1.c: Identify a specific question and gather information for purposeful investigation and inquiry.
CO.E2.4.1.d: Use text features to locate and interpret information. For example: table of contents, illustrations, diagrams, headings and bold type.
CO.E2.4.1.e: Use a variety of multimedia sources to answer questions of interest.
CO.E2.4.1.f: Ask primary questions of depth and breadth.
CO.E2.4.1.g: Recall information from experiences or gather information from provided sources to answer a question.
CO.M2.NBT.A: Understand that the three digits of a three-digit number represent amounts of hundreds, tens, and ones; e.g., 706 equals 7 hundreds, 0 tens, and 6 ones. Understand the following as special cases:
CO.M2.NBT.A.1.a: 100 can be thought of as a bundle of ten tens - called a “hundred.”
CO.M2.NBT.A.1.b: The numbers 100, 200, 300, 400, 500, 600, 700, 800, 900 refer to one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine hundreds (and 0 tens and 0 ones).
CO.M2.NBT.A.3: Read and write numbers to `1000` using base-ten numerals, number names, and expanded form.
CO.M2.NBT.A.4: Compare two three-digit numbers based on meanings of the hundreds, tens, and ones digits, using `>,=,and<` symbols to record the results of comparison.
CO.M2.NBT.B: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to add and subtract.
CO.M2.NBT.B.5: Fluently add and subtract within `100` using strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction.
CO.M2.NBT.B.6: Add up to four two-digit numbers using strategies based on place value and properties of operations.
CO.M2.NBT.B.7: Add and subtract within `1000`, using concrete models or drawings and strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction; relate the strategy to a written method. Understand that in adding or subtracting three-digit numbers, one adds or subtracts hundreds and hundreds, tens and tens, ones and ones; and sometimes it is necessary to compose or decompose tens or hundreds.
CO.M2.NBT.B.8: Mentally add `10or100` to a given number 100-900, and mentally subtract `10or100` from a given number 100-900.
CO.M2.NBT.B.9: Explain why addition and subtraction strategies work, using place value and the properties of operations.
CO.M2.OA.A: Represent and solve problems involving addition and subtraction.
CO.M2.OA.A.1: Use addition and subtraction within `100` to solve one- and two-step word problems involving situations of adding to, taking from, putting together, taking apart, and comparing, with unknowns in all positions, e.g., by using drawings and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.
CO.M2.OA.B.2: Fluently add and subtract within 20 using mental strategies. By end of Grade 2, know from memory all sums of two one-digit numbers.
CO.M2.OA.C: Work with equal groups of objects to gain foundations for multiplication.
CO.M2.OA.C.3: Determine whether a group of objects (up to 20) has an odd or even number of members, e.g., by pairing objects or counting them by `2text(s)`; write an equation to express an even number as a sum of two equal addends.
CO.M2.OA.C.4: Use addition to find the total number of objects arranged in rectangular arrays with up to `5` rows and up to `5` columns; write an equation to express the total as a sum of equal addends.
CO.M2.MD.A: Measure and estimate lengths in standard units.
CO.M2.MD.A.1: Measure the length of an object by selecting and using appropriate tools such as rulers, yardsticks, meter sticks, and measuring tapes.
CO.M2.MD.A.2: Measure the length of an object twice, using length units of different lengths for the two measurements; describe how the two measurements relate to the size of the unit chosen.
CO.M2.MD.A.3: Estimate lengths using units of inches, feet, centimeters, and meters.
CO.M2.MD.A.4: Measure to determine how much longer one object is than another, expressing the length difference in terms of a standard length unit.
CO.M2.MD.B: Relate addition and subtraction to length.
CO.M2.MD.B.5: Use addition and subtraction within `100` to solve word problems involving lengths that are given in the same units, e.g., by using drawings (such as drawings of rulers) and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.
CO.M2.MD.B.6: Represent whole numbers as lengths from `0` on a number line diagram with equally spaced points corresponding to the numbers 0,1,2, ..., and represent whole-number sums and differences within `100` on a number line diagram.
CO.M2.MD.C.7: Tell and write time from analog and digital clocks to the nearest five minutes, using a.m. and p.m.
CO.M2.MD.C.8: Solve word problems involving dollar bills, quarters, dimes, nickels, and pennies, using $ and ¢ symbols appropriately.
CO.M2.MD.D.9: Generate measurement data by measuring lengths of several objects to the nearest whole unit, or by making repeated measurements of the same object. Show the measurements by making a line plot, where the horizontal scale is marked off in whole-number units.
CO.M2.MD.D.10: Draw a picture graph and a bar graph (with single-unit scale) to represent a data set with up to four categories. Solve simple put-together, take-apart, and compare problems (see Appendix, Table 1) using information presented in a bar graph.
CO.M2.G.A: Reason with shapes and their attributes.
CO.M2.G.A.1: Recognize and draw shapes having specified attributes, such as a given number of angles or a given number of equal faces. (Sizes are compared directly or visually, not compared by measuring.) Identify triangles, quadrilaterals, pentagons, hexagons, and cubes.
CO.M2.G.A.2: Partition a rectangle into rows and columns of same-size squares and count to find the total number of them.
CO.M2.G.A.3: Partition circles and rectangles into two, three, or four equal shares, describe the shares using the words halves, thirds, half of, a third of, etc., and describe the whole as two halves, three thirds, four fourths. Recognize that equal shares of identical wholes need not have the same shape.
CO.S2.1.1: Matter exists as different substances that have observable different properties.
CO.S2.1.1.a: Plan and conduct an investigation to describe and classify different kinds of materials by their observable properties.
CO.S2.1.1.b: Analyze data obtained from testing different materials to determine which materials have the properties that are best suited for an intended purpose.
CO.S2.1.1.c: Make observations to construct an evidence-based account of how an object made of a small set of pieces can be disassembled and made into a new object.
CO.S2.1.1.d: Construct an argument with evidence that some changes caused by heating or cooling can be reversed and some cannot.
CO.S2.2.1: Plants depend on water and light to grow and on animals for pollination or to move their seeds around.
CO.S2.2.1.a: Plan and conduct an investigation to determine if plants need sunlight and water to grow.
CO.S2.2.1.b: Develop a simple model that mimics the function of an animal in dispersing seeds or pollinating plants.
CO.S2.2.2: A range of different organisms lives in different places.
CO.S2.2.2.a: Make observations of plants and animals to compare the diversity of life in different habitats.
CO.S2.3.1: Some events on Earth occur quickly; others can occur very slowly.
CO.S2.3.1.a: Use information from several sources to provide evidence that Earth events can occur quickly or slowly.
CO.S2.3.2: Wind and water can change the shape of the land; models can show the shape and these changes to the land.
CO.S2.3.2.a: Compare multiple solutions designed to slow or prevent wind or water from changing the shape of the land.
CO.S2.3.2.b: Develop a model to represent the shapes and kinds of land and bodies of water in an area.
CO.S2.3.2.c: Obtain information to identify where water is found on Earth and that it can be solid or liquid.
CO.SS2.1.1: Ask questions and discuss ideas taken from primary and secondary sources.
CO.SS2.1.1.a: Explain that the nature of history involves stories of the past preserved in various primary and secondary sources.
CO.SS2.1.1.b: Organize historical events by creating timelines and explaining the information conveyed by them.
CO.SS2.1.1.c: Identify local historical primary and secondary sources from multiple diverse perspectives and generate questions about their functions, significance, and perspective.
CO.SS2.1.2: Describe how people of various cultures influence neighborhoods and communities over time.
CO.SS2.1.2.a: Compare and contrast neighborhoods and/or communities, both past and present, through studies of their people and events.
CO.SS2.1.2.b: Describe the changes within one neighborhood and/or community over time.
CO.SS2.1.2.c: Analyze the interactions and contributions of various people and cultures that have lived in or migrated to neighborhoods and/or communities, including African Americans, Latinos, Asian Americans, Hawaiian/Pacific Islander, Indigenous Peoples, LGBTQ, and religious minorities.
CO.SS2.2.1: Use geographic terms and tools to locate and describe spatial patterns and places.
CO.SS2.2.1.a: Use map keys, legends, symbols, intermediate directions, and a compass rose to locate and describe spaces and places.
CO.SS2.2.1.b: Identify the purpose of the map being presented.
CO.SS2.2.1.c: Identify the hemispheres, Equator/Prime Meridian, and the North/South poles.
CO.SS2.2.1.d: Identify and locate cultural, human, political, and natural features using map keys and legends.
CO.SS2.2.2: Explain how people in communities manage, modify, and depend on their environment.
CO.SS2.2.2.a: Explain how communities manage and use nonrenewable and renewable resources.
CO.SS2.2.2.b: Explain how the environment influences why people settle in certain areas.
CO.SS2.2.2.c: Identify examples of how human activity influences environmental characteristics of a place over time.
CO.SS2.2.2.d: Identify examples of how culture and lifestyle are impacted by environmental characteristics.
CO.SS2.3.1: Explain how scarcity of resources means individuals may not have access to the goods and services they want or need.
CO.SS2.3.1.a: Explain scarcity of goods and resources.
CO.SS2.3.1.b: Identify and categorize goods and services and provide examples of each.
CO.SS2.3.1.c: Give examples of choices people make when resources are scarce.
CO.SS2.3.1.d: Identify possible solutions when there are limited resources and unlimited wants.
CO.SS2.4.1: Investigate ways in which ideas and actions can improve communities.
CO.SS2.4.1.a: Compare ways that people may effectively express their ideas and viewpoints while being respectful to others.
CO.SS2.4.1.b: Analyze how community members, including African American, Latino, Asian American, Hawaiian/Pacific Islander, Indigenous Peoples, LGBTQ, and religious minorities advocate for their interests and responsibly influence decisions in their community.
CO.SS2.4.1.c: Describe ways in which you can take an active part in improving your school or community.
CO.SS2.4.1.d: Identify and compare examples of civic responsibilities, such as volunteering in the community, that are important to privileged and marginalized individuals, families, and communities.
CO.SS2.4.1.e: Describe the characteristics that enable a community member to engage in the community responsibly and effectively.
CO.SS2.4.2: Explain the roles and characteristics of people who govern different communities.
CO.SS2.4.2.b: Identify the roles and characteristics of various leaders at the local, state, and national levels.
CO.SS2.4.2.c: Identify qualities of positive leadership and how leaders contribute to a group or community.
CO.SS2.4.2.d: Identify services provided by the local or state government.
CO.SS2.5.1: Investigate costs and benefits to make informed financial decisions.
CO.SS2.5.1.a: Assess priorities when making financial decisions.
CO.SS2.5.1.c: Recognize that different goods and services have different monetary values.
CO.SS2.5.1.d: Acknowledge that financial priorities vary among people and communities for goods and services.
CO.SS2.5.1.e: Predict positive and negative consequences when making financial decisions.
CO.SS2.5.1.f: Solve simple financial word problems to aid in making financial decisions.
CO.E3.1.1.a: Engage effectively in a range of collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in groups, and teacher-led) with diverse partners on grade 3 topics and texts, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly.
CO.E3.1.1.a.i: Come to discussions prepared, having read or studied required material; explicitly draw on that preparation and other information known about the topic to explore ideas under discussion.
CO.E3.1.1.a.ii: Follow agreed-upon rules for discussions (for example: gaining the floor in respectful ways, listening to others with care, speaking one at a time about the topics and texts under discussion).
CO.E3.1.1.a.iii: Ask questions to check understanding of information presented, stay on topic, and link their comments to the remarks of others.
CO.E3.1.1.a.iv: Explain their own ideas and understanding in light of the discussion.
CO.E3.1.1.b: Determine the main ideas and supporting details of a text read aloud or information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.
CO.E3.1.1.c: Ask and answer questions about information from a speaker, offering appropriate elaboration and detail.
CO.E3.1.2: Communicate using appropriate language in informal and formal situations.
CO.E3.1.2.a: Report on a topic or text, tell a story, or recount an experience with appropriate facts and relevant, descriptive details, speaking clearly at an understandable pace.
CO.E3.1.2.c: Speak clearly, using appropriate volume and pitch for the purpose and audience.
CO.E3.1.2.d: Select and organize ideas sequentially or around major points of information that relate to the formality of the audience.
CO.E3.1.2.e: Create engaging audio recordings of stories or poems that demonstrate fluid reading at an understandable pace; add visual displays when appropriate to emphasize or enhance certain facts or details.
CO.E3.1.2.f: Speak in complete sentences when appropriate to task and situation in order to provide requested detail or clarification.
CO.E3.2.1: Apply strategies to fluently read and comprehend various literary texts.
CO.E3.2.1.a: Use Key Ideas and Details to:
CO.E3.2.1.a.i: Ask and answer questions to demonstrate understanding of a text, referring explicitly to the text as the basis for the answers.
CO.E3.2.1.a.ii: Use a variety of comprehension strategies to interpret text (attending, searching, predicting, checking, and self-correcting).
CO.E3.2.1.a.iii: Recount stories, including fables, folktales, and myths from diverse cultures; determine the central message, lesson, or moral and explain how it is conveyed through key details in the text.
CO.E3.2.1.a.iv: Summarize central ideas and important details from a text.
CO.E3.2.1.a.v: Describe and draw inferences about the elements of plot, character, and setting in literary pieces, poems, and plays.
CO.E3.2.1.a.vi: Describe characters in a story (for example: their traits, motivations, or feelings) and explain how their actions contribute to the sequence of events.
CO.E3.2.1.b.i: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, distinguishing literal from nonliteral language.
CO.E3.2.1.b.ii: Use signal words (such as before, after, next) and text structure (narrative, chronology) to determine the sequence of major events.
CO.E3.2.1.b.iii: Refer to parts of stories, dramas, and poems when writing or speaking about a text, using terms such as chapter, scene, and stanza; describe how each successive part builds on earlier sections.
CO.E3.2.1.b.iv: Distinguish their own point of view from that of the narrator or those of the characters.
CO.E3.2.1.c: Use Integration of Knowledge and Ideas to:
CO.E3.2.1.c.i: Explain how specific aspects of a text's illustrations contribute to what is conveyed by the words in a story (for example: create mood, emphasize aspects of a character or setting).
CO.E3.2.1.c.ii: Compare and contrast the themes, settings, and plots of stories written by the same author about the same or similar characters (for example: in books from a series).
CO.E3.2.1.d: Use Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity to:
CO.E3.2.1.d.i: By the end of the year, read and comprehend literature, including stories, dramas, and poetry, at the high end of the grades 2-3 text complexity band independently and proficiently.
CO.E3.2.1.e: Read grade level text accurately and fluently, attending to phrasing, intonation, and punctuation.
CO.E3.2.2: Apply strategies to fluently read and comprehend various informational texts.
CO.E3.2.2.a: Use Key Ideas and Details to:
CO.E3.2.2.a.i: Ask and answer questions to demonstrate understanding of a text, referring explicitly to the text as the basis for the answers.
CO.E3.2.2.a.ii: Determine the main idea of a text; recount the key details and explain how they support the main idea.
CO.E3.2.2.a.iii: Identify a main topic of a multi-paragraph text as well as the focus of specific paragraphs within the text.
CO.E3.2.2.a.iv: Describe the relationship between a series of historical events, scientific ideas or concepts, or steps in technical procedures in a text, using language that pertains to time, sequence, and cause/effect.
CO.E3.2.2.b.i: Determine the meaning of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases in a text relevant to a grade 3 topic or subject area.
CO.E3.2.2.b.ii: Use text features and search tools (for example: key words, sidebars, hyperlinks) to locate information relevant to a given topic efficiently.
CO.E3.2.2.b.iii: Distinguish their own point of view from that of the author of a text.
CO.E3.2.2.b.iv: Use semantic cues and signal words (for example: because and although) to identify cause/effect and compare/contrast relationships.
CO.E3.2.2.c: Use Integration of Knowledge and Ideas to:
CO.E3.2.2.c.i: Use information gained from illustrations (for example: maps, photographs) and the words in a text to demonstrate understanding of the text (for example: where, when, why, and how key events occur).
CO.E3.2.2.c.ii: Describe the logical connection between particular sentences and paragraphs in a text (for example: comparison, cause/effect, first/second/third in a sequence).
CO.E3.2.2.c.iii: Compare and contrast the most important points and key details presented in two texts on the same topic.
CO.E3.2.2.d: Use Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity to:
CO.E3.2.2.d.i: By the end of the year, read and comprehend informational texts, including history/social studies, science, and technical texts, at the high end of the grades 2-3 text complexity band independently and proficiently.
CO.E3.2.3: Apply knowledge of spelling patterns (orthography), word meanings (morphology), and word relationships to decode words and increase vocabulary.
CO.E3.2.3.a: Know and apply grade-level phonics and word analysis skills in decoding words.
CO.E3.2.3.a.i: Identify and know the meaning of the most common prefixes and derivational suffixes.
CO.E3.2.3.a.ii: Decode words with common Latin suffixes.
CO.E3.2.3.b: Read with sufficient accuracy and fluency to support comprehension.
CO.E3.2.3.b.i: Read grade-level text with purpose and understanding.
CO.E3.2.3.b.ii: Read grade-level prose and poetry orally with accuracy, appropriate rate, and expression.
CO.E3.2.3.b.iii: Use context to confirm or self-correct word recognition and understanding, rereading as necessary.
CO.E3.2.3.c: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning word and phrases based on grade 3 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.
CO.E3.2.3.c.i: Use sentence-level context as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.
CO.E3.2.3.c.ii: Determine the meaning of the new word formed when a known affix is added to a known word (for example: agreeable/disagreeable, comfortable/uncomfortable, care/careless, heat/preheat).
CO.E3.2.3.c.iii: Use knowledge of word relationships to identify antonyms or synonyms to clarify meaning.
CO.E3.2.3.c.iv: Use a known root word as a clue to the meaning of an unknown word with the same root (for example: company, companion).
CO.E3.2.3.c.v: Use glossaries or beginning dictionaries, both print and digital, to determine or clarify the precise meaning of key words and phrases.
CO.E3.2.3.c.vi: Determine the meaning of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases in a text relevant to a grade 3 topic or subject area.
CO.E3.2.3.d: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships and nuances in word meanings.
CO.E3.2.3.d.i: Distinguish the literal and nonliteral meanings of words and phrases in context (for example: take steps).
CO.E3.2.3.d.ii: Identify real-life connections between words and their use (for example: describe people who are friendly or helpful).
CO.E3.2.3.d.iii: Distinguish shades of meaning among related words that describe states of mind or degrees of certainty (for example: knew, believed, suspected, heard, wondered).
CO.E3.2.3.e: Acquire and use accurately grade-appropriate conversational, general academic, and domain-specific words and phrases, including those that signal spatial and temporal relationships (for example: After dinner that night we went looking for them).
CO.E3.3.1: Write opinion pieces on topics or texts, supporting a point of view with reasons.
CO.E3.3.1.a: Introduce the topic or text they are writing about, state an opinion, and create an organizational structure that includes reasons.
CO.E3.3.1.b: Provide reasons that support the opinion.
CO.E3.3.1.c: Use linking words and phrases (for example: because, therefore, since, for example) to connect opinion and reasons.
CO.E3.3.1.d: Provide a concluding statement or section.
CO.E3.3.2: Write informative/explanatory texts developed with facts, definitions, and details, ending with a related concluding statement.
CO.E3.3.2.a: Introduce a topic and group related information together; include illustrations when useful to aiding comprehension.
CO.E3.3.2.b: Develop the topic with facts, definitions, and details.
CO.E3.3.2.c: Use linking words and phrases (for example: also, another, and, more, but) to connect ideas within categories of information.
CO.E3.3.2.d: Provide a concluding statement or section.
CO.E3.3.3: Write real or imagined narratives that use descriptive details, have a clear sequence of events, and provide closure.
CO.E3.3.3.a: Establish a situation and introduce a narrator and/or characters; organize an event sequence that unfolds naturally.
CO.E3.3.3.b: Use dialogue and descriptions of actions, thoughts, and feelings to develop experiences and events or show the response of characters to situations.
CO.E3.3.3.c: Use temporal words and phrases to signal event order.
CO.E3.3.4: Use a recursive process to plan, draft, revise, and edit writing, applying knowledge of the conventions of grammar, capitalization, punctuation, and spelling.
CO.E3.3.4.a: Demonstrate command of the conventions of Standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.
CO.E3.3.4.a.i: Explain the function of nouns, pronouns, verbs, adjectives, and adverbs in general and their functions in particular sentences.
CO.E3.3.4.a.iii: Form and use regular and irregular verbs.
CO.E3.3.4.a.iv: Form and use the simple (for example: I walked; I walk; I will walk) verb tenses.
CO.E3.3.4.a.vi: Form and use comparative and superlative adjectives and adverbs, and choose between them depending on what is to be modified.
CO.E3.3.4.a.viii: Produce simple, compound, and complex sentences using coordinating and subordinating conjunctions.
CO.E3.3.4.a.ix: Vary sentence beginnings, and use long and short sentences to create sentence fluency in longer texts.
CO.E3.3.4.b: Demonstrate command of the conventions of Standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.
CO.E3.3.4.b.iii: Use commas and quotation marks in dialogue.
CO.E3.3.4.b.v: Use conventional spelling for high-frequency and other studied words and for adding suffixes to base words (for example: sitting, smiled, cries, happiness).
CO.E3.3.4.b.vi: Use spelling patterns and generalizations (for example: word families, position-based spellings, syllable patterns, ending rules, meaningful word parts) in writing words.
CO.E3.3.4.b.vii: Consult reference materials, including beginning dictionaries, as needed to check and correct spellings.
CO.E3.3.4.c: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening.
CO.E3.3.4.c.i: Choose words and phrases for effect.
CO.E3.3.4.c.ii: Recognize and observe differences between the conventions of spoken and written standard English.
CO.E3.3.4.d: With guidance and support from adults, produce writing in which the development and organization are appropriate to task and purpose.
CO.E3.3.4.e: With guidance and support from peers and adults, develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, and editing.
CO.E3.3.4.f: With guidance and support from adults, use technology to produce and publish writing (using keyboarding skills) as well as to interact and collaborate with others.
CO.E3.3.4.g: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of discipline-specific tasks, purposes, and audiences.
CO.E3.4.1: Gather, interpret, and communicate information discovered during short research projects.
CO.E3.4.1.a: Conduct short research projects that build knowledge about a topic.
CO.E3.4.1.b: Interpret and communicate the information learned by developing a brief summary with supporting details.
CO.E3.4.1.c: Develop supporting visual information (for example: charts, maps, illustrations, models).
CO.E3.4.1.d: Present a brief report of the research findings to an audience.
CO.E3.4.1.e: Recall information from experiences or gather information from print and digital sources; take brief notes on sources and sort evidence into provided categories.
CO.M3.NBT.A: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to perform multi-digit arithmetic. A range of algorithms may be used.
CO.M3.NBT.A.1: Use place value understanding to round whole numbers to the nearest `10or100`.
CO.M3.NBT.A.2: Fluently add and subtract within `1000` using strategies and algorithms based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction.
CO.M3.NBT.A.3: Multiply one-digit whole numbers by multiples of `10` in the range `10-90` (e.g., `9xx80,5xx60`) using strategies based on place value and properties of operations.
CO.M3.NF.A: Develop understanding of fractions as numbers.
CO.M3.NF.A.1: Describe a fraction `1/b` as the quantity formed by `1` part when a whole is partitioned into `b` equal parts; understand a fraction `a/b` as the quantity formed by a parts of size `1/b`.
CO.M3.NF.A.2: Describe a fraction as a number on the number line; represent fractions on a number line diagram.
CO.M3.NF.A.2.a: Represent a fraction `1/b` on a number line diagram by defining the interval from `0` to `1` as the whole and partitioning it into `b` equal parts. Recognize that each part has size `1/b` and that the endpoint of the part based at `0` locates the number `1/b` on the number line.
CO.M3.NF.A.2.b: Represent a fraction `a/b` on a number line diagram by marking off a lengths `1/b` from `0`. Recognize that the resulting interval has size `a/b` and that its endpoint locates the number `a/b` on the number line.
CO.M3.NF.A.3: Explain equivalence of fractions in special cases, and compare fractions by reasoning about their size.
CO.M3.NF.A.3.a: Understand two fractions as equivalent (equal) if they are the same size, or the same point on a number line.
CO.M3.NF.A.3.b: Recognize and generate simple equivalent fractions, e.g., `1/2=2/4,4/6=2/3`. Explain why the fractions are equivalent, e.g., by using a visual fraction model.
CO.M3.NF.A.3.c: Express whole numbers as fractions, and recognize fractions that are equivalent to whole numbers.
CO.M3.NF.A.3.d: Compare two fractions with the same numerator or the same denominator by reasoning about their size. Recognize that comparisons are valid only when the two fractions refer to the same whole. Record the results of comparisons with the symbols `>,=,or<`, and justify the conclusions, e.g., by using a visual fraction model.
CO.M3.OA.A: Represent and solve problems involving multiplication and division.
CO.M3.OA.A.1: Interpret products of whole numbers, e.g., interpret `5xx7` as the total number of objects in `5` groups of `7` objects each.
CO.M3.OA.A.2: Interpret whole-number quotients of whole numbers, e.g., interpret `56-:8` as the number of objects in each share when `56` objects are partitioned equally into `8` shares, or as a number of shares when `56` objects are partitioned into equal shares of `8` objects each.
CO.M3.OA.A.3: Use multiplication and division within `100` to solve word problems in situations involving equal groups, arrays, and measurement quantities, e.g., by using drawings and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.
CO.M3.OA.A.4: Determine the unknown whole number in a multiplication or division equation relating three whole numbers.
CO.M3.OA.B: Apply properties of multiplication and the relationship between multiplication and division.
CO.M3.OA.B.5: Apply properties of operations as strategies to multiply and divide.
CO.M3.OA.B.6: Interpret division as an unknown-factor problem.
CO.M3.OA.C.7: Fluently multiply and divide within `100`, using strategies such as the relationship between multiplication and division (e.g., knowing that `8xx5=40`, one knows `40-:5=8`) or properties of operations. By the end of Grade 3, know from memory all products of two one-digit numbers.
CO.M3.OA.D: Solve problems involving the four operations, and identify and explain patterns in arithmetic.
CO.M3.OA.D.8: Solve two-step word problems using the four operations. Represent these problems using equations with a letter standing for the unknown quantity. Assess the reasonableness of answers using mental computation and estimation strategies including rounding.
CO.M3.OA.D.9: Identify arithmetic patterns (including patterns in the addition table or multiplication table) and explain them using properties of operations.
CO.M3.MD.A: Solve problems involving measurement and estimation of intervals of time, liquid volumes, and masses of objects.
CO.M3.MD.A.1: Tell and write time to the nearest minute and measure time intervals in `text(minutes)`. Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of time intervals in `text(minutes)`, e.g., by representing the problem on a number line diagram.
CO.M3.MD.A.2: Measure and estimate liquid volumes and masses of objects using standard units of grams (g), kilograms (kg), and liters (l). (This excludes compound units such as `text(cm)^3` and finding the geometric volume of a container.) Add, subtract, multiply, or divide to solve one-step word problems involving masses or volumes that are given in the same units, e.g., by using drawings (such as a beaker with a measurement scale) to represent the problem.
CO.M3.MD.B.3: Draw a scaled picture graph and a scaled bar graph to represent a data set with several categories. Solve one- and two-step “how many more” and “how many less” problems using information presented in scaled bar graphs.
CO.M3.MD.B.4: Generate measurement data by measuring lengths using rulers marked with `text(halves)andtext(fourths of an inch)`. Show the data by making a line plot, where the horizontal scale is marked off in appropriate units - `text(whole numbers),text(halves),ortext(quarters)`.
CO.M3.MD.C: Use concepts of area and relate area to multiplication and to addition.
CO.M3.MD.C.5: Recognize area as an attribute of plane figures and understand concepts of area measurement.
CO.M3.MD.C.5.a: A square with side length`1` `text(unit)`, called “a unit square,” is said to have “one square unit” of area, and can be used to measure area.
CO.M3.MD.C.5.b: A plane figure which can be covered without gaps or overlaps by `n` unit squares is said to have an area of `n` square units.
CO.M3.MD.C.6: Measure areas by counting unit squares (`text(square cm),text(square m),text(square in),text(square ft)`, and improvised units).
CO.M3.MD.C.7: Use concepts of area and relate area to the operations of multiplication and addition.
CO.M3.MD.C.7.a: Find the area of a rectangle with whole-number side lengths by tiling it, and show that the area is the same as would be found by multiplying the side lengths.
CO.M3.MD.C.7.b: Multiply side lengths to find areas of rectangles with whole-number side lengths in the context of solving real-world and mathematical problems, and represent whole-number products as rectangular areas in mathematical reasoning.
CO.M3.MD.C.7.c: Use tiling to show in a concrete case that the area of a rectangle with whole-number side lengths `aandb+c` is the sum of `axxbandaxxc`. Use area models to represent the distributive property in mathematical reasoning.
CO.M3.MD.D: Geometric measurement: Recognize perimeter as an attribute of plane figures and distinguish between linear and area measures.
CO.M3.MD.D.8: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving perimeters of polygons, including finding the perimeter given the side lengths, finding an unknown side length, and exhibiting rectangles with the same perimeter and different areas or with the same area and different perimeters.
CO.M3.G.A: Reason with shapes and their attributes.
CO.M3.G.A.1: Explain that shapes in different categories (e.g., rhombuses, rectangles, and others) may share attributes (e.g., having four sides), and that the shared attributes can define a larger category (e.g., quadrilaterals). Recognize rhombuses, rectangles, and squares as examples of quadrilaterals, and draw examples of quadrilaterals that do not belong to any of these subcategories.
CO.M3.G.A.2: Partition shapes into parts with equal areas. Express the area of each part as a unit fraction of the whole.
CO.S3.1.1: Patterns of motion can be used to predict future motion.
CO.S3.1.1.a: Plan and conduct an investigation to provide evidence of the effects of balanced and unbalanced forces on the motion of an object.
CO.S3.1.1.b: Make observations and/or measurements of an object's motion to provide evidence that a pattern can be used to predict future motion.
CO.S3.1.2: Objects in contact exert forces on each other; electric and magnetic forces between a pair of objects do not require contact.
CO.S3.1.2.a: Ask questions to determine cause - and - effect relationships of electric or magnetic interactions between two objects not in contact with each other.
CO.S3.1.2.b: Define a simple design problem that can be solved by applying scientific ideas about magnets.
CO.S3.2.1: Organisms have unique and diverse life cycles.
CO.S3.2.1.a: Develop models to describe that organisms have unique and diverse life cycles but all have in common birth, growth, reproduction and death.
CO.S3.2.2: Being part of a group helps animals obtain food, defend themselves and cope with changes.
CO.S3.2.2.a: Construct an argument that some animals form groups that help members survive.
CO.S3.2.3: Different organisms vary in how they look and function because they have different inherited information; the environment also affects the traits that an organism develops.
CO.S3.2.3.a: Analyze and interpret data to provide evidence that plants and animals have traits inherited from parents and that variation of these traits exists in a group of similar organisms.
CO.S3.2.3.b: Use evidence to support the explanation that traits can be influenced by the environment.
CO.S3.2.4: Some living organisms resemble organisms that once lived on Earth.
CO.S3.2.4.a: Analyze and interpret data from fossils to provide evidence of the organisms and the environments in which they lived long ago.
CO.S3.2.4.b: Use evidence to construct an explanation for how the variations in characteristics among individuals of the same species may provide advantages in surviving, finding mates and reproducing.
CO.S3.2.5: Sometimes differences in characteristics between individuals of the same species provide advantages in survival and reproduction.
CO.S3.2.5.a: Construct an argument with evidence that in a particular habitat some organisms can survive well, some survive less well and some cannot survive at all.
CO.S3.2.5.b: Make a claim about the merit of a solution to a problem caused when the environment changes and the types of plants and animals that live there may change.
CO.S3.3.1: Climate describes patterns of typical weather conditions over different scales and variations; historical weather patterns can be analyzed.
CO.S3.3.1.a: Represent data in tables and graphical displays to describe typical weather conditions expected during a particular season.
CO.S3.3.1.b: Obtain and combine information to describe climates in different regions of the world.
CO.S3.3.2: A variety of weather hazards result from natural process; humans cannot eliminate weather-related hazards but can reduce their impacts.
CO.S3.3.2.a: Make a claim about the merit of a design solution that reduces the impacts of a weather-related hazard.
CO.SS3.1.1: Compare primary and secondary sources when explaining the past.
CO.SS3.1.1.a: Compare primary sources with works of fiction about the same topic.
CO.SS3.1.1.b: Use a variety of primary sources such as artifacts, pictures, oral histories, and documents, to help determine factual information about historical events.
CO.SS3.1.1.c: Compare information from multiple sources recounting the same event.
CO.SS3.1.2: Identify how people in the past influence the development and interaction of different communities or regions.
CO.SS3.1.2.a: Compare past and present situations and events.
CO.SS3.1.2.b: Give examples of people, events, and developments that brought important changes to a community or region.
CO.SS3.1.2.c: Describe the history, interaction, and contribution of various peoples and cultures, including African American, Latino, Asian American, Hawaiian/Pacific Islander, Indigenous Peoples, LGBTQ, and religious minorities that have lived in or migrated to a community or region and how that migration has influenced change and development.
CO.SS3.2.1: Use geographic tools to develop spatial thinking skills.
CO.SS3.2.1.a: Read and interpret information from geographic tools and formulate geographic questions.
CO.SS3.2.1.b: Locate oceans and continents, major countries, bodies of water, mountains, urban areas, the state of Colorado, and neighboring states on maps.
CO.SS3.2.1.c: Describe the natural and man-made features of a specific area on a map.
CO.SS3.2.1.d: Identify geography-based problems and examine the ways that people have tried to solve them.
CO.SS3.2.2: Define the concept of region through an examination of similarities and differences in places and communities.
CO.SS3.2.2.a: Observe and describe the physical, cultural, and human-made characteristics of a local region.
CO.SS3.2.2.b: Identify the factors that make a region unique.
CO.SS3.2.2.c: Give examples of places that are similar and different from a local region.
CO.SS3.2.2.d: Characterize regions using different types of features such as physical, political, cultural, urban, and rural attributes.
CO.SS3.3.1: Explain how producers and consumers exchange goods and services in different ways.
CO.SS3.3.1.a: Describe the difference between producers and consumers and explain how they need each other.
CO.SS3.3.1.b: Describe and give examples of forms of exchange.
CO.SS3.3.1.c: Describe how the exchange of goods and services between businesses and consumers affects all parties.
CO.SS3.3.1.d: Recognize that different currencies exist and explain the functions of money.
CO.SS3.3.1.e: Cite evidence to show how trade benefits individuals, businesses, and communities, and increases interdependency.
CO.SS3.4.1: Respect the views and rights of others.
CO.SS3.4.1.a: Identify and apply the elements of civil discourse.
CO.SS3.4.1.b: Identify important personal rights in a democratic society and how they relate to others' rights.
CO.SS3.4.1.c: Give examples of the relationship between rights and responsibilities.
CO.SS3.4.1.d: Restate the view or opinion of others with their reasoning when it is different from one's own.
CO.SS3.4.2: Describe the origins, structures, and functions of local government.
CO.SS3.4.2.a: Explain the origins and structures of local government.
CO.SS3.4.2.b: Explain the services local governments provide and how those services are funded.
CO.SS3.4.2.c: Identify and explain a variety of roles leaders, citizens, and others play in local government.
CO.SS3.4.2.d: Describe how local government provides opportunities for people to exercise their rights and initiate change.
CO.SS3.4.2.e: Discuss the role of elections in choosing specific candidates to represent the public interest in local government.
CO.SS3.5.1: Create a plan to meet a financial goal.
CO.SS3.5.1.a: Give examples of short-term spending and savings goals.
CO.SS3.5.1.b: Identify activities that individuals can do to earn money to reach personal financial goals.
CO.SS3.5.1.c: Differentiate the role of income and expenses when creating a budget.
CO.SS3.5.1.d: Create a plan with specific steps to reach a short-term financial goal.
CO.SS3.5.1.e: Model strategies to achieve a personal financial goal using arithmetic operations.
CO.E4.1.1: Pose thoughtful questions after actively listening to others.
CO.E4.1.1.a: Engage effectively in a range of collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in groups, and teacher-led) with diverse partners on grade 4 topics and texts, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly.
CO.E4.1.1.a.i: Come to discussions prepared, having read or studied required material; explicitly draw on that preparation and other information known about the topic to explore ideas under discussion.
CO.E4.1.1.a.ii: Follow agreed-upon rules for discussions and carry out assigned roles.
CO.E4.1.1.a.iii: Pose and respond to specific questions to clarify or follow up on information, and make comments that contribute to the discussion and link to the remarks of others.
CO.E4.1.1.a.iv: Review the key ideas expressed and explain their own ideas and understanding in light of the discussion.
CO.E4.1.1.b: Paraphrase portions of a text read aloud or information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.
CO.E4.1.1.c: Identify the reasons and evidence a speaker provides to support particular points.
CO.E4.1.2: Create a plan to effectively present information both informally and formally.
CO.E4.1.2.a: Report on a topic or text, tell a story, or recount an experience in an organized manner, using appropriate facts and relevant, descriptive details to support main ideas or themes; speak clearly at an understandable pace.
CO.E4.1.2.b: Add audio recordings and visual displays to presentations when appropriate to enhance the development of main ideas or themes.
CO.E4.1.2.c: Differentiate between contexts that call for formal English (for example: presenting ideas) and situations where informal discourse is appropriate (for example: small-group discussion); use formal English when appropriate to task and situation.
CO.E4.2.1: Apply strategies to comprehend and interpret literary texts.
CO.E4.2.1.a: Use Key Ideas and Details to:
CO.E4.2.1.a.i: Refer to details and examples in a text when explaining what the text says explicitly and when drawing inferences from the text.
CO.E4.2.1.a.ii: Determine a theme of a story, drama, or poem from details in the text; summarize the text.
CO.E4.2.1.a.iii: Describe in depth a character, setting, or event in a story or drama, drawing on specific details in the text (for example: a character's thoughts, words, or actions).
CO.E4.2.1.a.iv: Describe the development of plot (such as the origin of the central conflict, the action of the plot, and how the conflict is resolved).
CO.E4.2.1.b.i: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including those that allude to significant characters found in mythology (for example: Herculean).
CO.E4.2.1.b.ii: Explain major differences between poems, drama, and prose, and refer to the structural elements of poems (for example: verse, rhythm, meter) and drama (for example, casts of characters, settings, descriptions, dialogue, stage directions) when writing or speaking about a text.
CO.E4.2.1.b.iii: Compare and contrast the point of view from which different stories are narrated, including the difference between first- and third-person narrations.
CO.E4.2.1.c: Use Integration of Knowledge and Ideas to:
CO.E4.2.1.c.i: Make connections between the text of a story or drama and a visual or oral presentation of the text, identifying where each version reflects specific descriptions and directions in the text.
CO.E4.2.1.c.ii: Compare and contrast the treatment of similar themes and topics (for example: opposition of good and evil) and patterns of events (for example: the quest) in stories, myths, and traditional literature from different cultures.
CO.E4.2.1.d: Use Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity to:
CO.E4.2.1.d.i: By the end of the year, read and comprehend literature, including stories, dramas, and poetry, in the grades 4-5 text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.
CO.E4.2.1.d.ii: Read familiar texts orally with fluency, accuracy, and prosody (expression).
CO.E4.2.2: Apply strategies to comprehend and interpret informational texts.
CO.E4.2.2.a: Use Key Ideas and Details to:
CO.E4.2.2.a.i: Refer to details and examples in a text when explaining what the text says explicitly and when drawing inferences from the text.
CO.E4.2.2.a.ii: Determine the main idea of a text and explain how it is supported by key details; summarize the text.
CO.E4.2.2.a.iii: Explain events, procedures, ideas, or concepts in a historical, scientific, or technical text, including what happened and why, based on specific information in the text.
CO.E4.2.2.b.i: Determine the meaning of general academic and domain-specific words or phrases in a text relevant to a grade 4 topic or subject area.
CO.E4.2.2.b.ii: Describe the overall structure (for example, chronology, comparison, cause/effect, problem/solution) of events, ideas, concepts, or information in a text or part of a text.
CO.E4.2.2.b.iii: Compare and contrast a firsthand and secondhand account of the same event or topic; describe the differences in focus and the information provided.
CO.E4.2.2.c: Use Integration of Knowledge and Ideas to:
CO.E4.2.2.c.i: Interpret information presented visually, orally, or quantitatively (for example: in charts, graphs, diagrams, time lines, animations, or interactive elements on Web pages) and explain how the information contributes to an understanding of the text in which it appears.
CO.E4.2.2.c.ii: Explain how an author uses reasons and evidence to support particular points in a text.
CO.E4.2.2.c.iii: Integrate information from two texts on the same topic in order to write or speak about the subject knowledgeably.
CO.E4.2.2.d: Use Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity to:
CO.E4.2.2.d.i: By the end of year, read and comprehend informational texts, including history/social studies, science, and technical texts, in the grades 4-5 text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.
CO.E4.2.3: Apply knowledge of spelling patterns (orthography) and word meanings (morphology) to decode multisyllable words and determine the meaning of unknown words.
CO.E4.2.3.a: Know and apply grade-level phonics and word analysis skills in decoding words.
