CO.E4.2.3.a.i: Use combined knowledge of all letter-sound correspondences, syllabication patterns, and morphology (for example, roots and affixes) to read accurately unfamiliar multisyllabic words in context and out of context.
CO.E4.2.3.b: Read with sufficient accuracy and fluency to support comprehension.
CO.E4.2.3.b.i: Read grade-level text with purpose and understanding.
CO.E4.2.3.b.ii: Read grade-level prose and poetry orally with accuracy, appropriate rate, and expression.
CO.E4.2.3.b.iii: Use context to confirm or self-correct word recognition and understanding, rereading as necessary.
CO.E4.2.3.c: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grade 4 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.
CO.E4.2.3.c.i: Use context (for example: definitions, examples, or restatements in text) as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.
CO.E4.2.3.c.ii: Use common, grade-appropriate Greek and Latin affixes and roots as clues to the meaning of a word (for example: telegraph, photograph, autograph).
CO.E4.2.3.c.iii: Read and understand words with common prefixes (for example: un-, re-, dis-) and derivational suffixes (for example: -ful, -ly, -ness).
CO.E4.2.3.c.iv: Read and understand words that change spelling to show past tense (for example: write/wrote, catch/caught, teach/taught).
CO.E4.2.3.c.v: Read multisyllabic words with and without inflectional and derivational suffixes.
CO.E4.2.3.c.vi: Infer meaning of words using explanations offered within a text.
CO.E4.2.3.c.vii: Consult reference materials (for example: dictionaries, glossaries, thesauruses), both print and digital, to find the pronunciation and determine or clarify the precise meaning of key words and phrases.
CO.E4.2.3.d: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.
CO.E4.2.3.d.i: Explain the meaning of simple similes and metaphors (for example, as pretty as a picture) in context.
CO.E4.2.3.d.ii: Recognize and explain the meaning of common idioms, adages, and proverbs.
CO.E4.2.3.d.iii: Demonstrate understanding of words by relating them to their opposites (antonyms) and to words with similar but not identical meanings (synonyms).
CO.E4.2.3.e: Acquire and use accurately grade-appropriate general academic and domain-specific words and phrases, including those that signal precise actions, emotions, or states of being (for example: quizzed, whined, stammered) and that are basic to a particular topic (for example: wildlife, conservation, and endangered when discussing animal preservation).
CO.E4.3.1: Write opinion pieces on topics or texts supporting a point of view with reasons and information.
CO.E4.3.1.a: Introduce a topic or text clearly, state an opinion, and create an organizational structure in which related ideas are grouped to support the writer's purpose.
CO.E4.3.1.b: Provide reasons that are supported by facts and details.
CO.E4.3.1.c: Link opinion and reasons using words and phrases (for example: for instance, in order to, in addition).
CO.E4.3.1.d: Provide a concluding statement or section related to the opinion presented.
CO.E4.3.2: Write informative/explanatory texts using text structures appropriate for the purpose and developed through facts, definitions, concrete details, precise language, and domain-specific vocabulary.
CO.E4.3.2.a: Introduce a topic clearly and group related information in paragraphs and sections; include formatting (for example: headings), illustrations, and multimedia when useful to aiding comprehension.
CO.E4.3.2.b: Identify a text structure appropriate to purpose (sequence, chronology, description, explanation, and comparison-and-contrast).
CO.E4.3.2.c: Organize relevant ideas and details to convey a central idea or prove a point.
CO.E4.3.2.d: Develop the topic with facts, definitions, concrete details, quotations, or other information and examples related to the topic.
CO.E4.3.2.e: Link ideas within categories of information using words and phrases (for example: another, for example, also, because).
CO.E4.3.2.f: Use precise language and domain-specific vocabulary to inform about or explain the topic.
CO.E4.3.2.g: Provide a concluding statement or section related to the information or explanation presented.
CO.E4.3.3: Write engaging, real or imagined narratives using descriptive details and dialogue to convey a sequence of related events.
CO.E4.3.3.a: Orient the reader by establishing a situation and introducing a narrator and/or characters; organize an event sequence that unfolds naturally.
CO.E4.3.3.b: Use dialogue and description to develop experiences and events or show the responses of characters to situations.
CO.E4.3.3.c: Use a variety of transitional words and phrases to manage the sequence of events.
CO.E4.3.3.d: Use concrete words and phrases and sensory details to convey experiences and events precisely.
CO.E4.3.3.e: Provide a conclusion that follows from the narrated experiences or events.
CO.E4.3.4: Understand why and how writers use the conventions of Standard English grammar, usage, and mechanics to clarify their meaning.
CO.E4.3.4.a: Demonstrate command of the conventions of Standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.
CO.E4.3.4.a.i: Use relative pronouns (who, whose, whom, which, that) and relative adverbs (where, when, why).
CO.E4.3.4.a.ii: Form and use the progressive (for example: I was walking; I am walking; I will be walking) verb tenses.
CO.E4.3.4.a.iii: Use modal auxiliaries (for example: can, may, must) to convey various conditions.
CO.E4.3.4.a.iv: Order adjectives within sentences according to conventional patterns (for example: a small red bag rather than a red small bag).
CO.E4.3.4.a.vi: Use compound subjects (for example: Tom and Pat went to the store) and compound verbs (for example: Harry thought and worried about the things he said to Jane) to create sentence fluency in writing.
CO.E4.3.4.a.vii: Produce complete simple, compound, and complex sentences.
CO.E4.3.4.a.viii: Recognize and correct inappropriate fragments and run-ons. (adapted from.
CO.E4.3.4.a.ix: Correctly use frequently confused words (for example: to, too, two; there,* their).
CO.E4.3.4.b: Demonstrate command of the conventions of Standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.
CO.E4.3.4.b.ii: Use commas and quotation marks to mark direct speech and quotations from a text.
CO.E4.3.4.b.iii: Use a comma before a coordinating conjunction in a compound sentence.
CO.E4.3.4.b.iv: Spell grade-appropriate words correctly, consulting references as needed.
CO.E4.3.4.c: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening.
CO.E4.3.4.c.i: Choose words and phrases to convey ideas precisely.
CO.E4.3.4.c.iii: Differentiate between contexts that call for formal English (for example: presenting ideas) and situations where informal discourse is appropriate (for example: small-group discussion).
CO.E4.3.4.d: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development and organization are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.
CO.E4.3.4.e: With guidance and support from peers and adults, develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, and editing.
CO.E4.3.4.f: With some guidance and support from adults, use technology, including the Internet, to produce and publish writing as well as to interact and collaborate with others; demonstrate sufficient command of keyboarding skills to type a minimum of one page in a single sitting.
CO.E4.3.4.g: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of discipline-specific tasks, purposes, and audiences.
CO.E4.4.1: Use a variety of resources to build and communicate knowledge related to open-ended research questions.
CO.E4.4.1.a: Conduct short research projects that build knowledge through investigation of different aspects of a topic.
CO.E4.4.1.a.i: Identify a topic and formulate open-ended research questions for further inquiry and learning.
CO.E4.4.1.a.ii: Present a brief report of the research findings to an audience.
CO.E4.4.1.b: Recall relevant information from experiences or gather relevant information from print and digital sources; take notes and categorize information, and provide a list of sources.
CO.E4.4.1.c: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.
CO.E4.4.1.c.i: Apply grade 4 Reading standards to literature (for example: “Describe in depth a character, setting, or event in a story or drama, drawing on specific details in the text [for example: a character's thoughts, words, or actions].”).
CO.E4.4.1.c.ii: Apply grade 4 Reading standards to informational texts (for example: “Explain how an author uses reasons and evidence to support particular points in a text”).
CO.M4.NBT.A: Generalize place value understanding for multi-digit whole numbers.
CO.M4.NBT.A.1: Explain that in a multi-digit whole number, a digit in one place represents ten times what it represents in the place to its right.
CO.M4.NBT.A.2: Read and write multi-digit whole numbers using base-ten numerals, number names, and expanded form. Compare two multi-digit numbers based on meanings of the digits in each place, using `>,=,and<` symbols to record the results of comparisons.
CO.M4.NBT.A.3: Use place value understanding to round multi-digit whole numbers to any place.
CO.M4.NBT.B: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to perform multi-digit arithmetic.
CO.M4.NBT.B.4: Fluently add and subtract multi-digit whole numbers using the standard algorithm.
CO.M4.NBT.B.5: Multiply a whole number of up to `text(four digits)` by a `text(one-digit whole number)`, and multiply `text(two two-digit)` numbers, using strategies based on place value and the properties of operations. Illustrate and explain the calculation by using equations, rectangular arrays, and/or area models.
CO.M4.NBT.B.6: Find whole-number quotients and remainders with up to four-digit dividends and one-digit divisors, using strategies based on place value, the properties of operations, and/or the relationship between multiplication and division. Illustrate and explain the calculation by using equations, rectangular arrays, and/or area models.
CO.M4.NF.A: Extend understanding of fraction equivalence and ordering.
CO.M4.NF.A.1: Explain why a fraction `a/b` is equivalent to a fraction `(nxxa)/(nxxb)` by using visual fraction models, with attention to how the number and size of the parts differ even though the two fractions themselves are the same size. Use this principle to recognize and generate equivalent fractions.
CO.M4.NF.A.2: Compare two fractions with different numerators and different denominators, e.g., by creating common denominators or numerators, or by comparing to a benchmark fraction such as `1/2`. Recognize that comparisons are valid only when the two fractions refer to the same whole. Record the results of comparisons with symbols `>,=,or<`, and justify the conclusions, e.g., by using a visual fraction model.
CO.M4.NF.B.3: Understand a fraction `a/b` with `a>1` as a sum of fractions `1/b`.
CO.M4.NF.B.3.a: Understand addition and subtraction of fractions as joining and separating parts referring to the same whole.
CO.M4.NF.B.3.b: Decompose a fraction into a sum of fractions with like denominators in more than one way, recording each decomposition by an equation. Justify decompositions, e.g., by using a visual fraction model.
CO.M4.NF.B.3.c: Add and subtract mixed numbers with like denominators, e.g., by replacing each mixed number with an equivalent fraction, and/or by using properties of operations and the relationship between addition and subtraction.
CO.M4.NF.B.3.d: Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions referring to the same whole and having like denominators, e.g., by using visual fraction models and equations to represent the problem.
CO.M4.NF.B.4: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication to multiply a fraction by a whole number.
CO.M4.NF.B.4.a: Understand a fraction `a/b` as a multiple of `1/b`.
CO.M4.NF.B.4.b: Understand a multiple of `a/b` as a multiple of `1/b`, and use this understanding to multiply a fraction by a whole number.
CO.M4.NF.B.4.c: Solve word problems involving multiplication of a fraction by a whole number, e.g., by using visual fraction models and equations to represent the problem.
CO.M4.NF.C: Use decimal notation for fractions, and compare decimal fractions.
CO.M4.NF.C.5: Express a fraction with denominator `10` as an equivalent fraction with denominator `100`, and use this technique to add two fractions with respective denominators `10and100`.
CO.M4.NF.C.6: Use decimal notation for fractions with denominators `10or100`.
CO.M4.NF.C.7: Compare two decimals to hundredths by reasoning about their size. Recognize that comparisons are valid only when the two decimals refer to the same whole. Record the results of comparisons with the symbols `>,=,or<`, and justify the conclusions, e.g., by using a visual model.
CO.M4.OA.A: Use the four operations with whole numbers to solve problems.
CO.M4.OA.A.1: Interpret a multiplication equation as a comparison, e.g., interpret `35=5xx7` as a statement that `35` is `5` times as many as `7and7` times as many as `5`. Represent verbal statements of multiplicative comparisons as multiplication equations.
CO.M4.OA.A.2: Multiply or divide to solve word problems involving multiplicative comparison, e.g., by using drawings and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem, distinguishing multiplicative comparison from additive comparison.
CO.M4.OA.A.3: Solve multistep word problems posed with whole numbers and having whole-number answers using the four operations, including problems in which remainders must be interpreted. Represent these problems using equations with a letter standing for the unknown quantity. Assess the reasonableness of answers using mental computation and estimation strategies including rounding.
CO.M4.OA.B: Gain familiarity with factors and multiples.
CO.M4.OA.B.4: Find all factor pairs for a whole number in the range `1-100`. Recognize that a whole number is a multiple of each of its factors. Determine whether a given whole number in the range `1-100` is a multiple of a given one-digit number. Determine whether a given whole number in the range `1-100` is prime or composite.
CO.M4.OA.C.5: Generate a number or shape pattern that follows a given rule. Identify apparent features of the pattern that were not explicit in the rule itself.
CO.M4.MD.A: Solve problems involving measurement and conversion of measurements from a larger unit to a smaller unit.
CO.M4.MD.A.1: Know relative sizes of measurement units within one system of units including `text(km, m, cm; kg, g; lb, oz.; l, ml; hr, min, sec)`. Within a single system of measurement, express measurements in a larger unit in terms of a smaller unit. Record measurement equivalents in a two-column table.
CO.M4.MD.A.2: Use the four operations to solve word problems involving distances, intervals of time, liquid volumes, masses of objects, and money, including problems involving simple fractions or decimals, and problems that require expressing measurements given in a larger unit in terms of a smaller unit. Represent measurement quantities using diagrams such as number line diagrams that feature a measurement scale.
CO.M4.MD.A.3: Apply the area and perimeter formulas for rectangles in real-world and mathematical problems.
CO.M4.MD.B.4: Make a line plot to display a data set of measurements in fractions of a unit `(1/2,1/4,1/8)`. Solve problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions by using information presented in line plots.
CO.M4.MD.C: Geometric measurement: Understand concepts of angle and measure angles.
CO.M4.MD.C.5: Recognize angles as geometric shapes that are formed wherever two rays share a common endpoint, and understand concepts of angle measurement.
CO.M4.MD.C.5.a: An angle is measured with reference to a circle with its center at the common endpoint of the rays, by considering the fraction of the circular arc between the points where the two rays intersect the circle. An angle that turns through `1/360` of a circle is called a “one-degree angle,” and can be used to measure angles.
CO.M4.MD.C.5.b: An angle that turns through `n` `text(one-degree)` angles is said to have an angle measure of `n` `text(degrees)`.
CO.M4.MD.C.6: Measure angles in whole-number degrees using a protractor. Sketch angles of specified measure.
CO.M4.MD.C.7: Recognize angle measure as additive. When an angle is decomposed into non-overlapping parts, the angle measure of the whole is the sum of the angle measures of the parts. Solve addition and subtraction problems to find unknown angles on a diagram in real-world and mathematical problems, e.g., by using an equation with a symbol for the unknown angle measure.
CO.M4.G.A: Draw and identify lines and angles, and classify shapes by properties of their lines and angles.
CO.M4.G.A.1: Draw points, lines, line segments, rays, angles (right, acute, obtuse), and perpendicular and parallel lines. Identify these in two-dimensional figures.
CO.M4.G.A.2: Classify two-dimensional figures based on the presence or absence of parallel or perpendicular lines, or the presence or absence of angles of a specified size. Recognize right triangles as a category, and identify right triangles.
CO.M4.G.A.3: Recognize a line of symmetry for a two-dimensional figure as a line across the figure such that the figure can be folded along the line into matching parts. Identify line-symmetric figures and draw lines of symmetry.
CO.S4.1.1: The faster an object moves the more energy it has.
CO.S4.1.1.a: Use evidence to construct an explanation relating the speed of an object to the energy of that object.
CO.S4.1.2: Energy can be moved from place to place.
CO.S4.1.2.a: Make observations to provide evidence that energy can be transferred from place to place by sound, light, heat and electric currents.
CO.S4.1.3: When objects collide contact forces transfer so as to change objects' motion.
CO.S4.1.3.a: Ask questions and predict outcomes about the changes in energy that occur when objects collide.
CO.S4.1.4: Energy can be produced, used or released by converting stored energy.
CO.S4.1.4.a: Apply scientific ideas to design, test and refine a device that converts energy from one form to another.
CO.S4.1.5: Waves are regular patterns of motion.
CO.S4.1.5.a: Develop a model of waves to describe patterns in terms of amplitude and wavelength and that waves can cause objects to move.
CO.S4.1.6: An object can be seen when light reflected from its surface enters the eyes.
CO.S4.1.6.a: Develop a model to describe that light reflecting from objects and entering the eye allows objects to be seen.
CO.S4.1.7: Patterns can encode, send, receive and decode information.
CO.S4.1.7.a: Generate and compare multiple solutions that use patterns to transfer information.
CO.S4.2.1: Organisms have both internal and external structures that serve various functions.
CO.S4.2.1.a: Construct an argument that plants and animals have internal and external structures that function to support survival, growth, behavior and reproduction.
CO.S4.2.1.b: Use a model to describe that animals receive different types of information through their senses, process the information in their brain, and respond to the information in different ways.
CO.S4.3.1.a: Identify evidence from patterns in rock formations and fossils in rock layers to support an explanation for changes in a landscape over time.
CO.S4.3.2.a: Make observations and/or measurements to provide evidence of the effects of weathering or the rate of erosion by water, ice, wind, or vegetation.
CO.S4.3.3: Earth's physical features occur in patterns.
CO.S4.3.3.a: Analyze and interpret data from maps to describe patterns of Earth's features.
CO.S4.3.4: Energy and fuels that humans use are derived from natural sources and their use affects the environment in multiple ways.
CO.S4.3.4.a: Obtain and combine information to describe that energy and fuels are derived from natural resources and their uses affect the environment.
CO.S4.3.5: A variety of hazards result from natural process; humans cannot eliminate natural hazards but can reduce their impacts' effect.
CO.S4.3.5.a: Generate and compare multiple solutions to reduce the impacts of natural Earth processes on humans.
CO.SS4.1.1: Analyze primary and secondary sources from multiple points of view to develop an understanding of the history of Colorado.
CO.SS4.1.1.a: Draw inferences about Colorado history from primary sources such as journals, diaries, maps, treaties, oral histories, etc.
CO.SS4.1.1.b: Identify cause-and-effect relationships using primary sources to understand the history of Colorado's development.
CO.SS4.1.1.c: Explain, through multiple perspectives, the human interactions among people and cultures that are indigenous to or migrated to present-day Colorado.
CO.SS4.1.1.d: Identify and describe how political and cultural groups have affected the development of the region.
CO.SS4.1.1.e: Discuss the multiple perspectives of settler colonialism/Westward Expansion and the impact on the political and cultural landscape of the region presently known as Colorado.
CO.SS4.1.2: Describe the historical eras, individuals, groups, ideas, and themes in Colorado history and their relationship to key events in the United States within the same historical period.
CO.SS4.1.2.a: Construct a timeline of the major events in Colorado history.
CO.SS4.1.2.b: Explain the relationship between major events in Colorado history and events in United States history during the same era.
CO.SS4.1.2.c: Describe both past and present interactions among the people and cultures in Colorado.
CO.SS4.1.2.d: Describe the impact of various technological developments.
CO.SS4.2.1: Use geographic tools to research and answer questions about Colorado geography.
CO.SS4.2.1.a: Answer questions about Colorado regions using maps and other geographic tools.
CO.SS4.2.1.b: Use geographic grids, including latitude and longitude, to locate places and answer questions about maps and images of Colorado.
CO.SS4.2.1.c: Create and investigate geographic questions about Colorado in relation to other places.
CO.SS4.2.1.d: Illustrate, using geographic tools, how places in Colorado have changed and developed over time due to human activity.
CO.SS4.2.1.e: Describe similarities and differences between the physical geography of Colorado and its neighboring states.
CO.SS4.2.2: Examine the relationship between the physical environment and its effect on human activity.
CO.SS4.2.2.a: Describe how the physical environment provides opportunities for and places constraints on human activities.
CO.SS4.2.2.b: Explain how physical environments influence immigration into the state.
CO.SS4.2.2.c: Analyze how people use geographic factors in creating settlements and have adapted to and modified the local physical environment.
CO.SS4.2.2.d: Describe how places in Colorado are connected by movement of goods, services, and technology.
CO.SS4.3.1: Explain how people respond to positive and negative incentives.
CO.SS4.3.1.a: Define positive and negative economic incentives and describe how people typically respond to those incentives.
CO.SS4.3.1.b: In a given situation, create a plan of appropriate incentives to achieve a desired result.
CO.SS4.3.1.c: Give examples of the kinds of goods and services produced in Colorado, in different historical periods, and their connection to economic incentives.
CO.SS4.3.1.d: Explain how productive resources (natural, human, and capital) have influenced the types of goods produced and services provided in Colorado.
CO.SS4.4.1: Investigate multiple perspectives on civic issues.
CO.SS4.4.1.a: Give examples of issues faced by the state of Colorado and develop possible solutions.
CO.SS4.4.1.b: Provide supportive arguments for both sides of a current public policy debate involving diverse stakeholders.
CO.SS4.4.1.c: Discuss how various individuals and groups influence the way an issue affecting the state is viewed and resolved.
CO.SS4.4.1.d: Identify and use appropriate sources to investigate and analyze issues from multiple diverse perspectives.
CO.SS4.4.2: Describe the origins, structures, and functions of the Colorado government.
CO.SS4.4.2.a: Explain the historical foundation and events that led to the Colorado Constitution and the formation of the three branches of Colorado government.
CO.SS4.4.2.b: Identify and explain a variety of roles leaders, citizens, and others play in state government.
CO.SS4.4.2.c: Identify and explain the services the state government provides and how those services are funded.
CO.SS4.4.2.d: Describe how the decisions of the state government affect local governments and interact with the federal government and sovereign indigenous nations.
CO.SS4.4.2.e: Describe how a citizen might engage in local and state government to demonstrate their rights or initiate change.
CO.SS4.5.1: Determine the opportunity cost when making a choice.
CO.SS4.5.1.b: Determine the relationship between long-term goals and opportunity cost.
CO.SS4.5.1.c: Analyze scenarios of choices including opportunity cost.
CO.E5.1.1: Collaborate in discussions that serve various purposes and address various situations.
CO.E5.1.1.a: Listen to others' ideas and form their own opinions.
CO.E5.1.1.b: Engage effectively in a range of collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in groups, and teacher-led) with diverse partners on grade 5 topics and texts, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly.
CO.E5.1.1.b.i: Come to discussions prepared, having read or studied required material; explicitly draw on that preparation and other information known about the topic to explore ideas under discussion.
CO.E5.1.1.b.ii: Follow agreed-upon rules for discussions and carry out assigned roles.
CO.E5.1.1.b.iii: Pose and respond to specific questions by making comments that contribute to the discussion and elaborate on the remarks of others.
CO.E5.1.1.b.iv: Review the key ideas expressed and draw conclusions in light of information and knowledge gained from the discussions.
CO.E5.1.1.c: Summarize a written text read aloud or information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.
CO.E5.1.1.d: Summarize the points a speaker makes and explain how each claim is supported by reasons and evidence.
CO.E5.1.2: Present to express an opinion, persuade, or explain/provide information.
CO.E5.1.2.a: Report on a topic or text or present an opinion, sequencing ideas logically and using appropriate facts and relevant, descriptive details to support main ideas or themes.
CO.E5.1.2.b: Use appropriate eye contact and speak clearly at an understandable pace.
CO.E5.1.2.c: Include multimedia components (for example: graphics, sound) and visual displays in presentations when appropriate to enhance the development of main ideas or themes.
CO.E5.1.2.d: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and tasks.
CO.E5.1.2.e: Adapt language as appropriate to purpose: to persuade, explain/provide information, or express an opinion.
CO.E5.2.1: Apply strategies to interpret and analyze various types of literary texts.
CO.E5.2.1.a: Use pre-reading strategies, such as identifying a purpose for reading, generating questions to answers while reading, previewing sections of texts and activating prior knowledge.
CO.E5.2.1.b: Use Key Ideas and Details to:
CO.E5.2.1.b.i: Quote accurately from a text when explaining what the text says explicitly and when drawing inferences from the text.
CO.E5.2.1.b.ii: Determine a theme of a story, drama, or poem from details in the text, including how characters in a story or drama respond to challenges or how the speaker in a poem reflects upon a topic; summarize the text.
CO.E5.2.1.b.iii: Compare and contrast two or more character's points of view, settings, or events in a story or drama, drawing on specific details in the text (for example: how characters interact).
CO.E5.2.1.c.i: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including figurative language such as metaphors and similes.
CO.E5.2.1.c.ii: Explain how a series of chapters, scenes, or stanzas fits together to provide the overall structure of a particular story, drama, or poem.
CO.E5.2.1.c.iii: Describe how a narrator's or speaker's point of view influences how events are described.
CO.E5.2.1.c.iv: Locate information to support opinions, predictions, inferences, and identification of the author's message or theme.
CO.E5.2.1.d: Use Integration of Knowledge and Ideas to:
CO.E5.2.1.d.i: Analyze how visual and multimedia elements contribute to the meaning, tone, or beauty of a text (for example: graphic novel, multimedia presentation of fiction, folktale, myth, and poem).
CO.E5.2.1.d.ii: Compare and contrast stories in the same genre (for example: mysteries and adventure stories) on their approaches to similar themes and topics.
CO.E5.2.1.d.iii: Use knowledge of literary devices (such as imagery, rhythm, foreshadowing, and simple metaphors) to understand and respond to text.
CO.E5.2.1.e: Use Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity to:
CO.E5.2.1.e.i: By the end of the year, read and comprehend literature, including stories, dramas, and poetry, at the high end of the grades 4-5 text complexity band independently and proficiently.
CO.E5.2.2: Apply strategies to interpret and analyze various types of informational texts.
CO.E5.2.2.a: Use Key Ideas and Details to:
CO.E5.2.2.a.i: Quote accurately from a text when explaining what the text says explicitly and when drawing inferences from the text.
CO.E5.2.2.a.ii: Determine two or more main ideas of a text and explain how they are supported by key details; summarize the text.
CO.E5.2.2.a.iii: Explain the relationships or interactions between two or more individuals, events, ideas, or concepts in a historical, scientific, or technical text based on specific information in the text.
CO.E5.2.2.a.iv: Distinguish between fact and opinion, providing support for judgments made.
CO.E5.2.2.b.i: Determine the meaning of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases in a text relevant to a grade 5 topic or subject area.
CO.E5.2.2.b.ii: Compare and contrast the overall structure (for example: chronology, comparison, cause/effect, problem/solution) of events, ideas, concepts, or information in two or more texts.
CO.E5.2.2.b.iii: Analyze multiple accounts of the same event or topic, noting important similarities and differences in the point of view they represent.
CO.E5.2.2.b.iv: Use informational text features (such as bold type, headings, graphic organizers, numbering schemes, glossary) and text structures to organize or categorize information, to answer questions, or to perform specific tasks.
CO.E5.2.2.c: Use Integration of Knowledge and Ideas to:
CO.E5.2.2.c.i: Draw on information from multiple print or digital sources, demonstrating the ability to locate an answer to a question quickly or to solve a problem efficiently.
CO.E5.2.2.c.ii: Explain how an author uses reasons and evidence to support particular points in a text, identifying which reasons and evidence support which point(s).
CO.E5.2.2.c.iii: Integrate information from several texts on the same topic in order to write or speak about the subject knowledgeably.
CO.E5.2.2.d: Use Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity to:
CO.E5.2.2.d.i: By the end of the year, read and comprehend informational texts, including history/social studies, science, and technical texts, at the high end of the grades 4-5 text complexity band independently and proficiently.
CO.E5.2.3: Apply knowledge of word meanings (morphology) and word relationships to determine the meaning of unknown words in and out of context.
CO.E5.2.3.a: Know and apply grade-level phonics and word analysis skills in decoding words.
CO.E5.2.3.a.i: Use combined knowledge of all letter-sound correspondences, syllabication patterns, and morphology (for example, roots and affixes) to read accurately unfamiliar multisyllabic words in context and out of context.
CO.E5.2.3.b: Read with sufficient accuracy and fluency to support comprehension.
CO.E5.2.3.b.i: Read grade-level text with purpose and understanding.
CO.E5.2.3.b.ii: Read grade-level prose and poetry orally with accuracy, appropriate rate, and expression.
CO.E5.2.3.b.iii: Use context to confirm or self-correct word recognition and understanding, rereading as necessary.
CO.E5.2.3.c: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening.
CO.E5.2.3.c.i: Expand, combine, and reduce sentences for meaning, reader/listener interest, and style.
CO.E5.2.3.c.ii: Compare and contrast the varieties of English (for example: dialects, registers) used in stories, dramas, or poems.
CO.E5.2.3.d: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grade 5 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.
CO.E5.2.3.d.i: Use context (for example: cause/effect relationships and comparisons in text) as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.
CO.E5.2.3.d.ii: Use common, grade-appropriate Greek and Latin affixes and roots as clues to the meaning of a word (for example: photograph, photosynthesis).
CO.E5.2.3.d.iii: Consult reference materials (for example, dictionaries, glossaries, thesauruses), both print and digital, to find the pronunciation and determine or clarify the precise meaning of key words and phrases.
CO.E5.2.3.e: Read and identify the meaning of words with sophisticated prefixes and suffixes.
CO.E5.2.3.f: Apply knowledge of derivational suffixes that change the part of speech of the base word (for example active and activity).
CO.E5.2.3.g: Infer meaning of words using structural analysis, context, and knowledge of multiple meanings.
CO.E5.2.3.h: Read and identify the meaning of roots and related word families in which the pronunciation of the root does not change.
CO.E5.2.3.i: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.
CO.E5.2.3.i.i: Interpret figurative language, including similes and metaphors, in context.
CO.E5.2.3.i.ii: Recognize and explain the meaning of common idioms, adages, and proverbs.
CO.E5.2.3.i.iii: Use the relationship between particular words (for example: synonyms, antonyms, homographs) to better understand each of the words.
CO.E5.2.3.j: Acquire and use accurately grade-appropriate general academic and domain-specific words and phrases, including those that signal contrast, addition, and other logical relationships (for example: however, although, nevertheless, similarly, moreover, in addition).
CO.E5.3.1: Write opinion pieces on topics or texts, supporting a point of view with reasons and information, for a variety of purposes and audiences.
CO.E5.3.1.a: Introduce a topic or text clearly, state an opinion, and create an organizational structure in which ideas are logically grouped to support the writer's purpose.
CO.E5.3.1.b: Provide logically ordered reasons that are supported by facts and details.
CO.E5.3.1.c: Link opinion and reasons using words, phrases, and clauses (for example: consequently, specifically).
CO.E5.3.1.d: Provide a concluding statement or section related to the opinion presented.
CO.E5.3.2: Write informative/explanatory texts that provide a clear focus and the use of text features to group related information on a well- developed topic, using precise language and domain-specific vocabulary.
CO.E5.3.2.a: Introduce a topic clearly, provide a general observation and focus, and group related information logically; include formatting (for example: headings), illustrations, and multimedia when useful to aiding comprehension.
CO.E5.3.2.b: Develop the topic with facts, definitions, concrete details, quotations, or other information and examples related to the topic.
CO.E5.3.2.c: Link ideas within and across categories of information using words, phrases, and clauses (for example: in contrast, especially).
CO.E5.3.2.d: Use precise language and domain-specific vocabulary to inform about or explain the topic.
CO.E5.3.2.e: Provide a concluding statement or section related to the information or explanation presented.
CO.E5.3.3: Write engaging, real or imagined narratives using literary techniques, character development, sensory and descriptive details, and a variety of transition words to signal a clear sequence of events.
CO.E5.3.3.a: Orient the reader by establishing a situation and introducing a narrator and/or characters; organize an event sequence that unfolds naturally.
CO.E5.3.3.b: Use narrative techniques, such as dialogue, description, and pacing, to develop experiences and events or show the responses of characters to situations.
CO.E5.3.3.c: Use a variety of transitional words, phrases, and clauses to manage the sequence of events.
CO.E5.3.3.d: Use concrete words and phrases and sensory details to convey experiences and events precisely.
CO.E5.3.3.e: Provide a conclusion that follows from the narrated experiences or events.
CO.E5.3.4: Apply understanding of the conventions of Standard English grammar, usage, and mechanics to make meaning clear and to strengthen style.
CO.E5.3.4.a: Demonstrate command of the conventions of Standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.
CO.E5.3.4.a.i: Explain the function of conjunctions, prepositions, and interjections in general and their function in particular sentences.
CO.E5.3.4.a.ii: Form and use the perfect (for example: I had walked; I have walked; I will have walked) verb tenses.
CO.E5.3.4.a.iii: Use verb tense to convey various times, sequences, states, and conditions.
CO.E5.3.4.a.iv: Recognize and correct inappropriate shifts in verb tense.
CO.E5.3.4.a.v: Use correlative conjunctions (for example: either/or, neither/nor).
CO.E5.3.4.a.vi: Expand, combine, and reduce sentences for meaning, reader/listener interest, and style.
CO.E5.3.4.b: Demonstrate command of the conventions of Standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.
CO.E5.3.4.b.i: Use punctuation to separate items in a series.
CO.E5.3.4.b.ii: Use a comma to separate an introductory element from the rest of the sentence.
CO.E5.3.4.b.iii: Use a comma to set off the words yes and no (for example: Yes, thank you), to set off a tag question from the rest of the sentence (for example: It's true, isn't it?), and to indicate direct address (for example: Is that you, Steve?).
CO.E5.3.4.b.iv: Use underlining, quotation marks, or italics to indicate titles of works.
CO.E5.3.4.b.v: Spell grade-appropriate words correctly, consulting references as needed.
CO.E5.3.4.c: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development and organization are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.
CO.E5.3.4.d: With guidance and support from peers and adults, develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach.
CO.E5.3.4.e: With some guidance and support from adults, use technology, including the Internet, to produce and publish writing as well as to interact and collaborate with others.
CO.E5.3.4.f: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of discipline-specific tasks, purposes, and audiences.
CO.E5.4.1: Research to locate, summarize, synthesize and document information from print and digital sources, and communicate findings appropriately.
CO.E5.4.1.a: Conduct short research projects that use several sources to build knowledge through investigation of different aspects of a topic.
CO.E5.4.1.a.ii: Demonstrate comprehension of information with supporting logical and valid inferences.
CO.E5.4.1.a.iii: Develop and present a brief (oral or written) research report with clear focus and supporting detail for an intended audience.
CO.E5.4.1.b: Recall relevant information from experiences or gather relevant information from print and digital sources; summarize or paraphrase information in notes and finished work, and provide a list of sources.
CO.E5.4.1.b.i: Develop relevant supporting visual information (for example: charts, maps, graphs, photo evidence, models).
CO.E5.4.1.b.ii: Provide documentation of sources used in a grade-appropriate format.
CO.E5.4.1.c: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.
CO.E5.4.1.c.i: Apply grade 5 Reading standards to literature (for example: “Compare and contrast two or more characters, settings, or events in a story or a drama, drawing on specific details in the text [for example: how characters interact]”).
CO.E5.4.1.c.ii: Apply grade 5 Reading standards to informational texts (for example: “Explain how an author uses reasons and evidence to support particular points in a text, identifying which reasons and evidence support which point[s]”).
CO.M5.NBT.A.1: Recognize that in a multi-digit number, a digit in one place represents `10` times as much as it represents in the place to its right and `1/10` of what it represents in the place to its left.
CO.M5.NBT.A.2: Explain patterns in the number of zeros of the product when multiplying a number by powers of `10`, and explain patterns in the placement of the decimal point when a decimal is multiplied or divided by a power of `10`. Use whole-number exponents to denote powers of `10`.
CO.M5.NBT.A.3: Read, write, and compare decimals to thousandths.
CO.M5.NBT.A.3.a: Read and write decimals to thousandths using base-ten numerals, number names, and expanded form, e.g., `347.392=3xx100+4xx10+7xx1+3xx(1/10)+9xx(1/100)+2xx(1/1000)`.
CO.M5.NBT.A.3.b: Compare two decimals to thousandths based on meanings of the digits in each place, using `>,=,and<` symbols to record the results of comparisons.
CO.M5.NBT.A.4: Use place value understanding to round decimals to any place.
CO.M5.NBT.B: Perform operations with multi-digit whole numbers and with decimals to hundredths.
CO.M5.NBT.B.5: Fluently multiply multi-digit whole numbers using the standard algorithm.
CO.M5.NBT.B.6: Find whole-number quotients of whole numbers with up to four-digit dividends and two-digit divisors, using strategies based on place value, the properties of operations, and/or the relationship between multiplication and division. Illustrate and explain the calculation by using equations, rectangular arrays, and/or area models.
CO.M5.NBT.B.7: Add, subtract, multiply, and divide decimals to hundredths, using concrete models or drawings and strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction; relate the strategy to a written method and explain the reasoning used.
CO.M5.NF.A: Use equivalent fractions as a strategy to add and subtract fractions.
CO.M5.NF.A.1: Add and subtract fractions with unlike denominators (including mixed numbers) by replacing given fractions with equivalent fractions in such a way as to produce an equivalent sum or difference of fractions with like denominators.
CO.M5.NF.A.2: Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions referring to the same whole, including cases of unlike denominators, e.g., by using visual fraction models or equations to represent the problem. Use benchmark fractions and number sense of fractions to estimate mentally and assess the reasonableness of answers.
CO.M5.NF.B: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication and division.
CO.M5.NF.B.3: Interpret a fraction as division of the numerator by the denominator `(a/b=a-:b)`. Solve word problems involving division of whole numbers leading to answers in the form of fractions or mixed numbers, e.g., by using visual fraction models or equations to represent the problem.
CO.M5.NF.B.4: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication to multiply a fraction or whole number by a fraction.
CO.M5.NF.B.4.a: Interpret the product `a/bxxq` as a parts of a partition of `q` into `b` equal parts; equivalently, as the result of a sequence of operations `axxq-:b`.
CO.M5.NF.B.4.b: Find the area of a rectangle with fractional side lengths by tiling it with unit squares of the appropriate unit fraction side lengths, and show that the area is the same as would be found by multiplying the side lengths. Multiply fractional side lengths to find areas of rectangles, and represent fraction products as rectangular areas.
CO.M5.NF.B.5.a: Comparing the size of a product to the size of one factor on the basis of the size of the other factor, without performing the indicated multiplication.
CO.M5.NF.B.5.b: Explaining why multiplying a given number by a fraction greater than `1` results in a product greater than the given number (recognizing multiplication by whole numbers greater than `1` as a familiar case); explaining why multiplying a given number by a fraction less than `1` results in a product smaller than the given number; and relating the principle of fraction equivalence `a/b=(nxxa)/(nxxb)` to the effect of multiplying `a/b` by `1`.
CO.M5.NF.B.6: Solve real-world problems involving multiplication of fractions and mixed numbers, e.g., by using visual fraction models or equations to represent the problem.
CO.M5.NF.B.7: Apply and extend previous understandings of division to divide unit fractions by whole numbers and whole numbers by unit fractions.
CO.M5.NF.B.7.a: Interpret division of a unit fraction by a non-zero whole number, and compute such quotients.
CO.M5.NF.B.7.b: Interpret division of a whole number by a unit fraction, and compute such quotients.
CO.M5.NF.B.7.c: Solve real-world problems involving division of unit fractions by non-zero whole numbers and division of whole numbers by unit fractions, e.g., by using visual fraction models and equations to represent the problem.
CO.M5.OA.A.1: Use grouping symbols (parentheses, brackets, or braces) in numerical expressions, and evaluate expressions with these symbols.
CO.M5.OA.A.2: Write simple expressions that record calculations with numbers, and interpret numerical expressions without evaluating them.
CO.M5.OA.B.3: Generate two numerical patterns using two given rules. Identify apparent relationships between corresponding terms. Form ordered pairs consisting of corresponding terms from the two patterns, and graph the ordered pairs on a coordinate plane.
CO.M5.MD.A: Convert like measurement units within a given measurement system.
CO.M5.MD.A.1: Convert among different-sized standard measurement units within a given measurement system (e.g., convert `5` `text(cm)` to `0.05` `text(m)`), and use these conversions in solving multi-step, real-world problems.
CO.M5.MD.B.2: Make a line plot to display a data set of measurements in fractions of a unit `(1/2,1/4,1/8)`. Use operations on fractions for this grade to solve problems involving information presented in line plots.
CO.M5.MD.C: Geometric measurement: Understand concepts of volume and relate volume to multiplication and to addition.
CO.M5.MD.C.3: Recognize volume as an attribute of solid figures and understand concepts of volume measurement.
CO.M5.MD.C.3.a: A cube with side length`1` `text(unit)`, called a “unit cube,” is said to have “one cubic unit” of volume and can be used to measure volume.
CO.M5.MD.C.3.b: A solid figure which can be packed without gaps or overlaps using `n` unit cubes is said to have a volume of `n` cubic units.
CO.M5.MD.C.4: Measure volumes by counting unit cubes, using cubic cm, cubic in, cubic ft, and improvised units.
CO.M5.MD.C.5: Relate volume to the operations of multiplication and addition and solve real-world and mathematical problems involving volume.
CO.M5.MD.C.5.a: Model the volume of a right rectangular prism with whole-number side lengths by packing it with unit cubes, and show that the volume is the same as would be found by multiplying the edge lengths, equivalently by multiplying the height by the area of the base. Represent threefold whole-number products as volumes, e.g., to represent the associative property of multiplication.
CO.M5.MD.C.5.b: Apply the formulas `V=lxxwxxhandV=bxxh` for rectangular prisms to find volumes of right rectangular prisms with whole-number edge lengths in the context of solving real-world and mathematical problems.
CO.M5.MD.C.5.c: Use the additive nature of volume to find volumes of solid figures composed of two non-overlapping right rectangular prisms by adding the volumes of the non-overlapping parts, applying this technique to solve real-world problems.
CO.M5.G.A: Graph points on the coordinate plane to solve real-world and mathematical problems.
CO.M5.G.A.1: Use a pair of perpendicular number lines, called axes, to define a coordinate system, with the intersection of the lines (the origin) arranged to coincide with the `0` on each line and a given point in the plane located by using an ordered pair of numbers, called its coordinates. Understand that the first number indicates how far to travel from the origin in the direction of one axis, and the second number indicates how far to travel in the direction of the second axis, with the convention that the names of the two axes and the coordinates correspond (e.g., `xtext(-axis)andxtext(-coordinate),ytext(-axis)` and y- coordinate).
CO.M5.G.A.2: Represent real-world and mathematical problems by graphing points in the first quadrant of the coordinate plane, and interpret coordinate values of points in the context of the situation.
CO.M5.G.B: Classify two-dimensional figures into categories based on their properties.
CO.M5.G.B.3: Explain that attributes belonging to a category of two-dimensional figures also belong to all subcategories of that category.
CO.M5.G.B.4: Classify two-dimensional figures in a hierarchy based on properties.
CO.S5.1.1: Matter exists as particles that are too small to be seen; measurements of a variety of observable properties can be used to identify particular materials.
CO.S5.1.1.a: Develop a model to describe that matter is made of particles too small to be seen.
CO.S5.1.1.b: Make observations and measurements to identify materials based on their properties.
CO.S5.1.2: Chemical Reactions that occur when substances are mixed can be identified by the emergence of substances with different properties; the total mass remains the same.
CO.S5.1.2.a: Measure and graph quantities to provide evidence that regardless of the type of change that occurs when heating, cooling or mixing substances, the total weight of matter is conserved.
CO.S5.1.2.b: Conduct an investigation to determine whether the mixing of two or more substances results in new substances.
CO.S5.1.3: The gravitational force of Earth acting on an object near Earth's surface pulls that object toward the planet's center.
CO.S5.1.3.a: Support an argument that the gravitational force exerted by Earth on objects is directed down.
CO.S5.1.4: The energy released from food was once energy from the sun.
CO.S5.1.4.a: Use models to describe that energy in animals' food (used for body repair, growth and motion and to maintain body warmth) was once energy from the sun.
CO.S5.2.1: Plants acquire their material from growth chiefly from air and water.
CO.S5.2.1.a: Support an argument that plants get the materials they need for growth chiefly from air and water.
CO.S5.2.2: Matter cycles between air and soil and among plants, animals and microbes as these organisms live and die.
CO.S5.2.2.a: Develop a model to describe the movement of matter among plants, animals, decomposers, and the environment.
CO.S5.3.1: Stars range greatly in size and distance from Earth, and this can explain their relative brightness.
CO.S5.3.1.a: Support an argument that differences in the apparent brightness of the sun compared to other stars is due to their relative distances from the Earth.
CO.S5.3.2: Earth's orbit and rotation and the orbit of the moon around earth cause observable patterns.
CO.S5.3.2.a: Represent data in graphical displays to reveal patterns of daily changes in length and direction of shadows, day and night, and the seasonal appearance of some stars in the night sky.
CO.S5.3.3: Earth's major systems interact in multiple ways to affect Earth's surface materials and processes.
CO.S5.3.3.a: Develop a model using an example to describe ways the geosphere, biosphere, hydrosphere and/or atmosphere interact.
CO.S5.3.4: Most of Earth's water is in the ocean and much of Earth's freshwater in glaciers or underground.
CO.S5.3.4.a: Describe and graph the amounts and percentages of saltwater and freshwater in various reservoirs to provide evidence about the distribution of water on Earth.
CO.S5.3.5: Societal activities have had major effects on land, ocean, atmosphere and even outer space.
CO.S5.3.5.a: Obtain and combine information about ways individual communities use science ideas to protect the Earth's resources and environment.
CO.SS5.1: Analyze primary and secondary sources from multiple points of view to develop an understanding of early United States history.
CO.SS5.1.a: Recognize how historical context can affect the perspective of historical sources.
CO.SS5.1.c: Interpret timelines of eras and themes in North America from early Indigenous Peoples through the European Age of Exploration/post-Columbian colonization and the establishment of the United States Government.
CO.SS5.1.d: Analyze cartoons, artifacts, artwork, charts, and graphs related to eras and themes in early North America.
CO.SS5.2: Examine the historical eras, individuals, groups, ideas, and themes in North America from early Indigenous Peoples through the European Age of Exploration/post-Columbian colonization and the establishment of the United States Government.
CO.SS5.2.a: Explain interactions among various groups such as Indigenous Peoples, enslaved individuals (both Indigenous and African), and European colonists.
CO.SS5.2.b: Identify and describe the contributions of significant individuals and groups of Indigenous Peoples, enslaved individuals, and European colonists through the American Revolution.
CO.SS5.2.c: Describe the political, social, and economic reasons for the settlement of the European and American colonies and how it affected Indigenous Peoples and enslaved Africans.
CO.SS5.2.d: Analyze important political, social, economic, and military developments leading to and during the American Revolution.
CO.SS5.2.e: Investigate causes and effects of significant events in early United States history.
CO.SS5.2.1: Use geographic tools and sources to research and answer questions about United States geography.
CO.SS5.2.1.a: Answer questions about regions of North America and the United States using various types of maps.
CO.SS5.2.1.b: Use geographic tools to identify, locate, and describe places and regions in North America and the United States and suggest reasons for their location.
CO.SS5.2.1.c: Describe the influence of accessible resources on the development of local and regional communities throughout North America and the United States.
CO.SS5.2.2: Examine causes and consequences of movement.
CO.SS5.2.2.a: Identify variables associated with discovery, exploration, and migration.
CO.SS5.2.2.b: Explain migration, trade, and cultural patterns that result from interactions among people, groups, and cultures.
CO.SS5.2.2.c: Describe and analyze how specific physical and political features influenced historical events, movements, and adaptation to the environment.
CO.SS5.2.2.d: Analyze how cooperation and conflict among diverse groups of people contribute(d) to political, economic, and social divisions in the United States.
CO.SS5.2.2.e: Give examples of the influence of geography on the history of the United States.
CO.SS5.3.1: Explain how patterns of trade shaped the development of Early America.
CO.SS5.3.1.a: Identify examples of the productive resources and explain how they are used to produce goods and services.
CO.SS5.3.1.b: Compare ways in which people and communities exchanged goods and services.
CO.SS5.3.1.c: Identify the goods and services that were traded among different cultures and regions.
CO.SS5.3.1.d: Describe how patterns of trade evolved within Early America.
CO.SS5.3.1.e: Explain some of the challenges that American colonists faced that would eventually lead them to the creation of commercial banks.
CO.SS5.4.1: Construct an understanding of the foundations, rights, and responsibilities of citizenship in the United States.
CO.SS5.4.1.a: Describe and explain examples of individual rights as a foundation of citizenship.
CO.SS5.4.1.b: Give examples of group and individual actions that illustrate civic ideals in the founding of the United States.
CO.SS5.4.1.c: Discuss how the concept of citizenship changed over time in the early American colonies.
CO.SS5.4.2: Investigate the origins, structures, and functions of the United States government.
CO.SS5.4.2.a: Explain the foundational documents and significance of the events that led to the establishment of the United States government.
CO.SS5.4.2.b: Identify political principles of American democracy and how the Constitution and Bill of Rights reflect and preserve these principles.
CO.SS5.4.2.c: Explain the origins, structures, and functions of the three branches of the United States government and the relationships among them.
CO.SS5.4.2.d: Describe how the Constitution balances the power of national and state governments.
CO.SS5.5.1: Examine how individuals use financial institutions to manage personal finances.
CO.SS5.5.1.c: Distinguish between different types of financial institutions such as banks and credit unions, and the services provided.
CO.SS5.5.1.d: Create a way to keep track of money spent and money saved.
CO.E6.1.1: Employ appropriate presentation and collaboration strategies to meet the needs of a given task and purpose.
CO.E6.1.1.a: Engage effectively in a range of collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in groups, and teacher-led) with diverse partners on grade 6 topics, texts, and issues, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly.
CO.E6.1.1.a.i: Come to discussions prepared, having read or studied required material; explicitly draw on that preparation by referring to evidence on the topic, text, or issue to probe and reflect on ideas under discussion.
CO.E6.1.1.a.ii: Follow rules for collegial discussions, set specific goals and deadlines, and define individual roles as needed.
CO.E6.1.1.a.iii: Pose and respond to specific questions with elaboration and detail by making comments that contribute to the topic, text, or issue under discussion.
CO.E6.1.1.a.iv: Review the key ideas expressed and demonstrate understanding of multiple perspectives through reflection and paraphrasing.
CO.E6.1.1.b: Interpret information presented in diverse media and formats (for example: visually, quantitatively, orally) and explain how it contributes to a topic, text, or issue under study.
CO.E6.1.1.c: Delineate a speaker's argument and specific claims, distinguishing claims that are supported by reasons and evidence from claims that are not.
CO.E6.1.2: Develop, organize, and present ideas and opinions effectively.
CO.E6.1.2.a: Present claims and findings, sequencing ideas logically and using pertinent descriptions, facts, and details to accentuate main ideas or themes; use appropriate eye contact, adequate volume, and clear pronunciation.
CO.E6.1.2.b: Include multimedia components (for example: graphics, images, music, sound) and visual displays in presentations to clarify information.
CO.E6.1.2.c: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate.
CO.E6.2.1: Analyze literary elements within different types of literature to make meaning.
CO.E6.2.1.a: Use Key Ideas and Details to:
CO.E6.2.1.a.i: Cite textual evidence to support analysis of what the text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text.
CO.E6.2.1.a.ii: Determine a theme or central idea of a text and how it is conveyed through particular details; provide a summary of the text distinct from personal opinions or judgments.
CO.E6.2.1.a.iii: Describe how a particular story's or drama's plot unfolds in a series of episodes as well as how the characters respond or change as the plot moves toward a resolution.
CO.E6.2.1.b.i: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including figurative and connotative meanings; analyze the impact of a specific word choice on meaning and tone.
CO.E6.2.1.b.ii: Analyze how a particular sentence, chapter, scene, or stanza fits into the overall structure of a text and contributes to the development of the theme, setting, or plot.
CO.E6.2.1.b.iii: Explain how an author develops the point of view of the narrator or speaker in a text.
CO.E6.2.1.c: Use Integration of Knowledge and Ideas to:
CO.E6.2.1.c.i: Compare and contrast the experience of reading a story, drama, or poem to listening to or viewing an audio, video, or live version of the text, including contrasting what they “see” and “hear” when reading the text to what they perceive when they listen or watch.
CO.E6.2.1.c.ii: Compare and contrast texts in different forms or genres (for example: stories and poems; historical novels and fantasy stories) in terms of their approaches to similar themes and topics.
CO.E6.2.1.d: Use Range of Reading and Complexity of Text to:
CO.E6.2.1.d.i: By the end of the year, read and comprehend literature, including stories, dramas, and poems, in the grades 6-8 text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.
CO.E6.2.2: Analyze organization and structure of informational text to make meaning.
CO.E6.2.2.a: Use Key Ideas and Details to:
CO.E6.2.2.a.i: Cite textual evidence to support analysis of what the text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text.
CO.E6.2.2.a.ii: Determine a central idea of a text and how it is conveyed through particular details; provide a summary of the text distinct from personal opinions or judgments.
CO.E6.2.2.a.iii: Analyze in detail how a key individual, event, or idea is introduced, illustrated, and elaborated on in a text (for example: through examples or anecdotes).
CO.E6.2.2.b.i: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including figurative, connotative, and technical meanings.
CO.E6.2.2.b.ii: Analyze how a particular sentence, paragraph, chapter, or section fits into the overall structure of a text and contributes to the development of the ideas.
CO.E6.2.2.b.iii: Determine an author's point of view or purpose in a text and explain how it is conveyed in the text.
CO.E6.2.2.c: Use Integration of Knowledge and Ideas to:
CO.E6.2.2.c.i: Integrate information presented in different media or formats (for example: visually, quantitatively) as well as in words to develop a coherent understanding of a topic or issue.
CO.E6.2.2.c.ii: Trace and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, distinguishing claims that are supported by reasons and evidence from claims that are not.
CO.E6.2.2.c.iii: Compare and contrast one author's presentation of events with that of another (for example: a memoir written by and a biography on the same person).
CO.E6.2.2.d: Use Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity to:
CO.E6.2.2.d.i: By the end of the year, read and comprehend literary nonfiction in the grades 6-8 text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.
CO.E6.2.3: Apply knowledge of word relationships, word structures, and sentence structures to determine the meaning of new words in context.
CO.E6.2.3.a: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grade 6 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.
CO.E6.2.3.a.i: Use context (for example: the overall meaning of a sentence or paragraph; a word's position or function in a sentence) as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.
CO.E6.2.3.a.ii: Use common, grade-appropriate Greek or Latin affixes and roots as clues to the meaning of a word (for example: audience, auditory, audible).
CO.E6.2.3.a.iii: Consult reference materials (for example: dictionaries, glossaries, thesauruses), both print and digital, to find the pronunciation of a word or determine or clarify its precise meaning or its part of speech.
CO.E6.2.3.a.iv: Verify the preliminary determination of the meaning of a word or phrase (for example: by checking the inferred meaning in context or in a dictionary).
CO.E6.2.3.b: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.
CO.E6.2.3.b.i: Interpret figures of speech (for example: personification) in context.
CO.E6.2.3.b.ii: Use the relationship between particular words (for example: cause/effect, part/whole, item/category) to better understand each of the words.
CO.E6.2.3.b.iii: Distinguish among the connotations (associations) of words with similar denotations (definitions) (for example: stingy, scrimping, economical, unwasteful, and thrifty).
CO.E6.2.3.c: Acquire and use accurately grade-appropriate general academic and domain-specific words and phrases; gather vocabulary knowledge when considering a word or phrase important to comprehension or expression.
CO.E6.3.1: Write arguments that support claim(s) using clear reasons, relevant evidence, credible sources, and a formal style.
CO.E6.3.1.a: Write arguments to support claims with clear reasons and relevant evidence.
CO.E6.3.1.a.i: Introduce claim(s) and organize the reasons and evidence clearly.
CO.E6.3.1.a.ii: Support claim(s) with clear reasons and relevant evidence, using credible sources and demonstrating an understanding of the topic or text.
CO.E6.3.1.a.iii: Use words, phrases, and clauses to clarify the relationships among claim(s) and reasons.
CO.E6.3.1.a.iv: Establish and maintain a formal style.
CO.E6.3.1.a.v: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from the argument presented.
CO.E6.3.2: Write informative/explanatory texts characterized by appropriate organization, ample development, precise language and formal style.
CO.E6.3.2.a: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine a topic and convey ideas, concepts, and information through the selection, organization, and analysis of relevant content.
CO.E6.3.2.a.i: Introduce a topic; organize ideas, concepts, and information, using strategies such as definition, classification, comparison/contrast, and cause/effect; include formatting (for example: headings), graphics (for example: charts, tables), and multimedia when useful to aiding comprehension.
CO.E6.3.2.a.ii: Develop the topic with relevant facts, definitions, concrete details, quotations, or other information and examples.
CO.E6.3.2.a.iii: Use appropriate transitions to clarify the relationships among ideas and concepts.
CO.E6.3.2.a.iv: Use precise language and domain-specific vocabulary to inform about or explain the topic.
CO.E6.3.2.a.v: Establish and maintain a formal style.
CO.E6.3.2.a.vi: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from the information or explanation presented.
CO.E6.3.3: Write engaging real or imagined narratives using techniques such as sensory language, dialogue, description and sequencing to convey experiences and events.
CO.E6.3.3.a: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, relevant descriptive details, and well-structured event sequences.
CO.E6.3.3.a.i: Engage and orient the reader by establishing a context and introducing a narrator and/or characters; organize an event sequence that unfolds naturally and logically.
CO.E6.3.3.a.ii: Use narrative techniques, such as dialogue, pacing, and description, to develop experiences, events, and/or characters.
CO.E6.3.3.a.iii: Use a variety of transition words, phrases, and clauses to convey sequence and signal shifts from one time frame or setting to another.
CO.E6.3.3.a.iv: Use precise words and phrases, relevant descriptive details, and sensory language to convey experiences and events.
CO.E6.3.3.a.v: Provide a conclusion that follows from the narrated experiences or events.
CO.E6.3.3.a.vi: Use stylistic techniques (for example: alliteration, onomatopoeia, rhyme scheme); figurative language (for example: simile, metaphor, personification); and graphic elements (for example: capital letters, line length, word position) to express personal or narrative voice.
CO.E6.3.4: Plan, draft, edit, and revise as needed to craft clear and coherent writing that demonstrates a grasp of standard conventions for grammar, usage, and mechanics as well as a style appropriate for purpose and audience.
CO.E6.3.4.a: Demonstrate command of the conventions of Standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.
CO.E6.3.4.a.i: Ensure that pronouns are in the proper case (subjective, objective, and possessive).
CO.E6.3.4.a.iii: Recognize and correct inappropriate shifts in pronoun number and person.
CO.E6.3.4.a.iv: Recognize and correct vague pronouns (i.e., ones with unclear or ambiguous antecedents).
CO.E6.3.4.a.v: Recognize variations from Standard English in their own and others' writing and speaking, and identify and use strategies to improve expression in conventional language.
CO.E6.3.4.b: Demonstrate command of the conventions of Standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.
CO.E6.3.4.b.i: Use punctuation (commas, parentheses, dashes) to set off nonrestrictive/parenthetical elements.
CO.E6.3.4.b.ii: Correctly spell frequently used words and consult reference materials (for example: dictionaries, both print and digital, spell check, and/or trusted peers and/or adults) to determine the spelling of less frequent vocabulary.
CO.E6.3.4.c: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening.
CO.E6.3.4.c.i: Vary sentence patterns for meaning, reader/listener interest, and style.
CO.E6.3.4.c.ii: Maintain consistency in style and tone.
CO.E6.3.4.d: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.
CO.E6.3.4.e: With some guidance and support from peers and adults, develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach.
CO.E6.3.4.f: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce and publish writing as well as to interact and collaborate with others.
CO.E6.3.4.g: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of discipline-specific tasks, purposes, and audiences.
CO.E6.4.1: Pose research question(s), gather, synthesize, and credit relevant and credible resources, and present findings.
CO.E6.4.1.a: Conduct short research projects to answer a question, drawing on several sources and refocusing the inquiry when appropriate.
CO.E6.4.1.b: Gather relevant information from multiple print and digital sources; assess the credibility of each source; and quote or paraphrase the data and conclusions of others while avoiding plagiarism and providing basic bibliographic information for sources.
CO.E6.4.1.c: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.
CO.E6.4.1.c.i: Apply grade 6 Reading standards to literature (for example: “Compare and contrast texts in different forms or genres [for example: stories and poems; historical novels and fantasy stories] in terms of their approaches to similar themes and topics”).
CO.E6.4.1.c.ii: Apply grade 6 Reading standards to literary nonfiction (for example: “Trace and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, distinguishing claims that are supported by reasons and evidence from claims that are not”).
CO.M6.RP.A: Understand ratio concepts and use ratio reasoning to solve problems.
CO.M6.RP.A.1: Apply the concept of a ratio and use ratio language to describe a ratio relationship between two quantities.
CO.M6.RP.A.2: Apply the concept of a unit rate `a/b` associated with a ratio `a:b` with `b!=0`, and use rate language in the context of a ratio relationship.
CO.M6.RP.A.3: Use ratio and rate reasoning to solve real-world and mathematical problems, e.g., by reasoning about tables of equivalent ratios, tape diagrams, double number line diagrams, or equations.
CO.M6.RP.A.3.a: Make tables of equivalent ratios relating quantities with whole-number measurements, find missing values in the tables, and plot the pairs of values on the coordinate plane. Use tables to compare ratios.
CO.M6.RP.A.3.b: Solve unit rate problems including those involving unit pricing and constant speed.
CO.M6.RP.A.3.c: Find a percent of a quantity as a rate `text(per)` `100` (e.g., `30%` of a quantity means `30/100` times the quantity); solve problems involving finding the whole, given a part and the percent.
CO.M6.RP.A.3.d: Use ratio reasoning to convert measurement units; manipulate and transform units appropriately when multiplying or dividing quantities.
CO.M6.NS.A: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication and division to divide fractions by fractions.
CO.M6.NS.A.1: Interpret and compute quotients of fractions, and solve word problems involving division of fractions by fractions, e.g., by using visual fraction models and equations to represent the problem.
CO.M6.NS.B: Compute fluently with multi-digit numbers and find common factors and multiples.
CO.M6.NS.B.2: Fluently divide multi-digit numbers using the standard algorithm.
CO.M6.NS.B.3: Fluently add, subtract, multiply, and divide multi-digit decimals using the standard algorithm for each operation.
CO.M6.NS.B.4: Find the greatest common factor of two whole numbers less than or equal to `100` and the least common multiple of two whole numbers less than or equal to `12`. Use the distributive property to express a sum of two whole numbers `1-100` with a common factor as a multiple of a sum of two whole numbers with no common factor.
CO.M6.NS.C: Apply and extend previous understandings of numbers to the system of rational numbers.
CO.M6.NS.C.5: Explain why positive and negative numbers are used together to describe quantities having opposite directions or values (e.g., temperature above/below zero, elevation above/below sea level, credits/debits, positive/negative electric charge); use positive and negative numbers to represent quantities in real-world contexts, explaining the meaning of `0` in each situation.
CO.M6.NS.C.6: Describe a rational number as a point on the number line. Extend number line diagrams and coordinate axes familiar from previous grades to represent points on the line and in the plane with negative number coordinates.
CO.M6.NS.C.6.a: Use opposite signs of numbers as indicating locations on opposite sides of `0` on the number line; identify that the opposite of the opposite of a number is the number itself, e.g., `-(-3)=3`, and that `0` is its own opposite.
CO.M6.NS.C.6.b: Understand signs of numbers in ordered pairs as indicating locations in quadrants of the coordinate plane; explain that when two ordered pairs differ only by signs, the locations of the points are related by reflections across one or both axes.
CO.M6.NS.C.6.c: Find and position integers and other rational numbers on a horizontal or vertical number line diagram; find and position pairs of integers and other rational numbers on a coordinate plane.
CO.M6.NS.C.7: Order and find absolute value of rational numbers.
CO.M6.NS.C.7.a: Interpret statements of inequality as statements about the relative position of two numbers on a number line diagram.
CO.M6.NS.C.7.b: Write, interpret, and explain statements of order for rational numbers in real-world contexts.
CO.M6.NS.C.7.c: Define the absolute value of a rational number as its distance from `0` on the number line; interpret absolute value as magnitude for a positive or negative quantity in a real-world situation.
CO.M6.NS.C.7.d: Distinguish comparisons of absolute value from statements about order.
CO.M6.NS.C.8: Solve real-world and mathematical problems by graphing points in all four quadrants of the coordinate plane. Include use of coordinates and absolute value to find distances between points with the same first coordinate or the same second coordinate.
CO.M6.EE.A: Apply and extend previous understandings of arithmetic to algebraic expressions.
CO.M6.EE.A.1: Write and evaluate numerical expressions involving whole-number exponents.
CO.M6.EE.A.2: Write, read, and evaluate expressions in which letters stand for numbers.
CO.M6.EE.A.2.a: Write expressions that record operations with numbers and with letters standing for numbers.
CO.M6.EE.A.2.b: Identify parts of an expression using mathematical terms (sum, term, product, factor, quotient, coefficient); view one or more parts of an expression as a single entity.
CO.M6.EE.A.2.c: Evaluate expressions at specific values of their variables. Include expressions that arise from formulas used in real-world problems. Perform arithmetic operations, including those involving whole-number exponents, in the conventional order when there are no parentheses to specify a particular order (Order of Operations).
CO.M6.EE.A.3: Apply the properties of operations to generate equivalent expressions.
CO.M6.EE.A.4: Identify when two expressions are equivalent (i.e., when the two expressions name the same number regardless of which value is substituted into them).
CO.M6.EE.B: Reason about and solve one-variable equations and inequalities.
CO.M6.EE.B.5: Describe solving an equation or inequality as a process of answering a question: Which values from a specified set, if any, make the equation or inequality true? Use substitution to determine whether a given number in a specified set makes an equation or inequality true.
CO.M6.EE.B.6: Use variables to represent numbers and write expressions when solving a real-world or mathematical problem; recognize that a variable can represent an unknown number, or, depending on the purpose at hand, any number in a specified set.
CO.M6.EE.B.7: Solve real-world and mathematical problems by writing and solving equations of the form `x+-p=qandpx=q` for cases in which `p,qandx` are all nonnegative rational numbers.
CO.M6.EE.B.8: Write an inequality of the form `x>c,x>=c,x<c,orx<=c` to represent a constraint or condition in a real-world or mathematical problem. Show that inequalities of the form `x>c,x>=c,x<c,orx<=c` have infinitely many solutions; represent solutions of such inequalities on number line diagrams.
CO.M6.EE.C: Represent and analyze quantitative relationships between dependent and independent variables.
CO.M6.EE.C.9: Use variables to represent two quantities in a real-world problem that change in relationship to one another; write an equation to express one quantity, thought of as the dependent variable, in terms of the other quantity, thought of as the independent variable. Analyze the relationship between the dependent and independent variables using graphs and tables, and relate these to the equation.
CO.M6.SP.A.1: Identify a statistical question as one that anticipates variability in the data related to the question and accounts for it in the answers.
CO.M6.SP.A.2: Demonstrate that a set of data collected to answer a statistical question has a distribution that can be described by its center, spread, and overall shape.
