CO.S9-12.1.5: Forces at a distance are explained by fields that can transfer energy and can be described in terms of the arrangement and properties of the interacting objects and the distance between them.
CO.S9-12.1.5.a: Use mathematical representations of Newton's Law of Gravitation and Coulomb's Law to describe and predict the gravitational and electrostatic forces between objects.
CO.S9-12.1.5.b: Plan and conduct an investigation to provide evidence that an electric current can produce a magnetic field and that a changing magnetic field can produce an electric current.
CO.S9-12.1.5.c: Communicate scientific and technical information about why the molecular- level structure is important in the functioning of designed materials.
CO.S9-12.1.6: Energy is a quantitative property of a system that depends on the motion and interactions of matter and radiation within that system.
CO.S9-12.1.6.a: Create a computational model to calculate the change in the energy of one component in a system when the change in energy of the other component(s) and energy flows in and out of the system are known.
CO.S9-12.1.6.b: Develop and use models to illustrate that energy at the macroscopic scale can be accounted for as a combination of energy associated with the motion of particles (objects) and energy associated with the relative positions of particles (objects).
CO.S9-12.1.6.c: Design, build, and refine a device that works within given constraints to convert one form of energy into another form of energy.
CO.S9-12.1.7: Energy cannot be created or destroyed, but it can be transported from one place to another and transferred between systems.
CO.S9-12.1.7.a: Create a computational model to calculate the change in the energy of one component in a system when the change in energy of the other component(s) and energy flows in and out of the system are known.
CO.S9-12.1.7.b: Plan and conduct an investigation to provide evidence that the transfer of thermal energy when two components of different temperature are combined within a closed system results in a more uniform energy distribution among the components in the system (second law of thermodynamics).
CO.S9-12.1.8: Force fields (gravitational, electric, and magnetic) contain energy and can transmit energy across space from one object to another.
CO.S9-12.1.8.a: Develop and use a model of two objects interacting through electric or magnetic fields to illustrate the forces between objects and the changes in energy of the objects due to the interaction.
CO.S9-12.1.9: Although energy cannot be destroyed, it can be converted to less useful forms as it is captured, stored and transferred.
CO.S9-12.1.9.a: Design, build, and refine a device that works within given constraints to convert one form of energy into another form of energy.
CO.S9-12.1.9.b: Plan and conduct an investigation to provide evidence that the transfer of thermal energy when two components of different temperature are combined within a closed system results in a more uniform energy distribution among the components in the system (second law of thermodynamics).
CO.S9-12.1.10: Waves have characteristic properties and behaviors.
CO.S9-12.1.10.a: Use mathematical representations to support a claim regarding relationships among the frequency, wavelength, and speed of waves traveling in various media.
CO.S9-12.1.10.b: Evaluate questions about the advantages of using a digital transmission and storage of information.
CO.S9-12.1.11: Both an electromagnetic wave model and a photon model explain features of electromagnetic radiation broadly and describe common applications of electromagnetic radiation.
CO.S9-12.1.11.a: Evaluate the claims, evidence, and reasoning behind the idea that electromagnetic radiation can be described either by a wave model or a particle model, and that for some situations one model is more useful than the other.
CO.S9-12.1.11.b: Evaluate the validity and reliability of claims in published materials of the effects that different frequencies of electromagnetic radiation have when absorbed by matter.
CO.S9-12.1.11.c: Communicate technical information about how some technological devices use the principles of wave behavior and wave interactions with matter to transmit and capture information and energy.
CO.S9-12.1.12: Multiple technologies that are part of everyday experiences are based on waves and their interactions with matter.
CO.S9-12.1.12.a: Communicate technical information about how some technological devices use the principles of wave behavior and wave interactions with matter to transmit and capture information and energy.
CO.S9-12.2.1: DNA codes for the complex hierarchical organization of systems that enable life's functions.
CO.S9-12.2.1.a: Construct an explanation based on evidence for how the structure of DNA determines the structure of proteins which carry out the essential functions of life through systems of specialized cells.
CO.S9-12.2.1.b: Develop and use a model to illustrate the hierarchical organization of interacting systems that provide specific functions within multicellular organisms.
CO.S9-12.2.1.c: Plan and conduct an investigation to provide evidence that feedback mechanisms maintain homeostasis.
CO.S9-12.2.2: Growth and division of cells in complex organisms occurs by mitosis, which differentiates specific cell types.
CO.S9-12.2.2.a: Use a model to illustrate the role of cellular division (mitosis) and differentiation in producing and maintaining complex organisms.
CO.S9-12.2.3: Organisms use matter and energy to live and grow.
CO.S9-12.2.3.a: Use a model to illustrate how photosynthesis transforms light energy into stored chemical energy.
CO.S9-12.2.3.b: Construct and revise an explanation based on evidence for how carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen from sugar molecules may combine with other elements to form amino acids and/or other large carbon-based molecules.
CO.S9-12.2.3.c: Use a model to illustrate that cellular respiration is a chemical process whereby the bonds of food molecules and oxygen molecules are broken and the bonds in new compounds are formed resulting in a net transfer of energy.
CO.S9-12.2.4: Organisms interact with the living and nonliving components of the environment to obtain matter and energy.
CO.S9-12.2.4.a: Use mathematical and/or computational representations to support explanations of factors that affect carrying capacity of ecosystems at different scales.
CO.S9-12.2.4.b: Use mathematical representations to support and revise explanations based on evidence about factors affecting biodiversity and populations in ecosystems of different scales.
CO.S9-12.2.5: Matter and energy necessary for life are conserved as they move through ecosystems.
CO.S9-12.2.5.a: Construct and revise an explanation based on evidence for the cycling of matter and flow of energy in aerobic and anaerobic conditions.
CO.S9-12.2.5.b: Use mathematical representations to support claims for the cycling of matter and flow of energy among organisms in an ecosystem.
CO.S9-12.2.5.c: Develop a model to illustrate the role of photosynthesis and cellular respiration in the cycling of carbon among the biosphere, atmosphere, hydrosphere, and geosphere.
CO.S9-12.2.6: A complex set of interactions determine how ecosystems respond to disturbances.
CO.S9-12.2.6.a: Evaluate claims, evidence, and reasoning that the complex interactions in ecosystems maintain relatively consistent numbers and types of organisms in stable conditions, but changing conditions may result in a new ecosystem.
CO.S9-12.2.6.b: Design, evaluate, and refine a solution for reducing the impacts of human activities on the environment and biodiversity.
CO.S9-12.2.7: Organisms interact in groups to benefit the species.
CO.S9-12.2.7.a: Evaluate evidence for the role of group behavior on individual and species' chances to survive and reproduce.
CO.S9-12.2.8: The characteristics of one generation are dependent upon the genetic information inherited from previous generations.
CO.S9-12.2.8.a: Ask questions to clarify relationships about the role of DNA and chromosomes in coding the instructions for characteristic traits passed from parents to offspring.
CO.S9-12.2.9: Variation between individuals results from genetic and environmental factors.
CO.S9-12.2.9.a: Apply concepts of statistics and probability to explain the variation and distribution of expressed traits in a population.
CO.S9-12.2.9.b: Make and defend a claim based on evidence that inheritable genetic variations may result from: (1) new genetic combinations through meiosis, (2) viable errors occurring during replication, and/or (3) mutations caused by environmental factors.
CO.S9-12.2.10: Evidence of common ancestry and diversity between species can be determined by examining variations including genetic, anatomical and physiological differences.
CO.S9-12.2.10.a: Communicate scientific information that common ancestry and biological evolution are supported by multiple lines of empirical evidence.
CO.S9-12.2.11: Genetic variation among organisms affects survival and reproduction.
CO.S9-12.2.11.a: Construct an explanation based on evidence that the process of evolution primarily results from four factors: (1) the potential for a species to increase in number, (2) the heritable genetic variation of individuals in a species due to mutation and sexual reproduction, (3) competition for limited resources, and (4) the proliferation of those organisms that are better able to survive and reproduce in the environment.
CO.S9-12.2.11.b: Apply concepts of statistics and probability to support explanations that organisms with an advantageous heritable trait tend to increase in proportion to organisms lacking this trait.
CO.S9-12.2.12: The environment influences survival and reproduction of organisms over multiple generations.
CO.S9-12.2.12.a: Construct an explanation based on evidence for how natural selection leads to adaptation of populations.
CO.S9-12.2.12.b: Evaluate the evidence supporting claims that changes in environmental conditions may result in (1) increases in the number of individuals of some species, (2) the emergence of new species over time, and (3) the extinction of other species.
CO.S9-12.2.13: Humans have complex interactions with ecosystems and have the ability to influence biodiversity on the planet.
CO.S9-12.2.13.a: Create or revise a simulation to test a solution to mitigate adverse impacts of human activity on biodiversity.
CO.S9-12.3.1: All stars, including the sun, undergo stellar evolution, and the study of stars' light spectra and brightness is used to identify compositional elements of stars, their movements, and their distances from Earth.
CO.S9-12.3.1.a: Develop a model based on evidence to illustrate the life span of the sun and the role of nuclear fusion in the sun's core to release energy that eventually reaches Earth in the form of radiation.
CO.S9-12.3.1.b: Construct an explanation of the Big Bang theory based on astronomical evidence of light spectra, motion of distant galaxies, and composition of matter in the universe.
CO.S9-12.3.1.c: Communicate scientific ideas about the way stars, over their life cycle, produce elements.
CO.S9-12.3.2: Explanations of and predictions about the motions of orbiting objects are described by the laws of physics.
CO.S9-12.3.2.a: Use mathematical or computational representations to predict the motion of orbiting objects in the solar system.
CO.S9-12.3.3: The rock record resulting from tectonic and other geoscience processes as well as objects from the solar system can provide evidence of Earth's early history and the relative ages of major geologic formations.
CO.S9-12.3.3.a: Evaluate evidence of the past and current movements of continental and oceanic crust and the theory of plate tectonics to explain the ages of crustal rocks.
CO.S9-12.3.3.b: Apply scientific reasoning and evidence from ancient Earth materials, meteorites, and other planetary surfaces to construct an account of Earth's formation and early history.
CO.S9-12.3.4: Earth's systems, being dynamic and interacting, cause feedback effects that can increase or decrease the original changes, and these effects occur on different time scales, from sudden (e.g., volcanic ash clouds) to intermediate (ice ages) to very long-term tectonic cycles.
CO.S9-12.3.4.a: Develop a model to illustrate how Earth's internal and surface processes operate at different spatial and temporal scales to form continental and ocean-floor features.
CO.S9-12.3.4.b: Analyze geoscience data to make the claim that one change to Earth's surface can create feedbacks that cause changes to other Earth systems.
CO.S9-12.3.4.c: Develop a model based on evidence of Earth's interior to describe the cycling of matter by thermal convection.
CO.S9-12.3.4.d: Use a model to describe how variations in the flow of energy into and out of Earth's systems result in changes in climate.
CO.S9-12.3.5: Plate tectonics can be viewed as the surface expression of mantle convection, which is driven by heat from radioactive decay within Earth's crust and mantle.
CO.S9-12.3.5.a: Develop a model to illustrate how Earth's internal and surface processes operate at different spatial and temporal scales to form continental and ocean-floor features.
CO.S9-12.3.5.b: Develop a model based on evidence of Earth's interior to describe the cycling of matter by thermal convection.
CO.S9-12.3.6: The planet's dynamics are greatly influenced by water's unique chemical and physical properties.
CO.S9-12.3.6.a: Plan and conduct an investigation of the properties of water and its effects on Earth materials and surface processes.
CO.S9-12.3.7: The role of radiation from the sun and its interactions with the atmosphere, ocean, and land are the foundation for the global climate system. Global climate models are used to predict future changes, including changes influenced by human behavior and natural factors.
CO.S9-12.3.7.a: Analyze geoscience data to make the claim that one change to Earth's surface can create feedbacks that cause changes to other Earth systems.
CO.S9-12.3.7.b: Use a model to describe how variations in the flow of energy into and out of Earth's systems result in changes in climate.
CO.S9-12.3.7.c: Develop a quantitative model to describe the cycling of carbon among the hydrosphere, atmosphere, geosphere, and biosphere.
CO.S9-12.3.7.d: Construct an argument based on evidence about the simultaneous co- evolution of Earth's systems and life on Earth.
CO.S9-12.3.8: The biosphere and Earth's other systems have many interconnections that cause a continual co-evolution of Earth's surface and life on it.
CO.S9-12.3.8.a: Construct an argument based on evidence about the simultaneous co- evolution of Earth's systems and life on Earth.
CO.S9-12.3.9: Resource availability has guided the development of human society and use of natural resources has associated costs, risks, and benefits.
CO.S9-12.3.9.a: Construct an explanation based on evidence for how the availability of natural resources, occurrence of natural hazards, and changes in climate have influenced human activity.
CO.S9-12.3.9.b: Evaluate competing design solutions for developing, managing, and utilizing energy and mineral resources based on cost-benefit ratios.
CO.S9-12.3.10: Natural hazards and other geological events have shaped the course of human history at local, regional, and global scales.
CO.S9-12.3.10.a: Construct an explanation based on evidence for how the availability of natural resources, occurrence of natural hazards, and changes in climate have influenced human activity.
CO.S9-12.3.11: Sustainability of human societies and the biodiversity that supports them requires responsible management of natural resources, including the development of technologies.
CO.S9-12.3.11.a: Create a computational simulation to illustrate the relationships among the management of natural resources, the sustainability of human populations, and biodiversity.
CO.S9-12.3.11.b: Evaluate or refine a technological solution that reduces impacts of human activities on natural systems.
CO.S9-12.3.12: Global climate models used to predict future climate change continue to improve our understanding of the impact of human activities on the global climate system.
CO.S9-12.3.12.a: Analyze geoscience data and the results from global climate models to make an evidence-based forecast of the current rate of global or regional climate change and associated future impacts to Earth's systems.
CO.S9-12.3.12.b: Use a computational representation to illustrate the relationships among Earth systems and how those relationships are being modified due to human activity.
CO.SS9-12.1.1: Apply the historical method of inquiry to formulate compelling questions, evaluate primary and secondary sources, analyze and interpret data, and argue for an interpretation defended by textual evidence.
CO.SS9-12.1.1.a: Formulate compelling and supporting questions after evaluating primary sources for point of view and historical context.
CO.SS9-12.1.1.b: Gather and analyze historical information to address questions from a range of primary and secondary sources containing a variety of perspectives.
CO.SS9-12.1.1.c: Gather and analyze historical information from a range of qualitative and quantitative sources.
CO.SS9-12.1.1.d: Construct and defend a historical argument that evaluates interpretations by analyzing, critiquing, and synthesizing evidence from a wide range of relevant historical sources.
CO.SS9-12.1.2: Analyze and evaluate key concepts of continuity and change, cause and effect, complexity, unity and diversity, and significant ideas in the United States from Reconstruction to the present.
CO.SS9-12.1.2.a: Analyze continuity and change over the course of United States history.
CO.SS9-12.1.2.b: Investigate causes and effects of significant events throughout United States history.
CO.SS9-12.1.2.c: Analyze the complexity of events throughout United States history.
CO.SS9-12.1.2.d: Examine and evaluate issues of unity and diversity from Reconstruction to present.
CO.SS9-12.1.2.e: Investigate the historical development and impact of major scientific and technological innovations in the Industrial Age, the Space Age, and the Digital Age.
CO.SS9-12.1.2.f: Evaluate the historical development and impact of political thought, theory, and actions.
CO.SS9-12.1.2.g: Analyze how opposing perspectives, compromise, and cooperation have shaped national unity and diversity.
CO.SS9-12.1.2.h: Analyze and evaluate ideas critical to the understanding of American history.
CO.SS9-12.1.2.i: Describe and analyze the historical development and impact of the arts and literature on the culture of the United States.
CO.SS9-12.1.2.j: Examine and evaluate how the United States was involved in and responded to international events over the course of history.
CO.SS9-12.1.3: Analyze and evaluate key concepts of continuity and change, cause and effect, complexity, unity and diversity, and significant ideas throughout the world from the Renaissance to the present.
CO.SS9-12.1.3.a: Evaluate continuity and change over the course of world history.
CO.SS9-12.1.3.b: Investigate causes and effects of significant events from the Renaissance to the present.
CO.SS9-12.1.3.c: Analyze the complexity of events from the Renaissance to the present.
CO.SS9-12.1.3.d: Examine and evaluate issues of unity and diversity in world history from the Renaissance to the present.
CO.SS9-12.1.3.e: Evaluate the historical development and impact of philosophical and political movements and belief systems.
CO.SS9-12.1.3.f: Investigate the historical development and impact of major scientific and technological innovations.
CO.SS9-12.1.3.g: Describe and analyze the historical development and impact of the arts and literature on the cultures of the world.
CO.SS9-12.2.1: Use geographic tools and resources to analyze Earth's human systems and physical features to investigate and address geographic issues.
CO.SS9-12.2.1.a: Analyze variations in spatial patterns of cultural and environmental characteristics at multiple scales while gathering geographic data from a variety of valid sources.
CO.SS9-12.2.1.b: Create and interpret maps to display and explain the spatial patterns of cultural and environmental characteristics using geospatial and related technologies.
CO.SS9-12.2.1.c: Evaluate relationships between the locations of places and regions and their political, cultural, and economic relationships using maps, satellite images, photographs, and other representations.
CO.SS9-12.2.2: Make connections among geographic variables that influence the interactions of people, places, and environments.
CO.SS9-12.2.2.a: Identify, evaluate, and communicate strategies to respond to constraints placed on human systems by the physical environment.
CO.SS9-12.2.2.b: Analyze, interpret, and predict the influences of migration and the distribution of human populations based on reciprocal patterns.
CO.SS9-12.2.2.c: Examine patterns of distribution and arrangements of settlements and the processes of the diffusion of human activities.
CO.SS9-12.2.2.d: Explain how altering the environment has brought prosperity to some places and created environmental dilemmas for others.
CO.SS9-12.2.2.e: Research and interpret viewpoints from diverse groups.
CO.SS9-12.2.2.f: Evaluate the influence of long-term climate variability on human migration and settlement patterns, resource use, and land uses at local-to-global scales.
CO.SS9-12.2.3: Investigate patterns of the interconnected nature of the world, its people, and places.
CO.SS9-12.2.3.a: Explain how the uneven distribution of resources in the world can lead to conflict, competition, or cooperation among nations, regions, and cultural groups.
CO.SS9-12.2.3.b: Explain how shifts in the world's population are connected to and dependent upon other people for both human and natural resources.
CO.SS9-12.2.3.c: Explain how migration of people and movement of goods and ideas can contribute to and enrich cultures, but also create tensions.
CO.SS9-12.2.3.d: Analyze how culture, and cooperation and conflict influence both the division and unification of Earth.
CO.SS9-12.2.3.e: Make predictions and draw conclusions about the positive and negative global impact of cultural diffusion and assimilation.
CO.SS9-12.2.3.f: Examine geographic concepts through the lens of multiple diverse perspectives from various regions of the world and with consideration for indigenous, dominant, and marginalized populations.
CO.SS9-12.3.1: Analyze how the scarcity of productive resources (land, labor, capital) forces choices to be made about how individuals, households, businesses, and governments allocate these resources.
CO.SS9-12.3.1.a: Explain the economic way of thinking: The condition of scarcity requires choice and choice has a cost (opportunity cost).
CO.SS9-12.3.1.b: Analyze how the principles of economic thinking influence the choices made by individuals, households, businesses, and governments.
CO.SS9-12.3.1.c: Analyze how factors of production (land, labor, capital) are brought together to produce goods and services in an economic system.
CO.SS9-12.3.2: Evaluate how mixed economic systems, market structures, competition, government policies, and the roles of producers and consumers affect market outcomes.
CO.SS9-12.3.2.a: Compare and contrast economic systems in terms of their ability to achieve or impede economic goals.
CO.SS9-12.3.2.b: Use supply and demand analysis to explain how competitive markets efficiently allocate scarce resources.
CO.SS9-12.3.2.c: Compare and contrast the market outcomes created by various market structures including monopolistic competition, oligopoly, and monopoly.
CO.SS9-12.3.2.d: Explore the role of government in addressing market failures.
CO.SS9-12.3.2.e: Compare and contrast different types of taxing.
CO.SS9-12.3.2.f: Explore the multiple roles governments can play dealing with economic crises, including monetary and fiscal policy changes, and reallocation of resources and redistribution of wealth.
CO.SS9-12.3.2.g: Explore how economic crises create an environment where genocide is allowed to occur.
CO.SS9-12.3.3: Analyze how the business cycle affects the macroeconomy and evaluate the use of government policies to stabilize the economy.
CO.SS9-12.3.3.a: Describe how economic indicators provide various perspectives of the health of the economy and vary with the business cycle.
CO.SS9-12.3.3.b: Describe how fiscal and monetary policy are used to manipulate the economy including their potential lasting consequences.
CO.SS9-12.3.3.c: Explore how all policies have costs and benefits that impact participants of an economic system in different ways.
CO.SS9-12.3.4: Analyze how globalization and international trade affect the allocation of goods, services, and resources.
CO.SS9-12.3.4.a: Analyze the role of comparative advantage in international trade of goods and services.
CO.SS9-12.3.4.c: Explain how trade policies affect international trade and domestic markets.
CO.SS9-12.3.4.d: Explore the effects of current globalization trends and policies.
CO.SS9-12.4.1: Research and formulate positions on government policies and on local, state, tribal, and national issues to be able to participate and engage in a civil society.
CO.SS9-12.4.1.a: Research and discuss current issues to participate in civil discourse.
CO.SS9-12.4.1.b: Describe and evaluate the effectiveness and acceptability of a variety of methods of civic participation that individuals and groups may use to shape policy at various levels of government.
CO.SS9-12.4.1.c: Explain the roles and influence of individuals, groups, and the press, as checks on governmental practices.
CO.SS9-12.4.1.d: Evaluate traditional and non-traditional types of media (both historic and modern), including social media for reliability, credibility, and how they may influence government policy and public opinion.
CO.SS9-12.4.1.e: Engage as active community members with local, state, tribal, or federal levels of government on policy issues or for individual or group rights.
CO.SS9-12.4.2: Evaluate the purposes, roles, and limitations of the structures and functions of government.
CO.SS9-12.4.2.a: Describe the origins, purposes, and limitations of government, and include the contribution of key philosophers and American historical figures of diverse backgrounds.
CO.SS9-12.4.2.b: Identify the structure, function, and roles of current members of local, state, and national governments.
CO.SS9-12.4.2.c: Analyze the processes for amending the Constitutions of Colorado and the United States and the significant changes that have occurred to those documents including both the Colorado and the United States' Bills of Rights.
CO.SS9-12.4.2.d: Explain the principles of a democracy and analyze how competing democratic values are balanced.
CO.SS9-12.4.2.e: Describe the role and development of the founding documents of Colorado and the United States from their inception to modern day.
CO.SS9-12.4.2.f: Evaluate the role of the judicial system in protecting life, liberty, and property for all persons in the United States.
CO.SS9-12.4.2.g: Understand the structure of the American judicial system, the process of judicial appointments and key court decisions, in both Colorado and the United States, that affect the system of checks and balances and interactions of the local, state, tribal, and federal systems.
CO.SS9-12.4.2.h: Analyze how current global issues impact American policy.
CO.SS9-12.4.2.i: Compare and contrast how other systems of government function.
CO.SS9-12.4.2.j: Describe the relationship of tribal governments with state and federal governments.
CO.SS9-12.4.3: Analyze the impact of civic participation on political institutions and public policy.
CO.SS9-12.4.3.a: Describe how members of a civil society can impact public policy on local, state, national, or international issues by exercising their civic rights and responsibilities.
CO.SS9-12.4.3.b: Evaluate opportunities for people to participate in and influence government through interest groups and social movements.
CO.SS9-12.4.3.c: Analyze the impact of state and federal policies on campaigns and elections.
CO.SS9-12.4.3.d: Analyze how individual rights have been affected over time by court decisions, legislative debates at various levels of government, or by the advocacy of individuals and groups.
CO.SS9-12.4.3.e: Examine how people in other systems of government exercise their civic rights and responsibilities.
CO.SS9-12.4.3.f: Examine the advantages and disadvantages of a two-party system or a multiparty system within a democratic government.
CO.SS9-12.5.1: Apply reliable information to make systematic personal financial decisions based on individual and community values and goals.
CO.SS9-12.5.1.a: Recognize the alternatives, consequences, and responsibilities associated with personal financial decisions.
CO.SS9-12.5.1.b: Use reliable information resources when making financial decisions.
CO.SS9-12.5.1.c: Formulate strategies to protect personal and financial information.
CO.SS9-12.5.1.d: Develop a system for keeping and using financial records.
CO.SS9-12.5.2: Analyze sources of income and the relationship between career preparation, continuing education, and its impact on lifetime earning potential.
CO.SS9-12.5.2.a: Compare different sources of personal income and compensation.
CO.SS9-12.5.2.b: Analyze the impact of economic conditions and cost of living factors on income and purchasing power.
CO.SS9-12.5.2.c: Predict the potential impact of education and skill development choices on career earnings, including starting salary by field and level of degree or credential.
CO.SS9-12.5.2.d: Investigate the total cost, affordability, and payment options associated with postsecondary options, degrees, and credentials, including personal savings, scholarships, grants, employer tuition programs, work study, and public and private loans.
CO.SS9-12.5.2.e: Review the purpose and the process of accessing state and federal financial aid.
CO.SS9-12.5.2.f: Analyze student loan repayment options, terms, requirements, and state and federal repayment programs and their impact on a student's financial future.
CO.SS9-12.5.2.g: Analyze the monetary and non-monetary value of employee benefits in addition to pay.
CO.SS9-12.5.2.h: Simulate a sustainable household budget based on future personal and career goals.
CO.SS9-12.5.3: Apply consumer skills to budgeting, spending, saving, and borrowing decisions.
CO.SS9-12.5.3.a: Analyze how inflation and cost of living impact consumer purchasing and saving power.
CO.SS9-12.5.3.b: Summarize factors to consider when selecting borrowing options, including costs, relevance, payoffs, and tradeoffs.
CO.SS9-12.5.3.c: Explain how an individual's credit history can affect borrowing power.
CO.SS9-12.5.3.d: Design a household budget (using gross and net income) that addresses financial obligations and integrates saving for future goals and retirement based on your values and goals.
CO.SS9-12.5.3.e: Describe how to use and manage different types of accounts and payment methods.
CO.SS9-12.5.3.f: Compare the advantages and disadvantages of various types of credit.
CO.SS9-12.5.3.g: Summarize the advantages and disadvantages of leasing versus purchasing automobiles, homes, and other large purchases.
CO.SS9-12.5.4: Explore a diversified investment strategy that is compatible with personal financial goals.
CO.SS9-12.5.4.a: Select financial investments that align with financial goals, risk tolerance, and personal and retirement options for different life stages.
CO.SS9-12.5.4.b: Analyze how financial markets react to changes in market conditions, monetary policy, fiscal policy, and information.
CO.SS9-12.5.5: Choose risk management strategies for protection from the financial risk of lost income, lost or damaged property, health issues, or identity fraud.
CO.SS9-12.5.5.a: Evaluate strategies for consumers to avoid financial risk, reduce risk, accept risk, or transfer risk to others through insurance.
CO.SS9-12.5.5.b: Identify the cost and benefits of purchasing insurance.
CO.SS9-12.5.5.c: Explain the types and purpose of insurance products.
CO.SS9-12.5.5.d: Outline steps to monitor and safeguard personal financial data to minimize, avoid and/or resolve identity theft or fraud issues.
CO.SS9-12.5.5.e: Analyze consumer and financial information for relevance, credibility, and accuracy.
CO.SS9-12.5.5.f: Identify consumer responsibilities, rights, and consumer protection laws that regulate contracts and financial transactions.
FL.EK.F.1.1: Demonstrate knowledge of the basic concepts of print.
FL.EK.F.1.1a: Locate a printed word on a page.
FL.EK.F.1.1b: Distinguish letters from words within sentences.
FL.EK.F.1.1c: Match print to speech to demonstrate that language is represented by print.
FL.EK.F.1.1d: Identify parts of a book (front cover, back cover, title page).
FL.EK.F.1.1e: Move top to bottom and left to right on the printed page; returning to the beginning of the next line.
FL.EK.F.1.1f: Identify all upper- and lowercase letters of the alphabet.
FL.EK.F.1.1g: Recognize that print conveys specific meaning and pictures may support meaning.
FL.EK.F.1.2a: Blend and segment syllables in spoken words.
FL.EK.F.1.2b: Identify and produce alliterative and rhyming words.
FL.EK.F.1.2c: Blend and segment onset and rimes of single-syllable words.
FL.EK.F.1.2d: Identify the initial, medial, and final sound of spoken words.
FL.EK.F.1.2e: Add or delete phonemes at the beginning or end of a spoken word and say the resulting word.
FL.EK.F.1.2f: Segment and blend phonemes in single-syllable spoken words.
FL.EK.F.1.3: Use knowledge of grade-appropriate phonics and word-analysis skills to decode words accurately.
FL.EK.F.1.3a: Demonstrate knowledge of the most frequent sound for each consonant.
FL.EK.F.1.3b: Demonstrate knowledge of the short and long sounds for the five major vowels.
FL.EK.F.1.4: Recognize and read with automaticity grade-level high frequency words.
FL.EK.R.1.1: Describe the main character(s), setting, and important events in a story.
FL.EK.R.1.3: Explain the roles of author and illustrator of a story.

FL.MK.GR.1.5: Combine two-dimensional figures to form a given composite figure. Figures used to form a composite shape are limited to triangles, rectangles and squares.
FL.MK.DP.1: Develop an understanding for collecting, representing and comparing data.
FL.MK.DP.1.1: Collect and sort objects into categories and compare the categories by counting the objects in each category. Report the results verbally, with a written numeral or with drawings.

LA.SS7.11.b: Explain the development of education and prison reform movements.

LA.SS7.12: Explain the ideas, key people, and events related to the growth of sectionalism and rising tension prior to the Civil War.

LA.SS7.12.c: Compare and contrast various arguments on the issue of slavery and state's rights.

LA.SS7.13.b: Explain Louisiana's decision to secede from the Union and its effects.
LA.SS7.13.c: Describe the events leading to, significance of, and reaction to the Battle of Fort Sumter.
LA.SS7.13.d: Describe the importance and outcomes of the major military engagements of the Civil War.
LA.SS7.13.e: Describe the roles and experiences of soldiers, women, enslaved people, and freed people during the Civil War.
LA.SS7.13.f: Analyze the role of Louisiana in the Civil War and how the conflict affected Louisiana and its people.
LA.SS7.13.g: Analyze the purpose, significance, and consequences of the Emancipation Proclamation.
LA.SS7.13.h: Describe the roles and contributions of key individuals in the Civil War.
LA.SS7.13.i: Analyze Lincoln's Gettysburg Address and Second Inaugural Address, and explain how the ideas expressed affected the course of the war and show how ideas about equality changed over time.
LA.SS7.13.j: Describe the significance of Lincoln's assassination, and how it affected the nation.
LA.SS7.14: Analyze the major events, key people, and effects of Reconstruction.

LA.SS7.14.c: Explain how federal action affected individual rights and freedoms during the Reconstruction era, and analyze the challenges, achievements, and effectiveness of each.
LA.SS7.14.d: Explain the rise of violence and intimidation of Black Americans by groups and describe the significance of the Opelousas and Colfax Massacres.
LA.SS7.14.e: Describe the role and motivations of carpetbaggers and scalawags during Reconstruction.
LA.SS7.14.f: Explain the roles of Black politicians in Southern states during Reconstruction.
LA.SS7.14.g: Explain how the presidential election of 1876 and the Compromise of `1877` led to the end of Reconstruction, and analyze short-term effects of the collapse of Reconstruction.
LA.SS7.14.h: Analyze how Black Codes affected the lives of Black Americans.
LA.SS7.14.i: Analyze how national events and amendments to the U.S. Constitution influenced Louisiana from the `text(1860s)` to `1877`.
LA.SS8.1: Explain ideas, events, and developments in the history of the United States of America from `1877` to `2008` and how they progressed, changed, or remained the same over time.
LA.SS8.2: Analyze connections between events and developments in U.S. history within their global context from `1877` to `2008`.
LA.SS8.3: Compare and contrast events and developments in U.S. history from `1877` to `2008`.
LA.SS8.4: geographic representations and historical data to analyze events and developments in U.S. history from `1877` to `2008`.
LA.SS8.5: maps to identify absolute location (latitude, and longitude) and describe geographic characteristics of places in Louisiana, North America, and the world.
LA.SS8.6: Use a variety of primary and secondary sources to:
LA.SS8.6.c: Compare and contrast multiple sources and accounts.
LA.SS8.6.d: Explain how the availability of sources affects historical interpretations.
LA.SS8.7: Construct and express claims that are supported with relevant evidence from primary and/or secondary sources, social studies content knowledge, and clear reasoning and explanations to:
LA.SS8.7.a: Demonstrate an understanding of social studies content.
LA.SS8.7.b: Compare and contrast content and viewpoints.
LA.SS8.8: Analyze the causes and effects of technological and industrial advances during the late `text(nineteenth century)` and the `text(early twentieth century)`.
LA.SS8.8.a: Analyze factors that contributed to and effects of the growth of the industrial economy.
LA.SS8.8.b: Explain the social and economic effects of innovations in technology, transportation, and communication during the `text(late 1800s)` and `text(early 1900)`.
LA.SS8.8.c: Explain how industrialists and corporations revolutionized business and influenced the U.S. economy and society, with an emphasis on business practices (vertical and horizontal integration, formation of monopolies/trusts), development of major industries (oil, steel, railroad, banking), and the role of entrepreneurs.
LA.SS8.9: Analyze the social, political, and economic changes that developed in the United States during the `text(late nineteenth)` and `text(early twentieth century)`.
LA.SS8.9.a: Explain how industrialization influenced the movement of people from rural to urban areas and the effects of urbanization.
LA.SS8.9.b: Explain the causes and effects of immigration to the United States during the `text(late 1800s)` and `text(early 1900s)`, and compare and contrast experiences of immigrants.
LA.SS8.9.c: Describe the working conditions and struggles experienced by the labor force that led to the labor movement (child labor, hours, safety, wages, standard of living), and evaluate the effectiveness of efforts to improve conditions.
LA.SS8.9.d: Describe the reasons for and effects of the rise of Populism in the United States and Louisiana during the `text(late 1800s)`.
LA.SS8.9.e: Analyze the causes and outcomes of the Progressive movement and the role of muckrakers.
LA.SS8.9.f: Analyze the government's response to the rise of trusts and monopolies.
LA.SS8.9.g: Describe important ideas and events of presidential administrations during the `text(late 1800s)` and `text(early 1900s)`, with emphasis on Theodore Roosevelt's administration and his support for trust busting, regulation, consumer protection laws, and conservation.
LA.SS8.9.h: Explain the origins and development of Louisiana public colleges and universities.
LA.SS8.9.i: Analyze the events leading to Plessy v. Ferguson (`1896`) and the consequences of the decision.
LA.SS8.9.j: Explain the emergence of the Jim Crow system and how it affected Black Americans.
LA.SS8.9.k: Explain the goals and strategies used by civil rights leaders of the late 1800s and `text(early 1900s)`, and analyze differing viewpoints of key figures and groups.
LA.SS8.10: Analyze ideas and events related to the expansion of the United States during the `text(late nineteenth century)` and `text(early twentieth century)`.
LA.SS8.10.a: Explain the motivations for migration to and settlement of the West by various groups, including Exodusters, and how their motivations relate to the American Dream.
LA.SS8.10.b: Analyze Frederick Turner's “The Significance of the Frontier in American History.”
LA.SS8.10.c: Analyze how lives of Native Americans changed as a result of westward expansion and U.S. policies.
LA.SS8.10.d: Analyze the causes and effects of conflict between Native Americans and the U.S. government and settlers during the `text(late nineteenth century)` and `text(early twentieth century)`.
LA.SS8.10.e: Analyze the events leading to and effects of the U.S. acquisition of Hawaii.
LA.SS8.10.f: Analyze the ideas and events leading to the Spanish-American War and the short- and long-term outcomes.
LA.SS8.10.g: Analyze foreign policy achievements of Theodore Roosevelt.
LA.SS8.11: Analyze the causes, course and consequences of World War I.
LA.SS8.11.a: Describe the causes of World War I.
LA.SS8.11.b: Explain the reasons for the initial U.S. policy of neutrality and isolationism.
LA.SS8.11.c: Analyze the events leading to U.S. involvement in World War I.
LA.SS8.11.d: Analyze how the United States mobilized for war and ways the American people contributed to the war effort on the home front and abroad, with an emphasis on military service, role of women and minority groups, liberty bonds, and victory gardens.
LA.SS8.11.e: Explain how the U.S. government directed public support and responded to dissent during World War I.
LA.SS8.11.f: Explain how military strategies and advances in technology affected warfare and the course of World War I.
LA.SS8.11.g: Describe the goals of leaders at the Paris Peace Conference, comparing Woodrow Wilson's Fourteen Points, and the Treaty of Versailles.
LA.SS8.11.h: Explain the reaction of the U.S. Senate to the Treaty of Versailles and League of Nations, and describe the return to isolationism after the war.
LA.SS8.12: Analyze the political, social, cultural and economic effects of events and developments during the `text(early twentieth century)`.
LA.SS8.12.a: Differentiate between the benefits and detriments of capitalism and communism, and explain how the concepts affected society during the `text(early 1900s)`.
LA.SS8.12.b: Describe the causes and consequences of Prohibition and the Eighteenth Amendment.
LA.SS8.12.c: Explain how advances in transportation, technology, and media during the `text(early twentieth century)` changed society and culture in the United States.
LA.SS8.12.d: Explain the importance of the woman's suffrage movement and events leading to the passage of the Nineteenth Amendment.
LA.SS8.12.e: Explain the causes and effects of social and cultural changes of the `text(1920s)` and `text(1930s)` on the United States, and describe the influence of notable figures of the Harlem Renaissance and cultural figures.
LA.SS8.12.f: Explain how various factors affected Louisiana's economy during the `text(early twentieth century)`.
LA.SS8.12.g: Describe the causes of the Great Mississippi River Flood of `1927`, and explain how the disaster and government response affected Louisianans.
LA.SS8.12.h: Analyze Louisiana politics in the `text(early twentieth century)`.
LA.SS8.12.i: Analyze causes and effects of changes to the Louisiana Constitution over time, with emphasis on revisions from `1879` to `1974`.
LA.SS8.12.j: Explain the causes and effects of migration and population shifts in the United States during the `text(early twentieth century)`.
LA.SS8.12.k: Analyze factors leading to and consequences of social and economic tensions in the `text(early twentieth century)`.
LA.SS8.13: Analyze the causes and effects of the Great Depression.
LA.SS8.13.a: Explain the causes of the Great Depression, with an emphasis on how bank failures, buying stock on margin, overextension of credit, overproduction, high tariffs and protectionism, and the `1929` stock market crash contributed to the economic crisis.
LA.SS8.13.b: Explain the effects of the Great Depression on people.
LA.SS8.13.c: Describe the causes and effects of the Dust Bowl.
LA.SS8.13.d: Describe the government response to the Great Depression, comparing the reaction of the Hoover and Roosevelt administrations.
LA.SS8.13.e: Analyze the purpose and effectiveness of the New Deal.
LA.SS8.14: Describe the causes, course, and consequences of World War II.
LA.SS8.14.a: Explain the rise and spread of militarism and totalitarianism internationally, examining the similarities and differences between the ideologies of Imperial Japan, fascist Italy and Nazi Germany, and the communist Soviet Union, as well as the origins and effects of violence and mass murder in the `text(1930s)` and `text(1940s)` as demonstrated by the Nanjing Massacre, the Holodomor, the Holocaust, and treatment of political opponents and prisoners of war during World War II.
LA.SS8.14.b: Describe the acts of aggression leading to World War II in both Europe and Asia, and explain the effectiveness of policies and reactions.
LA.SS8.14.c: Describe the causes of World War II, and analyze events that led to U.S. involvement in World War II, with emphasis on the attack on Pearl Harbor.
LA.SS8.14.d: Describe the role of alliances during World War II.
LA.SS8.14.e: Explain the significance of major military actions and turning points during World War II in the Atlantic Theater and the Pacific Theater.
LA.SS8.14.f: Describe the roles and importance of key figures of World War.
LA.SS8.14.g: Explain the causes and consequences of the Holocaust.
LA.SS8.14.h: Describe the Tuskegee Study conducted on Black Americans from the `text(1930s)` to `1972`.
LA.SS8.14.i: Explain the causes and effects of Japanese internment in the United States during World War II.
LA.SS8.14.j: Explain the sacrifices and contributions of U.S. soldiers during World War II.
LA.SS8.14.k: Analyze how Louisiana contributed to the war effort during World War II and the effects of the war on Louisiana.
LA.SS8.14.l: Explain how life in the United States changed during and immediately after World War II, with an emphasis on wartime production and the workforce, rationing, conservation, victory gardens, financing through war bonds, propaganda campaigns, and the Servicemen's Readjustment Act (GI Bill).
LA.SS8.14.m: Explain the events that led to, and the conditions of the surrender of the Axis Powers in Europe and Asia, and describe the United States' critical role in the Allied victory.
LA.SS8.14.n: Describe the importance of the Manhattan Project and development of atomic bombs, and analyze the decision to use them.
LA.SS8.14.o: Explain how key decisions from Allied conferences during World War II.
LA.SS8.15: Analyze causes, major events, and key leaders of the Civil Rights Movement from `1954` to `1968`.
LA.SS8.15.a: Analyze events during and immediately after World War II leading to the civil rights movement.
LA.SS8.15.b: Explain the origins and goals of the civil rights movement of the `text(1950s)` and `text(1960s)`, and how segregation (de jure and de facto) affected African Americans and influenced the movement.
LA.SS8.15.c: Analyze how the murder of Emmett Till affected support for the civil rights movement.
LA.SS8.15.d: Analyze the importance of the Brown v. Board of Education (1954) decision and subsequent efforts to desegregate schools.
LA.SS8.15.e: Analyze the cause, course, and outcome of efforts to desegregate transportation.
LA.SS8.15.f: Evaluate the effectiveness of methods (civil disobedience, boycotts, sit-ins, marches, drives) during the civil rights movement.
LA.SS8.15.g: Analyze works of civil rights leaders and explain how the ideas expressed in the works influenced the course of the civil rights movement.
LA.SS8.15.h: Explain the role and importance of key individuals and groups of the civil rights movement.
LA.SS8.15.i: Explain reactions to the civil rights movement by opposing individuals and groups.
LA.SS8.15.j: Analyze the role of the Supreme Court in advancing civil rights and freedoms during the `text(1950s)` and `text(1960s)`.
LA.SS8.15.k: Evaluate legislation and amendments passed in response to the civil rights movement.
LA.SS8.16: Explain the causes, course, and consequences of the Cold War.
LA.SS8.16.a: Explain how the ideologies of communism in the Soviet Union and capitalism in the United States influenced the Cold War and global tensions from `1945-1989`.
LA.SS8.16.b: Evaluate the effectiveness of U.S. policies, programs, and negotiation efforts in accomplishing their intended goals.
LA.SS8.16.c: Analyze Cold War crises and conflicts and how they contributed escalating tensions.
LA.SS8.16.d: Describe the role of organizations and alliances during the Cold War.
LA.SS8.16.e: Explain how events during the Cold War affected American society.
LA.SS8.16.f: Explain how advances in technology and media during the `text(mid-)` to late`text( twentieth century)` changed society and public perception.
LA.SS8.16.g: Explain events and policies leading to the end of the Cold War and collapse of the Soviet Union under the leadership of President Reagan.
LA.SS8.17: Describe the importance of key ideas, events, and developments of the modern era.
LA.SS8.17.a: Explain how events and developments of the modern era have affected American society.
LA.SS8.17.b: Explain how relationships between the United States and Middle East affected events and developments during the modern era.
LA.SS8.17.c: Describe the effects of natural disasters on Louisiana and the United States.
LA.SS8.17.d: Describe important issues of the `2008` presidential election and the significance of the election of Barack Obama.
MA.EPK.RL.1: With prompting and support, ask and answer questions about a story or poem read aloud.
MA.EPK.RL.2: With prompting and support, retell a sequence of events from a story read aloud.
MA.EPK.RL.3: With prompting and support, act out characters and events from a story or poem read aloud.
MA.EPK.RL.4: With prompting and support, ask and answer questions about unfamiliar words in a story or poem read aloud.
MA.EPK.RL.5: Show awareness of the rhythmic structure of a poem or song by clapping or through movement.
MA.EPK.RL.6: With prompting and support, “read” the illustrations in a picture book by describing a character or place depicted, or by telling how a sequence of events unfolds.
MA.EPK.RL.7: With prompting and support, make predictions about what happens next in a picture book after examining and discussing the illustrations.
MA.EPK.RL.9: With prompting and support, make connections between a story or poem and their own experiences.
MA.EPK.RL.10: Listen actively as an individual and as a member of a group to a variety of age-appropriate literature read aloud.
MA.EPK.RI.1: With prompting and support, ask and answer questions about an informational text read aloud.
MA.EPK.RI.2: With prompting and support, recall important facts from an informational text after hearing it read aloud.
MA.EPK.RI.3: With prompting and support, represent or act out concepts learned from hearing an informational text read aloud (e.g., make a skyscraper out of blocks after listening to a book about cities or, following a read-aloud on animals, show how an elephant's gait differs from a bunny's hop).
MA.EPK.RI.4: With prompting and support, ask and answer questions about unfamiliar words in an informational text read aloud.
MA.EPK.RI.6: With prompting and support, “read” illustrations in an informational picture book by describing facts learned from the pictures (e.g., how a seed grows into a plant).
MA.EPK.RI.7: With prompting and support, describe important details from an illustration or photograph.
MA.EPK.RI.9: With prompting and support, identify several books on a favorite topic or several books by a favorite author or illustrator.
MA.EPK.RI.10: Listen actively as an individual and as a member of a group to a variety of age-appropriate informational texts read aloud.
MA.EPK.RF.1: With guidance and support, demonstrate understanding of the organization and basic features of printed and written text: books, words, letters, and the alphabet.
MA.EPK.RF.1.a: Handle books respectfully and appropriately, holding them right-side-up and turning pages one at a time from front to back.
MA.EPK.RF.1.d: Recognize and name some uppercase letters of the alphabet and the lowercase letters in their own name.
MA.EPK.RF.2: With guidance and support, demonstrate understanding of spoken words, syllables, and sounds (phonemes).
MA.EPK.RF.2.a: With guidance and support, recognize and produce rhyming words (e.g., identify words that rhyme with /cat/ such as /bat/ and /sat/).
MA.EPK.RF.2.b: With guidance and support, segment words in a simple sentence by clapping and naming the number of words in the sentence.
MA.EPK.RF.2.c: Identify the initial sound of a spoken word and, with guidance and support, generate several other words that have the same initial sound.
MA.EPK.RF.3: Demonstrate beginning understanding of phonics and word analysis skills.
MA.EPK.RF.3.a: Link an initial sound to a picture of an object that begins with that sound and, with guidance and support, to the corresponding printed letter (e.g., link the initial sound /b/ to a picture of a ball and, with support, to a printed or written “B”).
MA.EPK.RF.3.c: Recognize their own name and familiar common signs and labels (e.g., STOP).
MA.EPK.W.1: Dictate words to express a preference or opinion about a topic (e.g., “I would like to go to the fire station to see the truck and meet the firemen.”).
MA.EPK.W.2: Use a combination of dictating and drawing to supply information about a topic.
MA.EPK.W.3: Use a combination of dictating and drawing to tell a story.
MA.EPK.W.6: Recognize that digital tools (e.g., computers, mobile phones, cameras) are used for communication and, with guidance and support, use them to convey messages in pictures and/or words.
MA.EPK.SL.1: Participate in collaborative conversations with diverse partners during daily routines and play.
MA.EPK.SL.1.a: Observe and use appropriate ways of interacting in a group (e.g., taking turns in talking, listening to peers, waiting to speak until another person is finished talking, asking questions and waiting for an answer, gaining the floor in appropriate ways).
MA.EPK.SL.1.b: Continue a conversation through multiple exchanges.
MA.EPK.SL.2: Recall information for short periods of time and retell, act out, or represent information from a text read aloud, a recording, or a video (e.g., watch a video about birds and their habitats and make drawings or constructions of birds and their nests).
MA.EPK.SL.3: Ask and answer questions in order to seek help, get information, or clarify something that is not understood.
MA.EPK.SL.5: Create representations of experiences or stories (e.g., drawings, constructions with blocks or other materials, clay models) and explain them to others.
MA.EPK.SL.6: Speak audibly and express thoughts, feelings, and ideas.
MA.EPK.L.1: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when speaking.
MA.EPK.L.1.a: Demonstrate the ability to speak in complete sentences and to form questions using frequently occurring nouns, verbs, question words, and prepositions; name and use in context numbers 0-10.
MA.EPK.L.4: Ask and answer questions about the meanings of new words and phrases introduced through books, activities, and play.
MA.EPK.L.4.a: With guidance and support, generate words that are similar in meaning (e.g., happy/glad, angry/mad).
MA.EPK.L.5: With guidance and support from adults, explore word relationships and nuances in word meanings.
MA.EPK.L.5.a: Demonstrate understanding of concepts by sorting common objects into categories (e.g., sort objects by color, shape, texture).
MA.EPK.L.5.c: Apply words learned in classroom activities to real-life examples (e.g., name places in school that are fun, quiet, or noisy).
MA.EPK.L.6: Use words and phrases acquired through conversations, listening to books read aloud, activities, and play.
MA.MPK.CC.A: Know number names and the counting sequence.

MA.MPK.CC.B: Count to tell the number of objects.
MA.MPK.CC.B.3: Understand the relationships between numerals and quantities up to 10.
MA.MPK.CC.C.4: Count many kinds of concrete objects and actions up to ten, using one-to-one correspondence, and accurately count as many as seven things in a scattered configuration. Recognize the “one more,” “one less” patterns.
MA.MPK.CC.C.5: Use comparative language, such as more/less than, equal to, to compare and describe collections of objects.
MA.MPK.OA.A: Understand addition as putting together and adding to, and understand subtraction as taking apart and taking from.
MA.MPK.OA.A.1: Use concrete objects to model real-world addition (putting together) and subtraction (taking away) problems up through five.

MA.MPK.MD.B: Classify objects and count the number of objects in each category.
MA.MPK.MD.B.3: Sort, categorize, and classify objects by more than one attribute.
MA.MPK.MD.C.4: Recognize that certain objects are coins and that dollars and coins represent money.
MA.MPK.G.A: Identify and describe shapes (squares, circles, triangles, rectangles).
MA.MPK.G.A.1: Identify relative positions of objects in space, and use appropriate language (e.g., beside, inside, next to, close to, above, below, apart).
MA.MPK.G.A.2: Identify various two-dimensional shapes using appropriate language.
MA.MPK.G.B: Analyze, compare, create, and compose shapes.
MA.MPK.G.B.3: Create and represent three-dimensional shapes (ball/sphere, square box/cube, tube/cylinder) using various manipulative materials (such as Popsicle sticks, blocks, pipe cleaners, pattern blocks).
MA.SPK.ESS.1.1: Demonstrate awareness that the Moon can be seen in the daytime and at night, and of the different apparent shapes of the Moon over a month.
MA.SPK.ESS.1.2: Observe and use evidence to describe that the Sun is in different places in the sky during the day.
MA.SPK.ESS.2.1: Raise questions and engage in discussions about how different types of local environments (including water) provide homes for different kinds of living things.

MA.SPK.ESS.2.3: Explore and describe different places water is found in the local environment.

MA.SPK.ESS.2.5: Describe how local weather changes from day to day and over the seasons and recognize patterns in those changes.
MA.SPK.ESS.2.6: Provide examples of the impact of weather on living things.
MA.SPK.ESS.3.1: Engage in discussion and raise questions using examples about local resources (including soil and water) humans use to meet their needs.
MA.SPK.ESS.3.2: Observe and discuss the impact of people's activities on the local environment.

MA.SPK.LS.2.1: Use evidence from animals and plants to define several characteristics of living things that distinguish them from non-living things.

MA.SPK.LS.3.2: Use observations to recognize differences and similarities among themselves and their friends.

MA.SPK.PS.1.3: Differentiate between the properties of an object and those of the material of which it is made.
MA.SPK.PS.1.4: Recognize through investigation that physical objects and materials can change under different circumstances.
MA.SPK.PS.2.1: Using evidence, discuss ideas about what is making something move the way it does and how some movements can be controlled.
MA.SPK.PS.2.2: Through experience, develop awareness of factors that influence whether things stand or fall.

MA.SPK.PS.4.1: Investigate sounds made by different objects and materials and discuss explanations about what is causing the sounds. Through play and investigations, identify ways to manipulate different objects and materials that make sound to change volume and pitch.
MA.SPK.PS.4.2: Connect daily experiences and investigations to demonstrate the relationships between the size and shape of shadows, the objects creating the shadow, and the light source.
