MA.EK.RL.4: Ask and answer questions about unknown words in a text.
MA.EK.RL.5: Recognize common types of texts and characteristics of their structure (e.g., story elements in books; rhyme, rhythm, and repetition in poems).
MA.EK.RL.6: With prompting and support, explain that reading the cover or title page is how to find out who created a book; name the author and illustrator of a book and define the role of each in telling the story.
MA.EK.RL.7: With prompting and support, describe the relationship between illustrations and the story in which they appear (e.g., what moment in a story an illustration depicts).
MA.EK.RL.9: With prompting and support, compare and contrast the adventures and experiences of characters in familiar stories.
MA.EK.RL.10: Actively engage in group reading activities with purpose and understanding.
MA.EK.RI.1: With prompting and support, ask and answer questions about key details in a text.
MA.EK.RI.2: With prompting and support, identify the main topic and retell key details of a text.
MA.EK.RI.3: With prompting and support, describe the connection between two individuals, events, ideas, or pieces of information in a text.
MA.EK.RI.4: With prompting and support, ask and answer questions about unknown words in a text.
MA.EK.RI.5: Identify the front cover, back cover, and title page of a book.
MA.EK.RI.6: Name the author and illustrator of a text and define the role of each in presenting the ideas or information in the text.
MA.EK.RI.7: With prompting and support, describe the relationship between illustrations and the text in which they appear (e.g., what person, place, thing, or idea in the text an illustration depicts).
MA.EK.RI.8: With prompting and support, identify the reasons an author gives to support points in a text.
MA.EK.RI.9: With prompting and support, identify basic similarities in and differences between two texts on the same topic (e.g., in illustrations, descriptions, procedures).
MA.EK.RI.10: Actively engage in group reading activities with purpose and understanding.
MA.EK.RF.1: Demonstrate understanding of the organization and basic features of print.
MA.EK.RF.1.a: Follow words from left to right, top to bottom, and page by page.
MA.EK.RF.1.b: Recognize that spoken words are represented in written language by specific sequences of letters.
MA.EK.RF.1.c: Understand that words are separated by spaces in print.
MA.EK.RF.1.d: Recognize and name all upper- and lowercase letters of the alphabet.
MA.EK.RF.2: Demonstrate understanding of spoken words, syllables, and sounds (phonemes).
MA.EK.RF.2.b: Count, pronounce, blend, and segment syllables in spoken words.
MA.EK.RF.2.c: Blend and segment onsets and rimes of single-syllable spoken words.
MA.EK.RF.2.d: Isolate and pronounce the initial, medial vowel, and final sounds (phonemes) in three-phoneme (consonant-vowel-consonant, or CVC) words.
MA.EK.RF.3: Know and apply grade-level phonics and word analysis skills in decoding words.
MA.EK.RF.3.a: Demonstrate basic knowledge of one-to-one letter-sound correspondences by producing the primary sound or many of the most frequent sounds for each consonant.
MA.EK.RF.3.b: Associate the long and short sounds with common spellings (graphemes) for the five major vowels.
MA.EK.RF.3.c: Read common high-frequency words by sight (e.g., the, of, to, you, she, my, is, are, do, does).
MA.EK.RF.3.d: Distinguish between similarly spelled words by identifying the sounds of the letters that differ.
MA.EK.RF.4: Read early-emergent-reader texts with purpose and understanding.
MA.EK.W.1: Use a combination of drawing, dictating, and writing to compose opinion pieces that tell a reader the topic or the name of the book they are writing about and state an opinion or preference about the topic or book (e.g., My favorite book is...).
MA.EK.W.2: Use a combination of drawing, dictating, and writing to compose informative/explanatory texts that name and supply some information about a topic.
MA.EK.W.3: Use a combination of drawing, dictating, and writing to narrate a single event or experience, or several loosely linked events or experiences; sequence the narrative appropriately and provide a reaction to what it describes.
MA.EK.W.3.a: For poems, use rhyming words to create structure.
MA.EK.W.5: With guidance and support from adults, respond to questions and suggestions from peers and add details to strengthen writing as needed.
MA.EK.W.5.b: Demonstrate the ability to use vocabulary appropriate for kindergarten (as described in kindergarten Language Standards 4-6).
MA.EK.W.6: With guidance and support from adults, explore a variety of digital tools to produce and publish writing, including collaboration with peers.
MA.EK.W.7: Participate in shared research and writing projects (e.g., explore a number of books by a favorite author and express opinions about them).
MA.EK.W.8: With guidance and support from adults, recall information from experiences or gather information from provided sources to answer a question.
MA.EK.W.10: Write or dictate writing routinely for a range of tasks, purposes, and audiences.
MA.EK.SL.1: Participate in collaborative conversations with diverse partners about kindergarten topics and texts with peers and adults in small and larger groups.
MA.EK.SL.1.a: Follow agreed-upon rules for discussions (e.g., listening to others and taking turns speaking about the topics and texts under discussion).
MA.EK.SL.1.b: Continue a conversation through multiple exchanges.
MA.EK.SL.2: Confirm understanding of a text read aloud or information presented orally or through other media by asking and answering questions about key details and requesting clarification if something is not understood.
MA.EK.SL.3: Ask and answer questions in order to seek help, get information, or clarify something that is not understood.
MA.EK.SL.4: Describe familiar people, places, things, and events and, with prompting and support, provide additional detail.
MA.EK.SL.5: Add drawings or other visual displays to descriptions as desired to provide additional detail.
MA.EK.SL.6: Speak audibly and express thoughts, feelings, and ideas clearly.
MA.EK.L.1: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking; retain and further develop language skills learned previously.
MA.EK.L.1.a: Demonstrate the ability to produce and expand complete sentences using frequently occurring nouns, pronouns, adjectives, verbs, question words, and prepositions; name and use in context numbers 0-100 (see kindergarten mathematics standards for Counting and Cardinality).
MA.EK.L.1.b: Form questions that seek additional information, rather than a simple yes/no answer.
MA.EK.L.1.c: Form regular plural nouns orally by adding /s/ or /es/.
MA.EK.L.2: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.
MA.EK.L.2.b: Capitalize the first word in a sentence and the pronoun I.
MA.EK.L.2.d: Write a letter or letters for most consonant and short-vowel sounds (phonemes).
MA.EK.L.2.e: Spell simple words phonetically, drawing on knowledge of sound-letter relationships.
MA.EK.L.2.f: Write numbers 0-20 (see kindergarten mathematics standards for Counting and Cardinality).
MA.EK.L.4: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on kindergarten reading and content.
MA.EK.L.4.a: Identify new meanings for familiar words and apply them accurately (e.g., knowing duck is a bird and learning the verb to duck).
MA.EK.L.5: With guidance and support from adults, explore word relationships and nuances in word meanings.
MA.EK.L.5.a: Sort common objects into categories (e.g., shapes, foods) to gain a sense of the concepts the categories represent.
MA.EK.L.5.b: Demonstrate understanding of frequently occurring verbs and adjectives by relating them to their opposites (antonyms).
MA.EK.L.5.c: Identify real-life connections between words and their use (e.g., note places at school that are colorful).
MA.EK.L.5.d: Distinguish shades of meaning among verbs describing the same general action (e.g., walk, march, strut, prance) by acting out the meanings.
MA.EK.L.6: Use words and phrases acquired through conversations, activities in the kindergarten curriculum, reading and being read to, and responding to texts.
MA.MK.CC.A: Know number names and the count sequence.
MA.MK.CC.A.1: Count to 100 by ones and by tens.
MA.MK.CC.A.2: Count forward beginning from a given number within the known sequence (instead of having to begin at one).
MA.MK.CC.A.3: Write numbers from 0 to 20. Represent a number of objects with a written numeral 0-20 (with 0 representing a count of no objects).
MA.MK.CC.B: Count to tell the number of objects.
MA.MK.CC.B.4: Understand the relationship between numbers and quantities; connect counting to cardinality.
MA.MK.CC.B.4.a: When counting objects, say the number names in the standard order, pairing each object with one and only one number name and each number name with one and only one object.
MA.MK.CC.B.4.b: Understand that the last number name said tells the number of objects counted. The number of objects is the same regardless of their arrangement or the order in which they were counted.
MA.MK.CC.B.4.c: Understand that each successive number name refers to a quantity that is one larger. Recognize the one more pattern of counting using objects.
MA.MK.CC.B.5: Count to answer “how many?” questions about as many as 20 things arranged in a line, a rectangular array, or a circle, or as many as 10 things in a scattered configuration; given a number from 1-20, count out that many objects.
MA.MK.CC.C.6: Identify whether the number of objects in one group is greater than, less than, or equal to the number of objects in another group for groups with up to 10 objects, e.g., by using matching and counting strategies.
MA.MK.CC.C.7: Compare two numbers between `1and10` presented as written numerals.
MA.MK.OA.A: Understand addition as putting together and adding to, and understand subtraction as taking apart and taking from.
MA.MK.OA.A.1: Represent addition and subtraction with objects, fingers, mental images, drawings, sounds (e.g., claps), acting out situations, verbal explanations, expressions, or equations.
MA.MK.OA.A.2: Solve addition and subtraction word problems, and add and subtract within 10, e.g., by using objects or drawings to represent the problem.
MA.MK.OA.A.3: Decompose numbers less than or equal to 10 into pairs in more than one way, e.g., by using objects or drawings, and record each decomposition by a drawing or equation (e.g., 5 = 2 + 3 and 5 = 4 + 1).
MA.MK.OA.A.4: For any number from 1 to 9, find the number that makes 10 when added to the given number, e.g., by using objects or drawings, and record the answer with a drawing or equation.
MA.MK.OA.A.5: Fluently add and subtract within 5, including zero.
MA.MK.NBT.A: Work with numbers 11-19 to gain foundations for place value.
MA.MK.NBT.A.1: Compose and decompose numbers from 11 to 19 into ten ones and some further ones, e.g., by using objects or drawings, and record each composition or decomposition by a drawing or equation (e.g., 18 = 10 + 8); understand that these numbers are composed of ten ones and one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine ones.
MA.MK.MD.A.1: Describe measurable attributes of objects, such as length or weight. Describe several measurable attributes of a single object.
MA.MK.MD.A.2: Directly compare two objects with a measurable attribute in common, to see which object has “more of”/“less of” the attribute, and describe the difference.
MA.MK.MD.B: Classify objects and count the number of objects in each category.
MA.MK.MD.B.3: Classify objects into given categories; count the numbers of objects in each category (up to and including 10) and sort the categories by count.
MA.MK.G.A: Identify and describe shapes (squares, circles, triangles, rectangles, hexagons, cubes, cones, cylinders, and spheres).
MA.MK.G.A.1: Describe objects in the environment using names of shapes, and describe the relative positions of these objects using terms such as above, below, beside, in front of, behind, and next to.
MA.MK.G.A.2: Correctly name shapes regardless of their orientation or overall size.
MA.MK.G.A.3: Identify shapes as two-dimensional (lying in a plane, “flat”) or three-dimensional (“solid”).
MA.MK.G.B: Analyze, compare, create, and compose shapes.
MA.MK.G.B.4: Analyze and compare two- and three-dimensional shapes, in different sizes and orientations, using informal language to describe their similarities, differences, parts (e.g., number of sides and vertices/“corners”) and other attributes (e.g., having sides of equal length).
MA.MK.G.B.5: Model shapes in the world by building shapes from components (e.g., sticks and clay balls) and drawing shapes.
MA.MK.G.B.6: Compose simple shapes to form larger shapes.
MA.SK.ESS.2.1: Use and share quantitative observations of local weather conditions to describe patterns over time.
MA.SK.ESS.2.2: Construct an argument supported by evidence for how plants and animals (including humans) can change the environment.
MA.SK.ESS.3.2: Obtain and use information about weather forecasting to prepare for, and respond to, different types of local weather.
MA.SK.ESS.3.3: Communicate solutions to reduce the amount of natural resources an individual uses.
MA.SK.LS.1: From Molecules To Organisms: Structures & Processes
MA.SK.LS.1.1: Observe and communicate that animals (including humans) and plants need food, water, and air to survive. Animals get food from plants or other animals. Plants make their own food and need light to live and grow.
MA.SK.LS.1.2: Recognize that all plants and animals grow and change over time.
MA.SK.PS.1.1: Investigate and communicate the idea that different kinds of materials can be solid or liquid depending on temperature.
MA.SK.PS.2.1: Compare the effects of different strengths or different directions of pushes and pulls on the motion of an object.
MA.SK.PS.3.1: Make observations to determine that sunlight warms materials on Earth's surface.
MA.SK.PS.3.2: Use tools and materials to design and build a model of a structure that will reduce the warming effect of sunlight on an area.
MA.TK-2.CAS.a.1: Demonstrate proper ergonomics (e.g., body position, stretching) when using devices.
MA.TK-2.CAS.a.2: Use electrical devices safely and in moderation (e.g., unplug devices by pulling the plug rather than the cord, do not mix water/food and electric devices, avoid gaming and walking).
MA.TK-2.CAS.a.3: Care for devices appropriately (e.g., handling devices gently, completely shutting down devices when not in use, storing devices in the appropriate container).
MA.TK-2.CAS.a.4: Explain that a password helps protect the privacy of information.
MA.TK-2.CAS.a.5: Identify safe and unsafe examples of online communications.
MA.TK-2.CAS.a.6: Explain why we keep personal information (e.g., name, location, phone number, home address) private.
MA.TK-2.CAS.a.7: Identify which personal information (e.g., user name or real name, school name or home address) should and should not be shared online and with whom.
MA.TK-2.CAS.a.8: Explain why it is necessary to report inappropriate electronic content or contact.
MA.TK-2.CAS.b.1: Define good digital citizenship as using technology safely, responsibly, and ethically.
MA.TK-2.CAS.b.2: Demonstrate responsible use of computers, peripheral devices, and resources as outlined in school rules.
MA.TK-2.CAS.b.3: Explain that most digital artifacts have owners.
MA.TK-2.CAS.b.4: Explain the importance of giving credit to media creators/owners when using their work.
MA.TK-2.CAS.c.5: Identify and describe how people (e.g., students, parents, police officers) use many types of technologies in their daily work and personal lives.
MA.TK-2.CAS.c.6: Recognize when the purpose of content is to provide information or to influence you to act.
MA.TK-2.DTC.a.1: Operate a variety of digital tools (e.g., open/close, find, save/print, navigate, use input/output devices).
MA.TK-2.DTC.a.2: Identify, locate, and use letters, numbers, and special keys on a keyboard (e.g., Space Bar, Shift, Delete).
MA.TK-2.DTC.a.4: Use appropriate digital tools individually and collaboratively to create, review, and revise simple artifacts that include text, images and audio.
MA.TK-2.DTC.b.1: Collaboratively use digital tools and media resources to communicate key ideas and details in a way that informs, persuades, and/or entertains.
MA.TK-2.DTC.b.2: Use a variety of digital tools to exchange information and feedback with teachers.
MA.TK-2.DTC.b.3: Use a variety of digital tools to present information to others.
MA.TK-2.DTC.c.1: Conduct basic keyword searches to gather information from teacher-provided digital sources (e.g., online library catalog, databases).
MA.TK-2.DTC.c.2: Create an artifact individually and collaboratively that answers a research question, while clearly expressing thoughts and ideas.
MA.TK-2.DTC.c.3: Acknowledge and name sources of information or media (e.g., title of book, author of book, website).
MA.TK-2.CS.a.1: Identify different kinds of computing devices in the classroom and other places (e.g., laptops, tablets, smart phones, desktops).
MA.TK-2.CS.a.2: Identify visible components of computing devices (e.g., keyboard, screen, monitor, printer, pointing device).
MA.TK-2.CS.a.3: Explain that computing devices function when applications, programs, or commands are executed.
MA.TK-2.CS.a.4: Operate a variety of computing systems (e.g., turn on, use input/output devices such as a mouse, keyboard, or touch screen; find, navigate, launch a program).
MA.TK-2.CS.b.1: Explain that computing devices are machines that are not alive but can be used to help humans with tasks.
MA.TK-2.CS.b.2: Recognize that some tasks are best completed by humans and others by computing devices (e.g., a human might be able to rescue someone in a normal environment, but robots would be better to use in a dangerous environment).
MA.TK-2.CS.b.3: Recognize that different tools can solve the same problem (e.g., pen and paper, calculators, and smart phones can all be used to solve simple mathematical problems).
MA.TK-2.CS.c.1: Explain that networks link computers and devices locally and around the world allowing people to access and communicate information.
MA.TK-2.CT.a.1: List the attributes of a common object, for example, cars have a color, type (e.g., pickup, van, sedan), number of seats, etc.
MA.TK-2.CT.b.1: Define an algorithm as a sequence of defined steps.
MA.TK-2.CT.b.2: Create a simple algorithm, individually and collaboratively, without using computers to complete a task (e.g., making a sandwich, getting ready for school, checking a book out of the library).
MA.TK-2.CT.b.3: Enact an algorithm using tangible materials (e.g., manipulatives, your body) or present the algorithm in a visual medium (e.g., storyboard).
MA.TK-2.CT.c.1: Identify different kinds of information (e.g., text, charts, graphs, numbers, pictures, audio, video, collections of objects.)
MA.TK-2.CT.c.2: Identify, research, and collect information on a topic, issue, problem, or question using age- appropriate digital technologies.
MA.TK-2.CT.c.3: Individually and collaboratively, propose a solution to a problem or question based on an analysis of information.
MA.TK-2.CT.c.4: Individually and collaboratively, create information visualizations (e.g., charts, infographics).
MA.TK-2.CT.c.5: Explain that computers can save information as data that can be stored, searched, retrieved, and deleted.
MA.TK-2.CT.d.1: Define a computer program as a set of commands created by people to do something.
MA.TK-2.CT.d.2: Explain that computers only follow the program's instructions.
MA.TK-2.CT.d.3: Individually or collaboratively, create a simple program using visual instructions or tools that do not require a textual programming language (e.g., “unplugged” programming activities, a block- based programming language).
MA.TK-2.CT.e.1: Describe how models represent a real-life system (e.g., globe, map, solar system, digital elevation model, weather map).
MA.TK-2.CT.e.2: Define simulation and identify the concepts illustrated by a simple simulation (e.g., growth and health, butterfly life cycle).
MA.E1.RL.1: Ask and answer questions about key details in a text.
MA.E1.RL.2: Retell stories, including key details, and demonstrate understanding of their central message or lesson.
MA.E1.RL.3: Describe characters, settings, and major events in a story, using key details.
MA.E1.RL.4: Identify words and phrases in stories or poems that suggest feelings or appeal to the senses.
MA.E1.RL.5: Identify characteristics of common types of stories, including folktales and fairy tales.
MA.E1.RL.6: Identify who is telling the story at various points in a text.
MA.E1.RL.7: Use illustrations and details in a story to describe its characters, setting, or events.
MA.E1.RL.9: Compare and contrast the adventures and experiences of characters in stories.
MA.E1.RL.10: With prompting and support, read and comprehend literary texts representing a variety of genres, cultures, and perspectives and exhibiting complexity appropriate for at least grade 1.
MA.E1.RI.1: Ask and answer questions about key details in a text.
MA.E1.RI.2: Identify the main topic and retell key details of a text.
MA.E1.RI.3: Describe the connection between two individuals, events, ideas, or pieces of information in a text.
MA.E1.RI.4: Ask and answer questions to help determine or clarify the meaning of words and phrases in a text.
MA.E1.RI.5: Know and use various text features (e.g., headings, tables of contents, glossaries, electronic menus, icons) to locate key facts or information in a text.
MA.E1.RI.6: Distinguish between information provided by pictures or other illustrations and information provided by the words in a text.
MA.E1.RI.7: Use the illustrations and details in a text to describe its key ideas.
MA.E1.RI.8: Identify the reasons an author gives to support points in a text.
MA.E1.RI.9: Identify basic similarities in and differences between two texts on the same topic (e.g., in illustrations, descriptions, or procedures).
MA.E1.RI.10: With prompting and support, read and comprehend informational texts exhibiting complexity appropriate for at least grade 1.
MA.E1.RF.1: Demonstrate understanding of the organization and basic features of print.
MA.E1.RF.1.a: Recognize the distinguishing features of a sentence (e.g., first word, capitalization, ending punctuation).
MA.E1.RF.2: Demonstrate understanding of spoken words, syllables, and sounds (phonemes).
MA.E1.RF.2.a: Distinguish long from short vowel sounds in spoken single-syllable words.
MA.E1.RF.2.b: Orally produce single-syllable words by blending sounds (phonemes), including consonant blends.
MA.E1.RF.2.c: Isolate and pronounce initial, medial vowel, and final sounds (phonemes) in spoken single- syllable words.
MA.E1.RF.2.d: Segment spoken single-syllable words into their complete sequence of individual sounds (phonemes).
MA.E1.RF.3: Know and apply grade-level phonics and word analysis skills in decoding words.
MA.E1.RF.3.a: Know the spelling-sound correspondences for common consonant digraphs.
MA.E1.RF.3.c: Know final -e and common vowel team conventions for representing long vowel sounds.
MA.E1.RF.3.d: Use knowledge that every syllable must have a vowel sound to determine the number of syllables in a printed word.
MA.E1.RF.3.e: Decode two-syllable words following basic patterns by breaking the words into syllables.
MA.E1.RF.3.g: Recognize and read grade-appropriate irregularly spelled words.
MA.E1.RF.4: Read with sufficient accuracy and fluency to support comprehension.
MA.E1.RF.4.a: Read grade-level text with purpose and understanding.
MA.E1.RF.4.b: Read grade-level text orally with accuracy, appropriate rate, and expression on successive readings.
MA.E1.RF.4.c: Use context to confirm or self-correct word recognition and understanding, rereading as necessary.
MA.E1.W.1: Write opinion pieces that introduce the topic or name the book they are writing about, state an opinion, supply a reason for the opinion, and provide some sense of closure.
MA.E1.W.2: Write informative/explanatory texts that name a topic, supply some facts about the topic, and provide some sense of closure.
MA.E1.W.3: Write narratives in prose or poem form that recount two or more appropriately sequenced events or experiences, include some details about what happened or was experienced, use temporal words to signal order where appropriate, and provide some sense of closure.

MA.E1.W.4: Produce writing in which the development and organization are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.
MA.E1.W.5: With guidance and support from adults, focus on a topic, respond to questions and suggestions from peers, and add details to strengthen writing as needed.
MA.E1.W.5.b: Demonstrate the ability to choose and use appropriate vocabulary (as described in Language Standards 4-6 up to and including grade 1).
MA.E1.W.6: With guidance and support from adults, use a variety of digital tools to produce and publish writing, including in collaboration with peers.
MA.E1.W.7: Participate in shared research and writing projects (e.g., explore a number of how-to books on a given topic and use them to write a sequence of instructions).
MA.E1.W.8: With guidance and support from adults, recall information from experiences or gather information from provided sources to answer a question.
MA.E1.W.10: Write routinely for a range of tasks, purposes, and audiences.
MA.E1.SL.1: Participate in collaborative conversations with diverse partners about grade 1 topics and texts with peers and adults in small and larger groups.

MA.E1.SL.1.b: Build on others' talk in conversations by responding to the comments of others through multiple exchanges.
MA.E1.SL.1.c: Ask questions to clear up any confusion about the topics and texts under discussion.
MA.E1.SL.2: Ask and answer questions about key details in a text read aloud or information presented orally or through other media.
MA.E1.SL.3: Ask and answer questions about what a speaker says in order to gather additional information or clarify something that is not understood.
MA.E1.SL.4: Describe people, places, things, and events with relevant details, expressing ideas and feelings clearly and using appropriate vocabulary.
MA.E1.SL.5: Add drawings or other visual displays to descriptions when appropriate to clarify ideas, thoughts, and feelings.
MA.E1.SL.6: Produce complete sentences when appropriate to task and situation.
MA.E1.L.1: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking; retain and further develop language skills learned in previous grades.
MA.E1.L.1.a: Produce and expand simple and compound sentences.
MA.E1.L.1.b: Demonstrate understanding that a question is a type of sentence.
MA.E1.L.1.c: Use singular and plural nouns with matching verbs in sentences.
MA.E1.L.1.d: Use verbs in sentences to convey a sense of past, present, and future.
MA.E1.L.1.e: Use common, proper, and possessive nouns.
MA.E1.L.1.f: Use personal, possessive, and indefinite pronouns.
MA.E1.L.1.g: Use frequently occurring prepositions, adjectives, adverbs, conjunctions, and articles.
MA.E1.L.2: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.
MA.E1.L.2.a: Print legibly all upper- and lowercase letters.
MA.E1.L.2.c: Capitalize the names of months and people.
MA.E1.L.2.d: Use commas in dates and to separate individual words in a series.
MA.E1.L.2.e: Use conventional spelling for words with common spelling patterns and for frequently occurring irregular words.
MA.E1.L.f: Spell untaught words phonetically, drawing on phonemic awareness and spelling conventions.

MA.E1.L.4.a: Use sentence-level context as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.
MA.E1.L.4.b: Use frequently occurring affixes as a clue to the meaning of a word.

MA.E1.L.5.c: Identify real-life connections between words and their use (e.g., note places at home that are cozy).
MA.E1.L.5.d: Distinguish shades of meaning among verbs differing in manner (e.g., look, peek, glance, stare, glare, scowl) and adjectives differing in intensity (e.g., large, gigantic) by defining or choosing them or by acting out the meanings.
MA.E1.L.6: Use words and phrases acquired through conversations, activities in the grade 1 curriculum, reading and being read to, and responding to texts, including using frequently occurring conjunctions (e.g., because) to signal simple relationships.
MA.M1.OA.A: Represent and solve problems involving addition and subtraction.
MA.M1.OA.A.1: Use addition and subtraction within 20 to solve word problems involving situations of adding to, taking from, putting together, taking apart, and comparing, with unknowns in all positions, e.g., by using objects, drawings, and equations (number sentences) with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.
MA.M1.OA.A.2: Solve word problems that call for addition of three whole numbers whose sum is less than or equal to 20, e.g., by using objects, drawings, and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.
MA.M1.OA.B: Understand and apply properties of operations and the relationship between addition and subtraction.
MA.M1.OA.B.3: Apply properties of operations to add.
MA.M1.OA.B.4: Understand subtraction as an unknown-addend problem.
MA.M1.OA.C.5: Relate counting to addition and subtraction (e.g., by counting on 2 to add 2).
MA.M1.OA.C.6: Add and subtract within 20, demonstrating fluency for addition and subtraction within 10. Use mental strategies such as counting on; making 10 (e.g., 8 + 6 = 8 + 2 + 4 = 10 + 4 = 14); decomposing a number leading to a 10 (e.g., 13 - 4 = 13 - 3 - 1 = 10 - 1 = 9); using the relationship between addition and subtraction (e.g., knowing that 8 + 4 = 12, one knows 12 - 8 = 4); and creating equivalent but easier or known sums (e.g., adding 6 + 7 by creating the known equivalent 6 + 6 + 1 = 12 + 1 = 13).
MA.M1.OA.D: Work with addition and subtraction equations.
MA.M1.OA.D.7: Understand the meaning of the equal sign, and determine if equations involving addition and subtraction are true or false.
MA.M1.OA.D.8: Determine the unknown whole number in an addition or subtraction equation relating three whole numbers.
MA.M1.NBT.A.1: Count to 120, starting at any number less than 120. In this range, read and write numerals and represent a number of objects with a written numeral.
MA.M1.NBT.B.2: Understand that the two digits of a two-digit number represent amounts of tens and ones. Understand the following as special cases:
MA.M1.NBT.B.2.a: 10 can be thought of as a bundle of ten ones - called a “ten.”
MA.M1.NBT.B.2.b: The numbers from 11 to 19 are composed of a ten and one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine ones.
MA.M1.NBT.B.2.c: The numbers 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90 refer to one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine tens (and 0 ones).
MA.M1.NBT.B.3: Compare two two-digit numbers based on meanings of the tens and ones digits, recording the results of comparisons with the symbols `>,=,and<`.
MA.M1.NBT.C: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to add and subtract.
MA.M1.NBT.C.4: Add within `100`, including adding a two-digit number and a one-digit number, and adding a two-digit number and a multiple of 10, using concrete models or drawings, and strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction; relate the strategy to a written method and explain the reasoning used. Understand that in adding two-digit numbers, one adds tens and tens, ones and ones; and sometimes it is necessary to compose a ten.
MA.M1.NBT.C.5: Given a two-digit number, mentally find 10 more or 10 less than the number, without having to count; explain the reasoning used. Identify arithmetic patterns of 10 more and 10 less than using strategies based on place value.
MA.M1.NBT.C.6: Subtract multiples of `10` in the range `10-90` from multiples of `10` in the range `10-90` (positive or zero differences), using concrete models or drawings and strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction; relate the strategy to a written method and explain the reasoning used.
MA.M1.MD.A: Measure lengths indirectly and by iterating length units.
MA.M1.MD.A.1: Order three objects by length; compare the lengths of two objects indirectly by using a third object.
MA.M1.MD.A.2: Express the length of an object as a whole number of length units, by laying multiple copies of a shorter object (the length unit) end to end; understand that the length measurement of an object is the number of same-size length units that span it with no gaps or overlaps.
MA.M1.MD.B.3: Tell and write time in `text(hours)` and half-hours using analog and digital clocks.
MA.M1.MD.C.4: Organize, represent, and interpret data with up to three categories; ask and answer questions about the total number of data points, how many in each category, and how many more or less are in one category than in another.
MA.M1.MD.D.5: Identify the values of all U.S. coins and know their comparative values (e.g., a dime is of greater value than a nickel). MA.M1.G.A: Reason with shapes and their attributes.

MA.M1.G.A.2: Compose two-dimensional shapes (rectangles, squares, trapezoids, triangles, half-circles, and quarter- circles) or three-dimensional shapes (cubes, right rectangular prisms, right circular cones, and right circular cylinders) to create a composite shape, and compose new shapes from the composite shape.
MA.M1.G.A.3: Partition circles and rectangles into two and four equal shares, describe the shares using the words halves, fourths, and quarters, and use the phrases half of, fourth of, and quarter of. Describe the whole as two of, or four of the shares. Understand for these examples that decomposing into more equal shares creates smaller shares.
MA.S1.ESS.1.1: Use observations of the Sun, Moon, and stars to describe that each appears to rise in one part of the sky, appears to move across the sky, and appears to set.
MA.S1.ESS.1.2: Analyze provided data to identify relationships among seasonal patterns of change, including relative sunrise and sunset time changes, seasonal temperature and rainfall or snowfall patterns, and seasonal changes to the environment.

MA.S1.LS.1.1: Use evidence to explain that (a) different animals use their body parts and senses in different ways to see, hear, grasp objects, protect themselves, move from place to place, and seek, find, and take in food, water, and air, and (b) plants have roots, stems, leaves, flowers, and fruits that are used to take in water, air, and other nutrients, and produce food for the plant.
MA.S1.LS.1.2: Obtain information to compare ways in which the behavior of different animal parents and their offspring help the offspring to survive.
MA.S1.LS.3.1: Use information from observations (first-hand and from media) to identify similarities and differences among individual plants or animals of the same kind.

MA.S1.PS.4.1: Demonstrate that vibrating materials can make sound and that sound can make materials vibrate.
MA.S1.PS.4.3: Conduct an investigation to determine the effect of placing materials that allow light to pass through them, allow only some light through them, block all the light, or redirect light when put in the path of a beam of light.
MA.S1.PS.4.4: Use tools and materials to design and build a device that uses light or sound to send a signal over a distance.
MA.S1.ETS.1.1: Ask questions, make observations, and gather information about a situation people want to change that can be solved by developing or improving an object or tool.

MA.E2.RL.6: Explain what dialogue is and how it can reveal characters' thoughts and perspectives.

MA.E2.RI.6: Identify the main purpose of a text, including what the author wants to answer, explain, or describe.

MA.E2.RI.8: Describe how reasons support specific points the author makes in a text.
MA.E2.RI.9: Compare and contrast the most important points presented by two texts on the same topic.
MA.E2.RI.10: Independently and proficiently read and comprehend informational texts, including history/social studies, science, mathematical, and technical texts, exhibiting complexity appropriate for at least grade 2.
MA.E2.RF.3: Know and apply grade-level phonics and word analysis skills in decoding words.

MA.E2.W.10: Write routinely for a range of tasks, purposes, and audiences.

MA.E2.L.2.d: Use an apostrophe to form contractions and frequently occurring possessives.

MA.E2.L.3.a: Compare formal and informal uses of English.

MA.E2.L.4.a: Use sentence-level context as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.
MA.E2.L.4.b: Determine the meaning of the new word formed when a known prefix is added to a known word (e.g., happy/unhappy, tell/retell).
MA.E2.L.4.c: Use a known root word as a clue to the meaning of an unknown word with the same root (e.g., addition, additional).

MA.E2.L.4.e: Use glossaries and beginning dictionaries, both print and digital, to determine or clarify the meaning of words and phrases.
MA.E2.L.4.f: Recognize and use appropriately abbreviations related to grade-level content or commonly used in everyday life (e.g., a.m., p.m.).
MA.E2.L.4.g: Recognize and use appropriately symbols related to grade-level content or commonly used in everyday life (e.g., $, ¢).

MA.E2.L.6: Use words and phrases acquired through conversations, activities in the grade 2 curriculum, reading and being read to, and responding to texts, including using adjectives and adverbs to describe.

MA.M2.NBT.A.1.b: The numbers 100, 200, 300, 400, 500, 600, 700, 800, 900 refer to one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine hundreds (and 0 tens and 0 ones).

MA.M2.NBT.A.4: Compare two three-digit numbers based on meanings of the hundreds, tens, and ones digits, using `>,=,and<` symbols to record the results of comparisons.
MA.M2.NBT.B: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to add and subtract.
MA.M2.NBT.B.5: Fluently add and subtract within `100` using strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction.
MA.M2.NBT.B.6: Add up to four two-digit numbers using strategies based on place value and properties of operations.
MA.M2.NBT.B.7: Add and subtract within `1text(,)000`, using concrete models or drawings and strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction; relate the strategy to a written method. MA.M2.NBT.B.9: Explain why addition and subtraction strategies work, using place value and the properties of operations.
