MD.EPK.RI.6: With modeling and support, define the role of the author and illustrator/photographer in presenting the ideas or information in a text.
MD.EPK.RI.7: With modeling and support, tell how the illustrations/ photographs support the text.
MD.EPK.RI.8: With modeling and support, identify the reasons an author gives to support points in a text.
MD.EPK.RI.9: With prompting and support, discuss similarities and differences between two texts on the same topic (e.g., in illustrations or descriptions).
MD.EPK.RI.10: Actively engage in-group reading activities with purpose and understanding.
MD.EPK.RF.1: Demonstrate understanding of basic features of print.
MD.EPK.RF.1.a: Demonstrate an awareness that words are read from left to right, top to bottom, and page by page.
MD.EPK.RF.1.b: Recognize that spoken words can be written and read.
MD.EPK.RF.1.c: Understand that words are separated by spaces in print.
MD.EPK.RF.1.d: Recognize and name some upper- and lowercase letters of the alphabet.
MD.EPK.RF.2: Demonstrate understanding of spoken words and sounds (phonemes).
MD.EPK.RF.2.a: Recognize rhyming words in spoken language.
MD.EPK.RF.2.b: Identify and isolate individual words in a spoken sentence.
MD.EPK.RF.2.c: Count, pronounce, blend, and segment syllables in spoken words.
MD.EPK.RF.2.d: Blend and segment onsets and rimes of single-syllable spoken words.
MD.EPK.RF.2.e: Isolate and pronounce the initial sound in spoken words.
MD.EPK.RF.2.f: Orally blend and segment individual phonemes in two-to-three phoneme words.
MD.EPK.RF.3: Know and apply grade-level phonics and word analysis skills in decoding words.
MD.EPK.RF.3.a: Recognize that words are made up of letters and their sounds.
MD.EPK.RF.3.b: Demonstrate basic knowledge of one-to-one letter sound correspondences by producing the most frequent sound for some consonants.
MD.EPK.RF.3.c: Recognize name in print as well as some environmental print (symbols/words).
MD.EPK.RF.4: Engage with a variety of texts (e.g., a variety of structures and/ or genres) with purpose and understanding.
MD.EPK.W.1: With modeling and support, use a combination of drawing, dictating, and developmentally appropriate writing to share opinion about an experience or book.
MD.EPK.W.2: Use a combination of drawing, dictating, or developmentally appropriate writing to state information on a topic.
MD.EPK.W.3: With modeling and support, use a combination of drawing, dictating, or developmentally appropriate writing to communicate a personal story about a single event and tell about the event in a meaningful sequence.
MD.EPK.W.5: With modeling, guidance, and support from adults, review drawing, dictation, or developmentally appropriate writing.
MD.EPK.W.6: With prompting and support from adults, explore a variety of digital tools to express ideas.
MD.EPK.W.7: Participate in shared research and shared writing projects.
MD.EPK.W.8: With modeling and support from adults, recall information from experiences or information from provided sources to answer a question.
MD.EPK.SL.1: Participate in collaborative conversations with diverse partners about pre-kindergarten topics and texts with peers and adults in small and larger groups.
MD.EPK.SL.1.a: Follow agreed-upon rules for discussions (e.g., listening to others and taking turns speaking about the topics and texts under discussion).
MD.EPK.SL.1.b: During scaffolded conversations, continue a conversation through multiple exchanges.
MD.EPK.SL.2: Confirm understanding of a text read aloud or information presented orally or through other media by asking and answering questions about key details with modeling and support.
MD.EPK.SL.3: Ask and answer questions in order to seek help, get information, or clarify something that is not understood.
MD.EPK.SL.4: Describe familiar people, places, things, and events with modeling and support.
MD.EPK.SL.5: Add drawings or visual displays to descriptions as desired to provide additional detail.
MD.EPK.SL.6: With modeling and support, speak audibly and express thoughts, feelings, and ideas clearly.
MD.EPK.L.1: Demonstrate beginning understanding of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when engaged in literacy activities.
MD.EPK.L.1.a: Print upper- and lowercase letters in first name.
MD.EPK.L.1.b: Use frequently occurring nouns and verbs.
MD.EPK.L.1.c: Develop understanding of singular and plural nouns (e.g., dog means one dog; dogs means more than one).
MD.EPK.L.1.d: Understand and begin to use question words (e.g., interrogatives who, what, where, when, why, how).
MD.EPK.L.1.e: Gain exposure to the most frequently occurring prepositions (e.g. to, from, in, out, on, off, for, of, by, with).
MD.EPK.L.1.f: Produce complete sentences in shared language activities.
MD.EPK.L.2: Gain exposure to conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling during shared reading and writing experiences.
MD.EPK.L.2.a: Recognize that their name begins with a capital letter.
MD.EPK.L.2.b: Demonstrate awareness of name and function of end punctuation (e.g., period, question mark, exclamation point).
MD.EPK.L.2.c: Use letter-like shapes, symbols, letters, and words to convey meaning.
MD.EPK.L.2.d: Develop fine motor skills necessary to control and sustain handwriting.
MD.EPK.L.4: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown words and phrases based on pre-kindergarten reading and content.
MD.EPK.L.5: With modeling and support from adults, explore word relationships and nuances in word meanings.
MD.EPK.L.5.a: With modeling and support, sort common objects into categories (e.g., shapes, foods) to gain a sense of the concepts the categories represent.
MD.EPK.L.5.b: With modeling and support, demonstrate understanding of frequently occurring verbs and adjectives by relating them to their opposites (antonyms).
MD.EPK.L.5.c: Identify real-life connections between words and their use (e.g., note objects in the classroom that are small).
MD.EPK.L.6: Use words and phrases acquired through conversations, being read to, and responding to texts.
MD.MPK.CC.A: Know number names and the count sequence
MD.MPK.CC.A.1: Verbally count to 10 by ones and then develop rote counting to 20 by ones.
MD.MPK.CC.A.2: Identify which number comes just after or just before a given number in the counting sequence to 10 with visual supports and manipulatives.
MD.MPK.CC.B: Count to tell the number of objects.
MD.MPK.CC.B.4: Understand the relationship between numbers and quantities to 5, then to 10; connect counting to cardinality.
MD.MPK.CC.B.4.a: When counting objects (1-10), say the number names in standard order, pairing each object with one and only one number name.
MD.MPK.CC.B.4.b: Recognize that the last number name said tells the number of objects counted. Recognize the count remains the same regardless of the order or arrangement of the objects.
MD.MPK.CC.B.4.c: Begin to recognize that each successive number name refers to a quantity that is one larger.
MD.MPK.CC.B.4.d: Recognize the number of objects in a set without counting (subitizing) using 1-5 objects. Use 1-3 objects of irregular or unfamiliar patterns and 4 or 5 objects with familiar patterns.
MD.MPK.CC.B.5: Represent a number (0-5, then to 10) by producing sets of objects with concrete materials, pictures, and or numerals. Correctly respond when asked “how many” after counting concrete objects.
MD.MPK.CC.C.6: Compare groups of objects (up to `5` and then to 10.) Identify whether the number of objects in one group is greater than, less than, or equal to the number of objects in another group, e.g., by using matching and counting strategies (includes groups with up to `5` objects).
MD.MPK.OA.A: Understand addition as putting together and adding to, and understand subtraction as taking apart and taking from.
MD.MPK.OA.A.1: Represent simple addition and subtraction problems with objects, fingers, mental images, drawings, sounds (e.g., claps), acting out situations, or verbal explanations (up to 5).
MD.MPK.OA.A.2: Decompose a quantity (less than or equal to 5, then to 10) into pairs in more than one way, e.g.by using objects or drawings.
MD.MPK.OA.A.3: For any quantity 1-5, use objects or drawings to find the quantity that must be added to make 5.
MD.MPK.MD.A.1: Describe measurable attributes of objects, such as length or weight.
MD.MPK.MD.A.2: Directly compare two objects with a measurable attribute in common, using words such as “bigger/smaller,” “longer/shorter,” “lighter/heavier,” or “taller/shorter.” Order up to 3 objects by a measurable attribute (e.g. biggest to smallest).
MD.MPK.MD.B: Sort objects into categories and compare quantities.
MD.MPK.MD.B.3: Sort objects into given categories and self-selected categories. Identify the attribute by which the objects were sorted.
MD.MPK.MD.B.4: Compare categories using words such as greater than/more, less than, and equal to/same.
MD.MPK.G.A: Identify and describe two dimensional shapes (circles, triangles, rectangles, including a square which is a special rectangle).
MD.MPK.G.A.1: Match like two-dimensional shapes and correctly name the shapes regardless of their orientations or overall size.
MD.MPK.G.A.2: Group the shapes by like attributes and distinguish between examples and non-examples of various two-dimensional shapes.
MD.MPK.G.B: Work with three-dimensional shapes to gain foundations for geometric thinking.
MD.MPK.G.B.4: Use real world examples to describe three-dimensional objects using correct mathematical vocabulary (cube, sphere, and cylinder).
MD.MPK.G.B.5: Compose and describe structures using three-dimensional shapes. Descriptions may include shape attributes, relative position, etc.
MD.EK.RL.1: With prompting and support, ask and answer questions about key details in a text.
MD.EK.RL.2: With prompting and support, retell familiar stories, including key details.
MD.EK.RL.3: With prompting and support, identify characters, settings, and major events in a story.
MD.EK.RL.4: Ask and answer questions about unknown words in a text.
MD.EK.RL.5: Recognize common types of texts (e.g., storybooks, poems).
MD.EK.RL.6: With prompting and support, name the author and illustrator of a story and define the role of each in telling the story.
MD.EK.RL.7: With prompting and support, describe the relationship between illustrations and the story in which they appear (e.g., what moment in a story an illustration depicts).
MD.EK.RL.9: With prompting and support, compare and contrast the adventures and experiences of characters in familiar stories.
MD.EK.RL.10: Actively engage in-group reading activities with purpose and understanding.
MD.EK.RI.1: With prompting and support, ask and answer questions about key ideas in a text.
MD.EK.RI.2: With prompting and support, identify the main topic and retell key details of a text.
MD.EK.RI.3: With prompting and support, describe the connection between two individuals, events, ideas, or pieces of information in a text.
MD.EK.RI.4: With prompting and support, ask and answer questions about unknown words in a text.
MD.EK.RI.5: Identify the front cover, back cover, and title page of a book.
MD.EK.RI.6: Name the author and illustrator of a text and define the role of each in presenting the ideas or information in a text.
MD.EK.RLI.7: With prompting and support, describe the relationship between illustrations and the text in which they appear (e.g., what person, place, thing, or idea in the text an illustration depicts).
MD.EK.RI.8: With prompting and support, identify the reasons an author gives to support points in a text.
MD.EK.RI.9: With prompting and support, describe the relationship between illustrations and the text in which they appear (e.g., what person, place, thing, or idea in the text an illustration depicts).
MD.EK.RI.10: Actively engage in-group reading activities with purpose and understanding.
MD.EK.RF.1: Demonstrate understanding of the organization and basic features of print.
MD.EK.RF.1.a: Follow words from left to right, top to bottom, and page by page.
MD.EK.RF.1.b: Recognize that spoken words are represented in written language by specific sequences of letters.
MD.EK.RF.1.c: Understand that words are separated by spaces in print.
MD.EK.RF.1.d: Recognize and name all upper- and lowercase letters of the alphabet.
MD.EK.RF.2: Demonstrate understanding of spoken words, syllables, and sounds (phonemes).
MD.EK.RF.2.b: Count, pronounce, blend, and segment syllables in spoken words.
MD.EK.RF.2.c: Blend and segment onsets and rimes of single-syllable spoken words.
MD.EK.RF.2.d: Isolate and pronounce the initial, medial vowel, and final sounds (phonemes) in three-phoneme (consonant-vowel consonant, or CVC) words.
MD.EK.RF.2.e: Add or substitute individual sounds (phonemes) in simple, one-syllable words to make new words.
MD.EK.RF.3: Know and apply grade-level phonics and word analysis skills in decoding words.
MD.EK.RF.3.a: Demonstrate basic knowledge of one-to-one letter-sound correspondences by producing the primary or many of the most frequent sound for each consonant
MD.EK.RF.3.b: Associate the long and short sounds with common spellings (graphemes) for the five major vowels.
MD.EK.RF.3.c: Read common high-frequency words by sight (e.g., the, of, to, you, she, my, is, are, do, does).
MD.EK.RF.3.d: Distinguish between similarly spelled words by identifying the sounds of the letters that differ.
MD.EK.RF.4: Read emergent-reader texts with purpose and understanding
MD.EK.W.1: Use a combination of drawing, dictating, and writing to compose opinion pieces in which they tell a reader the topic or the name of the book they are writing about and state an opinion or preference about the topic or book (e.g., My favorite book is...).
MD.EK.W.2: Use a combination of drawing, dictating, and writing to compose informative/explanatory texts in which they name what they are writing about and supply some information about the topic.
MD.EK.W.3: Use a combination of drawing, dictating, and writing to narrate a single event or several loosely linked events, tell about the events in the order in which they occurred, and provide a reaction to what happened.
MD.EK.W.5: With guidance and support from adults, respond to questions and suggestions from peers and add details to strengthen writing as needed.
MD.EK.W.6: With guidance and support from adults, explore a variety of digital tools to produce and publish writing, including in collaboration with peers.
MD.EK.W.7: Participate in shared research and writing projects (e.g., explore a number of books by a favorite author and express opinions about them).
MD.EK.W.8: With guidance and support from adults, recall information from experiences or gather information from provided sources to answer a question.
MD.EK.SL.1: Participate in collaborative conversations with diverse partners about kindergarten topics and texts with peers and adults in small and larger groups.
MD.EK.SL.1.a: Follow agreed-upon rules for discussions (e.g., listening to others and taking turns speaking about the topics and texts under discussion).
MD.EK.SL.1.b: Continue a conversation through multiple exchanges.
MD.EK.SL.2: Confirm understanding of a text read aloud or information presented orally or through other media by asking and answering questions about key details and requesting clarification if something is not understood.
MD.EK.SL.3: Ask and answer questions in order to seek help, get information, or clarify something that is not understood.
MD.EK.SL.4: Describe familiar people, places, things, and events and, with prompting and support, provide additional detail.
MD.EK.SL.5: Add drawings or other visual displays to descriptions as desired to provide additional detail.
MD.EK.SL.6: Speak audibly and express thoughts, feelings, and ideas clearly.
MD.EK.L.1: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.
MD.EK.L.1.a: Print many upper- and lowercase letters.
MD.EK.L.1.b: Use frequently occurring nouns and verbs.
MD.EK.L.1.c: Form regular plural nouns orally by adding /s/ or /es/ (e.g., dog, dogs; wish, wishes).
MD.EK.L.1.d: Understand and use question words (interrogatives) (e.g., who, what, where, when, why, how).
MD.EK.L.1.e: Use the most frequently occurring prepositions (e.g., to, from, in, out, on, off, for, of, by, with).
MD.EK.L.1.f: Produce and expand complete sentences in shared language activities.
MD.EK.L.2: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.
MD.EK.L.2.a: Capitalize the first word in a sentence and the pronoun I.
MD.EK.L.2.c: Write a letter or letters for most consonant and short-vowel sounds (phonemes).
MD.EK.L.2.d: Spell simple words phonetically, drawing on knowledge of sound-letter relationships.
MD.EK.L.4: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple meaning words and phrases based on kindergarten reading and content.
MD.EK.L.4.a: Identify new meanings for familiar words and apply them accurately (e.g., knowing duck is a bird and learning the verb to duck).
MD.EK.L.4.b: Use the most frequently occurring inflections and affixes (e.g., -ed, -s, re-, un-, pre-, -ful, -less) as a clue to the meaning of an unknown word.
MD.EK.L.5: With guidance and support from adults, explore word relationships and nuances in word meanings.
MD.EK.L.5.a: Sort common objects into categories (e.g., shapes, foods) to gain a sense of the concepts the categories represent.
MD.EK.L.5.b: Demonstrate understanding of frequently occurring verbs and adjectives by relating them to their opposites (antonyms).
MD.EK.L.5.c: Identify real-life connections between words and their use (e.g., note places at school that are colorful).
MD.EK.L.5.d: Distinguish shades of meaning among verbs describing the same general action (e.g. walk, march, strut, prance) by acting out the meanings.
MD.EK.L.6: Use words and phrases acquired through conversations, reading and being read to, and responding to texts.
MD.MK.CC.A: Know number names and the count sequence.
MD.MK.CC.A.1: Count to 100 by ones and by tens.
MD.MK.CC.A.2: Count forward beginning from a given number within the known sequence (instead of having to begin at 1).
MD.MK.CC.A.3: Write numbers from 0 to 20. Represent a number of objects with a written numeral 0-20 (with 0 representing a count of no objects).
MD.MK.CC.B: Count to tell the number of objects.
MD.MK.CC.B.4: Understand the relationship between numbers and quantities; connect counting to cardinality.
MD.MK.CC.B.4.a: When counting objects, say the number names in the standard order, pairing each object with one and only one number name and each number name with one and only one object.
MD.MK.CC.B.4.b: Understand that the last number name said tells the number of objects counted. The number of objects is the same regardless of their arrangement or the order in which they were counted.
MD.MK.CC.B.4.c: Understand that each successive number name refers to a quantity that is one larger.
MD.MK.CC.B.5: Count to answer “how many?” questions about as many as 20 things arranged in a line, a rectangular array, or a circle, or as many as 10 things in a scattered configuration; given a number from 1-20, count out that many objects.
MD.MK.CC.C.6: Identify whether the number of objects in one group is greater than, less than, or equal to the number of objects in another group, e.g., by using matching and counting strategies (Include groups with up to ten objects).
MD.MK.CC.C.7: Compare two numbers between `1and10` presented as written numerals.
MD.MK.OA.A: Understand addition as putting together and adding to, and undersatnd subtraction as taking apart and taking from.
MD.MK.OA.A.1: Represent addition and subtraction with objects, fingers, mental images, drawings, sounds (e.g., claps), acting out situations, or verbal explanations, expressions, or equations.
MD.MK.OA.A.2: Solve addition and subtraction word problems, and add and subtract within 10, e.g., by using objects or drawings to represent the problem.
MD.MK.OA.A.3: Decompose numbers less than or equal to 10 into pairs in more than one way, e.g., by using objects or drawings, and record each decomposition by a drawing or equation (e.g., 5 = 2 + 3 and 5 = 4 + 1).
MD.MK.OA.A.4: For any number from 1 to 9, find the number that makes 10 when added to the given number, e.g., by using objects or drawings, and record the answer with a drawing or equation.
MD.MK.NBT.A: work with numbers 11-19 to gain foundations for place value.
MD.MK.NBT.A.1: Compose and decompose numbers from 11 to 19 into ten ones and some further ones, e.g., by using objects or drawings, and record each composition or decomposition by a drawing or equation (such as 18 = 10 + 8); understand that these numbers are composed of ten ones and one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine ones.
MD.MK.MD.A.1: Describe measurable attributes of objects, such as length or weight. Describe several measurable attributes of a single object.
MD.MK.MD.A.2: Directly compare two objects with a measurable attribute in common, to see which object has “more of”/”less of” the attribute, and describe the difference.
MD.MK.MD.B: Classify objects and count the number of objects in each category.
MD.MK.MD.B.3: Classify objects into given categories; count the number of objects in each category and sort the categories by count (Limit category counts to be less than or equal to 10).
MD.MK.G.A: Identify and describe shapes (squares, circles, triangles, rectangles, hexagons, cubes, cones, cylinders, and spheres).
MD.MK.G.A.1: Describe objects in the environment using names of shapes, and describe the relative positions of these objects using terms such as above, below, beside, in front of, behind, and next to.
MD.MK.G.A.2: Correctly name shapes regardless of their orientations or overall size.
MD.MK.G.A.3: Identify shapes as two-dimensional (lying in a plane, “flat”) or three-dimensional (“solid”).
MD.MK.G.B: Analyze, compare, create, and compose shapes.
MD.MK.G.B.4: Analyze and compare two- and three-dimensional shapes, in different sizes and orientations, using informal language to describe their similarities, differences, parts (e.g., number of sides and vertices/”corners”) and other attributes (e.g., having sides of equal length).
MD.MK.G.B.5: Model shapes in the world by building shapes from components (e.g., sticks and clay balls) and drawing shapes.
MD.MK.G.B.6: Compose simple shapes to form larger shapes.
MD.E1.RL.1: Ask and answer questions about key details in a text.
MD.E1.RL.2: Retell stories, including key details, and demonstrate understanding of their central message or lesson.
MD.E1.RL.3: Describe characters, settings, and major events in a story, using key details.
MD.E1.RL.4: Identify words and phrases in stories or poems that suggest feelings or appeal to the senses.
MD.E1.RL.5: Explain major differences between books that tell stories and books that give information, drawing on a wide reading of a range of text types.
MD.E1.RL.6: Identify who is telling the story at various points in a text.
MD.E1.RL.7: Use illustrations and details in a story to describe its characters, setting, or events.
MD.E1.RL.9: Compare and contrast the adventures and experiences of characters in stories.
MD.E1.RL.10: With prompting and support, read prose and poetry of appropriate complexity for grade 1.
MD.E1.RI.1: Ask and answer questions about key details in a text.
MD.E1.RI.2: Identify the main topic and retell key details of a text.
MD.E1.RI.3: Describe the connection between two individuals, events, ideas, or pieces of information in a text.
MD.E1.RI.4: Ask and answer questions to help determine or clarify the meaning of words and phrases in a text.
MD.E1.RI.5: Know and use various text features (e.g., headings, tables of contents, glossaries, electronic menus, icons) to locate key facts or information in a text.
MD.E1.RI.6: Distinguish between information provided by pictures or other illustrations and information provided by the words in a text.
MD.E1.RI.7: Use the illustrations and details in a text to describe its key ideas.
MD.E1.RI.8: Identify the reasons an author gives to support points in a text.
MD.E1.RI.9: Identify basic similarities in and differences between two texts on the same topic (e.g., in illustrations, descriptions, or procedures).
MD.E1.RI.10: With prompting and support, read informational texts appropriately complex for grade 1.
MD.E1.RF.1: Demonstrate understanding of the organization and basic features of print.
MD.E1.RF.1.a: Recognize the distinguishing features of a sentence (e.g., first word, capitalization, ending punctuation).
MD.E1.RF.2: Demonstrate understanding of spoken words, syllables, and sounds (phonemes).
MD.E1.RF.2.a: Distinguish long from short vowel sounds in spoken single-syllable words.
MD.E1.RF.2.b: Orally produce single-syllable words by blending sounds (phonemes), including consonant blends.
MD.E1.RF.2.c: Isolate and pronounce initial, medial vowel, and final sounds (phonemes), in spoken single-syllable words.
MD.E1.RF.2.d: Segment spoken single-syllable words into their complete sequence of individual sounds (phonemes).
MD.E1.RF.3: Know and apply grade-level phonics and word analysis skills in decoding words.
MD.E1.RF.3.a: Know the spelling-sound correspondences for common consonant digraphs.
MD.E1.RF.3.c: Know final -e and common vowel team conventions for representing long vowel sounds.
MD.E1.RF.3.d: Use knowledge that every syllable must have a vowel sound to determine the number of syllables in a printed word.
MD.E1.RF.3.e: Decode two-syllable words following basic patterns by breaking the words into syllables.
MD.E1.RF.3.g: Recognize and read grade-appropriate irregularly spelled words.
MD.E1.RF.4: Read with sufficient accuracy and fluency to support comprehension.
MD.E1.RF.4.a: Read grade-level text with purpose and understanding.
MD.E1.RF.4.b: Read grade-level text orally with accuracy, appropriate rate, and expression on successive readings.
MD.E1.RF.4.c: Use context to confirm or self-correct word recognition and understanding, rereading as necessary.
MD.E1.W.1: Write opinion pieces in which they introduce the topic or name the book they are writing about, state an opinion, supply a reason for the opinion, and provide some sense of closure.
MD.E1.W.2: Write informative/explanatory texts in which they name a topic, supply some facts about the topic, and provide some sense of closure.
MD.E1.W.3: Write narratives in which they recount two or more appropriately sequenced events, include some details regarding what happened, use temporal words to signal event order, and provide some sense of closure.
MD.E1.W.5: With guidance and support from adults, focus on a topic, respond to questions and suggestions from peers, and add details to strengthen writing as needed.
MD.E1.W.6: With guidance and support from adults, explore a variety of digital tools to produce and publish writing, including in collaboration with peers.
MD.E1.W.7: Participate in shared research and writing projects (e.g., explore a number of “how-to” books on a given topic and use them to write a sequence of instructions).
MD.E1.W.8: With guidance and support from adults, recall information from experiences or gather information from provided sources to answer a question.
MD.E1.SL.1: Participate in collaborative conversations with diverse partners about grade 1 topics and texts with peers and adults in small and larger groups.
MD.E1.SL.1.a: Follow agreed-upon rules for discussion (e.g., listening to others with care, speaking one at a time about the topics and texts under discussion).
MD.E1.SL.1.b: Build on others' talk in conversations by responding to the comments of others through multiple exchanges.
MD.E1.SL.1.c: Ask questions to clear up any confusion about the topics and texts under discussion.
MD.E1.SL.2: Ask and answer questions about key details in a text read aloud or information presented orally or through other media.
MD.E1.SL.3: Ask and answer questions about what a speaker says in order to gather additional information, or clarify something that is not understood.
MD.E1.SL.4: Describe people, places, things, and events with relevant details, expressing ideas and feelings clearly.
MD.E1.SL.5: Add drawings or other visual displays to descriptions when appropriate to clarify ideas, thoughts, and feelings.
MD.E1.SL.6: Produce complete sentences when appropriate to task and situation.
MD.E1.L.1: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.
MD.E1.L.1.a: Print all upper- and lowercase letters.
MD.E1.L.1.b: Use common, proper, and possessive nouns.
MD.E1.L.1.c: Use singular and plural nouns with matching verbs in basic sentences (e.g., He hops; We hop).
MD.E1.L.1.d: Use personal, possessive, and indefinite pronouns (e.g., I, me, my; they, them, their, anyone, everything).
MD.E1.L.1.e: Use verbs to convey a sense of past, present, and future (e.g., Yesterday I walked home; Today I walk home; Tomorrow I will walk home).
MD.E1.L.1.g: Use frequently occurring conjunctions (e.g., and, but, or, so, because).
MD.E1.L.1.i: Use frequently occurring prepositions (e.g., during, beyond, toward).
MD.E1.L.1.j: Produce and expand complete simple and compound declarative, interrogative, imperative, and exclamatory sentences in response to prompts.
MD.E1.L.2: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.
MD.E1.L.2.a: Capitalize dates and names of people.
MD.E1.L.2.c: Use commas in dates and to separate single words in a series.
MD.E1.L.2.d: Use conventional spelling for words with common spelling patterns and for frequently occurring irregular words.
MD.E1.L.2.e: Spell untaught words phonetically, drawing on phonemic awareness and spelling conventions.
MD.E1.L.4: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grade 1 reading and content, choosing flexibly from an array of strategies.
MD.E1.L.4.a: Use sentence-level context as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.
MD.E1.L.4.b: Use frequently occurring affixes as a clue to the meaning of a word.
MD.E1.L.4.c: Identify frequently occurring root words (e.g., look) and their inflectional forms (e.g. looks, looked, looking).
MD.E1.L.5: With guidance and support from adults, demonstrate understanding of word relationships and nuances in word meanings.
MD.E1.L.5.a: Sort words into categories (e.g., colors, clothing) to gain a sense of the concepts the categories represent.
MD.E1.L.5.b: Define words by category and by one or more key attributes (e.g., a duck is a bird that swims; a tiger is a large cat with stripes).
MD.E1.L.5.c: Identify real-life connections between words and their use (e.g., note places at home that are cozy).
MD.E1.L.5.d: Distinguish shades of meaning among verbs differing in manner (e.g., look, peek, glance, stare, glare, scowl) and adjectives differing in intensity (e.g., large, gigantic) by defining or choosing them or by acting out the meanings.
MD.E1.L.6: Use words and phrases acquired through conversations, reading and being read to, and responding to texts, including using frequently occurring conjunctions to signal simple relationships (e.g., because).
MD.M1.OA.A: Represent and solve problems involving addition and subtraction.
MD.M1.OA.A.1: Use addition and subtraction within 20 to solve word problems involving situations of adding to, taking from, putting together, taking apart, and comparing, with unknowns in all positions, e.g., by using objects, drawings, and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.
MD.M1.OA.A.2: Solve word problems that call for addition of three whole numbers whose sum is less than or equal to 20, e.g., by using objects, drawings, and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.
MD.M1.OA.B: Understand and apply properties of operations and the relationship between addition and subtraction.
MD.M1.OA.B.3: Apply properties of operations as strategies to add and subtract.
MD.M1.OA.B.4: Understand subtraction as an unknown addend problem.
MD.M1.OA.C.5: Relate counting to addition and subtraction (e.g., by counting on 2 to add 2).
MD.M1.OA.C.6: Add and subtract within 20, demonstrating fluency for addition and subtraction within 10. Use strategies such as counting on, making ten (e.g. 8 + 6 = 8 + 2 + 4, which leads to 10 + 4 = 14); decomposing a number leading to a ten (e.g., 13 - 4 = 13 - 3 - 1, which leads to 10 - 1 = 9); using the relationship between addition and subtraction (e.g., knowing that 8 + 4 = 12, one knows 12 - 8 = 4); and creating equivalent but easier or known sums (e.g., adding 6 + 7 by creating the known equivalent 6 + 6 + 1 = 12 + 1, which equals 13).
MD.M1.OA.D: Work with addition and subtraction equations.
MD.M1.OA.D.7: Understand the meaning of the equal sign, and determine if equations involving addition and subtraction are true or false.
MD.M1.OA.D.8: Determine the unknown whole number in an addition or subtraction equation relating three whole numbers.
MD.M1.NBT.A.1: Count to 120 starting at any number less than 120. In this range, read and write numerals and represent a number of objects with a written numeral.
MD.M1.NBT.B.2: Understand that the two digits of a two-digit number represent amounts of tens and ones.
MD.M1.NBT.B.2.a: Understand the following as a special case: 10 can be thought of as a bundle of ten ones -- called a “ten.”
MD.M1.NBT.B.2.b: Understand the following as a special case: The numbers from 11 to 19 are composed of a ten and one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine ones.
MD.M1.NBT.B.2.c: Understand the following as a special case: The numbers 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90 refer to one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine tens (and 0 ones).
MD.M1.NBT.B.3: Compare two two-digit numbers based on meanings of the tens and ones digits, recording the results of comparisons with the symbols `>,=,and<`.
MD.M1.NBT.C: Use place value understanding and properties to add and subtract.
MD.M1.NBT.A.4: Add within `100`, including adding a two-digit number and a one-digit number, and adding a two-digit number and a multiple of 10, using concrete models or drawings and strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction; relate the strategy to a written method and explain the reasoning used. Understand that in adding two-digit numbers, one adds tens and tens, ones and ones, and sometimes it is necessary to compose a ten.
MD.M1.NBT.A.5: Given a two-digit number, mentally find 10 more or 10 less than the number, without having to count; explain the reasoning used.
MD.M1.NBT.A.6: Subtract multiples of `10` in the range of `10-90` from multiples of `10` in the range of `10-90` (positive or zero differences), using concrete models or drawings and strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction; relate the strategy to a written method and explain the reasoning used.
MD.M1.MD.A: Measure lengths indirectly and by iterating length units.
MD.M1.MD.A.1: Order three objects by length; compare the lengths of two objects indirectly by using a third object.
MD.M1.MD.A.2: Express the length of an object as a whole number of length units, by laying multiple copies of a shorter object (the length unit) end to end; understand that the length measurement of an object is the number of same-size length units that span it with no gaps or overlaps.
MD.M1.MD.B.3: Tell and write time in `text(hours)` and half-hours using analog and digital clocks.
MD.M1.MD.C.4: Organize, represent, and interpret data with up to three categories; ask and answer questions about the total number of data points, how many in each category, and how many more or less are in one category than in another.
MD.M1.G.A: Reason with shapes and their attributes.
MD.M1.G.A.1: Distinguish between defining attributes (e.g., triangles are closed and three-sided) versus non-defining attributes (e.g., color, orientation, overall size); build and draw shapes to possess defining attributes.
MD.M1.G.A.2: Compose two-dimensional shapes (rectangles, squares, trapezoids, triangles, half-circles, and quarter-circles) or three-dimensional shapes (cubes, right rectangular prisms, right circular cones, and right circular cylinders) to create a composite shape, and compose new shapes from the composite shape.
MD.M1.G.A.3: Partition circles and rectangles into two and four equal shares, describe the shares using the words halves, fourths, and quarters, and use the phrases half of, fourth of, and quarter of. Describe the whole as two of, or four of the shares. Understand for these examples that decomposing into more equal shares creates smaller shares.
MD.E2.RL.1: Ask and answer such questions as who, what, where, when, why, and how to demonstrate understanding of key details in a text.
MD.E2.RL.2: Recount stories, including fables and folktales from diverse cultures, and determine their central message, lesson, or moral.
MD.E2.RL.3: Describe how characters in a story respond to major events and challenges.
MD.E2.RL.4: Describe how words and phrases (e.g., regular beats, alliteration, rhymes, repeated lines) supply rhythm and meaning in a story, poem, or song.
MD.E2.RL.5: Describe the overall structure of a story, including describing how the beginning introduces the story and the ending concludes the action.
MD.E2.RL.6: Acknowledge differences in the points of view of characters, including by speaking in a different voice for each character when reading dialogue aloud.
MD.E2.RL.7: Use information gained from the illustrations and words in a print or digital text to demonstrate understanding of its characters, setting, or plot.
MD.E2.RL.9: Compare and contrast two or more versions of the same story (e.g., Cinderella stories) by different authors or from different cultures.
MD.E2.RL.10: By the end of the year, read and comprehend literature, including stories and poetry, in the grades 2-3 text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.
MD.E2.RI.1: Ask and answer such questions as who, what, where, when, why, and how to demonstrate understanding of key details in a text.
MD.E2.RI.2: Identify the main topic of a multipara graph text as well as the focus of specific paragraphs within the text.
MD.E2.RI.3: Describe the connection between a series of historic events, scientific ideas or concepts, or steps in technical procedures in a text.
MD.E2.RI.4: Determine the meaning of words and phrases in a text relevant to a grade 2 topic or subject area.
MD.E2.RI.5: Know and use various text features (e.g., captions, bold print, subheadings, glossaries, indexes, electronic menus, icons) to locate key facts or information in a text efficiently.
MD.E2.RI.6: Identify the main purpose of a text, including what the author wants to answer, explain, or describe.
MD.E2.RI.7: Explain how specific images (e.g., a diagram showing how a machine works) contribute to and clarify a text.
MD.E2.RI.8: Describe how reasons support specific points the author makes in a text.
MD.E2.RI.9: Compare and contrast the most important points presented by two texts on the same topic.
MD.E2.RI.10: By the end of the year, read and comprehend informational texts, including history/social studies, science, and technical texts, in the grades 2-3 text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.
MD.E2.RF.3: Know and apply grade-level phonics and word analysis skills in decoding words.
MD.E2.RF.3.a: Distinguish long and short vowels when reading regularly spelled one-syllable words.
MD.E2.RF.3.b: Know spelling-sound correspondences for additional common vowel teams.
MD.E2.RF.3.c: Decode regularly spelled two-syllable words with long vowels.
MD.E2.RF.3.d: Decode words with common prefixes and suffixes.
MD.E2.RF.3.e: Identify words with inconsistent but common spelling-sound correspondences.
MD.E2.RF.3.f: Recognize and read grade-appropriate irregularly spelled words.
MD.E2.RF.4: Read with sufficient accuracy and fluency to support comprehension.
MD.E2.RF.4.a: Read grade-level text with purpose and understanding.
MD.E2.RF.4.b: Read grade-level text orally with accuracy, appropriate rate, and expression on successive readings.
MD.E2.RF.4.c: Use context to confirm or self-correct word recognition and understanding, rereading as necessary.
MD.E2.W.1: Write opinion pieces in which they introduce the topic or book they are writing about, state an opinion, supply reasons that support the opinion, use linking words (e.g., because, and, also) to connect opinion and reasons, and provide a concluding statement or section.
MD.E2.W.2: Write informative/explanatory texts in which they introduce a topic, use facts and definitions to develop points, and provide a concluding statement or section.
MD.E2.W.3: Write narratives in which they recount a well- elaborated event or short sequence of events, include details to describe actions, thoughts, and feelings, use temporal words to signal event order, and provide a sense of closure.
MD.E2.W.5: With guidance and support from adults and peers, focus on a topic and strengthen writing as needed by revising and editing.
MD.E2.W.6: With guidance and support from adults, use a variety of digital tools to produce and publish writing, including in collaboration with peers.
MD.E2.W.7: Participate in shared research and writing projects (e.g., read a number of books on a single topic to produce a report; record science observations).
MD.E2.W.8: Recall information from experiences or gather information from provided sources to answer a question.
MD.E2.SL.1: Participate in collaborative conversations with diverse partners about grade 2 topics and texts with peers and adults in small and larger groups.
MD.E2.SL.1.a: Follow agreed-upon rules for discussion (e.g., gaining the floor in respectful ways, listening to others with care, speaking one at a time about the topics and texts under discussion).
MD.E2.SL.1.b: Build on others' talk in conversations by linking their comments to the remarks of others.
MD.E2.SL.1.c: Ask for clarification and further explanation as needed about the topics and texts under discussion.
MD.E2.SL.2: Recount or describe key ideas or details from a text read aloud or information presented orally or through other media.
MD.E2.SL.3: Ask and answer questions about what a speaker says in order to clarify comprehension, gather additional information, or deepen understanding of a topic or issue.
MD.E2.SL.4: Tell a story or recount an experience with appropriate facts and relevant, descriptive details, speaking audibly in coherent sentences.
MD.E2.SL.5: Create audio recordings of stories or poems; add drawings or other visual displays to stories or recounts of experiences when appropriate to clarify ideas, thoughts, and feelings.
MD.E2.SL.6: Produce complete sentences when appropriate to task and situation in order to provide requested detail or clarification.
MD.E2.L.1: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.
MD.E2.L.1.b: Form and use frequently occurring irregular plural nouns (e.g., feet, children, teeth, mice, fish).
MD.E2.L.1.d: Form and use the past tense of frequently occurring irregular verbs (e.g., sat, hid, told).
MD.E2.L.1.e: Use adjectives and adverbs, and choose between them depending on what is to be modified.
MD.E2.L.1.f: Produce, expand, and rearrange complete simple and compound sentences (e.g., The boy watched the movie; The little boy watched the movie; The action movie was watched by the little boy).
MD.E2.L.2: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.
MD.E2.L.2.a: Capitalize holidays, product names, and geographic names.
MD.E2.L.2.b: Use commas in greetings and closings of letters.
MD.E2.L.2.c: Use an apostrophe to form contractions and frequently occurring possessives.
MD.E2.L.2.d: Generalize learned spelling patterns when writing words (e.g., cage → badge; boy → boil).
MD.E2.L.2.e: Consult reference materials, including beginning dictionaries, as needed to check and correct spellings.
MD.E2.L.3: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening.
MD.E2.L.3.a: Compare formal and informal uses of English.
MD.E2.L.4: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple meaning words and phrases based on grade 2 reading and content, choosing flexibly from an array of strategies.
MD.E2.L.4.a: Use sentence-level context as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.
MD.E2.L.4.b: Determine the meaning of the new word formed when a known prefix is added to a known word (e.g., happy/unhappy, tell/retell).
MD.E2.L.4.c: Use a known root word as a clue to the meaning of an unknown word with the same root (e.g., addition, additional).
MD.E2.L.4.d: Use knowledge of the meaning of individual words to predict the meaning of compound words (e.g., birdhouse, lighthouse, housefly; bookshelf, notebook, bookmark).
MD.E2.L.4.e: Use glossaries and beginning dictionaries, both print and digital, to determine or clarify the meaning of words and phrases.
MD.E2.L.5: Demonstrate understanding of word relationships and nuances in word meanings.
MD.E2.L.5.a: Identify real-life connections between words and their use (e.g., describe foods that are spicy or juicy).
MD.E2.L.5.b: Distinguish shades of meaning among closely related verbs (e.g., toss, throw, hurl) and closely related adjectives (e.g., thin, slender, skinny, scrawny).
MD.E2.L.6: Use words and phrases acquired through conversations, reading and being read to, and responding to texts, including using adjectives and adverbs to describe (e.g., When other kids are happy that makes me happy).
MD.M2.OA.A: Represent and solve problems involving addition and subtraction.
MD.M2.OA.A.1: Use addition and subtraction within `100` to solve one- and two-step word problems involving situations of adding to, taking from, putting together, taking apart, and comparing, with unknowns in all positions, e.g., by using objects, drawings, and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.
MD.M2.OA.A.2: Fluently add and subtract within 20 using mental strategies. By end of Grade 2, know from memory all sums of two one-digit numbers.
MD.M2.OA.C: Work with equal groups of objects to gain foundations for mulitplication.
MD.M2.OA.C.3: Determine whether a group of objects (up to 20) has an odd or even number of members, e.g., by pairing objects or counting them by `2text(s)`; write an equation to express an even number as a sum of two equal addends.
MD.M2.OA.C.4: Use addition to find the total number of objects arranged in rectangular arrays with up to `5` rows and up to `5` columns; write an equation to express the total as a sum of equal addends.
MD.M2.NBT.A.1: Understand that the three digits of a three-digit number represent amounts of hundreds, tens, and ones; e.g., 706 equals 7 hundreds, 0 tens, and 6 ones.
MD.M2.NBT.A.1.a: Understand the following as a special case: 100 can be thought of as a bundle of ten tens -- called a “hundred.”
MD.M2.NBT.A.1.b: Understand the following as a special case: The numbers 100, 200, 300, 400, 500, 600, 700, 800, 900 refer to one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine hundreds (and 0 tens and 0 ones).
MD.M2.NBT.A.3: Read and write numbers to `1000` using base-ten numerals, number names, and expanded form.
MD.M2.NBT.A.4: Compare two three-digit numbers based on meanings of the hundreds, tens, and ones digits, using `>,=,and<` symbols to record the results of comparisons.
MD.M2.NBT.B: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to add and subtract.
MD.M2.NBT.B.5: Fluently add and subtract within `100` using strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction.
MD.M2.NBT.B.6: Add up to four two-digit numbers using strategies based on place value, properties of operations.
MD.M2.NBT.B.7: Add and subtract within `1000`, using concrete models or drawings and strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction; relate the strategy to a written method. Understand that in adding or subtracting three-digit numbers, one adds or subtracts hundreds and hundreds, tens and tens, ones and ones; and sometimes it is necessary to compose or decompose tens or hundreds.
MD.M2.NBT.B.8: Mentally add `10or100` to a given number 100-900, and mentally subtract `10or100` from a given number 100-900.
MD.M2.NBT.B.9: Explain why addition and subtraction strategies work, using place value and the properties of operations.
MD.M2.MD.A: Measure and estimate lengths in standard units.
MD.M2.MD.A.1: Measure the length of an object by selecting and using appropriate tools such as rulers, yardsticks, meter sticks, and measuring tapes.
MD.M2.MD.A.2: Measure the length of an object twice, using length units of different lengths for the two measurements; describe how the two measurements relate to the size of the unit chosen.
MD.M2.MD.A.3: Estimate lengths using units of inches, feet, centimeters, and meters.
MD.M2.MD.A.4: Measure to determine how much longer one object is than another, expressing the length difference in terms of a standard length unit.
MD.M2.MD.B: Relate addition and subtraction to length.
MD.M2.MD.B.5: Use addition and subtraction within `100` to solve word problems involving lengths that are given in the same units, e.g., by using drawings (such as drawings of rulers) and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.
MD.M2.MD.B.6: Represent whole numbers as lengths from `0` on a number line diagram with equally spaced points corresponding to the number 0, 1, 2, ..., and represent whole number sums and differences within `100` on a number line diagram.
MD.M2.MD.C.7: Tell and write time from analog and digital clocks to the nearest five minutes, using a.m. and p.m.
MD.M2.MD.C.8: Solve word problems involving dollar bills, quarters, dimes, nickels, and pennies, using $ and ¢ symbols appropriately.
MD.M2.MD.C.9: Generate measurement data by measuring lengths of several objects to the nearest whole unit, or by making repeated measurements of the same object. Show the measurements by making a line plot, where the horizontal scale is marked off in whole number units.
MD.M2.MD.C.10: Draw a picture graph and a bar graph (with single-unit scale) to represent a data set with up to four categories. Solve simple put-together, take-apart, and compare problems using information presented in a bar graph.
MD.M2.G.A: Reason with shapes and their attributes.
MD.M2.G.A.1: Recognize and draw shapes having specific attributes, such as a given number of angles or a given number of equal faces. Identify triangles, quadrilaterals, pentagons, hexagons, and cubes.
MD.M2.G.A.2: Partition a rectangle into rows and columns of same-size squares and count to find the total number of them.
MD.M2.G.A.3: Partition circles and rectangles into two, three, or four equal shares, describe the shares using the words halves, thirds, half of, a third of, etc., and describe the whole as two halves, three thirds, four fourths. Recognize that equal shares of identical wholes need not have the same shape.
MD.E3.RL.1: Ask and answer questions to demonstrate understanding of a text, referring explicitly to the text as the basis for the answers.
MD.E3.RL.2: Recount stories, including fables, folktales, and myths from diverse cultures; determine the central message, lesson, or moral and explain how it is conveyed through key details in the text.
MD.E3.RL.3: Describe characters in a story (e.g., their traits, motivations, or feelings) and explain how their actions contribute to the sequence of events.
MD.E3.RL.4: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, distinguishing literal from nonliteral language.
MD.E3.RL.5: Refer to parts of stories, dramas, and poems when writing or speaking about a text, using terms such as chapter, scene, and stanza; describe how each successive part builds on earlier sections.
MD.E3.RL.6: Distinguish their own point of view from that of the narrator or those of the characters.
MD.E3.RL.7: Explain how specific aspects of a text's illustrations contribute to what is conveyed by the words in a story (e.g., create mood, emphasize aspects of a character or setting).
MD.E3.RL.9: Compare and contrast the themes, settings, and plots of stories written by the same author about the same or similar characters (e.g., in books from a series).
MD.E3.RL.10: By the end of the year, read and comprehend literature, including stories, dramas, and poetry, at the high end of the grades 2-3 text complexity band independently and proficiently.
MD.E3.RI.1: Ask and answer questions to demonstrate understanding of a text, referring explicitly to the text as the basis for the answers.
MD.E3.RI.2: Determine the main idea of a text; recount the key details and explain how they support the main idea.
MD.E3.RI.3: Describe the relationship between a series of historical events, scientific ideas or concepts, or steps in technical procedures in a text, using language that pertains to time, sequence, and cause/effect.
MD.E3.RI.4: Determine the meaning of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases in a text relevant to a grade 3 topic or subject area.
MD.E3.RI.5: Use text features and search tools (e.g., key words, sidebars, hyperlinks) to locate information relevant to a given topic efficiently.
MD.E3.RI.6: Distinguish their own point of view from that of the author of a text.
MD.E3.RI.7: Use information gained from illustrations (e.g., maps, photographs) and the words in a text to demonstrate understanding of the text (e.g., where, when, why, and how key events occur).
MD.E3.RI.8: Describe the logical connection between particular sentences and paragraphs in a text (e.g., comparison, cause/effect, first/second/third in a sequence).
MD.E3.RI.9: Compare and contrast the most important points and key details presented in two texts on the same topic.
MD.E3.RI.10: By the end of the year, read and comprehend informational texts, including history/social studies, science, and technical texts, at the high end of the grades 2-3 text complexity band independently and proficiently.
MD.E3.RF.3: Know and apply grade-level phonics and word analysis skills in decoding words.
MD.E3.RF.3.a: Identify and know the meaning of the most common prefixes and derivational suffixes.
MD.E3.RF.3.b: Decode words with common Latin suffixes.
MD.E3.RF.4: Read with sufficient accuracy and fluency to support comprehension.
MD.E3.RF.4.a: Read grade-level text with purpose and understanding.
MD.E3.RF.4.b: Read grade-level prose and poetry orally with accuracy, appropriate rate, and expression on successive readings.
MD.E3.RF.4.c: Use context to confirm or self-correct word recognition and understanding,rereading as necessary.
MD.E3.W.1: Write opinion pieces on topics or texts, supporting a point of view with reasons.
MD.E3.W.1.a: Introduce the topic or text they are writing about, state an opinion, and create an organizational structure that lists reasons.
MD.E3.W.1.b: Provide reasons that support the opinion
MD.E3.W.1.c: Use linking words and phrases (e.g., because, therefore, since, for example) to connect opinion and reasons.
MD.E3.W.1.d: Provide a concluding statement or section.
MD.E3.W.2: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine a topic and convey ideas and information clearly.
MD.E3.W.2.a: Introduce a topic and group related information together; include illustrations when useful to aiding comprehension.
MD.E3.W.2.b: Develop the topic with facts, definitions, and details.
MD.E3.W.2.c: Use linking words and phrases (e.g., also, another, and, more, but) to connect ideas within categories of information.
MD.E3.W.2.d: Provide a concluding statement or section.
MD.E3.W.3: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, descriptive details, and clear event sequences.
MD.E3.W.3.a: Establish a situation and introduce a narrator and/or characters; organize an event sequence that unfolds naturally.
MD.E3.W.3.b: Use dialogue and descriptions of actions, thoughts, and feelings to develop experiences and events or show the response of characters to situations.
MD.E3.W.3.c: Use temporal words and phrases to signal event order.
MD.E3.W.4: With guidance and support from adults, produce writing in which the development and organization are appropriate to task and purpose.
MD.E3.W.5: With guidance and support from peers and adults, develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, and editing.
MD.E3.W.6: With guidance and support from adults, use technology to produce and publish writing (using keyboarding skills) as well as to interact and collaborate with others.
MD.E3.W.7: Conduct short research projects that build knowledge about a topic.
MD.E3.W.8: Recall information from experiences or gather information from print and digital sources; take brief notes on sources and sort evidence into provided categories.
MD.E3.W.10: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of discipline-specific tasks, purposes, and audiences.
MD.E3.SL.1: Engage effectively in a range of collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in groups, and teacher-led) with diverse partners on grade 3 topics and texts, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly.
MD.E3.SL.1.a: Come to discussions prepared, having read or studied required material; explicitly draw on that preparation and other information known about the topic to explore ideas under discussion.
MD.E3.SL.1.b: Follow agreed-upon rules for discussions (e.g., gaining the floor in respectful ways, listening to others with care, speaking one at a time about the topics and texts under discussion).
MD.E3.SL.1.c: Ask questions to check understanding of information presented, stay on topic, and link their comments to the remarks of others.
MD.E3.SL.1.d: Explain their own ideas and understanding in light of the discussion.
MD.E3.SL.2: Determine the main ideas and supporting details of a text read aloud or information presented in diverse media quantitatively, and orally.
MD.E3.SL.3: Ask and answer questions about information from a speaker, offering appropriate elaboration and detail.
MD.E3.SL.4: Report on a topic or text, tell a story, or recount an experience with appropriate facts and relevant, descriptive details, speaking clearly at an understandable pace.
MD.E3.SL.5: Create engaging audio recordings of stories or poems that demonstrate fluid reading at an understandable pace; add visual displays when appropriate to emphasize or enhance certain facts or details.
MD.E3.SL.6: Speak in complete sentences when appropriate to task and situation in order to provide requested detail or clarification.
MD.E3.L.1: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.
MD.E3.L.1.a: Explain the function of nouns, pronouns, verbs, adjectives, and adverbs in general and their functions in particular sentences.
MD.E3.L.1.b: Form and use regular and irregular plural nouns.
MD.E3.L.1.d: Form and use regular and irregular verbs.
MD.E3.L.1.e: Form and use the simple (e.g., I walked; I walk; I will walk) verb tenses.
MD.E3.L.1.g: Form and use comparative and superlative adjectives and adverbs, and choose between them depending on what is to be modified.
MD.E3.L.1.i: Produce simple, compound, and complex sentences.
MD.E3.L.2: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.
MD.E3.L.2.c: Use commas and quotation marks in dialogue.
MD.E3.L.2.e: Use conventional spelling for high-frequency and other studied words and for adding suffixes to base words (e.g., sitting, smiled, cries, happiness).
MD.E3.L.2.f: Use spelling patterns and generalizations (e.g., word families, position-based spellings,syllable patterns, ending rules, meaningful word parts) in writing words.
MD.E3.L.2.g: Consult reference materials, including beginning dictionaries, as needed to check and correct spellings.
MD.E3.L.3: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing,speaking, reading, or listening.
MD.E3.L.3.a: Choose words and phrases for effect.
MD.E3.L.3.b: Recognize and observe differences between the conventions of spoken and written standard English.
MD.E3.L.4: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning word and phrases based on grade 3 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.
MD.E3.L.4.a: Use sentence-level context as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.
MD.E3.L.4.b: Determine the meaning of the new word formed when a known affix is added to a known word (e.g., agreeable/disagreeable, comfortable/uncomfortable, care/careless, heat/preheat).
MD.E3.L.4.c: Use a known root word as a clue to the meaning of an unknown word with the same root (e.g., company, companion).
MD.E3.L.4.d: Use glossaries or beginning dictionaries, both print and digital, to determine or clarify the precise meaning of key words and phrases.
MD.E3.L.5: Demonstrate understanding of word relationships and nuances in word meanings.
MD.E3.L.5.a: Distinguish the literal and nonliteral meanings of words and phrases in context (e.g., take steps).
MD.E3.L.5.b: Identify real-life connections between words and their use (e.g., describe people who are friendly or helpful).
MD.E3.L.5.c: Distinguish shades of meaning among related words that describe states of mind or degrees of certainty (e.g., knew, believed, suspected, heard, wondered).
MD.E3.L.6: Acquire and use accurately grade appropriate conversational, general academic and domain-specific words and phrases, including those that signal spatial and temporal relationships (e.g., After dinner that night we went looking for them).
MD.M3.OA.A: Represent and solve problems involving multiplication and division.
MD.M3.OA.A.1: Interpret products of whole numbers, e.g., interpret `5xx7` as the total number of objects in `5` groups of `7` objects each.
MD.M3.OA.A.2: Interpret whole-number quotients of whole numbers, e.g., interpret `56-:8` as the number of objects in each share when `56` objects are partitioned equally into `8` shares, or as a number of shares when `56` objects are partitioned into equal shares of `8` objects each.
MD.M3.OA.A.3: Use multiplication and division within `100` to solve word problems in situations involving equal groups, or arrays, e.g., by using drawings and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.
MD.M3.OA.A.4: Determine the unknown whole number in a multiplication or division equation relating three whole numbers.
MD.M3.OA.B: Understand properties of multiplication and the relationship between multiplication and division.
MD.M3.OA.B.5: Apply properties of operations as strategies to multiply and divide.
MD.M3.OA.C.7: Fluently multiply and divide within `100`, using strategies such as the relationship between multiplication and division (e.g., knowing that `8xx5=40`, one knows `40-:5=8`) or properties of operations. By the end of Grade 3, know from memory all products of two one-digit numbers.
MD.M3.OA.D: Solve problems involving the four operations, and identify and explain patterns in arithmetic.
MD.M3.OA.D.8: Solve two-step word problems using the four operations. Represent these problems using equations with a letter standing for the unknown quantity. Assess the reasonableness of answers using mental computation and estimation strategies including rounding.
MD.M3.OA.D.9: Identify arithmetic patterns (including patterns in the addition table or multiplication table), and explain them using properties of operations.
MD.M3.NBT.A: Use place value understanding and properties of operation to perform multi-digit arithmetic.
MD.M3.NBT.A.1: Use place value understanding to round whole numbers to the nearest `10or100`.
MD.M3.NBT.A.2: Fluently add and subtract within `1000` using strategies and algorithms based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction.
MD.M3.NBT.A.3: Multiply one-digit whole numbers by multiples of `10` in the range of `10-90` (e.g., 9 × 80, 5 × 60) using strategies based on place value and properties of operations.
MD.M3.NF.A: Develop understanding of fractions as numbers.
MD.M3.NF.A.1: Understand a fraction `1/b` as the quantity formed by `1` part when a whole is partitioned into `b` equal parts; understand a fraction `a/b` as the quantity formed by a parts of size `1/b`.
MD.M3.NF.A.2: Understand a fraction as a number on the number line; represent fractions on a number line diagram.
MD.M3.NF.A.2.a: Represent a fraction `1/b` on a number line diagram by defining the interval from `0` to `1` as the whole and partitioning it into `b` equal parts. Recognize that each part has size `1/b` and that the endpoint of the part based at `0` locates the number `1/b` on the number line.
MD.M3.NF.A.2.b: Represent a fraction `a/b` on a number line diagram by marking off a lengths of `1/b` from `0`. Recognize that the resulting interval has size `a/b` and that its endpoint locates the number `a/b` on the number line.
MD.M3.NF.A.3: Explain equivalence of fractions in special cases, and compare fractions by reasoning about their size.
MD.M3.NF.A.3.a: Represent two fractions as equivalent (equal) if they are the same size, or the same point on the number line.
MD.M3.NF.A.3.b: Recognize and generate simple equivalent fractions, e.g., `1/2=2/4,4/6=2/3`. Explain why the fractions are equivalent, e.g., by using a visual fraction model.
MD.M3.NF.A.3.c: Express whole numbers as fractions, and recognize fractions that are equivalent to whole numbers.
MD.M3.NF.A.3.d: Compare two fractions with the same numerator or the same denominator by reasoning about their size. Recognize that comparisons are valid only when the two fractions refer to the same whole. Record the results of comparisons with the symbols `>,=,or<`, and justify the conclusions, e.g., by using a visual fraction model.
MD.M3.MD.A: Solve problems involving measurement and estimation of intervals of time, liquid volumes, and masses of objects.
MD.M3.MD.A.1: Tell and write time to the nearest minute and measure time intervals in `text(minutes)`. Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of time intervals in `text(minutes)`, e.g., by representing the problem on a number line diagram.
MD.M3.MD.A.2: Measure and estimate liquid volumes and masses of objects using standard units of grams (g), kilograms kg), and liters (l). Add, subtract, multiply, or divide to solve one-step word problems involving masses or volumes that are given in the same units, e.g., by using drawings (such as a beaker with a measurement scale) to represent the problem.
MD.M3.MD.B.3: Draw a scaled picture graph and a scaled bar graph to represent a data set with several categories. Solve one- and two-step “how many more” and “how may less” problems using information presented in scaled bar graphs.
MD.M3.MD.B.4: Generate measurement data by measuring lengths using rulers marked with `text(halves)andtext(fourths of an inch)`. Show the data by making a line plot where the horizontal scale is marked off in appropriate units - `text(whole numbers),text(halves),ortext(quarters)`.
MD.M3.MD.C: Understand concepts of area and relate area to multiplication and to addition.
MD.M3.MD.C.5: Recognize area as an attribute of plane figures and understand concept of area measurement.
MD.M3.MD.C.5.a: A square with side length`1` `text(unit)`, called “a unit square,” is said to have “one square unit” of area, and can be used to measure area.
MD.M3.MD.C.5.b: A plane figure which can be covered without gaps or overlaps by `n` unit squares is said to have an area of `n` square units.
MD.M3.MD.C.6: Measure areas by counting unit squares (square cm, square m, square in., square ft., and improvised units).
MD.M3.MD.C.7: Relate area to the operations of multiplication and addition.
MD.M3.MD.C.7.a: Find the area of a rectangle with whole-number side lengths by tiling it, and show that the area is the same as would be found by multiplying the side lengths.
MD.M3.MD.C.7.b: Multiply side lengths to find areas of rectangles with whole-number side lengths in the context of solving real-world and mathematical problems, and represent whole-number products as rectangular areas in mathematical reasoning.
MD.M3.MD.C.7.c: Use tiling to show in a concrete case that the area of a rectangle with whole-number side lengths `aandb+c` is the sum of `axxbandaxxc`. Use area models to represent the distributive property in mathematical reasoning.
MD.M3.MD.C.7.d: Recognize area as additive. Find areas of rectilinear figures by decomposing them into non-overlapping rectangles and adding the areas of the non-overlapping parts, applying this technique to solve real-world problems.
MD.M3.MD.D: Recognize perimeter as an attribute of plane figures and distinguish between linear and area measures.
MD.M3.MD.D.8: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving perimeters of polygons, including finding the perimeter given the side lengths, finding an unknown side length, and exhibiting rectangles with the same perimeter and different areas or with the same area and different perimeters.
MD.M3.G.A: Reason with shapes and their attributes.
MD.M3.G.A.1: Understand that shapes in different categories (e.g., rhombuses, rectangles, and others) may share attributes (e.g., having four sides), and that the shared attributes can define a larger category (e.g., quadrilaterals). Recognize rhombuses, rectangles, and squares as examples of quadrilaterals, and draw examples of quadrilaterals that do not belong to any of these subcategories.
MD.M3.G.A.2: Partition shapes into parts with equal areas. Express the area of each part as a unit fraction of the whole.
MD.E4.RL.1: Refer to details and examples in a text when explaining what the text says explicitly and when drawing inferences from the text.
MD.E4.RL.2: Determine a theme of a story, drama, or poem from details in the text; summarize the text.
MD.E4.RL.3: Describe in depth a character, setting, or event in a story or drama, drawing on specific details in the text (e.g., a character's thoughts, words, or actions).
MD.E4.RL.4: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including those that allude to significant characters found in mythology (e.g., Herculean).
MD.E4.RL.5: Explain major differences between poems, drama, and prose, and refer to the structural elements of poems (e.g., verse, rhythm, meter) and drama (e.g., casts of characters, settings, descriptions, dialogue, stage directions) when writing or speaking about a text.
MD.E4.RL.6: Compare and contrast the point of view from which different stories are narrated, including the difference between first- and third-person narrations.
MD.E4.RL.7: Make connections between the text of a story or drama and a visual or oral presentation of the text, identifying where each version reflects specific descriptions and directions in the text.
MD.E4.RL.9: Compare and contrast the treatment of similar themes and topics (e.g., opposition of good and evil) and patterns of events (e.g., the quest) in stories, myths, and traditional literature from different cultures.
MD.E4.RL.10: By the end of the year, read and comprehend literature, including stories, dramas, and poetry, in the grades 4-5 text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.
MD.E4.RI.1: Refer to details and examples in a text when explaining what the text says explicitly and when drawing inferences from the text.
MD.E4.RI.2: Determine the main idea of a text and explain how it is supported by key details; summarize the text.
MD.E4.RI.3: Explain events, procedures, ideas, or concepts in a historical, scientific, or technical text, including what happened and why, based on specific information in the text.
MD.E4.RI.4: Determine the meaning of general academic and domain-specific words or phrases in a text relevant to a grade 4 topic or subject area.
MD.E4.RI.5: Describe the overall structure (e.g., chronology, comparison, cause/effect, problem/solution) of events, ideas, concepts, or information in a text or part of a text.
MD.E4.RI.6: Compare and contrast a firsthand and secondhand account of the same event or topic; describe the differences in focus and the information provided.
MD.E4.Ri.7: Interpret information presented visually, orally, or quantitatively (e.g., in charts, graphs, diagrams, time lines, Web pages) and explain how the information contributes to an understanding of the text in which it appears.
MD.E4.RI.8: Explain how an author uses reasons and evidence to support particular points in a text.
MD.E4.RI.9: Integrate information from two texts on the same topic in order to write or speak about the subject knowledgeably.
MD.E4.RI.10: By the end of year, read and comprehend informational texts, including history/social studies, science, and technical texts, in the grades 4-5 text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.
MD.E4.RF.3: Know and apply grade-level phonics and word analysis skills in decoding words.
MD.E4.RF.3.a: Use combined knowledge of all letter-sound correspondences, syllabication patterns, and morphology (e.g., roots and affixes) to read accurately unfamiliar multisyllabic words in context and out of context.
MD.E4.RF.4: Read with sufficient accuracy and fluency to support comprehension.
MD.E4.RF.4.a: Read grade-level text with purpose and understanding.
MD.E4.RF.4.b: Read grade-level prose and poetry orally with accuracy, appropriate rate, and expression on successive readings.
MD.E4.RF.4.c: Use context to confirm or self-correct word recognition and understanding,rereading as necessary.
MD.E4.W.1: Write opinion pieces on topics or texts, supporting a point of view with reasons and information.
MD.E4.W.1.a: Introduce a topic or text clearly, state an opinion, and create an organizational structure in which related ideas are grouped to support the writer's purpose.
MD.E4.W.1.b: Provide reasons that are supported by facts and details.
MD.E4.W.1.c: Link opinion and reasons using words and phrases(e.g., for instance, in order to, in addition).
MD.E4.W.1.d: Provide a concluding statement or section related to the opinion presented.
MD.E4.W.2: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine a topic and convey ideas and information clearly.
MD.E4.W.2.a: Introduce a topic clearly and group related information in paragraphs and sections; include formatting (e.g., headings), illustrations, and multimedia when useful to aiding comprehension.
MD.E4.W.2.b: Develop the topic with facts, definitions, concrete details, quotations, or other information and examples related to the topic.
MD.E4.W.2.c: Link ideas within categories of information using words and phrases (e.g., another, for example, also, because).
MD.E4.W.2.d: Use precise language and domain-specific vocabulary to inform about or explain the topic.
MD.E4.W.2.e: Provide a concluding statement or section related to the information or explanation presented.
MD.E4.W.3: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, descriptive details, and clear event sequences.
MD.E4.W.3.a: Orient the reader by establishing a situation and introducing a narrator and/or characters; organize an event sequence that unfolds naturally.
MD.E4.W.3.b: Use dialogue and description to develop experiences and events or show the responses of characters to situations.
MD.E4.W.3.c: Use a variety of transitional words and phrases to manage the sequence of events.
MD.E4.W.3.d: Use concrete words and phrases and sensory details to convey experiences and events precisely.
MD.E4.W.3.e: Provide a conclusion that follows from the narrated experiences or events.
MD.E4.W.4: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development and organization are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.
MD.E4.W.5: With guidance and support from peers and adults, develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, and editing.
MD.E4.W.6: With some guidance and support from adults, use technology, including the Internet, to produce and publish writing as well as to interact and collaborate with others; demonstrate sufficient command of keyboarding skills to type a minimum of one page in a single sitting.
MD.E4.W.7: Conduct short research projects that build knowledge through investigation of different aspects of a topic.
MD.E4.W.8: Recall relevant information from experiences or gather relevant information from print and digital sources; take notes and categorize information, and provide a list of sources.
MD.E4.W.9: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.
MD.E4.W.9.a: Apply grade 4 Reading standards to literature (e.g., “Describe in depth a character, setting, or event in a story or drama, drawing on specific details in the text [e.g., a character's thoughts, words, or actions].”).
MD.E4.W.9.b: Apply grade 4 Reading standards to informational texts (e.g., “Explain how an author uses reasons and evidence to support particular points in a text”).
MD.E4.W.10: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of discipline-specific tasks, purposes, and audiences.
MD.E4.SL.1: Engage effectively in a range of collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in groups, and teacher-led) with diverse partners on grade 4 topics and texts, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly.
MD.E4.SL.1.a: Come to discussions prepared, having read or studied required material; explicitly draw on that preparation and other information known about the topic to explore ideas under discussion.
MD.E4.SL.1.b: Follow agreed-upon rules for discussions and carry out assigned roles.
MD.E4.SL.1.c: Pose and respond to specific questions to clarify or follow up on information, and make comments that contribute to the discussion and link to the remarks of others.
MD.E4.SL.1.d: Review the key ideas expressed and explain their own ideas and understanding in light of the discussion.
MD.E4.SL.2: Paraphrase portions of a text read aloud or information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.
MD.E4.SL.3: Identify the reasons and evidence a speaker provides to support particular points.
MD.E4.SL.4: Report on a topic or text, tell a story, or recount an experience in an organized manner, using appropriate facts and relevant, descriptive details to support main ideas or themes; speak clearly at an understandable pace.
MD.E4.SL.5: Add audio recordings and visual displays to presentations when appropriate to enhance the development of main ideas or themes.
MD.E4.SL.6: Differentiate between contexts that call for formal English (e.g., presenting ideas) and situations where informal discourse is appropriate (e.g., small-group discussion); use formal English when appropriate to task and situation.
MD.E4.L.1: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.
