MS.M9-12.G.G-CO.1: Know precise definitions of angle, circle, perpendicular line, parallel line, and line segment, based on the undefined notions of point, line, distance along a line, and distance around a circular arc.
MS.M9-12.G.G-CO.2: Represent transformations in the plane using, e.g., transparencies and geometry software; describe transformations as functions that take points in the plane as inputs and give other points as outputs. Compare transformations that preserve distance and angle to those that do not (e.g., translation versus horizontal stretch).
MS.M9-12.G.G-CO.3: Given a rectangle, parallelogram, trapezoid, or regular polygon, describe the rotations and reflections that carry it onto itself.
MS.M9-12.G.G-CO.4: Develop definitions of rotations, reflections, and translations in terms of angles, circles, perpendicular lines, parallel lines, and line segments.
MS.M9-12.G.G-CO.5: Given a geometric figure and a rotation, reflection, or translation, draw the transformed figure using, e.g., graph paper, tracing paper, or geometry software. Specify a sequence of transformations that will carry a given figure onto another.
MS.M9-12.G.G-CO.6: Use geometric descriptions of rigid motions to transform figures and to predict the effect of a given rigid motion on a given figure; given two figures, use the definition of congruence in terms of rigid motions to decide if they are congruent.
MS.M9-12.G.G-CO.7: Use the definition of congruence in terms of rigid motions to show that two triangles are congruent if and only if corresponding pairs of sides and corresponding pairs of angles are congruent.
MS.M9-12.G.G-CO.8: Explain how the criteria for triangle congruence (ASA, SAS, and SSS) follow from the definition of congruence in terms of rigid motions.
MS.M9-12.G.G-CO.9: Prove theorems about lines and angles.
MS.M9-12.G.G-CO.12: Make formal geometric constructions with a variety of tools and methods (compass and straightedge, string, reflective devices, paper folding, dynamic geometric software, etc.).
MS.M9-12.G.G-CO.13: Construct an equilateral triangle, a square, and a regular hexagon inscribed in a circle.
MS.M9-12.G.G-SRT.1: Verify experimentally the properties of dilations given by a center and a scale factor:
MS.M9-12.G.G-SRT.1.a: A dilation takes a line not passing through the center of the dilation to a parallel line, and leaves a line passing through the center unchanged.
MS.M9-12.G.G-SRT.1.b: The dilation of a line segment is longer or shorter in the ratio given by the scale factor.
MS.M9-12.G.G-SRT.2: Given two figures, use the definition of similarity in terms of similarity transformations to decide if they are similar; explain using similarity transformations the meaning of similarity for triangles as the equality of all corresponding pairs of angles and the proportionality of all corresponding pairs of sides.
MS.M9-12.G.G-SRT.3: Use the properties of similarity transformations to establish the AA criterion for two triangles to be similar.
MS.M9-12.G.G-SRT.5: Use congruence and similarity criteria for triangles to solve problems and to prove relationships in geometric figures.
MS.M9-12.G.G-SRT.6: Understand that by similarity, side ratios in right triangles are properties of the angles in the triangle, leading to definitions of trigonometric ratios for acute angles.
MS.M9-12.G.G-SRT.7: Explain and use the relationship between the sine and cosine of complementary angles.
MS.M9-12.G.G-SRT.8: Use trigonometric ratios and the Pythagorean Theorem to solve right triangles in applied problems.
MS.M9-12.G.G-C.1: Prove that all circles are similar.
MS.M9-12.G.G-C.2: Identify and describe relationships among inscribed angles, radii, and chords.
MS.M9-12.G.G-C.3: Construct the inscribed and circumscribed circles of a triangle, and prove properties of angles for a quadrilateral inscribed in a circle.
MS.M9-12.G.G-C.5: Derive using similarity the fact that the length of the arc intercepted by an angle is proportional to the radius, and define the radian measure of the angle as the constant of proportionality; derive the formula for the area of a sector.
MS.M9-12.G.G-GPE.1: Derive the equation of a circle of given center and radius using the Pythagorean Theorem; complete the square to find the center and radius of a circle given by an equation.
MS.M9-12.G.G-GPE.4: Use coordinates to prove simple geometric theorems algebraically.
MS.M9-12.G.G-GPE.5: Prove the slope criteria for parallel and perpendicular lines and use them to solve geometric problems (e.g., find the equation of a line parallel or perpendicular to a given line that passes through a given point).
MS.M9-12.G.G-GPE.6: Find the point on a directed line segment between two given points that partitions the segment in a given ratio.
MS.M9-12.G.G-GPE.7: Use coordinates to compute perimeters of polygons and areas of triangles and rectangles, e.g., using the distance formula.
MS.M9-12.G.G-GMD.1: Give an informal argument for the formulas for the circumference of a circle, area of a circle, volume of a cylinder, pyramid, and cone.
MS.M9-12.G.G-GMD.3: Use volume formulas for cylinders, pyramids, cones, and spheres to solve problems.*
MS.M9-12.G.G-GMD.4: Identify the shapes of two-dimensional cross-sections of three-dimensional objects, and identify three-dimensional objects generated by rotations of two-dimensional objects.
MS.M9-12.G.G-MG.1: Use geometric shapes, their measures, and their properties to describe objects (e.g., modeling a tree trunk or a human torso as a cylinder).
MS.M9-12.G.G-MG.2: Apply concepts of density based on area and volume in modeling situations (e.g., `text(persons per square mile),text(BTUs per cubic foot)`).
MS.M9-12.G.G-MG.3: Apply geometric methods to solve design problems (e.g., designing an object or structure to satisfy physical constraints or minimize cost; working with typographic grid systems based on ratios).

NC.M4.NF.1: Explain why a fraction is equivalent to another fraction by using area and length fraction models, with attention to how the number and size of the parts differ even though the two fractions themselves are the same size.

NC.E6.W.1: Write arguments to support claims with clear reasons and relevant evidence.

NC.E6.W.1.b: Introduce claim(s) and organize the reasons and evidence clearly.

NC.E6.W.1.d: Use words, phrases, and clauses to clarify the relationships among claim(s) and reasons.
NC.E6.W.1.e: Establish and maintain a formal style.
NC.E6.W.1.f: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from the argument presented.
NC.E6.W.1.g: With some guidance and support from peers and adults, develop and strengthen writing as needed by revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach, with consideration to task, purpose, and audience.
NC.E6.W.2: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine a topic and convey ideas, concepts, and information through the selection, organization, and analysis of relevant content.

NC.E6.W.2.c: Develop the topic with relevant facts, definitions, concrete details, quotations, or other information and examples.
NC.E6.W.2.d: Use appropriate transitions to clarify the relationships among ideas and concepts.
NC.E6.W.2.e: Use precise language and domain-specific vocabulary to inform about or explain the topic.
NC.E6.W.2.f: Establish and maintain a formal style.
NC.E6.W.2.g: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from the information or explanation presented.
NC.E6.W.2.h: With some guidance and support from peers and adults, develop and strengthen writing as needed by revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach, with consideration to task, purpose, and audience.

NC.E6.W.3.a: Organize information and ideas around a topic to plan and prepare to write.
NC.E6.W.3.b: Engage and orient the reader by establishing a context and introducing a narrator and/or characters; organize an event sequence that unfolds naturally and logically.
NC.E6.W.3.c: Use narrative techniques, such as dialogue, pacing, and description, to develop experiences, events, and/or characters.
NC.E6.W.3.d: Use a variety of transition words, phrases, and clauses to convey sequence and signal shifts from one time frame or setting to another.
NC.E6.W.3.e: Use precise words and phrases, relevant descriptive details, and sensory language to convey experiences and events.
NC.E6.W.3.f: Provide a conclusion that follows from the narrated experiences or events.
NC.E6.W.3.g: With some guidance and support from peers and adults, develop and strengthen writing as needed by revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach, with consideration to task, purpose, and audience.

NC.E6.W.5: Conduct short research projects to answer a question, drawing on several sources and refocusing the investigation when appropriate.
NC.E6.W.6: Gather relevant information from multiple print and digital sources; assess the credibility of each source; and quote or paraphrase the data and conclusions of others while avoiding plagiarism and providing basic bibliographic information for sources.
NC.E6.SL.1: Engage effectively in a range of collaborative discussions (one on one, in groups, and teacher-led) with diverse partners on grade 6 topics, texts, and issues, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly.

NC.E6.SL.1.b: Follow rules for collegial discussions, set specific goals and deadlines, and define individual roles as needed.
NC.E6.SL.1.c: Pose and respond to specific questions with elaboration and detail by making comments that contribute to the topic, text, or issue under discussion.
NC.E6.SL.1.d: Review the key ideas expressed and demonstrate understanding of multiple perspectives through reflection and paraphrasing.
NC.E6.SL.2: Interpret information presented in diverse media and formats and explain how it contributes to a topic, text, or issue under study.
NC.E6.SL.3: Delineate a speaker's argument and specific claims, distinguishing claims that are supported by reasons and evidence from claims that are not.
NC.E6.SL.4: Present claims and findings, sequencing ideas logically and using pertinent descriptions, facts, and details to accentuate main ideas or themes; adapt speech to a variety of contexts and tasks.
NC.E6.SL.5: Include multimedia components and visual displays in presentations to clarify information.
NC.E6.L.1: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking; demonstrate proficiency within the 6-8 grammar continuum.
NC.E6.L.2: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing; demonstrate proficiency within the 6-8 conventions continuum.
NC.E6.L.3: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening.
NC.E6.L.3.a: Vary sentence patterns for meaning, reader/listener interest, and style.
NC.E6.L.3.b: Maintain consistency in style and tone.
NC.E6.L.4: Determine and/or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grade 6 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies: context clues, word parts, word relationships, and reference materials.
NC.E6.L.5: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language and nuances in word meanings.
NC.E6.L.5.a: Interpret figures of speech in context based on grade 6 reading and content.
NC.E6.L.5.b: Distinguish among the connotations of words with similar denotations.

NC.M6.RP.1: Understand the concept of a ratio and use ratio language.
NC.M6.RP.1.a: Describe a ratio as a multiplicative relationship between two quantities.
NC.M6.RP.1.b: Model a ratio relationship using a variety of representations.
NC.M6.RP.2: Understand that ratios can be expressed as equivalent unit ratios by finding and interpreting both unit ratios in context.
NC.M6.RP.3: Use ratio reasoning with equivalent whole-number ratios to solve real-world and mathematical problems.
NC.M6.RP.3.a: Creating and using a table to compare ratios.
NC.M6.RP.3.b: Finding missing values in the tables.
NC.M6.RP.3.d: Converting and manipulating measurements using given ratios.
NC.M6.RP.3.e: Plotting the pairs of values on the coordinate plane.
NC.M6.RP.4: Use ratio reasoning to solve real-world and mathematical problems with percents.
NC.M6.RP.4.a: Understanding and finding a percent of a quantity as a ratio per `100`.
NC.M6.RP.4.b: Using equivalent ratios, such as benchmark percents (50%, 25%, 10%, 5%, 1%), to determine a part of any given quantity.
NC.M6.RP.4.c: Finding the whole, given a part and the percent.
NC.M6.NS.1: Use visual models and common denominators.
NC.M6.NS.1.a: Interpret and compute quotients of fractions.
NC.M6.NS.1.b: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving division of fractions.
NC.M6.NS.2: Fluently divide using long division with a minimum of a four-digit dividend and interpret the quotient and remainder in context.
NC.M6.NS.3: Apply and extend previous understandings of decimals to develop and fluently use the standard algorithms for addition, subtraction, multiplication and division of decimals.
NC.M6.NS.4: Understand and use prime factorization and the relationships between factors to:
NC.M6.NS.4.a: Find the unique prime factorization for a whole number.
NC.M6.NS.4.b: Find the greatest common factor of two whole numbers less than or equal to 100.
NC.M6.NS.4.c: Use the greatest common factor and the distributive property to rewrite the sum of two whole numbers, each less than or equal to 100.
NC.M6.NS.4.d: Find the least common multiple of two whole numbers less than or equal to 12 to add and subtract fractions with unlike denominators.
NC.M6.NS.5: Understand and use rational numbers to:
NC.M6.NS.5.a: Describe quantities having opposite directions or values.
NC.M6.NS.5.b: Represent quantities in real-world contexts, explaining the meaning of `0` in each situation.
NC.M6.NS.5.c: Understand the absolute value of a rational number as its distance from `0` on the number line to:
NC.M6.NS.6: Understand rational numbers as points on the number line and as ordered pairs on a coordinate plane.
NC.M6.NS.7.a: Interpret statements of inequality as statements about the relative position of two numbers on a number line diagram.
NC.M6.NS.7.b: Write, interpret, and explain statements of order for rational numbers in real-world contexts.
NC.M6.NS.8: Solve real-world and mathematical problems by graphing points in all four quadrants of the coordinate plane. Include use of coordinates and absolute value to find distances between points with the same first coordinate or the same second coordinate.
NC.M6.NS.9: Apply and extend previous understandings of addition and subtraction.
NC.M6.NS.9.a: Describe situations in which opposite quantities combine to make `0`.
NC.M6.NS.9.b: Understand 𝑝 + 𝑞 as the number located a distance q from p, in the positive or negative direction depending on the sign of q. Show that a number and its additive inverse create a zero pair.
NC.M6.NS.9.c: Understand subtraction of integers as adding the additive inverse, 𝑝 - 𝑞 = 𝑝 + (- 𝑞). Show that the distance between two integers on the number line is the absolute value of their difference.
NC.M6.NS.9.d: Use models to add and subtract integers from -20 to 20 and describe real-world contexts using sums and differences.
NC.M6.EE.1: Write and evaluate numerical expressions, with and without grouping symbols, involving whole-number exponents.
NC.M6.EE.2: Write, read, and evaluate algebraic expressions.
NC.M6.EE.2.a: Write expressions that record operations with numbers and with letters standing for numbers.
NC.M6.EE.2.b: Identify parts of an expression using mathematical terms and view one or more of those parts as a single entity.
NC.M6.EE.2.c: Evaluate expressions at specific values of their variables using expressions that arise from formulas used in real-world problems.
NC.M6.EE.3: Apply the properties of operations to generate equivalent expressions without exponents.
NC.M6.EE.4: Identify when two expressions are equivalent and justify with mathematical reasoning.
NC.M6.EE.5: Use substitution to determine whether a given number in a specified set makes an equation true.
NC.M6.EE.6: Use variables to represent numbers and write expressions when solving a real-world or mathematical problem.
NC.M6.EE.7: Solve real-world and mathematical problems by writing and solving equations.
NC.M6.EE.7.a: Writing and solving equations of the form x + 𝑝 = 𝑞 in which 𝑝, 𝑞 and x are all nonnegative rational numbers; and,
NC.M6.EE.7.b: Writing and solving equations of the form 𝑝 ∙ x = 𝑞 for cases in which 𝑝, 𝑞 and x are all nonnegative rational numbers.
NC.M6.EE.8.a: Using substitution to determine whether a given number in a specified set makes an inequality true.
NC.M6.EE.8.b: Writing an inequality of the form x > 𝑐 or x < 𝑐 to represent a constraint or condition in a real-world or mathematical problem.
NC.M6.EE.8.c: Recognizing that inequalities of the form x > 𝑐 or x < 𝑐 have infinitely many solutions.
NC.M6.EE.8.d: Representing solutions of inequalities on number line diagrams.
NC.M6.EE.9.a: Using variables to represent two quantities in a real-world or mathematical context that change in relationship to one another.
NC.M6.EE.9.b: Analyze the relationship between quantities in different representations (context, equations, tables, and graphs).
NC.M6.G.1: Create geometric models to solve real-world and mathematical problems.
NC.M6.G.1.a: Find the area of triangles by composing into rectangles and decomposing into right triangles.
NC.M6.G.1.b: Find the area of special quadrilaterals and polygons by decomposing into triangles or rectangles.
NC.M6.G.2: Apply and extend previous understandings of the volume of a right rectangular prism to find the volume of right rectangular prisms with fractional edge lengths. Apply this understanding to the context of solving real-world and mathematical problems.
NC.M6.G.3: Use the coordinate plane to solve real-world and mathematical problems.
NC.M6.G.3.a: Drawing polygons in the coordinate plane given coordinates for the vertices.
NC.M6.G.3.b: Using coordinates to find the length of a side joining points with the same first coordinate or the same second coordinate.
NC.M6.G.4: Represent right prisms and right pyramids using nets made up of rectangles and triangles, and use the nets to find the surface area of these figures. Apply these techniques in the context of solving real-world and mathematical problems.
NC.M6.SP.1: Recognize a statistical question as one that anticipates variability in the data related to the question and accounts for it in the answers.
NC.M6.SP.2: Understand that a set of data collected to answer a statistical question has a distribution which can be described by its center, spread, and overall shape.
NC.M6.SP.3: Understand that both a measure of center and a description of variability should be considered when describing a numerical data set.
NC.M6.SP.3.a: Determine the measure of center of a data set and understand that it is a single number that summarizes all the values of that data set.
NC.M6.SP.3.b: Understand that describing the variability of a data set is needed to distinguish between data sets in the same scale, by comparing graphical representations of different data sets in the same scale that have similar measures of center, but different spreads.
NC.M6.SP.4: Display numerical data in plots on a number line.
NC.M6.SP.4.a: Use dot plots, histograms, and box plots to represent data.
NC.M6.SP.4.b: Compare the attributes of different representations of the same data.
NC.M6.SP.5: Summarize numerical data sets in relation to their context.
NC.E7.RL.1: Cite several pieces of textual evidence to support analysis of what the text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text.

NC.M7.RP.1: Compute unit rates associated with ratios of fractions to solve real-world and mathematical problems.
NC.M7.RP.2: Recognize and represent proportional relationships between quantities.
NC.M7.RP.2.a: Understand that a proportion is a relationship of equality between ratios.
NC.M7.RP.2.b: Identify the unit rate (constant of proportionality) within two quantities in a proportional relationship using tables, graphs, equations, and verbal descriptions.
NC.M7.RP.2.c: Create equations and graphs to represent proportional relationships.
NC.M7.RP.2.d: Use a graphical representation of a proportional relationship in context to:
NC.M7.RP.3: Use scale factors and unit rates in proportional relationships to solve ratio and percent problems.
NC.M7.NS.1: Apply and extend previous understandings of addition and subtraction to add and subtract rational numbers, using the properties of operations, and describing real-world contexts using sums and differences.
NC.M7.NS.2: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication and division.
NC.M7.NS.2.a: Understand that a rational number is any number that can be written as a quotient of integers with a non-zero divisor.
NC.M7.NS.2.b: Apply properties of operations as strategies, including the standard algorithms, to multiply and divide rational numbers and describe the product and quotient in real-world contexts.
NC.M7.NS.2.c: Use division and previous understandings of fractions and decimals.
NC.M7.NS.3: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving numerical expressions with rational numbers using the four operations.
NC.M7.EE.1: Apply properties of operations as strategies to:
NC.M7.EE.1.a: Add, subtract, and expand linear expressions with rational coefficients.
NC.M7.EE.1.b: Factor linear expression with an integer GCF.
NC.M7.EE.2: Understand that equivalent expressions can reveal real-world and mathematical relationships. Interpret the meaning of the parts of each expression in context.
NC.M7.EE.3: Solve multi-step real-world and mathematical problems posed with rational numbers in algebraic expressions.
NC.M7.EE.3.a: Apply properties of operations to calculate with positive and negative numbers in any form.
NC.M7.EE.3.b: Convert between different forms of a number and equivalent forms of the expression as appropriate.
NC.M7.EE.4: Use variables to represent quantities to solve real-world or mathematical problems.
NC.M7.EE.4.a: Construct equations to solve problems by reasoning about the quantities.
NC.M7.EE.4.b: Construct inequalities to solve problems by reasoning about the quantities.
NC.M7.G.1: Solve problems involving scale drawings of geometric figures.
NC.M7.G.1.a: Building an understanding that angle measures remain the same and side lengths are proportional.
NC.M7.G.1.b: Using a scale factor to compute actual lengths and areas from a scale drawing.
NC.M7.G.2: Understand the characteristics of angles and side lengths that create a unique triangle, more than one triangle or no triangle. Build triangles from three measures of angles and/or sides.
NC.M7.G.4: Understand area and circumference of a circle.
NC.M7.G.4.a: Understand the relationships between the radius, diameter, circumference, and area.
NC.M7.G.4.b: Apply the formulas for area and circumference of a circle to solve problems.
NC.M7.G.5: Use facts about supplementary, complementary, vertical, and adjacent angles in a multi-step problem to write and solve equations for an unknown angle in a figure.
NC.M7.G.6.a: Area and perimeter of two-dimensional objects composed of triangles, quadrilaterals, and polygons.
NC.M7.G.6.b: Volume and surface area of pyramids, prisms, or three-dimensional objects composed of cubes, pyramids, and right prisms.
NC.M7.SP.1: Understand that statistics can be used to gain information about a population by:
NC.M7.SP.1.a: Recognizing that generalizations about a population from a sample are valid only if the sample is representative of that population.
NC.M7.SP.1.b: Using random sampling to produce representative samples to support valid inferences.
NC.M7.SP.2: Generate multiple random samples (or simulated samples) of the same size to gauge the variation in estimates or predictions, and use this data to draw inferences about a population with an unknown characteristic of interest.
NC.M7.SP.3: Recognize the role of variability when comparing two populations.
NC.M7.SP.3.a: Calculate the measure of variability of a data set and understand that it describes how the values of the data set vary with a single number.
NC.M7.SP.3.b: Informally assess the difference between two data sets by examining the overlap and separation between the graphical representations of two data sets.
NC.M7.SP.4: Use measures of center and measures of variability for numerical data from random samples to draw comparative inferences about two populations.
NC.M7.SP.5: Understand that the probability of a chance event is a number between `0and1 that expresses the likelihood of the event occurring.
NC.M7.SP.6: Collect data to calculate the experimental probability of a chance event, observing its long-run relative frequency. Use this experimental probability to predict the approximate relative frequency.

NC.M7.SP.7.a: Develop a uniform probability model by assigning equal probability to all outcomes, and use the model to determine probabilities of events.
NC.M7.SP.7.b: Develop a probability model (which may not be uniform) by repeatedly performing a chance process and observing frequencies in the data generated.

NC.E11-12.RI.3: Analyze a complex set of ideas or sequence of events and explain how specific individuals, ideas, or events interact and develop over the course of the text.
NC.E11-12.RI.4: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text; analyze how an author uses and refines the meaning of a key term or terms over the course of a text.
NC.E11-12.RI.5: Analyze and evaluate the effectiveness of the structure an author uses in his or her exposition or argument, including whether the structure makes points clear, convincing, and engaging.
NC.E11-12.RI.6: Determine an author's point of view or purpose in a text in which the rhetoric is particularly effective, analyzing how style and content contribute to the power, and/or persuasiveness of the text.
NC.E11-12.RI.7: Integrate and evaluate multiple sources of information presented in different media or formats, including visually and quantitatively, as well as in words in order to address a question or solve a problem.
NC.E11-12.RI.8: Delineate and evaluate the reasoning in influential U.S. and/or British texts, including the premises, purposes, and arguments in works of public advocacy.
NC.E11-12.RI.9: Analyze foundational U.S. and/or British documents of historical and literary significance for their themes, purposes, and rhetorical features.
NC.E11-12.RI.10: By the end of grade 11, read and understand informational texts within the 11-12 text complexity band proficiently and independently for sustained periods of time. Connect prior knowledge and experiences to text. By the end of grade 12, read and understand informational texts at the high end of the 11-12 text complexity band proficiently and independently for sustained periods of time. Connect prior knowledge and experiences to text.
NC.E11-12.W.1: Write arguments to support claims in an analysis of substantive topics or texts, using valid reasoning and relevant and sufficient evidence.
NC.E11-12.W.1.a: Organize information and ideas around a topic to plan and prepare to write.
NC.E11-12.W.1.b: Introduce precise, knowledgeable claim(s), establish the significance of the claim(s), distinguish the claim(s) from alternate or opposing claims, and create an organization that logically sequences claim(s), counterclaims, reasons, and evidence.
NC.E11-12.W.1.c: Develop claim(s) and counterclaims fairly and thoroughly, supplying the most relevant evidence for each while pointing out the strengths and limitations of both in a manner that anticipates the audience's knowledge level, concerns, values, and possible biases.
NC.E11-12.W.1.d: Use words, phrases, and clauses as well as varied syntax to link the major sections of the text, create cohesion, and clarify the relationships between claim(s) and reasons, between reasons and evidence, and between claim(s) and counterclaims.
NC.E11-12.W.1.e: Establish and maintain a formal style and objective tone while attending to the norms and conventions of the discipline in which they are writing.
NC.E11-12.W.1.f: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the argument presented.
NC.E11-12.W.1.g: Develop and strengthen writing as needed by revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach, focusing on addressing what is most significant for a specific purpose and audience.
NC.E11-12.W.2: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine and convey complex ideas, concepts, and information clearly and accurately through the effective selection, organization, and analysis of content.
NC.E11-12.W.2.a: Organize information and ideas around a topic to plan and prepare to write.
NC.E11-12.W.2.b: Introduce a topic; organize complex ideas, concepts, and information so that each new element builds on that which precedes it to create a unified whole; include formatting, graphics, and multimedia when useful to aiding comprehension.
NC.E11-12.W.2.c: Develop the topic thoroughly by selecting the most significant and relevant facts, extended definitions, concrete details, quotations, or other information and examples appropriate to the audience's knowledge of the topic.
NC.E11-12.W.2.d: Use appropriate and varied transitions and syntax to link the major sections of the text, create cohesion, and clarify the relationships among complex ideas and concepts.
NC.E11-12.W.2.e: Use precise language, domain-specific vocabulary, and techniques such as metaphor, simile, and analogy to manage the complexity of the topic.
NC.E11-12.W.2.f: Establish and maintain a formal style and objective tone while attending to the norms and conventions of the discipline in which they are writing.
NC.E11-12.W.2.g: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the information or explanation presented.
NC.E11-12.W.2.h: Develop and strengthen writing as needed by revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach, focusing on addressing what is most significant for a specific purpose and audience.
NC.E11-12.W.3: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, well-chosen details, and well-structured event sequences.
NC.E11-12.W.3.a: Organize information and ideas around a topic to plan and prepare to write.
NC.E11-12.W.3.b: Engage and orient the reader by setting out a problem, situation, or observation and its significance, establishing one or multiple point(s) of view, and introducing a narrator and/or characters; create a smooth progression of experiences or events.
NC.E11-12.W.3.c: Use narrative techniques, such as dialogue, pacing, description, reflection, and multiple plot lines, to develop experiences, events, and/or characters.
NC.E11-12.W.3.d: Use a variety of techniques to sequence events so that they build on one another to create a coherent whole and build toward a particular tone and outcome.
NC.E11-12.W.3.e: Use precise words and phrases, telling details, and sensory language to convey a vivid picture of the experiences, events, setting, and/or characters.
NC.E11-12.W.3.f: Provide a conclusion that follows from and reflects on what is experienced, observed, or resolved over the course of the narrative.
NC.E11-12.W.3.g: Develop and strengthen writing as needed by revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach, focusing on addressing what is most significant for a specific purpose and audience.
NC.E11-12.W.4: Develop and strengthen writing as needed by revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach, focusing on addressing what is most significant for a specific purpose and audience.
NC.E11-12.W.5: Conduct short as well as more sustained research projects to answer a question (including a self-generated question) or solve a problem; narrow or broaden the inquiry when appropriate; synthesize multiple sources on the subject, demonstrating understanding of the subject under investigation.
NC.E11-12.W.6: Gather relevant information from multiple authoritative print and digital sources, using advanced searches effectively; assess the strengths and limitations of each source in terms of the task, purpose, and audience; integrate information into the text selectively to maintain the flow of ideas, avoiding plagiarism and overreliance on any one source and following a standard format for citation.
NC.E11-12.SL.1: Initiate and participate effectively in a range of collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in groups, and teacher-led) with diverse partners on grades 11-12 topics, texts, and issues, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly and persuasively.
NC.E11-12.SL.1.a: Come to discussions prepared, having read and researched material under study; explicitly draw on that preparation by referring to evidence from texts and other research on the topic or issue to stimulate a thoughtful, well-reasoned exchange of ideas.
NC.E11-12.SL.1.b: Work with peers to promote civil, democratic discussions and decision-making, set clear goals and deadlines, and establish individual roles as needed.
NC.E11-12.SL.1.c: Propel conversations by posing and responding to questions that probe reasoning and evidence; ensure a hearing for a full range of positions on a topic or issue; clarify, verify, or challenge ideas and conclusions; and promote divergent and creative perspectives.
NC.E11-12.SL.1.d: Respond thoughtfully to diverse perspectives; synthesize comments, claims, and evidence made on all sides of an issue; resolve contradictions when possible; and determine what additional information or research is required to deepen the investigation or complete the task.
NC.E11-12.SL.2: Integrate multiple sources of information presented in diverse formats and media in order to make informed decisions and solve problems, evaluating the credibility and accuracy of each source and noting any discrepancies among the data.
NC.E11-12.SL.3: Evaluate a speaker's point of view, reasoning, and use of evidence and rhetoric, assessing the stance, premises, links among ideas, word choice, points of emphasis, and tone used.
NC.E11-12.SL.4: Present information, findings, and supporting evidence, conveying a clear and distinct perspective, such that listeners can follow the line of reasoning, alternative or opposing perspectives are addressed, and the organization, development, substance, and style are appropriate to purpose, audience, and a range of formal and informal tasks.
NC.E11-12.SL.5: Make strategic use of digital media in presentations to enhance understanding of findings, reasoning, and evidence and to add interest.
NC.E11-12.L.1: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking; demonstrate proficiency within the 9-12 grammar continuum.
NC.E11-12.L.2: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing; demonstrate proficiency within the 9-12 conventions continuum.
NC.E11-12.L.3: Apply knowledge of language to understand how language functions in different contexts, to make effective choices for meaning or style, and to comprehend more fully when reading or listening.
NC.E11-12.L.3.a: Vary syntax for effect, consulting references for guidance as needed; apply an understanding of syntax to the study of complex texts when reading.
NC.E11-12.L.4: Determine and/or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grades 11-12 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies: context clues, word parts, word relationships, and reference materials.
NC.E11-12.L.5: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language and nuances in word meanings.
NC.E11-12.L.5.a: Interpret figures of speech in context and analyze their role in the text based on grades 11-12 reading and content.
NC.E11-12.L.5.b: Analyze nuances in the meaning of words with similar denotations.
NC.E11-12.L.6: Acquire and use accurately general academic and domain-specific words and phrases, sufficient for reading, writing, speaking, and listening at the college and career readiness level; demonstrate independence in developing vocabulary knowledge when considering a word or phrase important to comprehension or expression.
NE.EK.F.1: Demonstrate knowledge of the organization and basic concepts of print.
NE.EK.F.1.a: Identify all upper and lowercase letters of the alphabet in isolation and in connected text.
NE.EK.F.1.b: Recognize that spoken words are represented in written language by specific sequences of letters, and that print carries meaning.
NE.EK.F.1.c: Demonstrate understanding that words are separated by spaces in print; demonstrate understanding of one-to- one correspondence between voice and print.
NE.EK.F.1.d: Demonstrate knowledge that print reads from left to right, top to bottom, and page by page.
NE.EK.F.2: Demonstrate understanding of spoken words, syllables, and sounds (phonemes).
NE.EK.F.2.a: Segment and count spoken sentences into words.
NE.EK.F.2.b: Recognize and begin to produce oral rhymes.
NE.EK.F.2.c: Count, produce, and segment spoken words into syllables and identify syllable parts.
NE.EK.F.2.d: Blend onsets and rimes to form simple words (e.g., v-an, gr-ab).
NE.EK.F.2.e: Delete part of a syllable within a spoken word including compound words (e.g., “Say 'parsnip.' Say it again but don't say 'par;' e.g., “Say 'cowboy.' Say it again but don't say 'cow'”).
NE.EK.F.2.f: Isolate and pronounce the initial, medial vowel, and final sounds (phonemes) in two- and three-phoneme (VC or CVC) words, excluding CVC words ending with /l/, /r/, or /x/.
NE.EK.F.3: Know and apply phonics and word analysis skills in decoding and encoding (spelling) words.
NE.EK.F.3.a: Demonstrate basic knowledge of one-to-one sound to letter correspondences by producing the primary or many of the most frequent sounds for each consonant.
NE.EK.F.3.b: Demonstrate the long and short sounds with common spellings (graphemes) for the five major vowels.
NE.EK.F.3.e: Distinguish between similarly spelled words by identifying the sounds of the letters that differ.
NE.EK.F.4: Develop accuracy, phrasing, and expression/prosody while reading a variety of grade-level texts to support comprehension.
NE.EK.F.4.a: Recognize upper and lowercase letters automatically and accurately.
NE.EK.F.4.b: Read decodable consonant-vowel-consonant (CVC) words with automaticity and accuracy.
NE.EK.F.4.c: Read grade level high-frequency words with automaticity and accuracy (e.g. Fry or Dolch words or those included in instructional materials).
NE.EK.RP.1: With prompting and support, orally retell familiar stories, including key details, and demonstrate understanding of their central message or lesson.
NE.EK.RP.2: With prompting and support, identify main character(s), setting, and important events in a literary text.
NE.EK.RP.3: With prompting and support, define the role of author and illustrator in a literary text.
NE.EK.RP.4: With prompting and support, identify the basic characteristics of literary text.
NE.EK.RP.5: With prompting and support, compare and contrast the experiences of characters in familiar stories.
NE.EK.RP.6: With prompting and support, ask and answer questions about key details in a literary text.
NE.EK.RP.7: With prompting and support, make connections between own experiences and other cultures in literary texts.
NE.EK.RP.8: Actively engage in group reading activities with purpose and understanding.
NE.EK.RI.1: With prompting and support, identify the main topic and key details in an informational text.
NE.EK.RI.2: With prompting and support, identify key individuals, events, or pieces of information in an informational text.
NE.EK.RI.3: With prompting and support, define the role of author and illustrator in presenting the ideas or information in a text.
NE.EK.RI.4: With prompting and support, use text features (titles, headings, visuals) to predict or confirm the topic of a text.
NE.EK.RI.5: With prompting and support, identify basic similarities and differences between two informational texts on the same topic.
NE.EK.RI.6: With prompting and support, explain the difference between facts and opinions about a topic.
NE.EK.RI.7: With prompting and support, make connections between own experiences and other cultures in informational texts.
NE.EK.RI.8: Actively engage in group reading activities with purpose and understanding.
NE.EK.V.1: Recognize and use conversational and grade-level academic vocabulary.
NE.EK.V.1.a: With prompting and support, identify new meanings of familiar words (e.g., park, ring, fly).
NE.EK.V.1.b: With prompting and support, use commonly occurring inflections and affixes to determine the meaning of unknown words.
NE.EK.V.1.c: With prompting and support, determine the meanings of key words and phrases using provided reference materials and classroom resources.
NE.EK.V.2: Interpret an author's use of figurative, connotative, and technical language in grade-level literary and informational text.
NE.EK.V.2.a: With prompting and support, sort common words and phrases into conceptual categories to develop an understanding of word relationships.
NE.EK.V.2.b: With prompting and support, deepen understanding of words by identifying and relating them to their opposites.
NE.EK.V.2.c: With prompting and support, ask and answer questions about key words and phrases to determine their meaning.
NE.EK.V.2.d: With prompting and support, identify and explain descriptive words and phrases that suggest feelings or appeal to the senses.
NE.EK.FW: Foundations of Writing | Apply handwriting skills to communicate ideas and information.
NE.EK.FW.1.a: Identify and match upper and lowercase manuscript letters.
NE.EK.FW.1.b: Print many upper and lowercase manuscript letters using reference materials and classroom resources.
NE.EK.FW.1.c: Write left to right and use appropriate spacing between letters and words.
NE.EK.FW.2.a: Segment phonemes orally in single-syllable words.
NE.EK.FW.2.b: Demonstrate understanding that syllables are organized around vowel sounds.
NE.EK.W: Production of Writing | Use a recursive writing process to produce clear and coherent writing appropriate to the discipline, audience, and/or context.
NE.EK.W.1: With prompting and support, form and use complete simple sentences in shared language activities.
NE.EK.W.1.a: Capitalize the first word in a sentence and the pronoun I.
NE.EK.W.1.c: Identify nouns (e.g., singular and plural) and simple verbs (e.g., action).
NE.EK.W.1.d: Form regular plural nouns by adding /s/ or /es/.
NE.EK.W.1.f: Use subject-verb agreement in simple sentences.
NE.EK.W.2: With prompting and support, use a recursive writing process to develop, strengthen, and produce writing appropriate to the discipline, audience, and/or context.
NE.EK.W.2.a: Use prewriting activities and resources to generate ideas.
NE.EK.W.2.b: Adapt writing processes to sustain engagement in short and long-term writing tasks of increasing length and complexity.
NE.EK.W.2.c: Use feedback from others to improve writing and/or add details.
NE.EK.W.2.d: Use or decipher multiple formats of print and digital text (e.g., manuscript, font, graphics, symbols).
NE.EK.W.2.e: Use appropriate digital/multimedia tools to produce, enhance, and/or publish writing individually or with peers.
NE.EK.W.3: With prompting and support, narrate personal or fictional events in a sequential order using a combination of drawing, dictating, and/or writing.
NE.EK.W.4: With prompting and support, express an opinion about a topic or text with one supporting reason using a combination of drawing, dictating, and/or writing.
NE.EK.W.5: With prompting and support, write informative/explanatory pieces about a topic or text with one supporting fact using a combination of drawing, dictating, and/or writing.
NE.EK.W.6: With prompting and support, identify information from provided sources to answer a question using a combination of drawing, dictating, and/or writing.
NE.EK.SL.1: With prompting and support, participate with peers and adults in structured discussions and routines about Kindergarten topics and texts.
NE.EK.SL.1.a: Ask pertinent questions to acquire or confirm information.
NE.EK.SL.1.b: Demonstrate interpretation of verbal and non-verbal messages in a conversation.
NE.EK.SL.1.c: Converse with peers and adults in an all-inclusive manner to foster positive relationships while respecting diverse perspectives.
NE.EK.SL.1.d: Develop attentive listening skills (e.g., eye contact, nonverbal cues, recalling).
NE.EK.SL.1.e: Complete a task following one/two-step directions.
NE.EK.SL.2: With prompting and support, describe familiar people, places, things, and events, and provide additional detail.
NE.EK.SL.2.a: Demonstrate appropriate speaking techniques (e.g., appropriate eye contact, adequate volume, clear pronunciation) for a variety of purposes and situations.
NE.EK.SL.2.b: Convey a personal perspective with clear reasons.
NE.EK.SL.2.c: Explain the purpose of information being presented.
NE.EK.SL.2.d: Demonstrate awareness of and sensitivity to the appropriate use of words (e.g., helpful/hurtful words).
NE.EK.SL.2.e: Use appropriate visual and/or digital tools to support verbal communication.
NE.MK.N.1: Subitizing: Students will quantify briefly shown collections and verbally label the arrangements without counting.
NE.MK.N.1.a: Without counting, recognize and verbally label arrangements for briefly shown collections up to 10 (e.g., “I saw 5.” “How did you know?” “I saw 3 and 2, that is 5.”)
NE.MK.N.2: Counting and Cardinality: Students will understand the relationship between numbers and quantities.
NE.MK.N.2.a: Use one-to-one correspondence when counting objects to show the relationship between numbers and quantities and understand the last number counted is a direct representation of the total objects in a given set.
NE.MK.N.2.b: Understand that each successive number name refers to a quantity that is one larger.
NE.MK.N.2.c: Count out the number of objects given a number from 1 to 20.
NE.MK.N.2.d: Count up to 20 objects arranged in a line, a rectangular array, or a circle, and count up to 10 objects in a scattered configuration.
NE.MK.N.2.e: Count verbally forward and backward from any given number within 20.
NE.MK.N.2.f: Count verbally in sequential order by ones and by tens to 100, making accurate decade transitions (e.g., 89 to 90).
NE.MK.N.2.g: Write and name numbers 0 to 20. Represent a number of objects with a written numeral 0 to 20.
NE.MK.N.2.h: Compare the number of objects in two groups, up to 20, using the words fewer than, more than, the same as.
Base Ten: Students will work with numbers 11 to 19 to gain a foundation for place value.
NE.MK.N.3.a: Compose and decompose numbers from 11 to 19 into a group of ten ones and some more ones using a model, drawing, or equation.
NE.MK.N.4: Number and Algebraic Relationships: Students will understand and demonstrate the meaning of addition and subtraction.
NE.MK.N.4.a: Represent and explain addition and subtraction as part-whole relationships, with addition as putting together and/or adding to and subtraction as taking apart and/or taking from, using objects, drawings, numbers, and equations.
NE.MK.N.4.b: Compose and decompose numbers less than or equal to 10 into pairs in more than one way using verbal explanations, objects, or drawings.
NE.MK.N.4.c: For any number from 1 to 9, find the number that makes 10 when added to the given number, sharing the answer with a model, drawing, or equation.
NE.MK.N.4.d: Efficiently, flexibly, and accurately add and subtract within 5.
NE.MK.N.4.e: Solve authentic problems that involve addition and subtraction within 10 (e.g., by using objects, drawings, and equations to represent the problem).
NE.MK.G.1: Shapes and Their Attributes: Students will identify and represent the attributes of two-dimensional shapes and three-dimensional solids.
NE.MK.G.1.a: Identify and name two-dimensional shapes including circles, triangles, squares, and rectangles regardless of orientation or size.
NE.MK.G.1.b: Identify and name three-dimensional shapes including spheres, cubes, cylinders, and cones regardless of orientation or size.
NE.MK.G.1.c: Describe the relative positions of shapes in relation to other objects or shapes using terms such as above, below, in front of, behind, and next to.
NE.MK.G.1.d: Create shapes using given materials and describe one or more of the attributes such as number of sides/corners.
NE.MK.G.1.e: Combine simple shapes to compose larger shapes.
NE.MK.G.2: Measurement: Students will describe and compare measurable attributes.
NE.MK.G.2.a: Describe measurable attributes of authentic objects including length, capacity, and weight.
NE.MK.G.2.b: Directly compare two objects with a measurable attribute in common to describe which object is longer/shorter, heavier/lighter, and has more/less-capacity.
NE.MK.G.3: Time and Money: Students will know coin names and values and tell time to the hour.
NE.MK.G.3.a: Identify the name and value of pennies, nickels, and dimes.
NE.MK.G.3.b: Identify the parts of digital and analog clocks. Tell and write time to the hour using digital clocks and analog clocks using only the hour hand.
NE.MK.D.1: Classification: Students will sort and classify objects using one or more attributes.
NE.MK.D.1.a: Identify, sort, and classify objects by size, shape, color, and other attributes.
NE.MK.D.1.b: Identify objects that do not belong to a particular group and explain the reasoning used.
NE.SK.1.1: Gather, analyze, and communicate evidence of forces and their interactions.
NE.SK.1.1.a: Plan and conduct an investigation to compare the effects of different strengths or different directions of pushes and pulls on the motion of an object.
NE.SK.1.1.b: Analyze data to determine if a design solution works as intended to change the speed or direction of an object with a push or a pull.
NE.SK.7.2: Gather, analyze, and communicate evidence of interdependent relationships in ecosystems.
NE.SK.7.2.a: Use observations to describe patterns of what plants and animals (including humans) need to survive.
NE.SK.7.2.b: Construct an argument supported by evidence for how plants and animals (including humans) can change the environment to meet their needs.
NE.SK.7.2.c: Use a model to represent the relationship between the needs of different plants or animals (including humans) and the places they live.
NE.SK.7.2.d: Communicate solutions that will increase the positive impact of humans on the land, water, air, and/or other living things in the local environment.
NE.SK.12.3: Gather, analyze, and communicate evidence of weather and climate.
NE.SK.12.3.a: Use and share observations of local weather conditions to describe patterns over time.
NE.SK.12.3.b: Ask questions to obtain information about the purpose of weather forecasting to prepare for, and respond to, severe weather.
NE.SK.12.3.c: Make observations to determine the effect of sunlight on Earth's surface.
NE.SK.12.3.d: Use tools and materials to design and build a structure that will reduce the warming effect of sunlight on an area.
NE.SK.12.3.e: Ask questions, make observations, and gather information about a situation people want to change to define a simple problem that can be solved through the development of a new or improved object or tool.
NE.E1.F.1: Demonstrate knowledge of the organization and basic concepts of print.
NE.E1.F.1.a: Recognize the distinguishing features of a sentence.
NE.E1.F.2: Demonstrate understanding of spoken words, syllables, and sounds (phonemes).
NE.E1.F.2.a: Identify, segment and blend phonemes in single syllable spoken three and four phoneme words including words with blends.
NE.E1.F.2.b: Delete initial and final phonemes in words.
NE.E1.F.2.c: Substitute phonemes in spoken words to build new words in single-syllable words with no blends.
NE.E1.F.2.d: Add or substitute individual sounds (phonemes in simple, one-syllable words to make new words), (e.g., “Say 'map.' Say it again and instead of /p/ say /t/. What is the new word? 'Mat'”).
NE.E1.F.3: Know and apply phonics and word analysis skills in decoding and encoding (spelling) words.
NE.E1.F.3.a: Decode and encode words using knowledge of sound-spelling correspondence for common consonant digraphs, tri-graphs, and blends.
NE.E1.F.3.b: Decode and encode simple words with r-controlled vowels.
NE.E1.F.3.c: Decode and encode regularly spelled one-syllable words.
NE.E1.F.3.d: Decode and encode final -e and common vowel team conventions for representing long vowel sounds.
NE.E1.F.3.e: Decode and encode two-syllable words with regular patterns by breaking the words into syllables.
NE.E1.F.3.f: Decode and encode words with inflectional endings.
NE.E1.F.3.g: Use knowledge that every syllable must have a vowel sound to determine the number of syllables in a printed word.
NE.E1.F.3.h: Recognize and read grade-appropriate, irregularly spelled words.
NE.E1.F.4: Develop accuracy, phrasing, and expression/prosody while reading a variety of grade-level texts to support comprehension.
NE.E1.F.4.a: Read decodable text accurately with appropriate rate, intonation, and expression/prosody to reflect meaning.
NE.E1.F.4.b: Read grade level high-frequency words with automaticity and accuracy (e.g., Fry or Dolch words or those included in instructional materials).
NE.E1.RP.1: Retell familiar stories, including key details, and demonstrate understanding of their central message or lesson from a literary text.
NE.E1.RP.2: Identify the main character(s), setting, and important events, drawing on key details in a literary text.
NE.E1.RP.3: Explain the difference between the roles of author and narrator or speaker in a literary text.
NE.E1.RP.4: Identify the basic characteristics of literary text, drawing on a wide range of text types.
NE.E1.RP.5: Compare and contrast the experiences of characters in familiar stories.
NE.E1.RP.6: Ask and answer questions about key details in a literary text.
NE.E1.RP.7: Make connections between own experiences and other cultures in literary texts.
NE.E1.RP.8: With prompting and support, read and comprehend a wide range of literary texts of appropriate complexity for Grade 1.
NE.E1.RI.1: Identify the main topic and key details in an informational text.
NE.E1.RI.2: Identify key individuals, events, or pieces of information in an informational text.
NE.E1.RI.3: Define the role of the author and illustrator in presenting the ideas or information in a text.
NE.E1.RI.4: Use text features (titles, headings, visuals) to predict or confirm the topic of a text.
NE.E1.RI.5: Identify basic similarities and differences between two informational texts on the same topic.
NE.E1.RI.6: Identify an author's opinion(s) about a text.
NE.E1.RI.7: Make connections between own experiences and other cultures in informational texts.
NE.E1.RI.8: With prompting and support, read and comprehend a wide range of informational texts of appropriate complexity for Grade 1.
NE.E1.V.1: Build and use a range of conversational, academic, and discipline-specific grade-level vocabulary.
NE.E1.V.1.a: Use sentence-level context clues to determine the meaning of a word or phrase.
NE.E1.V.1.b: Use commonly occurring affixes to determine the meaning of unknown words.
NE.E1.V.1.c: Identify commonly occurring root words and their inflectional forms.
NE.E1.V.1.d: Determine the meanings of key words and phrases using provided reference materials and classroom resources.
NE.E1.V.2: Interpret an author's use of figurative, connotative, and technical language in grade-level literary and informational text.
NE.E1.V.2.a: Sort common words and phrases into conceptual categories to develop an understanding of word relationships.
NE.E1.V.2.b: Define words by their category and simple attributes (e.g., a duck is a bird that swims).

NE.E1.SL.2.a: Demonstrate appropriate speaking techniques (e.g., appropriate eye contact, adequate volume, clear pronunciation) for a variety of purposes and situations, including interpreting 1st grade texts.

NE.M1.N.1: Subitizing: Students will quantify briefly shown collections and verbally label the arrangements without counting.
NE.M1.N.1.a: Without counting, recognize and verbally label arrangements for briefly shown collections up to 20 (e.g.,” I saw 16.” “How did you know?” “I saw 10 and 6, that is 16”).
NE.M1.N.2: Counting and Cardinality: Students will understand the relationship between numbers and quantities to extend the counting sequence.
NE.M1.N.2.a: Count verbally by ones and tens within 120 starting at any given number.
NE.M1.N.2.b: Count verbally by ones and tens within 120 starting at any given number. Understand that the given number is a direct representation of the total objects in a given set and counting on each successive number represents adding an additional object, and counting back each proceeding number represents removing an object.
NE.M1.N.2.c: Write numerals to match a representation of a given set of objects for numbers up to 120.
NE.M1.N.2.d: Understand patterns of skip counting by `2text(s),5text(s),and10text(s)`.
NE.M1.N.3: Base Ten: Students will represent and compare two-digit numbers to gain foundations for place value.
NE.M1.N.3.a: Understand 10 as a bundle, collection, or (more abstractly) composition of ten ones and that the two digits of a two-digit number represent a composition of some tens and some ones.
NE.M1.N.3.b: Compare two, two-digit numbers using words greater than, less than, equal to, and symbols <, >, =. Justify comparisons based on the number of tens and ones.
NE.M1.N.4: Number and Operations: Students will compute using addition and subtraction.
NE.M1.N.4.a: Add and subtract within 20, using flexible strategies such as counting on or counting back, making ten, using ten, and using doubles and near doubles.
NE.M1.N.4.b: Efficiently, flexibly, and accurately add and subtract within 10.
NE.M1.N.4.c: Find the difference between two numbers that are multiples of 10, ranging from 10 to 90 using concrete models, drawings, or strategies, and write the corresponding equation.
NE.M1.N.4.d: Mentally find 10 more or 10 less than a two-digit number without having to count and explain the reasoning used.
NE.M1.N.4.e: Add within `100`, including adding a two-digit number and a one-digit number, adding a two-digit number and a multiple of ten, using concrete models, drawings, and strategies that reflect an understanding of place value, the relationship between addition and subtraction, and the properties of operations. Relate the strategy to a written method and explain the reasoning used to solve.
NE.M1.N.4.f: Understand that in adding two-digit numbers, one adds tens and tens, ones and ones; sometimes it is necessary to compose a ten.
NE.M1.N.4.g: Subtract multiples of ten from two-digit numbers (positive or zero differences) using concrete models, drawings, and strategies that reflect an understanding of place value, the relationship between addition and subtraction, and the properties of operations. Relate the strategy to a written method and explain the reasoning used to solve.
NE.M1.N.5: Number and Algebraic Relationships: Students will understand and apply properties of operations and the relationship between addition and subtraction to solve problems.
NE.M1.N.5.a: Use the meaning of the equal sign to determine if equations are true and give examples of equations that are true (e.g., 4 = 4, 6 = 7 - 1, 6 + 3 = 3 + 6, 7 + 2 = 5 + 4).
NE.M1.N.5.b: Use the relationship of addition and subtraction to solve subtraction problems (e.g., find 12 - 9 = , using the addition fact 9 + 3 = 12).
NE.M1.N.5.c: Determine the unknown whole number in an addition or subtraction equation (e.g., 7 + ? = 13).
NE.M1.N.5.d: Use the commutative property of addition to develop addition strategies and compose/decompose numbers to develop addition and subtraction strategies.
NE.M1.N.5.e: Solve problems that call for addition of three whole numbers whose sum is less than or equal to 20 using flexible strategies with objects, drawings, and/or equations.
NE.M1.N.5.f: Solve authentic problems involving addition and subtraction within 20 in situations of adding to, taking from, putting together, taking apart, and comparing, with unknowns in all parts of the addition or subtraction problem by using objects, drawings, and/or equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.
NE.M1.N.5.g: Create an authentic problem to represent a given equation involving addition and subtraction within 20.
NE.M1.G.1: Shapes and Their Attributes: Students will represent and describe the attributes of two-dimensional shapes.
NE.M1.G.1.a: Determine geometric attributes of two-dimensional shapes regardless of orientation or size for rhombi, trapezoids, and hexagons (e.g., a hexagon is closed with six sides).
NE.M1.G.1.b: Determine geometric attributes of three-dimensional shapes including cones, cylinders, cubes, and rectangular prisms regardless of orientation or size.
NE.M1.G.1.c: Describe lines and sides of shapes as parallel or non-parallel.
NE.M1.G.1.d: Partition circles and rectangles into two and four equal parts using the language halves and fourths.
NE.M1.G.2: Measurement: Students will measure and compare lengths.
NE.M1.G.2.a: Measure the length of an object as a whole number of same-size, non-standard units by placing them end to end.
NE.M1.G.2.b: Order three objects by directly comparing their lengths or indirectly by using a third object.
NE.M1.G.3: Time and Money: Students will solve problems with coins and tell time to the half hour.
NE.M1.G.3.a: Understand the value of dimes and pennies (e.g., a dime is equal to ten pennies) relating to tens and ones and solve problems involving dimes and pennies using the ¢ symbol appropriately.
NE.M1.G.3.b: Count collections of like coins (penny, nickel, and dime) relating to patterns of counting by `1text(s),5text(s),and10text(s)`.
NE.M1.G.3.c: Tell and write time to the half hour and hour using analog and digital clocks.
NE.M1.D.1: Data Collection: Students will formulate questions to collect, organize, and represent data.
NE.M1.D.1.a: Collect, organize, and represent a data set with up to three categories using a picture graph.
NE.M1.D.2: Analyze Data and Interpret Results: Students will analyze the data and interpret the results.
NE.M1.D.2.a: Ask and answer questions about the total number of data points, how many in each category, and compare categories by identifying how many more or less are in a particular category using a picture graph.
NE.S1.2.1: Gather, analyze, and communicate evidence of light and sound waves.
NE.S1.2.1.a: Plan and conduct investigations to provide evidence that vibrating materials can make sound and that sound can make materials vibrate.
NE.S1.2.1.b: Make observations to construct an evidence-based explanation that objects can be seen only when illuminated.
NE.S1.2.1.c: Plan and conduct an investigation to determine the effect of placing objects made with different materials in the path of a beam of light.
NE.S1.2.1.d: Use tools and materials to design and build a device that uses light or sound to solve the problem of communicating over a distance.
NE.S1.6.2: Gather, analyze, and communicate evidence to show the relationship between structure and function in living things.
NE.S1.6.2.a: Use materials to design a solution to a human problem by mimicking how plants and/or animals use their external parts to help them survive, grow, and meet their needs.
NE.S1.6.2.b: Develop a simple sketch, drawing, or physical model to illustrate how the shape of an object helps it function as needed to solve a given problem.
NE.S1.6.2.c: Read grade appropriate texts and use media to determine patterns in a behavior of parents and offspring that help offspring survive.
NE.S1.6.2.d: Make observations to construct an evidence-based account that young plants and animals are like, but not exactly like, their parents.
NE.S1.11.3: Gather, analyze, and communicate evidence of patterns and cycles of space systems.
NE.S1.11.3.a: Use observations of the sun, moon, and stars to describe patterns that can be predicted.
NE.S1.11.3.b: Make observations at different times of the year to relate the amount of daylight to the time of year.
NE.E2.F.1: Demonstrate knowledge of the organization and basic concepts of print.
NE.E2.F.1.a: Recognize the distinguishing features of a paragraph including that multiple sentences may be used to form a paragraph and the author may indent or skip a line to signal a new paragraph.
NE.E2.F.2: LA.2.F.2 Demonstrate understanding of advanced phonemic awareness skills in spoken words, syllables, and sounds (phonemes).
NE.E2.F.2.a: Identify, segment, and blend phonemes in single syllable spoken five and six phoneme words including words with blends, digraphs, and trigraphs.
NE.E2.F.2.b: Substitute sounds in words with five or more phonemes.
NE.E2.F.2.c: Delete initial and final phonemes in words including words with blends.
NE.E2.F.3: Know and apply phonics and word analysis skills in decoding and encoding (spelling) words.
NE.E2.F.3.a: Decode words with variable vowel teams and vowel diphthongs.
NE.E2.F.3.b: Decode regularly spelled two-syllable words with long vowels.
NE.E2.F.3.c: Decode words with open and closed syllables and consonant -le.
NE.E2.F.3.d: Decode words with common Anglo roots and suffixes.
NE.E2.F.3.e: Decode words with silent letter combinations.

NE.E2.F.4.b: Read grade level high-frequency words with automaticity and accuracy (e.g., Fry or Dolch words or those included in instructional materials).
NE.E2.RP.1: Recount narratives and determine their central message, lesson, or moral.
NE.E2.RP.2: Describe characters and how they interact with one another.
NE.E2.RP.3: Determine and explain who is telling a story within and across literary texts.
NE.E2.RP.4: Describe the basic structure of a literary text, including how literary elements are introduced and developed and conflicts are resolved.
NE.E2.RP.5: Compare and contrast two or more versions of the same literary text by different authors or from different cultures.
NE.E2.RP.6: Ask and answer literal (e.g., recall/details) and simple inferential (e.g., why or how) questions about key details in a literary text.
NE.E2.RP.7: Compare and contrast topics in a variety of literary texts to build knowledge of cultures (e.g., history, values, beliefs, and behaviors).
NE.E2.RP.8: With scaffolding as needed, read and comprehend a wide range of literary texts of appropriate complexity for Grade 2.
NE.E2.RI.1: Identify the main topic and key details in a multi-paragraph text.
NE.E2.RI.2: Describe the connections between individuals, historical events, scientific ideas, or steps in a process.
NE.E2.RI.3: Determine and explain the author's purpose in an informational text, including what the author wants to answer, explain, or describe.
NE.E2.RI.4: Explain how text features (titles, headings, table of contents, glossaries, captions, graphs, maps, and/or other visuals) contribute to the meaning of texts.
NE.E2.RI.5: Compare and contrast the two most important ideas presented by two informational texts on the same topic.
NE.E2.RI.6: Explain an author's opinion(s) and supporting evidence from the text.
NE.E2.RI.7: Compare and contrast topics in a variety of informational texts to build knowledge of cultures (e.g., history, values, beliefs, and behaviors).
NE.E2.RI.8: With scaffolding as needed, read and comprehend a wide range of informational texts of appropriate complexity for Grade 2.

NE.E2.SL.1: Participate with peers and adults in structured discussions and routines about 2nd grade topics and texts.

NE.M2.N.1: Subitizing: Students will quantify briefly shown collections and verbally label the arrangements without counting.
NE.M2.N.1.a: Without counting, recognize and verbally label structured arrangements for briefly shown collections using groups, multiplicative thinking, and place value (e.g.,” I saw 48.” “How did you know?” “I saw 4 groups of 10 and 2 groups of 4 is 8...4 tens and 8 ones...48”).
NE.M2.N.2: Counting: Students will understand the relationship between numbers and quantities to extend the counting sequence.
NE.M2.N.2.a: Count within `1text(,)000`, including skip counting by `5text(s),10text(s),and100text(s)` starting at a variety of multiples of 5, 10, or 100.
NE.M2.N.3: Base Ten: Students will represent and compare three-digit numbers to apply concepts of place value.
NE.M2.N.3.a: Read and write numbers within the range of 0 to `1text(,)000` using standard, word, and expanded forms.
NE.M2.N.3.b: Understand 100 as a bundle, collection, or (more abstractly) composition of ten tens and that the three digits of a three- digit number represent a composition of some hundreds, some tens, and some ones.
NE.M2.N.3.c: Compare two three-digit numbers by using symbols <, >, = and justify the comparison based on the value of the hundreds, tens, and ones.
NE.M2.N.4: Number and Operations: Students will compute using addition and subtraction.
NE.M2.N.4.b: Add and subtract using 100 strategies based on place value including properties of operations, relationships between addition and subtraction, and algorithms.
NE.M2.N.4.c: Mentally add or subtract `10or100` to or from a given number 100 to 900.
NE.M2.N.4.d: Add up to three two-digit numbers using strategies based on place value and understanding of properties.
NE.M2.N.4.e: Add and subtract within `1text(,)000` using concrete models, drawings, and strategies that reflect an understanding of place value and the properties of operations.
Number and Algebraic Relationships: Students will create and solve problems involving addition and subtraction and work with equal groups of objects to gain foundations for multiplication.
NE.M2.N.5.a: Solve authentic problems involving addition and subtraction within `100` in situations of addition and subtraction, including adding to, subtracting from, joining and separating, and comparing situations with unknowns in all positions using objects, models, drawings, verbal explanations, expressions, and equations.
NE.M2.N.5.b: Create authentic problems to represent one-step addition and subtraction within `100` with unknowns in all positions.
NE.M2.N.5.c: Use repeated addition to find the total number of objects arranged in an array no larger than five rows and five columns and write an equation to express the total.
NE.M2.N.5.d: Identify a group of objects from 0 to 20 as even or odd by counting by `2text(s)` or by showing even numbers as a sum of two equal parts.
NE.M2.G.1: Shapes and Their Attributes: Students will recognize and represent the attributes of two-dimensional shapes and three-dimensional solids.
NE.M2.G.1.a: Recognize and describe all faces of three-dimensional shapes as two-dimensional shapes. Identify and count attributes of solid shapes including the edges, faces, and vertices.
NE.M2.G.1.b: Recognize and draw two-dimensional shapes having a specific number of sides, angles, and vertices including triangles, quadrilaterals, pentagons, and hexagons.
NE.M2.G.1.c: Partition a rectangle into rows and columns of equal-sized squares and count to find the total.
NE.M2.G.1.d: Divide circles and rectangles into two, three, or four equal parts and describe the parts using the language of halves, thirds, fourths, half of, a third of, and a fourth of.
NE.M2.G.1.e: Recognize that equal shares of identical wholes need not have the same shape.
NE.M2.G.2: Describe Measurable Attributes: Students will measure, estimate, and compare lengths to build meaning of the measurement process.
NE.M2.G.2.a: Measure the length of an object using two different length units and describe how the measurements relate to the size of the specific unit.
NE.M2.G.2.b: Compare the difference in length of objects using inches and feet or centimeters and meters.
NE.M2.G.3: Measurement: Students will use tools to measure and estimate length using standard units.
NE.M2.G.3.a: Identify and use appropriate tools for measuring length.
NE.M2.G.3.b: Measure and estimate lengths using whole numbers with inches, feet, centimeters, and meters.
NE.M2.G.4: Relate Addition and Subtraction to Measurement: Students will add or subtract to solve length problems.
NE.M2.G.4.a: Represent whole numbers as equally spaced lengths on a number line diagram. Use number lines to find sums and differences within `100`.
NE.M2.G.4.b: Use addition and subtraction within `100` to solve problems using the same standard-length units.
NE.M2.G.5: Time and Money: Students will solve problems with dollar bills and coins and tell time to the nearest five-minute interval.
NE.M2.G.5.a: Solve problems involving dollar bills, quarters, dimes, nickels, and pennies using $ and ¢ symbols appropriately.
NE.M2.G.5.b: Identify and write time to five-minute intervals using analog and digital clocks and both a.m. and p.m.
NE.M2.D.1: Data Collection: Students will formulate questions to collect, organize, and represent data.
NE.M2.D.1.a: Ask authentic questions to generate data and represent the data using scaled picture graphs with up to four categories.
NE.M2.D.1.b: Ask authentic questions to generate data and represent the data using bar graphs with up to four categories.
NE.M2.D.1.c: Create and represent a data set by making a line plot using whole numbers.
NE.M2.D.2: Analyze Data and Interpret Results: Students will analyze the data and interpret the results.
NE.M2.D.2.a: Analyze data using scaled picture graphs or bar graphs with up to four categories. Solve problems including one-step comparison problems, using information from the graphs.
NE.S2.3.1: Gather, analyze, and communicate evidence of the structure, properties, and interactions of matter.
NE.S2.3.1.a: Plan and conduct an investigation to describe and classify different kinds of materials by their observable properties.
NE.S2.3.1.b: Analyze data obtained from testing different materials to determine which materials have the properties that are best suited for an intended purpose.
NE.S2.3.1.c: Analyze data from tests of two objects, designed to solve the same problem, to compare the strengths and weaknesses based on the properties.
NE.S2.3.1.d: Make observations to construct an evidence-based account of how an object made of a small set of pieces can be disassembled and made into a new object.
NE.S2.3.1.e: Construct an argument with evidence that some changes caused by heating or cooling can be reversed and some cannot.
NE.S2.7.2: Gather, analyze, and communicate evidence of interdependent relationships in ecosystems.
NE.S2.7.2.a: Plan and conduct an investigation to determine if plants need sunlight and water to grow.
NE.S2.7.2.b: Develop a simple model that mimics the function of an animal in dispersing seeds or pollinating plants.
NE.S2.7.2.c: Make observations of plants and animals to compare the diversity of life in different habitats.
