NE.M3.N.1: Numeric Relationships: Students will demonstrate and represent multi-digit numbers using place value understanding.
NE.M3.N.1.a: Read, write, and demonstrate multiple equivalent representations for numbers up to 10,000 using objects or visual representations including standard form and expanded form.
NE.M3.N.1.b: Represent and justify comparisons of whole numbers up to 10,000 using number lines and reasoning strategies.
NE.M3.N.2: Fractions: Students will develop understanding of fractions as numbers.
NE.M3.N.2.a: Partition two-dimensional figures into equal areas and express the area of each part as a unit fraction of the whole.
NE.M3.N.2.b: Find parts of a whole using visual fraction models.
NE.M3.N.2.c: Represent and understand a fraction as a number on a number line.
NE.M3.N.2.d: Show and identify equivalent fractions using visual representations including pictures, manipulatives, and number lines.
NE.M3.N.2.e: Justify whole numbers as fractions and identify fractions that are equivalent to whole numbers.
NE.M3.N.2.f: Compare and order fractions having the same numerators or denominators by reasoning about their size.
NE.M3.A.1: Operations and Algebraic Thinking: Students will extend understanding of multiplication and apply operational properties to solve problems.
NE.M3.A.1.a: Add and subtract up to four-digit whole numbers with or without regrouping using strategies based on place value and algorithms.
NE.M3.A.1.b: Determine the reasonableness of whole number sums and differences using estimations and number sense.
NE.M3.A.1.c: Solve and write one-step whole number equations to represent authentic problems using the four operations including equations with an unknown start, unknown change, or unknown result.
NE.M3.A.1.d: Interpret and solve two-step authentic problems involving whole numbers and the four operations.
NE.M3.A.1.e: Apply commutative, associative, distributive, identity, and zero properties as strategies to multiply and divide.
NE.M3.A.1.f: Use drawings, words, arrays, symbols, repeated addition, equal groups, and number lines to interpret and explain the meaning of multiplication and division and their relationship.
NE.M3.A.1.g: Fluently multiply and divide within `100` using strategies based on understanding and properties of operations.
NE.M3.A.1.h: Multiply one-digit whole numbers by multiples of `10` in the range of 10 to 90 using strategies based on place value and properties of operations.
NE.M3.G.1: Shapes and Their Attributes: Students will recognize and represent the attributes of two-dimensional shapes.
NE.M3.G.1.a: Sort quadrilaterals into categories according to their attributes.
NE.M3.G.2: Area and Perimeter: Students will recognize perimeter and area as attributes of plane figures and understand concepts of area measurement.
NE.M3.G.2.a: Solve authentic problems involving perimeters of polygons when given the side lengths or when given the perimeter and unknown side length(s).
NE.M3.G.2.b: Use concrete and pictorial models to measure areas in `text(square units)` by counting square units.
NE.M3.G.2.c: Find the area of a rectangle with whole-number side lengths by modeling with unit squares; show that area can be additive and is the same as would be found by multiplying the side lengths.
NE.M3.G.3: Measurement: Students will use tools to solve measurement problems.
NE.M3.G.3.a: Identify and use the appropriate tools and units of measurement, both customary and metric, to solve authentic problems involving length, weight, mass, liquid volume, and capacity (within the same system and unit).
NE.M3.G.3.b: Estimate and measure length to the nearest half inch, fourth inch, and centimeter.
NE.M3.G.4: Time: Students will tell time to the nearest minute and find elapsed time.
NE.M3.G.4.a: Tell and write time to the minute using both analog and digital clocks.
NE.M3.G.4.b: Solve authentic problems involving addition and subtraction of time intervals and find elapsed time.
NE.M3.D.1: Data Collection: Students will formulate questions to collect, organize, and represent data.
NE.M3.D.1.a: Create scaled picture graphs and scaled bar graphs to represent a data set with more than four categories, including data collected through observations, surveys, and experiments.
NE.M3.D.1.b: Generate and represent data using line plots where the horizontal scale is marked off in halves and whole number units.
NE.M3.D.2: Analyze Data and Interpret Results: Students will analyze the data and interpret the results.
NE.M3.D.2.a: Analyze data and make simple statements using information represented in picture graphs, line plots, and bar graphs.
NE.S3.1.1: Gather, analyze, and communicate evidence of forces and their interactions.
NE.S3.1.1.a: Plan and conduct an investigation to provide evidence of the effects of balanced and unbalanced forces on the motion of an object.
NE.S3.1.1.b: Make observations and/or measurements of an object's motion to provide evidence that a pattern can be used to predict future motion.
NE.S3.1.1.c: Ask questions to determine cause and effect relationships of electrical or magnetic interactions between two objects not in contact with each other.
NE.S3.1.1.d: Define a simple design problem that can be solved by applying scientific ideas about magnets.
NE.S3.7.2: Gather, analyze, and communicate evidence of the interdependent relations in ecosystems.
NE.S3.7.2.a: Construct an argument that some animals form groups that help members survive.
NE.S3.7.2.b: Analyze and interpret data from fossils to provide evidence of the organisms and environments in which they lived long ago.
NE.S3.7.2.c: Construct an argument with evidence that in a particular habitat some organisms can survive well, some survive less well, and some cannot survive at all.
NE.S3.7.2.d: Make a claim about the merit of a solution to a problem caused when the environment changes and the types of plants and animals that live there may change.
NE.S3.7.2.e: Generate and compare multiple possible solutions to a problem based on how well each is likely to meet the criteria and constraints of the problem.
NE.S3.9.3: Gather and analyze data to communicate an understanding of inheritance and variation of traits through life cycles and environmental influences.
NE.S3.9.3.a: Develop models to describe that organisms have unique and diverse life cycles but all have in common birth, growth, reproduction, and death.
NE.S3.9.3.b: Analyze and interpret data to provide evidence that plants and animals have traits inherited from parents and that variation of these traits exists in a group of similar organisms.
NE.S3.9.3.c: Use evidence to support the explanation that traits can be influenced by the environment.
NE.S3.9.3.d: Use evidence to construct an explanation for how the variations in characteristics among individuals of the same species may provide advantages in surviving, finding mates, and reproducing.
NE.S3.12.4: Gather and analyze data to communicate an understanding of weather and climate.
NE.S3.12.4.a: Represent data in table, pictograph, and bar graph displays to describe typical weather conditions expected during a particular season.
NE.S3.12.4.b: Obtain and combine information to describe climates in different regions of the world.
NE.S3.12.4.c: Make a claim about the merit of a design solution that reduces the impacts of a weather-related hazard.

NE.M4.N.1: Numeric Relationships: Students will demonstrate and represent multi-digit numbers using relationships with the base-ten number system.
NE.M4.N.1.a: Read, write, and demonstrate multiple equivalent representations for whole numbers up to `1text(,)000text(,)000` and decimals to the hundredths using visual representations, standard form, and expanded form.
NE.M4.N.1.b: Represent and justify comparisons of whole numbers up to `1text(,)000text(,)000` and decimals through the hundredths place using number lines and reasoning strategies.
NE.M4.N.1.c: Recognize a digit in one place represents ten times what it represents in the place to its right.
NE.M4.N.1.d: Use decimal notation for fractions with denominators of `10or100` (e.g., 43/100 = 0.43).
NE.M4.N.2: Fractions and Decimals: Students will extend understanding of fractions by equivalence and ordering and will develop an understanding of decimals.
NE.M4.N.2.a: Explain and demonstrate how a mixed number is equivalent to a fraction greater than one and how a fraction greater than one is equivalent to a mixed number using visual fraction models and reasoning strategies.
NE.M4.N.2.b: Explain and demonstrate how equivalent fractions are generated by multiplying by a fraction equivalent to 1 using visual fraction models and the Identity Property of Multiplication.
NE.M4.N.2.c: Compare and order fractions having unlike numerators or denominators using number lines, benchmarks, reasoning strategies, and/or equivalence.
NE.M4.N.3: Operations with Fractions: Students will understand and demonstrate fractional computation.
NE.M4.N.3.a: Decompose a fraction into a sum of fractions with the same denominator in more than one way and record each decomposition with an equation and a visual representation.
NE.M4.N.3.b: Explain the meaning of addition and subtraction of fractions with like denominators using visual fraction models, properties of operations, and reasoning strategies.
NE.M4.N.3.c: Add and subtract fractions and mixed numbers with like denominators.
NE.M4.N.3.d: Solve authentic problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions and mixed numbers with like denominators.
NE.M4.N.3.e: Multiply a fraction by a whole number using visual fraction models and properties of operations.
NE.M4.N.4: Factors and Multiples: Students will find factors and multiples and classify numbers as prime or composite.
NE.M4.N.4.a: Determine whether a given whole number up to 100 is a multiple of a given one-digit number.
NE.M4.N.4.b: Determine factors of any whole number up to 100 and classify a number up to 100 as prime or composite.
NE.M4.A.1: Operations and Algebraic Thinking: Students will extend understanding of multiplication and division and apply operational properties to solve problems involving variables.
NE.M4.A.1.a: Add and subtract multi-digit numbers using an algorithm.
NE.M4.A.1.b: Multiply up to a four-digit whole number by a one-digit whole number and multiply a two-digit whole number by a two- digit whole number, using strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and algorithms.
NE.M4.A.1.c: Divide up to a four-digit whole number by a one-digit divisor with and without a remainder using strategies based on place value.
NE.M4.A.1.d: Determine the reasonableness of whole number products and quotients using estimations and number sense.
NE.M4.A.1.e: Create a simple algebraic expression or equation using a variable for an unknown number to represent an authentic mathematical situation (e.g., 3 + n = 15, 81 ÷ n = 9).
NE.M4.A.1.f: Solve one- and two-step authentic problems using the four operations including interpreting remainders and the use of a letter to represent the unknown quantity.
NE.M4.G.1: Shapes and Their Attributes: Students will draw and identify lines and angles and classify shapes by properties of their lines and angles.
NE.M4.G.1.a: Identify, create, and describe points, lines, line segments, rays, angles, parallel lines, perpendicular lines, and intersecting lines.
NE.M4.G.1.b: Justify the classification of angles as acute, obtuse, or right.
NE.M4.G.1.c: Justify the classification of two-dimensional shapes based on the presence or absence of parallel and perpendicular lines or the presence or absence of specific angles.
NE.M4.G.1.d: Recognize, draw, and justify lines of symmetry in two-dimensional shapes.
NE.M4.G.2: Measurement: Students will generate simple conversions from a larger unit to a smaller unit to solve authentic problems and measure angles.
NE.M4.G.2.a: Identify and use the appropriate tools, operations, and units of measurement, both customary and metric, to solve authentic problems involving time, length, weight, mass, and capacity.
NE.M4.G.2.b: Determine the reasonableness of measurements involving time, length, weight, mass, capacity, and angles.
NE.M4.G.2.c: Generate simple conversions from a larger unit to a smaller unit within the customary and metric systems of measurement.
NE.M4.G.2.d: Measure angles in whole number degrees using a protractor and relate benchmark angle measurements to their rotation through a circle (e.g., `180°=1/2` of a circle).
NE.M4.G.2.e: Recognize angle measures as additive and solve problems involving addition and subtraction to find unknown angles on a diagram.
NE.M4.G.3: Area and Perimeter: Students will apply perimeter and area formulas for rectangles.
NE.M4.G.3.a: Apply perimeter and area formulas for rectangles to solve authentic problems.
NE.M4.D.1: Data Collection: Students will formulate questions to collect, organize, and represent data.
NE.M4.D.1.a: Generate and represent data using line plots where the horizontal scale is marked off in appropriate units-whole numbers, halves, fourths, or eighths.
NE.M4.D.2: Analyze Data and Interpret Results: Students will analyze the data and interpret the results.
NE.M4.D.2.a: Solve authentic problems and analyze data involving addition or subtraction of fractions presented in line plots.
NE.S4.2.1: Gather, analyze, and communicate evidence of waves and the information they transfer.
NE.S4.2.1.a: Develop a model of waves to describe patterns in terms of amplitude and wavelength and that waves can cause objects to move.
NE.S4.2.1.b: Generate and compare multiple solutions that use patterns to transfer information.
NE.S4.4.2: Gather, analyze and communicate evidence of energy conservation and transfer.
NE.S4.4.2.a: Use evidence to construct an explanation relating the speed of an object to the energy of that object.
NE.S4.4.2.b: Make observations to provide evidence that energy can be transferred from place to place by sound, light, heat, and electrical currents.
NE.S4.4.2.c: Ask questions and predict outcomes about the changes in energy that occur when objects collide.
NE.S4.4.2.d: Apply scientific ideas to design, test, and refine a device that converts energy from one form to another.
NE.S4.4.2.e: Plan and carry out fair tests in which variables are controlled and failure points are considered to identify aspects of a model or prototype that can be improved.
NE.S4.4.2.f: Obtain and combine information to describe that energy and fuels are derived from natural resources and that their uses affect the environment.
NE.S4.6.3: Gather and analyze data to communicate an understanding of structure, function and information processing of living things.
NE.S4.6.3.a: Develop a model to describe that light reflecting from objects and entering the eyes allows objects to be seen.
NE.S4.6.3.b: Construct an argument that plants and animals have internal and external structures that function to support survival, growth, behavior, and reproduction.
NE.S4.6.3.c: Use a model to describe that animals receive different types of information through their senses, process the information in their brain, and respond to the information.
NE.S4.13.4: Gather and analyze data to communicate an understanding of Earth's systems and processes that shape the Earth.
NE.S4.13.4.a: Identify evidence from patterns in rock formations and fossils in rock layers to support an explanation for changes in a landscape over time.
NE.S4.13.4.b: Make observations and/or measurements to provide evidence of the effects of weathering or the rate of erosion by water, ice, wind, or vegetation.
NE.S4.13.4.c: Analyze and interpret data from maps to describe patterns of Earth's features.
NE.S4.13.4.d: Generate and compare multiple solutions to reduce the impacts of natural Earth processes on humans.
NE.E5.F.3: Know and apply phonics and word analysis skills in decoding and encoding (spelling) words.
NE.E5.F.3.a: Decode words with common Greek derived words.
NE.E5.F.3.b: Use combined knowledge of letter-sound correspondences, syllabication patterns, and morphology (e.g., roots and affixes) to decode unfamiliar multisyllabic words in and out of context.
NE.E5.F.4: Develop accuracy, phrasing, and expression/prosody while reading a variety of grade-level texts to support comprehension.
NE.E5.F.4.a: Read a variety of texts accurately using appropriate rate, expression/prosody, and intonation to reflect meaning.
NE.E5.F.4.b: Adjust pace and prosody based on the purpose, complexity, form, and/or style of a text.
NE.E5.RP.1: Explain the theme in a literary text and how it is conveyed through key details.
NE.E5.RP.2: Compare and contrast two or more characters, settings, or events in a literary text or texts.
NE.E5.RP.3: Describe how a narrator or speaker's point of view influences the meaning of a literary text.
NE.E5.RP.4: Explain how a sequence of chapters, scenes, or stanzas fit together to provide the overall structure of literary texts.
NE.E5.RP.5: Compare and contrast the treatment of themes and topics in literary texts of the same genre.
NE.E5.RP.6: Analyze a literary text to answer and develop inferential questions to enhance the comprehension of self and others, quoting or paraphrasing specific evidence from the text.
NE.E5.RP.7: Explain the relationships between two or more characters, events, or ideas in a range of literary texts.
NE.E5.RP.8: Read and comprehend a wide range of literary texts of appropriate complexity for Grade 5 independently and proficiently.
NE.E5.RI.1: Explain the central idea in an informational text and how it is conveyed through key details.
NE.E5.RI.2: Compare and contrast two or more individuals, events, scientific ideas or concepts, or steps in a process, drawing on supporting details from an informational text or texts.
NE.E5.RI.3: Determine the author's purpose(s) and describe how the author's perspective (e.g., beliefs, assumptions, biases) influences the meaning of an informational text.
NE.E5.RI.4: Explain how text features (titles, headings, table of contents, glossaries, captions, graphs, maps, and/or other visuals) contribute to the meaning of texts.
NE.E5.RI.5: Integrate information from multiple texts on the same topic in order to demonstrate knowledge of the topic.
NE.E5.RI.6: Analyze the development of an author's claim(s) and how supporting evidence is used to support the claim(s).
NE.E5.RI.7: Explain the relationships between two or more individuals, events, ideas, or concepts in a range of informational texts.
NE.E5.RI.8: Read and comprehend a wide range of informational text of appropriate complexity for Grade 5 independently and proficiently.
NE.E5.V.1: Acquire and use grade-level academic vocabulary appropriately.
NE.E5.V.1.a: Use context clues (e.g., cause/effect relationships and comparisons in text) to determine the meanings of words and phrases.
NE.E5.V.1.b: Use commonly occurring Greek and Latin affixes and roots to determine the meanings of words.
NE.E5.V.1.c: Determine or clarify the precise meanings or pronunciations of words and phrases using reference materials and classroom resources.
NE.E5.V.2: Interpret an author's use of figurative, connotative, and technical language in grade-level literary and informational text.
NE.E5.V.2.a: Interpret figurative language, including similes and metaphors, in context.
NE.E5.V.2.b: Recognize and explain the meaning of commonly occurring idioms, adages, and proverbs.
NE.E5.V.2.c: Demonstrate knowledge of relationships between particular words (e.g., synonyms, antonyms, homographs) to better understand each of the words.
NE.E5.W.1: Create grammatically correct multi-paragraph compositions with varied sentence structures.
NE.E5.W.1.a: Apply knowledge of rules for capitalization; use underlining, quotation marks, or italics to indicate titles of works.
NE.E5.W.1.b: Use a comma to separate an introductory element from the rest of a sentence, to separate clauses, to set off a question, and to indicate direct address.
NE.E5.W.1.c: Explain the function of and use frequently occurring interjections, verb tenses (e.g., perfect), and correlative conjunctions.
NE.E5.W.1.d: Distinguish between and use types of adjectives (e.g., comparative, superlative).
NE.E5.W.1.e: Identify and revise fragment and run-on sentences and inappropriate shifts in verb tenses.
NE.E5.W.2: Use a recursive writing process to develop, strengthen, and produce writing appropriate to the audience, purpose, and discipline.
NE.E5.W.2.a: Use prewriting activities and resources to plan, organize, and draft writing.
NE.E5.W.2.b: Adapt writing processes to sustain engagement in short and long-term writing tasks of increasing length and complexity.
NE.E5.W.2.c: Improve and clarify the content, structure, and organization of writing by revising, considering feedback from adults and peers.
NE.E5.W.2.d: Improve and clarify writing by editing and proofreading, considering feedback from adults and peers.
NE.E5.W.2.e: Use or decipher multiple formats of print and digital text (e.g., manuscript, cursive, font, graphics, symbols).
NE.E5.W.2.f: Use appropriate print and digital/multimedia tools to produce, enhance, and/or publish writing individually or in collaboration with peers.
NE.E5.W.3: Write creative and/or expressive pieces that describe a well-developed event or experience.
NE.E5.W.3.a: Establish a situation and introduce a narrator and/or characters.
NE.E5.W.3.b: Use precise words and phrases, descriptive/sensory details, dialogue, and sensory language to convey thoughts, feelings, experiences, and events.
NE.E5.W.3.c: Use a variety of transitional words and phrases to organize a sequence of events that unfolds naturally.
NE.E5.W.3.d: Provide a conclusion related to the creative or expressive event or experience.
NE.E5.W.4: Write opinion pieces that explain a perspective with supporting reasons and evidence.
NE.E5.W.4.a: Introduce a topic or text clearly, state an opinion or perspective, and develop a structure in which ideas are grouped logically.
NE.E5.W.4.b: Use facts and details to support reasons and/or evidence.
NE.E5.W.4.c: Use words, phrases, and key vocabulary to connect ideas.
NE.E5.W.4.d: Provide a concluding statement or section related to the perspective.
NE.E5.W.5: Write informative/explanatory pieces to examine a topic or text and clearly convey ideas and information.
NE.E5.W.5.a: Introduce a topic clearly and provide a general focus, grouping information logically and including text features, illustrations, and/or multimedia elements.
NE.E5.W.5.b: Develop the topic with information (e.g., facts, definitions, details, quotations) related to the topic.
NE.E5.W.5.c: Use linking words and phrases and key vocabulary to connect ideas and categories of information.
NE.E5.W.5.d: Provide a concluding statement or section related to the information or explanation(s).
NE.E5.W.6: Locate and summarize relevant information and evidence from literary and informational text sources to answer questions about a topic.
NE.E5.W.6.a: Paraphrase information and evidence to support ideas while avoiding plagiarism.
NE.E5.W.6.b: Locate and evaluate credibility of evidence (e.g., motivation and/or potential bias of an information product) from print and digital sources to generate and answer questions and create new understandings.
NE.E5.W.6.c: Sort evidence into categories using an appropriate note-taking format to collect and organize information.
NE.E5.W.6.d: Demonstrate academic integrity by avoiding overreliance on any one source and referencing sources in writing and speaking; provide a list of sources using a standard format.
NE.E5.W.6.e: Practice safe and ethical behaviors when communicating and interacting with others digitally (e.g., safe information to share, utilize appropriate sites and materials, appropriate language use, respect diverse perspectives).
NE.E5.SL.1: Prepare for and participate in structured discussions and collaborations about 5th grade topics and texts.
NE.E5.SL.1.a: Ask relevant questions to build on ideas, clarify own ideas, or acquire or confirm information.
NE.E5.SL.1.b: Demonstrate interpretation of verbal and non-verbal messages in a conversation.
NE.E5.SL.1.c: Converse with peers and adults an all-inclusive manner to foster positive relationships while respecting diverse perspectives.
NE.E5.SL.1.d: Demonstrate active and attentive listening skills (e.g., eye contact, nonverbal cues, taking notes, recalling, questioning).
NE.E5.SL.1.e: Complete a task following multi-step directions.
NE.E5.SL.2: Report on a topic or text, or present an opinion, sequencing ideas logically and using appropriate facts and relevant, descriptive details to support themes or central ideas.
NE.E5.SL.2.a: Demonstrate appropriate speaking techniques (e.g., appropriate eye contact, adequate volume, clear pronunciation) for a variety of purposes and situations, including interpreting 5th grade texts.
NE.E5.SL.2.b: Convey a perspective with clear reasoning and support.
NE.E5.SL.2.c: Identify the purpose and credibility of information being presented.
NE.E5.SL.2.d: Demonstrate awareness of and sensitivity to the appropriate use of words (e.g., stereotypes, multiple meanings of words).
NE.E5.SL.2.e: Use appropriate visual and/or digital tools to enhance verbal communication and add interest.
NE.M5.N.1: Numeric Relationships: Students will understand the place value system.
NE.M5.N.1.a: Read, write, and demonstrate multiple equivalent representations for multi-digit whole numbers and decimals through the thousandths place using standard form and expanded form.
NE.M5.N.1.b: Recognize a digit in one place represents `1/10` of what it represents in the place to its left.
NE.M5.N.1.c: Use whole number exponents to denote powers of `10`.
NE.M5.N.2: Fractions and Decimals: Students will extend understanding of fraction and decimal equivalence and ordering.
NE.M5.N.2.a: Generate equivalent forms of commonly used fractions and decimals (e.g., halves, fourths, fifths, tenths).
NE.M5.N.2.b: Represent and justify comparisons of whole numbers, fractions, mixed numbers, and decimals through the thousandths place using number lines, reasoning strategies, and/or equivalence.
NE.M5.N.3: Operations with Fractions and Decimals: Students will apply and extend previous understandings of whole number operations to add, subtract, multiply and divide fractions and decimals.
NE.M5.N.3.a: Interpret a fraction as division of the numerator by the denominator.
NE.M5.N.3.b: Multiply a whole number by a fraction or a fraction by a fraction, including mixed numbers, using visual fraction models and properties of operations.
NE.M5.N.3.c: Divide a unit fraction by a whole number and a whole number by a unit fraction using visual fraction models and properties of operations.
NE.M5.N.3.d: Solve authentic problems involving addition, subtraction, and multiplication of fractions and mixed numbers with like and unlike denominators.
NE.M5.N.3.e: Add and subtract fractions and mixed numbers with unlike denominators without simplifying.
NE.M5.N.3.f: Solve authentic problems involving division of unit fractions by whole numbers and division of whole numbers by unit fractions.
NE.M5.N.3.g: Add, subtract, multiply, and divide decimals to hundredths using strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or algorithms.
NE.M5.A.1: Operations and Algebraic Thinking: Students will extend understanding of division and apply operational properties to solve problems involving order of operations.
NE.M5.A.1.a: Multiply multi-digit whole numbers using an algorithm.
NE.M5.A.1.b: Divide four-digit whole numbers by a two-digit divisor, with and without remainders, using strategies based on place value.
NE.M5.A.1.c: Justify the reasonableness of computations involving whole numbers, fractions, and decimals.
NE.M5.A.1.d: Simplify authentic numerical or algebraic expressions using order of operations (excluding exponents).
Shapes and Their Attributes: Students will classify two-dimensional figures into categories based on their properties.
NE.M5.G.1.a: Identify and describe faces, edges, and vertices of rectangular prisms.
NE.M5.G.1.b: Recognize volume as an attribute of solid figures that is measured in `text(cubic units)`.
NE.M5.G.1.c: Justify the classification of two and three-dimensional figures in a hierarchy based on their properties.
NE.M5.G.2: Coordinate Geometry: Graph points on the coordinate plane to solve authentic problems.
NE.M5.G.2.a: Identify the origin, x axis, and y axis of the coordinate plane.
NE.M5.G.2.b: Graph and name points in the first quadrant of the coordinate plane using ordered pairs of whole numbers.
NE.M5.G.2.c: Form ordered pairs from authentic problems involving rules or patterns, graph the ordered pairs in the first quadrant on a coordinate plane, and interpret coordinate values in the context of the situation.
NE.M5.G.3: Measurement: Generate conversions within the customary and metric systems of measurement to solve authentic problems.
NE.M5.G.3.a: Generate conversions in authentic mathematical situations from larger units to smaller units and smaller units to larger units, within the customary and metric systems of measurement.
NE.M5.G.4: Area and Volume: Students will extend area problems for rectangles to include fractions and build meaning for measuring volume.
NE.M5.G.4.a: Find the area of a rectangle with fractional side lengths by tiling it with unit squares of the fraction side lengths and show that the area is the same as would be found by multiplying the side lengths.
NE.M5.G.4.b: Multiply fractional side lengths to find areas of rectangles and represent fraction products as rectangular areas.
NE.M5.G.4.c: Use concrete models to measure the volume of rectangular prisms by counting cubic units.
NE.M5.G.4.d: Find the volume of a rectangular prism with whole-number side lengths by modeling with unit cubes and show that the volume can be additive and is the same as would be found by multiplying the area of the base times height.
NE.M5.G.4.e: Solve authentic problems by applying the formulas `V=lxxwxxhandV=Bxxh` for rectangular prisms to find volumes of rectangular prisms with whole number edge lengths.
NE.M5.D.1: Data Collection: Students will formulate questions to collect, organize, and represent data.
NE.M5.D.2: Analyze Data and Interpret Results: Students will analyze the data and interpret the results.
NE.M5.D.2.a: Represent, analyze, and solve authentic problems using information presented in one or more tables or line plots including whole numbers and fractions.
NE.S5.3.1: Gather, analyze, and communicate evidence of structure and properties of matter.
NE.S5.3.1.a: Develop a model to describe that matter is made of particles too small to be seen.
NE.S5.3.1.b: Measure and graph quantities to provide evidence that regardless of the type of change that occurs when heating, cooling, or mixing substances, the total weight of matter is conserved.
NE.S5.3.1.c: Make observations and measurements to identify materials based on their properties.
NE.S5.3.1.d: Conduct an investigation to determine whether the mixing of two or more substances results in new substances.
NE.S5.8.2: Gather and analyze data to communicate understanding of matter and energy in organisms and ecosystems.
NE.S5.8.2.a: Use models to describe that energy in animals' food (used for body repair, growth, and motion and to maintain body warmth) was once energy from the sun.
NE.S5.8.2.b: Support an argument that plants get the materials they need for growth chiefly from air and water.
NE.S5.8.2.c: Develop a model to describe the movement of matter among plants, animals, decomposers, and the environment.
NE.S5.11.3: Gather and analyze data to communicate understanding of space systems: Earth's stars and solar system.
NE.S5.11.3.a: Support an argument that the gravitational force exerted by Earth on objects is directed down toward Earth's center.
NE.S5.11.3.b: Support an argument that differences in the apparent brightness of the sun compared to other stars is due to their relative distances from Earth.
NE.S5.11.3.c: Represent data in graphical displays to reveal patterns of daily changes in the length and direction of shadows, length of day and night, and the seasonal appearance of some stars in the night sky.
NE.S5.13.4: Gather and analyze data to communicate understanding of Earth's systems.
NE.S5.13.4.a: Develop a model using an example to describe ways the geosphere, biosphere, hydrosphere, and/or atmosphere interact.
NE.S5.13.4.b: Describe and graph the amounts of salt water and fresh water in various reservoirs to provide evidence about the distribution of water on Earth.
NE.S5.13.4.c: Obtain and combine information about ways individual communities use science ideas to protect the Earth's resources and environment.
NE.S5.13.4.d: Define a simple design problem that can be solved by applying scientific ideas about the conservation of fresh water on Earth.
NE.S5.13.4.e: Define a simple design problem reflecting a need or a want that includes specified criteria for success and constraints on materials, time, or cost.
NE.E6.RP.1: Determine the implied or explicit theme of a literary text and how it develops over the course of a text.
NE.E6.RP.2: Explain how a plot unfolds as well as how the characters respond to events or changes as the plot moves toward a resolution.
NE.E6.RP.3: Explain how an author establishes and conveys the point(s) of view of a narrator or speaker in a literary text.
NE.E6.RP.4: Analyze how a sequence of chapters, scenes, or stanzas contribute to the development of literary elements (e.g. theme, setting, or plot).
NE.E6.RP.5: Compare and contrast texts in different forms or genres (e.g., stories and poems, historical novels, fantasy stories) and their treatment of similar themes and topics.
NE.E6.RP.6: Analyze a literary text to answer and develop inferential and evaluative questions to enhance the comprehension of self and others, quoting or paraphrasing specific evidence from the text.
NE.E6.RP.7: Compare and contrast regional, national, and/or multicultural perspectives within and across literary texts.
NE.E6.RP.8: Read and comprehend a wide range of literary text of appropriate complexity for the 6-8 grade band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.
NE.E6.RI.1: Determine the implied or explicit central idea of an informational text and how it develops over the course of a text.
NE.E6.RI.2: Explain how a key individual, event, or idea or concept is introduced and developed, drawing on specific supporting details in an informational text.
NE.E6.RI.3: Explain how an author establishes and conveys a perspective or purpose in an informational text.
NE.E6.RI.4: Analyze how a particular sentence, paragraph, chapter, or section fits into the overall structure of a text and contributes to the development of the ideas.
NE.E6.RI.5: Compare and contrast one author's presentation of information with that of another.
NE.E6.RI.6: Analyze the development of an argument and identify the type(s) of reasoning used to support the argument.
NE.E6.RI.7: Compare and contrast regional, national, and/or multicultural perspectives within and across informational texts.
NE.E6.RI.8: Read and comprehend a wide range of informational texts of appropriate complexity for the 6-8 grade band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.
NE.E6.V.1: Integrate grade-level academic vocabulary appropriately for a variety of tasks and purposes.
NE.E6.V.1.a: Use context clues (e.g. the overall meaning of a sentence or paragraph; a word's position or function in a sentence) to determine the meanings of words and phrases.
NE.E6.V.1.b: Use commonly occurring Greek and Latin affixes and roots to determine the meanings of words (e.g., audience, audible).
NE.E6.V.1.c: Consult reference materials to determine or clarify the precise meanings, pronunciations, or parts of speech of words.
NE.E6.V.2: Interpret an author's use of figurative, connotative, and technical language in grade-level literary and informational text.
NE.E6.V.2.a: Interpret figures of speech (e.g., literary, biblical, or mythological allusions) in context.
NE.E6.V.2.b: Determine the relationship between words (e.g., cause/effect, part/whole, item/category).
NE.E6.V.2.c: Distinguish between the connotations of words with similar denotations (e.g., economical, thrifty).
NE.E6.W.1: Create grammatically correct multi-paragraph compositions with varied sentence structures.
NE.E6.W.1.a: Apply knowledge of rules for capitalization.
NE.E6.W.1.b: Use punctuation (e.g., commas, parentheses, dashes) to set off non-restrictive clauses.
NE.E6.W.1.c: Use a colon to introduce items in a series; use a semicolon to combine independent clauses.
NE.E6.W.1.d: Explain the function of articles (e.g., definite and indefinite) and apply knowledge to writing.
NE.E6.W.1.e: Identify and use verb tenses (e.g., progressive).
NE.E6.W.1.f: Distinguish between and use different types of phrases (e.g., prepositional and appositive).
NE.E6.W.1.g: Identify and revise fragment and run-on sentences and inappropriate shifts in verb tenses.
NE.E6.W.2: Use a recursive writing process to develop, strengthen, and produce writing appropriate to the audience, purpose, and discipline.
NE.E6.W.2.a: Use prewriting activities and inquiry tools to plan, organize, and draft writing.
NE.E6.W.2.b: Adapt writing processes to sustain engagement in short and long-term writing tasks of increasing length and complexity.
NE.E6.W.2.c: Improve and clarify the content, structure, and organization of writing by revising, considering feedback from adults and peers.
NE.E6.W.2.d: Improve and clarify writing by editing and proofreading, considering feedback from adults and peers.
NE.E6.W.2.e: Use appropriate print and digital/multimedia tools to produce, enhance, and/or publish writing individually or in collaboration with peers.
NE.E6.W.3: Write in a variety of literary forms to convey real or imagined experiences or events in which the development and structure are appropriate to the task, purpose, and audience.
NE.E6.W.3.a: Engage and orient the reader by establishing a context and introducing a narrator and/or character(s) and point of view; organize an event sequence that unfolds naturally and logically.
NE.E6.W.3.b: Use literary techniques (e.g. dialogue, pacing, description) to develop characters, events, settings, and conflicts.
NE.E6.W.3.c: Use a variety of transitional words and phrases to signal shifts from one character, time frame, or setting to another.
NE.E6.W.3.d: Use precise words and phrases, descriptive/sensory details, and figurative language to express personal or narrative voice.
NE.E6.W.3.e: Provide a conclusion that is clearly related to and appropriately reflects on the literary experiences or events.
NE.E6.W.4: Write arguments that explain a perspective with supporting reasons and evidence.
NE.E6.W.4.a: Introduce a claim clearly and develop a structure in which the ideas are grouped logically.
NE.E6.W.4.b: Use relevant evidence from two or more credible sources.
NE.E6.W.4.c: Use words, phrases, and key vocabulary to clarify the relationship between claim(s) and supporting evidence.
NE.E6.W.4.d: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from the argument presented.
NE.E6.W.5: Write informative/explanatory pieces to examine a topic or text and clearly convey ideas and information.
NE.E6.W.5.a: Introduce a topic clearly and provide a general focus, grouping information logically and including text features, illustrations, and/or multimedia elements.
NE.E6.W.5.b: Develop a topic with information (e.g., facts, definitions, concrete details, quotations, examples) related to the topic.
NE.E6.W.5.c: Use appropriate transitions and key vocabulary to clarify relationships among ideas and concepts.
NE.E6.W.5.d: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from the information or explanation(s).
NE.E6.W.6: Gather and use credible evidence from trustworthy sources and assess its relevance in answering a research question.
NE.E6.W.6.a: Paraphrase and quote evidence to support ideas while avoiding plagiarism.
NE.E6.W.6.b: Locate and evaluate credibility of evidence (e.g., motivation and/or potential bias of an information product) from print and digital sources to generate and answer questions and create new understandings.
NE.E6.W.6.c: Select and use appropriate note-taking formats to collect and organize information.
NE.E6.W.6.d: Demonstrate academic integrity by avoiding overreliance on any one source and referencing sources in writing and speaking; provide a list of sources using a standard format.
NE.E6.W.6.e: Practice safe and ethical behaviors when communicating and interacting with others digitally (e.g., safe information to share, utilize appropriate sites and materials, appropriate language use, respect diverse perspectives).
NE.E6.SL.1: Prepare for and participate in structured discussions and collaborations about 6th grade topics and texts.
NE.E6.SL.1.a: Ask relevant questions to build on ideas, clarify own ideas, or acquire or confirm information.
NE.E6.SL.1.b: Demonstrate interpretation of verbal and non-verbal messages in a conversation.
NE.E6.SL.1.c: Converse with diverse individuals in an all-inclusive manner to foster positive relationships while respecting diverse perspectives.
NE.E6.SL.1.d: Demonstrate active and attentive listening skills (e.g., eye contact, nonverbal cues, taking notes, summarizing, questioning).
NE.E6.SL.1.e: Complete a task following multi-step directions.
NE.E6.SL.2: Present claims and findings, sequencing ideas logically and using relevant descriptions, facts, and details to clarify themes or central ideas.
NE.E6.SL.2.a: Demonstrate and adjust speaking techniques (e.g., appropriate eye contact, pacing, adequate volume, clear pronunciation) for a variety of purposes and situations, including interpreting 6th grade texts.
NE.E6.SL.2.b: Convey a perspective with clear reasoning and support.
NE.E6.SL.2.c: Analyze the purpose and credibility of information being presented.
NE.E6.SL.2.d: Demonstrate awareness of and sensitivity to the appropriate use of words (e.g., stereotypes, connotations, subtleties of language).
NE.E6.SL.2.e: Use appropriate visual and/or digital tools to enhance verbal communication and add interest.
NE.M6.N.1: Numeric Relationships: Students will demonstrate, represent, and show relationships among fractions, decimals, percents, and integers within the base-ten number system.
NE.M6.N.1.a: Determine common factors and common multiples.
NE.M6.N.1.b: Determine prime factorization of numbers with and without exponents.
NE.M6.N.1.c: Model integers using drawings, words, number lines, models, and symbols.
NE.M6.N.1.d: Determine absolute value of rational numbers.
NE.M6.N.1.e: Compare and order numbers including non-negative fractions and decimals, integers, and absolute values and locate them on the number line.
NE.M6.N.2: Operations: Students will compute with fractions and decimals accurately.
NE.M6.N.2.a: Divide multi-digit whole numbers and decimals using an algorithm.
NE.M6.N.2.b: Divide non-negative fractions and mixed numbers.
NE.M6.N.2.c: Evaluate numerical expressions including absolute value and/or positive exponents with respect to order of operations.
NE.M6.R.1: Ratios and Rates: Students will understand the concept of ratios and unit rates, use language to describe the relationship between two quantities, and use ratios and unit rates to solve authentic situations.
NE.M6.R.1.a: Determine ratios from concrete models, drawings, and/or words.
NE.M6.R.1.c: Find a percent of a quantity as a rate per `100` and solve problems involving finding the whole, given a part and the percent.
NE.M6.R.1.d: Convert among fractions, decimals, and percents using multiple representations.
NE.M6.R.1.e: Solve authentic problems using ratios, unit rates, and percents.
NE.M6.R.1.f: Use ratio reasoning to convert measurement units; manipulate and transform units appropriately when multiplying or dividing quantities.
NE.M6.R.2: Represent: Students will represent ratios and rates on the coordinate plane.
NE.M6.R.2.a: Identify the ordered pair of a given point in the coordinate plane.
NE.M6.R.2.b: Plot the location of an ordered pair in the coordinate plane.
NE.M6.R.2.c: Identify the location of a given point in the coordinate plane (e.g., axis, origin, quadrant).
NE.M6.R.2.d: Make tables of equivalent ratios relating quantities with whole number measurements.
NE.M6.R.2.e: Use the constant of proportionality to find the missing value in ratio tables.
NE.M6.R.2.f: Plot the pair of values from a ratio table on the coordinate plane.
NE.M6.R.2.g: Explain what a point `(x,y)` on the graph of a proportional relationship means in terms of the situation.
NE.M6.A.1: Algebraic Processes: Students will apply the operational properties when evaluating expressions and solving equations and inequalities.
NE.M6.A.1.a: Recognize and generate equivalent algebraic expressions involving the distributive property and combining like terms.
NE.M6.A.1.b: Given the value of the variable, evaluate algebraic expressions with non-negative rational numbers with respect to order of operations, which may include absolute value.
NE.M6.A.1.c: Use substitution to determine if a given value for a variable makes an equation or inequality true.
NE.M6.A.1.d: Solve one-step equations with non-negative rational numbers using addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division.
NE.M6.A.1.e: Solve one-step inequalities with whole numbers using addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division and represent solutions on a number line (e.g., graph 3x > 3).
NE.M6.A.2: Applications: Students will solve authentic problems with algebraic expressions, equations, and inequalities.
NE.M6.A.2.a: Create algebraic expressions (e.g., one operation, one variable as well as multiple operations, one variable) from word phrases.
NE.M6.A.2.b: Write equations (e.g., one operation, one variable) to represent authentic situations involving non-negative rational numbers.
NE.M6.A.2.c: Write inequalities (e.g., one operation, one variable) to represent authentic situations involving whole numbers.
NE.M6.G.1: Attributes: Students will identify and describe geometric attributes of two-dimensional shapes.
NE.M6.G.1.a: Identify and create nets to represent two-dimensional drawings of prisms and pyramids.
NE.M6.G.2: Coordinate Geometry: Students will determine location, orientation, and relationships on the coordinate plane.
NE.M6.G.3: Measurement: Students identify geometric attributes that create two- and three-dimensional shapes in order to perform measurements and apply formulas to find area and volume.
NE.M6.G.3.a: Determine the area of quadrilaterals and triangles by composition and decomposition of these shapes, as well as applications of properties and formulas. Quadrilaterals include parallelograms and trapezoids.
NE.M6.G.3.b: Determine the surface area of rectangular prisms and triangular prisms using nets as well as application of formulas.
NE.M6.G.3.c: Apply volume formulas for triangular prisms.
NE.M6.D.1: Data Collection and Statistical Methods: Students will formulate statistical investigative questions, collect data, and organize data.
NE.M6.D.2: 6.D.2 Analyze Data and Interpret Results: Students will represent and analyze the data and interpret the results.
NE.M6.D.2.a: Represent data using dot plots, box-and-whisker plots, and histograms.
NE.M6.D.2.b: Solve problems using information presented in dot plots, box-and-whisker plots, histograms, and circle graphs.
NE.M6.D.2.c: Find and interpret the mean, median, mode, and range for a set of data.
NE.M6.D.2.d: Compare the mean, median, mode, and range from two sets of data.
NE.M6.D.2.e: Compare and interpret data sets based upon their measures of central tendency and graphical representations (e.g., center, spread, shape).
NE.M6.D.3: Probability: Students will interpret and apply concepts of probability.
NE.M6.D.3.a: Identify a list of possible outcomes for a simple event.
NE.M6.D.3.b: Describe the theoretical and experimental probability of an event using a fraction, percentage, and decimal.
NE.M6.D.3.c: Express the degree of likelihood (possible, impossible, certain, more likely, equally likely, or less likely) of simple events.
NE.M6.D.3.d: Compare and contrast theoretical and experimental probabilities.
NE.S6.4.1: Gather, analyze, and communicate evidence of energy.
NE.S6.4.1.a: Apply scientific principles to design, construct, and test a device that either minimizes or maximizes thermal energy transfer.
NE.S6.4.1.b: Define the criteria and constraints of a design problem with sufficient precision to ensure a successful solution, taking into account relevant scientific principle and potential impacts on people and the natural environment that may limit possible solutions.
NE.S6.4.1.c: Plan an investigation to determine the relationships among the energy transferred, type of matter, mass, and change in average kinetic energy of particles as measured by the temperature of the sample.
NE.S6.4.1.d: Construct, use, and present arguments to support the claim that when kinetic energy of an object changes, energy is transferred to or from the object.
NE.S6.6.2: Gather, analyze, and communicate evidence of the relationship between structure and function in living things.
NE.S6.6.2.a: Conduct an investigation to provide evidence that living things are made of cells; either one cell or many varied cells.
NE.S6.6.2.b: Develop and use a model to describe the function of a cell as a whole and ways parts of a cell contribute to the function.
NE.S6.6.2.c: Use argument supported by evidence for how the body is a system of interacting subsystems composed of groups of cells.
NE.S6.6.2.d: Gather and synthesize information that sensory receptors respond to stimuli by sending messages to the brain for immediate behavior or stored as memories.
NE.S6.9.3: Gather, analyze, and communicate evidence of the inheritance and variation of traits.
NE.S6.9.3.a: Construct an argument based on evidence for how plant and animal adaptations affect the probability of successful reproduction.
NE.S6.9.3.b: Construct a scientific explanation based on evidence for how environmental and genetic factors influence the growth of organisms.
NE.S6.9.3.c: Develop and use a model to describe why asexual reproduction results in offspring with identical genetic information and sexual reproduction results in offspring with genetic variation.
NE.S6.12.4: Gather, analyze, and communicate evidence of factors and interactions that affect weather and climate.
NE.S6.12.4.a: Collect data to provide evidence for how the motions and complex interactions of air masses result in changes in weather conditions.
NE.S6.12.4.b: Develop and use a model to describe how unequal heating and rotation of the Earth cause patterns of atmospheric and oceanic circulation that determine regional climates.
NE.S6.12.4.c: Ask questions to clarify evidence of the factors that have caused the change in global temperatures over thousands of years.
NE.S6.12.4.d: Analyze and interpret data on weather and climate to forecast future catastrophic events and inform the development of technologies to mitigate their effect.
NE.S6.13.5: Gather, analyze, and communicate evidence of the flow of energy and cycling of matter associated with Earth's materials and processes.
NE.S6.13.5.a: Develop a model to describe how the water cycle is driven by the sun's energy and the force of gravity.
NE.E7.RP.1: Determine two or more implied or explicit themes in a literary text and how they are supported with key details.
NE.E7.RP.2: Analyze how particular events, lines of dialogue, or descriptive details develop the plot, reveal aspects of characters, or create meaning.
NE.E7.RP.3: Analyze how an author establishes, conveys, and contrasts the points of view of different characters or narrators in a literary text.
NE.E7.RP.4: Analyze the structure of a literary text, and how the structure contributes to its theme(s) and meaning.
NE.E7.RP.5: Compare and contrast a fictional portrayal of a time, place, or character and a historical account of the same period.
NE.E7.RP.6: Synthesize the implied or stated theme(s) in a literary text to draw conclusions and deepen understanding of self and others.
NE.E7.RP.7: Compare and contrast regional, national, and/or multicultural perspectives by explaining how an author or narrator/speaker introduces, illustrates, or describes characters or individuals, events, and ideas within and across literary texts.
NE.E7.RP.8: Read and comprehend a wide range of literary texts of appropriate complexity for the 6-8 grade band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.
NE.E7.RI.1: Determine two or more implied or explicit central ideas of an informational text and how they are supported with key details.
NE.E7.RI.2: Analyze the relationships and interactions between individuals, events, and/or ideas or concepts, drawing on specific supporting details in an informational text.
NE.E7.RI.3: Analyze how an author establishes or conveys a perspective or purpose and distinguishes it from that of others.
NE.E7.RI.4: Analyze how the major sections of text contribute to the development of ideas in an informational text.
NE.E7.RI.5: Compare and contrast how two or more authors provide conflicting information on the same topic, including where the texts disagree on matters of evidence or interpretation.
NE.E7.RI.6: Analyze the development of an argument and identify the type(s) of reasoning used to support the argument.
NE.E7.RI.7: Compare and contrast regional, national, and/or multicultural perspectives by explaining how an author or narrator/speaker introduces, illustrates, or describes characters or individuals, events, and ideas within and across informational texts.
NE.E7.RI.8: Read and comprehend a wide range of informational texts of appropriate complexity for the 6-8 grade band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.
NE.E7.V.1: Integrate grade-level academic vocabulary appropriately for a variety of tasks and purposes.
NE.E7.V.1.a: Use context clues (e.g., the overall meaning of a sentence or paragraph; a word's position or function in a sentence) to determine the meanings of words and phrases.
NE.E7.V.1.b: Use commonly occurring Greek and Latin affixes and roots to determine the meanings of words (e.g., audience, audible).
NE.E7.V.1.c: Consult general and specialized reference materials to determine or clarify the precise meanings, pronunciations, or parts of speech of words.
NE.E7.V.2: Interpret an author's use of figurative, connotative, and technical language in grade-level literary and informational text.
NE.E7.V.2.a: Interpret figures of speech (e.g., literary, biblical, or mythological allusions) in context.
NE.E7.V.2.b: Determine the relationship between words (e.g., cause/effect, part/whole, item/category).
NE.E7.V.2.c: Distinguish between the connotations of words with similar denotations (e.g., polite, diplomatic).
NE.E7.W.1: Create grammatically correct multi-paragraph compositions with varied sentence structures.
NE.E7.W.1.a: Apply knowledge of rules for capitalization.
NE.E7.W.1.b: b. Use a comma to separate coordinate adjectives.
NE.E7.W.1.c: Distinguish between and use types of clauses (e.g., noun, relative, adverbial), modifiers (e.g., misplaced and dangling), and adjectives (coordinate and cumulative).
NE.E7.W.1.d: Use a variety of prepositional and appositive phrases in sentences and paragraphs.
NE.E7.W.1.e: Identify and revise fragment and run-on sentences and inappropriate shifts in verb tenses.
NE.E7.W.2: Use a recursive writing process to develop, strengthen, and produce writing appropriate to the audience, purpose, and discipline.
NE.E7.W.2.a: Use prewriting activities and inquiry tools to plan, organize, and draft writing.
NE.E7.W.2.b: Adapt writing processes to sustain engagement in short and long-term writing tasks of increasing length and complexity.
NE.E7.W.2.c: Improve and clarify the content, structure, and organization of writing by revising, considering feedback from adults and peers.
NE.E7.W.2.d: Improve and clarify writing by editing and proofreading, considering feedback from adults and peers.
NE.E7.W.2.e: Use appropriate print and digital/multimedia tools to produce, enhance, and/or publish writing individually or in collaboration with peers.
NE.E7.W.3: Write in a variety of literary forms to convey real or imagined experiences or events in which the development and structure are appropriate to the task, purpose, and audience.
NE.E7.W.3.a: Engage and orient the reader by establishing a context and introducing a narrator and/or character(s), establishing and maintaining a point of view, and organizing an event sequence that unfolds naturally and logically.
NE.E7.W.3.b: Use literary techniques (e.g., dialogue, pacing, description) to develop characters, events, settings, and conflicts.
NE.E7.W.3.c: Use a variety of transitional words and phrases to signal shifts from one character, time frame, or setting to another.
NE.E7.W.3.d: Use precise words and phrases, descriptive/sensory details, and figurative language to express personal or narrative voice.
NE.E7.W.3.e: Provide a conclusion that is clearly related to and appropriately reflects on the literary experiences or events.
NE.E7.W.4: Write arguments that develop a perspective with supporting reasons and evidence, organized as appropriate to the task, purpose, and audience.
NE.E7.W.4.a: Develop a structure to sequence ideas appropriately; introduce a clear claim where appropriate.
NE.E7.W.4.b: Explain and cite relevant evidence from multiple credible sources.
NE.E7.W.4.c: Use words, phrases, and key vocabulary to create cohesion and clarify the relationship between claim(s) and supporting evidence.
NE.E7.W.4.d: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the argument(s) presented.
NE.E7.W.5: Write informative/explanatory pieces to examine a topic or text and clearly convey ideas and information.
NE.E7.W.5.a: Introduce a topic clearly and provide a specific focus, grouping information logically and including text features, illustrations, and/or multimedia elements.
NE.E7.W.5.b: Develop a topic with information (e.g., facts, definitions, concrete details, quotations, examples) related to the topic.
NE.E7.W.5.c: Use appropriate transitions and key vocabulary to clarify relationships among ideas and concepts.
NE.E7.W.5.d: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from the information or explanation(s).
NE.E7.W.6: Gather and use credible evidence from multiple trustworthy sources and assess its relevance in answering the research question.
NE.E7.W.6.a: Integrate evidence into writing by quoting or paraphrasing data and conclusions while avoiding plagiarism.
NE.E7.W.6.b: Locate and evaluate the credibility of evidence (e.g., motivation and/or potential bias of an information product) from print and digital sources to generate and answer questions and create new understandings.
NE.E7.W.6.c: Select and use appropriate note-taking formats to collect and organize information.
NE.E7.W.6.d: Demonstrate academic integrity by avoiding overreliance on any one source and citing sources within text (e.g., parenthetical and numerical); provide a list of sources using a standard format.
NE.E7.W.6.e: Practice safe and ethical behaviors when communicating and interacting with others digitally (e.g., safe information to share, utilize appropriate sites and materials, appropriate language use, respect diverse perspectives).
NE.E7.SL.1: Prepare for and participate in structured discussions and collaborations about 7th grade topics and texts.
NE.E7.SL.1.a: Ask relevant questions to build on ideas, clarify own ideas, or acquire or confirm information.
NE.E7.SL.1.b: Demonstrate interpretation of verbal and non-verbal messages in a conversation.
NE.E7.SL.1.c: Converse with peers and adults in an all-inclusive manner to foster positive relationships while respecting diverse perspectives.
NE.E7.SL.1.d: Demonstrate active and attentive listening skills (e.g., eye contact, nonverbal cues, taking notes, summarizing, questioning).
NE.E7.SL.1.e: Complete a task following multi-step directions.
NE.E7.SL.2: Present claims and findings, emphasizing key ideas in a focused, coherent manner with relevant descriptions, facts, details, and examples to clarify themes or central ideas.
NE.E7.SL.2.a: Demonstrate and adjust speaking techniques (e.g., appropriate eye contact, pacing, adequate volume, clear pronunciation) for a variety of purposes and situations, including interpreting 7th grade texts.
NE.E7.SL.2.b: Convey a perspective with clear reasoning and valid evidence.
NE.E7.SL.2.c: Analyze the purpose and credibility of information being presented.
NE.E7.SL.2.d: Demonstrate awareness of and sensitivity to the appropriate use of words (e.g., stereotypes, multiple meanings of words).
NE.E7.SL.2.e: Use appropriate visual and/or digital tools to enhance verbal communication and add interest.
NE.M7.N.1: Numeric Relationships: Students will demonstrate, represent, and show relationships among rational numbers within the base-ten number system.
NE.M7.N.2: Operations: Students will compute with rational numbers accurately.
NE.M7.N.2.a: Add, subtract, multiply, and divide rational numbers (e.g., positive and negative fractions, decimals, and integers).
NE.M7.N.2.b: Apply properties of operations (commutative, associative, distributive, identity, inverse, zero) as strategies for problem solving with rational numbers.
NE.M7.R.1: Proportional Relationships: Students will understand the concept of proportions, use language to describe the relationship between two quantities, and use proportions to solve authentic situations.
NE.M7.R.1.a: Decide whether two quantities are in a proportional relationship (e.g., by testing for equivalent ratios in a table).
NE.M7.R.1.b: Represent and solve authentic problems with proportions.
NE.M7.R.1.c: Use proportional relationships to solve authentic percent problems (e.g., percent change, sales tax, mark-up, discount, tip.)
NE.M7.R.1.d: Solve authentic problems involving scale drawings.
NE.M7.A.1: Algebraic Processes: Students will apply the operational properties when evaluating expressions, and solving equations and inequalities.
NE.M7.A.1.a: Use factoring and properties of operations to create equivalent algebraic expressions (e.g., 2x + 6 = 2(x + 3)).
NE.M7.A.1.b: Given the value of the variable(s), evaluate algebraic expressions, which may include absolute value.
NE.M7.A.1.c: Solve one- and two-step equations involving rational numbers.
NE.M7.A.1.d: Solve equations using the distributive property and combining like terms.
NE.M7.A.1.e: Solve one- and two-step inequalities involving integers and represent solutions on a number line.
NE.M7.A.2: Applications: Students will solve authentic problems with algebraic expressions, equations, and inequalities.
NE.M7.A.2.a: Write one- and two-step equations involving rational numbers from words, tables, and authentic situations.
NE.M7.A.2.b: Write one- and two-step inequalities to represent authentic situations involving integers.
NE.M7.G.1: Attributes: Students will identify angle relationships and apply properties to determine angle measures.
NE.M7.G.1.a: Apply properties of adjacent, complementary, supplementary, linear pair, and vertical angles to find missing angle measures.
NE.M7.G.2: Coordinate Geometry: Students will determine location, orientation, and relationships on the coordinate plane.
NE.M7.G.2.a: Draw polygons in the coordinate plane given coordinates for the vertices.
NE.M7.G.2.b: Calculate vertical and horizontal distances in the coordinate plane to find perimeter and area of rectangles.
NE.M7.G.3: Measurement: Students will identify geometric attributes that create two- and three-dimensional shapes in order to perform measurements and apply formulas to find area and volume.
NE.M7.G.3.a: Solve authentic problems involving perimeter and area of composite shapes made from triangles and quadrilaterals.
NE.M7.G.3.b: Determine surface area and volume of composite rectangular and triangular prisms.
NE.M7.G.3.c: Determine the area and circumference of circles both on and off the coordinate plane using 3.14 for the value of Pi.
NE.M7.D.1: Data Collection and Statistical Methods: Students will formulate statistical investigative questions, collect data, and organize data.
NE.M7.D.1.a: Create an investigative question and collect data.
NE.M7.D.1.b: Generate conclusions about a population based on a random sample.
NE.M7.D.1.c: Identify and critique biases in various data representations.
NE.M7.D.2: Analyze Data and Interpret Results: Students will represent and analyze the data and interpret the results.
NE.M7.D.3: Probability: Students will interpret and apply concepts of probability.
NE.M7.D.3.a: Find theoretical and experimental probabilities for compound independent and dependent events.
NE.M7.D.3.b: Identify complementary events and calculate their probabilities.
NE.S7.3.1: Gather, analyze, and communicate evidence of the structure, properties, and interactions of matter.
NE.S7.3.1.a: Develop models to describe the atomic composition of simple molecules.
NE.S7.3.1.b: Gather and make sense of information to describe how natural materials may undergo chemical reactions to create new synthetic materials and have an impact on society.
NE.S7.3.1.c: Develop a model that predicts and describes changes in particle motion, temperature, and state of a pure substance when thermal energy is added or removed.
NE.S7.5.2: Gather, analyze, and communicate evidence of chemical reactions.
NE.S7.5.2.a: Analyze and interpret data on the properties of substances before and after the substances interact to determine if a chemical reaction has occurred.
NE.S7.5.2.b: Develop and use a model to describe how the total number of atoms does not change in a chemical reaction and thus mass is conserved.
NE.S7.5.2.c: Undertake a design project to construct, test, and modify a device that either releases or absorbs thermal energy by chemical processes.
NE.S7.5.2.d: Analyze data from tests to determine similarities and differences among several design solutions to identify the best characteristics of each that can be combined into a new solution to better meet the criteria for success.
NE.S7.7.3: Gather, analyze, and communicate evidence of interdependent relationships in ecosystems.
NE.S7.7.3.a: Construct an explanation that predicts patterns of interactions among organisms across multiple ecosystems.
NE.S7.7.3.b: Develop and use a model to describe how stable ecosystems maintain biodiversity and ecosystem services.
NE.S7.7.3.c: Evaluate competing design solutions using a systematic process to determine how well they meet the criteria and constraints of the problem.
NE.S7.7.3.d: Apply scientific principles to design a method for monitoring and increasing positive human impact on the environment.
NE.S7.8.4: Gather, analyze, and communicate evidence of the flow of energy and cycling of matter in organisms and ecosystems.
NE.S7.8.4.a: Construct a scientific explanation based on evidence for the role of photosynthesis in the cycling of matter and flow of energy into and out of organisms.
NE.S7.8.4.b: Develop a model to describe how food is rearranged through chemical reactions forming new molecules that support growth and/or release energy as matter moves through an organism.
NE.S7.8.4.c: Analyze and interpret data to provide evidence for the effects of resource availability on organisms and populations of organisms in an ecosystem.
NE.S7.8.4.d: Develop a model to describe the cycling of matter and flow of energy among living and nonliving parts of an ecosystem.
NE.S7.8.4.e: Construct an argument supported by evidence that changes to physical or biological components of an ecosystem affect populations.
NE.S7.13.5: Gather, analyze, and communicate evidence of the flow of energy and cycling of matter associated with Earth's materials and processes.
NE.S7.13.5.a: Develop a model to describe the cycling of Earth's materials and the flow of energy that drives this process.
NE.S7.13.5.b: Construct a scientific explanation based on evidence for how the uneven distributions of Earth's mineral, energy, and groundwater resources are the result of past and current geoscience processes.
NE.S7.13.5.c: Construct an argument supported by evidence for how increases in human population and per-capita consumption of natural resources impact Earth's systems.
NE.S7.14.6: Gather, analyze, and communicate evidence to explain Earth's history.
NE.S7.14.6.a: Construct an explanation based on evidence for how geoscience processes have changed Earth's surface at varying time and spatial scales.
NE.S7.14.6.b: Analyze and interpret data on the distribution of fossils and rocks, continental shapes, and seafloor structures to provide evidence of past plate motions.
NE.S7.14.6.c: Analyze and interpret data on geologic hazards to forecast future catastrophic events and inform the development of technologies to mitigate their effects.
NE.E8.RP.1: Determine two or more implied or explicit themes of a text and how they develop over the course of a literary text, including their relationship to supporting ideas.
NE.E8.RP.2: Analyze how particular events, lines of dialogue, or descriptive details develop the plot, reveal aspects of characters, or create meaning.
