NJ.E3.L.KL.1: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening.
NJ.E3.L.KL.1.A: Acquire and use accurately grade-appropriate conversational, general academic, and domain-specific words and phrases.
NJ.E3.L.KL.1.B: Choose words and phrases for effect.
NJ.E3.L.KL.1.C: Recognize and observe differences between the conventions of spoken and written English.
NJ.E3.L.VL.2: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning academic and domain-specific words and phrases based on grade 3 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.
NJ.E3.L.VL.2.A: Use sentence-level context as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.
NJ.E3.L.VL.2.B: Determine the meaning of the new word formed when a known affix is added to a known word (e.g., agreeable/disagreeable, comfortable/uncomfortable, care/careless, heat/ preheat).
NJ.E3.L.VL.2.C: Use a known root word as a clue to the meaning of an unknown word with the same root (e.g., company, companion).
NJ.E3.L.VL.2.D: Use glossaries or beginning dictionaries, both print and digital, to determine or clarify the precise meaning of key words and phrases.
NJ.E3.L.VI.3: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships and nuances in word meanings.
NJ.E3.L.VI.3.A: Distinguish the literal and nonliteral meanings of words and phrases in context (e.g., take steps).
NJ.E3.L.VI.3.B: Identify real-life connections between words and their use (e.g., describe people who are friendly or helpful).
NJ.E3.L.VI.3.C: Distinguish shades of meaning among related words that describe states of mind or degrees of certainty (e.g., knew, believed, suspected, heard, wondered).
NJ.E3.R.RL.CR.1: Ask and answer questions and make relevant connections to demonstrate understanding of a literary text, referring explicitly to textual evidence as the basis for the answers.
NJ.E3.R.RL.CI.2: Recount in oral and written form key details from a text and explain how they support the theme (in literary texts, e.g., fables, folktales, and myths from diverse cultures).
NJ.E3.R.RL.IT.3: Describe the development of individual character's traits, motivations, or feelings and explain how their actions contribute to the plot within a text.
NJ.E3.R.RL.TS.4: Utilize and reference features of a text when writing or speaking about a text, referring to parts of stories, dramas, and poems, using terms such as chapter, scene, and stanza; describe how each successive part builds on earlier sections.
NJ.E3.R.RL.PP.5: Distinguish their own point of view from that of the narrator or those of the characters.
NJ.E3.R.RL.MF.6: Explain how specific aspects of a text's illustrations contribute to what is conveyed by the words in a story (e.g., create mood, emphasize aspects of a character or setting).
NJ.E3.R.RL.CT.8: Compare and contrast the elements (theme, settings, and plots) of literary texts written by the same author about similar characters (e.g., in books from a series).
NJ.E3.R.RI.CR.1: Ask and answer questions and make relevant connections to demonstrate understanding of an informational text, referring explicitly to textual evidence as the basis for the answers.
NJ.E3.R.RI.CI.2: Recount in oral and written form the key details from a multi-paragraph informational text and explain how they support the main idea.
NJ.E3.R.RI.IT.3: Describe the relationship between a series of historical events, scientific ideas or concepts, or steps in technical procedures in a text, using language that pertains to time, sequence, and cause/effect.
NJ.E3.R.RI.TS.4: Utilize and reference features of a text when writing or speaking about a text, using text features (e.g., graphics, images, captions, headings) and search tools (e.g., key words, sidebars, hyperlinks) to locate and integrate information relevant to a given topic efficiently.
NJ.E3.R.RI.PP.5: Distinguish their own point of view from that of the author of a text.
NJ.E3.R.RI.MF.6: Use information gained from text features (e.g., illustrations, maps, photographs) and the words in a text to demonstrate understanding of the text (e.g., where, when, why, and how key events occur).
NJ.E3.R.RI.AA.7: Describe the logical connection between particular sentences and paragraphs in a text (e.g., comparison, cause/effect, first/second/third in a sequence) to support specific points the author makes in a text.
NJ.E3.R.RI.CT.8: Compare and contrast the elements of informational texts regarding the most important points and key details presented in two texts on the same topic.
NJ.E3.W.AW.1: Write opinion texts to present an idea with reasons and information.
NJ.E3.W.AW.1.B: Support the opinion with facts, definitions, reasons text evidence, or other information and examples related to the topic.
NJ.E3.W.AW.1.C: Link ideas within sections of information using transition words and phrases (e.g., then, because, also, therefore, since, for example) to connect opinion and reasons.
NJ.E3.W.AW.1.D: Provide a conclusion related to the opinion presented.
NJ.E3.W.IW.2: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine a topic and convey ideas and information clearly.
NJ.E3.W.IW.2.B: Develop the topic with facts, definitions, and concrete details, text evidence, or other information and examples related to the topic.
NJ.E3.W.IW.2.C: Include text features (e.g.: illustrations, diagrams, captions) when useful to support comprehension.
NJ.E3.W.IW.2.D: Link ideas within sections of information using transition words and phrases (e.g., then, because, also, another, therefore).
NJ.E3.W.IW.2.E: Provide a conclusion related to the information or explanation presented.
NJ.E3.W.NW.3: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events with basic story elements.
NJ.E3.W.NW.3.A: Orient the reader by establishing a situation and introduce a narrator and/or characters; clearly organize an event sequence.
NJ.E3.W.NW.3.B: Use dialogue and description to develop experiences and events or show the responses of characters to situations.
NJ.E3.W.NW.3.C: Use transitional words and phrases to manage the sequence of events.
NJ.E3.W.NW.3.D: Use concrete words and phrases and sensory details to convey experiences and events.
NJ.E3.W.NW.3.E: Provide a conclusion or sense of closure that follows the narrated experiences or events.
NJ.E3.W.WP.4: With guidance and support from peers and adults, develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, and editing.
NJ.E3.W.WP.4.A: Identify audience, purpose, and intended length of composition before writing.
NJ.E3.W.WP.4.B: Consider writing as a process, including self-evaluation, revision and editing.
NJ.E3.W.WP.4.C: With adult and peer feedback, and digital or print tools such as a dictionary, thesaurus, and/or spell checker, find and correct errors and improve word choice.
NJ.E3.W.WR.5: Generate questions about a topic and independently locate related information from at least two reference sources (print and non-print) to obtain information on that topic.
NJ.E3.W.SE.6: Use discussion, books, or media resources to gather ideas, outline them, and prioritize the information to include while planning to write about a topic.
NJ.E3.W.RW.7: Engage in independent and task-based writing for both short and extended periods of time, producing written work routinely.
NJ.E3.SL.PE.1: Engage effectively in a range of collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in groups, and teacher led) with diverse partners on grade 3 topics and texts, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly.
NJ.E3.SL.PE.1.A: Explicitly draw on previously read text or material and other information known about the topic to explore ideas under discussion.
NJ.E3.SL.PE.1.B: Follow agreed-upon norms for discussions (e.g., gaining the floor in respectful ways, listening to others with care, speaking one at a time about the topics and texts under discussion).
NJ.E3.SL.PE.1.C: Ask questions to check understanding of information presented, stay on topic, and link their comments to the remarks of others.
NJ.E3.SL.PE.1.D: Explain their own ideas and understanding in light of the discussion.
NJ.E3.SL.II.2: Determine the main ideas and supporting details of a text read aloud or information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.
NJ.E3.SL.ES.3: Ask and answer questions about information from a speaker, offering appropriate elaboration and detail.
NJ.E3.SL.PI.4: Report on a topic or text, tell a story, or recount an experience with appropriate facts and relevant, descriptive details, speaking clearly at an understandable pace.
NJ.E3.SL.UM.5: Use multimedia to demonstrate fluid reading at an understandable pace; add visual displays when appropriate to emphasize or enhance certain facts or details.
NJ.E3.SL.AS.6: Speak in complete sentences when appropriate to task and situation in order to provide requested detail or clarification.
NJ.M3.OA.A: Represent and solve problems involving multiplication and division.
NJ.M3.OA.A.1: Interpret products of whole numbers, e.g., interpret as the total number of objects in 5 groups of 7 objects each.
NJ.M3.OA.A.2: Interpret whole-number quotients of whole numbers, e.g., interpret as the number of objects in each share when 56 objects are partitioned equally into 8 shares, or as a number of shares when 56 objects are partitioned into equal shares of 8 objects each.
NJ.M3.OA.A.3: Use multiplication and division within `100` to solve word problems in situations involving equal groups, arrays, and measurement quantities, e.g., by using drawings and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.
NJ.M3.OA.A.4: Determine the unknown whole number in a multiplication or division equation relating three whole numbers.
NJ.M3.OA.B: Understand properties of multiplication and the relationship between multiplication and division.
NJ.M3.OA.B.5: Apply properties of operations as strategies to multiply and divide.
NJ.M3.OA.B.6: Understand division as an unknown-factor problem.
NJ.M3.OA.C.7: With accuracy and efficiency, multiply and divide within `100`, using strategies such as the relationship between multiplication and division (e.g., knowing that, one knows) or properties of operations. By the end of Grade 3, know from memory all products of two one-digit numbers.
NJ.M3.OA.D: Solve problems involving the four operations, and identify and explain patterns in arithmetic.
NJ.M3.OA.D.8: Solve two-step word problems, including problems involving money, using the four operations. Represent these problems using equations with a letter standing for the unknown quantity. Assess the reasonableness of answers using mental computation and estimation strategies including rounding.
NJ.M3.OA.D.9: Identify arithmetic patterns (including patterns in the addition table or multiplication table) and explain them using properties of operations.
NJ.M3.NBT.A: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to perform multi-digit arithmetic.
NJ.M3.NBT.A.1: Use place value understanding to round whole numbers to the nearest `10or100`.
NJ.M3.NBT.A.2: With accuracy and efficiency, add and subtract within `1000` using strategies and algorithms based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction.
NJ.M3.NBT.A.3: Multiply one-digit whole numbers by multiples of `10` in the range `10-90` (e.g., `9xx80,5xx60`) using strategies based on place value and properties of operations.
NJ.M3.NF.A: Develop understanding of fractions as numbers.
NJ.M3.NF.A.1: Understand a fraction  as the quantity formed by `1` part when a whole is partitioned into `b` equal parts; understand a fraction  as the quantity formed by a parts of size.
NJ.M3.NF.A.2: Understand a fraction as a number on the number line; represent fractions on a number line diagram.
NJ.M3.NF.A.2.a: Represent a fraction  on a number line diagram by defining the interval from `0` to `1` as the whole and partitioning it into `b` equal parts. Recognize that each part has size and that the endpoint of the part based at 0 locates the number  on the number line.
NJ.M3.NF.A.2.b: Represent a fraction  on a number line diagram by marking off a lengths  from `0`. Recognize that the resulting interval has size  and that its endpoint locates the number on the number line.
NJ.M3.NF.A.3: Explain equivalence of fractions in special cases, and compare fractions by reasoning about their size.
NJ.M3.NF.A.3.a: Understand two fractions as equivalent (equal) if they are the same size. Understand two fractions as equivalent if they are located at the same point on a number line.
NJ.M3.NF.A.3.b: Recognize and generate simple equivalent fractions by reasoning about their size, (e.g., `1/2=2/4,4/6=2/3`). Explain why the fractions are equivalent with the support of a visual fraction model.
NJ.M3.NF.A.3.c: Express whole numbers as fractions, and recognize fractions that are equivalent to whole numbers.
NJ.M3.NF.A.3.d: Compare two fractions with the same numerator or the same denominator by reasoning about their size. Recognize that comparisons are valid only when the two fractions refer to the same whole. Record the results of comparisons with the symbols `>,=,or<`, and justify the conclusions with the support of a visual fraction model.
NJ.M3.MD.A: Solve problems involving measurement and estimation of intervals of time, liquid volumes, and masses of objects.
NJ.M3.MD.A.1: Tell and write time to the nearest minute and measure time intervals in `text(minutes)`. Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of time intervals in `text(minutes)`, e.g., by representing the problem on a number line diagram.
NJ.M3.MD.A.2: Measure and estimate liquid volumes and masses of objects using standard units of grams (g), kilograms (kg), and liters (l). Add, subtract, multiply, or divide to solve one-step word problems involving masses or volumes that are given in the same units, e.g., by using drawings (such as a beaker with a measurement scale) to represent the problem.
NJ.M3.MD.B.3: Draw a scaled picture graph and a scaled bar graph to represent a data set with several categories. Solve one- and two-step “how many more” and “how many less” problems using information presented in scaled bar graphs.
NJ.M3.MD.B.4: Generate measurement data by measuring lengths using rulers marked with `text(halves)andtext(fourths of an inch)`. Show the data by making a line plot, where the horizontal scale is marked off in appropriate units-`text(whole numbers),text(halves),ortext(quarters)`.
NJ.M3.MD.C: Geometric measurement: understand concepts of area and relate area to multiplication and to addition.
NJ.M3.MD.C.5: Recognize area as an attribute of plane figures and understand concepts of area measurement.
NJ.M3.MD.C.5.a: A square with side length`1` `text(unit)`, called “a unit square,” is said to have “one square unit” of area, and can be used to measure area.
NJ.M3.MD.C.5.b: A plane figure which can be covered without gaps or overlaps by  unit squares is said to have an area of  square units.
NJ.M3.MD.C.6: Measure areas by counting unit squares (`text(square cm),text(square m),text(square in),text(square ft)`, and non-standard units).
NJ.M3.MD.C.7: Relate area to the operations of multiplication and addition.
NJ.M3.MD.C.7.a: Find the area of a rectangle with whole-number side lengths by tiling it and show that the area is the same as would be found by multiplying the side lengths.
NJ.M3.MD.C.7.b: Multiply side lengths to find areas of rectangles with whole number side lengths in the context of solving real world and mathematical problems, and represent whole-number products as rectangular areas in mathematical reasoning.
NJ.M3.MD.C.7.c: Use tiling to show in a concrete case that the area of a rectangle with whole-number side lengths and is the sum of and. Use area models to represent the distributive property in mathematical reasoning.
NJ.M3.MD.C.7.d: Recognize area as additive. Find areas of rectilinear figures by decomposing them into non-overlapping rectangles and adding the areas of the non-overlapping parts, applying this technique to solve real world problems.
NJ.M3.MD.D: Geometric measurement: recognize perimeter as an attribute of plane figures and distinguish between linear and area measures.
NJ.M3.MD.D.8: Solve real world and mathematical problems involving perimeters of polygons, including finding the perimeter given the side lengths, finding an unknown side length, and exhibiting rectangles with the same perimeter and different areas or with the same area and different perimeters.
NJ.M3.G.A: Reason with shapes and their attributes.
NJ.M3.G.A.1: Understand that shapes in different categories (e.g., rhombuses, rectangles, and others) may share attributes (e.g., having four sides), and that the shared attributes can define a larger category (e.g., quadrilaterals). Recognize rhombuses, rectangles, and squares as examples of quadrilaterals, and draw examples of quadrilaterals that do not belong to any of these subcategories.
NJ.M3.G.A.2: Partition shapes into parts with equal areas. Express the area of each part as a unit fraction of the whole.
NJ.S3.PS.2.1: Plan and conduct an investigation to provide evidence of the effects of balanced and unbalanced forces on the motion of an object.
NJ.S3.PS.2.2: Make observations and/or measurements of an object's motion to provide evidence that a pattern can be used to predict future motion.
NJ.S3.PS.2.3: Ask questions to determine cause and effect relationships of electric or magnetic interactions between two objects not in contact with each other.
NJ.S3.PS.2.4: Define a simple design problem that can be solved by applying scientific ideas about magnets.
NJ.S3.LS.1: From Molecules To Organisms: Structures & Processes
NJ.S3.LS.1.1: Develop models to describe that organisms have unique and diverse life cycles, but all have in common birth, growth, reproduction, and death.
NJ.S3.LS.2.1: Construct an argument that some animals form groups that help members survive.
NJ.S3.LS.3.1: Analyze and interpret data to provide evidence that plants and animals have traits inherited from parents and that variation of these traits exists in a group of similar organisms.
NJ.S3.LS.3.2: Use evidence to support the explanation that traits can be influenced by the environment.
NJ.S3.LS.4.1: Analyze and interpret data from fossils to provide evidence of the organisms and the environments in which they lived long ago.
NJ.S3.LS.4.2: Use evidence to construct an explanation for how the variations in characteristics among individuals of the same species may provide advantages in surviving, finding mates, and reproducing.
NJ.S3.LS.4.3: Construct an argument with evidence that in a particular habitat some organisms can survive well, some survive less well, and some cannot survive at all.
NJ.S3.LS.4.4: Make a claim about the merit of a solution to a problem caused when the environment changes and the types of plants and animals that live there may change.
NJ.S3.ESS.2.1: Represent data in tables and graphical displays to describe typical weather conditions expected during a particular season.
NJ.S3.ESS.2.2: Obtain and combine information to describe climates in different regions of the world.
NJ.S3.ESS.3.1: Make a claim about the merit of a design solution that reduces the impacts of climate change and/or a weather-related hazard.
NJ.S3-5.ETS.1.1: Define a simple design problem reflecting a need or a want that includes specified criteria for success and constraints on materials, time, or cost.
NJ.S3-5.ETS.1.2: Generate and compare multiple possible solutions to a problem based on how well each is likely to meet the criteria and constraints of the problem.
NJ.S3-5.ETS.1.3: Plan and carry out fair tests in which variables are controlled and failure points are considered to identify aspects of a model or prototype that can be improved.
NJ.E4.L.RF.3: Know and apply grade-level phonics and word analysis skills in decoding and encoding words; use combined knowledge of all letter-sound correspondences, syllabication patterns, and morphology (e.g., roots and affixes) to read accurately unfamiliar multisyllabic words in context and out of context.
NJ.E4.L.RF.4: Read with sufficient accuracy and fluency to support comprehension.
NJ.E4.L.RF.4.A: Read grade-level text with purpose and understanding.
NJ.E4.L.RF.4.B: Read grade-level text orally with accuracy, appropriate rate, and expression.
NJ.E4.L.RF.4.C: Use context to confirm or self-correct word recognition and understanding, rereading as necessary.
NJ.E4.L.WF.2: Demonstrate command of the conventions of encoding and spelling.
NJ.E4.L.WF.2.A: Analyze and spell multi-syllable words with the most common Latin roots, prefixes, and suffixes.
NJ.E4.L.WF.2.B: Write affixed words that involve a sound or spelling change in the base word.
NJ.E4.L.WF.2.C: Spell grade-appropriate words correctly, consulting references as needed.
NJ.E4.L.WF.2.D: Consult reference materials (e.g., dictionaries, glossaries, thesauruses), both print and digital, to find the pronunciation and determine or clarify the precise meaning of key words and phrases.
NJ.E4.L.WF.3: Demonstrate command of the conventions of writing, including those listed under grade three foundational skills:
NJ.E4.L.WF.3.A: Use basic paragraphing, including using paragraph indentations and using paragraphs in dialogue.
NJ.E4.L.WF.3.B: Place adjectives and adverbs and form comparative and superlative adjectives and adverbs.
NJ.E4.L.WF.3.C: Use independent clauses and coordinating conjunctions.
NJ.E4.L.WF.3.D: Form irregular verbs; form and use progressive tenses.
NJ.E4.L.WF.3.E: Form and use possessive nouns and pronouns.
NJ.E4.L.WF.3.F: Capitalize the first word in quotations as appropriate, capitalize other important words (e.g., section headings).
NJ.E4.L.WF.3.G: Use underlining, quotation marks, or italics for titles; use quotation marks for direct speech; use comma before a coordinating conjunction in a compound sentence.
NJ.E4.L.KL.1: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening.
NJ.E4.L.KL.1.A: Acquire and use accurately grade-appropriate general academic and domain-specific words and phrases.
NJ.E4.L.KL.1.B: Choose words and phrases to convey ideas precisely.
NJ.E4.L.KL.1.D: Differentiate between contexts that call for formal English (e.g., presenting ideas) and situations where informal discourse is appropriate (e.g., small-group discussion).
NJ.E4.L.VL.2: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning academic and domain-specific words and phrases based on grade 4 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.
NJ.E4.L.VL.2.A: Use context (e.g., definitions, examples, or restatements in text) as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.
NJ.E4.L.VL.2.B: Use common, grade-appropriate Greek and Latin affixes and roots as clues to the meaning of a word (e.g., telegraph, photograph, autograph).
NJ.E4.L.VL.2.C: Consult reference materials (e.g., dictionaries, glossaries, thesauruses), both print and digital, to find the pronunciation and determine or clarify the precise meaning of key words and phrases.
NJ.E4.L.VI.3: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.
NJ.E4.L.VI.3.A: Explain the meaning of simple similes and metaphors (e.g., as pretty as a picture) in context.
NJ.E4.L.VI.3.B: Determine the meaning of words and phrases that allude to significant characters found in literature.
NJ.E4.L.VI.3.C: Recognize and explain the meaning of common idioms, adages, and proverbs.
NJ.E4.L.VI.3.D: Demonstrate understanding of words by relating them to their opposites (antonyms) and to words with similar but not identical meanings (synonyms).
NJ.E4.R.RL.CR.1: Refer to details and examples as textual evidence when explaining what a literary text says explicitly and make relevant connections when drawing inferences from the text.
NJ.E4.R.RL.CI.2: Summarize a literary text and interpret the author's theme citing key details from the text.
NJ.E4.R.RL.IT.3: Describe the impact of individuals and events throughout the course of a text, using an in-depth analysis of the character, setting, or event that draws on textual evidence.
NJ.E4.R.RL.TS.4: Explain major differences between poems, drama, and prose, and refer to the structural elements of poems (e.g., verse, rhythm, meter) and drama (e.g., casts of characters, settings, descriptions, dialogue, stage directions) when writing or speaking about a text.
NJ.E4.R.RL.PP.5: Compare and contrast the point of view from which different stories are narrated, including the difference between first- and third-person narrations.
NJ.E4.R.RL.MF.6: Make connections between specific descriptions and directions in a text and a visual or oral representation of the text.
NJ.E4.R.RL.CT.8: Compare and contrast the treatment of similar themes, topics and patterns of events in literary texts from authors of different cultures.
NJ.E4.R.RI.CR.1: Refer to details and examples as textual evidence when explaining what an informational text says explicitly and make relevant connections when drawing inferences from the text.
NJ.E4.R.RI.CI.2: Summarize an informational text and interpret the author's purpose or main idea citing key details from the text.
NJ.E4.R.RI.IT.3: Describe the impact of individuals and events throughout the course of a text, explaining events, procedures, ideas, or concepts in a historical, scientific, or technical text, including what happened and why, based on evidence in the text.
NJ.E4.R.RI.TS.4: Describe the overall structure (e.g., chronology, comparison, cause/effect, problem/ solution) of events, ideas, concepts, or information in a text or part of a text.
NJ.E4.R.RI.PP.5: Compare and contrast multiple accounts of the same event or topic; noting important similarities and differences in in the point of view they represent.
NJ.E4.R.RI.MF.6: Use evidence to show how graphics and visuals (e.g., illustrations, charts, graphs, diagrams, timelines, animations) support central ideas.
NJ.E4.R.RI.AA.7: Analyze how an author uses facts, details and explanations to develop ideas or to support their reasoning.
NJ.E4.R.RI.CT.8: Compare and contrast the treatment of similar themes, topics and patterns of events in informational texts from authors of different cultures.
NJ.E4.W.AW.1: Write opinion pieces on topics or texts, supporting a point of view with reasons and information.
NJ.E4.W.AW.1.A: Introduce a topic or text clearly, state an opinion, and create an organizational structure in which related ideas are grouped to support the writer's purpose.
NJ.E4.W.AW.1.B: Provide reasons that are supported by facts from texts and/or other sources.
NJ.E4.W.AW.1.C: Link opinion and reasons using words and phrases (e.g., for instance, in order to, in addition).
NJ.E4.W.AW.1.D: Provide a conclusion related to the opinion presented.
NJ.E4.W.IW.2: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine a topic and convey ideas and information clearly.
NJ.E4.W.IW.2.A: Introduce a topic clearly and group related information in paragraphs and sections; include formatting (e.g., headings), text features (e.g., illustrations, diagrams, captions) and multimedia when useful to aid in comprehension.
NJ.E4.W.IW.2.B: Develop the topic with facts, definitions, concrete details, text evidence, or other information and examples related to the topic.
NJ.E4.W.IW.2.C: Link ideas within paragraphs and sections of information using words and phrases (e.g., another, for example, also, because).
NJ.E4.W.IW.2.D: Use precise language and domain-specific vocabulary to inform about or explain the topic.
NJ.E4.W.IW.2.E: Provide a conclusion related to the information or explanation presented.
NJ.E4.W.NW.3: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using narrative technique, descriptive details, and clear event sequences.
NJ.E4.W.NW.3.A: Orient the reader by establishing a situation and introducing a narrator and/or characters; organize an event sequence that unfolds naturally.
NJ.E4.W.NW.3.B: Use dialogue and description to develop experiences and events or show the responses of characters to situations.
NJ.E4.W.NW.3.C: Use a variety of transitional words and phrases to manage the sequence of events.
NJ.E4.W.NW.3.D: Use concrete words, phrases, and sensory details and explore using figurative language to convey experiences and events precisely.
NJ.E4.W.NW.3.E: Provide a conclusion that follows from the narrated experiences or events.
NJ.E4.W.WP.4: With guidance and support from peers and adults, develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, and editing.
NJ.E4.W.WP.4.A: Identify audience, purpose, and intended length of composition before writing.
NJ.E4.W.WP.4.B: Use specialized, topic-specific language appropriate for the audience, purpose and subject matter.
NJ.E4.W.WP.4.C: Consider writing as a process, including self-evaluation, revision and editing.
NJ.E4.W.WP.4.D: With adult and peer feedback, and digital or print tools such as a dictionary, thesaurus, and/or spell checker, evaluate whether the writing achieved its goal and make changes in content or form as necessary.
NJ.E4.W.WP.4.E: After initial drafting, expand, combine, and reduce sentences for meaning, audience, and style.
NJ.E4.W.WR.5: Conduct short research projects that use multiple reference sources (print and non-print) and build knowledge through investigation of different aspects of a topic.
NJ.E4.W.SE.6: Gather relevant information from multiple print and digital sources; take notes, prioritize and categorize information; provide a list of sources.
NJ.E4.W.RW.7: Write routinely over extended time frames (with time for research and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting) for a range of tasks, purposes, and audiences.
NJ.E4.SL.PE.1: Engage effectively in a range of collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in groups, and teacher-led) with diverse partners on grade 4 topics and texts, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly.
NJ.E4.SL.PE.1.A: Explicitly draw on previously read text or material and other information known about the topic to explore ideas under discussion.
NJ.E4.SL.PE.1.B: Follow agreed-upon rules for discussions and carry out assigned roles.
NJ.E4.SL.PE.1.C: Pose and respond to specific questions to clarify or follow up on information, and make comments that contribute to the discussion and link to the remarks of others.
NJ.E4.SL.PE.1.D: Review the key ideas expressed and explain their own ideas and understanding in light of the discussion.
NJ.E4.SL.II.2: Paraphrase portions of a text read aloud or information presented in diverse media and formats (e.g., visually, quantitatively, and orally).
NJ.E4.SL.ES.3: Identify the reasons and evidence a speaker provides to support particular points.
NJ.E4.SL.PI.4: Report on a topic or text, tell a story, or recount an experience in an organized manner, using appropriate facts and relevant, descriptive details to support main ideas or themes; speak clearly at an understandable pace.
NJ.E4.SL.UM.5: Add audio recordings and visual displays to presentations when appropriate to enhance the development of main ideas or themes.
NJ.E4.SL.AS.6: Differentiate between contexts that call for formal English (e.g., presenting ideas) and situations where informal discourse is appropriate (e.g., small-group discussion); use formal English when appropriate to task and situation.
NJ.M4.OA.A: Use the four operations with whole numbers to solve problems.
NJ.M4.OA.A.1: Interpret a multiplication equation as a comparison, e.g., interpret  as a statement that 35 is 5 times as many as 7 and 7 times as many as 5. Represent verbal statements of multiplicative comparisons as multiplication equations.
NJ.M4.OA.A.2: Multiply or divide to solve word problems involving multiplicative comparison, e.g., by using drawings and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem, distinguishing multiplicative comparison from additive comparison.
NJ.M4.OA.A.3: Solve multi-step word problems posed with whole numbers and having whole-number answers using the four operations, including problems in which remainders must be interpreted. Represent these problems using equations with a letter standing for the unknown quantity. Assess the reasonableness of answers using mental computation and estimation strategies including rounding.
NJ.M4.OA.B: Gain familiarity with factors and multiples.
NJ.M4.OA.B.4: Find all factor pairs for a whole number in the range `1-100`. Recognize that a whole number is a multiple of each of its factors. Determine whether a given whole number in the range `1-100` is a multiple of a given one-digit number. Determine whether a given whole number in the range `1-100` is prime or composite.
NJ.M4.OA.C.5: Generate a number or shape pattern that follows a given rule. Identify apparent features of the pattern that were not explicit in the rule itself.
NJ.M4.NBT.A: Generalize place value understanding for multi-digit whole numbers.
NJ.M4.NBT.A.1: Recognize that in a multi-digit whole number, a digit in one place represents ten times what it represents in the place to its right.
NJ.M4.NBT.A.2: Read and write multi-digit whole numbers using base-ten numerals, number names, and expanded form. Compare two multi-digit numbers based on meanings of the digits in each place, using `>,=,and<` symbols to record the results of comparisons.
NJ.M4.NBT.A.3: Use place value understanding to round multi-digit whole numbers to any place.
NJ.M4.NBT.B: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to perform multi-digit arithmetic.
NJ.M4.NBT.B.4: With accuracy and efficiency, add and subtract multi-digit whole numbers using the standard algorithm.
NJ.M4.NBT.B.5: Multiply a whole number of up to `text(four digits)` by a `text(one-digit whole number)`, and multiply `text(two two-digit)` numbers, using strategies based on place value and the properties of operations. Illustrate and explain the calculation by using equations, rectangular arrays, and/or area models.
NJ.M4.NBT.B.6: Find whole-number quotients and remainders with up to four-digit dividends and one-digit divisors, using strategies based on place value, the properties of operations, and/or the relationship between multiplication and division. Illustrate and explain the calculation by using equations, rectangular arrays, and/or area model.
NJ.M4.NF.A: Extend understanding of fractions equivalence and ordering.
NJ.M4.NF.A.1: Explain why a fraction `a/b` is equivalent to a fraction `(nxxa)/(nxxb)` by using visual fraction models, with attention to how the number and size of the parts differ even though the two fractions themselves are the same size. Use this principle to recognize and generate equivalent fractions.
NJ.M4.NF.A.2: Compare two fractions with different numerators and different denominators, e.g., by creating common denominators or numerators, or by comparing to a benchmark fraction such as `1/2`. Recognize that comparisons are valid only when the two fractions refer to the same whole. Record the results of comparisons with symbols `>,=,or<`, and justify the conclusions, e.g., by using a visual fraction model.
NJ.M4.NF.B: Build fractions from unit fractions by applying and extending previous understandings of operations on whole numbers.
NJ.M4.NF.B.3: Understand a fraction  with  as a sum of fractions.
NJ.M4.NF.B.3.a: Understand addition and subtraction of fractions as joining and separating parts referring to the same whole.
NJ.M4.NF.B.3.b: Decompose a fraction into a sum of fractions with the same denominator in more than one way, recording each decomposition by an equation. Justify decompositions, e.g., by using a visual fraction model.
NJ.M4.NF.B.3.c: Add and subtract mixed numbers with like denominators, e.g., by replacing each mixed number with an equivalent fraction, and/or by using properties of operations and the relationship between addition and subtraction.
NJ.M4.NF.B.3.d: Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions referring to the same whole and having like denominators, e.g., by using visual fraction models and equations to represent the problem.
NJ.M4.NF.B.4: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication to multiply a fraction by a whole number.
NJ.M4.NF.B.4.a: Understand a fraction `a/b` as a multiple of `1/b`.
NJ.M4.NF.B.4.b: Understand a multiple of `a/b` as a multiple of `1/b`, and use this understanding to multiply a fraction by a whole number.
NJ.M4.NF.B.4.c: Solve word problems involving multiplication of a fraction by a whole number, e.g., by using visual fraction models and equations to represent the problem.
NJ.M4.NF.C: Understand decimal notation for fractions, and compare decimal fractions.
NJ.M4.NF.C.5: Express a fraction with denominator `10` as an equivalent fraction with denominator `100`, and use this technique to add two fractions with respective denominators `10and100`.
NJ.M4.NF.C.6: Use decimal notation for fractions with denominators `10or100`.
NJ.M4.NF.C.7: Compare two decimals to hundredths by reasoning about their size. Recognize that comparisons are valid only when the two decimals refer to the same whole. Record the results of comparisons with the symbols `>,=,or<`, and justify the conclusions, e.g., by using a visual model.
NJ.M4.MD.A: Solve problems involving measurement and conversion of measurements from a larger unit to a smaller unit.
NJ.M4.MD.A.1: Know relative sizes of measurement units within one system of units including km, m, cm. mm; kg, g; lb, oz.; l, ml; hr, min, sec. Within a single system of measurement, express measurements in a larger unit in terms of a smaller unit. Record measurement equivalents in a two-column table.
NJ.M4.MD.A.2: Use the four operations to solve word problems involving distances, intervals of time, liquid volumes, masses of objects, and money, including problems involving simple fractions or decimals, and problems that require expressing measurements given in a larger unit in terms of a smaller unit. Represent measurement quantities using diagrams such as number line diagrams that feature a measurement scale.
NJ.M4.MD.A.3: Apply the area and perimeter formulas for rectangles in real world and mathematical problems.
NJ.M4.MD.B.4: Make a line plot to display a data set of measurements in fractions of a unit (`1/2`, `1/4`, `1/8`). Solve problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions by using information presented in line plots.
NJ.M4.M.C: Geometric measurement: understand concepts of angle and measure angles.
NJ.M4.MD.C.5: Recognize angles as geometric shapes that are formed wherever two rays share a common endpoint, and understand concepts of angle measurement.
NJ.M4.MD.C.5.a: An angle is measured with reference to a circle with its center at the common endpoint of the rays, by considering the fraction of the circular arc between the points where the two rays intersect the circle. An angle that turns through `1/360` of a circle is called a “one-degree angle,” and can be used to measure angles.
NJ.M4.MD.C.5.b: An angle that turns through  one-degree angles is said to have an angle measure of  degrees.
NJ.M4.MD.C.6: Measure angles in whole-number degrees using a protractor. Sketch angles of specified measure.
NJ.M4.MD.C.7: Recognize angle measure as additive. When an angle is decomposed into non-overlapping parts, the angle measure of the whole is the sum of the angle measures of the parts. Solve addition and subtraction problems to find unknown angles on a diagram in real world and mathematical problems, e.g., by using an equation with a symbol for the unknown angle measure.
NJ.M4.G.A: Draw and identify lines and angles, and classify shapes by properties of their lines and angles.
NJ.M4.G.A.1: Draw points, lines, line segments, rays, angles (right, acute, obtuse), and perpendicular and parallel lines. Identify these in two-dimensional figures.
NJ.M4.G.A.2: Classify two-dimensional figures based on the presence or absence of parallel or perpendicular lines, or the presence or absence of angles of a specified size. Recognize right triangles as a category and identify right triangles.
NJ.M4.G.A.3: Recognize a line of symmetry for a two-dimensional figure as a line across the figure such that the figure can be folded along the line into matching parts. Identify line-symmetric figures and draw lines of symmetry.
NJ.S4.PS.3.1: Use evidence to construct an explanation relating the speed of an object to the energy of that object.
NJ.S4.PS.3.2: Make observations to provide evidence that energy can be transferred from place to place by sound, light, heat, and electric currents.
NJ.S4.PS.3.3: Ask questions and predict outcomes about the changes in energy that occur when objects collide.
NJ.S4.PS.3.4: Apply scientific ideas to design, test, and refine a device that converts energy from one form to another.
NJ.S4.PS.4: Waves & Their Applications In Technologies For Information Transfer
NJ.S4.PS.4.1: Develop a model of waves to describe patterns in terms of amplitude and wavelength and that waves can cause objects to move.
NJ.S4.PS.4.2: Develop a model to describe that light reflecting from objects and entering the eye allows objects to be seen.
NJ.S4.PS.4.3: Generate and compare multiple solutions that use patterns to transfer information.
NJ.S4.LS.1: From Molecules To Organisms: Structures & Processes
NJ.S4.LS.1.1: Construct an argument that plants and animals have internal and external structures that function to support survival, growth, behavior, and reproduction.
NJ.S4.LS.1.2: Use a model to describe that animals receive different types of information through their senses, process the information in their brain, and respond to the information in different ways.
NJ.S4.ESS.1.1: Identify evidence from patterns in rock formations and fossils in rock layers to support an explanation for changes in a landscape over time.
NJ.S4.ESS.2.1: Make observations and/or measurements to provide evidence of the effects of weathering or the rate of erosion by water, ice, wind, or vegetation.
NJ.S4.ESS.2.2: Analyze and interpret data from maps to describe patterns of Earth's features.
NJ.S4.ESS.3.1: Obtain and combine information to describe that energy and fuels are derived from natural resources and their uses affect the environment.
NJ.S4.ESS.3.2: Generate and compare multiple solutions to reduce the impacts of natural Earth processes and climate change have on humans.
NJ.E5.L.RF.3: Know and apply grade-level phonics and word analysis skills in decoding and encoding words; use combined knowledge of all letter-sound correspondences, syllabication patterns, and morphology (e.g., roots and affixes) to read accurately unfamiliar multisyllabic words in context and out of context.
NJ.E5.L.RF.4: Read with sufficient accuracy and fluency to support comprehension.
NJ.E5.L.RF.4.A: Read grade-level text with purpose and understanding.
NJ.E5.L.RF.4.B: Read grade-level text orally with accuracy, appropriate rate, and expression.
NJ.E5.L.RF.4.C: Use context to confirm or self-correct word recognition and understanding, rereading as necessary.
NJ.E5.L.WF.2: Demonstrate command of the conventions of writing, including those listed under grade four foundational skills.
NJ.E5.L.WF.2.A: Avoid fragments, run-ons and rambling sentences, and comma splices.
NJ.E5.L.WF.2.B: Maintain consistency in verb tense; place phrases and clauses; choose between adjectives and adverbs.
NJ.E5.L.WF.2.C: Ensure agreement between subject and verb and between pronoun and antecedent.
NJ.E5.L.WF.2.E: Use idiomatic language and choose words for effect; use punctuating for meaning and effect.
NJ.E5.L.WF.2.F: Use punctuation to separate items in a series; use commas in a series of phrases or clauses.
NJ.E5.L.WF.2.G: Use a comma to separate an introductory element from the rest of the sentence; use a comma to set off the words yes and no (e.g., Yes, thank you), to set off a tag question from the rest of the sentence (e.g., It's true, isn't it?), and to indicate direct address (e.g., Is that you, Emma?).
NJ.E5.L.WF.2.H: Spell grade appropriate words correctly, consulting references as needed.
NJ.E5.L.KL.1: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening.
NJ.E5.L.KL.1.A: Acquire and use accurately grade-appropriate general academic and domain-specific words and phrases.
NJ.E5.L.KL.1.B: Expand, combine, and reduce sentences for meaning, reader/listener interest, and style.
NJ.E5.L.KL.1.C: Compare and contrast the varieties of English (e.g., dialects, registers) used in stories, dramas, or poems.
NJ.E5.L.VL.2: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning academic and domain-specific words and phrases based on grade 5 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.
NJ.E5.L.VL.2.A: Use context (e.g., cause/effect relationships and comparisons in text) as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.
NJ.E5.L.VL.2.B: Use common, grade-appropriate Greek and Latin affixes and roots as clues to the meaning of a word (e.g., photograph, photosynthesis).
NJ.E5.L.VL.2.C: Consult reference materials (e.g., dictionaries, glossaries, thesauruses), both print and digital, to find the pronunciation and determine or clarify the precise meaning of key words and phrases.
NJ.E5.L.VI.3: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.
NJ.E5.L.VI.3.A: Interpret figurative language, including similes and metaphors, in context.
NJ.E5.L.VI.3.B: Recognize and explain the meaning of common idioms, adages, and proverbs.
NJ.E5.L.VI.3.C: Use the relationship between particular words (e.g., synonyms, antonyms, homographs) to better understand each of the words.
NJ.E5.R.RL.CR.1: Quote accurately from a literary text when explaining what the text says explicitly and make relevant connections when drawing inferences from the text.
NJ.E5.R.RL.CI.2: Determine the theme of a literary text (e.g., stories, plays or poetry) and explain how it is supported by key details; summarize the text.
NJ.E5.R.RL.IT.3: Analyze the impact of two or more individuals and events throughout the course of a text, comparing and contrasting two or more characters, settings, or events in a story or drama, drawing on specific textual evidence (e.g., how characters interact).
NJ.E5.R.RL.TS.4: Explain how a series of chapters, scenes, or stanzas fits together to provide the overall structure of a particular story, drama, or poem.
NJ.E5.R.RL.PP.5: Describe how a narrator's or speaker's point of view influences how events are described, and how that may influence the reader's interpretation.
NJ.E5.R.RL.MF.6: Analyze how visual and multimedia elements contribute to the meaning, tone, or beauty of a text (e.g., graphic novel, multimedia presentation of fiction, folktale, myth, poem).
NJ.E5.R.RL.CT.8: Compare and contrast the authors' approaches across two or more literary texts within the same genre or about the same or similar topics.
NJ.E5.R.RI.CR.1: Quote accurately from an informational text when explaining what the text says explicitly and make relevant connections when drawing inferences from the text.
NJ.E5.R.RI.CI.2: Determine the central idea of an informational text and explain how it is supported by key details; summarize the text.
NJ.E5.R.RI.IT.3: Analyze the impact of two or more individuals and events throughout the course of a text, explaining the relationships or interactions between two or more individuals, events, ideas, or concepts in a historical, scientific, or technical text based on specific evidence in the text.
NJ.E5.R.RI.TS.4: Compare and contrast the overall structure (e.g., chronology, comparison, cause/ effect, problem/solution) of events, ideas, concepts, or information in two or more texts.
NJ.E5.R.RI.PP.5: Analyze multiple accounts of the same event or topic, noting important similarities and differences in the point of view they represent and how that may influence the reader's interpretation.
NJ.E5.R.RI.MF.6: Interpret information presented visually, orally, or quantitatively (e.g., in charts, graphs, diagrams, timelines, animations, or interactive elements on web pages) and explain how the information contributes to an understanding of the text in which it appears.
NJ.E5.R.RI.AA.7: Explain how an author uses reasons and evidence to support particular points in a text, identifying which reasons and evidence support which point(s).
NJ.E5.R.RI.CT.8: Compare and contrast the authors' approaches across two or more informational texts within the same genre or about texts on the same or similar topics.
NJ.E5.W.AW.1: Write opinion pieces on topics or texts, supporting a point of view with reasons and information.
NJ.E5.W.AW.1.A: Introduce a topic or text clearly, state an opinion, and create an organizational structure in which ideas are logically grouped to support the writer's purpose.
NJ.E5.W.AW.1.B: Provide logically ordered reasons that are supported by facts and details from text(s), quote directly from text when appropriate.
NJ.E5.W.AW.1.C: Link opinion and reasons using words, phrases, and clauses (e.g., consequently, specifically).
NJ.E5.W.AW.1.D: Provide a conclusion related to the opinion presented.
NJ.E5.W.IW.2: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine a topic and convey ideas and information clearly.
NJ.E5.W.IW.2.A: Introduce a topic clearly to provide a focus and group related information logically; include text features such as headings, illustrations, and multimedia when useful to aid in comprehension.
NJ.E5.W.IW.2.B: Develop the topic with facts, definitions, concrete details, quotations, or other information and examples related to the topic.
NJ.E5.W.IW.2.C: Link ideas within paragraphs and sections of information using words, phrases, and clauses (e.g., in contrast, especially).
NJ.E5.W.IW.2.D: Use precise language and domain-specific vocabulary to inform about or explain the topic.
NJ.E5.W.IW.2.E: Provide a conclusion related to the information of explanation presented.
NJ.E5.W.NW.3: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, descriptive details, and clear event sequences.
NJ.E5.W.NW.3.A: Orient the reader by establishing a situation and introducing a narrator and/or characters; organize an event sequence that unfolds naturally.
NJ.E5.W.NW.3.B: Use narrative techniques, such as dialogue, description, and pacing, to develop experiences and events or show the responses of characters to situations.
NJ.E5.W.NW.3.C: Use a variety of transitional words, phrases, and clauses to manage the sequence of events.
NJ.E5.W.NW.3.D: Use concrete words and phrases and sensory details to convey experiences and events precisely.
NJ.E5.W.NW.3.E: Provide a conclusion that follows from the narrated experiences or events.
NJ.E5.W.WP.4: With guidance and support from peers and adults, develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach.
NJ.E5.W.WP.4.A: Consider audience, purpose, and intent before writing.
NJ.E5.W.WP.4.B: Plan appropriately to use specialized, topic-specific language appropriate for the audience, purpose and subject matter.
NJ.E5.W.WP.4.C: Consider writing as a process, including self-evaluation, revision and editing.
NJ.E5.W.WP.4.D: With adult and peer feedback, and digital or print tools such as a dictionary, thesaurus, and/or spell checker, evaluate whether the writing achieved its goal and make changes in content or form as necessary.
NJ.E5.W.WP.4.E: After initial drafting, expand, combine, and reduce sentences for meaning, audience, and style.
NJ.E5.W.WR.5: Establish a central idea about a topic, investigation, issue or event and use several sources to support the proposed central idea.
NJ.E5.W.SE.6: Gather relevant information from multiple valid and reliable print and digital sources; summarize or paraphrase information in notes and finished work, making note of any similarities and differences among ideas presented; and provide a list of sources.
NJ.E5.W.RW.7: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of tasks, purposes, and audiences.
NJ.E5.SL.PE.1: Engage effectively in a range of collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in groups, and teacher-led) with diverse partners on grade 5 topics and texts, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly.
NJ.E5.SL.PE.1.A: Explicitly draw on previously read text or material and other information known about the topic to explore ideas under discussion.
NJ.E5.SL.PE.1.B: Follow agreed-upon rules for discussions and carry out assigned roles.
NJ.E5.SL.PE.1.C: Pose and respond to specific questions by making comments that contribute to the discussion and elaborate on the remarks of others.
NJ.E5.SL.PE.1.D: Review the key ideas expressed and draw conclusions in light of information and knowledge gained from the discussions.
NJ.E5.SL.II.2: Summarize a written text read aloud or information presented in diverse media and formats (e.g., visually, quantitatively, and orally).
NJ.E5.SL.ES.3: Summarize the points a speaker makes and explain how each claim is supported by reasons and evidence.
NJ.E5.SL.PI.4: Report on a topic or text or present an opinion, sequencing ideas logically and using appropriate facts and relevant, descriptive details to support main ideas or themes; speak clearly at an understandable pace.
NJ.E5.SL.UM.5: Include multimedia components (e.g., graphics, sound) and visual displays in presentations when appropriate to enhance the development of main ideas or themes.
NJ.E5.SL.AS.6: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and tasks, using formal English when appropriate to task and situation.
NJ.M5.OA.A.1: Use parentheses, brackets, or braces in numerical expressions, and evaluate expressions with these symbols.
NJ.M5.OA.A.2: Write simple expressions that record calculations with numbers, and interpret numerical expressions without evaluating them.
NJ.M5.OA.B.3: Generate two numerical patterns using two given rules. Identify apparent relationships between corresponding terms. Form ordered pairs consisting of corresponding terms from the two patterns, and graph the ordered pairs on a coordinate plane.
NJ.M5.NBT.A.1: Recognize that in a multi-digit number, a digit in one place represents `10` times as much as it represents in the place to its right and `1/10` of what it represents in the place to its left.
NJ.M5.NBT.A.2: Explain patterns in the number of zeros of the product when multiplying a number by powers of `10`, and explain patterns in the placement of the decimal point when a decimal is multiplied or divided by a power of `10`. Use whole-number exponents to denote powers of `10`.
NJ.M5.NBT.A.3: Read, write, and compare decimals to thousandths.
NJ.M5.NBT.A.3.a: Read and write decimals to thousandths using base-ten numerals, number names, and expanded form, e.g., `347.392=3xx100+4xx10+7xx1+3xx(1/10)+9xx(1/100)+2xx(1/1000)`.
NJ.M5.NBT.A.3.b: Compare two decimals to thousandths based on meanings of the digits in each place, using `>,=,and<` symbols to record the results of comparisons.
NJ.M5.NBT.A.4: Use place value understanding to round decimals to any place.
NJ.M5.NBT.B: Perform operations with multi-digit whole numbers and with decimals to hundredths.
NJ.M5.NBT.B.5: Fluently multiply multi-digit whole numbers using the standard algorithm.
NJ.M5.NBT.B.6: Find whole-number quotients of whole numbers with up to four-digit dividends and two-digit divisors, using strategies based on place value, the properties of operations, and/or the relationship between multiplication and division. Illustrate and explain the calculation by using equations, rectangular arrays, and/or area models.
NJ.M5.NBT.B.7: Add, subtract, multiply, and divide decimals to hundredths, using concrete models or drawings and strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction; relate the strategy to a written method and explain the reasoning used.
NJ.M5.NF.A: Use equivalent fractions as a strategy to add and subtract fractions.
NJ.M5.NF.A.1: Add and subtract fractions with unlike denominators (including mixed numbers) by replacing given fractions with equivalent fractions in such a way as to produce an equivalent sum or difference of fractions with like denominators.
NJ.M5.NF.A.2: Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions referring to the same whole, including cases of unlike denominators, e.g., by using visual fraction models or equations to represent the problem. Use benchmark fractions and number sense of fractions to estimate mentally and assess the reasonableness of answers.
NJ.M5.NF.B: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication and division to multiply and divide fractions.
NJ.M5.NF.B.3: Interpret a fraction as division of the numerator by the denominator `(a/b=a-:b)`. Solve word problems involving division of whole numbers leading to answers in the form of fractions or mixed numbers, e.g., by using visual fraction models or equations to represent the problem.
NJ.M5.NF.B.4: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication to multiply a fraction or whole number by a fraction.
NJ.M5.NF.B.4.a: Interpret the product `(a/b)xxq` as a parts of a partition of `q` into `b` equal parts; equivalently, as the result of a sequence of operations `axxq-:b`.
NJ.M5.NF.B.4.b: Find the area of a rectangle with fractional side lengths by tiling it with unit squares of the appropriate unit fraction side lengths, and show that the area is the same as would be found by multiplying the side lengths.
