PA.S8.B.3.1.3: Explain relationships among organisms (e.g., producers/consumers, predator/prey) in an ecosystem.
PA.S8.B.3.2: Identify evidence of change to infer and explain the ways different variables may affect change in natural or human-made systems.
PA.S8.B.3.2.1: Use evidence to explain factors that affect changes in populations (e.g., deforestation, disease, land use, natural disaster, invasive species).
PA.S8.B.3.2.2: Use evidence to explain how diversity affects the ecological integrity of natural systems.
PA.S8.B.3.2.3: Describe the response of organisms to environmental changes (e.g., changes in climate, hibernation, migration, coloration) and how those changes affect survival.
PA.S8.B.3.3: Explain how renewable and nonrenewable resources provide for human needs or how these needs impact the environment.
PA.S8.B.3.3.1: Explain how human activities may affect local, regional, and global environments.
PA.S8.B.3.3.2: Explain how renewable and nonrenewable resources provide for human needs (i.e., energy, food, water, clothing, and shelter).
PA.S8.B.3.3.3: Describe how waste management affects the environment (e.g., recycling, composting, landfills, incineration, sewage treatment).
PA.S8.B.3.3.4: Explain the long-term effects of using integrated pest management (e.g., herbicides, natural predators, biogenetics) on the environment.
PA.S8.C.1: Structure, Properties & Interaction Of Matter & Energy
PA.S8.C.1.1: Explain concepts about the structure and properties (physical and chemical) of matter.
PA.S8.C.1.1.1: Explain the differences among elements, compounds, and mixtures.
PA.S8.C.1.1.2: Use characteristic physical or chemical properties to distinguish one substance from another (e.g., density, thermal expansion/contraction, freezing/melting points, streak test).
PA.S8.C.1.1.3: Identify and describe reactants and products of simple chemical reactions.
PA.S8.C.2: Forms, Sources, Conversion & Transfer Of Energy
PA.S8.C.2.1: Describe energy sources, transfer of energy, or conversion of energy.
PA.S8.C.2.1.1: Distinguish among forms of energy (e.g., electrical, mechanical, chemical, light, sound, nuclear) and sources of energy (i.e., renewable and nonrenewable energy).
PA.S8.C.2.1.2: Explain how energy is transferred from one place to another through convection, conduction, or radiation.
PA.S8.C.2.1.3: Describe how one form of energy (e.g., electrical, mechanical, chemical, light, sound, nuclear) can be converted into a different form of energy.
PA.S8.C.2.2: Compare the environmental impact of different energy sources chosen to support human endeavors.
PA.S8.C.2.2.1: Describe the Sun as the major source of energy that impacts the environment.
PA.S8.C.2.2.2: Compare the time span of renewability for fossil fuels and the time span of renewability for alternative fuels.
PA.S8.C.2.2.3: Describe the waste (i.e., kind and quantity) derived from the use of renewable and nonrenewable resources and their potential impact on the environment.
PA.S8.C.3.1: Describe the effect of multiple forces on the movement, speed, or direction of an object.
PA.S8.C.3.1.1: Describe forces acting on objects (e.g., friction, gravity, balanced versus unbalanced).
PA.S8.C.3.1.2: Distinguish between kinetic and potential energy.
PA.S8.C.3.1.3: Explain that mechanical advantage helps to do work (physics) by either changing a force or changing the direction of the applied force (e.g., simple machines, hydraulic systems).
PA.S8.D.1: Earth Features & Processes That Change Earth & Its Resources
PA.S8.D.1.1: Describe constructive and destructive natural processes that form different geologic structures and resources.
PA.S8.D.1.1.1: Explain the rock cycle as changes in the solid earth and rock types (igneous - granite, basalt, obsidian, pumice; sedimentary - limestone, sandstone, shale, coal; and metamorphic - slate, quartzite, marble, gneiss).
PA.S8.D.1.1.2: Describe natural processes that change Earth's surface (e.g., landslides, volcanic eruptions, earthquakes, mountain building, new land being formed, weathering, erosion, sedimentation, soil formation).
PA.S8.D.1.1.3: Identify soil types (i.e., humus, topsoil, subsoil, loam, loess, and parent material) and their characteristics (i.e., particle size, porosity, and permeability) found in different biomes and in Pennsylvania, and explain how they formed.
PA.S8.D.1.1.4: Explain how fossils provide evidence about plants and animals that once lived throughout Pennsylvania's history (e.g., fossils provide evidence of different environments).
PA.S8.D.1.2: Describe the potential impact of human-made processes on changes to Earth's resources and how they affect everyday life.
PA.S8.D.1.2.1: Describe a product's transformation process from production to consumption (e.g., prospecting, propagating, growing, maintaining, adapting, treating, converting, distributing, disposing) and explain the process's potential impact on Earth's resources.
PA.S8.D.1.2.2: Describe potential impacts of human-made processes (e.g., manufacturing, agriculture, transportation, mining) on Earth's resources, both nonliving (i.e., air, water, or earth materials) and living (i.e., plants and animals).
PA.S8.D.1.3: Describe characteristic features of Earth's water systems or their impact on resources.
PA.S8.D.1.3.1: Describe the water cycle and the physical processes on which it depends (i.e., evaporation, condensation, precipitation, transpiration, runoff, infiltration, energy inputs, and phase changes).
PA.S8.D.1.3.2: Compare and contrast characteristics of freshwater and saltwater systems on the basis of their physical characteristics (i.e., composition, density, and electrical conductivity) and their use as natural resources.
PA.S8.D.1.3.3: Distinguish among different water systems (e.g., wetland systems, ocean systems, river systems, watersheds) and describe their relationships to each other as well as to landforms.
PA.S8.D.1.3.4: Identify the physical characteristics of a stream and how these characteristics determine the types of organisms found within the stream environment (e.g., biological diversity, water quality, flow rate, tributaries, surrounding watershed).
PA.S8.D.2.1: Explain how pressure, temperature, moisture, and wind are used to describe atmospheric conditions that affect regional weather or climate.
PA.S8.D.2.1.1: Explain the impact of water systems on the local weather or the climate of a region (e.g., lake effect snow, land/ocean breezes).
PA.S8.D.2.1.2: Identify how global patterns of atmospheric movement influence regional weather and climate.
PA.S8.D.2.1.3: Identify how cloud types, wind directions, and barometric pressure changes are associated with weather patterns in different regions of the country.
PA.S8.D.3.1: Explain the relationships between and among the objects of our solar system.
PA.S8.D.3.1.1: Describe patterns of earth's movements (i.e., rotation and revolution) in relation to the moon and sun (i.e., phases, eclipses, and tides).
PA.S8.D.3.1.2: Describe the role of gravity as the force that governs the movement of the solar system and universe.
PA.S8.D.3.1.3: Compare and contrast characteristics of celestial bodies found in the solar system (e.g., moons, asteroids, comets, meteors, inner and outer planets).
RI.EK.RL.1: With prompting and support, ask and answer questions about key details in a text.
RI.EK.RL.2: With prompting and support, retell familiar stories, including key details.
RI.EK.RL.3: With prompting and support, identify characters, settings, and major events in a story.
RI.EK.RL.4: Ask and answer questions about unknown words in a text.
RI.EK.RL.5: Recognize common types of texts and characteristics of their structure (e.g., story elements in books; rhyme, rhythm, and repetition in poems).
RI.EK.RL.6: With prompting and support, explain that reading the cover or title page is how to find out who created a book; name the author and illustrator of a book and define the role of each in telling the story.
RI.EK.RL.7: With prompting and support, describe the relationship between illustrations and the story in which they appear (e.g., what moment in a story an illustration depicts).
RI.EK.RL.9: With prompting and support, compare and contrast the adventures and experiences of characters in familiar stories.
RI.EK.RL.10: Actively engage in group reading activities with purpose and understanding.
RI.EK.RI.E1: With prompting and support, ask and answer questions about key details in a text.
RI.EK.RI.E2: With prompting and support, identify the main topic and retell key details of a text.
RI.EK.RI.E3: With prompting and support, describe the connection between two individuals, events, ideas, or pieces of information in a text.
RI.EK.RI.E4: With prompting and support, ask and answer questions about unknown words in a text.
RI.EK.RI.E5: Identify the front cover, back cover, and title page of a book.
RI.EK.RI.E6: Name the author and illustrator of a text and define the role of each in presenting the ideas or information in the text.
RI.EK.RI.E7: With prompting and support, describe the relationship between illustrations and the text in which they appear (e.g., what person, place, thing, or idea in the text an illustration depicts).
RI.EK.RI.E8: With prompting and support, identify the reasons an author gives to support points in a text.
RI.EK.RI.E9: With prompting and support, identify basic similarities in and differences between two texts on the same topic (e.g., in illustrations, descriptions, procedures).
RI.EK.RI.E10: Actively engage in group reading activities with purpose and understanding.
RI.EK.RF.1: Demonstrate understanding of the organization and basic features of print.
RI.EK.RF.1.a: Follow words from left to right, top to bottom, and page by page.
RI.EK.RF.1.b: Recognize that spoken words are represented in written language by specific sequences of letters.
RI.EK.RF.1.c: Understand that words are separated by spaces in print.
RI.EK.RF.1.d: Recognize and name all upper- and lowercase letters of the alphabet.
RI.EK.RF.2: Demonstrate understanding of spoken words, syllables, and sounds (phonemes).
RI.EK.RF.2.b: Count, pronounce, blend, and segment syllables in spoken words.
RI.EK.RF.2.c: Blend and segment onsets and rimes of single-syllable spoken words.
RI.EK.RF.2.d: Isolate and pronounce the initial, medial vowel, and final sounds (phonemes) in three-phoneme (consonant-vowel-consonant, or CVC) words.
RI.EK.RF.3: Know and apply grade-level phonics and word analysis skills in decoding words.
RI.EK.RF.3.a: Demonstrate basic knowledge of one-to-one letter-sound correspondences by producing the primary sound or many of the most frequent sounds for each consonant.
RI.EK.RF.3.b: Associate the long and short sounds with common spellings (graphemes) for the five major vowels.
RI.EK.RF.3.c: Read common high-frequency words by sight (e.g., the, of, to, you, she, my, is, are, do, does).
RI.EK.RF.3.d: Distinguish between similarly spelled words by identifying the sounds of the letters that differ.
RI.EK.RF.4: Read early-emergent-reader texts with purpose and understanding.
RI.EK.W.1: Use a combination of drawing, dictating, and writing to compose opinion pieces that tell a reader the topic or the name of the book they are writing about and state an opinion or preference about the topic or book (e.g., My favorite book is ...).
RI.EK.W.2: Use a combination of drawing, dictating, and writing to compose informative/explanatory texts that name and supply some information about a topic.
RI.EK.W.3: Use a combination of drawing, dictating, and writing to narrate a single event or experience, or several loosely linked events or experiences; sequence the narrative appropriately and provide a reaction to what it describes.
RI.EK.W.3.a: For poems, use rhyming words to create structure.
RI.EK.W.5: With guidance and support from adults, respond to questions and suggestions from peers and add details to strengthen writing as needed.
RI.EK.W.5.b: Demonstrate the ability to use vocabulary appropriate for kindergarten.
RI.EK.W.6: With guidance and support from adults, explore a variety of digital tools to produce and publish writing, including collaboration with peers.
RI.EK.W.7: Participate in shared research and writing projects (e.g., explore a number of books by a favorite author and express opinions about them).
RI.EK.W.8: With guidance and support from adults, recall information from experiences or gather information from provided sources to answer a question.
RI.EK.W.10: Write or dictate writing routinely for a range of tasks, purposes, and audiences.
RI.EK.SL.1: Participate in collaborative conversations with diverse partners about kindergarten topics and texts with peers and adults in small and larger groups.
RI.EK.SL.1.a: Follow agreed-upon rules for discussions (e.g., listening to others and taking turns speaking about the topics and texts under discussion).
RI.EK.SL.1.b: Continue a conversation through multiple exchanges.
RI.EK.SL.2: Confirm understanding of a text read aloud or information presented orally or through other media by asking and answering questions about key details and requesting clarification if something is not understood.
RI.EK.SL.3: Ask and answer questions in order to seek help, get information, or clarify something that is not understood.
RI.EK.SL.4: Describe familiar people, places, things, and events and, with prompting and support, provide additional detail.
RI.EK.SL.5: Add drawings or other visual displays to descriptions as desired to provide additional detail.
RI.EK.SL.6: Speak audibly and express thoughts, feelings, and ideas clearly.
RI.EK.L.1: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking; retain and further develop language skills learned previously.
RI.EK.L.1.a: Demonstrate the ability to produce and expand complete sentences using frequently occurring nouns, pronouns, adjectives, verbs, question words, and prepositions; name and use in context numbers 0-100.
RI.EK.L.1.b: Form questions that seek additional information, rather than a simple yes/no answer.
RI.EK.L.1.c: Form regular plural nouns orally by adding /s/ or /es/.
RI.EK.L.2: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.
RI.EK.L.2.b: Capitalize the first word in a sentence and the pronoun I.
RI.EK.L.2.d: Write a letter or letters for most consonant and short-vowel sounds (phonemes).
RI.EK.L.2.e: Spell simple words phonetically, drawing on knowledge of sound-letter relationships.
RI.EK.L.4: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on kindergarten reading and content.
RI.EK.L.4.a: Identify new meanings for familiar words and apply them accurately (e.g., knowing duck is a bird and learning the verb to duck).
RI.EK.L.5: With guidance and support from adults, explore word relationships and nuances in word meanings.
RI.EK.L.5.a: Sort common objects into categories (e.g., shapes, foods) to gain a sense of the concepts the categories represent.
RI.EK.RF.5.b: Demonstrate understanding of frequently occurring verbs and adjectives by relating them to their opposites (antonyms).
RI.EK.RF.5.c: Identify real-life connections between words and their use (e.g., note places at school that are colorful).
RI.EK.RF.5.d: Distinguish shades of meaning among verbs describing the same general action (e.g., walk, march, strut, prance) by acting out the meanings.
RI.EK.L.6: Use words and phrases acquired through conversations, activities in the kindergarten curriculum, reading and being read to, and responding to texts.
RI.MK.CC.A: Know number names and the count sequence.
RI.MK.CC.A.1: Count to 100 by ones and by tens.
RI.MK.CC.A.2: Count forward beginning from a given number within the known sequence (instead of having to begin at one).
RI.MK.CC.A.3: Write numbers from 0 to 20. Represent a number of objects with a written numeral 0-20 (with 0 representing a count of no objects).
RI.MK.CC.B: Count to tell the number of objects.
RI.MK.CC.B.4: Understand the relationship between numbers and quantities; connect counting to cardinality.
RI.MK.CC.B.4.a: When counting objects, say the number names in the standard order, pairing each object with one and only one number name and each number name with one and only one object.
RI.MK.CC.B.4.b: Understand that the last number name said tells the number of objects counted. The number of objects is the same regardless of their arrangement or the order in which they were counted.
RI.MK.CC.B.4.c: Understand that each successive number name refers to a quantity that is one larger. Recognize the one more pattern of counting using objects.
RI.MK.CC.B.5: Count to answer “how many?” questions about as many as 20 things arranged in a line, a rectangular array, or a circle, or as many as 10 things in a scattered configuration; given a number from 1-20, count out that many objects.
RI.MK.CC.C.6: Identify whether the number of objects in one group is greater than, less than, or equal to the number of objects in another group for groups with up to 10 objects, e.g., by using matching and counting strategies.
RI.MK.CC.C.7: Compare two numbers between `1and10` presented as written numerals.
RI.MK.OA.A: Understand addition as putting together and adding to, and understand subtraction as taking apart and taking from.
RI.MK.OA.A.1: Represent addition and subtraction with objects, fingers, mental images, drawings, sounds (e.g., claps), acting out situations, verbal explanations, expressions, or equations.
RI.MK.OA.A.2: Solve addition and subtraction word problems, and add and subtract within 10, e.g., by using objects or drawings to represent the problem.
RI.MK.OA.A.3: Decompose numbers less than or equal to 10 into pairs in more than one way, e.g., by using objects or drawings, and record each decomposition by a drawing or equation (e.g., 5 = 2 + 3 and 5 = 4 +1).
RI.MK.OA.A.4: For any number from 1 to 9, find the number that makes 10 when added to the given number, e.g., by using objects or drawings, and record the answer with a drawing or equation.
RI.MK.OA.A.5: Fluently add and subtract within 5, including zero.
RI.MK.NBT.A: Work with numbers 11-19 to gain foundations for place value.
RI.MK.NBT.A.1: Compose and decompose numbers from 11 to 19 into ten ones and some further ones, e.g., by using objects or drawings, and record each composition or decomposition by a drawing or equation (e.g., 18 = 10 + 8); understand that these numbers are composed of ten ones and one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine ones.
RI.MK.MD.A.1: Describe measurable attributes of objects, such as length or weight. Describe several measurable attributes of a single object.
RI.MK.MD.A.2: Directly compare two objects with a measurable attribute in common, to see which object has “more of”/“less of” the attribute, and describe the difference.
RI.MK.MD.B: Classify objects and count the number of objects in each category.
RI.MK.MD.B.3: Classify objects into given categories; count the numbers of objects in each category (up to and including 10) and sort the categories by count.
RI.MK.G.A: Identify and describe shapes(squares, circles, triangles, rectangles, hexagons, cubes, cones, cylinders, and spheres).
RI.MK.G.A.1: Describe objects in the environment using names of shapes, and describe the relative positions of these objects using terms such as above, below, beside, in front of, behind, and next to.
RI.MK.G.A.2: Correctly name shapes regardless of their orientation or overall size.
RI.MK.G.A.3: Identify shapes as two-dimensional (lying in a plane, “flat”) or three-dimensional(“solid”).
RI.MK.G.B: Analyze, compare, create, and compose shapes.
RI.MK.G.B.4: Analyze and compare two- and three-dimensional shapes, in different sizes and orientations, using informal language to describe their similarities, differences, parts (e.g., number of sides and vertices/“corners”) and other attributes (e.g., having sides of equal length).
RI.MK.G.B.5: Model shapes in the world by building shapes from components (e.g., sticks and clay balls) and drawing shapes.
RI.MK.G.B.6: Compose simple shapes to form larger shapes.
RI.E1.RL.1: Ask and answer questions about key details in a text.
RI.E1.RL.2: Retell stories, including key details, and demonstrate understanding of their central message or lesson.
RI.E1.RL.3: Describe characters, settings, and major events in a story, using key details.
RI.E1.RL.4: Identify words and phrases in stories or poems that suggest feelings or appeal to the senses.
RI.E1.RL.5: Identify characteristics of common types of stories, including folktales and fairy tales.
RI.E1.RL.6: Identify who is telling the story at various points in a text.
RI.E1.RL.7: Use illustrations and details in a story to describe its characters, setting, or events.
RI.E1.RL.9: Compare and contrast the adventures and experiences of characters in stories.
RI.E1.RL.10: With prompting and support, read and comprehend literary texts representing a variety of genres, cultures, and perspectives and exhibiting complexity appropriate for at least grade 1.
RI.E1.RI.E1: Ask and answer questions about key details in a text.
RI.E1.RI.E2: Identify the main topic and retell key details of a text.
RI.E1.RI.E3: Describe the connection between two individuals, events, ideas, or pieces of information in a text.
RI.E1.RI.E4: Ask and answer questions to help determine or clarify the meaning of words and phrases in a text.
RI.E1.RI.E5: Know and use various text features (e.g., headings, tables of contents, glossaries, electronic menus, icons) to locate key facts or information in a text.
RI.E1.RI.E6: Distinguish between information provided by pictures or other illustrations and information provided by the words in a text.
RI.E1.RI.E7: Use the illustrations and details in a text to describe its key ideas.
RI.E1.RI.E8: Identify the reasons an author gives to support points in a text.
RI.E1.RI.E9: Identify basic similarities in and differences between two texts on the same topic (e.g., in illustrations, descriptions, or procedures).
RI.E1.RI.E10: With prompting and support, read and comprehend informational texts exhibiting complexity appropriate for at least grade 1.
RI.E1.RF.1: Demonstrate understanding of the organization and basic features of print.
RI.E1.RF.1.a: Recognize the distinguishing features of a sentence (e.g., first word, capitalization, ending punctuation).
RI.E1.RF.2: Demonstrate understanding of spoken words, syllables, and sounds (phonemes).
RI.E1.RF.2.a: Distinguish long from short vowel sounds in spoken single-syllable words.
RI.E1.RF.2.b: Orally produce single-syllable words by blending sounds (phonemes), including consonant blends.
RI.E1.RF.2.c: Isolate and pronounce initial, medial vowel, and final sounds (phonemes) in spoken single-syllable words.
RI.E1.RF.2.d: Segment spoken single-syllable words into their complete sequence of individual sounds (phonemes).
RI.E1.RF.3: Know and apply grade-level phonics and word analysis skills in decoding words.
RI.E1.RF.3.a: Know the spelling-sound correspondences for common consonant digraphs.
RI.E1.RF.3.c: Know final -e and common vowel team conventions for representing long vowel sounds.
RI.E1.RF.3.d: Use knowledge that every syllable must have a vowel sound to determine the number of syllables in a printed word.
RI.E1.RF.3.e: Decode two-syllable words following basic patterns by breaking the words into syllables.
RI.E1.RF.3.g: Recognize and read grade-appropriate irregularly spelled words.
RI.E1.RF.4: Read with sufficient accuracy and fluency to support comprehension.
RI.E1.RF.4.a: Read grade-level text with purpose and understanding.
RI.E1.RF.4.b: Read grade-level text orally with accuracy, appropriate rate, and expression on successive readings.
RI.E1.RF.4.c: Use context to confirm or self-correct word recognition and understanding, rereading as necessary.
RI.E1.W.1: Write opinion pieces that introduce the topic or name the book they are writing about, state an opinion, supply a reason for the opinion, and provide some sense of closure.
RI.E1.W.2: Write informative/explanatory texts that name a topic, supply some facts about the topic, and provide some sense of closure.
RI.E1.W.3: Write narratives in prose or poem form that recount two or more appropriately sequenced events or experiences, include some details about what happened or was experienced, use temporal words to signal order where appropriate, and provide some sense of closure.
RI.E1.W.3.a: For poems, use rhyming words and words that repeat long or short vowel sounds to create structure.
RI.E1.W.4: Produce writing in which the development and organization are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.
RI.E1.W.5: With guidance and support from adults, focus on a topic, respond to questions and suggestions from peers, and add details to strengthen writing as needed.
RI.E1.W.5.b: Demonstrate the ability to choose and use appropriate vocabulary.
RI.E1.W.6: With guidance and support from adults, use a variety of digital tools to produce and publish writing, including in collaboration with peers.
RI.E1.W.7: Participate in shared research and writing projects (e.g., explore a number of how-to books on a given topic and use them to write a sequence of instructions).
RI.E1.W.8: With guidance and support from adults, recall information from experiences or gather information from provided sources to answer a question.
RI.E1.W.10: Write routinely for a range of tasks, purposes, and audiences.
RI.E1.SL.1: Participate in collaborative conversations with diverse partners about grade 1 topics and texts with peers and adults in small and larger groups.
RI.E1.SL.1.a: Follow agreed-upon rules for discussions (e.g., listening to others with care, speaking one at a time about the topics and texts under discussion).
RI.E1.SL.1.b: Build on others' talk in conversations by responding to the comments of others through multiple exchanges.
RI.E1.SL.1.c: Ask questions to clear up any confusion about the topics and texts under discussion.
RI.E1.SL.2: Ask and answer questions about key details in a text read aloud or information presented orally or through other media.
RI.E1.SL.3: Ask and answer questions about what a speaker says in order to gather additional information or clarify something that is not understood.
RI.E1.SL.4: Describe people, places, things, and events with relevant details, expressing ideas and feelings clearly and using appropriate vocabulary.
RI.E1.SL.5: Add drawings or other visual displays to descriptions when appropriate to clarify ideas, thoughts, and feelings.
RI.E1.SL.6: Produce complete sentences when appropriate to task and situation.
RI.E1.L.1: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking; retain and further develop language skills learned in previous grades.
RI.E1.L.1.a: Produce and expand simple and compound sentences.
RI.E1.L.1.b: Demonstrate understanding that a question is a type of sentence.
RI.E1.L.1.c: Use singular and plural nouns with matching verbs in sentences.
RI.E1.L.1.d: Use verbs in sentences to convey a sense of past, present, and future.
RI.E1.L.1.e: Use common, proper, and possessive nouns.
RI.E1.L.1.f: Use personal, possessive, and indefinite pronouns.
RI.E1.L.1.g: Use frequently occurring prepositions, adjectives, adverbs, conjunctions, and articles.
RI.E1.L.2: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.
RI.E1.L.2.a: Print legibly all upper- and lowercase letters.
RI.E1.L.2.c: Capitalize the names of months and people.
RI.E1.L.2.d: Use commas in dates and to separate individual words in a series.
RI.E1.L.2.e: Use conventional spelling for words with common spelling patterns and for frequently occurring irregular words.
RI.E1.L.2.f: Spell untaught words phonetically, drawing on phonemic awareness and spelling conventions.
RI.E1.L.2.g: Write numerals up to 120 (; understand that numbers are also written as words; write words for numbers from one to ten.
RI.E1.L.4: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grade 1 reading and content, choosing flexibly from an array of strategies.
RI.E1.L.4.a: Use sentence-level context as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.
RI.E1.L.4.b: Use frequently occurring affixes as a clue to the meaning of a word.
RI.E1.L.4.c: Identify frequently occurring root words (e.g., look) and their inflectional forms (e.g., looks, looked, looking).
RI.E1.L.5: With guidance and support from adults, demonstrate understanding of word relationships and nuances in word meanings.
RI.E1.L.5.a: Sort words into categories (e.g., colors, clothing) to gain a sense of the concepts the categories represent.
RI.E1.L.5.b: Define words by category and by one or more key attributes (e.g., a duck is a bird that swims; a tiger is a large cat with stripes).
RI.E1.L.5.c: Identify real-life connections between words and their use (e.g., note places at home that are cozy).
RI.E1.L.3.d: Distinguish shades of meaning among verbs differing in manner (e.g., look, peek, glance, stare, glare, scowl) and adjectives differing in intensity (e.g., large, gigantic) by defining or choosing them or by acting out the meanings.
RI.E1.L.6: Use words and phrases acquired through conversations, activities in the grade 1 curriculum, reading and being read to, and responding to texts, including using frequently occurring conjunctions (e.g., because) to signal simple relationships.
RI.M1.OA.A: Represent and solve problems involving addition and subtraction.
RI.M1.OA.A.1: Use addition and subtraction within 20 to solve word problems involving situations of adding to, taking from, putting together, taking apart, and comparing, with unknowns in all positions, e.g., by using objects, drawings, and equations (number sentences) with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.
RI.M1.OA.A.2: Solve word problems that call for addition of three whole numbers whose sum is less than or equal to 20, e.g., by using objects, drawings, and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.
RI.M1.OA.B: Understand and apply properties of operations and the relationship between addition and subtraction.
RI.M1.OA.B.3: Apply properties of operations to add.
RI.M1.OA.B.4: Understand subtraction as an unknown-addend problem.
RI.M1.OA.C.5: Relate counting to addition and subtraction (e.g., by counting on 2 to add 2).
RI.M1.OA.C.6: Add and subtract within 20, demonstrating fluency for addition and subtraction within 10. Use mental strategies such as counting on; making 10 (e.g., 8 + 6 = 8 + 2 + 4 = 10 + 4 = 14); decomposing a number leading to a 10 (e.g., 13 - 4 = 13 - 3 - 1 = 10 - 1 = 9); using the relationship between addition and subtraction (e.g., knowing that 8 + 4 = 12, one knows 12 - 8 = 4); and creating equivalent but easier or known sums (e.g., adding 6 + 7 by creating the known equivalent 6 + 6 + 1 = 12 + 1 =13).
RI.M1.OA.D: Work with addition and subtraction equations.
RI.M1.OA.D.7: Understand the meaning of the equal sign, and determine if equations involving addition and subtraction are true or false.
RI.M1.OA.D.8: Determine the unknown whole number in an addition or subtraction equation relating three whole numbers.
RI.M1.NBT.A.1: Count to 120, starting at any number less than 120. In this range, read and write numerals and represent a number of objects with a written numeral.
RI.M1.NBT.B.2: Understand that the two digits of a two-digit number represent amounts of tens and ones. Understand the following as special cases:
RI.M1.NBT.B.2.a: 10 can be thought of as a bundle of ten ones - called a“ten.”
RI.M1.NBT.B.2.b: The numbers from 11 to 19 are composed of a ten and one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine ones.
RI.M1.NBT.B.2.c: The numbers 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90 refer to one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine tens (and 0 ones).
RI.M1.NBT.B.3: Compare two two-digit numbers based on meanings of the tens and ones digits, recording the results of comparisons with the symbols `>,=,and<`.
RI.M1.NBT.C: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to add and subtract.
RI.M1.NBT.C.4: Add within `100`, including adding a two-digit number and a one-digit number, and adding a two-digit number and a multiple of 10, using concrete models or drawings, and strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction; relate the strategy to a written method and explain the reasoning used. Understand that in adding two-digit numbers, one adds tens and tens, ones and ones; and sometimes it is necessary to compose aten.
RI.M1.NBT.C.5: Given a two-digit number, mentally find 10 more or 10 less than the number, without having to count; explain the reasoning used. Identify arithmetic patterns of 10 more and 10 less than using strategies based on place value.
RI.M1.NBT.C.6: Subtract multiples of `10` in the range `10-90` from multiples of `10` in the range `10-90` (positive or zero differences), using concrete models or drawings and strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction; relate the strategy to a written method and explain the reasoning used.
RI.M1.MD.A: Measure lengths indirectly and by iterating length units.
RI.M1.MD.A.1: Order three objects by length; compare the lengths of two objects indirectly by using a third object.
RI.M1.MD.A.2: Express the length of an object as a whole number of length units, by laying multiple copies of a shorter object (the length unit) end to end; understand that the length measurement of an object is the number of same-size length units that span it with no gaps or overlaps. Limit to contexts where the object being measured is spanned by a whole number of length units with no gaps or overlaps.
RI.M1.MD.B.3: Tell and write time in `text(hours)` and half-hours using analog and digital clocks
RI.M1.MD.C.4: Organize, represent, and interpret data with up to three categories; ask and answer questions about the total number of data points, how many in each category, and how many more or less are in one category than in another.
RI.M1.MD.D.5: Identify the values of all U.S. coins and know their comparative values (e.g., a dime is of greater value than a nickel). Find equivalent values (e.g., a nickel is equivalent to five pennies). Use appropriate notation (e.g., 69¢). Use the values of coins in the solutions of problems (up to 100¢).
RI.M1.G.A: Reason with shapes and their attributes.
RI.M1.G.A.1: Distinguish between defining attributes (e.g., triangles are closed and three-sided) versus non-defining attributes (e.g., color, orientation, overall size); build and draw shapes that possess defining attributes.
RI.M1.G.A.2: Compose two-dimensional shapes (rectangles, squares, trapezoids, triangles, half-circles, and quarter-circles) or three-dimensional shapes (cubes, right rectangular prisms, right circular cones, and right circular cylinders) to create a composite shape, and compose new shapes from the compositeshape.
RI.M1.G.A.3: Partition circles and rectangles into two and four equal shares, describe the shares using the words halves, fourths, and quarters, and use the phrases half of, fourth of, and quarter of. Describe the whole as two of, or four of the shares. Understand for these examples that decomposing into more equal shares creates smallershares.
RI.E2.RL.1: Ask and answer such questions as who, what, where, when, why, and how to demonstrate understanding of key details in a text.
RI.E2.RL.2: Retell stories, including fables and folktales from diverse cultures, and determine their central message, lesson, or moral.
RI.E2.RL.3: Describe how characters in a story respond to major events and challenges.
RI.E2.RL.4: Describe how words and phrases (e.g., regular beats, alliteration, rhymes, repeated lines) supply rhythm and meaning in a story, poem, or song.
RI.E2.RL.5: Describe the overall structure of a story, including describing how the beginning introduces the story and the ending concludes the action.
RI.E2.RL.6: Explain what dialogue is and how it can reveal characters' thoughts and perspectives.
RI.E2.RL.7: Use information gained from the illustrations and words in a print or digital text to demonstrate understanding of its characters, setting, or plot.
RI.E2.RL.9: Compare and contrast two or more versions of the same story (e.g., Cinderella stories) by different authors or from different cultures.
RI.E2.RL.10: Independently and proficiently read and comprehend literary texts representing a variety of genres, cultures, and perspectives and exhibiting complexity appropriate for at least grade 2.
RI.E2.RI.E1: Ask and answer such questions as who, what, where, when, why, and how to demonstrate understanding of key details in a text.
RI.E2.RI.E2: Identify the main topic of a multi-paragraph text as well as the focus of specific paragraphs within the text.
RI.E2.RI.E3: Describe the connection between a series of historical events, scientific ideas or concepts, mathematical ideas or concepts, or steps in technical procedures in a text.
RI.E2.RI.E4: Determine the meaning of words and phrases in a text relevant to a grade 2 topic or subject area.
RI.E2.RI.E5: Know and use various text features (e.g., captions, bold print, subheadings, glossaries, indexes, electronic menus, icons) to locate key facts or information in a text efficiently.
RI.E2.RI.E6: Identify the main purpose of a text, including what the author wants to answer, explain, or describe.
RI.E2.RI.E7: Explain how specific images (e.g., a diagram showing how a machine works) contribute to and clarify a text.
RI.E2.RI.E8: Describe how reasons support specific points the author makes in a text.
RI.E2.RI.E9: Compare and contrast the most important points presented by two texts on the same topic.
RI.E2.RI.E10: Independently and proficiently read and comprehend informational texts, including history/social studies, science, mathematical, and technical texts, exhibiting complexity appropriate for at least grade 2.
RI.E2.RF.3: Know and apply grade-level phonics and word analysis skills in decoding words.
RI.E2.RF.3.a: Distinguish long and short vowels when reading regularly spelled one-syllable words.
RI.E2.RF.3.b: Know spelling-sound correspondences for additional common vowel teams.
RI.E2.RF.3.c: Decode regularly spelled two-syllable words with long vowels.
RI.E2.RF.3.d: Decode words with common prefixes and suffixes.
RI.E2.RF.3.e: Identify words with inconsistent but common spelling-sound correspondences.
RI.E2.RF.3.f: Recognize and read grade-appropriate irregularly spelled words.
RI.E2.RF.4: Read with sufficient accuracy and fluency to support comprehension.
RI.E2.RF.4.a: Read grade-level text with purpose and understanding.
RI.E2.RF.4.b: Read grade-level text orally with accuracy, appropriate rate, and expression on successive readings.
RI.E2.RF.4.c: Use context to confirm or self-correct word recognition and understanding, rereading as necessary.
RI.E2.W.1: Write opinion pieces that introduce the topic or book they are writing about, state an opinion, supply reasons that support the opinion, use linking words (e.g., because, and, also) to connect opinion and reasons, and provide a concluding statement or section.
RI.E2.W.2: Write informative/explanatory texts that introduce a topic, use facts and definitions to develop points, and provide a concluding statement or section.
RI.E2.W.3: Write narratives in prose or poem form that recount a well-elaborated event or experience, or a set of events or experiences; include details and dialogue to show actions, thoughts, and feelings; use temporal words to signal order where appropriate; and provide a sense of closure.
RI.E2.W.3.a: For poems, use words and phrases that form patterns of sounds (e.g., regular beats, alliteration, end rhymes, repeated sounds in words or lines) to create structure.
RI.E2.W.4: Produce writing in which the development and organization are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.
RI.E2.W.6: Demonstrate the ability to choose and use appropriate vocabulary.
RI.E2.W.7: With guidance and support from adults, use a variety of digital tools to produce and publish writing, including in collaboration with peers.
RI.E2.W.8: Participate in shared research and writing projects (e.g., read a number of books on a single topic to produce a report; record science observations).
RI.E2.W.10: Write routinely for a range of tasks, purposes, and audiences.
RI.E2.SL.1: Participate in collaborative conversations with diverse partners about grade 2 topics and texts with peers and adults in small and larger groups.
RI.E2.SL.1.a: Follow agreed-upon rules for discussions (e.g., gaining the floor in respectful ways, listening to others with care, speaking one at a time about the topics and texts under discussion).
RI.E2.SL.1.b: Build on others' talk in conversations by linking their comments to the remarks of others.
RI.E2.SL.1.c: Ask for clarification and further explanation as needed about the topics and texts under discussion.
RI.E2.SL.2: Recount or describe key ideas or details from a text read aloud or information presented orally or through other media.
RI.E2.SL.3: Ask and answer questions about what a speaker says in order to clarify comprehension, gather additional information, or deepen understanding of a topic or issue.
RI.E2.SL.4: Tell a story, recount an experience, or explain how to solve a mathematical problem with appropriate facts and relevant, descriptive details, speaking audibly in coherent sentences and using appropriate vocabulary.
RI.E2.SL.5: Create audio recordings of stories or poems; add drawings or other visual displays to stories or descriptions of experiences when appropriate to clarify ideas, thoughts, and feelings.
RI.E2.SL.6: Produce complete sentences when appropriate to task and situation in order to provide requested detail or clarification.
RI.E2.L.1: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking; retain and further develop language skills learned in previous grades.
RI.E2.L.1.a: Produce and expand complete simple and compound declarative, interrogative, imperative, and exclamatory sentences and choose among sentence types depending on the meaning to be conveyed.
RI.E2.L.1.b: Use adjectives and adverbs in sentences and choose between them depending on what is to be modified.
RI.E2.L.1.c: Use collective nouns and frequently occurring irregular plural nouns.
RI.E2.L.1.e: Form and use the past tense of frequently occurring irregular verbs.
RI.E2.L.2: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.
RI.E2.L.2.a: Print upper- and lowercase letters legibly and fluently.
RI.E2.L.2.b: Capitalize holidays, product names, and geographic names.
RI.E2.L.2.c: Use commas in greetings and closings of letters.
RI.E2.L.2.d: Use an apostrophe to form contractions and frequently occurring possessives.
RI.E2.L.2.e: Generalize learned spelling patterns when writing words (e.g., cage → badge; boy → boil).
RI.E2.L.2.f: Consult reference materials, including beginning dictionaries, as needed to check and correct spellings.
RI.E2.L.2.g: Demonstrate understanding that context determines whether the writer uses a numeral or a written number (e.g., numerals in 1 + 3 = 4, but written words in “When I was one, I was just begun, / When I was two, I was still quite new” from A. A. Milne's poem “Now We Are Six”).
RI.E2.L.3: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening.
RI.E2.L.3.a: Compare formal and informal uses of English.
RI.E2.L.4: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grade 2 reading and content, choosing flexibly from an array of strategies.
RI.E2.L.4.a: Use sentence-level context as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.
RI.E2.L.4.b: Determine the meaning of the new word formed when a known prefix is added to a known word (e.g., happy/unhappy, tell/retell).
RI.E2.L.4.c: Use a known root word as a clue to the meaning of an unknown word with the same root (e.g., addition, additional).
RI.E2.L.4.d: Use knowledge of the meaning of individual words to predict the meaning of compound words (e.g., birdhouse, lighthouse, housefly; bookshelf, notebook, bookmark).
RI.E2.L.4.e: Use glossaries and beginning dictionaries, both print and digital, to determine or clarify the meaning of words and phrases.
RI.E2.L.4.f: Recognize and use appropriately abbreviations related to grade-level content or commonly used in everyday life (e.g., a.m., p.m.).
RI.E2.L.4.g: Recognize and use appropriately symbols related to grade-level content or commonly used in everyday life (e.g., $, ¢).
RI.E2.L.5: Demonstrate understanding of word relationships and nuances in word meanings.
RI.E2.L.5.a: Identify real-life connections between words and their use (e.g., describe foods that are spicy or juicy).
RI.E2.RF.5.b: Distinguish shades of meaning among closely related verbs (e.g., toss, throw, hurl) and closely related adjectives (e.g., thin, slender, skinny, scrawny).
RI.E2.L.6: Use words and phrases acquired through conversations, activities in the grade 2 curriculum, reading and being read to, and responding to texts, including using adjectives and adverbs to describe.
RI.M2.OA.A: Represent and solve problems involving addition and subtraction.
RI.M2.OA.A.1: Use addition and subtraction within `100` to solve one- and two-step word problems involving situations of adding to, taking from, putting together, taking apart, and comparing, with unknowns in all positions, e.g., by using drawings and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.
RI.M2.OA.B.2: Fluently add and subtract within 20 using mental strategies. By end of grade 2, know from memory all sums of two single-digit numbers and related differences.
RI.M2.OA.C: Work with equal groups of objects to gain foundations for multiplication.
RI.M2.OA.C.3: Determine whether a group of objects (up to 20) has an odd or even number of members, e.g., by pairing objects or counting them by `2text(s)`; write an equation to express an even number as a sum of two equal addends.
RI.M2.OA.C.4: Use addition to find the total number of objects arranged in rectangular arrays with up to five rows and up to five columns; write an equation to express the total as a sum of equal addends.
RI.M2.NBT.A.1: Understand that the three digits of a three-digit number represent amounts of hundreds, tens, and ones; e.g., 706 equals 7 hundreds, 0 tens, and 6 ones. Understand the following as special cases:
RI.M2.NBT.A.1.a: 100 can be thought of as a bundle of ten tens - called a “hundred.”
RI.M2.NBT.A.1.b: The numbers 100, 200, 300, 400, 500, 600, 700, 800, 900 refer to one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine hundreds (and 0 tens and 0ones).
RI.M2.NBT.A.2: Count within `1text(,)000`; skip-count by `5text(s),10text(s),and100text(s)`. Identify patterns in skip counting starting at any number.
RI.M2.NBT.A.3: Read and write numbers to `1text(,)000` using base-ten numerals, number names, and expanded form.
RI.M2.NBT.A.4: Compare two three-digit numbers based on meanings of the hundreds, tens, and ones digits, using `>,=,and<` symbols to record the results of comparisons.
RI.M2.NBT.B: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to add and subtract.
RI.M2.NBT.B.5: Fluently add and subtract within `100` using strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction.
RI.M2.NBT.B.6: Add up to four two-digit numbers using strategies based on place value and properties of operations.
RI.M2.NBT.B.7: Add and subtract within `1text(,)000`, using concrete models or drawings and strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction; relate the strategy to a written method. Understand that in adding or subtracting three-digit numbers, one adds or subtracts hundreds and hundreds, tens and tens, ones and ones; and sometimes it is necessary to compose or decompose tens or hundreds.
RI.M2.NBT.B.8: Mentally add `10or100` to a given number 100-900, and mentally subtract `10or100` from a given number 100-900.
RI.M2.NBT.B.9: Explain why addition and subtraction strategies work, using place value and the properties of operations.
RI.M2.MD.A: Measure and estimate lengths in standard units.
RI.M2.MD.A.1: Measure the length of an object by selecting and using appropriate tools such as rulers, yardsticks, meter sticks, and measuring tapes.
RI.M2.MD.A.2: Measure the length of an object twice, using length units of different lengths for the two measurements; describe how the two measurements relate to the size of the unit chosen.
RI.M2.MD.A.3: Estimate lengths using units of inches, feet, centimeters, and meters.
RI.M2.MD.A.4: Measure to determine how much longer one object is than another, expressing the length difference in terms of a standard length unit.
RI.M2.MD.B: Relate addition and subtraction to length.
RI.M2.MD.B.5: Use addition and subtraction within `100` to solve word problems involving lengths that are given in the same units, e.g., by using drawings (such as drawings of rulers) and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.
RI.M2.MD.B.6: Represent whole numbers as lengths from `0` on a number line diagram with equally spaced points corresponding to the numbers 0, 1, 2, ..., and represent whole-number sums and differences within `100` on a number line diagram.
RI.M2.MD.C.7: Tell and write time from analog and digital clocks to the nearest five minutes, using a.m. and p.m.
RI.M2.MD.C.7.a: Know the relationships of time, including seconds in a minute, minutes in an hour, hours in a day, days in a week; days in a month and a year and approximate number of weeks in a month and weeks in a year.
RI.M2.MD.C.8: Solve word problems involving dollar bills, quarters, dimes, nickels, and pennies (up to $10), using $and ¢ symbols appropriately and whole dollar amounts.
RI.M2.MD.D.9: Generate measurement data by measuring lengths of several objects to the nearest whole unit, or by making repeated measurements of the same object. Organize and record the data on a line plot (dot plot) where the horizontal scale is marked off in whole-numberunits.
RI.M2.MD.D.10: Draw a picture graph and a bar graph (with single-unit scale) to represent a data set with up to four categories. Solve simple put-together, take-apart, and compare problems, using information presented in a bar graph.
RI.M2.G.A: Reason with shapes and their attributes.
RI.M2.G.A.1: Recognize and draw shapes having specified attributes, such as a given number of angles or a given number of equal faces. Identify triangles, squares, rectangles, rhombuses, trapezoids, pentagons, hexagons, and cubes.
RI.M2.G.A.2: Partition a rectangle into rows and columns of same-size squares and count to find the total number of them.
RI.M2.G.A.3: Partition circles and rectangles into two, three, or four equal shares, describe the shares using the words halves, thirds, half of, a third of, etc., and describe the whole as two halves, three thirds, four fourths. Recognize that equal shares of identical wholes need not have the sameshape.
RI.E3.RL.1: Ask and answer questions to demonstrate understanding of a text, referring explicitly to the text as the basis for the answers.
RI.E3.RL.2: Retell stories, including fables, folktales, and myths from diverse cultures; determine the central message, lesson, or moral and explain how it is conveyed through key details in a text.
RI.E3.RL.3: Describe characters in a story (e.g., their traits, motivations, or feelings) and explain how their actions contribute to the sequence of events.
RI.E3.RL.4: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, distinguishing literal from figurative language.
RI.E3.RL.5: Identify common structural elements of fiction (e.g., problem, solution); describe how each successive part of a text builds on earlier sections.
RI.E3.RL.6: Distinguish their own point of view from that of a text's narrator or those of its characters.
RI.E3.RL.7: Explain how specific aspects of a text's illustrations contribute to what is conveyed by the words in a story (e.g., create mood, emphasize aspects of a character or setting).
RI.E3.RL.9: Compare and contrast the themes, settings, and plots of stories written by the same author about the same or similar characters (e.g., in books from a series).
RI.E3.RL.10: Independently and proficiently read and comprehend literary texts representing a variety of genres, cultures, and perspectives and exhibiting complexity appropriate for at least grade 3.
RI.E3.RI.E1: Ask and answer questions to demonstrate understanding of a text, referring explicitly to the text as the basis for the answers.
RI.E3.RI.E2: Determine the main idea of a text; recount the key details and explain how they support the main idea.
RI.E3.RI.E3: Describe the relationship between a series of historical events, scientific ideas or concepts, mathematical ideas or concepts, or steps in technical procedures in a text, using language that pertains to time, sequence, and cause/effect.
RI.E3.RI.E4: Determine the meaning of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases in a text relevant to a grade 3 topic or subject area.
RI.E3.RI.E5: Use text features and search tools (e.g., key words, sidebars, hyperlinks) to locate information relevant to a given topic efficiently.
RI.E3.RI.E6: Distinguish their own point of view from that of the author of a text.
RI.E3.RI.E7: Use information gained from illustrations (e.g., maps, photographs) and the words, numbers, and symbols in a text to demonstrate understanding of the text (e.g., where, when, why, and how key events occur).
RI.E3.RI.E8: Describe the logical connection between particular sentences and paragraphs in a text (e.g., comparison, cause/effect, first/second/third in a sequence).
RI.E3.RI.E9: Compare and contrast the most important points and key details presented in two texts on the same topic.
RI.E3.RI.E10: Independently and proficiently read and comprehend informational texts, including history/social studies, science, mathematical, and technical texts, exhibiting complexity appropriate for at least grade 3.
RI.E3.RF.3: Know and apply grade-level phonics and word analysis skills in decoding words.
RI.E3.RF.3.a: Identify and know the meaning of the most common prefixes and derivational suffixes.
RI.E3.RF.3.b: Decode words with common Latin suffixes.
RI.E3.RF.4: Read with sufficient accuracy and fluency to support comprehension.
RI.E3.RF.4.a: Read grade-level text with purpose and understanding.
RI.E3.RF.4.b: Read grade-level prose and poetry orally with accuracy, appropriate rate, and expression on successive readings.
RI.E3.RF.4.c: Use context to confirm or self-correct word recognition and understanding, rereading as necessary.
RI.E3.W.1: Write opinion pieces on topics or texts, supporting an opinion with reasons.
RI.E3.W.1.a: Introduce the topic or text they are writing about, state an opinion, and create an organizational structure that lists reasons.
RI.E3.W.1.b: Provide reasons that support the opinion.
RI.E3.W.1.c: Use linking words and phrases (e.g., because, therefore, since, for example) to connect opinion and reasons.
RI.E3.W.1.d: Provide a concluding statement or section.
RI.E3.W.2: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine a topic and convey ideas and information clearly.
RI.E3.W.2.a: Introduce a topic and group-related information together; include illustrations when useful to aiding comprehension.
RI.E3.W.2.b: Develop the topic with facts, definitions, and details.
RI.E3.W.2.c: Use linking words and phrases (e.g., also, another, and, more, but) to connect ideas within categories of information.
RI.E3.W.2.d: Provide a concluding statement or section.
RI.E3.W.3: Write narratives in prose or poem form to develop experiences or events using effective literary techniques, descriptive details, and clear sequences.
RI.E3.W.3.a: Establish a situation and introduce a speaker, narrator, and/or characters; organize an appropriate narrative sequence.
RI.E3.W.3.b: Use dialogue and descriptions of actions, thoughts, and feelings to develop experiences or events or show responses to situations.
RI.E3.W.3.c: Use figurative language to suggest images.
RI.E3.W.3.d: Use temporal words and phrases to signal order where appropriate.
RI.E3.W.3.f: For poems, use words and phrases that form patterns of sound (e.g., rhyme, repetition of sounds within words or within lines) to create meaning or effect.
RI.E3.W.4: Produce writing in which the development and organization are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.
RI.E3.W.5: Develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, and editing.
RI.E3.W.5.a: Demonstrate command of standard English conventions.
RI.E3.W.5.b: Demonstrate the ability to choose and use appropriate vocabulary.
RI.E3.W.6: Use technology to produce and publish writing (using keyboarding skills) as well as to interact and collaborate with others.
RI.E3.W.7: Conduct short research projects that build knowledge about a topic.
RI.E3.W.8: Recall information from experiences or gather information from print and digital sources; take brief notes on sources and sort evidence into provided categories.
RI.E3.W.10: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of discipline-specific tasks, purposes, and audiences.
RI.E3.SL.1: Engage effectively in a range of collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in groups, and teacher-led) with diverse partners on grade 3 topics and texts, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly.
RI.E3.SL.1.a: Come to discussions prepared, having read or studied required material; explicitly draw on that preparation and other information known about the topic to explore ideas under discussion.
RI.E3.SL.1.b: Follow agreed-upon rules for discussions (e.g., gaining the floor in respectful ways, listening to others with care, speaking one at a time about the topics and texts under discussion).
RI.E3.SL.1.c: Ask questions to check understanding of information presented, stay on topic, and link their comments to the remarks of others.
RI.E3.SL.1.d: Explain their own ideas and understanding in light of the discussion.
RI.E3.SL.2: Determine the main ideas and supporting details of a text read aloud or information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.
RI.E3.SL.3: Ask and answer questions about information from a speaker, offering appropriate elaboration and detail.
RI.E3.SL.4: Report on a topic, text, or solution to a mathematical problem, tell a story, or recount an experience with appropriate facts and relevant, descriptive details, speaking clearly at an understandable pace and using appropriate vocabulary.
RI.E3.SL.5: Create engaging audio recordings of stories or poems that demonstrate fluid reading at an understandable pace; add visual displays when appropriate to emphasize or enhance certain facts or details.
RI.E3.SL.6: Speak in complete sentences when appropriate to task and situation in order to provide requested detail or clarification.
RI.E3.L.1: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking; retain and further develop language skills learned in previous grades.
RI.E3.L.1.a: Produce, expand, and rearrange complete simple, compound, and complex sentences.
RI.E3.L.1.c: Use verbs in the present, past, and future tenses and choose among them depending on the overall meaning of the sentence.
RI.E3.L.1.d: Use coordinating and subordinating conjunctions and choose between them depending on the overall meaning of the sentence.
RI.E3.L.1.e: Form and use comparative and superlative adjectives and adverbs and choose between them depending on what is to be modified and the overall meaning of the sentence.
RI.E3.L.1.g: Form and use regular and irregular plural nouns and the past tense of regular and irregular verbs.
RI.E3.L.2: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.
RI.E3.L.2.a: Write legibly and fluently by hand, using either printing or cursive handwriting.
RI.E3.L.2.d: Use commas and quotation marks in dialogue.
RI.E3.L.2.f: Use conventional spelling for high-frequency and other studied words and for adding suffixes to base words (e.g., sitting, smiled, cries, happiness).
RI.E3.L.2.g: Demonstrate understanding that numerals used at the beginning of a sentence are written as words and capitalized (e.g., “Three pandas could be seen eating leaves high in the bamboo grove.”).
RI.E3.L.2.h: Use spelling patterns and generalizations (e.g., word families, position-based spellings, syllable patterns, ending rules, meaningful word parts) in writing words.
RI.E3.L.2.i: Consult reference materials, including beginning dictionaries, as needed to check and correct spellings.
RI.E3.L.3: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening.
RI.E3.L.3.a: Choose words and phrases for effect.
RI.E3.L.3.b: Recognize and observe differences between the conventions of spoken and written English.
RI.E3.L.4: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grade 3 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.
RI.E3.L.4.a: Use sentence-level context as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.
RI.E3.L.4.b: Determine the meaning of the new word formed when a known affix is added to a known word (e.g., agreeable/disagreeable, comfortable/uncomfortable, care/careless, heat/preheat).
RI.E3.L.4.c: Use a known root word as a clue to the meaning of an unknown word with the same root (e.g., company, companion).
RI.E3.L.4.d: Use glossaries or beginning dictionaries, both print and digital, to determine or clarify the precise meaning of key words and phrases.
RI.E3.L.4.e: Recognize and use appropriately abbreviations related to grade-level content or common in everyday life (e.g., N, S, E, W on a map).
RI.E3.L.4.f: Recognize and use appropriately symbols related to grade-level content or common in everyday life (e.g., <, >).
RI.E3.L.5: Demonstrate understanding of word relationships and nuances in word meanings.
RI.E3.L.5.a: Distinguish the literal and nonliteral meanings of words and phrases in context (e.g., take steps).
RI.E3.RF.5.b: Identify real-life connections between words and their use (e.g., describe people who are friendly or helpful).
RI.E3.RF.5.c: Distinguish shades of meaning among related words that describe states of mind or degrees of certainty (e.g., knew, believed, suspected, heard, wondered).
RI.E3.L.6: Acquire and use accurately grade-appropriate conversational, general academic, and domain-specific words and phrases, including those that signal spatial and temporal relationships.
RI.M3.OA.A: Represent and solve problems involving multiplication and division.
RI.M3.OA.A.1: Interpret products of whole numbers, e.g., interpret `5xx7` as the total number of objects in five groups of seven objects each.
RI.M3.OA.A.2: Interpret whole-number quotients of whole numbers, e.g., interpret `56-:8` as the number of objects in each share when `56` objects are partitioned equally into `8` shares, or as a number of shares when `56` objects are partitioned into equal shares of `8` objects each.
RI.M3.OA.A.3: Use multiplication and division within `100` to solve word problems in situations involving equal groups, arrays, and measurement quantities, e.g., by using drawings and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.
RI.M3.OA.A.4: Determine the unknown whole number in a multiplication or division equation relating three whole numbers.
RI.M3.OA.B: Understand properties of multiplication and the relationship between multiplication and division.
RI.M3.OA.B.5: Apply properties of operations to multiply.
RI.M3.OA.B.6: Understand division as an unknown-factor problem.
RI.M3.OA.C.7: Fluently multiply and divide within `100`, using strategies such as the relationship between multiplication and division (e.g., knowing that `8xx5=40`, one knows `40-:5=8`) or properties of operations. By the end of grade 3, know from memory all products of two single-digit numbers and related division facts.
RI.M3.OA.D: Solve problems involving the four operations, and identify and explain patterns in arithmetic.
RI.M3.OA.D.8: Solve two-step word problems using the four operations for problems posed with whole numbers and having whole number answers. Represent these problems using equations with a letter standing for the unknown quantity. Assess the reasonableness of answers using mental computation and estimation strategies, including rounding.
RI.M3.OA.D.9: Identify arithmetic patterns (including patterns in the addition table or multiplication table) and explain them using properties of operations.
RI.M3.NBT.A: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to perform multi-digit arithmetic.
RI.M3.NBT.A.1: Use place value understanding to round whole numbers to the nearest `10or100`.
RI.M3.NBT.A.2: Fluently add and subtract within `1text(,)000` using strategies and algorithms based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction.
RI.M3.NBT.A.3: Multiply one-digit whole numbers by multiples of `10` in the range `10-90` (e.g., `9xx80,5xx60`) using strategies based on place value and properties of operations.
RI.M3.NF.A: Develop understanding of fractions as numbers for fractions with denominators `2,3,4,6,and8`.
RI.M3.NF.A.1: Understand a fraction `1/b` as the quantity formed by `1` part when a whole (a single unit) is partitioned into `b` equal parts; understand a fraction `a/b` as the quantity formed by a parts of size `1/b`.
RI.M3.NF.A.2: Understand a fraction as a number on the number line; represent fractions on a number line diagram.
RI.M3.NF.A.2.a: Represent a unit fraction, `1/b`, on a number line diagram by defining the interval from `0` to `1` as the whole and partitioning it into `b` equal parts. Recognize that each part has size `1/b`, and that the fraction `1/b` is located `1/b` of a whole unit from `0` on the number line.
RI.M3.NF.A.2.b: Represent a fraction `a/b` on a number line diagram by marking off a lengths `1/b` from `0`. Recognize that the resulting interval has size `a/b` and that its endpoint locates the number `a/b` on the number line.
RI.M3.NF.A.3: Explain equivalence of fractions in special cases, and compare fractions by reasoning about their size.
RI.M3.NF.A.3.a: Understand two fractions as equivalent (equal) if they are the same size, or the same point on a number line.
RI.M3.NF.A.3.b: Recognize and generate simple equivalent fractions, e.g., 1/2 = 2 /4, 4/6 = 2/3. Explain why the fractions are equivalent, e.g., by using a visual fraction model.
RI.M3.NF.A.3.c: Express whole numbers as fractions, and recognize fractions that are equivalent to whole numbers.
RI.M3.NF.A.3.d: Compare two fractions with the same numerator or the same denominator by reasoning about their size. Recognize that comparisons are valid only when the two fractions refer to the same whole. Record the results of comparisons with the symbols `>,=,or<`, and justify the conclusions, e.g., by using a visual fraction model.
RI.M3.MD.A: Solve problems involving measurement and estimation of intervals of time, liquid volumes, and masses of objects.
RI.M3.MD.A.1: Tell and write time to the nearest minute and measure time intervals in `text(minutes)`. Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of time intervals in `text(minutes)`, e.g., by representing the problem on a number line diagram.
RI.M3.MD.A.2: Measure and estimate liquid volumes and masses of objects using standard metric units of grams (g), kilograms (kg), and liters (l). Add, subtract, multiply, or divide to solve one-step word problems involving masses or volumes that are given in the same metric units, e.g., by using drawings (such as a beaker with a measurement scale) to represent the problem.
RI.M3.MD.B.3: Draw a scaled picture graph and a scaled bar graph to represent a data set with several categories. Solve one- and two-step “how many more” and “how many less” problems using information presented in scaled bar graphs.
RI.M3.MD.B.4: Generate measurement data by measuring lengths of objects using rulers marked with `text(halves)andtext(fourths of an inch)`. Record and show the data by making a line plot (dot plot), where the horizontal scale is marked off in appropriate units - whole numbers, halves, or fourths.
RI.M3.MD.C: Geometric measurement: understand concepts of area and relate area to multiplication and to addition.
RI.M3.MD.C.5: Recognize area as an attribute of plane figures and understand concepts of area measurement.
RI.M3.MD.C.5.a: A square with side length of one unit, called “a unit square,” is said to have “one square unit” of area, and can be used to measure area.
RI.M3.MD.C.5.b: A plane figure which can be covered without gaps or overlaps by `n` `text(unit squares)` is said to have an area of `n` `text(square units)`.
RI.M3.MD.C.6: Measure areas by counting unit squares (square cm, square m, square in., square ft., and non-standard units).
RI.M3.MD.C.7: Relate area to the operations of multiplication and addition.
RI.M3.MD.C.7.a: Find the area of a rectangle with whole-number side lengths by tiling it, and show that the area is the same as would be found by multiplying the side lengths.
RI.M3.MD.C.7.b: Multiply side lengths to find areas of rectangles with whole-number side lengths in the context of solving real-world and mathematical problems, and represent whole-number products as rectangular areas in mathematicalreasoning.
RI.M3.MD.C.7.c: Use tiling to show in a concrete case that the area of a rectangle with whole-number side lengths `aandb+c` is the sum of `axxbandaxxc`. Use area models to represent the distributive property in mathematical reasoning.
RI.M3.MD.C.7.d: Recognize area as additive. Find areas of rectilinear figures by decomposing them into non-overlapping rectangles and adding the areas of the non-overlapping parts, applying this technique to solve real-world problems.
RI.M3.MD.D: Geometric measurement: recognize perimeter as an attribute of plane figures and distinguish between linear and area measures.
RI.M3.MD.D.8: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving perimeters of polygons, including finding the perimeter given the side lengths, finding an unknown side length, and exhibiting rectangles with the same perimeter and different areas or with the same area and different perimeters.
RI.M3.G.A: Reason with shapes and their attributes.
RI.M3.G.A.1: Understand that shapes in different categories (e.g., rhombuses, rectangles, and others) may share attributes (e.g., having four sides), and that the shared attributes can define a larger category (e.g., quadrilaterals). Compare and classify shapes by their sides and angles (right angle/non-right angle). Recognize rhombuses, rectangles, squares, and trapezoids as examples of quadrilaterals, and draw examples of quadrilaterals that do not belong to any of these subcategories.
RI.M3.G.A.2: Partition shapes into parts with equal areas. Express the area of each part as a unit fraction of the whole.
RI.E4.RL.1: Refer to details and examples in a text when explaining what the text states explicitly and when drawing inferences from the text.
RI.E4.RL.2: Determine a theme of a story, drama, or poem from details in the text; summarize a text.
RI.E4.RL.3: Describe in depth a character, setting, or event in a story or drama, drawing on specific details in the text (e.g., a character's thoughts, words, or actions).
RI.E4.RL.4: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including those that allude to significant characters found in mythology (e.g., Herculean); explain how figurative language (e.g., simile, metaphor) enriches a text.
RI.E4.RL.5: Explain major differences among prose, poetry, and drama and refer to the structural elements of each (e.g., paragraphs and chapters for prose; stanza and verse for poetry; scene, stage directions, cast of characters for drama) when writing or speaking about a text.
RI.E4.RL.6: Compare and contrast the points of view from which different stories are narrated, including the difference between first- and third-person narrations.
RI.E4.RL.7: Make connections between a written story or drama and its visual or oral presentation, identifying where the presentation reflects specific descriptions and directions in the written text.
RI.E4.RL.9: Compare and contrast the treatment of similar themes and topics (e.g., opposition of good and evil) and patterns of events (e.g., the quest) in stories, myths, and traditional literature from different cultures.
RI.E4.RL.10: Independently and proficiently read and comprehend literary texts representing a variety of genres, cultures, and perspectives and exhibiting complexity appropriate for at least grade 4.
RI.E4.RI.E1: Refer to details and examples in a text when explaining what the text states explicitly and when drawing inferences from the text.
RI.E4.RI.E2: Determine the main idea of a text and explain how it is supported by key details; summarize a text.
RI.E4.RI.E3: Explain events, procedures, ideas, or concepts in a historical, scientific, mathematical, or technical text, including what happened and why, based on specific information in the text.
RI.E4.RI.E4: Determine the meaning of general academic and domain-specific words or phrases in a text relevant to a grade 4 topic or subject area.
RI.E4.RI.E5: Describe the overall structure (e.g., chronology, comparison, cause/effect, problem/solution) of events, ideas, concepts, or information in a text or part of a text.
RI.E4.RI.E6: Compare and contrast a firsthand and secondhand account of the same event or topic; describe the differences in focus and the information provided.
RI.E4.RI.E7: Interpret information presented visually, orally, or quantitatively (e.g., in charts, graphs, diagrams, timelines, animations, or interactive elements on webpages) and explain how the information contributes to an understanding of the text in which it appears.
RI.E4.RI.E8: Explain how an author uses reasons and evidence to support particular points in a text.
RI.E4.RI.E9: Integrate information from two texts on the same topic in order to write or speak knowledgeably about the subject.
RI.E4.RI.E10: Independently and proficiently read and comprehend informational texts, including history/social studies, science, mathematical, and technical texts, exhibiting complexity appropriate for at least grade 4.
RI.E4.RF.3: Know and apply grade-level phonics and word analysis skills in decoding words.
RI.E4.RF.3.a: Use combined knowledge of all letter-sound correspondences, syllabication patterns, and morphology (e.g., roots and affixes) to read accurately unfamiliar multisyllabic words in context and out of context.
RI.E4.RF.4: Read with sufficient accuracy and fluency to support comprehension.
RI.E4.RF.4.a: Read grade-level text with purpose and understanding.
RI.E4.RF.4.b: Read grade-level prose and poetry orally with accuracy, appropriate rate, and expression on successive readings.
RI.E4.RF.4.c: Use context to confirm or self-correct word recognition and understanding, rereading as necessary.
RI.E4.W.1: Write opinion pieces on topics or texts, supporting a point of view with reasons and information.
RI.E4.W.1.a: Introduce a topic or text clearly, state an opinion, and create an organizational structure in which related ideas are grouped in paragraphs and sections to support the writer's purpose.
RI.E4.W.1.b: Provide reasons that are supported by facts and details.
RI.E4.W.1.c: Link opinion and reasons using words and phrases (e.g., for instance, in order to, in addition).
RI.E4.W.1.d: Provide a concluding statement or section related to the opinion presented.
RI.E4.W.2: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine a topic and convey ideas and information clearly.
RI.E4.W.2.a: Introduce a topic clearly and group related information in paragraphs and sections; include text features (e.g., headings), illustrations, and multimedia when useful to aiding comprehension.
RI.E4.W.2.b: Develop the topic with facts, definitions, concrete details, quotations, or other information and examples related to the topic.
RI.E4.W.2.c: Link ideas within categories of information using words and phrases (e.g., another, for example, also, because).
RI.E4.W.2.d: Use precise language and domain-specific vocabulary to inform about or explain the topic.
RI.E4.W.2.e: Provide a concluding statement or section related to the information or explanation presented.
RI.E4.W.3: Write narratives in prose or poem form to develop experiences or events using effective literary techniques, descriptive details, and clear sequences.
RI.E4.W.3.a: Orient the reader by establishing a situation and introducing a speaker, narrator, and/or characters; organize an appropriate narrative sequence.
RI.E4.W.3.b: Use dialogue and description to develop experiences or events or show responses to situations.
RI.E4.W.3.c: Use a variety of transitional words and phrases to manage sequence.
RI.E4.W.3.d: Use concrete words and phrases, figurative language such as similes and metaphors, and sensory details to convey experiences or events precisely.
RI.E4.W.3.e: Provide a sense of closure appropriate to the narrated experiences or events.
RI.E4.W.3.f: For poems, use patterns of sound (e.g., rhyme, rhythm, alliteration, consonance) and visual patterns (e.g., line length, grouped lines as stanzas or verses) to create works that are distinctly different in form from prose narratives.
RI.E4.W.4: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development and organization are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.
RI.E4.W.5: Develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, and editing.
RI.E4.W.5.a: Demonstrate command of standard English conventions.
RI.E4.W.5.b: Demonstrate the ability to use general academic and domain-specific vocabulary appropriately.
RI.E4.W.6: Use technology, including current web-based communication platforms, to produce and publish writing as well as to interact and collaborate with others; demonstrate sufficient command of keyboarding skills to type a minimum of one page in a single sitting.
RI.E4.W.7: Conduct short research projects that build knowledge through investigation of different aspects of a topic.
RI.E4.W.8: Recall relevant information from experiences or gather relevant information from print and digital sources; take notes and categorize information, and provide a list of sources.
RI.E4.W.9: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support written analysis, reflection, and research, applying one or more grade 4 standards for Reading Literature or Reading Information as needed.
RI.E4.W.10: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of discipline-specific tasks, purposes, and audiences.
