RI.E4.SL.1: Engage effectively in a range of collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in groups, and teacher-led) with diverse partners on grade 4 topics and texts, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly.
RI.E4.SL.1.a: Come to discussions prepared, having read or studied required material; explicitly draw on that preparation and other information known about the topic to explore ideas under discussion.
RI.E4.SL.1.b: Follow agreed-upon rules for discussions and carry out assigned roles.
RI.E4.SL.1.c: Pose and respond to specific questions to clarify or follow up on information, and make comments that contribute to the discussion and link to the remarks of others.
RI.E4.SL.1.d: Review the key ideas expressed and explain their own ideas and understanding in light of the discussion.
RI.E4.SL.2: Paraphrase portions of a written text read aloud or information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.
RI.E4.SL.3: Identify the reasons and evidence a speaker provides to support particular points.
RI.E4.SL.4: Report on a topic, text, procedure, or solution to a mathematical problem, tell a story, or recount an experience in an organized manner, using appropriate facts and relevant, descriptive details to support main ideas or themes; speak clearly at an understandable pace and use appropriate vocabulary.
RI.E4.SL.5: Add audio recordings and visual displays to presentations when appropriate to enhance the development of main ideas or themes.
RI.E4.SL.6: Differentiate between contexts that call for formal English (e.g., presenting research findings) and situations where informal discourse is appropriate (e.g., small-group discussion); use formal English when appropriate to task and situation.
RI.E4.L.1: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking; retain and further develop language skills learned in previous grades.
RI.E4.L.1.a: Produce complete sentences, using knowledge of subject and predicate to recognize and correct inappropriate sentence fragments and run-on sentences.9
RI.E4.L.1.b: Correctly use frequently confused words (e.g., their/there).
RI.E4.L.1.c: Use helping verbs, also known as auxiliaries (e.g., can, may, might, should), to convey various conditions of possibility, likelihood, obligation, or permission, choosing among helping verbs depending on the overall meaning of the sentence.
RI.E4.L.1.d: Use relative pronouns and relative adverbs to add more information about a noun or verb used in a sentence.
RI.E4.L.1.e: Form and use prepositional phrases in sentences to add more information about qualities such as location, time, agency, and direction.
RI.E4.L.1.f: Form and use progressive verb tenses.
RI.E4.L.2: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.
RI.E4.L.2.a: Write legibly and fluently by hand, using either printing or cursive handwriting; write their given name signature in cursive.
RI.E4.L.2.c: Use commas and quotation marks to mark direct speech and quotations from a text.
RI.E4.L.2.d: Use a comma before a coordinating conjunction in a compound sentence.
RI.E4.L.2.e: Spell grade-appropriate words correctly, consulting references as needed.
RI.E4.L.3: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening.
RI.E4.L.3.a: Choose words and phrases to convey ideas precisely.
RI.E4.L.3.c: Differentiate between contexts that call for formal English (e.g., presenting research findings) and situations where informal discourse is appropriate (e.g., small-group discussion).
RI.E4.L.4: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grade 4 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.
RI.E4.L.4.a: Use context (e.g., definitions, examples, or restatements in text) as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.
RI.E4.L.4.b: Use common, grade-appropriate Greek and Latin affixes and roots as clues to the meaning of a word (e.g., telegraph, photograph, autograph).
RI.E4.L.4.c: Consult reference materials (e.g., dictionaries, glossaries, thesauruses), both print and digital, to find the pronunciation and determine or clarify the precise meaning of key words and phrases.
RI.E4.L.4.d: Recognize and use appropriately abbreviations related to grade-level content or common in everyday life (e.g., hr., min., sec.).
RI.E4.L.4.e: Recognize and use appropriately symbols related to grade-level content or common in everyday life (e.g., &, #, *).
RI.E4.L.5: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.
RI.E4.L.5.a: Explain the meaning of simple similes and metaphors (e.g., as pretty as a picture) in context.
RI.E4.RF.5.b: Recognize and explain the meaning of common idioms, adages, and proverbs.
RI.E4.RF.5.c: Demonstrate understanding of words by relating them to their opposites (antonyms) and to words with similar but not identical meanings (synonyms).
RI.E4.L.6: Acquire and use accurately grade-appropriate general academic and domain-specific words and phrases, including those that signal precise actions, emotions, or states of being (e.g., quizzed, whined, stammered) and that are basic to a particular topic (e.g., wildlife, conservation, and endangered when discussing animal preservation).
RI.M4.OA.A: Use the four operations with whole numbers to solve problems.
RI.M4.OA.A.1: Interpret a multiplication equation as a comparison, e.g., interpret `35=5xx7` as a statement that `35` is `5` times as many as `7and7` times as many as `5`. Represent verbal statements of multiplicative comparisons as multiplication equations.
RI.M4.OA.A.2: Multiply or divide to solve word problems involving multiplicative comparison, e.g., by using drawings and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem, distinguishing multiplicative comparison from additive comparison.
RI.M4.OA.A.3: Solve multi-step word problems posed with whole numbers and having whole-number answers using the four operations, including problems in which remainders must be interpreted. Represent these problems using equations with a letter standing for the unknown quantity. Assess the reasonableness of answers using mental computation and estimation strategies including rounding.
RI.M4.OA.A.3.a: Know multiplication facts and related division facts through 12 x12.
RI.M4.OA.B: Gain familiarity with factors and multiples.
RI.M4.OA.B.4: Find all factor pairs for a whole number in the range `1-100`. Recognize that a whole number is a multiple of each of its factors. Determine whether a given whole number in the range `1-100` is a multiple of a given one-digit number. Determine whether a given whole number in the range `1-100` is prime or composite.
RI.M4.OA.C.5: Generate a number or shape pattern that follows a given rule. Identify apparent features of the pattern that were not explicit in the rule itself.
RI.M4.NBT.A: Recognize that in a multi-digit whole number, a digit in any place represents `10` times as much as it represents in the place to its right.
RI.M4.NBT.A.1: Recognize that in a multi-digit whole number, a digit in any place represents `10` times as much as it represents in the place to its right.
RI.M4.NBT.A.2: Read and write multi-digit whole numbers using base-ten numerals, number names, and expanded form. Compare two multi-digit numbers based on meanings of the digits in each place, using `>,=,and<` symbols to record the results of comparisons.
RI.M4.NBT.A.3: Use place value understanding to round multi-digit whole numbers to any place.
RI.M4.NBT.B: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to perform multi-digit arithmetic on whole numbers less than or equal to `1text(,)000text(,)000`.
RI.M4.NBT.B.4: Fluently add and subtract multi-digit whole numbers using the standard algorithm.
RI.M4.NBT.B.5: Multiply a whole number of up to `text(four digits)` by a `text(one-digit whole number)`, and multiply `text(two two-digit)` numbers, using strategies based on place value and the properties of operations. Illustrate and explain the calculation by using equations, rectangular arrays, and/or area models.
RI.M4.NBT.B.6: Find whole-number quotients and remainders with up to four-digit dividends and one-digit divisors, using strategies based on place value, the properties of operations, and/or the relationship between multiplication and division. Illustrate and explain the calculation by using equations, rectangular arrays, and/or area models.
RI.M4.NF.A: Extend understanding of fraction equivalence and ordering for fractions with denominators `2,3,4,5,6,8,10,12,and100`.
RI.M4.NF.A.1: Explain why a fraction `a/b` is equivalent to a fraction `(nxxa)/(nxxb)` by using visual fraction models, with attention to how the numbers and sizes of the parts differ even though the two fractions themselves are the same size. Use this principle to recognize and generate equivalent fractions, including fractions greater than `1`.
RI.M4.NF.A.2: Compare two fractions with different numerators and different denominators, e.g., by creating common denominators or numerators, or by comparing to a benchmark fraction such as `1/2`. Recognize that comparisons are valid only when the two fractions refer to the same whole. Record the results of comparisons with symbols `>,=,or<`, and justify the conclusions, e.g., by using a visual fraction model.
RI.M4.NF.B: Build fractions from unit fractions by applying and extending previous understandings of operations on whole numbers for fractions with denominators 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12, and100.
RI.M4.NF.B.3: Understand a fraction `a/b` with `a>1` as a sum of fractions `1/b`.
RI.M4.NF.B.3.a: Understand addition and subtraction of fractions as joining and separating parts referring to the same whole. (The whole can be a set of objects.)
RI.M4.NF.B.3.b: Decompose a fraction into a sum of fractions with the same denominator in more than one way, recording each decomposition by an equation. Justify decompositions, e.g., by using drawings or visual fraction models.
RI.M4.NF.B.3.c: Add and subtract mixed numbers with like denominators, e.g., by replacing each mixed number with an equivalent fraction, and/or by using properties of operations and the relationship between addition and subtraction.
RI.M4.NF.B.3.d: Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions referring to the same whole and having like denominators, e.g., by using drawings or visual fraction models and equations to represent the problem.
RI.M4.NF.B.4: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication to multiply a fraction by a whole number.
RI.M4.NF.B.4.a: Understand a fraction `a/b` as a multiple of `1/b`
RI.M4.NF.B.4.b: Understand a multiple of `a/b` as a multiple of `1/b`, and use this understanding to multiply a fraction by a whole number.
RI.M4.NF.B.4.c: Solve word problems involving multiplication of a fraction by a whole number, e.g., by using visual fraction models and equations to represent the problem.
RI.M4.NF.C: Understand decimal notation for fractions, and compare decimal fractions.
RI.M4.NF.C.5: Express a fraction with denominator `10` as an equivalent fraction with denominator `100`, and use this technique to add two fractions with respective denominators `10and100`.
RI.M4.NF.C.6: Use decimal notation to represent fractions with denominators `10or100`.
RI.M4.NF.C.7: Compare two decimals to hundredths by reasoning about their size. Recognize that comparisons are valid only when the two decimals refer to the same whole. Record the results of comparisons with the symbols `>,=,or<`, and justify the conclusions, e.g., by using a visual model.
RI.M4.MD.A: Solve problems involving measurement and conversion of measurements from a larger unit to a smaller unit.
RI.M4.MD.A.1: Know relative sizes of measurement units within one system of units, including `text(km, m, cm; kg, g; lb, oz.; l, ml; hr, min, sec)`. Within a single system of measurement, express measurements in a larger unit in terms of a smaller unit. Record measurement equivalents in a two-column table.
RI.M4.MD.A,2: Use the four operations to solve word problems involving distances, intervals of time, liquid volumes, masses of objects, and money, including problems involving simple fractions or decimals, and problems that require expressing measurements given in a larger unit in terms of a smaller unit. Represent measurement quantities using diagrams such as number line diagrams that feature a measurement scale.
RI.M4.MD.A.3: Apply the area and perimeter formulas for rectangles in real-world and mathematical problems.
RI.M4.MD.B.4: Make a line plot (dot plot) representation to display a data set of measurements in fractions of a unit `(1/2,1/4,1/8)`. Solve problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions by using information presented in line plots (dot plots).
RI.M4.MD.C: Geometric measurement: Understand concepts of angle and measure angles.
RI.M4.MD.C.5: Recognize angles as geometric shapes that are formed wherever two rays share a common endpoint, and understand concepts of angle measurement.
RI.M4.MD.C.5.a: An angle is measured with reference to a circle with its center at the common endpoint of the rays, by considering the fraction of the circular arc between the points where the two rays intersect the circle. An angle that turns through `1/360` of a circle is called a “one-degree angle,” and can be used to measure angles.
RI.M4.MD.C.5.b: An angle that turns through `n` `text(one-degree)` angles is said to have an angle measure of `n` `text(degrees)`.
RI.M4.MD.C.6: Measure angles in whole-number degrees using a protractor. Sketch angles of specified measure.
RI.M4.MD.C.7: Recognize angle measure as additive. When an angle is decomposed into non-overlapping parts, the angle measure of the whole is the sum of the angle measures of the parts. Solve addition and subtraction problems to find unknown angles on a diagram in real-world and mathematical problems, e.g., by using an equation with a symbol for the unknown angle measure.
RI.M4.G.A: Draw and identify lines and angles, and classify shapes by properties of their lines and angles.
RI.M4.G.A.1: Draw points, lines, line segments, rays, angles (right, acute, obtuse), and perpendicular and parallel lines. Identify these in two-dimensional figures.
RI.M4.G.A.2: Classify two-dimensional figures based on the presence or absence of parallel or perpendicular lines, or the presence or absence of angles of a specified size. Recognize right triangles as a category, and identify right triangles.
RI.M4.G.A.3: Recognize a line of symmetry for a two-dimensional figure as a line across the figure such that the figure can be folded along the line into matching parts. Identify line-symmetric figures and draw lines of symmetry.
RI.E5.RL.1: Quote or paraphrase a text accurately when explaining what the text states explicitly and when drawing inferences from the text.
RI.E5.RL.2: Determine a theme of a story, drama, or poem from details in the text, including how characters in a story or drama respond to challenges or how the speaker in a poem reflects upon a topic; summarize a text.
RI.E5.RL.3: Compare and contrast two or more characters, settings, or events in a story or drama, drawing on specific details in the text (e.g., how characters interact).
RI.E5.RL.4: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text; identify and explain the effects of figurative language such as metaphors and similes.
RI.E5.RL.5: Explain how a series of chapters, scenes, or stanzas fits together to provide the overall structure of a particular story, drama, or poem.
RI.E5.RL.6: Describe how a narrator's or speaker's point of view influences how events are described in a story, myth, poem, or drama.
RI.E5.RL.7: Analyze how visual and multimedia elements contribute to the meaning, tone, or beauty of a text (e.g., graphic novel; multimedia presentation of fiction, folktale, myth, poem).
RI.E5.RL.9: Compare and contrast stories in the same genre (e.g., mysteries or adventure stories) on their approaches to similar themes and topics.
RI.E5.RL.10: Independently and proficiently read and comprehend literary texts representing a variety of genres, cultures, and perspectives and exhibiting complexity appropriate for at least grade 5.
RI.E5.RI.E1: Quote or paraphrase a text accurately when explaining what the text states explicitly and when drawing inferences from the text.
RI.E5.RI.E2: Determine one or more main ideas of a text and explain how they are supported by key details; summarize a text.
RI.E5.RI.E3: Explain the relationships or interactions between two or more individuals, events, ideas, or concepts in a historical, scientific, mathematical, or technical text based on specific information in the text.
RI.E5.RI.E4: Determine the meaning of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases in a text relevant to a grade 5 topic or subject area.
RI.E5.RI.E5: Describe how an author uses one or more structures (e.g., chronology, comparison, cause/effect, problem/solution) of events, to present information in a text.
RI.E5.RI.E6: Analyze multiple accounts of the same event or topic, noting important similarities and differences among the points of view they represent.
RI.E5.RI.E7: Draw on information from multiple print or digital sources, demonstrating the ability to locate an answer to a question quickly or to solve a problem efficiently.
RI.E5.RI.E8: Explain how an author uses reasons and evidence to support particular points in a text, identifying which reasons and evidence support which point(s).
RI.E5.RI.E9: Integrate information from several texts on the same topic in order to write or speak knowledgeably about the subject.
RI.E5.RI.E10: Independently and proficiently read and comprehend informational texts, including history/social studies, science, mathematical, and technical texts, exhibiting complexity appropriate for at least grade 5.
RI.E5.RF.3: Know and apply grade-level phonics and word analysis skills in decoding words.
RI.E5.RF.3.a: Use combined knowledge of all letter-sound correspondences, syllabication patterns, and morphology (e.g., roots and affixes) to read accurately unfamiliar multisyllabic words in context and out of context.
RI.E5.RF.4: Read with sufficient accuracy and fluency to support comprehension.
RI.E5.RF.4.a: Read grade-level text with purpose and understanding.
RI.E5.RF.4.b: Read grade-level prose and poetry orally with accuracy, appropriate rate, and expression on successive readings.
RI.E5.RF.4.c: Use context to confirm or self-correct word recognition and understanding, rereading as necessary.
RI.E5.W.1: Write opinion pieces on topics or texts, supporting a point of view with reasons and information.
RI.E5.W.1.a: Introduce a topic or text clearly, state an opinion, and create an organizational structure in which ideas are logically grouped in paragraphs and sections to support the writer's purpose.
RI.E5.W.1.b: Provide logically ordered reasons that are supported by facts and details.
RI.E5.W.1.c: Link opinion and reasons using words, phrases, and clauses (e.g., consequently, specifically).
RI.E5.W.1.d: Provide a concluding statement or section related to the opinion presented.
RI.E5.W.2: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine a topic and convey ideas and information clearly.
RI.E5.W.2.a: Introduce a topic clearly, provide a general observation and focus, and group related information logically in paragraphs and sections; include text features (e.g., headings), illustrations, and multimedia when useful to aiding comprehension.
RI.E5.W.2.b: Develop the topic with facts, definitions, concrete details, quotations, or other information and examples related to the topic.
RI.E5.W.2.c: Link ideas within and across categories of information using words, phrases, and clauses (e.g., in contrast, especially).
RI.E5.W.2.d: Use precise language and domain-specific vocabulary to inform about or explain the topic.
RI.E5.W.2.e: Provide a concluding statement or section related to the information or explanation presented.
RI.E5.W.3: Write narratives in prose or poem form to develop experiences or events using effective literary techniques, descriptive details, and clear sequences.
RI.E5.W.3.a: Orient the reader by establishing a situation and introducing a speaker, narrator, and/or characters; organize an appropriate narrative sequence.
RI.E5.W.3.b: Use narrative techniques such as dialogue, description, and pacing to develop experiences or events or show responses to situations.
RI.E5.W.3.c: Use a variety of transitional words, phrases, and clauses to manage sequence.
RI.E5.W.3.d: Use concrete words and phrases and sensory details to convey experiences or events precisely.
RI.E5.W.3.e: Provide a sense of closure appropriate to the narrated experiences or events.
RI.E5.W.3.f: For prose narratives, draw on characteristics of traditional or modern genres (e.g., tall tales, myths, mysteries, fantasies, historical fiction) from diverse cultures as models for writing.
RI.E5.W.3.g: For poems, draw on characteristics of traditional poetic forms (e.g., ballads, couplets) or modern free verse from diverse cultures as models for writing.
RI.E5.W.4: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development and organization are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.
RI.E5.W.5: Develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach.
RI.E5.W.5.a: Demonstrate command of standard English conventions.
RI.E5.W.5.b: Demonstrate the ability to use general academic and domain-specific vocabulary appropriately.
RI.E5.W.6: Use technology, including current web-based communication platforms, to produce and publish writing as well as to interact and collaborate with others; demonstrate sufficient command of keyboarding skills to type a minimum of two pages in a single sitting.
RI.E5.W.7: Conduct short research projects that use several sources to build knowledge through investigation of different aspects of a topic.
RI.E5.W.8: Recall relevant information from experiences or gather relevant information from print and digital sources; summarize or paraphrase information in notes and finished work, and provide a list of sources.
RI.E5.W.9: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support written analysis, reflection, and research, applying one or more grade 5 standards for Reading Literature or Reading Information as needed.
RI.E5.W.10: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of discipline-specific tasks, purposes, and audiences.
RI.E5.SL.1: Engage effectively in a range of collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in groups, and teacher-led) with diverse partners on grade 5 topics and texts, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly.
RI.E5.SL.1.a: Come to discussions prepared, having read or studied required material; explicitly draw on that preparation and other information known about the topic to explore ideas under discussion.
RI.E5.SL.1.b: Follow agreed-upon rules for discussions and carry out assigned roles.
RI.E5.SL.1.c: Pose and respond to specific questions by making comments that contribute to the discussion and elaborate on the remarks of others.
RI.E5.SL.1.d: Review the key ideas expressed and draw conclusions in light of information and knowledge gained from the discussions.
RI.E5.SL.2: Summarize a written text read aloud or information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.
RI.E5.SL.3: Summarize the points a speaker makes and explain how each claim is supported by reasons and evidence.
RI.E5.SL.4: Report on a topic, text, procedure, or solution to a mathematical problem, or present an opinion, sequencing ideas logically and using appropriate facts and relevant, descriptive details to support main ideas or themes; speak clearly at an understandable pace and use appropriate vocabulary.
RI.E5.SL.5: Include multimedia components and visual displays in presentations when appropriate to enhance the development of main ideas or themes.
RI.E5.SL.6: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and tasks, using formal English when appropriate to task and situation.
RI.E5.L.1: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking; retain and further develop language skills learned in previous grades.
RI.E5.L.1.a: Use verb tense to convey various times, sequences, states, and conditions, choosing among verb tenses depending on the overall meaning of the sentence.
RI.E5.L.1.b: Recognize and correct inappropriate shifts in verb tense.
RI.E5.L.1.c: Use active and passive verbs, choosing between them depending on the overall meaning of the sentence.
RI.E5.L.1.d: Form and use perfect verb tenses.
RI.E5.L.2: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.
RI.E5.L.2.a: Write legibly and fluently by hand, using either print or cursive handwriting; write their given and family name signature in cursive.
RI.E5.L.2.b: Use punctuation to separate items in a series.
RI.E5.L.2.c: Use a comma to separate an introductory element from the rest of the sentence.
RI.E5.L.2.d: Use a comma to set off the words yes and no (e.g., Yes, thank you), to set off a tag question from the rest of the sentence (e.g., It's true, isn't it?), and to indicate direct address (e.g., Is that you, Steve?).
RI.E5.L.2.e: Use underlining, quotation marks, or italics to indicate titles of works.
RI.E5.L.2.f: Spell grade-appropriate words correctly, consulting references as needed.
RI.E5.L.3: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening.
RI.E5.L.3.a: Expand, combine, and reduce sentences for meaning, reader/listener interest, and style.
RI.E5.L.3.b: Compare and contrast the varieties of English (e.g., dialects, registers) used in stories, dramas, or poems.
RI.E5.L.4: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grade 5 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.
RI.E5.L.4.a: Use context (e.g., cause/effect relationships and comparisons in text) as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.
RI.E5.L.4.b: Use common, grade-appropriate Greek and Latin affixes and roots as clues to the meaning of a word (e.g., photograph, photosynthesis).
RI.E5.L.4.c: Consult reference materials (e.g., dictionaries, glossaries, thesauruses), both print and digital, to find the pronunciation and determine or clarify the precise meaning of key words and phrases.
RI.E5.L.4.d: Recognize and use appropriately abbreviations related to grade-level content or common in everyday life, including abbreviations derived from words or phrases in other languages (e.g., lb., oz., etc.).
RI.E5.L.4.e: Recognize and use appropriately symbols related to grade-level content or common in everyday life, including symbols with multiple meanings (e.g., parentheses in mathematics and in writing, ° to measure angles and temperature).
RI.E5.L.5: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.
RI.E5.L.5.a: Interpret figurative language, including similes and metaphors, in context.
RI.E5.RF.5.b: Recognize and explain the meaning of common idioms, adages, and proverbs.
RI.E5.RF.5.c: Use the relationship between particular words (e.g., synonyms, antonyms, homographs) to better understand each of the words.
RI.E5.L.6: Acquire and use accurately grade-appropriate general academic and domain-specific words and phrases, including those that signal contrast, addition, and other logical relationships (e.g., however, although, nevertheless, similarly, moreover, in addition).
RI.M5.OA.A.1: Use parentheses, brackets, or braces in numerical expressions, and evaluate expressions with these symbols, e.g.,(6xx30)+(6xx1/2)`.
RI.M5.OA.A.2: Write simple expressions that record calculations with numbers, and interpret numerical expressions without evaluating them.
RI.M5.OA.B.3: Generate two numerical patterns using two given rules. Identify apparent relationships between corresponding terms. Form ordered pairs consisting of corresponding terms from the two patterns, and graph the ordered pairs on a coordinate plane.
RI.M5.NBT.A.1: Recognize that in a multi-digit number, including decimals, a digit in any place represents `10` times as much as it represents in the place to its right and `1/10` of what it represents in the place to its left.
RI.M5.NBT.A.2: Explain patterns in the number of zeros of the product when multiplying a number by powers of `10`,and explain patterns in the placement of the decimal point when a decimal is multiplied or divided by a power of `10`. Use whole-number exponents to denote powers of `10`.
RI.M5.NBT.A.3: Read, write, and compare decimals to thousandths.
RI.M5.NBT.A.3.a: Read and write decimals to thousandths using base-ten numerals, number names, and expanded form, e.g., `347.392=3xx100+4xx10+7xx1+3xx(1/10)+9xx(1/100)+2xx(1/1000)`.
RI.M5.NBT.A.3.b: Compare two decimals to thousandths based on meanings of the digits in each place, using >,=, and < symbols to record the results of comparisons.
RI.M5.NBT.A.4: Use place value understanding to round decimals to any place.
RI.M5.NBT.B: Perform operations with multi-digit whole numbers and with decimals to hundredths.
RI.M5.NBT.B.5: Fluently multiply multi-digit whole numbers. (Include `text(two-digit)xxtext(four-digit)` numbers and, `text(three-digit)xxtext(three-digit)` numbers) using the standard algorithm.
RI.M5.NBT.B.6: Find whole-number quotients of whole numbers with up to four-digit dividends and two-digit divisors, using strategies based on place value, the properties of operations, and/or the relationship between multiplication and division. Illustrate and explain the calculation by using equations, rectangular arrays, and/or area models.
RI.M5.NBT.B.7: Add, subtract, multiply, and divide decimals to hundredths, using concrete models or drawings and strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction and between multiplication and division; relate the strategy to a written method and explain the reasoning used.
RI.M5.NF.A: Use equivalent fractions as a strategy to add and subtract fractions.
RI.M5.NF.A.1: Add and subtract fractions with unlike denominators (including mixed numbers) by replacing given fractions with equivalent fractions in such a way as to produce an equivalent sum or difference of fractions with like denominators.
RI.M5.NF.A.2: Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions referring to the same whole (the whole can be a set of objects), including cases of unlike denominators, e.g., by using visual fraction models or equations to represent the problem. Use benchmark fractions and number sense of fractions to estimate mentally and assess the reasonableness of answers.
RI.M5.NF.B: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication and division to multiply and divide fractions.
RI.M5.NF.B.3: Interpret a fraction as division of the numerator by the denominator `(a/b=a-:b)`. Solve word problems involving division of whole numbers leading to answers in the form of fractions or mixed numbers, e.g., by using visual fraction models or equations to represent the problem.
RI.M5.NF.B.4: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication to multiply a fraction or whole number by a fraction.
RI.M5.NF.B.4.a: Interpret the product (a/b) × q as a parts of a partition of q into `b` equal parts; equivalently, as the result of a sequence of operations a × q ÷b.
RI.M5.NF.B.4.b: Find the area of a rectangle with fractional side lengths by tiling it with unit squares of the appropriate unit fraction side lengths, and show that the area is the same as would be found by multiplying the side lengths. Multiply fractional side lengths to find areas of rectangles, and represent fraction products as rectangular areas.
RI.M5.NF.B.5.a: Comparing the size of a product to the size of one factor on the basis of the size of the other factor, without performing the indicated multiplication.
RI.M5.NF.B.5.b: Explaining why multiplying a given number by a fraction greater than `1` results in a product greater than the given number (recognizing multiplication by whole numbers greater than `1` as a familiar case); explaining why multiplying a given number by a fraction less than `1` results in a product smaller than the given number; and relating the principle of fraction equivalence `a/b=(nxxa)/(nxxb)` to the effect of multiplying `a/b` by `1`.
RI.M5.NF.B.6: Solve real-world problems involving multiplication of fractions and mixed numbers, e.g., by using visual fraction models or equations to represent the problem.
RI.M5.NF.B.7: Apply and extend previous understandings of division to divide unit fractions by whole numbers and whole numbers by unit fractions.
RI.M5.NF.B.7.a: Interpret division of a unit fraction by a non-zero whole number, and compute such quotients.
RI.M5.NF.B.7.b: Interpret division of a whole number by a unit fraction, and compute such quotients.
RI.M5.NF.B.7.c: Solve real-world problems involving division of unit fractions by non-zero whole numbers and division of whole numbers by unit fractions, e.g., by using visual fraction models and equations to represent the problem.
RI.M5.MD.A: Convert like measurement units within a given measurement system.
RI.M5.MD.A.1: Convert among different-sized standard measurement units within a given measurement system (e.g., convert `5` `text(cm)` to `0.05` `text(m)`), and use these conversions in solving multi-step, real-world problems.
RI.M5.MD.B.2: Make a line plot (dot plot) to display a data set of measurements in fractions of a unit. Use operations on fractions for this grade to solve problems involving information presented in line plot (dot plot).
RI.M5.MD.C: Geometric measurement: Understand concepts of volume and relate volume to multiplication and to addition.
RI.M5.MD.C.3: Recognize volume as an attribute of solid figures and understand concepts of volume measurement.
RI.M5.MD.C.3.a: A cube with side length`1` `text(unit)`, called a “unit cube,” is said to have “one cubic unit” of volume, and can be used to measure volume.
RI.M5.MD.C.3.b: A solid figure which can be packed without gaps or overlaps using `n` `text(unit cubes)` is said to have a volume of `n` `text(cubic units)`.
RI.M5.MD.C.4: Measure volumes by counting unit cubes, using cubic cm, cubic in., cubic ft., and non-standard units.
RI.M5.MD.C.5: Relate volume to the operations of multiplication and addition and solve real-world and mathematical problems involving volume.
RI.M5.MD.C.5.a: Find the volume of a right rectangular prism with whole-number edge lengths by packing it with unit cubes, and show that the volume is the same as would be found by multiplying the edge lengths, equivalently by multiplying the height by the area of the base. Represent threefold whole-number products as volumes, e.g., to represent the associative property of multiplication.
RI.M5.MD.C.5.b: Apply the formula `V=lxxwxxhandV=Bxxh` (where B stands for the area of the base) for rectangular prisms to find volumes of right rectangular prisms with whole-number edge lengths in the context of solving real-world and mathematical problems.
RI.M5.MD.C.5.c: Recognize volume as additive. Find volumes of solid figures composed of two non-overlapping right rectangular prisms by adding the volumes of the non-overlapping parts, applying this technique to solve real-world problems.
RI.M5.G.A: Graph points on the coordinate plane to solve real-world and mathematical problems.
RI.M5.G.A.1: Use a pair of perpendicular number lines, called axes, to define a coordinate system, with the intersection of the lines (the origin) arranged to coincide with the zero on each line and a given point in the plane located by using an ordered pair of numbers, called its coordinates. Understand that the first number indicates how far to travel from the origin in the direction of one axis, and the second number indicates how far to travel in the direction of the second axis, with the convention that the names of the two axes and the coordinates correspond (e.g., `xtext(-axis)andxtext(-coordinate),ytext(-axis)` and`ytext(-coordinate)`).
RI.M5.G.A.2: Represent real-world and mathematical problems by graphing points in the first quadrant of the coordinate plane, and interpret coordinate values of points in the context of the situation.
RI.M5.G.B: Classify two-dimensional figures into categories based on their properties.
RI.M5.G.B.3: Understand that attributes belonging to a category of two-dimensional figures also belong to all subcategories of that category.
RI.M5.G.B.4: Classify two-dimensional figures in a hierarchy based on properties.
RI.E6.RL.1: Cite textual evidence to support analysis of what a text states explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text, quoting or paraphrasing as appropriate.
RI.E6.RL.2: Determine a theme or central idea of a text and how it is conveyed through particular details; provide a summary of a text distinct from personal opinions or judgments.

RI.E6.RL.4: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including figurative and connotative meanings; analyze the impact of specific word choices, including those that create repeated sounds and rhythms in poetry, on meaning, tone (i.e., author's attitude toward subject or audience), or mood (i.e., emotional atmosphere).
RI.E6.RL.5: Analyze how a particular sentence, chapter, scene, or stanza fits into the overall structure of a text and contributes to the development of the theme, setting, or plot.
RI.E6.RL.6: Explain how an author develops the point of view of the narrator or speaker in a text.
RI.E6.RL.7: Compare and contrast the experience of reading a story, drama, or poem to that of listening to or viewing the same text.
RI.E6.RL.9: Compare and contrast texts in different forms or genres (e.g., stories and poems, historical novels and fantasy stories) in terms of their approaches to similar themes and topics.
RI.E6.RL.10: Independently and proficiently read and comprehend literary texts representing a variety of genres, cultures, and perspectives and exhibiting complexity appropriate for at least grade 6.
RI.E6.RI.E1: Cite textual evidence to support analysis of what a text states explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text, quoting or paraphrasing as appropriate.
RI.E6.RI.E2: Determine a text's central idea(s) and how particular details help convey the idea(s); provide a summary of a text distinct from personal opinions or judgments.
RI.E6.RI.E3: Analyze in detail how a key individual, event, or idea is introduced, illustrated, and elaborated in a text (e.g., through examples or anecdotes).
RI.E6.RI.E4: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including figurative, connotative, and technical meanings; explain how word choice affects meaning and tone.

RI.E6.RI.E8: Trace and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, distinguishing claims that are supported by reasons and evidence from claims that are not.

RI.E6.W.1: Write arguments (e.g., essays, letters to the editor, advocacy speeches) to support claims with clear reasons and relevant evidence.
RI.E6.W.1.a: Introduce claim(s) and organize the reasons and evidence clearly in paragraphs and sections.
RI.E6.W.1.b: Support claim(s) with clear reasons and relevant evidence, using credible sources and demonstrating an understanding of the topic or text.
RI.E6.W.1.c: Use words, phrases, and clauses to clarify the relationships among claim(s) and reasons.
RI.E6.W.1.d: Establish and maintain a style appropriate to audience and purpose (e.g., formal for academic writing).
RI.E6.W.1.e: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from the argument presented.

RI.E6.W.2.a: Introduce a topic; organize ideas, concepts, and information in paragraphs and sections, using strategies such as definition, classification, comparison/contrast, and cause/effect; include text features (e.g., headings), graphics (e.g., charts, tables), and multimedia when useful to aiding comprehension.
RI.E6.W.2.b: Develop the topic with relevant facts, definitions, concrete details, quotations, or other information and examples.
RI.E6.W.2.c: Use appropriate transitions to clarify the relationships among ideas and concepts.
RI.E6.W.2.d: Use precise language and domain-specific vocabulary to inform about or explain the topic.
RI.E6.W.2.e: Establish and maintain a style appropriate to audience and purpose (e.g., formal for academic writing).
RI.E6.W.2.f: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from the information or explanation presented.
RI.E6.W.3: Write narratives to develop experiences or events using effective literary techniques, relevant descriptive details, and well-structured sequences.
RI.E6.W.3.a: Engage and orient the reader by establishing a context and introducing a narrator and/or characters; organize an appropriate narrative sequence.
RI.E6.W.3.b: Use narrative techniques, such as dialogue, pacing, and description, to develop experiences, events, and/or characters.
RI.E6.W.3.c: Use a variety of transition words, phrases, and clauses to convey sequence and signal shifts from one time frame or setting to another.
RI.E6.W.3.d: Use precise words and phrases, relevant descriptive details, figurative and sensory language, and techniques such as personification (e.g., “the fog crept in”) to convey experiences or events.
RI.E6.W.3.e: Provide a conclusion that follows from the narrated experiences or events.
RI.E6.W.4: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.
RI.E6.W.5: Develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach.
RI.E6.W.5.a: Demonstrate command of standard English conventions.
RI.E6.W.5.b: Demonstrate the ability to select accurate vocabulary.
RI.E6.W.6: Use technology, including current web-based communication platforms, to produce and publish writing as well as to interact and collaborate with others; demonstrate sufficient command of keyboarding skills to type a minimum of three pages in a single sitting.
RI.E6.W.7: Conduct short as well as more sustained research projects to answer a question, drawing on several sources and refocusing the inquiry when appropriate.

RI.E6.W.9: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support written analysis, interpretation, reflection, and research, applying one or more grade 6 standards for Reading Literature or Reading Information as needed.

RI.E6.SL.1: Engage effectively in a range of collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in groups, and teacher-led) with diverse partners on grade 6 topics, texts, and issues, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly.

RI.E6.SL.1.b: Follow rules for collegial discussions, set specific goals and deadlines, and define individual roles as needed.
RI.E6.SL.1.c: Pose and respond to specific questions with elaboration and detail by making comments that contribute to the topic, text, or issue under discussion.
RI.E6.SL.1.d: Review the key ideas expressed and demonstrate understanding of multiple perspectives through reflection and paraphrasing.
RI.E6.SL.2: Interpret information presented in diverse media and formats (e.g., visually, quantitatively, orally) and explain how it contributes to a topic, text, or issue under study.
RI.E6.SL.3: Delineate a speaker's argument and specific claims, distinguishing claims that are supported by reasons and evidence from claims that are not.
RI.E6.SL.4: Present claims and findings, sequencing ideas logically and using pertinent descriptions, facts, and details to accentuate main ideas or themes; use appropriate vocabulary, eye contact, volume, and pronunciation.
RI.E6.SL.5: Include multimedia components and visual displays in presentations to clarify information.
RI.E6.SL.6: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate.
RI.E6.L.1: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking; retain and further develop language skills learned in previous grades.
RI.E6.L.1.a: Use simple, compound, complex, and compound-complex sentences to communicate ideas clearly and to add variety to writing.
RI.E6.L.1.b: Explain the function of phrases and clauses in general, how phrases and clauses differ, and how their use conveys a particular meaning in a specific written or spoken sentence.
RI.E6.L.1.c: Place or rearrange phrases and clauses within a sentence, recognizing and correcting misplaced and dangling modifiers.
RI.E6.L.2: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.
RI.E6.L.2.a: Use punctuation (commas, parentheses, dashes) to set off nonrestrictive/parenthetical elements.
RI.E6.L.2.b: Spell correctly, recognizing that some words have commonly accepted variations (e.g., donut/doughnut).
RI.E6.L.3: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening.
RI.E6.L.3.a: Maintain appropriate consistency in style and tone while varying sentence patterns for meaning and audience interest.
RI.E6.L.3.b: Recognize variations from standard or formal English in writing and speaking, determine their appropriateness for the intended purpose and audience, and make changes as necessary.
RI.E6.L.4: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grade 6 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.
RI.E6.L.4.a: Use context (e.g., the overall meaning of a sentence or paragraph; a word's position or function in a sentence) as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.
RI.E6.L.4.b: Use common, grade-appropriate Greek or Latin affixes and roots as clues to the meaning of a word (e.g., audience, auditory, audible).
RI.E6.L.4.c: Consult reference materials (e.g., dictionaries, glossaries, thesauruses), both print and digital, to find the pronunciation of a word or determine or clarify its precise meaning or its part of speech.
RI.E6.L.4.d: Verify the preliminary determination of the meaning of a word or phrase (e.g., by checking the inferred meaning in context or in a dictionary).
RI.E6.L.5: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.
RI.E6.L.5.a: Interpret figures of speech (e.g., personification) in context.
RI.E6.RF.5.b: Use the relationship between particular words (e.g., cause/effect, part/whole, item/category) to better understand each of the words.
RI.E6.RF.5.c: Distinguish among the connotations (associations) of words with similar denotations (definitions) (e.g., stingy, scrimping, economical, unwasteful, thrifty).
RI.E6.L.6: Acquire and use accurately grade-appropriate general academic and domain-specific words and phrases; independently research words and gather vocabulary knowledge.
RI.M6.RP.A: Understand ratio and rate concepts and use ratio and rate reasoning to solve problems.
RI.M6.RP.A.1: Understand the concept of a ratio including the distinctions between part:part and part:whole and the value of a ratio; part/part and part/whole. Use ratio language to describe a ratio relationship between two quantities.
RI.M6.RP.A.2: Understand the concept of a unit rate `a/b` associated with a ratio `a:b` with `b!=0`, and use rate language in the context of a ratio relationship, including the use of units.
RI.M6.RP.A.3: Use ratio and rate reasoning to solve real-world and mathematical problems, e.g., by reasoning about tables of equivalent ratios, tape diagrams, double number line diagrams, or equations.
RI.M6.RP.A.3.a: Make tables of equivalent ratios relating quantities with whole-number measurements. Find missing values in the tables, and plot the pairs of values on the coordinate plane. Use tables to compare ratios.
RI.M6.RP.A.3.b: Solve unit rate problems, including those involving unit pricing, and constant speed.
RI.M6.RP.A.3.c: Find a percent of a quantity as a rate `text(per)` `100` (e.g., `30%` of a quantity means `30/100` times the quantity); solve problems involving finding the whole, given a part and the percent.
RI.M6.RP.A.3.d: Use ratio reasoning to convert measurement units within and between measurement systems; manipulate and transform units appropriately when multiplying or dividing quantities.
RI.M6.RP.A.3.e: Solve problems that relate the mass of an object to its volume.
RI.M6.NS.A: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication and division to divide fractions by fractions.
RI.M6.NS.A.1: Interpret and compute quotients of fractions, and solve word problems involving division of fractions by fractions, e.g., by using visual fraction models and equations to represent the problem.
RI.M6.NS.B: Compute fluently with multi-digit numbers and find common factors and multiples.
RI.M6.NS.B.2: Fluently divide multi-digit numbers using the standard algorithm.
RI.M6.NS.B.3: Fluently add, subtract, multiply, and divide multi-digit decimals using the standard algorithm for each operation.
RI.M6.NS.B.4: Use prime factorization to find the greatest common factor of two whole numbers less than or equal to `100` and the least common multiple of two whole numbers less than or equal to `12`. Use the distributive property to express a sum of two whole numbers `1-100` with a common factor as a multiple of a sum of two relatively prime numbers.
RI.M6.NS.C: Apply and extend previous understandings of numbers to the system of rational numbers.
RI.M6.NS.C.5: Understand that positive and negative numbers are used together to describe quantities having opposite directions or values (e.g., temperature above/below zero, elevation above/below sea level, credits/debits, and positive/negative electric charge). Use positive and negative numbers (whole numbers, fractions, and decimals) to represent quantities in real-world contexts, explaining the meaning of zero in each situation.
RI.M6.NS.C.6: Understand a rational number as a point on the number line. Extend number line diagrams and coordinate axes familiar from previous grades to represent points on the line and in the plane with negative number coordinates.
RI.M6.NS.C.6.a: Recognize opposite signs of numbers as indicating locations on opposite sides of `0` on the number line; recognize that the opposite of the opposite of a number is the number itself, e.g., `-(-3)=3`, and that zero is its own opposite.
RI.M6.NS.C.6.b: Understand signs of numbers in ordered pairs as indicating locations in quadrants of the coordinate plane; recognize that when two ordered pairs differ only by signs, the locations of the points are related by reflections across one or both axes.
RI.M6.NS.C.6.c: Find and position integers and other rational numbers on a horizontal or vertical number line diagram; find and position pairs of integers and other rational numbers on a coordinate plane.
RI.M6.NS.C.7: Understand ordering and absolute value of rational numbers.
RI.M6.NS.C.7.a: Interpret statements of inequality as statements about the relative positions of two numbers on a number line diagram.
RI.M6.NS.C.7.b: Write, interpret, and explain statements of order for rational numbers in real-world contexts.
RI.M6.NS.C.7.c: Understand the absolute value of a rational number as its distance from `0` on the number line; interpret absolute value as magnitude for a positive or negative quantity in a real-world situation.
RI.M6.NS.C.7.d: Distinguish comparisons of absolute value from statements about order
RI.M6.NS.C.8: Solve real-world and mathematical problems by graphing points in all four quadrants of the coordinate plane. Include use of coordinates and absolute value to find distances between points with the same first coordinate or the same second coordinate.
RI.M6.EE.A: Apply and extend previous understandings of arithmetic to algebraic expressions.
RI.M6.EE.A.1: Write and evaluate numerical expressions involving whole-number exponents.
RI.M6.EE.A.2: Write, read, and evaluate expressions in which letters stand for numbers.
RI.M6.EE.A.2.a: Write expressions that record operations with numbers and with letters standing for numbers.
RI.M6.EE.A.2.b: Identify parts of an expression using mathematical terms (sum, term, product, factor,quotient, and coefficient); view one or more parts of an expression as a single entity.
RI.M6.EE.A.2.c: Evaluate expressions at specific values of their variables. Include expressions that arise from formulas used in real-world problems. Perform arithmetic operations, including those involving whole-number exponents, in the conventional order when there are no parentheses to specify a particular order (Order of Operations).
RI.M6.EE.A.3: Apply the properties of operations to generate equivalent expressions.
RI.M6.EE.A.4: Identify when two expressions are equivalent (i.e., when the two expressions name the same number regardless of which value is substituted into them).
RI.M6.EE.B: Reason about and solve one-variable equations and inequalities.
RI.M6.EE.B.5: Understand solving an equation or inequality as a process of answering a question: Which values from a specified set, if any, make the equation or inequality true? Use substitution to determine whether a given number in a specified set makes an equation or inequality true.
RI.M6.EE.B.6: Use variables to represent numbers and write expressions when solving a real-world or mathematical problem; understand that a variable can represent an unknown number, or, depending on the purpose at hand, any number in a specified set.
RI.M6.EE.B.7: Solve real-world and mathematical problems by writing and solving equations of the form `x+p=qandpx=q` for cases in which `p,q,andx` are all nonnegative rational numbers.
RI.M6.EE.B.8: Write an inequality of the form `x>corx<c` to represent a constraint or condition in a real-world or mathematical problem. Recognize that inequalities of the form `x>corx<c` have infinitely many solutions; represent solutions of such inequalities on number line diagrams.
RI.M6.EE.C: Represent and analyze quantitative relationships between dependent and independent variables.
RI.M6.EE.C.9: Use variables to represent two quantities in a real-world problem that change in relationship to one another; write an equation to express one quantity, thought of as the dependent variable, in terms of the other quantity, thought of as the independent variable. Analyze the relationship between the dependent and independent variables using graphs and tables, and relate these to the equation.
RI.M6.G.A: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving area, surface area, and volume.
RI.M6.G.A.1: Find the area of right triangles, other triangles, special quadrilaterals, and polygons by composing into rectangles or decomposing into triangles and other shapes; apply these techniques in the context of solving real-world and mathematical problems.
RI.M6.G.A,2: Find the volume of a right rectangular prism with fractional edge lengths by packing it with unit cubes of the appropriate unit fraction edge lengths, and show that the volume is the same as would be found by multiplying the edge lengths of the prism. Apply the formulas `V=lxxwxxhandV=Bxxh` to find volumes of right rectangular prisms with fractional edge lengths in the context of solving real-world and mathematical problems.
RI.M6.G.A.3: Draw polygons in the coordinate plane given coordinates for the vertices; use coordinates to find the length of a side joining points with the same first coordinate or the same second coordinate. Apply these techniques in the context of solving real-world and mathematical problems.
RI.M6.G.A.4: Represent three-dimensional figures using nets made up of rectangles and triangles, and use the nets to find the surface areas of these figures. Apply these techniques in the context of solving real-world and mathematical problems.
RI.M6.SP.A.1: Recognize a statistical question as one that anticipates variability in the data related to the question and accounts for it in the answers.
RI.M6.SP.A.2: Understand that a set of data collected to answer a statistical question has a distribution, which can be described by its center (median, mean, and/or mode), spread (range, interquartile range), and overall shape.
RI.M6.SP.A.3: Recognize that a measure of center for a numerical data set summarizes all of its values with a single number, while a measure of variation describes how its values vary with a single number.
RI.M6.SP.B.4: Display numerical data in plots on a number line, including dot plots, histograms, and box plots.
RI.M6.SP.B.5: Summarize numerical data sets in relation to their context, such as by:
RI.M6.SP.B.5.b: Describing the nature of the attribute under investigation, including how it was measured and its units of measurement.
RI.M6.SP.B.5.c: Giving quantitative measures of center (median, and/or mean) and variability (range and/or interquartile range), as well as describing any overall pattern and any striking deviations from the overall pattern with reference to the context in which the data weregathered.
RI.M6.SP.B.5.d: Relating the choice of measures of center and variability to the shape of the data distribution and the context in which the data were gathered.
RI.E7.RL.1: Cite several pieces of textual evidence to support analysis of what a text states explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text, quoting or paraphrasing as appropriate.
RI.E7.RL.2: Determine a theme or central idea of a text and analyze its development over the course of the text; provide an objective summary of a text.
RI.E7.RL.3: Analyze how particular elements of a story, poem, or drama interact (e.g., how setting shapes the characters or plot).
RI.E7.RL.4: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including figurative and connotative meanings; analyze the impact of specific word choices on meaning, tone, or mood, including the impact of repeated use of particular images.
RI.E7.RL.5: Analyze how aspects of a literary work's structure contribute to its meaning or style (e.g., the effect of repetition in an epic, flashback in a novel, soliloquy in a drama).
RI.E7.RL.6: Analyze how an author develops and contrasts the points of view of different characters or narrators in a text.
RI.E7.RL.7: Compare and contrast a written story, drama, or poem to its audio, filmed, staged, or multimedia version.
RI.E7.RL.9: Compare and contrast a fictional portrayal of a time, place, or character and a historical account of the same period as a means of understanding how authors of fiction use or alter history.
RI.E7.RL.10: Independently and proficiently read and comprehend literary texts representing a variety of genres, cultures, and perspectives and exhibiting complexity appropriate for at least grade 7.
RI.E7.RI.E1: Cite several pieces of textual evidence to support analysis of what a text states explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text, quoting or paraphrasing as appropriate.
RI.E7.RI.E2: Determine a text's central idea(s) and analyze its/their development over the course of the text; provide an objective summary of a text.
RI.E7.RI.E3: Analyze the interactions between individuals, events, and ideas in a text (e.g., how ideas influence individuals or events, or how individuals influence ideas or events).
RI.E7.RI.E4: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including figurative, connotative, and technical meanings; analyze the impact of a specific word choice on meaning and tone.
RI.E7.RI.E5: Analyze the structure an author uses to organize a text, including how the major sections and text features (e.g., headings) contribute to the whole and to the development of the ideas.
RI.E7.RI.E6: Determine an author's point of view or purpose in a text and analyze how the author distinguishes his or her position from that of others.
RI.E7.RI.E7: Compare and contrast a written text to an audio, video, or multimedia version, analyzing each medium's portrayal of the subject (e.g., how the delivery of a speech affects the impact of the words).
RI.E7.RI.E8: Trace and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, assessing whether the reasoning is sound and the evidence is relevant and sufficient to support the claims.
RI.E7.RI.E9: Analyze how two or more authors writing about the same topic shape their presentations of key information by emphasizing different evidence or advancing different interpretations of facts.
RI.E7.RI.E10: Independently and proficiently read and comprehend literary nonfiction representing a variety of genres, cultures, and perspectives and exhibiting complexity appropriate for at least grade 7.
RI.E7.W.1: Write arguments (e.g., essays, letters to the editor, advocacy speeches) to support claims with clear reasons and relevant evidence.
RI.E7.W.1.a: Introduce claim(s), acknowledge alternate or opposing claims, and organize the reasons and evidence logically in paragraphs and sections.
RI.E7.W.1.b: Support claim(s) with logical reasoning and relevant evidence, using accurate, credible sources and demonstrating an understanding of the topic or text.
RI.E7.W.1.c: Use words, phrases, and clauses to create cohesion and clarify the relationships among claim(s), reasons, and evidence.
RI.E7.W.1.d: Establish and maintain a style appropriate to audience and purpose (e.g., formal for academic writing).
RI.E7.W.1.e: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the argument presented.
RI.E7.W.2: Write informative/explanatory texts (e.g., essays, oral reports, biographical feature articles) to examine a topic and convey ideas, concepts, and information through the selection, organization, and analysis of relevant content.
RI.E7.W.2.a: Introduce a topic clearly, previewing what is to follow; organize ideas, concepts, and information in paragraphs and sections, using strategies such as definition, classification, comparison/contrast, and cause/effect; include text features (e.g., headings), graphics (e.g., charts, tables), and multimedia when useful to aiding comprehension.
RI.E7.W.2.b: Develop the topic with relevant facts, definitions, concrete details, quotations, or other information and examples.
RI.E7.W.2.c: Use appropriate transitions to create cohesion and clarify the relationships among ideas and concepts.
RI.E7.W.2.d: Use precise language and domain-specific vocabulary to inform about or explain the topic.
RI.E7.W.2.e: Establish and maintain a style appropriate to audience and purpose (e.g., formal for academic writing).
RI.E7.W.2.f: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the information or explanation presented.
RI.E7.W.3: Write narratives to develop experiences or events using effective literary techniques, relevant descriptive details, and well-structured sequences.
RI.E7.W.3.a: Engage and orient the reader by establishing a context and point of view and introducing a narrator and/or characters; organize an appropriate narrative sequence.
RI.E7.W.3.b: Use narrative techniques, such as dialogue, pacing, and description, to develop experiences, events, and/or characters.
RI.E7.W.3.c: Use a variety of transition words, phrases, and clauses to convey sequence and signal shifts from one time frame or setting to another.
RI.E7.W.3.d: Use precise words and phrases, relevant descriptive details, and figurative and sensory language to establish a mood that evokes an emotion, to capture action, and to convey experiences or events.
RI.E7.W.3.e: Provide a conclusion that follows from and reflects on the narrated experiences or events.
RI.E7.W.4: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.
RI.E7.W.5: Develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach, focusing on how well purpose and audience have been addressed.
RI.E7.W.5.a: Demonstrate command of standard English conventions.
RI.E7.W.5.b: Demonstrate the ability to select accurate vocabulary appropriate for audience and purpose.
RI.E7.W.6: Use technology, including current web-based communication platforms, to produce and publish writing and link to and cite sources as well as to interact and collaborate with others.
RI.E7.W.7: Conduct short as well as more sustained research projects to answer a question, drawing on several sources and generating additional related, focused questions for further research and investigation.
RI.E7.W.8: When conducting research, gather relevant information from multiple print and digital sources, using search terms effectively; assess the credibility and accuracy of each source; and quote or paraphrase the data and conclusions of others while avoiding plagiarism and following a standard format for citation.
RI.E7.W.9: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support written analysis, interpretation, reflection, and research, applying one or more grade 7 Standards for Reading Literature or Reading Information as needed.
RI.E7.W.10: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of discipline-specific tasks, purposes, and audiences.
RI.E7.SL.1: Engage effectively in a range of collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in groups, and teacher-led) with diverse partners on grade 7 topics, texts, and issues, building on others' ideas and clearly expressing their own.
RI.E7.SL.1.a: Come to discussions prepared, having read or researched material under study; explicitly draw on that preparation by referring to evidence on the topic, text, or issue to probe and reflect on ideas under discussion.
RI.E7.SL.1.b: Follow rules for collegial discussions, track progress toward specific goals and deadlines, and define individual roles as needed.
RI.E7.SL.1.c: Pose questions that elicit elaboration and respond to others' questions and comments with relevant observations and ideas that bring the discussion back on topic as needed.
RI.E7.SL.1.d: Acknowledge new information expressed by others and, when warranted, modify their own views.
RI.E7.SL.2: Analyze the main ideas and supporting details presented in diverse media and formats (e.g., visually, quantitatively, orally) and explain how the ideas clarify a topic, text, or issue under study.
RI.E7.SL.3: Delineate a speaker's argument and specific claims, evaluating the soundness of the reasoning and the relevance and sufficiency of the evidence.
RI.E7.SL.4: Present claims and findings, emphasizing salient points in a focused, coherent manner with pertinent descriptions, facts, details, and examples; use appropriate vocabulary, eye contact, volume, and pronunciation.
RI.E7.SL.5: Include multimedia components and visual displays in presentations to clarify claims and findings and emphasize salient points.
RI.E7.SL.6: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate.
RI.E7.L.1: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking; retain and further develop language skills learned in previous grades.
RI.E7.L.1.a: Use phrases and clauses to communicate ideas precisely, with attention to skillful use of verb tenses to add clarity.
RI.E7.L.1.b: Recognize and correct vague pronouns (those that have unclear or ambiguous antecedents).
RI.E7.L.1.c: Recognize and correct inappropriate shifts in pronoun number and person in sentences with multiple clauses and phrases.
RI.E7.L.1.d: Recognize that changing the placement of a phrase or clause can add variety, emphasize particular relationships among ideas, or alter the meaning of a sentence or paragraph.
RI.E7.L.2: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.
RI.E7.L.2.a: Use a comma to separate coordinate adjectives (e.g., a fascinating, enjoyable movie).
RI.E7.L.2.b: Spell correctly, recognizing that some words have commonly accepted variations (e.g., donut/doughnut).
RI.E7.L.3: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening.
RI.E7.L.3.a: Maintain appropriate consistency in style and tone while varying sentence patterns for meaning and audience interest.
RI.E7.L.3.b: Recognize variations from standard or formal English in writing and speaking, determine their appropriateness for the intended purpose and audience, and make changes as necessary.
RI.E7.L.4: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grade 7 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.
RI.E7.L.4.a: Use context (e.g., the overall meaning of a sentence or paragraph; a word's position or function in a sentence) as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.
RI.E7.L.4.b: Use common, grade-appropriate Greek or Latin affixes and roots as clues to the meaning of a word (e.g., belligerent, bellicose, rebel).
RI.E7.L.4.c: Consult general and specialized reference materials (e.g., dictionaries, glossaries, thesauruses), both print and digital, to find the pronunciation of a word or determine or clarify its precise meaning or its part of speech.
RI.E7.L.4.d: Verify the preliminary determination of the meaning of a word or phrase (e.g., by checking the inferred meaning in context or in a dictionary).
RI.E7.L.5: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.
RI.E7.L.5.a: Interpret figures of speech (e.g., literary, biblical, mythological allusions) in context.
RI.E7.RF.5.b: Use the relationship between particular words (e.g., synonym/antonym, analogy) to better understand each of the words.
RI.E7.RF.5.c: Distinguish among the connotations (associations) of words with similar denotations (definitions) (e.g., refined, respectful, polite, diplomatic, condescending).
RI.E7.L.6: Acquire and use accurately grade-appropriate general academic and domain-specific words and phrases; independently research words and gather vocabulary knowledge.
RI.M7.RP.A: Analyze proportional relationships and use them to solve real-world and mathematical problems.
RI.M7.RP.A.1: Compute unit rates associated with ratios of fractions, including ratios of lengths, areas, and other quantities measured in like or different units.
RI.M7.RP.A.2: Recognize and represent proportional relationships between quantities.
RI.M7.RP.A.2.a: Decide whether two quantities are in a proportional relationship, e.g., by testing for equivalent ratios in a table, or graphing on a coordinate plane and observing whether the graph is a straight line through the origin.
RI.M7.RP.A.2.b: Identify the constant of proportionality (unit rate) in tables, graphs, equations, diagrams, and verbal descriptions of proportional relationships.
RI.M7.RP.A.2.d: Explain what a point `(x,y)` on the graph of a proportional relationship means in terms of the situation, with special attention to the points `(0,0)and(1,r)` where `r` is the unit rate.
RI.M7.RP.A.3: Use proportional relationships to solve multi-step ratio, rate, and percent problems.
RI.M7.NS.A: Apply and extend previous understandings of operations with fractions to add, subtract, multiply, and divide rational numbers.
RI.M7.NS.A.1: Apply and extend previous understandings of addition and subtraction to add and subtract integers and other rational numbers; represent addition and subtraction on a horizontal or vertical number line diagram.
RI.M7.NS.A.1.a: Describe situations in which opposite quantities combine to make zero.
RI.M7.NS.A.1.b: Understand `p+q` as the number located a distance `abs(q)` from `p`, in the positive or negative direction depending on whether `q` is positive or negative. Show that a number and its opposite have a sum of `0` (are additive inverses). Interpret sums of rational numbers by describing real-world contexts.
RI.M7.NS.A.1.c: Understand subtraction of rational numbers as adding the additive inverse, `p-q=p+(-q)`. Show that the distance between two rational numbers on the number line is the absolute value of their difference, and apply this principle in real-world contexts.
RI.M7.NS.A.1.d: Apply properties of operations as strategies to add and subtract rational numbers.
RI.M7.NS.A.2: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication and division and of fractions to multiply and divide integers and other rational numbers.
RI.M7.NS.A.2.a: Understand that multiplication is extended from fractions to rational numbers by requiring that operations continue to satisfy the properties of operations, particularly the distributive property, leading to products such as `(-1)(-1)=1` and the rules for multiplying signed numbers. Interpret products of rational numbers by describing real-world contexts.
RI.M7.NS.A.2.b: Understand that integers can be divided, provided that the divisor is not zero, and every quotient of integers (with non-zero divisor) is a rational number. If `pandq` are integers, then `-(p/q)=(-p)/q=p/(-q)`. Interpret quotients of rational numbers by describing real-world contexts.
RI.M7.NS.A.2.c: Apply properties of operations as strategies to multiply and divide rational numbers.
RI.M7.NS.A.2.d: Convert a rational number to a decimal using long division; know that the decimal form of a rational number terminates in 0s or eventually repeats.
RI.M7.NS.A.3: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving the four operations with integers and other rational numbers.
RI.M7.EE.A: Use properties of operations to generate equivalent expressions.
RI.M7.EE.A.1: Apply properties of operations to add, subtract, factor, and expand linear expressions with rational coefficients.
RI.M7.EE.A.2: Understand that rewriting an expression in different forms in a problem context can shed light on the problem and how the quantities in it are related.
RI.M7.EE.B: Solve real-life and mathematical problems using numerical and algebraic expressions and equations.
RI.M7.EE.B.3: Solve multi-step real-life and mathematical problems posed with positive and negative rational numbers in any form (whole numbers, fractions, and decimals), using tools strategically. Apply properties of operations to calculate with numbers in any form; convert between forms as appropriate; and assess the reasonableness of answers using mental computation and estimation strategies.
RI.M7.EE.B.4: Use variables to represent quantities in a real-world or mathematical problem, and construct simple equations and inequalities to solve problems by reasoning about the quantities.
RI.M7.EE.B.4.a: Solve word problems leading to equations of the form px + q = r and p(x ÷ q) = r, where p, q,and r are specific rational numbers. Solve equations of these forms fluently. Compare an algebraic solution to an arithmetic solution, identifying the sequence of the operations used in each approach.
RI.M7.EE.B.4.b: Solve word problems leading to inequalities of the form `px+q>rorpx+q<r`, where `p,q,andr` are specific rational numbers. Graph the solution set of the inequality and interpret it in the context of the problem.
RI.M7.EE.B.4.c: Extend analysis of patterns to include analyzing, extending, and determining an expression for simple arithmetic and geometric sequences (e.g., compounding, increasing area), using tables, graphs, words, and expressions.
RI.M7.G.A: Draw, construct, and describe geometrical figures and describe the relationships between them.
RI.M7.G.A.1: Solve problems involving scale drawings of geometric figures, such as computing actual lengths and areas from a scale drawing and reproducing a scale drawing at a different scale.
RI.M7.G.A.2: Draw (freehand, with ruler and protractor, and with technology) two-dimensional geometric shapes with given conditions. Focus on constructing triangles from three measures of angles or sides, noticing when the conditions determine a unique triangle, more than one triangle, or no triangle.
RI.M7.G.A.3: Describe the shape of the two-dimensional face of the figure that results from slicing three-dimensional figures, as in plane sections of right rectangular prisms and right rectangular pyramids.
RI.M7.G.B: Solve real-life and mathematical problems involving angle measure, area, surface area, and volume.
RI.M7.G.B.4.a: Know that a circle is a two-dimensional shape created by connecting all of the points equidistant from a fixed point called the center of the circle.
RI.M7.G.B.4.b: Understand and describe the relationships among the radius, diameter, and circumference of a circle.
RI.M7.G.B.4.c: Understand and describe the relationship among the radius, diameter, and area of a circle.
RI.M7.G.B.4.d: Know the formulas for the area and circumference of a circle and use them to solve problems.
RI.M7.G.B.4.e: Give an informal derivation of the relationship between the circumference and area of a circle.
RI.M7.G.B.5: Use facts about supplementary, complementary, vertical, and adjacent angles in a multi-step problem to write simple equations and use them to solve for an unknown angle in a figure.
RI.M7.G.B.6: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving area, volume, and surface area of two- and three-dimensional objects composed of triangles, quadrilaterals, polygons, cubes, and right prisms.
RI.M7.SP.A: Use random sampling to draw inferences about a population.
RI.M7.SP.A.1: Understand that statistics can be used to gain information about a population by examining a sample of the population; Generalizations about a population from a sample are valid only if the sample is representative of that population. Understand that random sampling tends to produce representative samples and support valid inferences.
RI.M7.SP.A.2: Use data from a random sample to draw inferences about a population with an unknown characteristic of interest. Generate multiple samples (or simulated samples) of the same size to gauge the variation in estimates or predictions.
RI.M7.SP.B: Draw informal comparative inferences about two populations.
RI.M7.SP.B.3: Informally assess the degree of visual overlap of two numerical data distributions with similar variabilities, measuring the difference between the centers by expressing it as a multiple of a measure of variability.
RI.M7.SP.B.4: Use measures of center and measures of variability for numerical data from random samples to draw informal comparative inferences about two populations.
RI.M7.SP.C: Investigate chance processes and develop, use, and evaluate probability models.
RI.M7.SP.C.5: Understand that the probability of a chance event is a number between `0and1` that expresses the likelihood of the event occurring. Larger numbers indicate greater likelihood. A probability near `0` indicates an unlikely event, a probability around `1/2` indicates an event that is neither unlikely nor likely, and a probability near `1` indicates a likely event.
RI.M7.SP.C.6: Approximate the probability of a chance event by collecting data on the chance process that produces it and observing its long-run relative frequency, and predict the approximate relative frequency given the probability.
