SC.EK.F.3.5: Blend letter sounds to decode vowel-consonant (VC) and consonant- vowel-consonant (CVC) words in isolation and in text.
SC.EK.F.3.6: Delete, add, and substitute the initial, medial, and final letters in CVC words to build or make new words.
SC.EK.F.3.7: Use knowledge that every syllable must have a vowel sound to determine the number of syllables in words.
SC.EK.F.3.8: Decode and encode words using VC, CV, CVC, consonant digraphs (i.e., ch, sh, th, wh), and combination (i.e., qu).
SC.EK.F.4: Read and reread grade-appropriate texts with accuracy and expression at an appropriate rate to support comprehension.
SC.EK.F.4.1: Read high-frequency words commonly found in grade-appropriate text with accuracy and automaticity.
SC.EK.F.4.2: Read texts orally with accuracy and expression.
SC.EK.F.4.3.a: Using letter-sound knowledge to segment and blend sounds together.
SC.EK.F.4.3.c: Using visuals from the text to support decoding and confirm recognition.
SC.EK.AOR.1: Evaluate and critique key literary elements that enhance and deepen meaning within and across texts.
SC.EK.AOR.1.1: Identify and describe the main character(s), setting, and events that move the plot forward.
SC.EK.AOR.1.2: Identify forms of figurative language to include alliteration and onomatopoeia, as well as descriptive words and rhyme in text.
SC.EK.AOR.2: Evaluate and critique the development of themes and central ideas within and across texts.
SC.EK.AOR.2.1: Retell familiar stories using main story elements in a literary text.
SC.EK.AOR.2.2: Retell familiar texts by identifying the topic and supporting details in an informational text.
SC.EK.AOR.3: Evaluate how an author's choice of point of view or perspective shapes style and meaning within and across literary texts.
SC.EK.AOR.3.1: Identify and explain the roles of the author and the illustrator of a story.
SC.EK.AOR.4: Evaluate and critique how an author's perspective and purpose shape style and meaning within and across informational texts.
SC.EK.AOR.4.1: Identify and explain the roles of the author and the illustrator in an informational text.
SC.EK.AOR.5: Evaluate and critique how an author uses words, phrases, and text structures to craft text.
SC.EK.AOR.5.1: Identify and describe the basic characteristics of literary text to include narrative, drama, and poetry.
SC.EK.AOR.5.2: Identify and use text features such as titles, headings, subheadings, illustrations, and/or photographs to predict and confirm the topic of informational texts.
SC.EK.AOR.5.3: Identify an author's opinion about a topic in an informational text.
SC.EK.AOR.6: Summarize and paraphrase text to support comprehension and understanding.
SC.EK.AOR.6.1: Retell a text orally to enhance comprehension.
SC.EK.AOR.6.1.a: Include main character(s), setting, and important events for a story.
SC.EK.AOR.6.1.b: Include topic and supporting details for an informational text.
SC.EK.AOR.7: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases.
SC.EK.AOR.7.1: Determine the meaning of known and unknown words and phrases, choosing from an array of strategies:
SC.EK.AOR.7.1.a: Ask and answer questions about words and phrases to determine their meaning.
SC.EK.AOR.7.1.b: Use words and phrases acquired through conversations, being read to, and responding to texts.
SC.EK.AOR.8: Analyze word relationships and nuances in word meanings within literary and informational texts.
SC.EK.AOR.8.1: Determine the effectiveness of an author's use of words and phrases in literary, informational, and multimedia texts.
SC.EK.AOR.8.1.a: Sort words and phrases into categories (e.g., apple, fruit and carrot, vegetable) to develop an understanding of word relationships.
SC.EK.AOR.8.1.b: Deepen understanding of words by relating words to their opposites.
SC.EK.AOR.8.1.c: Identify and explain descriptive words and phrases that suggest feelings or appeal to the senses.
SC.EK.AOR.9: Build and apply a range of academic vocabulary, as well as grade-level appropriate morphology to apply to reading, writing, and speaking.
SC.EK.AOR.9.1: Use knowledge of morphemes to extract meaning from oral language in grade-appropriate content.
SC.EK.AOR.10: Evaluate and critique multimedia presentations of a text or subject, including their impact on an audience.
SC.EK.AOR.10.1: Describe the relationship between visuals (e.g., illustrations, photographs) and the text.
SC.EK.R.1: Use critical thinking skills to investigate, evaluate, and synthesize a variety of sources to obtain and refine knowledge.
SC.EK.R.1.1: Ask and answer questions (who, what, when, where, why, and how) about print and non-print sources to obtain and refine knowledge.
SC.EK.C.1: Write arguments to support claims with clear reasons and relevant evidence.
SC.EK.C.1.1: Use a combination of drawing, dictating, and writing to state a topic and communicate an opinion and a supporting reason.
SC.EK.C.2: Write informative/expository texts to analyze and explain complex ideas and information.
SC.EK.C.2.1: Use a combination of drawing, dictating, and writing to compose informative/explanatory pieces about a topic with supporting details.
SC.EK.C.3: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences using effective techniques.
SC.EK.C.3.1: Use a combination of drawing, dictating, and writing to narrate a single event or linked events in a logical order.
SC.EK.C.4: Demonstrate command of standard English grammar and conventions when writing.
SC.EK.C.4.1: Form and use complete simple sentences. When writing:
SC.EK.C.4.1.a: Capitalize the first word in a sentence and the pronoun I.
SC.EK.C.4.1.b: Identify and name end punctuation marks (e.g., periods, exclamation points, and question marks).
SC.EK.C.4.1.c: Identify and use periods to punctuate sentences.
SC.EK.C.4.1.d: Identify and use common singular and plural nouns.
SC.EK.C.4.1.f: Identify and use simple and declarative sentences.
SC.EK.C.5: Revise writing to improve clarity and enhance style appropriate to audience, purpose, and task.
SC.EK.C.5.1: With guidance and support, plan, revise, edit, and build on personal ideas and the ideas of others to strengthen writing.
SC.EK.C.6: Write independently and legibly for a variety of tasks and purposes.
SC.EK.C.6.1: Print all uppercase and lowercase letters, focusing on pencil grasp, letter formation, legibility, and pacing; use appropriate spacing for letters, words, and sentences.
SC.EK.C.7: Organize and communicate ideas through a range of formats to engage a variety of audiences.
SC.EK.C.7.1: Present information orally in a logical order of events using conjunctions and temporal words (e.g., before, after).
SC.EK.C.8: Through collaboration, react and respond to information while building upon the ideas of others and respecting diverse perspectives.
SC.EK.C.8.1: Participate with peers and adults in structured discussions and routines about grade-appropriate topics and texts:
SC.EK.C.8.1.a: Enter a conversation by greeting, taking turns, and responding to others with statements, phrases, and/or questions.
SC.EK.C.8.1.b: Consider the ideas of others while engaging in conversations.
SC.EK.C.9: Evaluate and critique ideas and concepts interactively through listening and speaking.
SC.EK.C.9.1: Ask and answer questions in conversation on a topic.
SC.MK.DPSR.1: Collect and organize data and communicate through multiple representations.
SC.MK.DPSR.1.1: Sort pictures or objects into at least two categories. Count to determine how many are in each category. Limit to 20 pictures or objects.
SC.MK.DPSR.1.2: Answer questions about data organized in a t-chart, object graph, or picture graph.
SC.MK.MGSR.1: Describe and compare objects in real-world situations using units of length, weight, money, and time.
SC.MK.MGSR.1.1: Identify a penny, nickel, dime, and quarter.

SC.M2.NR.1: Represent multi-digit numbers in a variety of ways to build place value understanding.

SC.M2.PAFR.1.2: Determine and explain if an equation (within 20) is true using a variety of equation formats.

SC.M2.PAFR.1.5: Add and subtract number combinations flexibly and accurately within 20.

SC.M2.PAFR.1.7: Determine the unknown number in addition and subtraction equations within 20, with the unknown in any position.

SC.M3.MGSR.3.2: Identify, describe, and draw points, lines, line segments, rays, intersecting lines, perpendicular lines, and parallel lines. Identify these in two-dimensional figures.

SC.M3.NR.2.5: Recognize two fractions are equivalent based on the same size whole. Limit denominators to `2,3,4,6,and8`, and fractions should be limited to fractions between 0 and 1.
SC.M3.NR.2.6: Compare two fractions with the same numerator or same denominator based on the same size whole by reasoning about their size. SC.S8.LS.1.4: Use arguments, based on empirical evidence and scientific reasoning, to support an explanation for how characteristic animal behaviors and specialized plant structures affect the probability of successful reproduction of animals and plants respectively.

TN.EK.FL.PC.1: Demonstrate understanding of the organization and basic features of print.
TN.EK.FL.PC.1.a: Follow words from left to right, top to bottom, and page by page.
TN.EK.FL.PC.1.b: Recognize that spoken words are represented in written language by specific sequences of letters.
TN.EK.FL.PC.1.c: Understand that words are separated by spaces in print; demonstrate one-to-one correspondence between voice and print.
TN.EK.FL.PC.1.d: Recognize and name all upper and lowercase letters of the alphabet in isolation and in connected text.
TN.EK.FL.PA.2: Demonstrate understanding of spoken words, syllables, and sounds (phonemes).
TN.EK.FL.PA.2.a: Recognize and begin to produce rhyming words.
TN.EK.FL.PA.2.b: Count, pronounce, blend, and segment syllables in spoken words.
TN.EK.FL.PA.2.c: Blend and segment onsets and rimes of single-syllable spoken words.
TN.EK.FL.PA.2.d: Isolate and pronounce the initial, medial vowel, and final sounds (phonemes) in two- and three-phoneme (VC or CVC) words, excluding CVC words ending with /l/, /r/, or /x/.
TN.EK.FL.PA.2.e: Add or substitute individual sounds (phonemes) in simple, one-syllable words to make new words.
TN.EK.FL.PWR.3: Know and apply grade-level phonics and word analysis skills when decoding isolated words and in connected text.
TN.EK.FL.PWR.3.a: Demonstrate knowledge of one-to-one letter sound correspondence by producing the most frequent sound for each consonant.
TN.EK.FL.PWR.3.b: Associate the long and short phonemes with common spellings for the five major vowels.
TN.EK.FL.PWR.3.c: Read common high-frequency words by sight.
TN.EK.FL.PWR.3.e: Distinguish between similarly spelled words by identifying the letters that differ.
TN.EK.FL.WC.4: Know and apply grade-level phonics and word analysis skills when encoding words; write legibly.
TN.EK.FL.WC.4.a: Write uppercase and lowercase manuscript letters from memory.
TN.EK.FL.WC.4.b: Write a letter/letters for most consonant and short vowel sounds (phonemes).
TN.EK.FL.WC.4.c: Represent phonemes first to last in simple words using letters (graphemes) such as rop for rope.
TN.EK.FL.WC.4.d: Spell VC (at, in) and CVC (pet, mud) words with short vowels; spell V (a, I) and CV (be, go) words with long vowels.
TN.EK.FL.WC.4.e: Identify the letters used to represent vowel phonemes and those used to represent consonants; know that every syllable has a vowel.
TN.EK.FL.WC.4.f: Write some common, frequently used words (am, and, like, the).
TN.EK.FL.WC.4.g: Print many upper and lowercase letters.
TN.EK.FL.F.5: Read with sufficient accuracy and fluency to support comprehension.
TN.EK.FL.F.5.a: Read emergent-reader texts with purpose and understanding.
TN.EK.FL.SC.6: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when speaking and conventions of standard English grammar and usage, including capitalization and punctuation, when writing with adult support.
TN.EK.FL.SC.6.a: With modeling or verbal prompts, orally produce complete sentences.
TN.EK.FL.SC.6.b: Follow one-to-one correspondence between voice and print when writing a sentence.
TN.EK.FL.SC.6.c: Use frequently occurring nouns and verbs when speaking and in shared language activities.
TN.EK.FL.SC.6.d: Form regular plural nouns when speaking and in shared language activities.
TN.EK.FL.SC.6.e: Understand and use question words (interrogatives) when speaking and in shared language activities.
TN.EK.FL.SC.6.f: Use the most frequently occurring prepositions when speaking and in shared language activities.
TN.EK.FL.SC.6.g: Produce and expand complete sentences in shared language activities.
TN.EK.FL.SC.6.h: Capitalize the first word in a sentence and the pronoun I.
TN.EK.FL.VA.7a: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on Kindergarten conversations, reading, and content.
TN.EK.FL.VA.7a.i: Identify new meanings for familiar words and apply them accurately.
TN.EK.FL.VA.7a.ii: Use the most frequently occurring inflections and affixes as a clue to the meaning of an unknown word.
TN.EK.FL.VA.7b: With guidance and support from adults, explore word relationships and nuances in word meanings.
TN.EK.FL.VA.7b.i: Sort common objects into categories to gain a sense of the concepts the categories represent.
TN.EK.FL.VA.7b.ii: Demonstrate understanding of frequently occurring verbs and adjectives by relating them to their opposites.
TN.EK.FL.VA.7b.iii: Make real-life connections between words and their use.
TN.EK.FL.VA.7b.iv: Distinguish shades of meaning among verbs describing the same general action.
TN.EK.FL.VA.7c: Use words and phrases acquired through conversations, reading and being read to, and responding to texts.
TN.EK.RL.KID.1: With prompting and support, ask and answer questions about key details in a text.
TN.EK.RL.KID.2: With prompting and support, orally retell familiar stories, including key details.
TN.EK.RL.KID.3: With prompting and support, orally identify characters, setting, and major events in a story.
TN.EK.RL.CS.4: With prompting and support, ask and answer questions about unknown words in text.
TN.EK.RL.CS.6: With prompting and support, define the role of authors and illustrators in the telling of a story.
TN.EK.RL.IKI.7: With prompting and support, orally describe the relationship between illustrations and the story in which they appear.
TN.EK.RL.IKI.9: With prompting and support, orally compare and contrast the adventures and experiences of characters in familiar stories.
TN.EK.RL.RRTC: Range Of Reading & Level Of Text Complexity
TN.EK.RL.RRTC.10: With prompting and support, read stories and poems of appropriate complexity for Kindergarten.
TN.EK.RI.KID.1: With prompting and support, ask and answer questions about key details in a text.
TN.EK.RI.KID.2: With prompting and support, orally identify the main topic and retell key details of a text.
TN.EK.RI.KID.3: With prompting and support, orally identify the connection between two individuals, events, ideas, or pieces of information in a text.
TN.EK.RI.CS.4: With prompting and support, determine the meaning of words and phrases in a text relevant to a Kindergarten topic or subject area.
TN.EK.RI.CS.6: With prompting and support, define the role of an author and illustrator in presenting the ideas or information in a text.
TN.EK.RI.IKI.7: With prompting and support, orally describe the relationship between illustrations and the text in which they appear.
TN.EK.RI.IKI.8: With prompting and support, identify the reasons an author provides to support points in a text.
TN.EK.RI.IKI.9: With prompting and support, orally identify basic similarities and differences between two texts on the same topic.
TN.EK.RI.RRTC: Range Of Reading & Level Of Text Complexity
TN.EK.RI.RRTC.10: With prompting and support, read informational texts of appropriate complexity for Kindergarten.
TN.EK.SL.CC.1: Participate with varied peers and adults in collaborative conversations in small or large groups about appropriate Kindergarten topics.
TN.EK.SL.CC.2: Confirm understanding of a text read aloud or information presented orally or through other media by asking and answering questions about key details and requesting clarification if something is not understood.
TN.EK.SL.CC.3: Ask and answer questions in order to seek help, get information, or clarify something that is not understood.
TN.EK.SL.PKI.4: Describe familiar people, places, things, and events, and, with prompting and support, provide additional detail.
TN.EK.SL.PKI.5: Add drawings or other visual displays of descriptions as desired to provide additional detail.
TN.EK.SL.PKI.6: With guidance and support, express thoughts, feelings, and ideas through speaking.
TN.EK.W.TTP.1: With prompting and support, use a combination of drawing, dictating, and/or writing to compose opinion pieces.
TN.EK.W.TTP.2: With prompting and support, use a combination of drawing, dictating, and/or writing to compose informative/explanatory texts.
TN.EK.W.TTP.3: With prompting and support, use a combination of drawing, dictating, and/or writing to narrate a single event.
TN.EK.W.PDW.4: With guidance and support, produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.
TN.EK.W.PDW.5: With guidance and support from adults, respond to questions and suggestions from others and add details to strengthen writing as needed.
TN.EK.W.PDW.6: With guidance and support from adults, and in collaboration with peers, explore a variety of digital tools to produce and share writing.
TN.EK.W.RBPK.7: Participate in shared research and writing projects, such as reading a number of books by a favorite author and expressing opinions about them.
TN.EK.W.RBPK.8: With guidance and support from adults, recall information from experiences or gather information from provided sources to answer a question.
TN.EK.W.RW.10: With guidance and support from adults, engage routinely in writing activities to promote writing fluency and build writing stamina.
TN.MK.CC.A: Know number names and the counting sequence.
TN.MK.CC.A.1: Count to 100 by ones, fives, and tens. Count backward from 10.
TN.MK.CC.A,2: Count forward by ones beginning from any given number within the known sequence (instead of having to begin at 1).
TN.MK.CC.A.3: Write numbers from 0 to 20. Represent a quantity of objects with a written number 0-20.
TN.MK.CC.A.4: Recognize, describe, extend, and create patterns and explain a simple rule for a pattern using concrete materials. Analyze the structure of the repeating pattern by identifying the unit (core) of the pattern.
TN.MK.CC.B: Count to tell the number of objects.
TN.MK.CC.B.5: Understand the relationship between numbers and quantities; connect counting to cardinality.
TN.MK.CC.B.5.a: When counting objects 1-20, say the number names in the standard order, using one-to-one correspondence.
TN.MK.CC.B.5.b: Recognize that the last number name said tells the number of objects counted. The number of objects is the same regardless of their arrangement or the order in which they were counted.
TN.MK.CC.B.5.c: Recognize that each successive number name refers to a quantity that is one greater and each previous number is one less.
TN.MK.CC.B.6: Count to answer “how many?” questions about as many as 20 things arranged in a line, a rectangular array, a circle, or as many as 10 things in a scattered configuration. Given a number from 1-20, count out that many objects.
TN.MK.CC.C.7: Identify whether the number of objects in one group is greater than, less than, or equal to the number of objects in another group.
TN.MK.CC.C.8: Compare two given numbers up to 10, when written as numerals, using the terms greater than, less than, or equal to.
TN.MK.OA.A: Represent and solve problems involving addition and subtraction.
TN.MK.OA.A.1: Represent addition and subtraction with objects, fingers, drawings, acting out situations, verbal explanations, expressions, or equations.
TN.MK.OA.A.2: Represent addition and subtraction with objects, fingers, drawings, acting out situations, verbal explanations, expressions, or equations.
TN.MK.OA.A.3: Decompose numbers less than or equal to 10 into addend pairs in more than one way (e.g., 5 = 2 + 3 and 5 = 4 + 1) by using objects or drawings. Record each decomposition using a drawing or writing an equation.
TN.MK.OA.A.4: Find the number that makes 10, when added to any given number, from 1 to 9 using objects or drawings. Record the answer using a drawing or writing an equation.
TN.MK.OA.A.5: Use mental strategies flexibly to develop fluency in addition and subtraction within 10.
TN.MK.NBT.A: Work with numbers 11- 19 to gain foundations for place value.
TN.MK.NBT.A.1: Compose and decompose numbers from 11 to 19 into a group of ten ones and some more ones by using objects or drawings (e.g., 18 equals 10 + 8). Record the composition or decomposition using a drawing or by writing an equation
TN.MK.MD.A.1: Describe the measurable attributes of an object, such as length (long/short), height (tall/short), or weight (heavy/light).
TN.MK.MD.A.2: Directly compare two objects with a measurable attribute in common, to describe which object has more of/less of the attribute.
TN.MK.MD.B.3: Identify the penny, nickel, dime, and quarter based on their attributes (size and color) and recognize the value of each.
TN.MK.MD.C: Classify objects and count the number of objects in each category.
TN.MK.MD.C.4: Sort a collection of objects into a given category, with 10 or fewer in each category. Compare the categories by group size.
TN.MK.G.A: Identify and describe shapes and solids.
TN.MK.G.A.1: Describe objects in the environment using names of shapes and solids (squares, circles, triangles, rectangles, hexagons, cubes, cones, cylinders, and spheres). Describe the relative positions of these objects using terms such as above, below, beside, in front of, behind, between, and next to.
TN.MK.G.A.2: Correctly name shapes and solids (squares, circles, triangles, rectangles, hexagons, cubes, cones, cylinders, and spheres) regardless of their orientations or overall size.
TN.MK.G.A.3: Identify shapes (squares, circles, triangles, rectangles, and hexagons) as two-dimensional and solids (cubes, cones, cylinders, and spheres) as three-dimensional.
TN.MK.G.B: Analyze, compare, create, and compose shapes.
TN.MK.G.B.4: Describe similarities and differences between two- and three-dimensional shapes/solids, in different sizes and orientations.
TN.MK.G.B.5: Model shapes/solids in the world by building or drawing them.
TN.MK.G.B.6: Compose a figure using simple shapes/solids and identify smaller shapes/solids within the figure.
TN.SK.PS.1.1: Plan and conduct an investigation to describe and classify different kinds of materials including wood, plastic, metal, cloth, and paper by their observable properties (color, texture, hardness, and flexibility) and whether they are natural or human-made.
TN.SK.PS.1.2: Conduct investigations to understand that matter can exist in different states (solid and liquid) and has properties that can be observed and tested.
TN.SK.PS.1.3: Construct an evidence-based account of how an object made of a small set of pieces (blocks, snap cubes) can be disassembled and made into a new object.
TN.SK.LS.1: From Molecules To Organisms: Structure & Process
TN.SK.LS.1.1: Use information from observations to identify differences between plants and animals (locomotion, obtainment of food, and take in air/gasses).
TN.SK.LS.1.2: Recognize differences between living organisms and non-living materials and sort them into groups by observable physical attributes.
TN.SK.LS.1.3: Explain how humans use their five senses in making scientific findings.
TN.SK.LS.3.1: Make observations to describe that young plants and animals resemble their parents.
TN.SK.ESS.2.1: Analyze and interpret weather data (precipitation, wind, temperature, cloud cover) to describe weather patterns that occur over time (hourly, daily) using simple graphs, pictorial weather symbols, and tools (thermometer, rain gauge).
TN.SK.ESS.2.2: Develop and use models to predict weather and identify patterns in spring, summer, autumn, and winter.
TN.SK.ESS.3.1: Use a model to represent the relationship between the basic needs (shelter, food, water) of different plants and animals (including humans) and the places they live.
TN.SK.ESS.3.2: Explain the purpose of weather forecasting to prepare for, and respond to, severe weather in Tennessee.
TN.SK.ESS.3.3: Communicate solutions that will reduce the impact from humans on land, water, air, and other living things in the local environment.
TN.SK.ETS.1.1: Ask and answer questions about the scientific world and gather information using the senses.
TN.SK.ETS.1.2: Describe objects accurately by drawing and/or labeling pictures.
TN.SK.ETS.2: Links Among Engineering, Technology, Science & Society
TN.SK.ETS.2.1: Use appropriate tools (magnifying glass, rain gauge, basic balance scale) to make observations and answer testable scientific questions.
TN.SSK.1: Describe familiar people, places, things, and events within a student's home, school, and community.
TN.SSK.2: Compare and contrast family traditions and customs, including: food, clothing, homes, and games.
TN.SSK.4: Identify and explain how basic human needs of food, clothing, shelter, and transportation are met.
TN.SSK.5: Explain the benefits of saving money.
TN.SSK.6: Recognize and describe different types of jobs, including work done in the home, school, and community.
TN.SSK.7: Give examples of how people use money to make purchases.
TN.SSK.8: Use personal directions such as: up, down, near, far, left, right, in front of, and behind.
TN.SSK.9: Explain what a map and globe represent.
TN.SSK.10: Recall the student's and/or school's street address, city/town, and state.
TN.SSK.11: Give examples of the following concepts: authority, fairness, responsibility, and rules.
TN.SSK.12: Identify the following state and national symbols: American flag, Tennessee flag, and the words of the Pledge of Allegiance.
TN.SSK.13: Recognize and name the current President of the U.S.
TN.SSK.14: Explain that the President is the leader of the U.S.
TN.SSK.15: Describe roles of authority figures in the home, school, and community, including: caregivers, teachers, school principal, police officers, and fire/rescue workers.
TN.SSK.16: Explain the purpose of rules and laws.
TN.SSK.17: Use correct words and phrases related to chronology and time.
TN.SSK.18: Identify days of the week and months of the year.
TN.SSK.19: Locate and describe events on a calendar, including: birthdays, holidays, cultural events, and school events.
TN.SSK.20: Identify and discuss the following holidays, and analyze why we celebrate them.
TN.E1.FL.PC.1: Demonstrate understanding of the organization and basic features of print.
TN.E1.FL.PC.1.a: Recognize the distinguishing features of a sentence, such as first word, capitalization, and ending punctuation.
TN.E1.FL.PA.2: Demonstrate understanding of spoken words, syllables, and sounds (phonemes).
TN.E1.FL.PA.2.a: Distinguish long from short vowel sounds in spoken single-syllable words.
TN.E1.FL.PA.2.b: Orally produce single-syllable words by blending sounds (phonemes) in spoken single-syllable words.
TN.E1.FL.PA.2.c: Isolate and pronounce initial, medial vowel, and final sounds (phonemes) in spoken single-syllable words.
TN.E1.FL.PA.2.d: Segment spoken single-syllable words into their complete sequence of individual sounds (phonemes).
TN.E1.FL.PWR.3: Know and apply grade-level phonics and word analysis skills when decoding isolated words and in connected text.
TN.E1.FL.PWR.3.a: Know the sound-spelling correspondence for common consonant digraphs.
TN.E1.FL.PWR.3.c: Know the final -e and common vowel team conventions for representing long vowel sounds, including r controlled vowels.
TN.E1.FL.PWR.3.d: Use knowledge that every syllable must have a vowel sound to determine the number of syllables in a printed word.
TN.E1.FL.PWR.3.e: Decode two-syllable words following basic patterns by breaking the words into syllables.
TN.E1.FL.PWR.3.g: Recognize and read grade-appropriate irregularly spelled words.
TN.E1.FL.PWR.3.h: Read grade-level decodable text with purpose and understanding.
TN.E1.FL.WC.4: Know and apply grade-level phonics and word analysis skills when encoding words; write legibly.
TN.E1.FL.WC.4.a: Use conventional spelling for one-syllable words with common consonant spelling patterns, including consonant diagraphs, double letters, and initial and final consonant blends.
TN.E1.FL.WC.4.b: Use conventional spelling for one-syllable words with common vowel spelling patterns including VCVe, common vowel teams, final -y, and r-controlled vowels.
TN.E1.FL.WC.4.d: Spell two-syllable words that end in -y or -ly, are compounds, or have two closed syllables.
TN.E1.FL.WC.4.e: Spell untaught words phonetically, drawing on phonemic awareness and spelling conventions.
TN.E1.FL.WC.4.f: Write many common, frequently used words and some irregular words.
TN.E1.FL.WC.4.g: Print all upper and lowercase letters.
TN.E1.FL.F.5: Read with sufficient accuracy and fluency to support comprehension.
TN.E1.FL.F.5.a: Read grade-level text with purpose and understanding.
TN.E1.FL.F.5.b: Read grade-level text orally with accuracy, appropriate rate, and expression on successive readings.
TN.E1.FL.F.5.c: Use context to confirm or self-correct word recognition and understanding of words; reread as necessary.
TN.E1.FL.SC.6: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when speaking and conventions of standard English grammar and usage, including capitalization and punctuation, when writing.
TN.E1.FL.SC.6.a: Use common, proper, and possessive nouns.
TN.E1.FL.SC.6.b: Use singular and plural nouns with correct verbs in basic sentences.
TN.E1.FL.SC.6.c: Use personal, possessive, and indefinite pronouns.
TN.E1.FL.SC.6.d: Use verbs to convey a sense of past, present, and future.
TN.E1.FL.SC.6.h: Use frequently occurring prepositions, such as during, beyond, and toward.
TN.E1.FL.SC.6.i: Produce and expand simple and compound declarative, interrogative, imperative, and exclamatory sentences in response to prompts.
TN.E1.FL.SC.6.j: Capitalize names of people and dates.
TN.E1.FL.SC.6.l: Use commas in dates and to separate single words in a series.
TN.E1.FL.VA.7a: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grade 1 reading and content, choosing flexibly from an array of strategies.
TN.E1.FL.VA.7a.i: Use sentence-level context as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.
TN.E1.FL.VA.7a.ii: Use frequently occurring affixes as a clue to the meaning of a word.
TN.E1.FL.VA.7a.iii: Identify frequently occurring root words and their inflectional forms.
TN.E1.FL.VA.7b: With guidance and support from adults, demonstrate understanding of word relationships and nuances in word meanings.
TN.E1.FL.VA.7b.i: Sort words into categories to gain a sense of the concepts the categories represent.
TN.E1.FL.VA.7b.ii: Define words by category and by one or more key attributes.
TN.E1.FL.VA.7b.iii: Identify real-life connections between words and their use.
TN.E1.FL.VA.7b.iv: Distinguish shades of meaning among words by defining or choosing them or by acting out the meanings.
TN.E1.FL.VA.7c: Use words and phrases acquired through conversations, reading and being read to, and responding to texts, including using frequently occurring conjunctions to signal simple relationships.
TN.E1.RL.KID.1: Ask and answer questions about key details in a text.
TN.E1.RL.KID.2: Retell stories, including key details, and demonstrate understanding of their central message or lesson.
TN.E1.RL.KID.3: Using graphic organizers or including written details and illustrations when developmentally appropriate, describe characters, settings, and major events in a story using key details.
TN.E1.RL.CS.4: Identify words and phrases in stories and poems that suggest feelings or appeal to the senses.
TN.E1.RL.CS.5: Explain major differences between books that tell stories and books that give information, drawing on a wide range of text types.
TN.E1.RL.CS.6: Identify who is telling the story at various points in a text.
TN.E1.RL.IKI.7: Either orally or in writing when appropriate, use illustrations and words in a text to describe its characters, setting, or events.
TN.E1.RL.IKI.9: Compare and contrast the adventures and experiences of characters in stories including written details and illustrations when developmentally appropriate.
TN.E1.RL.RRTC: Range Of Reading & Level Of Text Complexity
TN.E1.RL.RRTC.10: With prompting and support, read stories and poems of appropriate complexity for grade 1.
TN.E1.RI.KID.1: Ask and answer questions about key details in a text.
TN.E1.RI.KID.2: Identify the main topic and retell key details of a text.
TN.E1.RI.KID.3: Using graphic organizers or including written details and illustrations when developmentally appropriate, describe the connections between two individuals, events, ideas, or pieces of information in a text.
TN.E1.RI.CS.4: Determine the meaning of words and phrases in a text relevant to a grade 1 topic or subject area.
TN.E1.RI.CS.5: Know and use various text features to locate key facts or information in a text.
TN.E1.RI.CS.6: Distinguish between information provided by pictures or other illustrations and information provided by the words in a text.
TN.E1.RI.IKI.7: Either orally or in writing when appropriate, use the illustrations and words in a text to describe its key ideas.
TN.E1.RI.IKI.8: Identify the reasons an author provides to support points in a text.
TN.E1.RI.IKI.9: Identify basic similarities and differences between two texts on the same topic including written details and illustrations when developmentally appropriate.
TN.E1.RI.RRTC: Range Of Reading & Level Of Text Complexity
TN.E1.RI.RRTC.10: With prompting and support, read informational texts of appropriate complexity for grade 1.
TN.E1.SL.CC.1: Participate with varied peers and adults in collaborative conversations in small or large groups about appropriate 1st grade topics and texts.
TN.E1.SL.CC.2: Ask and answer questions about key details in a text read aloud or information presented orally or through other media.
TN.E1.SL.CC.3: Ask and answer questions about what a speaker says in order to gather additional information or clarify something that is not understood.
TN.E1.SL.PKI.4: Describe people, places, things, and events with relevant details, expressing ideas and feelings clearly.
TN.E1.SL.PKI.5: Add drawings or other visual displays to descriptions, when appropriate, to clarify ideas, thoughts, and feelings.
TN.E1.SL.PKI.6: With prompting and support, speak in complete sentences when appropriate to task and situation.
TN.E1.W.TTP.1: With prompting and support, write opinion pieces introducing the topic or text, stating an opinion, supplying a reason for the opinion, and providing some sense of closure.
TN.E1.W.TTP.2: With prompting and support, write informative/explanatory texts, naming a topic, supplying some facts about the topic, and providing some sense of closure.
TN.E1.W.TTP.3: With prompting and support, write narratives recounting an event, including some details to describe actions, thoughts, and feelings; use time order words to signal event order and provide some sense of closure.
TN.E1.W.PDW.4: With guidance and support, produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.
TN.E1.W.PDW.5: With guidance and support from adults, focus on a topic, respond to questions and suggestions from others, and add details to strengthen writing as needed.
TN.E1.W.PDW.6: With guidance and support from adults, and in collaboration with peers, explore a variety of digital tools to produce and publish writing.
TN.E1.W.RBPK.7: Participate in shared research and writing projects, such as exploring a number of “how to” books on a given topic and using them to write a sequence of instructions.
TN.E1.W.RBPK.8: With guidance and support from adults, recall information from experiences or gather information from provided sources to answer a question.
TN.E1.W.RW.10: With guidance and support from adults, engage routinely in writing activities to promote writing fluency and build writing stamina.
TN.M1.OA.A: Represent and solve problems involving addition and subtraction.
TN.M1.OA.A.1: Add and subtract within 20 to solve contextual problems, with unknowns in all positions, involving situations of add to, take from, put together/take apart, and compare. Use objects, drawings, and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.
TN.M1.OA.A.2: Add three whole numbers whose sum is within 20 to solve contextual problems using objects, drawings, and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.
TN.M1.OA.B: Understand and apply properties of operations and the relationship between addition and subtraction.
TN.M1.OA.B.3: Apply properties of operations (additive identity, commutative, and associative) as strategies to add and subtract.
TN.M1.OA.B.4: Understand the relationship between addition and subtraction by representing subtraction as an unknown-addend problem.
TN.M1.OA.C.5: Add and subtract within 20 using strategies such as counting on, counting back, making 10, related known facts, and composing/decomposing numbers with an emphasis on making ten (e.g., 13 - 4 = 13 - 3 - 1 = 10 - 1 = 9 or adding 6 + 7 by creating the known equivalent 6 + 4 + 3 = 10 + 3 = 13 OR 6 + 6 + 1 = 12 + 1).

TN.M3.NF.A: Develop understanding of fractions as numbers.
TN.M3.NF.A.1: Understand a unit fraction, `1/b`, as the quantity formed by `1` part when a whole is partitioned into `b` equal parts; understand a non-unit fraction, `n/b`, as the quantity formed by n parts of size `1/b`.

TN.M3.NF.A.2.b: Represent a fraction n/b on a number line diagram by marking off n lengths `1/b` from `0`. Recognize that the resulting interval has size n/b and that its endpoint locates the number n/b on the number line.

TN.M4.OA.A: Use the four operations with whole numbers to solve problems.

TN.M4.OA.B.4: Find factor pairs for whole numbers in the range `1-100` using models. Recognize that a whole number is a multiple of each of its factors. Determine whether a given whole number is prime or composite and whether the given number is a multiple of a given one-digit number.

TN.M4.NBT.A: Generalize place value understanding for multi-digit whole numbers.

TN.M4.NBT.A.2: Read and write multi-digit whole numbers (less than or equal to `1text(,)000text(,)000`) using standard form, word form, and expanded notation (e.g. the expanded notation of `4256` is written as `(4xx1000)+(2xx100)+(5xx10)+(6xx1))`. Compare two multi-digit numbers based on meanings of the digits in each place and use the symbols `>,=,and<` to show the relationship.
TN.M4.NBT.A.3: Round multi-digit whole numbers to any place (up to and including the hundred-thousand place) using understanding of place value and use a number line to explain how the number was rounded.
TN.M4.NBT.B: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to perform multi-digit arithmetic.
TN.M4.NBT.B.4: Fluently add and subtract within `1text(,)000text(,)000` using efficient strategies and algorithms.
TN.M4.NBT.B.5: Multiply a whole number of up to four digits by a one-digit whole number and multiply two two-digit numbers, using strategies based on place value and the properties of operations. Illustrate and explain the calculation by using equations, rectangular arrays, and/or area models.
TN.M4.NBT.B.6: Find whole-number quotients and remainders with up to four-digit dividends and one-digit divisors, using strategies based on place value, the properties of operations, and/or the relationship between multiplication and division. Illustrate and explain the calculation by using equations, rectangular arrays, and/or area models.
TN.M4.NF.A: Extend understanding of fraction equivalence and comparison.
TN.M4.NF.A.1: Explain why a fraction `a/b` is equivalent to a fraction (axxn)/(bxxn)or(a-:n)/(b-:n)` using visual fraction models, with attention to how the number and size of the parts differ even though the two fractions themselves are the same size. Use this principle to recognize and generate equivalent fractions.
TN.M4.NF.A.2: Compare two fractions with different numerators and different denominators by creating common denominators or common numerators or by comparing to a benchmark such as `0or1/2or1`. Recognize that comparisons are valid only when the two fractions refer to the same whole. Use the symbols `>,=,or<` to show the relationship and justify the conclusions.
TN.M4.NF.B: Build fractions from unit fractions by applying and extending previous understandings of operations on whole numbers.
TN.M4.NF.B.3: Understand a fraction `a/b` with `a>1` as a sum of fractions `1/b`.

TN.M4.NF.B.3.b: Decompose a fraction into a sum of fractions with the same denominator in more than one way (e.g., `3/8=1/8+1/8+1/8;3/8=1/8+2/8;2``1/8=1+1+1/8=8/8+8/8+1/8`) recording each decomposition by an equation. Justify decompositions using a visual fraction model.

TN.M4.NF.B.3.d: Solve contextual problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions referring to the same whole and having like denominators.
TN.M4.NF.B.4: Apply and extend understanding of multiplication as repeated addition to multiply a whole number by a fraction.
TN.M4.NF.B.4.a: Understand a fraction `a/b` as a multiple of `1/b`.
TN.M4.NF.B.4.b: Understand a multiple of `a/b` as a multiple of `1/b` and use this understanding to multiply a whole number by a fraction.
TN.M4.NF.B.4.c: Solve contextual problems involving multiplication of a whole number by a fraction (e.g., by using visual fraction models and equations to represent the problem).
TN.M4.NF.C: Understand decimal notation for fractions and compare decimal fractions.
