TN.E6.SL.CC.1: Prepare for collaborative discussions on 6th grade level topics and texts; engage effectively with varied partners, building on others' ideas and expressing one's own ideas clearly.
TN.E6.SL.CC.2: Interpret information presented in diverse media formats; explain how source information contributes to a topic, text, or issue under study.
TN.E6.SL.CC.3: Explain a speaker's argument and specific claims, distinguishing claims that are supported by reasons and evidence from claims that are not.
TN.E6.SL.PKI.4: Present claims and findings, sequencing ideas logically and using pertinent descriptions, facts, and details to accentuate main ideas or themes; use appropriate eye contact, adequate volume, and clear pronunciation.
TN.E6.SL.PKI.5: Include multimedia components and visual displays in presentations to clarify information.
TN.E6.SL.PKI.6: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate.
TN.E6.W.TTP.1: Write arguments to support claims with clear reasons and relevant evidence.
TN.E6.W.TTP.1.b: Support claim(s) with logical reasoning and relevant, sufficient evidence; acknowledge alternate or opposing claim(s).
TN.E6.W.TTP.1.c: Organize the reasons and evidence clearly and clarify the relationships among claim(s) and reasons.
TN.E6.W.TTP.1.d: Use credible sources and demonstrate an understanding of the topic or source material.
TN.E6.W.TTP.1.e: Craft an effective and relevant conclusion that supports the argument presented.
TN.E6.W.TTP.1.f: Use precise language and content-specific vocabulary.
TN.E6.W.TTP.1.g: Use appropriate transitions to create cohesion and clarify the relationships among ideas and concepts.
TN.E6.W.TTP.1.h: Use varied sentence structure to enhance meaning and reader interest.
TN.E6.W.TTP.1.i: Establish and maintain a formal style.
TN.E6.W.TTP.2: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine a topic and convey ideas, concepts, and information through the selection, organization, and analysis of relevant content.
TN.E6.W.TTP.2.a: Introduce a topic clearly, using the introduction to prepare the reader for what is to follow.
TN.E6.W.TTP.2.b: Organize ideas, concepts, and information using effective strategies to create cohesion and aid in comprehension.
TN.E6.W.TTP.2.c: Develop the topic with relevant facts, definitions, concrete details, quotations, or other information and examples.
TN.E6.W.TTP.2.d: Thoroughly and accurately explain and elaborate on the evidence provided, demonstrating a clear understanding of the topic and the source material.
TN.E6.W.TTP.2.e: Craft an effective and relevant conclusion.
TN.E6.W.TTP.2.f: Include formatting, graphics, and multimedia when appropriate.
TN.E6.W.TTP.2.g: Use appropriate transitions to create cohesion and clarify the relationships among ideas and concepts.
TN.E6.W.TTP.2.h: Use precise language and domain-specific vocabulary.
TN.E6.W.TTP.2.i: Use varied sentence structure to enhance meaning and reader interest.
TN.E6.W.TTP.2.j: Establish and maintain a formal style.
TN.E6.W.TTP.3: Write narratives (fiction and nonfiction) to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective techniques, relevant descriptive details, and well-structured event sequences.
TN.E6.W.TTP.3.a: Engage and orient the reader by establishing a context and point of view and introducing a speaker/narrator and/or participants/characters.
TN.E6.W.TTP.3.b: Organize an event sequence that unfolds naturally and logically.
TN.E6.W.TTP.3.c: Create a smooth progression of experiences or events.
TN.E6.W.TTP.3.d: Use narrative techniques, such as dialogue, pacing, and description when appropriate, to develop experiences, events, and/or characters.
TN.E6.W.TTP.3.e: Use a variety of transition words, phrases, and clauses to convey sequence, signal shifts, and show the relationships among experiences and events.
TN.E6.W.TTP.3.f: Craft an effective and relevant conclusion that reflects on the narrated experiences or events.
TN.E6.W.TTP.3.g: Use precise words and phrases, relevant descriptive details, and sensory language to convey experiences and events.
TN.E6.W.PDW.4: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.
TN.E6.W.PDW.5: With some guidance and support from peers and adults, develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach.
TN.E6.W.PDW.6: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce and publish writing and to collaborate with others; type a complete product in a single sitting as defined in W.1-3.
TN.E6.W.RBPK.7: Conduct research to answer a question, drawing on multiple sources and refocusing the inquiry when appropriate.
TN.E6.W.RBPK.8: Integrate relevant and credible information from print and digital sources; quote or paraphrase the data and conclusions of others while avoiding plagiarism and providing basic bibliographic information for sources.
TN.E6.W.RBPK.9: Support interpretations, analyses, reflections, or research with evidence found in literature or informational texts, applying grade 6 standards for reading.
TN.E6.W.RW.10: Write routinely over extended time frames and shorter time frames for a range of discipline-specific tasks, purposes, and audiences.
TN.M6.RP.A: Understand ratio concepts and use ratio reasoning to solve problems.
TN.M6.RP.A.1: Understand the concept of a ratio and use ratio language to describe a ratio relationship between two quantities. Make a distinction between ratios and fractions.
TN.M6.RP.A.2: Understand the concept of a unit rate `a/b` associated with a ratio `a:b` with `b!=0`. Use rate language in the context of a ratio relationship.
TN.M6.RP.A.3: Use ratio and rate reasoning to solve real-world and mathematical problems (e.g., by reasoning about tables of equivalent ratios, tape diagrams, double number line diagrams, or equations).
TN.M6.RP.A.3.a: Make tables of equivalent ratios relating quantities with whole number measurements, find missing values in the tables, and plot the pairs of values on the coordinate plane. Use tables to compare ratios.
TN.M6.RP.A.3.b: Solve unit rate problems including those involving unit pricing and constant speed.
TN.M6.RP.A.3.c: Find a percent of a quantity as a rate `text(per)` `100` (e.g., `30%` of a quantity means `30/100` times the quantity); solve problems involving finding the whole, given a part and the percent.
TN.M6.RP.A.3.d: Use ratio reasoning to convert customary and metric measurement units (within the same system); manipulate and transform units appropriately when multiplying or dividing quantities.
TN.M6.NS.A: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication and division to divide fractions by fractions.
TN.M6.NS.A.1: Interpret and compute quotients of fractions, and solve real-world and mathematical problems involving division of fractions by fractions (e.g., connecting visual fraction models and equations to represent the problem is suggested).
TN.M6.NS.B: Compute fluently with multi-digit numbers and find common factors and multiples.
TN.M6.NS.B.2: Fluently divide multi-digit numbers using a standard algorithm.
TN.M6.NS.B.3: Fluently add, subtract, multiply, and divide multi-digit decimals using a standard algorithm and making connections to previous conceptual work with each operation.
TN.M6.NS.B.4: Find the greatest common factor of two whole numbers less than or equal to `100` and the least common multiple of two whole numbers less than or equal to `12`. Use the distributive property to express a sum of two whole numbers `1-100` with a common factor as a multiple of a sum of two whole numbers with no common factor.
TN.M6.NS.C: Apply and extend previous understandings of numbers to the system of rational numbers.
TN.M6.NS.C.5: Understand that positive and negative numbers are used together to describe quantities having opposite directions or values (e.g., temperature above/below zero, elevation above/below sea level, credits/debits, positive/negative electric charge); use positive and negative numbers to represent quantities in real-world contexts, explaining the meaning of `0` in each situation as well as describing situations in which opposite quantities can combine to make `0`.
TN.M6.NS.C.6: Apply and extend previous understandings of numbers to the system of rational numbers.
TN.M6.NS.C.6.a: Recognize opposite signs of numbers as indicating locations on opposite sides of `0` on the number line; recognize that the opposite of the opposite of a number is the number itself.
TN.M6.NS.C.6.b: Understand signs of numbers in ordered pairs as indicating locations in quadrants of the coordinate plane; recognize that when two ordered pairs differ only by signs, the locations of the points are related by reflections across one or both axes.
TN.M6.NS.C.6.c: Find and position integers and other rational numbers on a horizontal or vertical number line diagram; find and position pairs of integers and other rational numbers on a coordinate plane.
TN.M6.NS.C.7: Understand ordering and absolute value of rational numbers.
TN.M6.NS.C.7.a: Interpret statements of inequality as statements about the relative position of two numbers on a number line diagram.
TN.M6.NS.C.7.b: Write, interpret, and explain statements of order for rational numbers in real-world contexts.
TN.M6.NS.C.7.c: Understand the absolute value of a rational number as its distance from `0` on the number line and distinguish comparisons of absolute value from statements about order in a real-world context.
TN.M6.NS.C.8: Solve real-world and mathematical problems by graphing points in all four quadrants of the coordinate plane. Include use of coordinates and absolute value to find distances between points with the same first coordinate or the same second coordinate.
TN.M6.EE.A: Apply and extend previous understandings of arithmetic to algebraic expressions.
TN.M6.EE.A.1: Write and evaluate numerical expressions involving whole-number exponents.
TN.M6.EE.A.2: Write, read, and evaluate expressions in which variables stand for numbers.
TN.M6.EE.A.2.a: Write expressions that record operations with numbers and with variables.
TN.M6.EE.A.2.b: Identify parts of an expression using mathematical terms (sum, term, product, factor, quotient, coefficient); view one or more parts of an expression as a single entity.
TN.M6.EE.A.2.c: Evaluate expressions at specific values of their variables. Include expressions that arise from formulas used in real-world problems. Perform arithmetic operations, including those involving whole number exponents, in the conventional order when there are no parentheses to specify a particular order (Order of Operations).
TN.M6.EE.A.3: Apply the properties of operations (including, but not limited to, commutative, associative, and distributive properties) to generate equivalent expressions.
TN.M6.EE.A.4: Identify when expressions are equivalent (i.e., when the expressions name the same number regardless of which value is substituted into them).
TN.M6.EE.B: Reason about and solve one-variable equations and inequalities.
TN.M6.EE.B.5: Understand that a solution to an equation or inequality is the value(s) that makes that statement true. Use substitution to determine whether a given number in a specified set makes an equation or inequality true.
TN.M6.EE.B.6: Use variables to represent numbers and write expressions when solving real-world and mathematical problems; understand that a variable can represent an unknown number, or, depending on the purpose at hand, any number in a specified set.
TN.M6.EE.B.7: Solve real-world and mathematical problems by writing and solving one-step equations of the form `x+p=q,px=q,x-p=q,andx/p=q` for cases in which `p,q,andx` are all nonnegative rational numbers and `p!=0`.
TN.M6.EE.B.8: Interpret and write an inequality of the form `x>c,x<c,x<=c,orx>=c` which represents a condition or constraint in a real-world or mathematical problem. Recognize that inequalities have infinitely many solutions; represent solutions of inequalities on number line diagrams.
TN.M6.EE.C: Represent and analyze quantitative relationships between dependent and independent variables.
TN.M6.EE.C.9: Use variables to represent two quantities in a real-world problem that change in relationship to one another.
TN.M6.EE.C.9.a: Write an equation in the form of `y=px` where `y,p,andx` are all non-negative and `p!=0`, to express one quantity, thought of as the dependent variable, in terms of the other quantity, thought of as the independent variable.
TN.M6.EE.C.9.b: Analyze the relationship between the dependent and independent variables using graphs and tables, and relate these to the equation.
TN.M6.G.A: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving area, surface area, and volume.
TN.M6.G.A.1: Find the area of right triangles, other triangles, special quadrilaterals, and polygons by composing into rectangles or decomposing into triangles and other shapes; know and apply these techniques in the context of solving real-world and mathematical problems.
TN.M6.G.A.2: Find the volume of a right rectangular prism with fractional edge lengths by packing it with unit cubes of the appropriate unit fraction edge lengths, and show that the volume is the same as would be found by multiplying the edge lengths of the prism. Apply the formulas `V=lxxwxxhandV=Bxxh` where `B` is the area of the base to find volumes of right rectangular prisms with fractional edge lengths in the context of solving real-world and mathematical problems.
TN.M6.G.A.3: Draw polygons in the coordinate plane given coordinates for the vertices; use coordinates to find the length of a side that joins two vertices (vertical or horizontal segments only). Apply these techniques in the context of solving real-world and mathematical problems.
TN.M6.G.A.4: Represent three-dimensional figures using nets made up of rectangles and triangles, and use the nets to find the surface area of these figures. Apply these techniques in the context of solving real-world and mathematical problems.
TN.M6.SP.A.1: Recognize a statistical question as one that anticipates variability in the data related to the question and accounts for it in the answers.
TN.M6.SP.A.2: Understand that a set of data collected to answer a statistical question has a distribution which can be described by its measures of center (mean, median, mode), measures of variation (range only), and overall shape.
TN.M6.SP.A.3: Recognize that a measure of center (mean, median, mode) for a numerical data set summarizes all of its values with a single number, while a measure of variation describes how its values vary with a single number.
TN.M6.SP.B.4: Display a single set of numerical data using dot plots (line plots), box plots, pie charts and stem plots.
TN.M6.SP.B.5: Summarize numerical data sets in relation to their context.
TN.M6.SP.B.5.b: Describe the nature of the attribute under investigation, including how it was measured and its units of measurement.
TN.M6.SP.B.5.c: Give quantitative measures of center (median and/or mean) and variability (range) as well as describing any overall pattern with reference to the context in which the data were gathered.
TN.M6.SP.B.5.d: Relate the choice of measures of center to the shape of the data distribution and the context in which the data were gathered.
TN.S6.PS.3.1: Analyze the properties and compare sources of kinetic, elastic potential, gravitational potential, electric potential, chemical, and thermal energy.
TN.S6.PS.3.2: Construct a scientific explanation of the transformations between potential and kinetic energy.
TN.S6.PS.3.3: Analyze and interpret data to show the relationship between kinetic energy and the mass of an object in motion and its speed.
TN.S6.PS.3.4: Conduct an investigation to demonstrate the way that heat (thermal energy) moves among objects through radiation, conduction, or convection.
TN.S6.LS.2.1: Evaluate and communicate the impact of environmental variables on population size.
TN.S6.LS.2.2: Determine the impact of competitive, symbiotic, and predatory interactions in an ecosystem.
TN.S6.LS.2.3: Draw conclusions about the transfer of energy through a food web and energy pyramid in an ecosystem.
TN.S6.LS.2.4: Using evidence from climate data, draw conclusions about the patterns of abiotic and biotic factors in different biomes, specifically the tundra, taiga, deciduous forest, desert, grasslands, rainforest, marine, and freshwater ecosystems.
TN.S6.LS.2.5: Analyze existing evidence about the effect of a specific invasive species on native populations in Tennessee and design a solution to mitigate its impact.
TN.S6.LS.2.6: Research the ways in which an ecosystem has changed over time in response to changes in physical conditions, population balances, human interactions, and natural catastrophes.
TN.S6.LS.2.7: Compare and contrast auditory and visual methods of communication among organisms in relation to survival strategies of a population.
TN.S6.LS.4.1: Explain how changes in biodiversity would impact ecosystem stability and natural resources.
TN.S6.LS.4.2: Design a possible solution for maintaining biodiversity of ecosystems while still providing necessary human resources without disrupting environmental equilibrium.
TN.S6.ESS.2.1: Gather evidence to justify that oceanic convection currents are caused by the sun's transfer of heat energy and differences in salt concentration leading to global water movement.
TN.S6.ESS.2.2: Diagram convection patterns that flow due to uneven heating of the earth.
TN.S6.ESS.2.3: Construct an explanation for how atmospheric flow, geographic features, and ocean currents affect the climate of a region through heat transfer.
TN.S6.ESS.2.4: Apply scientific principles to design a method to analyze and interpret the impact of humans and other organisms on the hydrologic cycle.
TN.S6.ESS.2.5: Analyze and interpret data from weather conditions, weather maps, satellites, and radar to predict probable local weather patterns and conditions.
TN.S6.ESS.2.6: Explain how relationships between the movement and interactions of air masses, high and low pressure systems, and frontal boundaries result in weather conditions and severe storms.
TN.S6.ESS.3.1: Differentiate between renewable and nonrenewable resources by asking questions about their availability and sustainability.
TN.S6.ESS.3.2: Investigate and compare existing and developing technologies that utilize renewable and alternative energy resources.
TN.S6.ESS.3.3: Assess the impacts of human activities on the biosphere including conservation, habitat management, species endangerment, and extinction.
TN.S6.ETS.1.1: Evaluate design constraints on solutions for maintaining ecosystems and biodiversity.
TN.S6.ETS.1.2: Design and test different solutions that impact energy transfer.
TN.SS6.1: Identify the meaning of time designations and abbreviations used by historians.
TN.SS6.2: Describe the characteristics of the nomadic hunter-gatherer societies.
TN.SS6.3: Explain the impact of the Agricultural Revolution.
TN.SS6.4: Identify and explain the importance of key characteristics of civilizations.
TN.SS6.5: Identify and locate geographical features of ancient Mesopotamia.
TN.SS6.6: Explain how geographic and climatic features led to the region being known as the Fertile Crescent.
TN.SS6.7: Explain how irrigation, silt, metallurgy, production of tools, use of animals, slave labor, and inventions such as the wheel, sail, and plow led to advancements in agriculture.
TN.SS6.8: Analyze how advancements in agriculture in Sumer led to economic growth, expansion of trade and transportation, and the emergence of independent city-states.
TN.SS6.9: Explain the basic concepts of monarchy and empire, and identify Mesopotamia as the regional location of the world's first empire.
TN.SS6.10: Explain the concept of polytheism and its presence in Mesopotamia, with respect to beliefs about the relationship of deities to the natural world and their importance in everyday life.
TN.SS6.11: Identify important achievements of the Mesopotamian civilization, including cuneiform, clay tablets, and ziggurats, and identify the Epic of Gilgamesh as the oldest written epic.
TN.SS6.12: Analyze the impact of the introduction of written law in the Code of Hammurabi, and explain its basic principles of justice.
TN.SS6.13: Identify and locate geographical features of ancient Egypt.
TN.SS6.14: Explain how agricultural practices impacted life and economic growth in ancient Egypt.
TN.SS6.15: Explain the structure of ancient Egyptian society.
TN.SS6.16: Explain the polytheistic religion of ancient Egypt, with respect to beliefs about the afterlife, the reasons for mummification, and the use of pyramids.
TN.SS6.17: Analyze the impact of key figures from ancient Egypt.
TN.SS6.18: Analyze the achievements of ancient Egyptian civilization.
TN.SS6.19: Examine the cultural diffusion of ancient Egypt with surrounding civilizations through trade and conflict, including its relationship with Nubia.
TN.SS6.20: Identify and locate geographical features of ancient Israel.
TN.SS6.21: Describe the development of the ancient Israelites, and explain the reasons for their movements from Mesopotamia to Canaan (later called Israel), from Canaan to Egypt, and from Egypt back to Canaan.
TN.SS6.22: Describe the origins and central features of Judaism
TN.SS6.23: Identify the importance of Saul as the first king of Israel, David as the second king who founded Jerusalem as the capital, and Solomon as the third king who built the first temple.
TN.SS6.24: Summarize the breakup of the Kingdom of Israel, Babylonian captivity, and the return of the Jews to their homeland under the Persian Empire.
TN.SS6.25: Identify and locate geographical features of ancient India.
TN.SS6.26: Explain the emergence of the Harappan civilization in the Indus River Valley as an early agricultural civilization, and describe its achievements.
TN.SS6.27: Describe the social structure of the caste system, and explain its effect on everyday life in ancient India.
TN.SS6.28: Describe the origins and central features of Hinduism.
TN.SS6.29: Describe the origins and central features of Buddhism.
TN.SS6.30: Identify the long-lasting intellectual traditions that emerged during the late empire of ancient India.
TN.SS6.31: Identify and locate geographical features of ancient China.
TN.SS6.32: Analyze the influence of geographic features on the origins of ancient Chinese civilization in the Yellow River Valley, and explain how China's geography helped create a unique yet diverse cultural identity that was isolated from the rest of the world.
TN.SS6.33: Describe how the size of ancient China made governing difficult and how the concepts of the mandate of heaven and Legalism emerged as solutions to this problem.
TN.SS6.34: Identify the political and cultural problems prevalent in the time of Confucius and how the philosophy of Confucianism and The Analects emphasized the concepts of kinship, order, and hierarchy to address these problems.
TN.SS6.35: Explain the significance of the unification of ancient China into the first Chinese empire by Qin Shi Huangdi, beginning the Qin Dynasty.
TN.SS6.36: Explain how the implementation of the philosophy of Confucianism led to the political success and longevity of the Han Dynasty.
TN.SS6.37: Explain the major accomplishments of the Han Dynasty.
TN.SS6.38: Describe how the desire for Chinese goods influenced the creation of The Silk Road and initiated cultural diffusion throughout Eurasia.
TN.SS6.39: Identify and locate geographical features of ancient Greece.
TN.SS6.40: Analyze how the geographical features of ancient Greece, including its mountainous terrain and access to the Mediterranean Sea, contributed to its organization into city-states, role in maritime trade, and colonies in the Mediterranean.
TN.SS6.41: Examine the concept of the polis in Greek city-states.
TN.SS6.42: Explain the basic concepts of direct democracy and oligarchy.
TN.SS6.43: Explain the characteristics of the major Greek city-states of Athens and Sparta.
TN.SS6.44: Analyze the causes and consequences of the Persian Wars.
TN.SS6.45: Analyze the causes and consequences of the Peloponnesian Wars.
TN.SS6.46: Explain the polytheistic religion of ancient Greece, with respect to beliefs about the humanlike qualities of the deities, their importance in everyday life, and the emergence of the Olympic Games to honor Zeus.
TN.SS6.47: Explain the historical significance of ancient Greek literature.
TN.SS6.48: Examine the influence of ancient Greek philosophers (e.g., Aristotle, Plato, and Socrates) and their impact on education and society in Greece.
TN.SS6.49: Describe the purposes of major Greek architecture.
TN.SS6.50: Explain the unification of the Greek city-states by Macedonia, and analyze the impact of Alexander the Great and the diffusion of Hellenistic culture.
TN.SS6.51: Identify and locate the geographical features of ancient Rome.
TN.SS6.52: Analyze how the geographical location of ancient Rome contributed to its political and economic growth in the Mediterranean region and beyond.
TN.SS6.53: Describe the government of the Roman Republic.
TN.SS6.54: Describe the class system of ancient Rome.
TN.SS6.55: Describe the characteristics of Julius Caesar's rule.
TN.SS6.56: Analyze the influence of Augustus Caesar.
TN.SS6.57: Analyze how innovations in engineering and architecture contributed to Roman expansion.
TN.SS6.58: Explain the polytheistic religion of ancient Rome, with respect to beliefs about the humanlike qualities of the deities and their importance in everyday life.
TN.SS6.59: Describe the origins and central features of Christianity.
TN.SS6.60: Explain the expulsion of the Jews from their homeland by the Romans, which began the Jewish diaspora.
TN.SS6.61: Explain the division of the Roman Empire into East and West, and identify the later establishment of Constantinople as the capital by Constantine.
TN.SS6.62: Analyze the fall of the Western Roman Empire, including difficulty governing its large territory, political corruption, economic instability, and attacks by Germanic tribes, and identify the continuation of the Eastern Roman Empire as the Byzantine Empire.
TN.E7.L.CSE.1: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage.
TN.E7.L.CSE.1.a: When reading or listening, explain the function of phrases and clauses with effectively-placed modifiers.
TN.E7.L.CSE.1.b: When writing or speaking, produce simple, compound, and complex sentences with effectively-placed modifiers.
TN.E7.L.CSE.2: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling. When reading or writing, explain the function of commas to separate coordinate adjectives and use them correctly to do so.
TN.E7.L.KL.3: When writing and speaking, choose precise language to express ideas concisely.
TN.E7.L.VAU.4: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on 7th grade-level text by choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.
TN.E7.L.VAU.4.a: Use context as a clue to the meaning of a word or a phrase.
TN.E7.L.VAU.4.b: Use common grade-appropriate morphological elements as clues to the meaning of a word or a phrase.
TN.E7.L.VAU.4.c: Consult reference materials, both print and digital, to find the pronunciation of a word or phrase.
TN.E7.L.VAU.4.d: Use etymological patterns in spelling as clues to the meaning of a word or phrase.
TN.E7.L.VAU.5: When reading, listening, writing, and speaking, explain the function of figurative language, word relationships, and connotation/denotation and use them correctly and effectively.
TN.E7.L.VAU.6: Acquire and accurately use grade-appropriate general academic and domain-specific words and phrases; develop vocabulary knowledge when considering a word or phrase important to comprehension or expression.
TN.E7.RL.KID.1: Analyze what a text says explicitly and draw logical inferences; cite several pieces of textual evidence to support conclusions.
TN.E7.RL.KID.2: Determine a theme or central idea of a text and analyze its development over the course of the text; provide an objective summary.
TN.E7.RL.KID.3: Analyze how specific elements of a story or drama interact with and affect each other.
TN.E7.RL.CS.4: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including figurative and connotative meanings; analyze the impact of specific word choices on meaning and tone, including allusions to other texts and repetition of words and phrases.
TN.E7.RL.CS.5: Analyze the form or structure of a story, poem, or drama, considering how text form or structure contributes to its theme and meaning.
TN.E7.RL.CS.6: Analyze how an author establishes, conveys, and contrasts the points of view of different characters or narrators in a text.
TN.E7.RL.IKI.7: Compare and contrast a written story, drama, or poem to its audio, filmed, staged, or multi-media version, analyzing the effects of techniques unique to each medium.
TN.E7.RL.IKI.9: Compare and contrast an historical account with a fictional portrayal of the same time, place, or character.
TN.E7.RL.RRTC: Range Of Reading & Level Of Text Complexity
TN.E7.RL.RRTC.10: Read and comprehend a variety of literature throughout the grades 6-8 text complexity band proficiently, with a gradual release of scaffolding at the high end as needed.
TN.E7.RI.KID.1: Analyze what a text says explicitly and draw logical inferences; cite several pieces of textual evidence to support conclusions.
TN.E7.RI.KID.2: Determine a central idea of a text and analyze its development over the course of the text; provide an objective summary.
TN.E7.RI.KID.3: Analyze the relationships and interactions among individuals, events, and/or ideas in a text.
TN.E7.RI.CS.4: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including figurative, connotative, and technical meanings; analyze the impact of specific word choices on meaning and tone, including allusions to other texts and repetition of words and phrases.
TN.E7.RI.CS.5: Analyze the structure an author uses to organize a text, including how the major sections contribute to the whole and to the development of the ideas.
TN.E7.RI.CS.6: Determine an author's point of view or purpose in a text and analyze how an author distinguishes his or her position from that of others.
TN.E7.RI.IKI.7: Compare and contrast a text to an audio, video, or multimedia version of a text, analyzing each medium's portrayal of the subject.
TN.E7.RI.IKI.8: Trace and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, assessing whether the evidence is relevant and sufficient to support the claims.
TN.E7.RI.IKI.9: Analyze how two or more authors writing about the same topic shape their presentations of key information by emphasizing different evidence or advancing an alternate explanation of events.
TN.E7.RI.RRTC: Range Of Reading & Level Of Text Complexity
TN.E7.RI.RRTC.10: Read and comprehend a variety of literary nonfiction throughout the grades 6-8 text complexity band proficiently, with a gradual release of scaffolding at the high end as needed.
TN.E7.SL.CC.1: Prepare for collaborative discussions on 7th grade level topics and texts; engage effectively with varied partners, building on others' ideas and expressing one's own ideas clearly.
TN.E7.SL.CC.2: Analyze the main ideas and supporting details presented in diverse media formats; explain how this clarifies a topic, text, or issue under study.
TN.E7.SL.CC.3: Explain a speaker's argument and specific claims, focusing on whether the reasoning is sound, relevant, and sufficient.
TN.E7.SL.PKI.4: Present claims and findings, emphasizing salient points in a focused, coherent manner with pertinent descriptions, facts, details, and examples; use appropriate eye contact, adequate volume, and clear pronunciation.
TN.E7.SL.PKI.5: Include multimedia components and visual displays in presentations to clarify claims and findings and to emphasize major points.
TN.E7.SL.PKI.6: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate.
TN.E7.W.TTP.1: Write arguments to support claims with clear reasons and relevant evidence.
TN.E7.W.TTP.1.b: Support claim(s) with logical reasoning and relevant, sufficient evidence; acknowledge alternate or opposing claim(s).
TN.E7.W.TTP.1.c: Organize the reasons and evidence clearly and clarify the relationships among claim(s) and reasons.
TN.E7.W.TTP.1.d: Use credible sources and demonstrate an understanding of the topic or source material.
TN.E7.W.TTP.1.e: Craft an effective and relevant conclusion that supports the argument presented.
TN.E7.W.TTP.1.f: Use precise language and content-specific vocabulary.
TN.E7.W.TTP.1.g: Use appropriate transitions to create cohesion and clarify the relationships among ideas and concepts.
TN.E7.W.TTP.1.h: Use varied sentence structure to enhance meaning and reader interest.
TN.E7.W.TTP.1.i: Establish and maintain a formal style.
TN.E7.W.TTP.2: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine a topic and convey ideas, concepts, and information through the selection, organization, and analysis of relevant content.
TN.E7.W.TTP.2.a: Introduce a topic clearly, using the introduction to prepare the reader for what is to follow.
TN.E7.W.TTP.2.b: Organize ideas, concepts, and information using effective strategies to create cohesion and aid in comprehension.
TN.E7.W.TTP.2.c: Develop the topic with relevant facts, definitions, concrete details, quotations, or other information and examples.
TN.E7.W.TTP.2.d: Thoroughly and accurately explain and elaborate on the evidence provided, demonstrating a clear understanding of the topic and the source material.
TN.E7.W.TTP.2.e: Craft an effective and relevant conclusion.
TN.E7.W.TTP.2.f: Include formatting, graphics, and multimedia when appropriate.
TN.E7.W.TTP.2.g: Use appropriate transitions to create cohesion and clarify the relationships among ideas and concepts.
TN.E7.W.TTP.2.h: Use precise language and domain-specific vocabulary.
TN.E7.W.TTP.2.i: Use varied sentence structure to enhance meaning and reader interest.
TN.E7.W.TTP.2.j: Establish and maintain a formal style.
TN.E7.W.TTP.3: Write narratives (fiction and nonfiction) to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective techniques, relevant descriptive details, and well-structured event sequences.
TN.E7.W.TTP.3.a: Engage and orient the reader by establishing a context and point of view and introducing a narrator and/or participants/characters.
TN.E7.W.TTP.3.b: Organize an event sequence that unfolds naturally and logically.
TN.E7.W.TTP.3.c: Create a smooth progression of experiences or events.
TN.E7.W.TTP.3.d: Use narrative techniques, such as dialogue, pacing, and description when appropriate, to develop experiences, events, and/or characters.
TN.E7.W.TTP.3.e: Use a variety of transition words, phrases, and clauses to convey sequence, signal shifts, and show the relationships among experiences and events.
TN.E7.W.TTP.3.f: Craft an effective and relevant conclusion that reflects on the narrated experiences or events.
TN.E7.W.TTP.3.g: Use precise words and phrases, relevant descriptive details, and sensory language to convey experiences and events.
TN.E7.W.PDW.4: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.
TN.E7.W.PDW.5: With some guidance and support from peers and adults, develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach, focusing on how well purpose and audience have been addressed.
TN.E7.W.PDW.6: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce and publish writing and to collaborate with others; link to and cite sources; type a complete product in a single sitting as defined in W.1-3.
TN.E7.W.RBPK.7: Conduct research to answer a question, drawing on multiple sources and generating additional related, focused questions for further research and investigation.
TN.E7.W.RBPK.8: Integrate relevant and credible information from print and digital sources; quote or paraphrase the data and conclusions of others while avoiding plagiarism and following a standard format for citation.
TN.E7.W.RBPK.9: Support interpretations, analyses, reflections, or research with evidence found in literature or informational texts, applying grade 7 standards for reading; assess whether the evidence is relevant and sufficient to support the claims.
TN.E7.W.RW.10: Write routinely over extended time frames and shorter time frames for a range of discipline-specific tasks, purposes, and audiences.
TN.M7.RP.A: Analyze proportional relationships and use them to solve real-world and mathematical problems.
TN.M7.RP.A.1: Compute unit rates associated with ratios of fractions, including ratios of lengths, areas, and other quantities measured in like or different units.
TN.M7.RP.A.2: Recognize and represent proportional relationships between quantities.
TN.M7.RP.A.2.a: Decide whether two quantities are in a proportional relationship (e.g., by testing for equivalent ratios in a table or graphing on a coordinate plane and observing whether the graph is a straight line through the origin).
TN.M7.RP.A.2.b: Identify the constant of proportionality (unit rate) in tables, graphs, equations, diagrams, and verbal descriptions of proportional relationships.
TN.M7.RP.A.2.c: Use the concept of equality to represent proportional relationships with equations.
TN.M7.RP.A.2.d: Explain what a point `(x,y)` on the graph of a proportional relationship means in terms of the situation, with special attention to the points `(0,0)and(1,r)` where `r` is the unit rate.
TN.M7.RP.A.3: Use proportional relationships to solve multi-step ratio and percent problems.
TN.M7.NS.A: Apply and extend previous understandings of operations with fractions to add, subtract, multiply, and divide rational numbers.
TN.M7.NS.A.1: Apply and extend previous understandings of addition and subtraction to add and subtract rational numbers; represent addition and subtraction on a horizontal or vertical number line diagram.
TN.M7.NS.A.1.a: Understand `p+q` as the number located a distance `abs(q)` from `p`, in the positive or negative direction depending on whether `q` is positive or negative. Show that a number and its opposite have a sum of `0` (are additive inverses). Interpret sums of rational numbers by describing real-world contexts.
TN.M7.NS.A.1.b: Understand subtraction of rational numbers as adding the additive inverse, `p-q=p+(-q)`. Show that the distance between two rational numbers on the number line is the absolute value of their difference, and apply this principle in real-world contexts.
TN.M7.NS.A.1.c: Apply properties of operations as strategies to add and subtract rational numbers.
TN.M7.NS.A.2: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication and division and of fractions to multiply and divide rational numbers.
TN.M7.NS.A.2.a: Understand that multiplication is extended from fractions to all rational numbers by requiring that operations continue to satisfy the properties of operations, particularly the distributive property, leading to products such as `(-1)(-1)=1` and the rules for multiplying signed numbers. Interpret products of rational numbers by describing real-world contexts.
TN.M7.NS.A.2.b: Understand that integers can be divided, provided that the divisor is not zero, and every quotient of integers (with non-zero divisor) is a rational number. If `pandq` are integers, then `-(p/q)=(-p)/q=p/(-q)`. Interpret quotients of rational numbers by describing real-world contexts.
TN.M7.NS.A.2.c: Apply properties of operations as strategies to multiply and divide rational numbers.
TN.M7.NS.A.2.d: Convert a rational number to a decimal using long division; know that the decimal form of a rational number terminates or eventually repeats.
TN.M7.NS.A.3: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving the four operations with rational numbers.
TN.M7.EE.A: Use properties of operations to generate equivalent expressions.
TN.M7.EE.A.1: Apply properties of operations as strategies to add, subtract, factor, and expand linear expressions with rational coefficients.
TN.M7.EE.A.2: Rewrite and connect equivalent expressions in different forms in a contextual problem to provide multiple ways of interpreting the problem and investigating how the quantities in it are related.
TN.M7.EE.B: Solve real-world and mathematical problems using numerical and algebraic expressions and equations and inequalities.
TN.M7.EE.B.3: Solve multi-step real-world and mathematical problems posed with positive and negative rational numbers presented in any form (whole numbers, fractions, and decimals).
TN.M7.EE.B.3.a: Apply properties of operations to calculate with numbers in any form; convert between forms as appropriate.
TN.M7.EE.B.3.b: Assess the reasonableness of answers using mental computation and estimation strategies.
TN.M7.EE.B.4: Use variables to represent quantities in a real-world and mathematical problem, and construct simple equations and inequalities to solve problems by reasoning about the quantities.
TN.M7.EE.B.4.a: Solve real-world and mathematical problems leading to equations of the form `px+q=randp(x+q)=r` where `p,q,andr` are specific rational numbers. Solve equations of these forms fluently. Compare an algebraic solution to an arithmetic solution, identifying the sequence of the operations used in each approach.
TN.M7.EE.B.4.b: Solve real-world and mathematical problems leading to inequalities of the form `px+q>r,px+q<r,px+q>=r,andpx+q<=r`, where `p,q,andr` are specific rational numbers. Graph the solution set of the inequality on a number line and interpret it in the context of the problem.
TN.M7.G.A: Draw, construct, and describe geometrical figures and describe the relationships between them.
TN.M7.G.A.1: Solve problems involving scale drawings of congruent and similar geometric figures, including computing actual lengths and areas from a scale drawing and reproducing a scale drawing at a different scale.
TN.M7.G.A.2: Draw triangles with given conditions: three angle measures or three side measures. Notice when the conditions determine a unique triangle, more than one triangle, or no triangle.
TN.M7.G.B: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving angle measure, area, surface area, and volume.
TN.M7.G.B.3: Know the formulas for the area and circumference of a circle and use them to solve problems. Explore the relationships between the radius, the circumference, and the area of a circle, and the number `pi`.
TN.M7.G.B.4: Know and use facts about supplementary, complementary, vertical, and adjacent angles in a multi-step problem to write and solve simple equations for an unknown angle in a figure.
TN.M7.G.B.5: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving area of two-dimensional figures composed of triangles, quadrilaterals, and polygons, and volume and surface area of three-dimensional objects composed of cubes and right prisms.
TN.M7.SP.A: Use random sampling to draw inferences about a population.
TN.M7.SP.A.1: Explore how statistics can be used to gain information about a population by examining a sample of the population; generalizations about a population from a sample are valid only if the sample is representative of that population. Understand that random sampling tends to produce representative samples and support valid inferences.
TN.M7.SP.A.2: Collect and use data from a random sample to draw inferences about a population with an unknown characteristic of interest. Generate multiple samples (or simulated samples) of the same size to gauge the variation in estimates or predictions.
TN.M7.SP.B: Draw informal comparative inferences about two populations.
TN.M7.SP.B.3: Informally compare the measures of center (mean, median, mode) of two numerical data distributions with similar variabilities.
TN.M7.SP.B.4: Use measures of center and measures of variability for numerical data from random samples to draw informal comparative inferences about two populations.
TN.M7.SP.C: Investigate chance processes and develop, use, and evaluate probability models.
TN.M7.SP.C.5: Recognize that the probability of a chance event is a number between `0and1 and interpret the likelihood of the event occurring.
TN.M7.SP.C.6: Calculate theoretical and experimental probability of simple events.
TN.M7.SP.C.6.a: Approximate the probability of a chance event by collecting data on the chance process that produces it and observing its long-run relative frequency, and predict the approximate relative frequency given the probability.
TN.M7.SP.C.6.b: Calculate the theoretical probability of a simple event.
TN.M7.SP.C.6.c: Compare theoretical probabilities to experimental probabilities; explain any possible sources of discrepancy.
TN.M7.SP.C.7: Develop a probability model and use it to find experimental or theoretical probabilities of events.
TN.M7.SP.C.7.a: Use a uniform probability model, with equal probability assigned to all outcomes, to determine probabilities of events.
TN.M7.SP.7.b: Develop a probability model, including non-uniform models, by observing frequencies in data generated from a chance process. Use the model to estimate the probabilities of events.
TN.M7.SP.D: Summarize and describe numerical data sets.
TN.M7.SP.D.8: Summarize a numerical data set in relation to its context.
TN.M7.SP.D.8.a: Give quantitative measures of center (median and/or mean) and variability (range and/or interquartile range), as well as describe any overall pattern and any striking deviations from the overall pattern with reference to the context in which the data were gathered.
TN.M7.SP.D.8.b: Relate and understand the choice of measures of center (median and/or mean) and variability (range and/or interquartile range) to the shape of the data distribution and the context in which the data were gathered.
TN.S7.PS.1.1: Develop and use models to illustrate the structure of atoms, including the subatomic particles with their relative positions and charge.
TN.S7.PS.1.2: Compare and contrast elemental molecules and compound molecules.
TN.S7.PS.1.3: Classify matter as pure substances or mixtures based on composition.
TN.S7.PS.1.4: Analyze and interpret chemical reactions to determine if the total number of atoms in the reactants and products support the Law of Conservation of Mass.
TN.S7.PS.1.5: Use the periodic table as a model to analyze and interpret evidence relating to physical and chemical properties to identify a sample of matter.
TN.S7.PS.1.6: Create and interpret models of substances whose atoms represent the states of matter with respect to temperature and pressure.
TN.S7.LS.1: From Molecules To Organisms: Structure & Process
TN.S7.LS.1.1: Develop and construct models that identify and explain the structure and function of major cell organelles as they contribute to the life activities of the cell and organism.
TN.S7.LS.1.2: Conduct an investigation to demonstrate how the cell membrane maintains homeostasis through the process of passive transport.
TN.S7.LS.1.3: Evaluate evidence that cells have structural similarities and differences in organisms across kingdoms.
TN.S7.LS.1.4: Diagram the hierarchical organization of multicellular organisms from cells to organism.
TN.S7.LS.1.5: Explain that the body is a system comprised of subsystems that maintain equilibrium and support life through digestion, respiration, excretion, circulation, sensation (nervous and integumentary), and locomotion (musculoskeletal).
TN.S7.LS.1.6: Develop an argument based on empirical evidence and scientific reasoning to explain how behavioral and structural adaptations in animals and plants affect the probability of survival and reproductive success.
TN.S7.LS.1.7: Evaluate and communicate evidence that compares and contrasts the advantages and disadvantages of sexual and asexual reproduction.
TN.S7.LS.1.8: Construct an explanation demonstrating that the function of mitosis for multicellular organisms is for growth and repair through the production of genetically identical daughter cells.
TN.S7.LS.1.9: Construct a scientific explanation based on compiled evidence for the processes of photosynthesis, cellular respiration, and anaerobic respiration in the cycling of matter and flow of energy into and out of organisms.
TN.S7.LS.2.1: Develop a model to depict the cycling of matter, including carbon and oxygen, including the flow of energy among biotic and abiotic parts of an ecosystem.
TN.S7.LS.3.1: Hypothesize that the impact of structural changes to genes (i.e., mutations) located on chromosomes may result in harmful, beneficial, or neutral effects to the structure and function of the organism.
TN.S7.LS.3.2: Distinguish between mitosis and meiosis and compare the resulting daughter cells.
TN.S7.LS.3.3: Predict the probability of individual dominant and recessive alleles to be transmitted from each parent to offspring during sexual reproduction and represent the phenotypic and genotypic patterns using ratios.
TN.S7.ESS.3.1: Graphically represent the composition of the atmosphere as a mixture of gases and discuss the potential for atmospheric change.
TN.S7.ESS.3.2: Engage in a scientific argument through graphing and translating data regarding human activity and climate.
TN.S7.ETS.2: Links Among Engineering, Technology, Science & Society
TN.S7.ETS.2.1: Examine a problem from the medical field pertaining to biomaterials and design a solution taking into consideration the criteria, constraints, and relevant scientific principles of the problem that may limit possible solutions.
TN.SS7.1: Identify and locate the geographical features of East Asia.
TN.SS7.2: Describe how the reunification of China prior to the Tang Dynasty helped spread Buddhist beliefs.
TN.SS7.3: Summarize agricultural, commercial, and technological developments during the Song Dynasties, and describe the role of Confucianism during the Song.
TN.SS7.4: Examine the rise of the Mongol Empire, including the conquests of Genghis Khan.
TN.SS7.5: Describe Kublai Khan's conquest of China, and explain how he was able to maintain control of the Yuan Empire.
TN.SS7.6: Summarize the effects of the Mongolian empires on the Silk Roads, including the importance of Marco Polo's travels on the spread of Chinese technology and Eurasian trade.
TN.SS7.7: Analyze the achievements of the Ming Dynasty and reasons for its isolationism.
TN.SS7.8: Describe the origins and central features of Shintoism.
TN.SS7.9: Explain how Japanese culture changed through Chinese and Korean influences (including Buddhism and Confucianism) as shown in the Constitution of Prince Shotoku and the adoption of the Chinese writing system.
TN.SS7.10: Describe how the Heian aristocracy contributed to the development of a Japanese national culture.
TN.SS7.11: Analyze the rise of a military society in the late 12th century and the role of the shogun and samurai in Japanese society.
TN.SS7.12: Identify the continuation of the Eastern Roman Empire as the Byzantine Empire, and describe the diffusion of Christianity and the Latin language.
TN.SS7.13: Explain the importance of Justinian's political, social, and architectural achievements.
TN.SS7.14: Analyze the importance of regional geography and the location of Constantinople in maintaining European culture.
TN.SS7.15: Identify and locate the geographical features of Southwest Asia and North Africa.
TN.SS7.16: Describe the origins and central features of Islam.
TN.SS7.17: Describe the diffusion of Islam, its culture, and the Arabic language.
TN.SS7.18: Summarize the contributions of the region's scholars in the areas of art, medicine, geography, philosophy, literature, science, and mathematics.
TN.SS7.19: Explain the importance of Mehmed II the Conqueror, the fall of Constantinople, and the establishment of the Ottoman Empire.
TN.SS7.20: Analyze the development of trade routes throughout Asia, Africa, and Europe and the expanding role of merchants.
TN.SS7.21: Identify and locate the geographical features of West Africa.
TN.SS7.23: Analyze the growth of the kingdoms of Ghana, Mali, and Songhai, including cities such as Djenne and Timbuktu as centers of trade, culture, and learning.
TN.SS7.24: Describe the role of the Trans-Saharan caravan trade in the changing religious and cultural characteristics of West Africa and in the exchange of salt, gold, and slaves.
TN.SS7.25: Explain the importance of griots in the transmission of West African history and culture.
TN.SS7.26: Explain the importance of the Malian king Mansa Musa and his pilgrimage to Mecca in 1324.
TN.SS7.27: Identify and locate geographical features of Europe.
TN.SS7.28: Describe the role of monasteries in the preservation of knowledge and spread of the Catholic Church beyond the Alps.
TN.SS7.29: Explain how Charlemagne shaped and defined medieval Europe.
TN.SS7.30: Describe the development of feudalism and manorialism, their role in the medieval European economy, and the way in which they were influenced by physical geography (i.e., the role of the manor and the growth of towns).
TN.SS7.31: Analyze the Battle of Hastings and the long-term historical impact of William the Conqueror on England and Northern France.
TN.SS7.32: Describe how political relationships both fostered cooperation and led to conflict between the Papacy and European monarchs.
TN.SS7.33: Analyze the impact of the Magna Carta.
TN.SS7.34: Analyze the causes, effects, and key people of the 1st, 2nd, and 3rd Crusades.
TN.SS7.35: Explain how the Crusades impacted Christian, Muslim, and Jewish populations in Europe, with emphasis on the increasing contact with cultures outside Europe.
TN.SS7.36: Describe the economic and social effects of the spread of the Black Death (i.e., Bubonic Plague) from Central Asia to China, the Middle East, and Europe, and its impact on the global population.
TN.SS7.37: Analyze the importance of the Black Death on the emergence of a modern economy.
TN.SS7.38: Describe the significance of the Hundred Years War.
TN.SS7.39: Explain the significance of the Reconquista, Inquisition, and the rise of Spanish and Portuguese kingdoms in the Iberian Peninsula.
TN.SS7.40: Explain how the location of the Italian Peninsula impacted the movement of resources, knowledge, and culture throughout Italy's independent trade cities.
TN.SS7.41: Identify the importance of Florence, Italy and the Medici Family in the early stages of the Renaissance.
TN.SS7.42: Explain humanism, and describe how Thomas Aquinas's writings influenced humanistic thought and fostered a balance between reason and faith.
TN.SS7.43: Explain the development of Renaissance art.
TN.SS7.44: Analyze Johannes Gutenberg's printing press and William Tyndale's translation of the Bible into the English language as vehicles for the spread of books, growth of literacy, and dissemination of knowledge.
TN.SS7.45: Explain the significant causes of the Protestant Reformation.
TN.SS7.46: Analyze the development of the Protestant Reformation and the split with the Catholic Church.
TN.SS7.47: Explain the political and religious roles of Henry VIII and Mary I in England's transition between Catholicism and Protestantism.
TN.SS7.48: Analyze how the Catholic Counter-Reformation emerged as a response to Protestantism and revitalized the Catholic Church.
TN.SS7.49: Examine the Golden Age of the Tudor dynasty (i.e., Queen Elizabeth I), including the defeat of the Spanish Armada and the rise of English power in Europe.
TN.SS7.50: Compare and contrast heliocentric and geocentric theories of the Greeks (geocentric), Copernicus (heliocentric), and Kepler (elliptical orbits).
TN.SS7.51: Examine Galileo Galilei's theories and improvement of scientific tools.
TN.SS7.52: Explain the significance of the following in regards to the Scientific Revolution: Sir Francis Bacon in establishing the scientific method and Sir Isaac Newton's three Laws of Motion.
TN.SS7.53: Identify and locate the geographical features of the Americas.
TN.SS7.54: Explain the impact of geographic features on North American Indian cultures (i.e., Northeast, Southeast, and Plains).
TN.SS7.55: Describe the existence of diverse networks of North American Indian cultures (within present- day United States).
TN.SS7.56: Explain the impact of geographic features and climate on the agricultural practices and settlement of the Maya, Aztec, and Incan civilizations.
TN.SS7.57: Describe the social, economic, and political characteristics of the Maya, Aztec, and Incan civilizations.
TN.SS7.58: Analyze why European countries were motivated to explore the world.
TN.SS7.59: Identify the significance of the voyages and routes of discovery of the following explorers by their sponsoring country.
TN.SS7.60: Describe Prince Henry the Navigator's influence on exploration, voyages, cartographic improvements, and tools related to exploration (i.e., compass, caravel, astrolabe, and Harrison's chronometer) during the Age of Discovery.
TN.SS7.61: Locate and identify French, Spanish, English, Portuguese, and Dutch colonies in the Americas, and explain how religion impacted the location of settlement by each country.
TN.SS7.62: Describe how the Aztec and Inca empires were eventually defeated by Spanish Conquistadors (i.e., Hernan Cortes and Francisco Pizarro).
TN.SS7.63: Locate and identify the European regions that remained Catholic and those that became Protestant and how that division affected the distribution of religions in the New World.
TN.SS7.64: Explain the impact of the Columbian Exchange on people, plants, animals, technology, culture, ideas, and diseases among Europe, Africa, Asia, and the Americas in the 15th and 16th centuries, and examine the major economic and social effects on each continent.
TN.SS7.65: Explain how Spanish colonization introduced Christianity, the mission system, and the encomienda system to the Americas as well as Bartolome de la Casa's role in the transition to African slavery.

TN.E8.L.VAU.4.c: Consult reference materials, both print and digital, to find the pronunciation of a word or phrase.
TN.E8.L.VAU.4.d: Use etymological patterns in spelling as clues to the meaning of a word or phrase.

TN.E8.RL.KID.1: Analyze what a text says explicitly and draw logical inferences; support an interpretation of a text by citing relevant textual evidence.

TN.E8.RI.KID.1: Analyze what a text says explicitly and draw logical inferences; support an interpretation of a text by citing relevant textual evidence.
TN.E8.RI.KID.2: Determine a central idea of a text and analyze its development over the course of the text, including its relationship to supporting ideas; provide an objective summary.
TN.E8.RI.KID.3: Analyze the techniques used to distinguish between and to make connections among individuals, events, or ideas in a text.

TN.E8.SL.PKI.4: Present claims and findings in a focused, coherent manner with relevant evidence, valid reasoning, and well-chosen details; use appropriate eye contact, adequate volume, and clear pronunciation.
TN.E8.SL.PKI.5: Integrate multimedia and visual displays into presentations to clarify information, to strengthen claims and evidence, and to add interest.

TN.E8.W.TTP.1: Write arguments to support claims with clear reasons and relevant evidence.
TN.E8.W.TTP.1.b: Support claim(s) with logical reasoning and relevant, sufficient evidence; acknowledge and refute alternate or opposing claim(s).
TN.E8.W.TTP.1.c: Organize the reasons and evidence clearly and clarify the relationships among claim(s) and reasons.
TN.E8.W.TTP.1.d: Use credible sources and demonstrate an understanding of the topic or source material.
TN.E8.W.TTP.1.e: Craft an effective and relevant conclusion that supports the argument presented.
TN.E8.W.TTP.1.f: Use precise language and content-specific vocabulary.
TN.E8.W.TTP.1.g: Use appropriate transitions to create cohesion and clarify the relationships among ideas and concepts.
TN.E8.W.TTP.1.h: Use varied sentence structure to enhance meaning and reader interest.
TN.E8.W.TTP.1.i: Establish and maintain a formal style.

TN.E8.W.TTP.2.b: Synthesize and organize ideas, concepts, and information into broader categories using effective strategies to create cohesion and aid in comprehension.
TN.E8.W.TTP.2.c: Develop the topic with relevant facts, definitions, concrete details, quotations, or other information and examples.
TN.E8.W.TTP.2.d: Thoroughly and accurately explain and elaborate on the evidence provided, demonstrating a clear understanding of the topic and the source material.
TN.E8.W.TTP.2.e: Craft an effective and relevant conclusion.
TN.E8.W.TTP.2.f: Include formatting, graphics, and multimedia when appropriate.
TN.E8.W.TTP.2.g: Use appropriate and varied transitions to create cohesion and clarify the relationships among ideas and concepts.
TN.E8.W.TTP.2.h: Use precise language and domain-specific vocabulary.
TN.E8.W.TTP.2.i: Use varied sentence structure to enhance meaning and reader interest.
TN.E8.W.TTP.2.j: Establish and maintain a formal style.

TN.E8.W.TTP.3.c: Create a smooth progression of experiences or events.

TN.E8.W.TTP.3.g: Use precise words and phrases, relevant descriptive details, and sensory language to convey experiences and events.

TN.M8.NS.A: Know that there are numbers that are not rational, and approximate them by rational numbers.

TN.M8.NS.A.2: Use rational approximations of irrational numbers to compare the size of irrational numbers by locating them approximately on a number line diagram. Estimate the value of irrational expressions (such as `pi^2`).
TN.M8.EE.A: Work with radicals and integer exponents.
TN.M8.EE.A.1: Know and apply the properties of integer exponents to generate equivalent numerical expressions.
TN.M8.EE.A.2: Use square root and cube root symbols to represent solutions to equations of the form `x^2=pandx^3=p`, where `p` is a positive rational number. Evaluate square roots of small perfect squares and cube roots of small perfect cubes.
TN.M8.EE.A.3: Use numbers expressed in the form of a single digit times an integer power of `10` to estimate very large or very small quantities and to express how many times as much one is than the other.
TN.M8.EE.A.4: Using technology, solve real-world problems with numbers expressed in decimal and scientific notation. Use scientific notation and choose units of appropriate size for measurements of very large or very small quantities (e.g., use `text(millimeters per year)` for seafloor spreading).
TN.M8.EE.B: Understand the connections between proportional relationships, lines, and linear equations.
TN.M8.EE.B.5: Graph proportional relationships, interpreting the unit rate as the slope of the graph. Compare two different proportional relationships represented in different ways.
TN.M8.EE.B.6: Use similar triangles to explain why the slope `m` is the same between any two distinct points on a non-vertical line in the coordinate plane; know and apply the equation `y=mx` for a line through the origin and the equation `y=mx+b` for a line intercepting the vertical axis at `b`.
TN.M8.EE.C: Analyze and solve linear equations, linear inequalities, and systems of two linear equations.
TN.M8.EE.C.7: Solve linear equations in one variable.
TN.M8.EE.C.7.a: Give examples of linear equations in one variable with one solution, infinitely many solutions, or no solutions. Show which of these possibilities is the case by successively transforming the given equation into simpler forms, until an equivalent equation of the form `x=a,a=a,ora=b` results (where `aandb` are different numbers).
TN.M8.EE.C.7.b: Solve linear equations with rational number coefficients, including equations whose solutions require expanding expressions using the distributive property and combining like terms.
TN.M8.EE.C.8: Analyze and solve systems of two linear equations graphically.
TN.M8.EE.C.8.a: Understand that solutions to a system of two linear equations in two variables correspond to points of intersection of their graphs, because points of intersection satisfy both equations simultaneously.
TN.M8.EE.C.8.b: Estimate solutions by graphing a system of two linear equations in two variables. Identify solutions by inspecting graphs of a system of linear equations in two variables.
TN.M8.EE.C.9: By graphing on the coordinate plane or by analyzing a given graph, determine the solution set of a linear inequality in one or two variables.
TN.M8.F.A.1: Understand that a function is a rule that assigns to each input exactly one output. The graph of a function is the set of ordered pairs consisting of an input and the corresponding output.

TN.M8.F.A.3: Know and interpret the equation `y=mx+b` as defining a linear function, whose graph is a straight line; give examples of functions that are not linear.
TN.M8.F.B: Use functions to model relationships between quantities.
TN.M8.F.B.4: Construct a function to model a linear relationship between two quantities. Determine the rate of change and initial value of the function from a description of a relationship or from two `(x,y)` values, including reading these from a table or from a graph. Interpret the rate of change and initial value of a linear function in terms of the situation it models and in terms of its graph or a table of values.
TN.M8.F.B.5: Describe qualitatively the functional relationship between two quantities by analyzing a graph (e.g., where the function is increasing or decreasing, linear or nonlinear). Sketch a graph that exhibits the qualitative features of a function that has been described verbally.

TN.M8.G.A.1.a: Verify informally that lines are taken to lines, and determine when line segments are taken to line segments of the same length.

TN.M8.G.B.3: Explain a model of the Pythagorean Theorem and its converse.

TN.M8.SP.B.4.b: Represent sample spaces for compound events using methods such as organized lists, tables, and tree diagrams. For an event described in everyday language (e.g., “rolling double sixes”), identify the outcomes in the sample space which compose the event.

TN.M9-12.A1.F-IF.A: Understand the concept of a function and use function notation.

If `f` is a function and `x` is an element of its domain, then `f(x)` denotes the output of `f` corresponding to the input `x`. The graph of f is the graph of the equation `y=f(x)`.

TN.M9-12.A2.A-SSE.A.1: Interpret expressions that represent a quantity in terms of its context.

TN.M9-12.A2.A-SSE.A.1.b: Interpret complicated expressions by viewing one or more of their parts as a single entity.

TN.M9-12.A22.A-APR.A.1: Know and apply the Factor Theorem: For a polynomial `p(x)` and a number `a,p(a)=0` if and only if `(x-a)` is a factor of `p(x)`.

TN.M9-12.A2.A-CED.A: Create equations that describe numbers or relationships.
TN.M9-12.A2.A-CED.A.1: Create equations and inequalities in one variable and use them to solve problems in a real-world context.
TN.M9-12.A2.A-CED.A.2: Create equations and inequalities in two variables to represent relationships between quantities and use them to solve problems in a real-world context. Graph equations and inequalities with two variables on coordinate axes with labels and scales, and use the graphs to make predictions.
TN.M9-12.A2.A-CED.A.3: Rearrange formulas to isolate a quantity of interest using algebraic reasoning.
TN.M9-12.A2.A-REI.A: Understand solving equations as a process of reasoning and explain the reasoning.

TN.M9-12.A2.A-REI.A.2: Solve radical equations in one variable, and identify extraneous solutions when they exist.
TN.M9-12.A2.A-REI.B.3: Write and solve a system of linear equations in a real-world context.

TN.M9-12.A2.F-IF.A: Interpret functions that arise in applications in terms of the context.
TN.M9-12.A2.F-IF.A.1: For a function that models a relationship between two quantities, interpret key features of graphs and tables in terms of the quantities, and sketch graphs showing key features given a verbal description of the relationship.
TN.M9-12.A2.F-IF.A.2: Calculate and interpret the average rate of change of a function (presented algebraically or as a table) over a specified interval. Estimate and interpret the rate of change from a graph.
TN.M9-12.A2.F-IF.B.4: Graph functions expressed algebraically and show key features of the graph by hand and using technology.
TN.M9-12.A2.F-IF.B.5: Write a function defined by an expression in different but equivalent forms to reveal and explain different properties of the function.
TN.M9-12.A2.F-IF.B.5.a: Rewrite quadratic functions to show zeros, extreme values, and symmetry of the graph, and interpret these in terms of a real-world context.
TN.M9-12.A2.F-IF.B.5.b: Know and use the properties of exponents to interpret expressions for exponential functions in terms of a real-world context.
TN.M9-12.A2.F-IF.B.6: Compare properties of functions represented algebraically, graphically, numerically in tables, or by verbal descriptions.
TN.M9-12.A2.F-IF.B.6.a: Compare properties of two different functions. Functions may be of different types and/or represented in different ways.
TN.M9-12.A2.F-IF.B.6.b: Compare properties of the same function on two different intervals or represented in two different ways.
TN.M9-12.A2.F-BF.A: Build a function that models a relationship between two quantities.
TN.M9-12.A2.F-BF.A.1: Build a function that describes a relationship between two quantities.
TN.M9-12.A2.F-BF.A.1.a: Combine standard function types using arithmetic operations.
TN.M9-12.A2.F-BF.A.1.b: Combine standard function types using composition.
TN.M9-12.A2.F-BF.A.2: Define sequences as functions, including recursive definitions, whose domain is a subset of the integers. Write explicit and recursive formulas for arithmetic and geometric sequences in context and connect them to linear and exponential functions.

TN.M9-12.A2.F-BF.B.3: Identify the effect on the graph of replacing `f(x)` by `f(x)+k,kf(x),f(kx),andf(x+k)`  for specific values of `k` (both positive and negative); find the value of `k` given the graphs.
TN.M9-12.A2.F-BF.B.4: Find the inverse of a function.
TN.M9-12.A2.F-BF.B.4.a: Determine whether a function is one-to-one.
TN.M9-12.A2.F-BF.B.4.b: Find the inverse of a function on an appropriate domain.
TN.M9-12.A2.F-BF.B.4.c: Given an invertible function on an appropriate domain, identify the domain of the inverse function.
TN.M9-12.A2.F-LE.A: Construct and compare linear, quadratic, and exponential models and solve problems.
TN.M9-12.A2.F-LE.A.1: Know the relationship between exponential functions and logarithmic functions.
TN.M9-12.A2.F-LE.A.1.a: Solve exponential equations using a variety of strategies, including logarithms.
TN.M9-12.A2.F-LE.A.1.b: Understand that a logarithm is the solution to abᶜᵗ = d, where `a,b,c,andd` are numbers.
TN.M9-12.A2.F-LE.A.2: Know that a quantity increasing exponentially eventually exceeds a quantity increasing linearly, quadratically, or cubically.
TN.M9-12.A2.S-ID.A: Summarize, represent, and interpret data on a single count or measurement variable.
TN.M9-12.A2.S-ID.A.1: Use statistics appropriate to the shape of the data distribution to compare center (mean, median, and/or mode) and spread (range, standard deviation) of two or more different data sets.
TN.M9-12.A2.S-ID.A.2: Use the mean and standard deviation of a data set to fit it to a normal distribution and to estimate population percentages using the Empirical Rule.
TN.M9-12.A2.S-ID.A.3: Compute, interpret, and compare z-scores for normally distributed data in a real-world context.
TN.M9-12.A2.S-ID.B: Summarize, represent, and interpret data on two categorical and quantitative variables.
TN.M9-12.A2.S-ID.B.4: Represent data from two quantitative variables on a scatter plot, and describe how the variables are related. Fit a function to the data; use functions fitted to data to solve problems in the context of the data.
TN.M9-12.A2.S-IC.A: Make inferences and justify conclusions from sample surveys, experiments, and observational studies.
TN.M9-12.A2.S-IC.A.1: Recognize the purposes of and differences among sample surveys, experiments, and observational studies.
TN.M9-12.A2.S-IC.A.2: Identify potential sources of bias in statistical studies.
TN.M9-12.A2.S-IC.A.3: Distinguish between a statistic and a parameter. Evaluate reports based on data and recognize when poor conclusions are drawn from well-collected data.
TN.M9-12.A2.S-CP.A: Understand independence and conditional probability and use them to create visual representations of data.
TN.M9-12.A2.S-CP.A.1: Recognize and explain the concepts of conditional probability and independence in everyday language and everyday situations. Categorize events as independent or dependent.
TN.M9-12.A2.S-CP.B: Understand and apply basic concepts of probability.
TN.M9-12.A2.S-CP.B.2.a: Use the Fundamental Counting Principle to compute probabilities of compound events and solve problems.
TN.M9-12.A2.S-CP.B.2.b: Use permutations and combinations to compute probabilities of compound events and solve problems.
TN.M9-12.A2.S-CP.B.3: Use the Law of Large Numbers to assess the validity of a statistical claim.
TN.M9-12.A2.S-CP.C: Use the rules of probability to compute probabilities of compound events in a uniform probability model.
TN.M9-12.A2.S-CP.C.4: Find the conditional probability of A given B as the fraction of B's outcomes that also belong to A and interpret the answer in terms of the given context.
TN.M9-12.G.N-Q.A: Reason quantitatively and use units to solve problems.
TN.M9-12.G.N-Q.A.1: Use units as a way to understand real-world problems.
TN.M9-12.G.N-Q.A.1.a: Use appropriate quantities in formulas, converting units as necessary.
TN.M9-12.G.N-Q.A.1.b: Define and justify appropriate quantities within a context for the purpose of modeling.
TN.M9-12.G.N-Q.A.1.c: Choose an appropriate level of accuracy when reporting quantities.
TN.M9-12.G.G-CO.A: Experiment with transformations in the plane.
TN.M9-12.G.G-CO.A.1: Describe transformations as functions that take points in the plane (pre-image) as inputs and give other points (image) as outputs. Compare transformations that preserve distance and angle measure to those that do not, by hand for basic transformations and using technology for more complex cases.
TN.M9-12.G.G-CO.A.2: Given a rectangle, parallelogram, trapezoid, or regular polygon, determine the transformations that carry the shape onto itself and describe them in terms of the symmetry of the figure.
TN.M9-12.G.G-CO.A.3: Develop definitions of rotations, reflections, and translations in terms of angles, circles, perpendicular lines, parallel lines, and line segments.
TN.M9-12.G.G-CO.A.4: Given a geometric figure, draw the image of the figure after a sequence of one or more rigid motions, by hand and using technology. Identify a sequence of rigid motions that will carry a given figure onto another.
TN.M9-12.G.G-CO.B: Understand congruence in terms of rigid motions.
TN.M9-12.G.G-CO.B.5: Given two figures, use the definition of congruence in terms of rigid motions to determine informally if they are congruent.

TN.M9-12.G.G-CO.B.7: Explain how the criteria for triangle congruence (ASA, SAS, AAS, SSS, and HL) follow from the definition of congruence in terms of rigid motions.
TN.M9-12.G.G-CO.C: Use geometric theorems to justify relationships.
TN.M9-12.G.G-CO.C.8: Use definitions and theorems about lines and angles to solve problems and to justify relationships in geometric figures.
TN.M9-12.G.G-CO.C.9: Use definitions and theorems about triangles to solve problems and to justify relationships in geometric figures.
TN.M9-12.G.G-CO.C.10: Use definitions and theorems about parallelograms to solve problems and to justify relationships in geometric figures.
TN.M9-12.G.G-CO.D.11: Perform formal geometric constructions with a variety of tools and methods (compass and straightedge, string, reflective devices, paper folding, dynamic geometric software, etc.).
TN.M9-12.G.G-CO.D.12: Use geometric constructions to solve geometric problems in context, by hand and using technology.
TN.M9-12.G.G-SRT.A: Understand similarity in terms of similarity transformations.

TN.M9-12.G.G-SRT.C.5.c: Use the Law of Sines and Law of Cosines to solve non-right triangles in a real-world context.
TN.M9-12.G.G-C.A: Find areas of sectors of circles.
TN.M9-12.G.G-C.A.1: Use proportional relationships between the area of a circle and the area of a sector within the circle to solve problems in a real-world context.

TN.M9-12.G.G-MG.A: Apply geometric concepts in modeling situations.
TN.M9-12.G.G-MG.A.1: Use geometric shapes, their measures, and their properties to model objects found in a real-world context for the purpose of approximating solutions to problems.
TN.M9-12.G.S-CP.A: Understand independence and conditional probability and use them to create visual representations of data.
TN.M9-12.G.S-CP.A.1: Use set notation to represent contextual situations.
