TX.RK.1: Listening, speaking, discussion, and thinking--oral language. The student develops oral language through listening, speaking, and discussion. The student is expected to:
TX.RK.1A: Listen actively and ask questions to understand information and answer questions using multi-word responses.
TX.RK.1B: Restate and follow oral directions that involve a short, related sequence of actions.
TX.RK.1C: Share information and ideas by speaking audibly and clearly using the conventions of language.
TX.RK.1D: Work collaboratively with others by following agreed-upon rules for discussion, including taking turns.
TX.RK.1E: Develop social communication such as introducing himself/herself, using common greetings, and expressing needs and wants.
TX.RK.2: Listening, speaking, reading, writing, and thinking--beginning reading and writing. The student develops word structure knowledge through phonological awareness, print concepts, phonics, and morphology to communicate, decode, and spell. The student is expected to:
TX.RK.2A.ii: Recognizing spoken alliteration or groups of words that begin with the same spoken onset or initial sound.
TX.RK.2A.iii: Identifying the individual words in a spoken sentence.
TX.RK.2A.v: Blending syllables to form multisyllabic words.
TX.RK.2A.vii: Blending spoken onsets and rimes to form simple words.
TX.RK.2A.viii: Blending spoken phonemes to form one-syllable words.
TX.RK.2A.ix: Manipulating syllables within a multisyllabic word.
TX.RK.2A.x: Segmenting spoken one-syllable words into individual phonemes.
TX.RK.2B: Demonstrate and apply phonetic knowledge by:
TX.RK.2B.i: Identifying and matching the common sounds that letters represent.
TX.RK.2B.ii: Using letter-sound relationships to decode, including VC, CVC, CCVC, and CVCC words.
TX.RK.2B.iii: Recognizing that new words are created when letters are changed, added, or deleted such as it - pit - tip - tap.
TX.RK.2B.iv: Identifying and reading at least 25 high-frequency words from a research-based list.
TX.RK.2C.i: Spelling words with VC, CVC, and CCVC.
TX.RK.2C.iii: Spelling high-frequency words from a research-based list.
TX.RK.2D.i: Identifying the front cover, back cover, and title page of a book.
TX.RK.2D.ii: Holding a book right side up, turning pages correctly, and knowing that reading moves from top to bottom and left to right with return sweep.
TX.RK.2D.iii: Recognizing that sentences are comprised of words separated by spaces and recognizing word boundaries.
TX.RK.2D.iv: Recognizing the difference between a letter and a printed word.
TX.RK.2D.v: Identifying all uppercase and lowercase letters.
TX.RK.2E: Develop handwriting by accurately forming all uppercase and lowercase letters using appropriate directionality.
TX.RK.3: Listening, speaking, reading, writing, and thinking--vocabulary. The student uses newly acquired vocabulary expressively. The student is expected to:
TX.RK.3A: Use a resource such as a picture dictionary or digital resource to find words.
TX.RK.3B: Use illustrations and texts the student is able to read or hear to learn or clarify word meanings.
TX.RK.3C: Identify and use words that name actions; directions; positions; sequences; categories such as colors, shapes, and textures; and locations.
TX.RK.4: Listening, speaking, reading, writing, and thinking--self-sustained reading. The student reads grade-appropriate texts independently.
TX.RK.4A: Self-select text and interact independently with text for increasing periods of time.
TX.RK.5: Listening, speaking, reading, writing, and thinking using multiple texts. The student uses metacognitive skills to both develop and deepen comprehension of increasingly complex texts. The student is expected to:
TX.RK.5A: Establish purpose for reading assigned and self-selected texts with adult assistance.
TX.RK.5B: Generate questions about text before, during, and after reading to deepen understanding and gain information with adult assistance.
TX.RK.5C: Make and confirm predictions using text features and structures with adult assistance.
TX.RK.5D: Create mental images to deepen understanding with adult assistance.
TX.RK.5E: Make connections to personal experiences, ideas in other texts, and society with adult assistance.
TX.RK.5F: Make inferences and use evidence to support understanding with adult assistance.
TX.RK.5G: Evaluate details to determine what is most important with adult assistance.
TX.RK.5H: Synthesize information to create new understanding with adult assistance.
TX.RK.5I: Monitor comprehension and make adjustments such as re-reading, using background knowledge, checking for visual cues, and asking questions when understanding breaks down with adult assistance.
TX.RK.6: Listening, speaking, reading, writing, and thinking using multiple texts. The student responds to an increasingly challenging variety of sources that are read, heard, or viewed. The student is expected to:
TX.RK.6A: Describe personal connections to a variety of sources.
TX.RK.6B: Provide an oral, pictorial, or written response to a text.
TX.RK.6C: Use text evidence to support an appropriate response.
TX.RK.6D: Retell texts in ways that maintain meaning.
TX.RK.6E: Interact with sources in meaningful ways such as illustrating or writing.
TX.RK.6F: Respond using newly acquired vocabulary as appropriate.
TX.RK.7: Listening, speaking, reading, writing, and thinking using multiple texts--literary elements. The student recognizes and analyzes literary elements within and across increasingly complex traditional, contemporary, classical, and diverse literary texts.
TX.RK.7A: Discuss topics and determine the basic theme using text evidence with adult assistance.
TX.RK.7B: Identify and describe the main character(s).
TX.RK.7C: Describe the elements of plot development, including the main events, the problem, and the resolution for texts read aloud with adult assistance.
TX.RK.8: Listening, speaking, reading, writing, and thinking using multiple texts--genres. The student recognizes and analyzes genre-specific characteristics, structures, and purposes within nd across increasingly complex traditional, contemporary, classical, and diverse texts. The student is expected to:
TX.RK.8A: Demonstrate knowledge of distinguishing characteristics of well-known children's literature such as folktales, fables, fairy tales, and nursery rhymes.
TX.RK.8B: Discuss rhyme and rhythm in nursery rhymes and a variety of poems.
TX.RK.8D: Recognize characteristics and structures of informational text.
TX.RK.8D.i: The central idea and supporting evidence with adult assistance.
TX.RK.8D.ii: Titles and simple graphics to gain information.
TX.RK.8D.iii: The steps in a sequence with adult assistance.
TX.RK.8E: Recognize characteristics of persuasive text with adult assistance and state what the author is trying to persuade the reader to think or do.
TX.RK.8F: Recognize characteristics of multimodal and digital texts.
TX.RK.9: Listening, speaking, reading, writing, and thinking using multiple texts. The student uses critical inquiry to analyze the authors' choices and how they influence and communicate meaning within a variety of texts. The student analyzes and applies author's craft purposefully in order to develop his or her own products and performances. The student is expected to:
TX.RK.9A: Discuss with adult assistance the author's purpose for writing text.
TX.RK.9B: Discuss with adult assistance how the use of text structure contributes to the author's purpose.
TX.RK.9C: Discuss with adult assistance the author's use of print and graphic features to achieve specific purposes.
TX.RK.9D: Discuss with adult assistance how the author uses words that help the reader visualize.
TX.RK.9E: Listen to and experience first- and third-person texts.
TX.RK.10: Listening, speaking, reading, writing, and thinking using multiple texts--writing process. The student uses the writing process recursively to compose multiple texts that are legible and uses appropriate conventions. The student is expected to:
TX.RK.10A: Plan by generating ideas for writing through class discussions and drawings.
TX.RK.10B: Develop drafts in oral, pictorial, or written form by organizing ideas.
TX.RK.10C: Revise drafts by adding details in pictures or words.
TX.RK.10D: Edit drafts with adult assistance using standard English conventions, including:
TX.RK.10D.vi: Pronouns, including subjective, objective, and possessive cases.
TX.RK.10D.vii: Capitalization of the first letter in a sentence and name.
TX.RK.10D.viii: Punctuation marks at the end of declarative sentences.
TX.RK.10D.ix: Correct spelling of words with grade-appropriate orthographic patterns and rules and high-frequency words.
TX.RK.11: Listening, speaking, reading, writing, and thinking using multiple texts--genres. The student uses genre characteristics and craft to compose multiple texts that are meaningful. The student is expected to:
TX.RK.11A: Dictate or compose literary texts, including personal narratives.
TX.RK.12: Listening, speaking, reading, writing, and thinking using multiple texts. The student engages in both short-term and sustained recursive inquiry processes for a variety of purposes. The student is expected to:
TX.RK.12A: Generate questions for formal and informal inquiry with adult assistance.
TX.RK.12B: Develop and follow a research plan with adult assistance.
TX.RK.12C: Gather information from a variety of sources with adult assistance.
TX.RK.12D: Demonstrate understanding of information gathered with adult assistance.
TX.RK.12E: Use an appropriate mode of delivery, whether written, oral, or multimodal, to present results.
TX.MK.1: The student uses mathematical processes to acquire and demonstrate mathematical understanding. The student is expected to:
TX.MK.1A: Apply mathematics to problems arising in everyday life, society, and the workplace.
TX.MK.1B: Use a problem-solving model that incorporates analyzing given information, formulating a plan or strategy, determining a solution, justifying the solution, and evaluating the problem-solving process and the reasonableness of the solution.
TX.MK.1C: Select tools, including real objects, manipulatives, paper and pencil, and technology as appropriate, and techniques, including mental math, estimation, and number sense as appropriate, to solve problems.
TX.MK.1D: Communicate mathematical ideas, reasoning, and their implications using multiple representations, including symbols, diagrams, graphs, and language as appropriate.
TX.MK.1E: Create and use representations to organize, record, and communicate mathematical ideas.
TX.MK.1F: Analyze mathematical relationships to connect and communicate mathematical ideas.
TX.MK.1G: Display, explain, and justify mathematical ideas and arguments using precise mathematical language in written or oral communication.
TX.MK.2: The student applies mathematical process standards to understand how to represent and compare whole numbers, the relative position and magnitude of whole numbers, and relationships within the numeration system. The student is expected to:
TX.MK.2A: Count forward and backward to at least 20 with and without objects.
TX.MK.2B: Read, write, and represent whole numbers from 0 to at least 20 with and without objects or pictures.
TX.MK.2C: Count a set of objects up to at least 20 and demonstrate that the last number said tells the number of objects in the set regardless of their arrangement or order.
TX.MK.2D: Recognize instantly the quantity of a small group of objects in organized and random arrangements.
TX.MK.2E: Generate a set using concrete and pictorial models that represents a number that is more than, less than, and equal to a given number up to 20.
TX.MK.2F: Generate a number that is one more than or one less than another number up to at least 20.
TX.MK.2G: Compare sets of objects up to at least 20 in each set using comparative language.
TX.MK.2H: Use comparative language to describe two numbers up to 20 presented as written numerals.
TX.MK.2I: Compose and decompose numbers up to 10 with objects and pictures.
The student applies mathematical process standards to develop an understanding of addition and subtraction situations in order to solve problems. The student is expected to:
TX.MK.3A: Model the action of joining to represent addition and the action of separating to represent subtraction.
TX.MK.3B: Solve word problems using objects and drawings to find sums up to 10 and differences within 10.
TX.MK.3C: Explain the strategies used to solve problems involving adding and subtracting within 10 using spoken words, concrete and pictorial models, and number sentences.
TX.MK.4: The student applies mathematical process standards to identify coins in order to recognize the need for monetary transactions. The student is expected to:
TX.MK.4A: Identify U.S. coins by name, including pennies, nickels, dimes, and quarters.
TX.MK.5: The student applies mathematical process standards to identify the pattern in the number word list. The student is expected to:
TX.MK.5A: Recite numbers up to at least 100 by ones and tens beginning with any given number.
TX.MK.6: The student applies mathematical process standards to analyze attributes of two-dimensional shapes and three-dimensional solids to develop generalizations about their properties. The student is expected to:
TX.MK.6A: Identify two-dimensional shapes, including circles, triangles, rectangles, and squares as special rectangles.
TX.MK.6B: Identify three-dimensional solids, including cylinders, cones, spheres, and cubes, in the real world.
TX.MK.6C: Identify two-dimensional components of three-dimensional objects.
TX.MK.6D: Identify attributes of two-dimensional shapes using informal and formal geometric language interchangeably.
TX.MK.6E: Classify and sort a variety of regular and irregular two- and three-dimensional figures regardless of orientation or size.
TX.MK.6F: Create two-dimensional shapes using a variety of materials and drawings.
TX.MK.7: The student applies mathematical process standards to directly compare measurable attributes. The student is expected to:
TX.MK.7A: Give an example of a measurable attribute of a given object, including length, capacity, and weight.
TX.MK.7B: Compare two objects with a common measurable attribute to see which object has more of/less of the attribute and describe the difference.
TX.MK.8: The student applies mathematical process standards to collect and organize data to make it useful for interpreting information. The student is expected to:
TX.MK.8A: Collect, sort, and organize data into two or three categories.
TX.MK.8B: Use data to create real-object and picture graphs.
TX.MK.8C: Draw conclusions from real-object and picture graphs.
TX.MK.9: The student applies mathematical process standards to manage one's financial resources effectively for lifetime financial security. The student is expected to:
TX.MK.9B: Differentiate between money received as income and money received as gifts.
TX.MK.9C: List simple skills required for jobs.
TX.MK.9D: Distinguish between wants and needs and identify income as a source to meet one's wants and needs.

TX.M1.3: The student applies mathematical process standards to develop and use strategies for whole number addition and subtraction computations in order to solve problems. The student is expected to:
TX.M1.3A: Use concrete and pictorial models to determine the sum of a multiple of 10 and a one-digit number in problems up to 99.
TX.M1.3B: Use objects and pictorial models to solve word problems involving joining, separating, and comparing sets within 20 and unknowns as any one of the terms in the problem such as 2 + 4 = [ ]; 3 + [ ] = 7; and 5 = [ ] - 3.
TX.M1.3C: Compose 10 with two or more addends with and without concrete objects.
TX.M1.3D: Apply basic fact strategies to add and subtract within 20, including making 10 and decomposing a number leading to a 10.
TX.M1.3E: Explain strategies used to solve addition and subtraction problems up to 20 using spoken words, objects, pictorial models, and number sentences.
TX.M1.3F: Generate and solve problem situations when given a number sentence involving addition or subtraction of numbers within 20.
TX.M1.4: The student applies mathematical process standards to identify coins, their values, and the relationships among them in order to recognize the need for monetary transactions. The student is expected to:
TX.M1.4A: Identify U.S. coins, including pennies, nickels, dimes, and quarters, by value and describe the relationships among them.
TX.M1.4B: Write a number with the cent symbol to describe the value of a coin.
TX.M1.4C: Use relationships to count by twos, fives, and tens to determine the value of a collection of pennies, nickels, and/or dimes.
TX.M1.5: The student applies mathematical process standards to identify and apply number patterns within properties of numbers and operations in order to describe relationships. The student is expected to:
TX.M1.5A: Recite numbers forward and backward from any given number between 1 and 120.
TX.M1.5B: Skip count by twos, fives, and tens to determine the total number of objects up to 120 in a set.
TX.M1.5C: Use relationships to determine the number that is 10 more and 10 less than a given number up to 120.
TX.M1.5D: Represent word problems involving addition and subtraction of whole numbers up to 20 using concrete and pictorial models and number sentences.
TX.M1.5E: Understand that the equal sign represents a relationship where expressions on each side of the equal sign represent the same value(s).
TX.M1.5F: Determine the unknown whole number in an addition or subtraction equation when the unknown may be any one of the three or four terms in the equation.
TX.M1.5G: Apply properties of operations to add and subtract two or three numbers.
TX.M1.6: The student applies mathematical process standards to analyze attributes of two-dimensional shapes and three-dimensional solids to develop generalizations about their properties. The student is expected to:
TX.M1.6A: Classify and sort regular and irregular two-dimensional shapes based on attributes using informal geometric language.
TX.M1.6B: Distinguish between attributes that define a two-dimensional or three-dimensional figure and attributes that do not define the shape.
TX.M1.6C: Create two-dimensional figures, including circles, triangles, rectangles, and squares, as special rectangles, rhombuses, and hexagons.
TX.M1.6D: Identify two-dimensional shapes, including circles, triangles, rectangles, and squares, as special rectangles, rhombuses, and hexagons and describe their attributes using formal geometric language.
TX.M1.6E: Identify three-dimensional solids, including spheres, cones, cylinders, rectangular prisms (including cubes), and triangular prisms, and describe their attributes using formal geometric language.
TX.M1.6F: Compose two-dimensional shapes by joining two, three, or four figures to produce a target shape in more than one way if possible.
TX.M1.6G: Partition two-dimensional figures into two and four fair shares or equal parts and describe the parts using words.
TX.M1.6H: Identify examples and non-examples of halves and fourths.
TX.M1.7: The student applies mathematical process standards to select and use units to describe length and time. The student is expected to:
TX.M1.7A: Use measuring tools to measure the length of objects to reinforce the continuous nature of linear measurement.
TX.M1.7B: Illustrate that the length of an object is the number of same-size units of length that, when laid end-to-end with no gaps or overlaps, reach from one end of the object to the other.
TX.M1.7C: Measure the same object/distance with units of two different lengths and describe how and why the measurements differ.
TX.M1.7D: Describe a length to the nearest whole unit using a number and a unit.
TX.M1.7E: Tell time to the hour and half hour using analog and digital clocks.
TX.M1.8: The student applies mathematical process standards to organize data to make it useful for interpreting information and solving problems. The student is expected to:
TX.M1.8A: Collect, sort, and organize data in up to three categories using models/representations such as tally marks or T-charts.
TX.M1.8B: Use data to create picture and bar-type graphs.
TX.M1.8C: Draw conclusions and generate and answer questions using information from picture and bar-type graphs.
TX.M1.9: The student applies mathematical process standards to manage one's financial resources effectively for lifetime financial security. The student is expected to:
TX.M1.9B: Identify income as a means of obtaining goods and services, oftentimes making choices between wants and needs.
TX.R2.1: Listening, speaking, discussion, and thinking--oral language. The student develops oral language through listening, speaking, and discussion. The student is expected to:
TX.R2.1A: Listen actively, ask relevant questions to clarify information, and answer questions using multi-word responses.
TX.R2.1B: Follow, restate, and give oral instructions that involve a short, related sequence of actions.
TX.R2.1C: Share information and ideas that focus on the topic under discussion, speaking clearly at an appropriate pace and using the conventions of language.
TX.R2.1D: Work collaboratively with others by following agreed-upon rules for discussion, including listening to others, speaking when recognized, making appropriate contributions, and building on the ideas of others.
TX.R2.1E: Develop social communication such as distinguishing between asking and telling.
TX.R2.2: Listening, speaking, reading, writing, and thinking--beginning reading and writing. The student develops word structure knowledge through phonological awareness, print concepts, phonics, and morphology to communicate, decode, and spell. The student is expected to:
TX.R2.2A.i: Producing a series of rhyming words.
TX.R2.2A.ii: Distinguishing between long and short vowel sounds in one-syllable and multi-syllable words.
TX.R2.2A.iii: Recognizing the change in spoken word when a specified phoneme is added, changed, or removed.
TX.R2.2B: Demonstrate and apply phonetic knowledge by:
TX.R2.2B.i: Decoding words with short, long, or variant vowels, trigraphs, and blends.
TX.R2.2B.ii: Decoding words with silent letters such as knife and gnat.
TX.R2.2B.iii: Decoding multisyllabic words with closed syllables; open syllables; VCe syllables; vowel teams, including digraphs and diphthongs; r-controlled syllables; and final stable syllables.
TX.R2.2B.iv: Decoding compound words, contractions, and common abbreviations.
TX.R2.2B.v: Decoding words using knowledge of syllable division patterns such as VCCV, VCV, and VCCCV.
TX.R2.2B.vi: Decoding words with prefixes, including un-, re-, and dis-, and inflectional endings, including -s, -es, -ed, -ing, -er, and -est.
TX.R2.2B.vii: Identifying and reading high-frequency words from a research-based list.
TX.R2.2C.i: Spelling one-syllable and multisyllabic words with closed syllables; open syllables; VCe syllables; vowel teams, including digraphs and diphthongs; r-controlled syllables; and final stable syllables.
TX.R2.2C.ii: Spelling words with silent letters such as knife and gnat.
TX.R2.2C.iii: Spelling compound words, contractions, and common abbreviations.
TX.R2.2C.iv: Spelling multisyllabic words with multiple sound-spelling patterns.
TX.R2.2C.v: Spelling words using knowledge of syllable division patterns, including words with double consonants in the middle of the word.
TX.R2.2C.vi: Spelling words with prefixes, including un-, re-, and dis-, and inflectional endings, including -s, -es, -ed, -ing, -er, and -est.
TX.R2.2D: Alphabetize a series of words and use a dictionary or glossary to find words.
TX.R2.2E: Develop handwriting by accurately forming all cursive letters using appropriate strokes when connecting letters.
TX.R2.3: Listening, speaking, reading, writing, and thinking--vocabulary. The student uses newly acquired vocabulary expressively. The student is expected to:
TX.R2.3A: Use print or digital resources to determine meaning and pronunciation of unknown words.
TX.R2.3B: Use context within and beyond a sentence to determine the meaning of unfamiliar words.
TX.R2.3C: Identify the meaning of and use words with affixes un-, re-, -ly, -er, and -est (comparative and superlative), and -ion/tion/sion.
TX.R2.3D: Identify, use, and explain the meaning of antonyms, synonyms, idioms, and homographs in context.
TX.R2.4: Listening, speaking, reading, writing, and thinking--fluency. The student reads grade-level text with fluency and comprehension.
TX.R2.4A: Use appropriate fluency (rate, accuracy, and prosody) when reading grade-level text.
TX.R2.5: Listening, speaking, reading, writing, and thinking--self-sustained reading. The student reads grade-appropriate texts independently.
TX.R2.5A: Self-select text and read independently for a sustained period of time.
TX.R2.6: Listening, speaking, reading, writing, and thinking using multiple texts. The student uses metacognitive skills to both develop and deepen comprehension of increasingly complex texts. The student is expected to:
TX.R2.6A: Establish purpose for reading assigned and self-selected texts.
TX.R2.6B: Generate questions about text before, during, and after reading to deepen understanding and gain information.
TX.R2.6C: Make and correct or confirm predictions using text features, characteristics of genre, and structures.
TX.R2.6D: Create mental images to deepen understanding.
TX.R2.6E: Make connections to personal experiences, ideas in other texts, and society.
TX.R2.6F: Make inferences and use evidence to support understanding.
TX.R2.6G: EEvaluate details read to determine key ideas.
TX.R2.6H: Synthesize information to create new understanding.
TX.R2.6I: Monitor comprehension and make adjustments such as re-reading, using background knowledge, checking for visual cues, and asking questions when understanding breaks down.
TX.R2.7: Listening, speaking, reading, writing, and thinking using multiple texts. The student responds to an increasingly challenging variety of sources that are read, heard, or viewed. The student is expected to:
TX.R2.7A: Describe personal connections to a variety of sources.
TX.R2.7B: Write brief comments on literary or informational texts that demonstrate an understanding of the text.
TX.R2.7C: Use text evidence to support an appropriate response.
TX.R2.7D: Retell and paraphrase texts in ways that maintain meaning and logical order.
TX.R2.7E: Interact with sources in meaningful ways such as illustrating or writing.
TX.R2.7F: Respond using newly acquired vocabulary as appropriate.
TX.R2.8: Listening, speaking, reading, writing, and thinking using multiple texts--literary elements. The student recognizes and analyzes literary elements within and across increasingly complex traditional, contemporary, classical, and diverse literary texts.
TX.R2.8A: Discuss topics and determine theme using text evidence with adult assistance.
TX.R2.8B: Describe the main character's (characters') internal and external traits.
TX.R2.8C: Describe and understand plot elements, including the main events, the conflict, and the resolution, for texts read aloud and independently.
TX.R2.8D: Describe the importance of the setting.
TX.R2.9: Listening, speaking, reading, writing, and thinking using multiple texts--genres. The student recognizes and analyzes genre-specific characteristics, structures, and purposes within and across increasingly complex traditional, contemporary, classical, and diverse texts. The student is expected to:
TX.R2.9A: Demonstrate knowledge of distinguishing characteristics of well-known children's literature such as folktales, fables, and fairy tales.
TX.R2.9B: Explain visual patterns and structures in a variety of poems.
TX.R2.9C: Discuss elements of drama such as characters, dialogue, and setting.
TX.R2.9D: Recognize characteristics and structures of informational text.
TX.R2.9D.i: The central idea and supporting evidence with adult assistance.
TX.R2.9D.ii: Features and graphics to locate and gain information.
TX.R2.9D.iii: Organizational patterns such as chronological order and cause and effect stated explicitly.
TX.R2.9E: RecRecognize characteristics of persuasive text, including:
TX.R2.9E.i: Stating what the author is trying to persuade the reader to think or do.
TX.R2.9F: Recognize characteristics of multimodal and digital texts.
TX.R2.10: Listening, speaking, reading, writing, and thinking using multiple texts. The student uses critical inquiry to analyze the authors' choices and how they influence and communicate meaning within a variety of texts. The student analyzes and applies author's craft purposefully in order to develop his or her own products and performances. The student is expected to:
TX.R2.10A: Discuss the author's purpose for writing text.
TX.R2.10B: Discuss how the use of text structure contributes to the author's purpose.
TX.R2.10C: Discuss the author's use of print and graphic features to achieve specific purposes.
TX.R2.10D: Discuss the use of descriptive, literal, and figurative language.
TX.R2.10E: Identify the use of first or third person in a text.
TX.R2.10F: Identify and explain the use of repetition.
TX.R2.11: Listening, speaking, reading, writing, and thinking using multiple texts--writing process. The student uses the writing process recursively to compose multiple texts that are legible and uses appropriate conventions. The student is expected to:
TX.R2.11A: Plan a first draft by generating ideas for writing such as drawing and brainstorming.
TX.R2.11B: Develop drafts into a focused piece of writing by:
TX.R2.11B.ii: Developing an idea with specific and relevant details.
TX.R2.11C: Revise drafts by adding, deleting, or rearranging words, phrases, or sentences.
TX.R2.11D: Edit drafts using standard English conventions, including:
TX.R2.11D.ii: Past, present, and future verb tense.
TX.R2.11D.iii: Singular, plural, common, and proper nouns.
TX.R2.11D.v: Adverbs that convey time and adverbs that convey place.
TX.R2.11D.vii: Pronouns, including subjective, objective, and possessive cases.
TX.R2.11D.viii: Coordinating conjunctions to form compound subjects and predicates.
TX.R2.11D.ix: Capitalization of months, days of the week, and the salutation and conclusion of a letter.
TX.R2.11D.x: CorreEnd punctuation, apostrophes in contractions, and commas with items in a series and in dates.
TX.R2.11D.xi: Correct spelling of words with grade-appropriate orthographic patterns and rules and high-frequency words.
TX.R2.12: Listening, speaking, reading, writing, and thinking using multiple texts--genres. The student uses genre characteristics and craft to compose multiple texts that are meaningful. The student is expected to:
TX.R2.12A: Compose literary texts, including personal narratives and poetry.
TX.R2.12B: Compose informational texts, including procedural texts and reports.
TX.R2.12C: Compose correspondence such as thank you notes or letters.
TX.R2.13: Listening, speaking, reading, writing, and thinking using multiple texts. The student engages in both short-term and sustained recursive inquiry processes for a variety of purposes. The student is expected to:
TX.R2.13A: Generate questions for formal and informal inquiry with adult assistance.
TX.R2.13B: Develop and follow a research plan with adult assistance.
TX.R2.13C: Identify and gather relevant sources and information to answer the questions.
TX.R2.13G: Use an appropriate mode of delivery, whether written, oral, or multimodal, to present results.
TX.M2.1: The student uses mathematical processes to acquire and demonstrate mathematical understanding. The student is expected to:
TX.M2.1A: Apply mathematics to problems arising in everyday life, society, and the workplace.
TX.M2.1B: Use a problem-solving model that incorporates analyzing given information, formulating a plan or strategy, determining a solution, justifying the solution, and evaluating the problem-solving process and the reasonableness of the solution.
TX.M2.1C: Select tools, including real objects, manipulatives, paper and pencil, and technology as appropriate, and techniques, including mental math, estimation, and number sense as appropriate, to solve problems.
TX.M2.1D: Communicate mathematical ideas, reasoning, and their implications using multiple representations, including symbols, diagrams, graphs, and language as appropriate.
TX.M2.1E: Create and use representations to organize, record, and communicate mathematical ideas.
TX.M2.1F: Analyze mathematical relationships to connect and communicate mathematical ideas.
TX.M2.1G: Display, explain, and justify mathematical ideas and arguments using precise mathematical language in written or oral communication.
TX.M2.2: The student applies mathematical process standards to understand how to represent and compare whole numbers, the relative position and magnitude of whole numbers, and relationships within the numeration system related to place value. The student is expected to:
TX.M2.2A: Use concrete and pictorial models to compose and decompose numbers up to 1,200 in more than one way as a sum of so many thousands, hundreds, tens, and ones.
TX.M2.2B: Use standard, word, and expanded forms to represent numbers up to 1,200.
TX.M2.2C: Generate a number that is greater than or less than a given whole number up to 1,200.
TX.M2.2D: Use place value to compare and order whole numbers up to 1,200 using comparative language, numbers, and symbols (`>,<,or=`).
TX.M2.2E: Locate the position of a given whole number on an open number line.
TX.M2.2F: Name the whole number that corresponds to a specific point on a number line.
TX.M2.3: The student applies mathematical process standards to recognize and represent fractional units and communicates how they are used to name parts of a whole. The student is expected to:
TX.M2.3A: Partition objects into equal parts and name the parts, including halves, fourths, and eighths, using words.
TX.M2.3B: Explain that the more fractional parts used to make a whole, the smaller the part; and the fewer the fractional parts, the larger the part.
TX.M2.3C: Use concrete models to count fractional parts beyond one whole using words and recognize how many parts it takes to equal one whole.
TX.M2.3D: Identify examples and non-examples of halves, fourths, and eighths.
TX.M2.4: The student applies mathematical process standards to develop and use strategies and methods for whole number computations in order to solve addition and subtraction problems with efficiency and accuracy. The student is expected to:
TX.M2.4A: Recall basic facts to add and subtract within 20 with automaticity.
TX.M2.4B: Add up to four two-digit numbers and subtract two-digit numbers using mental strategies and algorithms based on knowledge of place value and properties of operations.
TX.M2.4C: Solve one-step and multi-step word problems involving addition and subtraction within `1text(,)000` using a variety of strategies based on place value, including algorithms.
TX.M2.4D: Generate and solve problem situations for a given mathematical number sentence involving addition and subtraction of whole numbers within `1text(,)000`.
TX.M2.5: The student applies mathematical process standards to determine the value of coins in order to solve monetary transactions. The student is expected to:
TX.M2.5A: Determine the value of a collection of coins up to one dollar.
TX.M2.5B: Use the cent symbol, dollar sign, and the decimal point to name the value of a collection of coins.
TX.M2.6: The student applies mathematical process standards to connect repeated addition and subtraction to multiplication and division situations that involve equal groupings and shares. The student is expected to:
TX.M2.6A: Model, create, and describe contextual multiplication situations in which equivalent sets of concrete objects are joined.
TX.M2.6B: Model, create, and describe contextual division situations in which a set of concrete objects is separated into equivalent sets.
TX.M2.7: The student applies mathematical process standards to identify and apply number patterns within properties of numbers and operations in order to describe relationships. The student is expected to:
TX.M2.7A: Determine whether a number up to 40 is even or odd using pairings of objects to represent the number.
TX.M2.7B: Use an understanding of place value to determine the number that is `10or100` more or less than a given number up to 1,200.
TX.M2.7C: Represent and solve addition and subtraction word problems where unknowns may be any one of the terms in the problem.
TX.M2.8: The student applies mathematical process standards to analyze attributes of two-dimensional shapes and three-dimensional solids to develop generalizations about their properties. The student is expected to:
TX.M2.8A: Create two-dimensional shapes based on given attributes, including number of sides and vertices.
TX.M2.8B: Classify and sort three-dimensional solids, including spheres, cones, cylinders, rectangular prisms (including cubes as special rectangular prisms), and triangular prisms, based on attributes using formal geometric language.
TX.M2.8C: Classify and sort polygons with 12 or fewer sides according to attributes, including identifying the number of sides and number of vertices.
TX.M2.8D: Compose two-dimensional shapes and three-dimensional solids with given properties or attributes.
TX.M2.8E: Decompose two-dimensional shapes such as cutting out a square from a rectangle, dividing a shape in half, or partitioning a rectangle into identical triangles and identify the resulting geometric parts.
TX.M2.9: he student applies mathematical process standards to select and use units to describe length, area, and time. The student is expected to:
TX.M2.9A: Find the length of objects using concrete models for standard units of length.
TX.M2.9B: Describe the inverse relationship between the size of the unit and the number of units needed to equal the length of an object.
TX.M2.9C: Represent whole numbers as distances from any given location on a number line.
TX.M2.9D: Determine the length of an object to the nearest marked unit using rulers, yardsticks, meter sticks, or measuring tapes.
TX.M2.9E: Determine a solution to a problem involving length, including estimating lengths.
TX.M2.9F: Use concrete models of square units to find the area of a rectangle by covering it with no gaps or overlaps, counting to find the total number of square units, and describing the measurement using a number and the unit.
TX.M2.9G: Read and write time to the nearest one-minute increment using analog and digital clocks and distinguish between a.m. and p.m.
TX.M2.10: The student applies mathematical process standards to organize data to make it useful for interpreting information and solving problems. The student is expected to:
TX.M2.10A: Explain that the length of a bar in a bar graph or the number of pictures in a pictograph represents the number of data points for a given category.
TX.M2.10B: Organize a collection of data with up to four categories using pictographs and bar graphs with intervals of one or more.
TX.M2.10C: Write and solve one-step word problems involving addition or subtraction using data represented within pictographs and bar graphs with intervals of one.
TX.M2.10D: Draw conclusions and make predictions from information in a graph.
TX.M2.11: The student applies mathematical process standards to manage one's financial resources effectively for lifetime financial security. The student is expected to:
TX.M2.11A: Calculate how money saved can accumulate into a larger amount over time.
TX.M2.11B: Explain that saving is an alternative to spending.
TX.M2.11C: Distinguish between a deposit and a withdrawal.
TX.M2.11D: Identify examples of borrowing and distinguish between responsible and irresponsible borrowing.
TX.M2.11E: Identify examples of lending and use concepts of benefits and costs to evaluate lending decisions.
TX.M2.11F: Differentiate between producers and consumers and calculate the cost to produce a simple item.
TX.R3.1: Listening, speaking, discussion, and thinking--oral language. The student develops oral language through listening, speaking, and discussion. The student is expected to:
TX.R3.1A: Listen actively, ask relevant questions to clarify information, and make pertinent comments.
TX.R3.1B: Follow, restate, and give oral instructions that involve a series of related sequences of action.
TX.R3.1C: Speak coherently about the topic under discussion, employing eye contact, speaking rate, volume, enunciation, and the conventions of language to communicate ideas effectively.
TX.R3.1D: Work collaboratively with others by following agreed-upon rules, norms, and protocols.
TX.R3.1E: Develop social communication such as conversing politely in all situations.
TX.R3.2: Listening, speaking, reading, writing, and thinking--beginning reading and writing. The student develops word structure knowledge through phonological awareness, print concepts, phonics, and morphology to communicate, decode, and spell. The student is expected to:
TX.R3.2A: Demonstrate and apply phonetic knowledge by:
TX.R3.2A.i: Decoding multisyllabic words with multiple sound-spelling patterns such as eigh, ough, and en.
TX.R3.2A.ii: Decoding multisyllabic words with closed syllables; open syllables; VCe syllables; vowel teams, including digraphs and diphthongs; r-controlled syllables; and final stable syllables.
TX.R3.2A.iii: Decoding compound words, contractions, and abbreviations.
TX.R3.2A.iv: Decoding words using knowledge of syllable division patterns such as VCCV, VCV, and VCCCV with accent shifts.
TX.R3.2A.v: Decoding words using knowledge of prefixes.
TX.R3.2A.vi: Decoding words using knowledge of suffixes, including how they can change base words such as dropping e, changing y to i, and doubling final consonants.
TX.R3.2A.vii: Identifying and reading high-frequency words from a research-based list.
TX.R3.2B.i: Spelling multisyllabic words with closed syllables; open syllables; VCe syllables; vowel teams, including digraphs and diphthongs; r-controlled syllables; and final stable syllables.
TX.R3.2B.iii: Spelling compound words, contractions, and abbreviations.
TX.R3.2B.iv: Spelling multisyllabic words with multiple sound-spelling patterns.
TX.R3.2B.v: Spelling words using knowledge of syllable division patterns such as VCCV, VCV, and VCCCV.
TX.R3.2B.vi: Spelling words using knowledge of prefixes.
TX.R3.2B.vii: Spelling words using knowledge of suffixes, including how they can change base words such as dropping e, changing y to i, and doubling final consonants.
TX.R3.2C: Alphabetize a series of words to the third letter.
TX.R3.2D: Write complete words, thoughts, and answers legibly in cursive leaving appropriate spaces between words.
TX.R3.3: Listening, speaking, reading, writing, and thinking--vocabulary. The student uses newly acquired vocabulary expressively. The student is expected to:
TX.R3.3A: Use print or digital resources to determine meaning, syllabication, and pronunciation.
TX.R3.3B: Use context within and beyond a sentence to determine the meaning of unfamiliar words and multiple-meaning words.
TX.R3.3C: Identify the meaning of and use words with affixes such as im- (into), non-, dis-, in- (not, non), pre-, -ness, -y, and -ful.
TX.R3.3D: Identify, use, and explain the meaning of antonyms, synonyms, idioms, homophones, and homographs in a text.
TX.R3.4: Listening, speaking, reading, writing, and thinking--fluency. The student reads grade-level text with fluency and comprehension.
TX.R3.4A: Use appropriate fluency (rate, accuracy, and prosody) when reading grade-level text.
TX.R3.5: Listening, speaking, reading, writing, and thinking--self-sustained reading. The student reads grade-appropriate texts independently.
TX.R3.5A: Self-select text and read independently for a sustained period of time.
TX.R3.6: Listening, speaking, reading, writing, and thinking using multiple texts. The student uses metacognitive skills to both develop and deepen comprehension of increasingly complex texts. The student is expected to:
TX.R3.6A: Establish purpose for reading assigned and self-selected texts.
TX.R3.6B: Generate questions about text before, during, and after reading to deepen understanding and gain information.
TX.R3.6C: Make and correct or confirm predictions using text features, characteristics of genre, and structures.
TX.R3.6D: Create mental images to deepen understanding.
TX.R3.6E: Make connections to personal experiences, ideas in other texts, and society.
TX.R3.6F: Make inferences and use evidence to support understanding.
TX.R3.6G: Evaluate details read to determine key ideas.
TX.R3.6H: Synthesize information to create new understanding.
TX.R3.6I: Monitor comprehension and make adjustments such as re-reading, using background knowledge, asking questions, and annotating when understanding breaks down.
TX.R3.7: Listening, speaking, reading, writing, and thinking using multiple texts. The student responds to an increasingly challenging variety of sources that are read, heard, or viewed. The student is expected to:
TX.R3.7A: Describe personal connections to a variety of sources, including self-selected texts.
TX.R3.7B: Write a response to a literary or informational text that demonstrates an understanding of a text.
TX.R3.7C: Use text evidence to support an appropriate response.
TX.R3.7D: Retell and paraphrase texts in ways that maintain meaning and logical order.
TX.R3.7E: Interact with sources in meaningful ways such as notetaking, annotating, freewriting, or illustrating.
TX.R3.7F: Respond using newly acquired vocabulary as appropriate.
TX.R3.7G: Discuss specific ideas in the text that are important to the meaning.
TX.R3.8: Listening, speaking, reading, writing, and thinking using multiple texts--literary elements. The student recognizes and analyzes literary elements within and across increasingly complex traditional, contemporary, classical, and diverse literary texts.
TX.R3.8A: Infer the theme of a work, distinguishing theme from topic.
TX.R3.8B: Explain the relationships among the major and minor characters.
TX.R3.8C: Analyze plot elements, including the sequence of events, the conflict, and the resolution.
TX.R3.8D: Explain the influence of the setting on the plot.
TX.R3.9: Listening, speaking, reading, writing, and thinking using multiple texts--genres. The student recognizes and analyzes genre-specific characteristics, structures, and purposes within and across increasingly complex traditional, contemporary, classical, and diverse texts. The student is expected to:
TX.R3.9A: Demonstrate knowledge of distinguishing characteristics of well-known children's literature such as folktales, fables, fairy tales, legends, and myths.
TX.R3.9B: Explain rhyme scheme, sound devices, and structural elements such as stanzas in a variety of poems.
TX.R3.9C: Discuss elements of drama such as characters, dialogue, setting, and acts.
TX.R3.9D: Recognize characteristics and structures of informational text.
TX.R3.9D.i: The central idea with supporting evidence.
TX.R3.9D.ii: Features such as sections, tables, graphs, timelines, bullets, numbers, and bold and italicized font to support understanding.
TX.R3.9D.iii: Organizational patterns such as cause and effect and problem and solution.
TX.R3.9E: Recognize characteristics and structures of argumentative text by:
TX.R3.9E.iii: Identifying the intended audience or reader.
TX.R3.9F: Recognize characteristics of multimodal and digital texts.
TX.R3.10: Listening, speaking, reading, writing, and thinking using multiple texts. The student uses critical inquiry to analyze the authors' choices and how they influence and communicate meaning within a variety of texts. The student analyzes and applies author's craft purposefully in order to develop his or her own products and performances. The student is expected to:
TX.R3.10A: Explain the author's purpose and message within a text.
TX.R3.10B: Explain how the use of text structure contributes to the author's purpose.
TX.R3.10C: Explain the author's use of print and graphic features to achieve specific purposes.
TX.R3.10D: Describe how the author's use of imagery, literal and figurative language such as simile, and sound devices such as onomatopoeia achieves specific purposes.
TX.R3.10E: Identify the use of literary devices, including first- or third-person point of view.
TX.R3.10F: Discuss how the author's use of language contributes to voice.
TX.R3.10G: Identify and explain the use of hyperbole.
TX.R3.11: Listening, speaking, reading, writing, and thinking using multiple texts--writing process. The student uses the writing process recursively to compose multiple texts that are legible and uses appropriate conventions. The student is expected to:
TX.R3.11A: Plan a first draft by selecting a genre for a particular topic, purpose, and audience using a range of strategies such as brainstorming, freewriting, and mapping.
TX.R3.11B: Develop drafts into a focused, structured, and coherent piece of writing by:
TX.R3.11B.i: Organizing with purposeful structure, including an introduction and a conclusion.
TX.R3.11B.ii: Developing an engaging idea with relevant details.
TX.R3.11C: Revise drafts to improve sentence structure and word choice by adding, deleting, combining, and rearranging ideas for coherence and clarity.
TX.R3.11D: Edit drafts using standard English conventions, including:
TX.R3.11D.i: Complete simple and compound sentences with subject-verb agreement.
TX.R3.11D.ii: Past, present, and future verb tense.
TX.R3.11D.iii: Singular, plural, common, and proper nouns.
TX.R3.11D.iv: Adjectives, including their comparative and superlative forms.
TX.R3.11D.v: Adverbs that convey time and adverbs that convey manner.
TX.R3.11D.vii: Pronouns, including subjective, objective, and possessive cases.
TX.R3.11D.viii: Coordinating conjunctions to form compound subjects, predicates, and sentences.
TX.R3.11D.ix: Capitalization of official titles of people, holidays, and geographical names and places.
TX.R3.11D.x: Punctuation marks, including apostrophes in contractions and possessives and commas in compound sentences and items in a series.
TX.R3.11D.xi: Correct spelling of words with grade-appropriate orthographic patterns and rules and high-frequency words.
TX.R3.11E: Publish written work for appropriate audiences.
TX.R3.12: Listening, speaking, reading, writing, and thinking using multiple texts--genres. The student uses genre characteristics and craft to compose multiple texts that are meaningful. The student is expected to:
TX.R3.12A: Compose literary texts, including personal narratives and poetry, using genre characteristics and craft.
TX.R3.12B: Compose informational texts, including brief compositions that convey information about a topic, using a clear central idea and genre characteristics and craft.
TX.R3.12C: Compose argumentative texts, including opinion essays, using genre characteristics and craft.
TX.R3.12D: Compose correspondence such as thank you notes or letters.
TX.R3.13: Listening, speaking, reading, writing, and thinking using multiple texts. The student engages in both short-term and sustained recursive inquiry processes for a variety of purposes. The student is expected to:
TX.R3.13A: Generate questions on a topic for formal and informal inquiry.
TX.R3.13B: Develop and follow a research plan with adult assistance.
TX.R3.13C: Identify and gather relevant information from a variety of sources.
TX.R3.13F: Recognize the difference between paraphrasing and plagiarism when using source materials.
TX.R3.13H: Use an appropriate mode of delivery, whether written, oral, or multimodal, to present results.
TX.M3.1: The student uses mathematical processes to acquire and demonstrate mathematical understanding. The student is expected to:
TX.M3.1A: Apply mathematics to problems arising in everyday life, society, and the workplace.
TX.M3.1B: Use a problem-solving model that incorporates analyzing given information, formulating a plan or strategy, determining a solution, justifying the solution, and evaluating the problem-solving process and the reasonableness of the solution.
TX.M3.1C: Select tools, including real objects, manipulatives, paper and pencil, and technology as appropriate, and techniques, including mental math, estimation, and number sense as appropriate, to solve problems.
TX.M3.1D: Communicate mathematical ideas, reasoning, and their implications using multiple representations, including symbols, diagrams, graphs, and language as appropriate.
TX.M3.1E: Create and use representations to organize, record, and communicate mathematical ideas.
TX.M3.1F: Analyze mathematical relationships to connect and communicate mathematical ideas.
TX.M3.1G: Display, explain, and justify mathematical ideas and arguments using precise mathematical language in written or oral communication.
TX.M3.2: The student applies mathematical process standards to represent and compare whole numbers and understand relationships related to place value. The student is expected to:
TX.M3.2A: Compose and decompose numbers up to `100text(,)000` as a sum of so many ten thousands, so many thousands, so many hundreds, so many tens, and so many ones using objects, pictorial models, and numbers, including expanded notation as appropriate.
TX.M3.2B: Describe the mathematical relationships found in the base-10 place value system through the hundred thousands place.
TX.M3.2C: Represent a number on a number line as being between two consecutive multiples of `10;100;1text(,)000;or10text(,)000` and use words to describe relative size of numbers in order to round whole numbers.
TX.M3.2D: Compare and order whole numbers up to `100text(,)000` and represent comparisons using the symbols `>,<,or=`.
TX.M3.3: The student applies mathematical process standards to represent and explain fractional units. The student is expected to:
TX.M3.3A: Represent fractions greater than zero and less than or equal to one with denominators of `2,3,4,6,and8` using concrete objects and pictorial models, including strip diagrams and number lines.
TX.M3.3B: Determine the corresponding fraction greater than zero and less than or equal to one with denominators of `2,3,4,6,and8` given a specified point on a number line.
TX.M3.3C: Explain that the unit fraction `1/b` represents the quantity formed by one part of a whole that has been partitioned into `b` equal parts where `b` is a non-zero whole number.
TX.M3.3D: Compose and decompose a fraction `a/b` with a numerator greater than zero and less than or equal to `b` as a sum of parts `1/b`.
TX.M3.3E: Solve problems involving partitioning an object or a set of objects among two or more recipients using pictorial representations of fractions with denominators of `2,3,4,6,and8`.
TX.M3.3F: Represent equivalent fractions with denominators of `2,3,4,6,and8` using a variety of objects and pictorial models, including number lines.
TX.M3.3G: Explain that two fractions are equivalent if and only if they are both represented by the same point on the number line or represent the same portion of a same size whole for an area model.
TX.M3.3H: Compare two fractions having the same numerator or denominator in problems by reasoning about their sizes and justifying the conclusion using symbols, words, objects, and pictorial models.
TX.M3.4: The student applies mathematical process standards to develop and use strategies and methods for whole number computations in order to solve problems with efficiency and accuracy. The student is expected to:
TX.M3.4A: Solve with fluency one-step and two-step problems involving addition and subtraction within `1text(,)000` using strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and the relationship between addition and subtraction.
TX.M3.4B: Round to the nearest `10or100` or use compatible numbers to estimate solutions to addition and subtraction problems.
TX.M3.4C: Determine the value of a collection of coins and bills.
TX.M3.4D: Determine the total number of objects when equally-sized groups of objects are combined or arranged in arrays up to `10` by `10`.
TX.M3.4E: Represent multiplication facts by using a variety of approaches such as repeated addition, equal-sized groups, arrays, area models, equal jumps on a number line, and skip counting.
TX.M3.4F: Recall facts to multiply up to `10` by `10` with automaticity and recall the corresponding division facts.
TX.M3.4G: Use strategies and algorithms, including the standard algorithm, to multiply a two-digit number by a one-digit number. Strategies may include mental math, partial products, and the commutative, associative, and distributive properties.
TX.M3.4H: Determine the number of objects in each group when a set of objects is partitioned into equal shares or a set of objects is shared equally.
TX.M3.4I: Determine if a number is even or odd using divisibility rules.
TX.M3.4J: Determine a quotient using the relationship between multiplication and division.
TX.M3.4K: Solve one-step and two-step problems involving multiplication and division within `100` using strategies based on objects; pictorial models, including arrays, area models, and equal groups; properties of operations; or recall of facts.
TX.M3.5: The student applies mathematical process standards to analyze and create patterns and relationships. The student is expected to:
TX.M3.5A: Represent one- and two-step problems involving addition and subtraction of whole numbers to `1text(,)000` using pictorial models, number lines, and equations.
TX.M3.5B: Represent and solve one- and two-step multiplication and division problems within `100` using arrays, strip diagrams, and equations.
TX.M3.5C: Describe a multiplication expression as a comparison such as `3xx24` represents `3` times as much as `24`.
TX.M3.5D: Determine the unknown whole number in a multiplication or division equation relating three whole numbers when the unknown is either a missing factor or product.
TX.M3.5E: Represent real-world relationships using number pairs in a table and verbal descriptions.
TX.M3.6: The student applies mathematical process standards to analyze attributes of two-dimensional geometric figures to develop generalizations about their properties. The student is expected to:
TX.M3.6A: Classify and sort two- and three-dimensional figures, including cones, cylinders, spheres, triangular and rectangular prisms, and cubes, based on attributes using formal geometric language.
TX.M3.6B: Use attributes to recognize rhombuses, parallelograms, trapezoids, rectangles, and squares as examples of quadrilaterals and draw examples of quadrilaterals that do not belong to any of these subcategories.
TX.M3.6C: Determine the area of rectangles with whole number side lengths in problems using multiplication related to the number of rows times the number of unit squares in each row.
TX.M3.6D: Decompose composite figures formed by rectangles into non-overlapping rectangles to determine the area of the original figure using the additive property of area.
TX.M3.6E: Decompose two congruent two-dimensional figures into parts with equal areas and express the area of each part as a unit fraction of the whole and recognize that equal shares of identical wholes need not have the same shape.
TX.M3.7: The student applies mathematical process standards to select appropriate units, strategies, and tools to solve problems involving customary and metric measurement. The student is expected to:
TX.M3.7A: Represent fractions of halves, fourths, and eighths as distances from zero on a number line.
TX.M3.7B: Determine the perimeter of a polygon or a missing length when given perimeter and remaining side lengths in problems.
TX.M3.7C: Determine the solutions to problems involving addition and subtraction of time intervals in `text(minutes)` using pictorial models or tools such as a `15text(-minute)` event plus a `30text(-minute)` event equals `45` `text(minutes)`.
TX.M3.7D: Determine when it is appropriate to use measurements of liquid volume (capacity) or weight.
TX.M3.7E: Determine liquid volume (capacity) or weight using appropriate units and tools.
TX.M3.8: The student applies mathematical process standards to solve problems by collecting, organizing, displaying, and interpreting data. The student is expected to:
TX.M3.8A: Summarize a data set with multiple categories using a frequency table, dot plot, pictograph, or bar graph with scaled intervals.
TX.M3.8B: Solve one- and two-step problems using categorical data represented with a frequency table, dot plot, pictograph, or bar graph with scaled intervals.
TX.M3.9: The student applies mathematical process standards to manage one's financial resources effectively for lifetime financial security. The student is expected to:
TX.M3.9A: Explain the connection between human capital/labor and income.
TX.M3.9B: Describe the relationship between the availability or scarcity of resources and how that impacts cost.
TX.M3.9C: Identify the costs and benefits of planned and unplanned spending decisions.
TX.M3.9D: Explain that credit is used when wants or needs exceed the ability to pay and that it is the borrower's responsibility to pay it back to the lender, usually with interest.
TX.M3.9E: List reasons to save and explain the benefit of a savings plan, including for college.
TX.M3.9F: Identify decisions involving income, spending, saving, credit, and charitable giving.
TX.R4.1: Listening, speaking, discussion, and thinking--oral language. The student develops oral language through listening, speaking, and discussion. The student is expected to:

TX.R4.1B: Follow, restate, and give oral instructions that involve a series of related sequences of action.
TX.R4.1C: Express an opinion supported by accurate information, employing eye contact, speaking rate, volume, enunciation, and the conventions of language to communicate ideas effectively.
TX.R4.1D: Work collaboratively with others to develop a plan of shared responsibilities.

TX.R4.5A: Self-select text and read independently for a sustained period of time.
TX.R4.6: Listening, speaking, reading, writing, and thinking using multiple texts. The student uses metacognitive skills to both develop and deepen comprehension of increasingly complex texts. The student is expected to:

TX.R4.8D: Explain the influence of the setting, including historical and cultural settings, on the plot.

TX.M4.1: The student uses mathematical processes to acquire and demonstrate mathematical understanding. The student is expected to:
TX.M4.1A: Apply mathematics to problems arising in everyday life, society, and the workplace.

TX.M4.1C: Select tools, including real objects, manipulatives, paper and pencil, and technology as appropriate, and techniques, including mental math, estimation, and number sense as appropriate, to solve problems.
TX.M4.1D: Communicate mathematical ideas, reasoning, and their implications using multiple representations, including symbols, diagrams, graphs, and language as appropriate.
TX.M4.1E: Create and use representations to organize, record, and communicate mathematical ideas.
TX.M4.1F: Analyze mathematical relationships to connect and communicate mathematical ideas.
TX.M4.1G: Display, explain, and justify mathematical ideas and arguments using precise mathematical language in written or oral communication.
TX.M4.2: The student applies mathematical process standards to represent, compare, and order whole numbers and decimals and understand relationships related to place value. The student is expected to:
TX.M4.2A: Interpret the value of each place-value position as `10` times the position to the right and as one-tenth of the value of the place to its left.
TX.M4.2B: Represent the value of the digit in whole numbers through `1text(,)000text(,)000text(,)000` and decimals to the hundredths using expanded notation and numerals.
TX.M4.2C: Compare and order whole numbers to `1text(,)000text(,)000text(,)000` and represent comparisons using the symbols `>,<,or=`.
TX.M4.2D: Round whole numbers to a given place value through the hundred thousands place.
TX.M4.2E: Represent decimals, including tenths and hundredths, using concrete and visual models and money.
TX.M4.2F: Compare and order decimals using concrete and visual models to the hundredths.
TX.M4.2G: Relate decimals to fractions that name tenths and hundredths.
TX.M4.2H: Determine the corresponding decimal to the tenths or hundredths place of a specified point on a number line.

TX.M4.3F: Evaluate the reasonableness of sums and differences of fractions using benchmark fractions `0,1/4,1/2,3/4,and1`, referring to the same whole.
TX.M4.3G: Represent fractions and decimals to the tenths or hundredths as distances from zero on a number line.

TX.M4.4A: Add and subtract whole numbers and decimals to the hundredths place using the standard algorithm.
TX.M4.4B: Determine products of a number and `10or100` using properties of operations and place value understandings.
TX.M4.4C: Represent the product of `2` `text(two-digit)` numbers using arrays, area models, or equations, including perfect squares through `15` by `15`.
