TX.M4.4G: Round to the nearest `10,100,or1text(,)000` or use compatible numbers to estimate solutions involving whole numbers.
TX.M4.4H: Solve with fluency one- and two-step problems involving multiplication and division, including interpreting remainders.
TX.M4.5: The student applies mathematical process standards to develop concepts of expressions and equations. The student is expected to:
TX.M4.5A: Represent multi-step problems involving the four operations with whole numbers using strip diagrams and equations with a letter standing for the unknown quantity.
TX.M4.5B: Represent problems using an input-output table and numerical expressions to generate a number pattern that follows a given rule representing the relationship of the values in the resulting sequence and their position in the sequence.
TX.M4.5C: Use models to determine the formulas for the perimeter of a rectangle (l + w + l + w or 2l + 2w), including the special form for perimeter of a square (4s) and the area of a rectangle (l x w).
TX.M4.5D: Solve problems related to perimeter and area of rectangles where dimensions are whole numbers.
TX.M4.6: The student applies mathematical process standards to analyze geometric attributes in order to develop generalizations about their properties. The student is expected to:
TX.M4.6A: Identify points, lines, line segments, rays, angles, and perpendicular and parallel lines.
TX.M4.6B: Identify and draw one or more lines of symmetry, if they exist, for a two-dimensional figure.
TX.M4.6C: Apply knowledge of right angles to identify acute, right, and obtuse triangles.
TX.M4.6D: Classify two-dimensional figures based on the presence or absence of parallel or perpendicular lines or the presence or absence of angles of a specified size.
TX.M4.7: The student applies mathematical process standards to solve problems involving angles less than or equal to 180 degrees. The student is expected to:
TX.M4.7A: Illustrate the measure of an angle as the part of a circle whose center is at the vertex of the angle that is “cut out” by the rays of the angle. Angle measures are limited to whole numbers.
TX.M4.7B: Illustrate degrees as the units used to measure an angle, where `1/360` of any circle is one degree and an angle that “cuts” n/360 out of any circle whose center is at the angle's vertex has a measure of `n` `text(degrees)`. Angle measures are limited to whole numbers.
TX.M4.7C: Determine the approximate measures of angles in degrees to the nearest whole number using a protractor.
TX.M4.7D: Draw an angle with a given measure.
TX.M4.7E: Determine the measure of an unknown angle formed by two non-overlapping adjacent angles given one or both angle measures.
TX.M4.8: The student applies mathematical process standards to select appropriate customary and metric units, strategies, and tools to solve problems involving measurement. The student is expected to:
TX.M4.8A: Identify relative sizes of measurement units within the customary and metric systems.
TX.M4.8B: Convert measurements within the same measurement system, customary or metric, from a smaller unit into a larger unit or a larger unit into a smaller unit when given other equivalent measures represented in a table.
TX.M4.8C: Solve problems that deal with measurements of length, intervals of time, liquid volumes, mass, and money using addition, subtraction, multiplication, or division as appropriate.
TX.M4.9: The student applies mathematical process standards to solve problems by collecting, organizing, displaying, and interpreting data. The student is expected to:
TX.M4.9A: Represent data on a frequency table, dot plot, or stem-and-leaf plot marked with whole numbers and fractions.
TX.M4.9B: Solve one- and two-step problems using data in whole number, decimal, and fraction form in a frequency table, dot plot, or stem-and-leaf plot.
TX.M4.10: The student applies mathematical process standards to manage one's financial resources effectively for lifetime financial security. The student is expected to:
TX.M4.10A: Distinguish between fixed and variable expenses.
TX.M4.10B: Calculate profit in a given situation.
TX.M4.10C: Compare the advantages and disadvantages of various savings options.
TX.M4.10D: Describe how to allocate a weekly allowance among spending; saving, including for college; and sharing.
TX.M4.10E: Describe the basic purpose of financial institutions, including keeping money safe, borrowing money, and lending.
TX.R5.1: Listening, speaking, discussion, and thinking--oral language. The student develops oral language through listening, speaking, and discussion. The student is expected to:
TX.R5.1A: Listen actively to interpret verbal and non-verbal messages, ask relevant questions, and make pertinent comments.
TX.R5.1B: Follow, restate, and give oral instructions that include multiple action steps.
TX.R5.1C: Give an organized presentation employing eye contact, speaking rate, volume, enunciation, natural gestures, and conventions of language to communicate ideas effectively.
TX.R5.1D: Work collaboratively with others to develop a plan of shared responsibilities.
TX.R5.2: Listening, speaking, reading, writing, and thinking--beginning reading and writing. The student develops word structure knowledge through phonological awareness, print concepts, phonics, and morphology to communicate, decode, and spell. The student is expected to:
TX.R5.2A: Demonstrate and apply phonetic knowledge by:
TX.R5.2A.i: Decoding words with consonant changes, including /t/ to /sh/ such as in select and selection and /k/ to /sh/ such as music and musician.
TX.R5.2A.ii: Decoding multisyllabic words with closed syllables; open syllables; VCe syllable; vowel teams, including digraphs and diphthongs; r-controlled syllables; and final stable syllables.
TX.R5.2A.iii: Decoding words using advanced knowledge of syllable division patterns.
TX.R5.2A.iv: Decoding words using advanced knowledge of the influence of prefixes and suffixes on base words.
TX.R5.2A.v: Identifying and reading high-frequency words from a research-based list.
TX.R5.2B.i: Spelling multisyllabic words with closed syllables; open syllables; VCe syllables; vowel teams, including digraphs and diphthongs; r-controlled syllables; and final stable syllables.
TX.R5.2B.ii: Spelling words with consonant changes, including /t/ to /sh/ such as in select and selection and /k/ to /sh/ such as music and musician.
TX.R5.2B.iii: Spelling multisyllabic words with multiple sound-spelling patterns.
TX.R5.2B.iv: Spelling words using advanced knowledge of syllable division patterns.
TX.R5.2B.v: Spelling words using knowledge of prefixes.
TX.R5.2B.vi: Spelling words using knowledge of suffixes, including how they can change base words such as dropping e, changing y to i, and doubling final consonants.
TX.R5.3: Listening, speaking, reading, writing, and thinking--vocabulary. The student uses newly acquired vocabulary expressively. The student is expected to:
TX.R5.3A: Use print or digital resources to determine meaning, syllabication, pronunciation, and word origin.
TX.R5.3B: Use context within and beyond a sentence to determine the relevant meaning of unfamiliar words or multiple-meaning words.
TX.R5.3C: Identify the meaning of and use words with affixes such as trans-, super-, -ive, and -logy and roots such as geo and photo.
TX.R5.3D: Identify, use, and explain the meaning of adages and puns.
TX.R5.4: Listening, speaking, reading, writing, and thinking--fluency. The student reads grade-level text with fluency and comprehension.
TX.R5.4A: Use appropriate fluency (rate, accuracy, and prosody) when reading grade-level text.
TX.R5.5: Listening, speaking, reading, writing, and thinking--self-sustained reading. The student reads grade-appropriate texts independently.
TX.R5.5A: Self-select text and read independently for a sustained period of time.
TX.R5.6: Listening, speaking, reading, writing, and thinking using multiple texts. The student uses metacognitive skills to both develop and deepen comprehension of increasingly complex texts. The student is expected to:
TX.R5.6A: Establish purpose for reading assigned and self-selected texts.
TX.R5.6B: Generate questions about text before, during, and after reading to deepen understanding and gain information.
TX.R5.6C: Make and correct or confirm predictions using text features, characteristics of genre, and structures.
TX.R5.6D: Create mental images to deepen understanding.
TX.R5.6E: Make connections to personal experiences, ideas in other texts, and society.
TX.R5.6F: Make inferences and use evidence to support understanding.
TX.R5.6G: Evaluate details read to determine key ideas.
TX.R5.6H: Synthesize information to create new understanding.
TX.R5.6I: Monitor comprehension and make adjustments such as re-reading, using background knowledge, asking questions, and annotating when understanding breaks down.
TX.R5.7: Listening, speaking, reading, writing, and thinking using multiple texts. The student responds to an increasingly challenging variety of sources that are read, heard, or viewed. The student is expected to:
TX.R5.7A: Describe personal connections to a variety of sources, including self-selected texts.
TX.R5.7B: Write responses that demonstrate understanding of texts, including comparing and contrasting ideas across a variety of sources.
TX.R5.7C: Use text evidence to support an appropriate response.
TX.R5.7D: Retell, paraphrase, or summarize texts in ways that maintain meaning and logical order.
TX.R5.7E: Interact with sources in meaningful ways such as notetaking, annotating, freewriting, or illustrating.
TX.R5.7F: Respond using newly acquired vocabulary as appropriate.
TX.R5.7G: Discuss specific ideas in the text that are important to the meaning.
TX.R5.8: Listening, speaking, reading, writing, and thinking using multiple texts--literary elements. The student recognizes and analyzes literary elements within and across increasingly complex traditional, contemporary, classical, and diverse literary texts.
TX.R5.8A: Infer multiple themes within a text using text evidence.
TX.R5.8B: Analyze the relationships of and conflicts among the characters.
TX.R5.8C: Analyze plot elements, including rising action, climax, falling action, and resolution.
TX.R5.8D: Analyze the influence of the setting, including historical and cultural settings, on the plot.
TX.R5.9: Listening, speaking, reading, writing, and thinking using multiple texts--genres. The student recognizes and analyzes genre-specific characteristics, structures, and purposes within and across increasingly complex traditional, contemporary, classical, and diverse texts. The student is expected to:
TX.R5.9A: Demonstrate knowledge of distinguishing characteristics of well-known children's literature such as folktales, fables, legends, myths, and tall tales.
TX.R5.9B: Explain the use of sound devices and figurative language and distinguish between the poet and the speaker in poems across a variety of poetic forms.
TX.R5.9C: Explain structure in drama such as character tags, acts, scenes, and stage directions.
TX.R5.9D: Recognize characteristics and structures of informational text.
TX.R5.9D.i: The central idea with supporting evidence.
TX.R5.9D.ii: Features such as insets, timelines, and sidebars to support understanding.
TX.R5.9D.iii: Organizational patterns such as logical order and order of importance.
TX.R5.9E: Recognize characteristics and structures of argumentative text by:
TX.R5.9E.ii: Explaining how the author has used facts for or against an argument.
TX.R5.9E.iii: Identifying the intended audience or reader.
TX.R5.9F: Recognize characteristics of multimodal and digital texts.
TX.R5.10: Listening, speaking, reading, writing, and thinking using multiple texts. The student uses critical inquiry to analyze the authors' choices and how they influence and communicate meaning within a variety of texts. The student analyzes and applies author's craft purposefully in order to develop his or her own products and performances. The student is expected to:
TX.R5.10A: Explain the author's purpose and message within a text.
TX.R5.10B: Analyze how the use of text structure contributes to the author's purpose.
TX.R5.10C: Analyze the author's use of print and graphic features to achieve specific purposes.
TX.R5.10D: Describe how the author's use of imagery, literal and figurative language such as simile and metaphor, and sound devices achieves specific purposes.
TX.R5.10E: Identify and understand the use of literary devices, including first- or third-person point of view.
TX.R5.10F: Examine how the author's use of language contributes to voice.
TX.R5.10G: Explain the purpose of hyperbole, stereotyping, and anecdote.
TX.R5.11: Listening, speaking, reading, writing, and thinking using multiple texts--writing process. The student uses the writing process recursively to compose multiple texts that are legible and uses appropriate conventions. The student is expected to:
TX.R5.11A: Plan a first draft by selecting a genre for a particular topic, purpose, and audience using a range of strategies such as brainstorming, freewriting, and mapping.
TX.R5.11B: Develop drafts into a focused, structured, and coherent piece of writing by:
TX.R5.11B.i: Organizing with purposeful structure, including an introduction, transitions, and a conclusion.
TX.R5.11B.ii: Developing an engaging idea reflecting depth of thought with specific facts and details.
TX.R5.11C: Revise drafts to improve sentence structure and word choice by adding, deleting, combining, and rearranging ideas for coherence and clarity.
TX.R5.11D: Edit drafts using standard English conventions, including:
TX.R5.11D.i: Complete simple and compound sentences with subject-verb agreement and avoidance of splices, run-ons, and fragments.
TX.R5.11D.iv: Adjectives, including their comparative and superlative forms.
TX.R5.11D.vi: Prepositions and prepositional phrases and their influence on subject-verb agreement.
TX.R5.11D.viii: Subordinating conjunctions to form complex sentences.
TX.R5.11D.ix: Capitalization of abbreviations, initials, acronyms, and organizations.
TX.R5.11D.x: Punctuation marks, including commas in compound and complex sentences, quotation marks in dialogue, and italics and underlining for titles and emphasis.
TX.R5.11D.xi: Correct spelling of words with grade-appropriate orthographic patterns and rules and high-frequency words.
TX.R5.11E: Publish written work for appropriate audiences.
TX.R5.12: Listening, speaking, reading, writing, and thinking using multiple texts--genres. The student uses genre characteristics and craft to compose multiple texts that are meaningful. The student is expected to:
TX.R5.12A: Compose literary texts such as personal narratives, fiction, and poetry using genre characteristics and craft.
TX.R5.12B: Compose informational texts, including brief compositions that convey information about a topic, using a clear central idea and genre characteristics and craft.
TX.R5.12C: Compose argumentative texts, including opinion essays, using genre characteristics and craft.
TX.R5.13: Listening, speaking, reading, writing, and thinking using multiple texts. The student engages in both short-term and sustained recursive inquiry processes for a variety of purposes. The student is expected to:
TX.R5.13A: Generate and clarify questions on a topic for formal and informal inquiry.
TX.R5.13B: Develop and follow a research plan with adult assistance.
TX.R5.13C: Identify and gather relevant information from a variety of sources.
TX.R5.13D: Understand credibility of primary and secondary sources.
TX.R5.13F: Differentiate between paraphrasing and plagiarism when using source materials.
TX.R5.13H: Use an appropriate mode of delivery, whether written, oral, or multimodal, to present results.
TX.M5.1: The student uses mathematical processes to acquire and demonstrate mathematical understanding. The student is expected to:
TX.M5.1A: Apply mathematics to problems arising in everyday life, society, and the workplace.
TX.M5.1B: Use a problem-solving model that incorporates analyzing given information, formulating a plan or strategy, determining a solution, justifying the solution, and evaluating the problem-solving process and the reasonableness of the solution.
TX.M5.1C: Select tools, including real objects, manipulatives, paper and pencil, and technology as appropriate, and techniques, including mental math, estimation, and number sense as appropriate, to solve problems.
TX.M5.1D: Communicate mathematical ideas, reasoning, and their implications using multiple representations, including symbols, diagrams, graphs, and language as appropriate.
TX.M5.1E: Create and use representations to organize, record, and communicate mathematical ideas.
TX.M5.1F: Analyze mathematical relationships to connect and communicate mathematical ideas.
TX.M5.1G: Display, explain, and justify mathematical ideas and arguments using precise mathematical language in written or oral communication.
TX.M5.2: The student applies mathematical process standards to represent, compare, and order positive rational numbers and understand relationships as related to place value. The student is expected to:
TX.M5.2A: Represent the value of the digit in decimals through the thousandths using expanded notation and numerals.
TX.M5.2B: Compare and order two decimals to thousandths and represent comparisons using the symbols `>,<,or=`.
TX.M5.2C: Round decimals to tenths or hundredths.
TX.M5.3: The student applies mathematical process standards to develop and use strategies and methods for positive rational number computations in order to solve problems with efficiency and accuracy. The student is expected to:
TX.M5.3A: Estimate to determine solutions to mathematical and real-world problems involving addition, subtraction, multiplication, or division.
TX.M5.3B: Multiply with fluency a three-digit number by a two-digit number using the standard algorithm.
TX.M5.3C: Solve with proficiency for quotients of up to a four-digit dividend by a two-digit divisor using strategies and the standard algorithm.
TX.M5.3D: Represent multiplication of decimals with products to the hundredths using objects and pictorial models, including area models.
TX.M5.3E: Solve for products of decimals to the hundredths, including situations involving money, using strategies based on place-value understandings, properties of operations, and the relationship to the multiplication of whole numbers.
TX.M5.3F: Represent quotients of decimals to the hundredths, up to four-digit dividends and two-digit whole number divisors, using objects and pictorial models, including area models.
TX.M5.3G: Solve for quotients of decimals to the hundredths, up to four-digit dividends and two-digit whole number divisors, using strategies and algorithms, including the standard algorithm.
TX.M5.3H: Represent and solve addition and subtraction of fractions with unequal denominators referring to the same whole using objects and pictorial models and properties of operations.
TX.M5.3I: Represent and solve multiplication of a whole number and a fraction that refers to the same whole using objects and pictorial models, including area models.
TX.M5.3J: Represent division of a unit fraction by a whole number and the division of a whole number by a unit fraction such as `(1/3)-:7and7-:(1/3)` using objects and pictorial models, including area models.
TX.M5.3K: Add and subtract positive rational numbers fluently.
TX.M5.3L: Divide whole numbers by unit fractions and unit fractions by whole numbers.
TX.M5.4: The student applies mathematical process standards to develop concepts of expressions and equations. The student is expected to:
TX.M5.4B: Represent and solve multi-step problems involving the four operations with whole numbers using equations with a letter standing for the unknown quantity.
TX.M5.4C: Generate a numerical pattern when given a rule in the form `y=axory=x+a` and graph.
TX.M5.4D: Recognize the difference between additive and multiplicative numerical patterns given in a table or graph.
TX.M5.4E: Describe the meaning of parentheses and brackets in a numeric expression.
TX.M5.4F: Simplify numerical expressions that do not involve exponents, including up to two levels of grouping.
TX.M5.4G: Use concrete objects and pictorial models to develop the formulas for the volume of a rectangular prism, including the special form for a cube `(V=lxxwxxh,V=sxxsxxs,andV=Bh)`.
TX.M5.4H: Represent and solve problems related to perimeter and/or area and related to volume.
TX.M5.5: The student applies mathematical process standards to classify two-dimensional figures by attributes and properties. The student is expected to
TX.M5.5A: Classify two-dimensional figures in a hierarchy of sets and subsets using graphic organizers based on their attributes and properties.
TX.M5.6: The student applies mathematical process standards to understand, recognize, and quantify volume. The student is expected to:
TX.M5.6A: Recognize a cube with side length of one unit as a unit cube having one cubic unit of volume and the volume of a three-dimensional figure as the number of unit cubes (n cubic units) needed to fill it with no gaps or overlaps if possible.
TX.M5.6B: Determine the volume of a rectangular prism with whole number side lengths in problems related to the number of layers times the number of unit cubes in the area of the base.
TX.M5.7: The student applies mathematical process standards to select appropriate units, strategies, and tools to solve problems involving measurement. The student is expected to
TX.M5.7A: Solve problems by calculating conversions within a measurement system, customary or metric.
TX.M5.8: The student applies mathematical process standards to identify locations on a coordinate plane. The student is expected to:
TX.M5.8A: Describe the key attributes of the coordinate plane, including perpendicular number lines (axes) where the intersection (origin) of the two lines coincides with zero on each number line and the given point `(0,0)`; the `xtext(-coordinate)`, the first number in an ordered pair, indicates movement parallel to the `xtext(-axis)` starting at the origin; and the `ytext(-coordinate)`, the second number, indicates movement parallel to the `ytext(-axis)` starting at the origin.
TX.M5.8B: Describe the process for graphing ordered pairs of numbers in the first quadrant of the coordinate plane.
TX.M5.8C: Graph in the first quadrant of the coordinate plane ordered pairs of numbers arising from mathematical and real-world problems, including those generated by number patterns or found in an input-output table.
TX.M5.9: The student applies mathematical process standards to solve problems by collecting, organizing, displaying, and interpreting data. The student is expected to:
TX.M5.9A: Represent categorical data with bar graphs or frequency tables and numerical data, including data sets of measurements in fractions or decimals, with dot plots or stem-and-leaf plots.
TX.M5.9B: Represent discrete paired data on a scatterplot.
TX.M5.9C: Solve one- and two-step problems using data from a frequency table, dot plot, bar graph, stem-and-leaf plot, or scatterplot.
TX.M5.10: The student applies mathematical process standards to manage one's financial resources effectively for lifetime financial security. The student is expected to:
TX.M5.10A: Define income tax, payroll tax, sales tax, and property tax.
TX.M5.10B: Explain the difference between gross income and net income.
TX.M5.10C: Identify the advantages and disadvantages of different methods of payment, including check, credit card, debit card, and electronic payments.
TX.M5.10D: Develop a system for keeping and using financial records.
TX.M5.10E: Describe actions that might be taken to balance a budget when expenses exceed income.

TX.R6.7B: Analyze how the characters' internal and external responses develop the plot.

TX.M6.1: The student uses mathematical processes to acquire and demonstrate mathematical understanding. The student is expected to:

TX.M6.1E: Create and use representations to organize, record, and communicate mathematical ideas.

TX.M6.7C: Determine if two expressions are equivalent using concrete models, pictorial models, and algebraic representations.

TX.M6.8: The student applies mathematical process standards to use geometry to represent relationships and solve problems. The student is expected to:

TX.M6.13B: Distinguish between situations that yield data with and without variability.
TX.M6.14: The student applies mathematical process standards to develop an economic way of thinking and problem solving useful in one's life as a knowledgeable consumer and investor. The student is expected to:

TX.M8.2: The student applies mathematical process standards to represent and use real numbers in a variety of forms. The student is expected to:
TX.M8.2A: Extend previous knowledge of sets and subsets using a visual representation to describe relationships between sets of real numbers.

TX.M8.2C: Convert between standard decimal notation and scientific notation.
TX.M8.2D: Order a set of real numbers arising from mathematical and real-world contexts.
TX.M8.3: The student applies mathematical process standards to use proportional relationships to describe dilations.
TX.M8.3A: Generalize that the ratio of corresponding sides of similar shapes are proportional, including a shape and its dilation.
TX.M8.3B: Compare and contrast the attributes of a shape and its dilation(s) on a coordinate plane.
TX.M8.3C: Use an algebraic representation to explain the effect of a given positive rational scale factor applied to two-dimensional figures on a coordinate plane with the origin as the center of dilation.
TX.M8.4: The student applies mathematical process standards to explain proportional and non-proportional relationships involving slope. The student is expected to:
TX.M8.4A: Use similar right triangles to develop an understanding that slope, m, given as the rate comparing the change in `ytext(-values)` to the change in `xtext(-values),(y_2-y_1)/(x_2-x_1)`, is the same for any two points `(x_1,y_1)and(x_2,y_2)` on the same line.
TX.M8.4B: Graph proportional relationships, interpreting the unit rate as the slope of the line that models the relationship.
TX.M8.4C: Use data from a table or graph to determine the rate of change or slope and `ytext(-intercept)` in mathematical and real-world problems.
TX.M8.5: The student applies mathematical process standards to use proportional and non-proportional relationships to develop foundational concepts of functions. The student is expected to:

TX.M8.5B: Represent linear non-proportional situations with tables, graphs, and equations in the form of `y=mx+b`, where `b!=0`.
TX.M8.5C: Contrast bivariate sets of data that suggest a linear relationship with bivariate sets of data that do not suggest a linear relationship from a graphical representation.
TX.M8.5D: Use a trend line that approximates the linear relationship between bivariate sets of data to make predictions.
TX.M8.5F: Distinguish between proportional and non-proportional situations using tables, graphs, and equations in the form `y=kxory=mx+b`, where `b!=0`.

TX.M8.5H: Identify examples of proportional and non-proportional functions that arise from mathematical and real-world problems.
TX.M8.5I: Write an equation in the form `y=mx+b` to model a linear relationship between two quantities using verbal, numerical, tabular, and graphical representations.
TX.M8.6: The student applies mathematical process standards to develop mathematical relationships and make connections to geometric formulas. The student is expected to:
TX.M8.6A: Describe the volume formula `V=Bh` of a cylinder in terms of its base area and its height.
TX.M8.6B: Model the relationship between the volume of a cylinder and a cone having both congruent bases and heights and connect that relationship to the formulas.
TX.M8.6C: Use models and diagrams to explain the Pythagorean theorem.

TX.M8.7A: Solve problems involving the volume of cylinders, cones, and spheres.
TX.M8.7B: Use previous knowledge of surface area to make connections to the formulas for lateral and total surface area and determine solutions for problems involving rectangular prisms, triangular prisms, and cylinders.
TX.M8.7C: Use the Pythagorean Theorem and its converse to solve problems.
TX.M8.7D: Determine the distance between two points on a coordinate plane using the Pythagorean Theorem.

TX.M8.9: The student applies mathematical process standards to use multiple representations to develop foundational concepts of simultaneous linear equations. The student is expected to:
TX.M8.9A: Identify and verify the values of `xandy` that simultaneously satisfy two linear equations in the form `y=mx+b` from the intersections of the graphed equations.

TX.M8.12: The student applies mathematical process standards to develop an economic way of thinking and problem solving useful in one's life as a knowledgeable consumer and investor. The student is expected to:

TX.M8.12F: Analyze situations to determine if they represent financially responsible decisions and identify the benefits of financial responsibility and the costs of financial irresponsibility.
TX.M8.12G: Estimate the cost of a two-year and four-year college education, including family contribution, and devise a periodic savings plan for accumulating the money needed to contribute to the total cost of attendance for at least the first year of college.

TX.M9-12.A.1E: Create and use representations to organize, record, and communicate mathematical ideas.
TX.M9-12.A.1F: Analyze mathematical relationships to connect and communicate mathematical ideas.
TX.M9-12.A.1G: Display, explain, and justify mathematical ideas and arguments using precise mathematical language in written or oral communication.

TX.M9-12.A.7B: Describe the relationship between the linear factors of quadratic expressions and the zeros of their associated quadratic functions.
TX.M9-12.A.7C: Determine the effects on the graph of the parent function `f(x)=x^2` when `f(x)` is replaced by `af(x),f(x)+d,f(x-c),f(bx)` for specific values of `a,b,c,andd`.
TX.M9-12.A.8: The student applies the mathematical process standards to solve, with and without technology, quadratic equations and evaluate the reasonableness of their solutions. The student formulates statistical relationships and evaluates their reasonableness based on real-world data. The student is expected to:
TX.M9-12.A.8A: Solve quadratic equations having real solutions by factoring, taking square roots, completing the square, and applying the quadratic formula.
TX.M9-12.A.8B: Write, using technology, quadratic functions that provide a reasonable fit to data to estimate solutions and make predictions for real-world problems.
TX.M9-12.A.9: The student applies the mathematical process standards when using properties of exponential functions and their related transformations to write, graph, and represent in multiple ways exponential equations and evaluate, with and without technology, the reasonableness of their solutions. The student formulates statistical relationships and evaluates their reasonableness based on real-world data. The student is expected to:
TX.M9-12.A.9A: Determine the domain and range of exponential functions of the form `f(x)=ab^x` and represent the domain and range using inequalities.
TX.M9-12.A.9B: Interpret the meaning of the values of `aandb` in exponential functions of the form `f(x)=ab^x` in real-world problems.
TX.M9-12.A.9C: Write exponential functions in the form `f(x)=ab^x` (where `b` is a rational number) to describe problems arising from mathematical and real-world situations, including growth and decay.
TX.M9-12.A.9D: Graph exponential functions that model growth and decay and identify key features, including `ytext(-intercept)` and asymptote, in mathematical and real-world problems.
TX.M9-12.A.9E: Write, using technology, exponential functions that provide a reasonable fit to data and make predictions for real-world problems.
TX.M9-12.A.10: The student applies the mathematical process standards and algebraic methods to rewrite in equivalent forms and perform operations on polynomial expressions. The student is expected to:
TX.M9-12.A.10A: Add and subtract polynomials of degree one and degree two.
TX.M9-12.A.10B: Multiply polynomials of degree one and degree two.
TX.M9-12.A.10C: Determine the quotient of a polynomial of degree one and polynomial of degree two when divided by a polynomial of degree one and polynomial of degree two when the degree of the divisor does not exceed the degree of the dividend.
TX.M9-12.A.10D: Rewrite polynomial expressions of degree one and degree two in equivalent forms using the distributive property.
TX.M9-12.A.10E: Factor, if possible, trinomials with real factors in the form `ax^2+bx+c`, including perfect square trinomials of degree two.
TX.M9-12.A.10F: Decide if a binomial can be written as the difference of two squares and, if possible, use the structure of a difference of two squares to rewrite the binomial.
TX.M9-12.A.11: The student applies the mathematical process standards and algebraic methods to rewrite algebraic expressions into equivalent forms. The student is expected to:
TX.M9-12.A.11A: Simplify numerical radical expressions involving square roots.
TX.M9-12.A.11B: Simplify numeric and algebraic expressions using the laws of exponents, including integral and rational exponents.
TX.M9-12.A.12: The student applies the mathematical process standards and algebraic methods to write, solve, analyze, and evaluate equations, relations, and functions. The student is expected to:
TX.M9-12.A.12A: Decide whether relations represented verbally, tabularly, graphically, and symbolically define a function.
TX.M9-12.A.12B: Evaluate functions, expressed in function notation, given one or more elements in their domains.
TX.M9-12.A.12C: Identify terms of arithmetic and geometric sequences when the sequences are given in function form using recursive processes.
TX.M9-12.A.12D: Write a formula for the `n^text(th)` term of arithmetic and geometric sequences, given the value of several of their terms.
TX.M9-12.A.12E: Solve mathematic and scientific formulas, and other literal equations, for a specified variable.
TX.M9-12.A2.1: The student uses mathematical processes to acquire and demonstrate mathematical understanding. The student is expected to:
TX.M9-12.A2.1A: Apply mathematics to problems arising in everyday life, society, and the workplace.
TX.M9-12.A2.1B: Use a problem-solving model that incorporates analyzing given information, formulating a plan or strategy, determining a solution, justifying the solution, and evaluating the problem-solving process and the reasonableness of the solution.
TX.M9-12.A2.1C: Select tools, including real objects, manipulatives, paper and pencil, and technology as appropriate, and techniques, including mental math, estimation, and number sense as appropriate, to solve problems.
TX.M9-12.A2.1D: Communicate mathematical ideas, reasoning, and their implications using multiple representations, including symbols, diagrams, graphs, and language as appropriate.
TX.M9-12.A2.1E: Create and use representations to organize, record, and communicate mathematical ideas.
TX.M9-12.A2.1F: Analyze mathematical relationships to connect and communicate mathematical ideas.
TX.M9-12.A2.1G: Display, explain, or justify mathematical ideas and arguments using precise mathematical language in written or oral communication.
TX.M9-12.A2.2: The student applies mathematical processes to understand that functions have distinct key attributes and understand the relationship between a function and its inverse. The student is expected to:
TX.M9-12.A2.2A: Graph the functions `f(x)=sqrt(x),f(x)=1/x,f(x)=x^3,f(x)=root(3)(x),f(x)=b^x,f(x)=abs(x),andf(x)=log_b(x)` where `b` is `2,10,ande`, and, when applicable, analyze the key attributes such as domain, range, intercepts, symmetries, asymptotic behavior, and maximum and minimum given an interval.
TX.M9-12.A2.2B: Graph and write the inverse of a function using notation such as `f^-1(x)`.
TX.M9-12.A2.2C: Describe and analyze the relationship between a function and its inverse (quadratic and square root, logarithmic and exponential), including the restriction(s) on domain, which will restrict its range.
TX.M9-12.A2.2D: Use the composition of two functions, including the necessary restrictions on the domain, to determine if the functions are inverses of each other.
TX.M9-12.A2.3: The student applies mathematical processes to formulate systems of equations and inequalities, use a variety of methods to solve, and analyze reasonableness of solutions. The student is expected to:
TX.M9-12.A2.3A: Formulate systems of equations, including systems consisting of three linear equations in three variables and systems consisting of two equations, the first linear and the second quadratic.
TX.M9-12.A2.3B: Solve systems of three linear equations in three variables by using Gaussian elimination, technology with matrices, and substitution.
TX.M9-12.A2.3C: Solve, algebraically, systems of two equations in two variables consisting of a linear equation and a quadratic equation.
TX.M9-12.A2.3D: Determine the reasonableness of solutions to systems of a linear equation and a quadratic equation in two variables.
TX.M9-12.A2.3E: Formulate systems of at least two linear inequalities in two variables.
TX.M9-12.A2.3F: Solve systems of two or more linear inequalities in two variables.
TX.M9-12.A2.3G: Determine possible solutions in the solution set of systems of two or more linear inequalities in two variables.
TX.M9-12.A2.4: The student applies mathematical processes to understand that quadratic and square root functions, equations, and quadratic inequalities can be used to model situations, solve problems, and make predictions. The student is expected to:
TX.M9-12.A2.4A: Write the quadratic function given three specified points in the plane.
TX.M9-12.A2.4B: Write the equation of a parabola using given attributes, including vertex, focus, directrix, axis of symmetry, and direction of opening.
TX.M9-12.A2.4C: Determine the effect on the graph of `f(x)=sqrt(x)` when `f(x)` is replaced by `af(x),f(x)+d,f(bx),andf(x-c)` for specific positive and negative values of `a,b,c,andd`.
TX.M9-12.A2.4D: Transform a quadratic function `f(x)=ax^2+bx+c` to the form `f(x)=a(x-h)^2+k` to identify the different attributes of f(x).
TX.M9-12.A2.4E: Formulate quadratic and square root equations using technology given a table of data.
TX.M9-12.A2.4F: Solve quadratic and square root equations.
TX.M9-12.A2.4G: Identify extraneous solutions of square root equations.
TX.M9-12.A2.5: The student applies mathematical processes to understand that exponential and logarithmic functions can be used to model situations and solve problems. The student is expected to:
TX.M9-12.A2.5A: Determine the effects on the key attributes on the graphs of `f(x)=b^xandf(x)=log_b(x)` where `b` is `2,10,ande` when `f(x)` is replaced by `af(x),f(x)+d,andf(x-c)` for specific positive and negative real values of `a,c,andd`.
TX.M9-12.A2.5B: Formulate exponential and logarithmic equations that model real-world situations, including exponential relationships written in recursive notation.
TX.M9-12.A2.5C: Rewrite exponential equations as their corresponding logarithmic equations and logarithmic equations as their corresponding exponential equations.
TX.M9-12.A2.5D: Solve exponential equations of the form `y=ab^x` where `a` is a nonzero real number and `b` is greater than zero and not equal to one and single logarithmic equations having real solutions.
TX.M9-12.A2.5E: Determine the reasonableness of a solution to a logarithmic equation.
TX.M9-12.A2.6: The student applies mathematical processes to understand that cubic, cube root, absolute value and rational functions, equations, and inequalities can be used to model situations, solve problems, and make predictions. The student is expected to:
TX.M9-12.A2.6A: Analyze the effect on the graphs of `f(x)=x^3andf(x)=root(3)(x)` when `f(x)` is replaced by `af(x),f(bx),f(x-c),andf(x)+d` for specific positive and negative real values of `a,b,c,andd`.
TX.M9-12.A2.6B: Solve cube root equations that have real roots.
TX.M9-12.A2.6C: Analyze the effect on the graphs of f(x)=|x| when `f(x)` is replaced by `af(x),f(bx),f(x-c),andf(x)+d` for specific positive and negative real values of `a,b,c,andd`.
TX.M9-12.A2.6G: Analyze the effect on the graphs of `f(x)=1/x` when `f(x)` is replaced by `af(x),f(bx),f(x-c),andf(x)+d` for specific positive and negative real values of `a,b,c,andd`.
TX.M9-12.A2.6H: Formulate rational equations that model real-world situations.
TX.M9-12.A2.6I: Solve rational equations that have real solutions.
TX.M9-12.A2.6J: Determine the reasonableness of a solution to a rational equation.
TX.M9-12.A2.6K: Determine the asymptotic restrictions on the domain of a rational function and represent domain and range using interval notation, inequalities, and set notation.
TX.M9-12.A2.6L: Formulate and solve equations involving inverse variation.
TX.M9-12.A2.7: The student applies mathematical processes to simplify and perform operations on expressions and to solve equations. The student is expected to:
TX.M9-12.A2.7A: Add, subtract, and multiply complex numbers.
TX.M9-12.A2.7C: Determine the quotient of a polynomial of degree three and of degree four when divided by a polynomial of degree one and of degree two.
TX.M9-12.A2.7D: Determine the linear factors of a polynomial function of degree three and of degree four using algebraic methods.
TX.M9-12.A2.7E: Determine linear and quadratic factors of a polynomial expression of degree three and of degree four, including factoring the sum and difference of two cubes and factoring by grouping.
TX.M9-12.A2.7F: Determine the sum, difference, product, and quotient of rational expressions with integral exponents of degree one and of degree two.
TX.M9-12.A2.7G: Rewrite radical expressions that contain variables to equivalent forms.
TX.M9-12.A2.7I: Write the domain and range of a function in interval notation, inequalities, and set notation.
TX.M9-12.A2.8: The student applies mathematical processes to analyze data, select appropriate models, write corresponding functions, and make predictions. The student is expected to:
TX.M9-12.A2.8A: Analyze data to select the appropriate model from among linear, quadratic, and exponential models.
TX.M9-12.A2.8B: Use regression methods available through technology to write a linear function, a quadratic function, and an exponential function from a given set of data.
TX.M9-12.A2.8C: Predict and make decisions and critical judgments from a given set of data using linear, quadratic, and exponential models.
TX.M9-12.G.1: The student uses mathematical processes to acquire and demonstrate mathematical understanding. The student is expected to:
TX.M9-12.G.1A: Apply mathematics to problems arising in everyday life, society, and the workplace.
TX.M9-12.G.1B: Use a problem-solving model that incorporates analyzing given information, formulating a plan or strategy, determining a solution, justifying the solution, and evaluating the problem-solving process and the reasonableness of the solution.
TX.M9-12.G.1C: Select tools, including real objects, manipulatives, paper and pencil, and technology as appropriate, and techniques, including mental math, estimation, and number sense as appropriate, to solve problems.
TX.M9-12.G.1D: Communicate mathematical ideas, reasoning, and their implications using multiple representations, including symbols, diagrams, graphs, and language as appropriate.
TX.M9-12.G.1E: Create and use representations to organize, record, and communicate mathematical ideas.
TX.M9-12.G.1F: Analyze mathematical relationships to connect and communicate mathematical ideas.
TX.M9-12.G.1G: Display, explain, and justify mathematical ideas and arguments using precise mathematical language in written or oral communication.
TX.M9-12.G.2: The student uses the process skills to understand the connections between algebra and geometry and uses the one- and two-dimensional coordinate systems to verify geometric conjectures. The student is expected to:
TX.M9-12.G.2A: Determine the coordinates of a point that is a given fractional distance less than one from one end of a line segment to the other in one- and two-dimensional coordinate systems, including finding the midpoint.
TX.M9-12.G.2B: Derive and use the distance, slope, and midpoint formulas to verify geometric relationships, including congruence of segments and parallelism or perpendicularity of pairs of lines.
TX.M9-12.G.2C: Determine an equation of a line parallel or perpendicular to a given line that passes through a given point.
TX.M9-12.G.3: The student uses the process skills to generate and describe rigid transformations (translation, reflection, and rotation) and non-rigid transformations (dilations that preserve similarity and reductions and enlargements that do not preserve similarity). The student is expected to:
TX.M9-12.G.3A: Describe and perform transformations of figures in a plane using coordinate notation.
TX.M9-12.G.3B: Determine the image or pre-image of a given two-dimensional figure under a composition of rigid transformations, a composition of non-rigid transformations, and a composition of both, including dilations where the center can be any point in the plane.
TX.M9-12.G.3C: Identify the sequence of transformations that will carry a given pre-image onto an image on and off the coordinate plane.
TX.M9-12.G.3D: Identify and distinguish between reflectional and rotational symmetry in a plane figure.
TX.M9-12.G.4: The student uses the process skills with deductive reasoning to understand geometric relationships. The student is expected to:
TX.M9-12.G.4A: Distinguish between undefined terms, definitions, postulates, conjectures, and theorems.
TX.M9-12.G.4B: Identify and determine the validity of the converse, inverse, and contrapositive of a conditional statement and recognize the connection between a biconditional statement and a true conditional statement with a true converse.
TX.M9-12.G.4C: Verify that a conjecture is false using a counterexample.
TX.M9-12.G.4D: Compare geometric relationships between Euclidean and spherical geometries, including parallel lines and the sum of the angles in a triangle.
TX.M9-12.G.5: The student uses constructions to validate conjectures about geometric figures. The student is expected to:
TX.M9-12.G.5A: Investigate patterns to make conjectures about geometric relationships, including angles formed by parallel lines cut by a transversal, criteria required for triangle congruence, special segments of triangles, diagonals of quadrilaterals, interior and exterior angles of polygons, and special segments and angles of circles choosing from a variety of tools.
TX.M9-12.G.5B: Construct congruent segments, congruent angles, a segment bisector, an angle bisector, perpendicular lines, the perpendicular bisector of a line segment, and a line parallel to a given line through a point not on a line using a compass and a straightedge.
TX.M9-12.G.5C: Use the constructions of congruent segments, congruent angles, angle bisectors, and perpendicular bisectors to make conjectures about geometric relationships.
TX.M9-12.G.5D: Verify the Triangle Inequality theorem using constructions and apply the theorem to solve problems.
TX.M9-12.G.6: The student uses the process skills with deductive reasoning to prove and apply theorems by using a variety of methods such as coordinate, transformational, and axiomatic and formats such as two-column, paragraph, and flow chart. The student is expected to:
TX.M9-12.G.6A: Verify theorems about angles formed by the intersection of lines and line segments, including vertical angles, and angles formed by parallel lines cut by a transversal and prove equidistance between the endpoints of a segment and points on its perpendicular bisector and apply these relationships to solve problems.
TX.M9-12.G.6B: Prove two triangles are congruent by applying the Side-Angle-Side, Angle-Side-Angle, Side-Side-Side, Angle-Angle-Side, and Hypotenuse-Leg congruence conditions.
TX.M9-12.G.6C: Apply the definition of congruence, in terms of rigid transformations, to identify congruent figures and their corresponding sides and angles.
TX.M9-12.G.6D: Verify theorems about the relationships in triangles, including proof of the Pythagorean Theorem, the sum of interior angles, base angles of isosceles triangles, midsegments, and medians, and apply these relationships to solve problems.
TX.M9-12.G.6E: Prove a quadrilateral is a parallelogram, rectangle, square, or rhombus using opposite sides, opposite angles, or diagonals and apply these relationships to solve problems.
TX.M9-12.G.7: The student uses the process skills in applying similarity to solve problems. The student is expected to:
TX.M9-12.G.7A: Apply the definition of similarity in terms of a dilation to identify similar figures and their proportional sides and the congruent corresponding angles.
TX.M9-12.G.7B: Apply the Angle-Angle criterion to verify similar triangles and apply the proportionality of the corresponding sides to solve problems.
TX.M9-12.G.8: The student uses the process skills with deductive reasoning to prove and apply theorems by using a variety of methods such as coordinate, transformational, and axiomatic and formats such as two-column, paragraph, and flow chart. The student is expected to:
TX.M9-12.G.8A: Prove theorems about similar triangles, including the Triangle Proportionality theorem, and apply these theorems to solve problems.
TX.M9-12.G.8B: Identify and apply the relationships that exist when an altitude is drawn to the hypotenuse of a right triangle, including the geometric mean, to solve problems.
TX.M9-12.G.9: The student uses the process skills to understand and apply relationships in right triangles. The student is expected to:
TX.M9-12.G.9A: Determine the lengths of sides and measures of angles in a right triangle by applying the trigonometric ratios sine, cosine, and tangent to solve problems.
TX.M9-12.G.9B: Apply the relationships in special right triangles `30°-60°-90°and45°-45°-90°` and the Pythagorean theorem, including Pythagorean triples, to solve problems.
TX.M9-12.G.10: The student uses the process skills to recognize characteristics and dimensional changes of two- and three-dimensional figures. The student is expected to:
TX.M9-12.G.10A: Identify the shapes of two-dimensional cross-sections of prisms, pyramids, cylinders, cones, and spheres and identify three-dimensional objects generated by rotations of two-dimensional shapes.
TX.M9-12.G.10B: Determine and describe how changes in the linear dimensions of a shape affect its perimeter, area, surface area, or volume, including proportional and non-proportional dimensional change.
TX.M9-12.G.11: The student uses the process skills in the application of formulas to determine measures of two- and three-dimensional figures. The student is expected to:
TX.M9-12.G.11A: Apply the formula for the area of regular polygons to solve problems using appropriate units of measure.
TX.M9-12.G.11B: Determine the area of composite two-dimensional figures comprised of a combination of triangles, parallelograms, trapezoids, kites, regular polygons, or sectors of circles to solve problems using appropriate units of measure.
TX.M9-12.G.11C: Apply the formulas for the total and lateral surface area of three-dimensional figures, including prisms, pyramids, cones, cylinders, spheres, and composite figures, to solve problems using appropriate units of measure.
TX.M9-12.G.11D: Apply the formulas for the volume of three-dimensional figures, including prisms, pyramids, cones, cylinders, spheres, and composite figures, to solve problems using appropriate units of measure.
TX.M9-12.G.12: The student uses the process skills to understand geometric relationships and apply theorems and equations about circles. The student is expected to:
TX.M9-12.G.12A: Apply theorems about circles, including relationships among angles, radii, chords, tangents, and secants, to solve non-contextual problems.
TX.M9-12.G.12B: Apply the proportional relationship between the measure of an arc length of a circle and the circumference of the circle to solve problems.
TX.M9-12.G.12C: Apply the proportional relationship between the measure of the area of a sector of a circle and the area of the circle to solve problems.
TX.M9-12.G.12D: Describe radian measure of an angle as the ratio of the length of an arc intercepted by a central angle and the radius of the circle.
TX.M9-12.G.12E: Show that the equation of a circle with center at the origin and radius r is x^2+ y^2= r^2 and determine the equation for the graph of a circle with radius r and center `(h,k),(x-h)^2+(y-k)^2=r^2`.
TX.M9-12.G.13: The student uses the process skills to understand probability in real-world situations and how to apply independence and dependence of events. The student is expected to:
TX.M9-12.G.13A: Develop strategies to use permutations and combinations to solve contextual problems.
TX.M9-12.G.13B: Determine probabilities based on area to solve contextual problems.
TX.M9-12.G.13C: Identify whether two events are independent and compute the probability of the two events occurring together with or without replacement.
TX.M9-12.G.13D: Apply conditional probability in contextual problems.
TX.M9-12.P.1: The student uses mathematical processes to acquire and demonstrate mathematical understanding. The student is expected to:
TX.M9-12.P.1A: Apply mathematics to problems arising in everyday life, society, and the workplace.
TX.M9-12.P.1B: Use a problem-solving model that incorporates analyzing given information, formulating a plan or strategy, determining a solution, justifying the solution, and evaluating the problem-solving process and the reasonableness of the solution.
TX.M9-12.P.1C: Select tools, including real objects, manipulatives, paper and pencil, and technology as appropriate, and techniques, including mental math, estimation, and number sense as appropriate, to solve problems.
TX.M9-12.P.1D: Communicate mathematical ideas, reasoning, and their implications using multiple representations, including symbols, diagrams, graphs, and language as appropriate.
TX.M9-12.P.1E: Create and use representations to organize, record, and communicate mathematical ideas.
TX.M9-12.P.1F: Analyze mathematical relationships to connect and communicate mathematical ideas.
TX.M9-12.P.1G: Display, explain, or justify mathematical ideas and arguments using precise mathematical language in written or oral communication.
TX.M9-12.P.2: The student uses process standards in mathematics to explore, describe, and analyze the attributes of functions. The student makes connections between multiple representations of functions and algebraically constructs new functions. The student analyzes and uses functions to model real-world problems. The student is expected to:
TX.M9-12.P.2A: Use the composition of two functions to model and solve real-world problems.
TX.M9-12.P.2B: Demonstrate that function composition is not always commutative.
TX.M9-12.P.2C: Represent a given function as a composite function of two or more functions.
TX.M9-12.P.2D: Describe symmetry of graphs of even and odd functions.
TX.M9-12.P.2E: Determine an inverse function, when it exists, for a given function over its domain or a subset of its domain and represent the inverse using multiple representations.
TX.M9-12.P.2F: Graph exponential, logarithmic, rational, polynomial, power, trigonometric, inverse trigonometric, and piecewise defined functions, including step functions.
TX.M9-12.P.2G: Graph functions, including exponential, logarithmic, sine, cosine, rational, polynomial, and power functions and their transformations, including `af(x),f(x)+d,f(x-c),f(bx)` for specific values of `a,b,c,andd`, in mathematical and real-world problems.
TX.M9-12.P.2H: Graph `arcsinx` and `arccosx` and describe the limitations on the domain.
TX.M9-12.P.2I: Determine and analyze the key features of exponential, logarithmic, rational, polynomial, power, trigonometric, inverse trigonometric, and piecewise defined functions, including step functions such as domain, range, symmetry, relative maximum, relative minimum, zeros, asymptotes, and intervals over which the function is increasing or decreasing.
TX.M9-12.P.2J: Analyze and describe end behavior of functions, including exponential, logarithmic, rational, polynomial, and power functions, using infinity notation to communicate this characteristic in mathematical and real-world problems.
TX.M9-12.P.2K: Analyze characteristics of rational functions and the behavior of the function around the asymptotes, including horizontal, vertical, and oblique asymptotes.
TX.M9-12.P.2L: Determine various types of discontinuities in the interval `(-oo,oo)` as they relate to functions and explore the limitations of the graphing calculator as it relates to the behavior of the function around discontinuities.
TX.M9-12.P.2M: Describe the left-sided behavior and the right-sided behavior of the graph of a function around discontinuities.
TX.M9-12.P.2N: Analyze situations modeled by functions, including exponential, logarithmic, rational, polynomial, and power functions, to solve real-world problems.
TX.M9-12.P.2O: Develop and use a sinusoidal function that models a situation in mathematical and real-world problems.
TX.M9-12.P.2P: Determine the values of the trigonometric functions at the special angles and relate them in mathematical and real-world problems.
TX.M9-12.P.3: The student uses the process standards in mathematics to model and make connections between algebraic and geometric relations. The student is expected to:
TX.M9-12.P.3A: Graph a set of parametric equations.
TX.M9-12.P.3B: Convert parametric equations into rectangular relations and convert rectangular relations into parametric equations.
TX.M9-12.P.3C: Use parametric equations to model and solve mathematical and real-world problems.
TX.M9-12.P.3D: Graph points in the polar coordinate system and convert between rectangular coordinates and polar coordinates.
TX.M9-12.P.3E: Graph polar equations by plotting points and using technology.
TX.M9-12.P.3F: Determine the conic section formed when a plane intersects a double-napped cone.
TX.M9-12.P.3G: Make connections between the locus definition of conic sections and their equations in rectangular coordinates.
TX.M9-12.P.3H: Use the characteristics of an ellipse to write the equation of an ellipse with center `(h,k)`.
TX.M9-12.P.3I: Use the characteristics of a hyperbola to write the equation of a hyperbola with center `(h,k)`.
TX.M9-12.P.4: The student uses process standards in mathematics to apply appropriate techniques, tools, and formulas to calculate measures in mathematical and real-world problems. The student is expected to:
TX.M9-12.P.4A: Determine the relationship between the unit circle and the definition of a periodic function to evaluate trigonometric functions in mathematical and real-world problems.
TX.M9-12.P.4B: Describe the relationship between degree and radian measure on the unit circle.
TX.M9-12.P.4C: Represent angles in radians or degrees based on the concept of rotation and find the measure of reference angles and angles in standard position.
TX.M9-12.P.4D: Represent angles in radians or degrees based on the concept of rotation in mathematical and real-world problems, including linear and angular velocity.
TX.M9-12.P.4E: Determine the value of trigonometric ratios of angles and solve problems involving trigonometric ratios in mathematical and real-world problems.
TX.M9-12.P.4F: Use trigonometry in mathematical and real-world problems, including directional bearing.
TX.M9-12.P.4G: Use the Law of Sines in mathematical and real-world problems.
TX.M9-12.P.4H: Use the Law of Cosines in mathematical and real-world problems.
TX.M9-12.P.4I: Use vectors to model situations involving magnitude and direction.
TX.M9-12.P.4J: Represent the addition of vectors and the multiplication of a vector by a scalar geometrically and symbolically.
TX.M9-12.P.4K: Apply vector addition and multiplication of a vector by a scalar in mathematical and real-world problems.
TX.M9-12.P.5: The student uses process standards in mathematics to evaluate expressions, describe patterns, formulate models, and solve equations and inequalities using properties, procedures, or algorithms. The student is expected to:
TX.M9-12.P.5A: Evaluate finite sums and geometric series, when possible, written in sigma notation.
TX.M9-12.P.5B: Represent arithmetic sequences and geometric sequences using recursive formulas.
TX.M9-12.P.5C: Calculate the `n^text(th)` term and the `n^text(th)` partial sum of an arithmetic series in mathematical and real-world problems.
TX.M9-12.P.5D: Represent arithmetic series and geometric series using sigma notation.
TX.M9-12.P.5E: Calculate the `n^text(th)` term of a geometric series, the `n^text(th)` partial sum of a geometric series, and sum of an infinite geometric series when it exists.
TX.M9-12.P.5F: Apply the Binomial Theorem for the expansion of `(a+b)^n` in powers of `aandb` for a positive integer n, where `aandb` are any numbers.
TX.M9-12.P.5G: Use the properties of logarithms to evaluate or transform logarithmic expressions.
TX.M9-12.P.5H: Generate and solve logarithmic equations in mathematical and real-world problems.
TX.M9-12.P.5I: Generate and solve exponential equations in mathematical and real-world problems.
TX.M9-12.P.5J: Solve polynomial equations with real coefficients by applying a variety of techniques in mathematical and real-world problems.
TX.M9-12.P.5K: Solve polynomial inequalities with real coefficients by applying a variety of techniques and write the solution set of the polynomial inequality in interval notation in mathematical and real-world problems.
TX.M9-12.P.5L: Solve rational inequalities with real coefficients by applying a variety of techniques and write the solution set of the rational inequality in interval notation in mathematical and real-world problems.
TX.M9-12.P.5M: Use trigonometric identities such as reciprocal, quotient, Pythagorean, cofunctions, even/odd, and sum and difference identities for cosine and sine to simplify trigonometric expressions.
TX.M9-12.P.5N: Generate and solve trigonometric equations in mathematical and real-world problems.
TX.M9-12.S.1: The student uses mathematical processes to acquire and demonstrate mathematical understanding. The student is expected to:
TX.M9-12.S.1A: Apply mathematics to problems arising in everyday life, society, and the workplace.
TX.M9-12.S.1B: Use a problem-solving model that incorporates analyzing given information, formulating a plan or strategy, determining a solution, justifying the solution, and evaluating the problem-solving process and the reasonableness of the solution.
TX.M9-12.S.1C: Select tools, including real objects, manipulatives, paper and pencil, and technology as appropriate, and techniques, including mental math, estimation, and number sense as appropriate, to solve problems.
TX.M9-12.S.1D: Communicate mathematical ideas, reasoning, and their implications using multiple representations, including symbols, diagrams, graphs, and language as appropriate.
TX.M9-12.S.1E: Create and use representations to organize, record, and communicate mathematical ideas.
TX.M9-12.S.1F: Analyze mathematical relationships to connect and communicate mathematical ideas.
TX.M9-12.S.1G: Display, explain, or justify mathematical ideas and arguments using precise mathematical language in written or oral communication.
TX.M9-12.S.2: The student applies mathematical processes to apply understandings about statistical studies, surveys, and experiments to design and conduct a study and use graphical, numerical, and analytical techniques to communicate the results of the study. The student is expected to:
TX.M9-12.S.2A: Compare and contrast the benefits of different sampling techniques, including random sampling and convenience sampling methods.
TX.M9-12.S.2B: Distinguish among observational studies, surveys, and experiments.
TX.M9-12.S.2C: Analyze generalizations made from observational studies, surveys, and experiments.
TX.M9-12.S.2D: Distinguish between sample statistics and population parameters.
TX.M9-12.S.2E: Formulate a meaningful question, determine the data needed to answer the question, gather the appropriate data, analyze the data, and draw reasonable conclusions.
TX.M9-12.S.2F: Communicate methods used, analyses conducted, and conclusions drawn for a data-analysis project through the use of one or more of the following: a written report, a visual display, an oral report, or a multi-media presentation.
TX.M9-12.S.2G: Critically analyze published findings for appropriateness of study design implemented, sampling methods used, or the statistics applied.
TX.M9-12.S.3: The student applies the mathematical process standards when describing and modeling variability. The student is expected to:
TX.M9-12.S.3A: Distinguish between mathematical models and statistical models.
TX.M9-12.S.3B: Construct a statistical model to describe variability around the structure of a mathematical model for a given situation.
TX.M9-12.S.3C: Distinguish among different sources of variability, including measurement, natural, induced, and sampling variability.
TX.M9-12.S.3D: Describe and model variability using population and sampling distributions.
TX.M9-12.S.4: The student applies the mathematical process standards to represent and analyze both categorical and quantitative data. The student is expected to:
TX.M9-12.S.4A: Distinguish between categorical and quantitative data.
TX.M9-12.S.4B: Represent and summarize data and justify the representation.
TX.M9-12.S.4C: Analyze the distribution characteristics of quantitative data, including determining the possible existence and impact of outliers.
TX.M9-12.S.4D: Compare and contrast different graphical or visual representations given the same data set.
TX.M9-12.S.4E: Compare and contrast meaningful information derived from summary statistics given a data set.
TX.M9-12.S.4F: Analyze categorical data, including determining marginal and conditional distributions, using two-way tables.
TX.M9-12.S.5: The student applies the mathematical process standards to connect probability and statistics. The student is expected to:
TX.M9-12.S.5A: Determine probabilities, including the use of a two-way table.
TX.M9-12.S.5B: Describe the relationship between theoretical and empirical probabilities using the Law of Large Numbers.
TX.M9-12.S.5C: Construct a distribution based on a technology-generated simulation or collected samples for a discrete random variable.
TX.M9-12.S.5D: Compare statistical measures such as sample mean and standard deviation from a technology-simulated sampling distribution to the theoretical sampling distribution.
TX.M9-12.S.6: The student applies the mathematical process standards to make inferences and justify conclusions from statistical studies. The student is expected to:
TX.M9-12.S.6A: Explain how a sample statistic and a confidence level are used in the construction of a confidence interval.
TX.M9-12.S.6B: Explain how changes in the sample size, confidence level, and standard deviation affect the margin of error of a confidence interval.
TX.M9-12.S.6C: Calculate a confidence interval for the mean of a normally distributed population with a known standard deviation.
TX.M9-12.S.6D: Calculate a confidence interval for a population proportion.
TX.M9-12.S.6E: Interpret confidence intervals for a population parameter, including confidence intervals from media or statistical reports.
TX.M9-12.S.6F: Explain how a sample statistic provides evidence against a claim about a population parameter when using a hypothesis test.
TX.M9-12.S.6G: Construct null and alternative hypothesis statements about a population parameter.
TX.M9-12.S.6H: Explain the meaning of the p-value in relation to the significance level in providing evidence to reject or fail to reject the null hypothesis in the context of the situation.
TX.M9-12.S.6I: Interpret the results of a hypothesis test using technology-generated results such as large sample tests for proportion, mean, difference between two proportions, and difference between two independent means.
TX.M9-12.S.6J: Describe the potential impact of Type I and Type II Errors.
TX.M9-12.S.7: The student applies the mathematical process standards to analyze relationships among bivariate quantitative data. The student is expected to:
TX.M9-12.S.7A: Analyze scatterplots for patterns, linearity, outliers, and influential points.
TX.M9-12.S.7B: Transform a linear parent function to determine a line of best fit.
TX.M9-12.S.7C: Compare different linear models for the same set of data to determine best fit, including discussions about error.
TX.M9-12.S.7D: Compare different methods for determining best fit, including median-median and absolute value.
TX.M9-12.S.7E: Describe the relationship between influential points and lines of best fit using dynamic graphing technology.
TX.M9-12.S.7F: Identify and interpret the reasonableness of attributes of lines of best fit within the context, including slope and `ytext(-intercept)`.
WI.MK.RF.1: Demonstrate understanding of the organization and basic features of print.
WI.MK.RF.1.a: Follow words from left to right, top to bottom, and page by page.
WI.MK.RF.1.b: Recognize spoken words are represented in written language by specific sequences of letters.
WI.MK.RF.1.c: Understand words are separated by spaces in print.
WI.MK.RF.1.d: Recognize and name all upper- and lowercase letters of the alphabet.
WI.MK.RF.2: Demonstrate understanding of spoken words, syllables, and sounds (phonemes).
WI.MK.RF.2.b: Count, pronounce, blend, and segment syllables in spoken words.
WI.MK.RF.2.c: Blend and segment onsets and rimes of single-syllable spoken words.
WI.MK.RF.2.d: Isolate and pronounce the initial, medial vowel, and final sounds (phonemes) in three-phoneme (consonant-vowel-consonant, or CVC) words.
WI.MK.RF.2.e: Add, delete, or substitute individual sounds (phonemes) in simple, one-syllable words to make new words.
WI.MK.RF.3: Know and apply grade-level phonics and word analysis skills in decoding words.
WI.MK.RF.3.a: Demonstrate basic knowledge of one-to-one letter-sound correspondences by producing the primary or many of the most frequent sounds for each consonant.
WI.MK.RF.3.b: Associate the long and short sounds with common spellings (graphemes) for the five major vowels.
WI.MK.RF.3.c: Read common high-frequency words by sight (e.g., the, of, to, you, she, my, is, are, do, does).
WI.MK.RF.3.d: Distinguish between similarly spelled words by identifying the sounds of the letters that differ.
WI.MK.RF.4: Read emergent-reader texts with purpose and understanding.

WI.MK.RL.2: With prompting and support, retell stories.
WI.MK.RL.3: With prompting and support, identify characters, settings, and important events in a story or pieces of information in a text.
WI.MK.RL.4: With prompting and support, identify specific words that express feelings or content- specific words within a text.
WI.MK.RL.6: Define the role of the author and the illustrator in presenting the ideas in a text.
WI.MK.RL.7: With prompting and support, describe the relationship between illustrations and the text.
WI.MK.RL.9: With prompting and support, compare and contrast two texts; recognize that texts reflect one's own and others' culture.
